articles._body: Contender Series 2026 Week 4 continues with a fight between Adam Darby and Patrick Rivera in the welterweight division. C heck out our Contender Series odds series for our Darby-Rivera prediction and pick. Adam Darby (7-1) brings an undefeated-since-2022 stretch into Week 4 of Dana White’s Contender Series, riding a six-fight win streak. He most recently earned a first-round submission via ninja choke over Thiago Habib in February 2026, following a third-round TKO of Robert Alexandru Constantin in September 2025 as he comes into his fight this Tuesday against Patrick Rivera. atrick Rivera brings a 13-4 record and a six-fight win streak into Week 4 of Dana White’s Contender Series. He most recently earned a third-round rear-naked choke submission over Rey Trujillo at Shogun Fights 32 in March 2026, following a second-round knockout of Cole Presley in November 2025 as he comes into his fight this Tuesday against Adam Darby. Contender Series Week 4 Odds, courtesy of BetOnline . Contender Series Week 4 Odds: Adam Darby-Patrick Rivera Odds Adam Darby: -400 Patrick Rivera: +316 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Why Adam Darby Will Win Adam Darby enters this fight with a 7-1 record and a six-fight winning streak, showing the kind of momentum that peaks at the right moment for a Contender Series opportunity. His most recent win, a first-round submission via ninja choke over Thiago Habib in February 2026, followed a third-round TKO of Robert Alexandru Constantin, proving he can finish fights standing and on the ground. That versatility is a real advantage against a 34-year-old Patrick Rivera, whose 13-4 record, while impressive, includes four career losses that suggest exploitable gaps. Darby’s youth and diverse finishing skill set give him more tools to adapt mid-fight than a more one-dimensional veteran. Darby’s 85.7% finish rate across his career also points to a fighter who doesn’t need to rely on judges, an important trait in a short-notice, high-pressure Contender Series bout. Rivera’s finishing consistency has come largely against regional competition at Shogun Fights, a step down from Darby’s Cage Warriors-level opposition. If Darby can mix his grappling threats with his striking, as he’s shown in recent finishes, he should be able to find openings against Rivera’s more limited toolkit. That combination of momentum, youth, and diverse finishing ability gives Darby the edge to extend his streak and leave Tuesday with a UFC contract in hand. Why Patrick Rivera Will Win Patrick Rivera enters this main event with a battle-tested 13-4 record and a six-fight winning streak, experience that Adam Darby simply hasn’t accumulated yet. His most recent win, a third-round rear-naked choke submission over Rey Trujillo in March 2026, shows he can finish fights deep into the later rounds when the pressure mounts. That championship pedigree matters here. Rivera has been defending a welterweight title at Crazy 88 MMA, meaning he’s used to high-stakes main event pressure, while Darby steps into his first true spotlight moment against a proven veteran. Rivera’s 77% finish rate across his career, including six knockouts, four submissions, and three decisions, shows a well-rounded attack that can adapt regardless of how the fight unfolds. That kind of experience against varied styles should help him problem-solve against Darby’s more limited sample size at the top level. At 34, Rivera brings the kind of savvy and durability that comes from 17 professional fights, compared to Darby’s much shorter eight-fight resume. If Rivera can draw on that experience to weather any early pressure from Darby, his championship-level composure and diverse finishing ability should allow him to take over as the fight progresses, giving him the tools to secure the biggest win of his career and a UFC contract. Final Adam Darby-Patrick Rivera Prediction & Pick This main event pits Adam Darby’s youthful momentum against Patrick Rivera’s battle-tested experience, and the deciding factor should be how well Darby’s finishing versatility holds up against a proven veteran. Darby enters on a six-fight streak, most recently submitting Thiago Habib via ninja choke in February 2026. Rivera, however, brings genuine championship pedigree, having defended his welterweight title at Crazy 88 MMA before submitting Rey Trujillo in March 2026 to extend his own six-fight streak. That experience against varied styles gives him real tools to adjust mid-fight. Given Rivera’s higher volume of professional experience at 13-4 compared to Darby’s 7-1, his composure under pressure should be the deciding edge in a close, competitive main event. The pick here leans toward Patrick Rivera finding a finish in the second or third round, using his savvy to solve Darby’s early pressure before submitting or wearing him down late. articles.title: 76ers’ Jaylen Brown stunned by special gift from Massachusetts
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers forward Jaylen Brown had an acrimonious exit from the Boston Celtics. Even before being traded, Brown did not hide his frustration with the Celtics following their first-round loss in the playoffs, incidentally, against the 76ers. He, however, maintained that he had a good rela
articles._body: Philadelphia 76ers forward Jaylen Brown had an acrimonious exit from the Boston Celtics. Even before being traded, Brown did not hide his frustration with the Celtics following their first-round loss in the playoffs, incidentally, against the 76ers. He, however, maintained that he had a good relationship with the front office. Still, that did not prevent him from being shipped to Philadelphia . Despite the ugly divorce, Brown was happy to return to Boston on Sunday to host 741 Frequency Fest. It was his way to thank the city and say goodbye to the fans after 10 seasons with the Celtics. The free event featured music, games, food, and giveaways. Brown, who also brought his championship ring and Finals MVP trophy, expressed his gratitude when he addressed the crowd, stressing that Boston will always have a special place in his heart. The feeling was mutual, as the 29-year-old star was surprised with a key to the state of Massachusetts, as reported by WEEI’s Justin Turpin. The Commonwealth of Massachusetts gifted Jaylen Brown a key to the state. pic.twitter.com/ObBt6OFFyC — Justin Turpin (@JustinmTurpin) August 30, 2026 Brown’s legacy in Boston extends well beyond basketball. He used his platform, resources, and influence to address some of the city’s biggest challenges, particularly racial injustice, educational inequality, and economic disparity. He founded 7uice Foundation in 2019, which focuses on helping underprivileged youth by connecting them with extracurricular opportunities. In 2025, the Boston City Council declared October 24 as Jaylen Brown Day in honor of his birthday and philantrophy. Brown will make his first return to TD Garden in January, when the Celtics host the 76ers. It is expected to be an emotionally charged game. In the meantime, he can cherish the special gift from Massachusetts and look back on the unforgettable decade he had in Boston. articles._body: Contender Series 2026 Week 4 continues with a fight between Brandon Holmes and Modestino Rodrigues in the middleweight division. C heck out our Contender Series odds series for our Holmes-Rodrigues prediction and pick. Brandon Holmes (6-1) enters Week 4 of Dana White’s Contender Series having bounced back strong from his lone loss on this same platform. He most recently earned a slam-and-punches KO over Preston LaGrange in January 2026, avenging a first-round TKO loss to Cameron Rowston in a previous Contender Series appearance in August 2025. With four finishes among his six wins, he comes into his fight this Tuesday against Modestino Rodrigues. Modestino Rodrigues (7-1) comes into Week 4 of Dana White’s Contender Series, backed by a four-fight finishing streak in Brazil’s regional circuit. He most recently stopped Virgilio Ailton via second-round TKO in June 2025, following a first-round TKO finish of Uilton Correa in April 2025. With seven of his eight career fights ending in stoppage, he comes into his fight this Tuesday against Brandon Holmes. Contender Series Week 4 Odds, courtesy of BetOnline . Contender Series Week 4 Odds: Brandon Holmes-Modestino Rodrigues Odds Brandon Holmes: -140 Modestino Rodrigues: +120 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Why Brandon Holmes Will Win Brandon Holmes enters Tuesday with a 6-1 record and something to prove, having already tasted the Contender Series stage once before. His most recent win, a slam-and-punches KO over Preston LaGrange in January 2026, showed real improvement after a first-round TKO loss to Cameron Rowston on this very platform back in August 2025. That prior exposure matters. Holmes already knows the pressure of fighting under Dana White’s spotlight, while Rodrigues, despite his impressive 7-1 record, has built his résumé almost entirely on Brazil’s regional circuit against less battle-tested opposition . Rodrigues finishes fights early and often, but that pattern has come against competition without the kind of live-round experience Holmes now carries into this bout. If Holmes can weather any early pressure, his improved composure and second Contender Series look should give him a mental edge Rodrigues hasn’t had to develop. Holmes’s four finishes in six wins show he’s no stranger to closing the show himself, and his response to adversity after the Rowston loss suggests real growth heading into this rematch of stages. That combination of hard-earned experience and demonstrated resilience gives Holmes the tools to outlast Rodrigues and finally punch his ticket to the UFC. Why Modestino Rodrigues Will Win Modestino Rodrigues enters this bout with a 7-1 record and a finishing rate that speaks for itself, having stopped seven of his eight career opponents. His most recent win, a second-round TKO of Virgilio Ailton in June 2025, followed a first-round finish of Uilton Correa just two months earlier, showing consistent, repeatable violence . At 6’2″, Rodrigues also likely holds a size and reach advantage over Holmes, giving him tools to control distance and dictate where the fight takes place. That physical edge, paired with his finishing instincts, could make it difficult for Holmes to find comfortable range to work his own offense. Holmes has been finished before, losing via first-round TKO to Cameron Rowston in his last Contender Series appearance in August 2025. That history of being stopped under similar high-pressure circumstances raises real questions about his chin and composure against another dangerous finisher like Rodrigues. Rodrigues’s nickname, “The Slenderman,” reflects his long, awkward frame that has given regional opposition fits, and his consistent finishing across multiple weight classes suggests his power translates broadly. If he can implement his size and keep the pace high, his superior finishing rate and physical tools should be enough to hand Holmes a second Contender Series loss and secure his own path to a UFC contract. That prior exposure could help him manage nerves and pace himself better than a Rodrigues who’s fought almost exclusively on Brazil’s regional circuit. Rodrigues’s size and finishing consistency give him a real path to victory if he can push the pace early. But if Holmes survives the opening exchanges, his experience and four career finishes suggest he has the tools to grind out a decision or find a finish of his own late, making this a competitive pick leaning toward Rodrigues by TKO. When it comes to Kentucky high school football teams in the Bluegrass State, no teams matchup to the Shamrocks, which have won 30 state championships in program history. articles._body: The Los Angeles Chargers hit the trade market Sunday ahead of finalizing their 53-man roster. So TeRah Edwards now boosts the defensive line for the Carolina Panthers . However, the Bolts never got the chance to complete their two-deep and entire roster under coach Jim Harbaugh. The Bolts left one position empty. But there’s a catch involving that special teams spot. NFL insider for The Ringer and Netflix Sports Tom Pelissero revealed the reason. “The Chargers released punter J.K. Scott, but it’s temporary: He is expected to return to the roster this week, per source,” Pelissero posted on the social media website X, formerly Twitter. So Harbaugh, quarterback Justin Herbert and the rest of the Chargers have no one who can punt at the moment. But again, they expect him to return. Yet Scott looked like he was on the fringe of a release anyway following one NFL Preseason blunder. Scott surrendered a punt return for the touchdown against the San Francisco 49ers, with Jacob Cowing taking it back 83 yards into the end zone. “The punt fell short and in the middle, and then we got out-flanked,” Harbaugh said to reporters following that Aug. 20 lopsided loss to SF 41-17. Scott worsened things on his end, though, through his infamous tackle attempt. “He’s got to have a plan when he’s in that position to make the tackle. Something we need to work on, coach up,” Harbaugh said. But still, the Chargers plan to save a roster spot for Scott to return once he clears waivers. Making the Chargers tardy in completing their 53-man roster. The post Chargers leave 1 position empty but there’s a catch appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Lions make unfortunate Brian Branch move before 2026 season
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions have not officially confirmed their 53-man roster for the beginning of the 2026 NFL season. However, there is some information coming out about the moves they are making. One of these moves confirms unfortunate news surrounding star safety Brian Branch. Branch is going to begin
articles._body: The Detroit Lions have not officially confirmed their 53-man roster for the beginning of the 2026 NFL season. However, there is some information coming out about the moves they are making. One of these moves confirms unfortunate news surrounding star safety Brian Branch. Branch is going to begin the season on the Physically Unable to Perform list, according to Netflix Sports NFL insider Tom Pelissero. The bad news is that the former second-round pick will miss at least four games to begin the season. There is still a chance he takes the field this season, though. Branch was having an excellent season for the Lions in 2025 before getting hurt. He tore his Achilles tendon against the Dallas Cowboys in early December last year. This injury cost him the remainder of the 2025 campaign. News of Branch’s injury status is brutal for Detroit early in 2026. The Lions had to place their other starting safety, Kerby Joseph , on the Physically Unable to Perform list as well. Joseph is dealing with a knee injury that caused him problems throughout the 2025 campaign. Branch and Joseph form one of the best safety pairings in the NFL. The two star defensive backs helped the Lions to a franchise record 15 wins in 2024. Unfortunately, Detroit was unable to win the Super Bowl that season, as they fell to the Commanders in the NFC Divisional Round. The Lions are hoping to get back to Super Bowl contention in 2026. However, they will need Branch to be 100% healthy before he can take the field again. We’ll see how Detroit’s defense holds up in Week 1 when they play host to Tyler Shough and the New Orleans Saints. After suffering his only loss via submission to Thomas Gantt in September 2025, he rebounded with a highlight-reel spinning back elbow knockout of Kyle Pufahl in May 2026, showing real technical growth and composure under pressure. If Livingston can absorb Smith’s early pressure and drag the fight into deeper rounds, his more varied toolkit and recent momentum should start to show. articles._body: To build a Super Bowl winning team, franchises across the league try to build their nucleus through the draft . For the New York Giants, that hasn’t been prosperous in recent year. On roster cut down day, the Giants moved on from offensive lineman Evan Neal . That means that only two players – Kayvon Thibodeaux and and Micah McFadden – remain from their 2022 draft class, via Evan Barnes of Newsday. Only two players are left from the 2023 class as well in Deonte Banks and John Michael Schmitz. Neal, selected No. 7 overall in 2022, appeared in 29 games with the team, starting 27 of them. Thirteen of those starts came during his rookie season, but then injuries took a major bite out of Neal’s career. He appeared in seven games during the 2023 season and nine in 2024. Ultimately, the Giants decided to go in a different direction. Looking elsewhere in the 2022 class, their second-round pick Wan’Dale Robinson signed with the Tennessee Titans over the offseason. Third-rounder Joshua Ezedu was recently traded to the Kansas City Chiefs while fellow third-rounder Cor’Dale Flott followed Robinson to the Titans. Despite all of those misses, the Giants have had some recent draft hits. Malik Nabers was their first-rounder in 2024. Abdul Carter, Jaxson Dart and Cam Skattebo all arrived in 2025. Arvell Reese and Francis Mauigoa were both selected in the first-round during the 2026 draft. Perhaps it’s a bit early to call all of those players hits. They all have potential, but they must prove themselves consistently at the NFL level. Ultimately though, the Giants are counting on their new core to come through after seeing how bad of a whiff 2022 was. Taking the top spot is last year’s Tennessee Secondary School Athletic Association ( TSSAA ) Division II-AAA state champion Baylor School Red Raiders after a 37-12 defeat of Loudoun Sports Academy last week. Baylor School Red Raiders (2-0) Baylor School started the season as Tennessee’s top-ranked high school football team and then dropped to the second spot behind Oakland before regaining the No. 1 ranking yet again after a 37-12 rout of Loudoun Sports Academy. The Red Raiders looked very impressive in their first game of the regular season as they soundly defeated Brentwood Academy, 38-20, a rematch of last year’s Division II-AAA state championship game. The Red Raiders bring back Tennessee 5-star running back commitment David Gabriel Georges and Ole Miss 4-star quarterback pledge Keegan Croucher . Baylor School will head to the mountains of North Georgia to take on Rabun Gap-Nacoochee School (Ga.) this Friday night. 2. McCallie School Blue Tornados (2-0) The 6-time TSSAA state champion Chattanooga (Tenn.) McCallie School Blue Tornadoes looked a lot more like one of the state’s best when they crushed St. Mary’s Ryken , 67-17, last Friday. The Blue Tornadoes ended last season with a 10-3 record and finished ranked No. 3 in the state according to the final 2025 Tennessee High School Football Massey Rankings. McCallie School still have in-state matchups ahead versus powerhouses Baylor School and Ensworth. The Blue Tornadoes will face three out-of-state programs during the season in Chattanooga, with Mallard Creek (NC) and Loudon Sports Academy (Va.). McCallie School goes on the road this week when they take on Father Ryan . 3. Oakland Patriots (2-0) The 9-time TSSAA state champion Murfreesboro (Tenn.) Oakland Patriots fell multiple spots after being ranked No. 1 as they are coming off a 50-20 victory over Centerville . The Patriots are coming off winning their latest state title in dominating fashion, but will have to chase championship No. 10 after being hit hard with a number of key graduations. Oakland will have to reload as the Patriots graduated a number of key starters from last year’s state championship winning team, including Ole Miss enrollee Craig Tutt , Tennessee enrollee Joel Wyatt and Middle Tennessee enrollee Justis Haggard . The Patriots will make their debut at home this season when they host Smyrna on Friday night. 4. Battle Ground Academy Wildcats (2-0) The Battle Ground Academy Wildcats are rolling offensively behind the play of 2027 3-star quarterback Bo Bryan , who is son of country superstar Luke Bryan . Battle Ground Academy finished the 2025 campaign with 13-1 record and won the TSSAA Division II-AA state championship, defeating Franklin Road Academy, 61-27. The Wildcats return a star studded cast of players, including 2028 four-star wide receiver Maximus Curry , 2028 three-star safety Jeisun Thompson and 2028 three-star athlete Dustin Bennett . A showdown with No. 24 Pearl-Cohn is on tap for this week. 5. articles._body: Contender Series 2026 Week 4 kicks off with a fight between Charlie Cleveland and Gabriel Lourenco in the heavyweight division. C heck out our Contender Series odds series for our Cleveland-Lourenço prediction and pick. Charlie Cleveland (6-1) enters Week 4 of Dana White’s Contender Series riding serious heat, with four knockouts and one submission in 5 of his 6 wins. He most recently blitzed Nyle Bartling via first-round KO at LFA 230 in April 2026, following a 1:03 TKO finish of Benjamin Wunder at LFA 226 in February. Five straight finishes highlight his power as he comes into this fight Tuesday against Gabriel Lourenço. Gabriel Lourenço (7-1) brings a 7-1 record into Week 4 of Dana White’s Contender Series, built on relentless first-round finishing power. His two most recent bouts showcase that trend: a TKO win over Tiago Afonso in June 2025 and a unanimous decision over Alan Oliveira in November 2024, his lone trip to the scorecards. He’s finished six of seven wins as he comes into his fight this Tuesday against Charlie Cleveland. Contender Series Week 4 Odds, courtesy of BetOnline . Contender Series Week 4 Odds: Charlie Cleveland-Gabriel Lourenço Odds Charlie Cleveland: -180 Gabriel Lourenço: +157 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Why Charlie Cleveland Will Win Charlie Cleveland enters this matchup with a five-fight finishing streak that includes four knockouts and a submission. His most recent win, a first-round TKO of Nyle Bartling in April 2026, showed the kind of early aggression Lourenço has struggled to answer. Cleveland is also younger in his development curve as a finisher, using length and kicks effectively, as seen in his fight with Mark Gordon Jr., where both men were similar in weight and reach. That comfort staying long with kicks gives him a distance-management edge against a heavier but less tested Lourenço. Lourenço’s 7-1 record looks impressive on paper, but six of those wins came against opposition with modest Elo ratings, averaging around 1494 heading into this fight. That schedule strength gap matters against a Contender Series-caliber striker like Cleveland. At 6’2″ and 248 pounds, Cleveland carries more of his mass efficiently compared to the 6’3″, 265-pound Lourenço, who has never faced someone with Cleveland’s finishing consistency. Cleveland’s ability to end fights early, paired with a cleaner developmental resume, points to him imposing his pace from the opening bell. Given his pattern of quick finishes and Lourenço’s untested chin against elite pressure, Cleveland looks positioned to add a seventh win, likely by knockout, before the fight reaches deep into the second round. Why Gabriel Lourenço Will Win Gabriel Lourenço brings a 7-1 record and has finished six of his seven wins, proof he’s more than capable of ending the fight before it reaches the judges. At 6’3″ and roughly 265 pounds, he holds a notable size advantage over the 6’2″, 248-pound Cleveland heading into Tuesday’s clash. That extra size and reach could prove decisive against a Cleveland who tends to fight long and rely on kicks, since Lourenço’s frame allows him to close distance and smother that kicking game. His association with Chute Boxe, a camp known for developing well-rounded strikers, also suggests polish that could exploit gaps in Cleveland’s approach . Lourenço’s only loss came via decision, meaning he’s never actually been finished in his career, unlike Cleveland who has tasted defeat as well. That durability, paired with real knockout power evidenced by his TKO finish of Tiago Afonso in June 2025, gives him a path to end the fight early if he can time his entries . If Lourenço uses his physical advantages to pressure Cleveland into the fence and cut off his preferred kicking range, his heavier hands and finishing instincts could take over. His size, power, and unblemished finishing resume make a strong case for him leaving Tuesday’s Contender Series bout with the win. Final Charlie Cleveland-Gabriel Lourenço Prediction & Pick This looks like a striking-heavy clash where distance management decides everything, and Charlie Cleveland’s finishing instincts should give him the edge. His five-fight streak of stoppages, capped by an April 2026 first-round TKO of Nyle Bartling, shows a fighter who capitalizes on openings quickly . Gabriel Lourenço’s size and reach advantage at 6’3″ and roughly 265 pounds are real, but his path to seven finishes has come against lighter competition, with an average opponent Elo near 1494 . That gap in schedule strength raises questions about how he handles adversity against a live striker. Expect Cleveland to use kicks early to keep Lourenço at range, similar to his approach against Mark Gordon Jr., before looking to counter as Lourenço closes distance. If Lourenço can’t cut the cage effectively, Cleveland’s hands should find a home. The pick here is Charlie Cleveland by TKO, likely in the first or second round, extending his finishing streak and punching his ticket toward a UFC contract. Final Charlie Cleveland-Gabriel Lourenço Prediction & Pick: Charlie Cleveland (-180) The post Charlie Cleveland vs. Gabriel Lourenço prediction, odds, pick for Contender Series Week 4 appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.summary: As the Indianapolis Colts put the finishing touches on their 2026 roster, they have to account for Cam Taylor-Britt’s one-game suspension. Because of that, an intriguing offensive lineman has made the final 53. Tackle Luke Tenuta is officially on the Colts’ final roster, via Noah Comp
articles._body: As the Indianapolis Colts put the finishing touches on their 2026 roster, they have to account for Cam Taylor-Britt’s one-game suspension . Because of that, an intriguing offensive lineman has made the final 53. Tackle Luke Tenuta is officially on the Colts’ final roster, via Noah Compton of Sports Illustrated. He initially wasn’t on the roster once officially released, but secured his spot due to Taylor-Britt’s suspension. When the cornerback returns, what happens to Tenuta is yet to be seen. The Colts assuredly want Taylor-Britt on their roster , and seeing as Tenuta was the last man in he would make the most sense as a potential cut. However, perhaps the Colts decide they need a bit more offensive line bulk moving forward. That will be a problem for future Indianapolis. For now, the tackle can celebrate officially making an NFL roster. He was originally a sixth-round pick by the Buffalo Bills back in 2022. He appeared in three games with the Green Bay Packers that season and another four with the Colts in 2025. While he only has seven games and no starts of experience to his name, Tuneta understands what the Colts are looking for. He is going on his second season with the team, and it’s clear head coach Shane Steichen trusts what he provides at tackle. Taylor-Britt’s return will again put Tuneta’s spot in jeopardy. But him making the roster is a sign to Indianapolis and teams across the league that he has plenty to offer. In Week 1 at least, he will be helping the Colts try to start their season with a win. articles.title: Barion Brown makes NFL roster, Dane Key waived
articles.summary: Two of the most popular wide receivers of the Mark Stoops era in Lexington received news on their NFL futures at the 53-man roster deadline on Sunday. Both showed elite promise and produced early and often at Kentucky before a late breakup in their college careers, landing them elsewhere. On the goo
articles._body: Two of the most popular wide receivers of the Mark Stoops era in Lexington received news on their NFL futures at the 53-man roster deadline on Sunday. Both showed elite promise and produced early and often at Kentucky before a late breakup in their college careers, landing them elsewhere. On the good news front, Barion Brown made the official regular season roster in New Orleans after being drafted in the sixth round by the Saints. He’s one of five receivers on the 53, joining Chris Olave, Devaughn Vele, Bryce Lance and Kevin Austin Jr., with a real shot at earning reps as a rookie out of LSU and formerly of Kentucky. The former Wildcat was a training camp standout, then followed it up with a strong preseason, including a touchdown score in the finale on Friday. Saints 6th-round pick Barion Brown finds the end zone Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/s3lAfyzFq0 — NFL (@NFL) August 29, 2026 Brown drew comparisons to Seattle receiver Rashid Shaheed, a former burner for the Saints before he was traded to the Seahawks this past season. It didn’t take long for New Orleans to find an adequate replacement. “They’re basically the same player, I ain’t gonna lie,” Olave said of Brown. “Barion reminds me a lot of ‘Shid. Me and ‘Shid came in the same draft class. Just how he’s impacting the game, he stretches the field and he can run routes. I’m super excited for his future.” With rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson placed on IR to open the season, Brown could find himself starting on Sundays in September. Elsewhere, Brown’s former Kentucky teammate from the high school class of 2022, Dane Key , received some bad news on Sunday. Signing with the Denver Broncos as an undrafted free agent in the spring, teaming up with his brother, Devon, Key was waived by the franchise ahead of the cutdown deadline. Denver waived defensive tackle Israel Antwine, cornerback Brent Austin, wide receiver Michael Bandy, long snapper Luke Basso, cornerback Sean Fresch, defensive back Ricardo Hallman, tackle Reid Holskey, tight end Justin Joly, wide receiver Kolbe Katsis, wide receiver Dane Key,… — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 30, 2026 Just last month, all three of Key (Broncos), Will Levis (Titans) and Josh Kattus (Bengals) were slinging the pigskin around back in Lexington at the Kentucky practice fields. No one in that group survived 53-man roster cuts, unfortunately. Will Levis was dropping bombs to Dane Key and Josh Kattus at Kentucky, just like the good ol’ days. pic.twitter.com/7kRD88UxkI — KSR (@KSRonX) July 11, 2026 There is still hope for Key to make a practice squad — potentially back in Denver, where his brother did make the 53-man roster — after a solid preseason with the Broncos. Still, though, it’s always tough to come up just short, right at the deadline. Sam Ehlinger with a laser to Dane Key MINvsDEN on @NFLNetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/gLJNoKLzRx — NFL (@NFL) August 29, 2026 Brown caught 122 passes at Kentucky for 1,528 yards and 11 touchdowns to go with 228 rushing yards and two scores on the ground and five touchdowns on kick returns across three seasons in Lexington. He’d finish his career with 532 receiving yards and a touchdown, plus another 33 rushing yards and a kick return score at LSU. As for Key, he went for 1,870 yards and 14 touchdowns across three seasons as a Wildcat before ending his career with another 452 yards and five scores at Nebraska. We all wish the situation had been better at the end of their Kentucky careers, but it marked the start of the end of Stoops’ time in Lexington, with all parties involved playing a part in that ugly finish. That being said, no one can ignore how good things were at times with both Brown and Key, and we wish them the best in the pros.

articles._body: Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown continues to show major love for the Boston community despite his departure from the Celtics this offseason. Brown represented the Celtics for 10 seasons, serving as the longest-tenured member as he helped the team win the title in 2024. However, his stint came to an end when Boston sent him to the Philadelphia 76ers in exchange for Paul George and draft compensation. Brown did a lot for the Boston community, providing contributions to families in need while teaching aspiring players who look up to him as a role model. During a recent event he hosted, Brown was very thankful for everything Boston fans gave him throughout his time with the franchise. “I just want to say thank you to Boston. Thank you to the city. I love you,” Brown said, per reporter Justin Turpin. Jaylen Brown: “I just want to say thank you to Boston. Thank you to the city. I love you.” pic.twitter.com/WT8cmt655d — Justin Turpin (@JustinmTurpin) August 30, 2026 What lies ahead for Jaylen Brown, 76ers next season Jaylen Brown walks away as one of the greatest Celtics players in history. His resume would be deserving of his number going up in the rafters after he retires. Until then, his time with the 76ers looks to be exciting as he competes for another championship with Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and LeBron James. Brown’s final campaign in Boston was remarkable, seeing him land on the All-NBA second team. He averaged 28.7 points, 6.9 rebounds and 5.1 assists per game throughout 71 appearances. In the playoffs, he produced 25.7 points, 5.7 rebounds and 3.3 assists per contest. Philadelphia finished with a 45-37 record last season, securing the seventh seed in the Eastern Conference standings. They stunned the Boston Celtics in a 3-1 series comeback before losing in a four-game sweep to the New York Knicks in the East Semifinals. The 76ers are gearing up for a big season with championship aspirations. With a starting five that can strike fear into opponents when healthy, Philadelphia fans can prepare for the opportunity to compete for their first NBA championship since 1983. articles._body: A static site generator for small web based store front for a brick and mortar store. It uses a local data store: FOSS This software is intended to fill the gap between a "full" frontend/backend solution and a simple static front end site in that it employs local data stores to create a static website that can be easily updated by the store owner. Features: - A python script run by the user that accesses a local CSV data store and builds a static html page. This greatly reduces complexity while still giving the user the ability to modify the data. - It is run by executing a python script from the command line. - After the initial html file is built, the user will use the hosting provider's website to upload the html file to the hosting server. - The script is simple enough that an beginning/intermediate python/html dev can update the script, data store and resulting index.html file without additional research or support. Using this software should be within ability range of a superuser. - This software and its output is written as simply as possible to allow for customization as needed. + It uses no additional frameworks, just native html/CSS. + It uses no libraries not included in standard python. + No JavaScript is used. The output is simple html/CSS. All the CSS is embedded in the html file to make it easier to manage the files. Only the resulting index.html file needs to be uploaded to the hosting server. + It uses common spreadsheet software to manage the data for both the Store Information and the products to be listed. - This software is Free and Open Source Software(FOSS) and can be edited by the user or their agent. Suitability: This software is suitable to the small store owner that is looking to move into online sales/marketing, but doesn't want to commit to a large development project or ongoing costs. It can be advertised using a QR code linking to the hosting provider. This eliminates the need for a domain name. Possible Uses: - Small brick and mortar stores - SwapMeet vendors - Yard sales Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49504284 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

Scottie Scheffler won his second FedEx Cup in three years on Sunday, beating Viktor Hovland [
articles._body: If there was ever any doubt that Scottie Scheffler was the No. 1 player in the world, it has been removed after he won the Tour Championship and the FedEx Cup for the second time in the last three years. Scottie Scheffler won his second FedEx Cup in three years on Sunday, beating Viktor Hovland by 3 shots at the TOUR Championship Perhaps even more notable, Scheffler passed Tiger Woods for most career PGA Tour winnings pic.twitter.com/I66Ld8fQHS — ESPN Insights (@ESPNInsights) August 30, 2026 Scheffler played error-free golf at the East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta, beating runner-up Viktor Hovland by three strokes. Scheffler was remarkably consistent in the event following his opening rounds of 65 and 67 with back-to-back scores of 66 on moving day and in the final round. There were times during the season that Scheffler was not at his best, and after winning the opening event he played this season, he didn’t win another until the FedEx Cup playoffs started. He won two of the final three tournaments. Scheffler earned $10 million with the win in the Tour Championship, and that allowed him to pass Tiger Woods for the most money won in tour events. Scheffler has won $130.4 million throughout his career, and that is $9 million more than Woods has won on the golf course in official events. Woods offered his congratulations to Scheffler for his dynamic play throughout the season. “Three wins, five runner-ups and finishing the season No. 1. Those are some numbers to be proud of. Incredible consistency all season long. Congrats on a historic season, Scottie,” Woods posted on X . Scheffler explained that he has been able to maintain consistency by taking each round of golf he plays on the PGA Tour as a privilege. “Overall, I just continued to battle, day in and day out,” Scheffler said. “It’s something that I’m very proud of. It’s a gift to be out here on tour. Each and every day, I’m going to try to give it my best.”   The post Scottie Scheffler passes Tiger Woods’ PGA Tour record after FedEx Cup win appeared first on ClutchPoints .

They’ll be paying close attention to Charbonnet and hope he’ll be ready to go once those four weeks are up. But the most important thing is the running back being fully healthy. In his absence, Jadarian Price and George Holani should get plenty of run. Holani took on a greater role when Charbonnet went down while Price was Seattle’s first-round pick in 2026. The Seahawks are counting on both to lead their rushing attack. Once Charbonnet returns, he should reclaim a key place in the offense. He has 1,761 rushing yards and 21 touchdowns during his three years with the team. During the 2025 season, the running back turned 184 carries into 730 yards and 12 touchdowns. After seeing Kenneth Walker leave in free agency, the Seahawks’ ground game is going to look much different in 2026. For at least four weeks, their offense won’t include Charbonnet either. Once he is past his injury though, Seattle is hoping to unleash a different rushing dynamic on the NFL. articles.title: Rae Burrell highlights important learning curve amid career season
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES – After finding themselves down by 17 points late in the first half at home against the Washington Mystics, the Los Angeles Sparks rallied back in the second half to come away with an 88-82 win on Friday night. Helping lead the way as she done for most of this season, Rae Burrel
articles._body: LOS ANGELES – After finding themselves down by 17 points late in the first half at home against the Washington Mystics, the Los Angeles Sparks rallied back in the second half to come away with an 88-82 win on Friday night. Helping lead the way as she done for most of this season, Rae Burrell scored 12 of her 15 points in the fourth quarter to seal the win for the Sparks. The former first round pick missed only one shot (5-of-6) in the final period after going 1-of-6 through the first three quarters. After the Sparks’ win, Burrell acknowledged that her early performance could be chalked up to missing some shots she normally makes, but that her improvement in the fourth quarter was also due to her learning to adjust on the fly to how the defense is guarding her. “I think just making the right reads, and sometimes I know if I’m short that sometimes it’s just a tweak that I need to make,” Burrell told a small group of reporters postgame. “Sometimes it’s not going into a body instead of absorbing the contact, going away from the contact. So I think just recognizing that as well cause I think that was some of my misses, some of the problems with my misses as well. There’s definitely tweaks in the game that I’m thinking about with those misses that I’m trying to correct.” This season has been a career year for Rae Burrell , who has spent the entirety of her five seasons in the WNBA with the Sparks. The organization selected her with the No. 9 overall pick in the 2022 draft, and she’s arguably become the team’s most promising young player. She’s appeared in 38 games this season, moving into a full-time starting role following Kelsey Plum’s injury and subsequent trade. She’s putting up a career-best 14.4 points, 2.3 rebounds and 2.6 assists while shooting 46.6 percent from the field, 39 percent from the 3-point line and 79.1 percent from the free-throw line. She reached her career-high in points with 28 back on Aug. 13 against the New York Liberty, a game in which the Sparks rallied back from a 28-point deficit, only to fall short in the end, but with Burrell putting on a similar second half performance. For her, one of the biggest areas of growth she’s seen is being able to bounce back from a sluggish start here or there and rebound in big way rather than let it linger in her head. “I think just my resilience. Just making the right plays as well even when my shots aren’t falling,” Burrell said. “I’m just happy I was taking the right shots and still making plays in any way that I can. And I’m still on the defensive end being aggressive as well. So I’m just proud of the decision-making that I’ve continued to show and my experience.” The Sparks have four games left in the year , and then Burrell will hit restricted free agency in the offseason. It’s a good bet she’ll probably draw interest from opposing teams, but the organization should do everything in their power to keep her in a Sparks jersey. articles.title: Phillies sweep of Angels results in feat last done in 1991
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Phillies closed their three-game series against the Los Angeles Angels with a 5-2 win Sunday, completing a sweep and reaching a franchise milestone. Philadelphia recorded its fourth sweep of a series lasting at least three games this month, the first time the team has accomplishe
articles._body: The Philadelphia Phillies closed their three-game series against the Los Angeles Angels with a 5-2 win Sunday, completing a sweep and reaching a franchise milestone. Philadelphia recorded its fourth sweep of a series lasting at least three games this month, the first time the team has accomplished that in a single month since August 1991 . The sweep continued a torrid August for the Phillies, who improved to 20-7 this month with one game remaining. Philadelphia has now won 13 of its last 15 games and sits a season-high 17 games above .500. Zack Wheeler played a huge role in the victory while ending a difficult stretch. The right-hander entered the game after going 0-3 with an 8.38 ERA across his previous four starts and carrying a 7.18 ERA in the second half. He initially ran into trouble again, loading the bases with no outs in the first inning, but a run-scoring double play and a strikeout limited the Angels to one run. Wheeler settled down afterward and finished six innings with four hits, one run, three walks and six strikeouts. He threw 108 pitches, with his four-seam fastball accounting for half of them while averaging 95.4 mph and reaching 96.3 mph. His sixth-inning strikeout of Jose Siri on a full-count curveball ended another threat and preserved the tie. The Phillies offense then broke the game open late. JT Realmuto tied the score with a solo homer in the third before Edmundo Sosa launched a go-ahead solo shot in the seventh. Sosa also hit a ninth-inning grand slam in Friday’s 5-3 comeback win and has seven home runs this season. He entered Sunday batting .423 with 15 RBIs in 26 August at-bats. Philadelphia added two runs in the eighth through Luis Arraez’s pinch-hit sacrifice fly and Brandon Marsh’s pinch-hit RBI single. Bryce Harper followed with an RBI double in the ninth and extended his career-best on-base streak to 32 games. Alex McFarlane worked a scoreless seventh, while Orion Kerkering logged the final four outs for his second save despite allowing Mike Trout’s ninth-inning RBI double. The Phillies now head to Arizona for a three-game series with the Diamondbacks, who currently occupy the third NL wild-card spot, 4.5 games behind Philadelphia. articles.summary: It’s been a roller coaster of a career for Isaiah Simmons, as the linebacker-safety hybrid just hasn’t quite found a home in the NFL. After playing five games for the Carolina Panthers last season and fighting for a spot on the roster this year, his time with the club came to an end o
articles._body: It’s been a roller coaster of a career for Isaiah Simmons , as the linebacker-safety hybrid just hasn’t quite found a home in the NFL. After playing five games for the Carolina Panthers last season and fighting for a spot on the roster this year, his time with the club came to an end on Sunday. Reports indicate that the 28-year-old defender was released by Carolina , according to Ari Meirov of The 33rd Team. Simmons is currently entering the 2026-27 campaign as a free agent unless another team ends up signing him before the start of the season. “ The Panthers are releasing LB/S Isaiah Simmons,” Meirov reported. “The former No. 8 overall pick, known for his versatility, appeared in 5 games for Carolina last season and re-signed on a 1-year deal this offseason.” Simmons was a first-round pick by the Arizona Cardinals in the 2020 NFL Draft. He was viewed as an intriguing prospect as he is a highly versatile player who can play both linebacker and safety. But his time in Arizona only lasted three seasons after the franchise traded him to the New York Giants, where he played for two years. The ex-Clemson Tigers star played nearly every single contest in his first five years in the league, missing just one game in his rookie year with the Cardinals. That all changed when he signed with the Panthers last season, as Isaiah Simmons was limited to just five games. He was initially a cut candidate last training camp but signed with the Panthers as a late-season acquisition. Simmons hits free agency with 331 combined tackles (227 solo), 8.5 sacks, five interceptions, nine forced fumbles, and three fumble recoveries accumulated throughout his career. articles.title: Ryan Hampton dropped 40 points in his senior HS debut back in Texas
articles.summary: The future Kentucky Wildcat went for 40 points in his first game back at Rockwall-Heath
articles._body: Ryan Hampton chose not to reclassify and get a head start on training for his freshman season at Kentucky . Instead, the top-25 recruit decided to return home for his senior year of high school, back to Rockwall-Heath in Texas. It’s where he became a household name before taking his talents to Dynamic Prep (2024) and DME Academy (2025) for his sophomore and junior seasons, respectively. Now, he’s closing this chapter of his life where it all started — and things couldn’t have gone better for him in his part-two 2026 debut, dropping 40 points in a preseason showcase. Taking on Eastern Hills in The War HS Extravaganza , located in Duncanville, TX, on Saturday, Hampton threw down explosive dunk after explosive dunk and converted tough shot after tough shot. He looked closer to the five-star, top-10 talent that put him on Mark Pope’s radar at Kentucky to begin with. Take a look at the future Wildcat getting after it back home to begin his last ride: View this post on Instagram Hampton seriously considered a jump to 2026 and an early start at Kentucky, along with other prep school options after settling on 2027, but eventually opted for a return to Rockwall-Heath back on August 9. “I came back here just to be a kid again, being at a public school with my friends and playing basketball, the sport that I love. Coming back here and setting the standard. Obviously, I came to Rockwall-Heath my freshman year, had a great experience,” Hampton announced at the time. “After that, I left, played prep school against the Montverdes and Prolific Preps. Now, being back here, I’m ready to be my ultimate self again. … I love Texas, I love being at home, so a whole year being at home before college is gonna be great.” He previously committed to Kentucky on June 7, choosing the Wildcats over the likes of LSU, SMU, Texas, Texas A&M, Baylor, Tennessee, Louisville and Kansas, among others. Over a month later at the Nike EYBL Peach Jam in North Augusta, where he helped lead Nightrydas to the event semifinals, Hampton told KSR he had only grown more confident in his pick. The 6-foot-6 shooting guard is in a solid spot with his development, but the UK staff in Lexington will help him take the next steps toward his ultimate goals as a championship-caliber player in college before turning pro. “It’s been great. I love that I made that decision,” Hampton told KSR. “Kentucky, I think it’s a great place for me to grow and really just build up my game and when I get to college. Coach Pope, Coach Mo Williams, Coach Mikhail (McLean), all of them, they’re preparing me on how to be a man on and off the court. I’m very glad I made that decision. … “I’m very happy because I know I made the right decision. I know they’re like a family and me and my family are definitely comfortable with that decision. I’m very grateful for it. … I mean, it’s like no other.” Until then, he’ll continue dropping 40-burgers as a high school senior at Rockwall-Heath. Let the countdown begin.

articles._body: The Cleveland Browns are preparing to enter a new era under head coach Todd Monken . Cornerback Michael Coats will now be a part of it. Coats joined the Browns as an undrafted free agent over the offseason. Now, he has officially made the 53-man roster , via Adam Schefter of ESPN. The cornerback didn’t play high school football, first picking up the sport at East Central Community College. He would ultimately transfer to Nevada before ending his college career at West Virginia. And now, despite being a late football bloomer, and an UDFA, Coats has defied the odds by earning a roster spot. Over his three years at the college level, Coats put up 84 tackles, 24 passes defended and five interceptions. He set new career-highs in 2024, recording 41 tackles, 13 pass break ups and four picks. Coats was awarded First-team All-Mountain West for his efforts. Now on the Browns, Coats will be joining a cornerback room led by Denzel Ward. As a whole, Cleveland finished the 2025 season ranked fourth in total defense, allowing 283.6 yards per game. Their pass defense ranked third, allowing 167.2 YPG. After trading away Myles Garrett , things are sure to look mighty different for the Browns in 2026. Still, Monken and company will do everything in their power to get everything they can out of their current unit. In his current state, Coats won’t suddenly turn Cleveland into world beaters. But it’s clear he is a player the Browns believe in. If he continues developing as is, his story from starting to play in college to the NFL will only get wilder. articles._body: Allisha Gray filled up the stat sheet en route to making incredible franchise history in the Atlanta Dream’s 89-81 win over the Minnesota Lynx on Sunday night. Gray is going through the 10th season of her WNBA career, her fourth with the Dream. She shines as one of the best players in the league, landing on the All-WNBA First Team last year. articles._body: The Los Angeles Chargers announced earlier on Sunday that veteran safety Tony Jefferson was released from the roster. However, hours later, the organization chose not to cut Jefferson, as he is not part of the 53-man roster. Reports indicate that after trading away two defenders, the franchise decided to keep the 34-year-old on the team as a roster spot became available, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. Jefferson will begin the 2026-27 season with the Chargers after all. “Update: after trading away a defensive lineman and a cornerback in two separate trades today and having two additional roster spots, the Chargers pivoted and kept veteran safety Tony Jefferson on their 53-man roster,” Schefter reported. Jefferson is entering his 12th year in the NFL, and his third with the Chargers . He played 13 games for the club last season (eight starts) and put up great numbers. The former undrafted free agent ended last year with 57 combined tackles (37 solo), seven pass deflections (career-high), and four interceptions (career-high). Considering he was initially a cut candidate, expectations should be for Jefferson to play a backup role in L.A. RJ Mickens and Elijah Molden are in line to start in the two safety positions for the Chargers. Fourth-round rookie Genesis Smith should also make appearances in the secondary as a backup. With the final roster set, Los Angeles will begin the new season with a Week 1 home opener against the Arizona Cardinals. The Chargers will enjoy two consecutive home games to begin the campaign, as they won’t play on the road until Week 3 against the Buffalo Bills. articles.title: Countdown to kickoff prediction series: South Carolina will utilize new rule to increase scoring opportunities
articles.summary: Continuing the countdown to kickoff prediction series: South Carolina will utilize new rule to steal late-half points
articles._body: In May, when the calendar revealed that it was 100 days until South Carolina kicked off the season, I posted a story on GamecockCentral entitled “100 predictions for the 2026 Gamecocks.” Now, that countdown is down to just six days. The prediction paired with day six read, “Head coach Shane Beamer and special teams coordinator Matthew Smiley will attempt to utilize the new post-fair catch free kick field goal rule this season.” Let’s break down that prognostication. Have a question for the GamecockCentral staff? Ask it now on The Insiders Forum. A new rule for a new coordinator College football has seen more than a few rule changes this offseason. Not only have eligibility standards changed dramatically (plus all of the court cases in the aftermath) and transfer portal windows shifted, but some on-field rules were adjusted. Targeting no longer carries an ejection/suspension penalty for first-time offenders, and appeals are now more allowable. Offensive pass interference will now be worth 10 yards (down from 15), just like the NFL. The most interesting change for special teams provides teams with another opportunity to earn points. If a player fair catches a kick, the receiving team may elect to try a free kick field goal. This unrushed, untimed attempt would come with a holder or via drop kick. Like any field goal, it would be worth three points. Intriguingly, teams can free kick if the game clock expired during the play in which there was the fair catch. The new rule will not be utilized much, as it primarily makes sense only for end-of-half situations. It also typically requires a kick to be caught on the positive side of the 50-yard line, limiting realistic opportunities. However, if South Carolina feels like they have a kicker with the range, fans can rest assured that head coach Shane Beamer and new special teams coordinator Matthew Smiley will have this rule in the back of their minds in 2026. Instead of allowing a team backed up in their own territory to run out the clock at the end of the first half, perhaps the Gamecocks will use their timeouts to force a punt. In the past, Carolina has tried to block late punt attempts, and that still could happen here. However, if the opponent gets the kick off cleanly, a fair catch in plus territory could yield a three-point opportunity. What does this mean for the Gamecocks? Fellow subscribers are discussing it now on The Insiders Forum. Beamer Ball at South Carolina Finding advantages on special teams is one of the key tenets of “Beamer Ball.” Obviously popularized first by his father Frank Beamer at Virginia Tech, Shane Beamer has emphasized many of the same principles at South Carolina. Because of that, Beamer and his special teams coordinators have worked in lockstep to make sure that the Gamecocks win the special teams battle each week. At times, the game’s third phase has completely flipped the game in favor of South Carolina. Pete Lembo (2021-2023) was excellent in Columbia, and Joe DeCamillis (2024 and 2025) had good moments, as well. The special teams emphasis is not just limited to blocked kicks, fakes, and the return game. Beamer has also spoken at length about the importance of special teams coverage units and the need for blocking, both in protecting the kicking and punting units and for earning extra yardage on return opportunities. If South Carolina elects to keep the fair catch free kick in their back pocket this fall, it will become something the Gamecocks take seriously. New special teams coordinator Matthew Smiley comes from the NFL, where the rule has already been in place. In 2024, the Los Angeles Chargers made one in a win over the Denver Broncos. It will be worth watching to see if South Carolina takes advantage of this new rule. What’s your prediction? Share it with fellow subscribers on The Insiders Forum.

articles._body: As the Dallas Cowboys made the surprising move to cut running back Jaydon Blue ahead of the team finalizing the 53-man roster, long-time fan and sports analyst Skip Bayless would give his thoughts on the release. While Bayless has weighed in on many Cowboys’ moves in the past, he would explain why he isn’t shocked by the decision to cut Blue. As a 5th-rounder, he just never showed quite enough. But I do hope he falls through waivers and winds up on the Dallas practice squad. He did run 4.38 coming out of Texas,” Bayless wrote on X, formerly Twitter. As many thought Blue would be the running back behind Javonte Williams in the depth chart, it looks like Malik Davis “won the job,” as Todd Archer said. It may not be too shocking to see if Blue ends up on the Cowboys’ practice squad, especially with how much head coach Brian Schottenheimer has praised the 22-year-old for his maturity. “I think he came back with a different mentality, which is great. He’s always been extremely bright and picked up the scheme very, very well,” Schottenheimer said, via Sports Illustrated. Looking at his rookie year, he recorded 129 yards on 38 carries with a touchdown, as it remains to be seen where Blue goes next and whether it will be back with Dallas on the practice squad. articles._body: The Los Angeles Chargers have traded defensive tackle TeRah Edwards to the Carolina Panthers for a 2028 sixth-round draft pick, according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. The move came just ahead of Sunday’s 6 p.m. ET deadline for NFL teams to finalize their 53-man rosters. Edwards entered the league as an undrafted free agent from the Illinois Fighting Illini in 2025 after spending five years in college between Northwestern and Illinois. From 2020 through 2024, he recorded 67 combined tackles, including 7.0 tackles for loss, along with 4.0 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery. The 6-foot-2, 305-pound defensive lineman did not play in a regular-season game during his rookie year and instead spent the 2025 season developing on Los Angeles’ practice squad. He did, however, see preseason action, appearing in three games and finishing with 10 combined tackles, 11 pressures and seven stops. Edwards continued to make an impact during the 2026 preseason. In the Chargers’ preseason finale against the Los Angeles Rams, he made four tackles and generated two pressures while repeatedly showing an ability to disrupt opposing backfields. Despite that production, Edwards was competing for a roster spot in a crowded defensive interior. Los Angeles already had Teair Tart, Dalvin Tomlinson, Jamaree Caldwell, Justin Eboigbe and Nick Barrett in the defensive tackle group, with the organization having committed heavy draft capital and salary-cap resources to the position. The Chargers therefore opted to turn Edwards’ preseason performance into draft compensation rather than risk losing him through the waiver process. articles.title: Last-minute move Bears must make after Rams’ Aaron Donald signing
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams have been recognized as one of the strongest teams in the NFL as they prepare for the start of the 2026 season. They added superstar pass rusher Myles Garrett in a trade with the Cleveland Browns in the offseason, and they have been flirting with a return to play by explosive
articles._body: The Los Angeles Rams have been recognized as one of the strongest teams in the NFL as they prepare for the start of the 2026 season. They added superstar pass rusher Myles Garrett in a trade with the Cleveland Browns in the offseason, and they have been flirting with a return to play by explosive edge rusher Aaron Donald throughout training camp. That situation became reality when Donald sent a written communication to commissioner Roger Goodell that he was back. That simple announcement has resonated with every NFL team that hopes to have a chance at playing for the NFL championship this year — including the Chicago Bears. The Bears are the defending NFC North champions and they won a Wild Card playoff game against the Green Bay Packers before their season came to an end in a divisional playoff loss in overtime to the Rams. The Bears do not face the Rams in the regular season, but general manager Ryan Poles and head coach Ben Johnson have to keep their eyes on all teams that the Bears look at as potential road blocks this season. The Rams have to be at the top of the list. The combination of Garrett and Donald on an already formidable defense means that this team has a chance to rank with the greatest teams that the NFL has seen in the last two decades. They have game-changing players on offense including quarterback Matthew Stafford and wide receiver Puka Nacua, and one of the sharpest head coaches in the NFL in Sean McVay. The Rams are motivated after losing to the eventual Super Bowl champion and NFC West rival Seattle Seahawks in the NFC Championship Game last year. Bears must stay focused on the immediate task at hand Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images While the Rams appear to have a defense that may be the best in the league and one that has significant advantages over the Bears, Johnson and Chicago defensive coordinator Dennis Allen can’t panic. They are not going to find pass rushers like Garrett and Donald as street free agents, nor can they complete an immediate trade for an explosive pass rusher. Instead, they have to concentrate on getting the most out of their own pass rushers. That means they have to look at defensive end Montez Sweat for an elite season when it comes to putting pressure on opposing quarterbacks. Sweat led the Bears with 10.0 sacks last year, and he has had as many as 12.5 sacks in his career. Sweat has an excellent first step and he also has a relentless quality that allows him to pursue quarterbacks and come up with the sack even when he doesn’t get it right away. Sweat cannot be a one-man gang and he needs plenty of help from fellow defensive end Austin Booker, who had 35 tackles, 4.5 sacks , 3 passes defensed and 1 forced fumble a year ago. Booker improved as the season progressed, and he has a chance to upgrade his sack numbers significantly this season. Bears must focus on their own strengths as they compete for division title The main thing the Bears have to do is keep their minds on the business of playing consistently during the regular season and taking care of their opponents in the NFC North. They must win the division title — or at least gain a playoff spot as a Wild-Card team — before they have to compete directly with the Rams. This means that Johnson has to emphasize the Bears’ strengths with Caleb Williams at quarterback, Rome Odunze and Luther Burden at wide receiver, Colston Loveland at tight end and D’Andre Swift at running back in order to get the best of their NFC North rivals. This will be the focus throughout the 18 weeks of the regular season that begins with their season opener on the road against the Carolina Panthers. However, Johnson and his coaching staff have to keep an eye on the Rams and the defending champion Seahawks as the season progresses. If they are going to stand up to either of those teams, the Bears’ offensive line will have to attack the defensive fronts with ferocity. While that will be particularly difficult against Donald and Garrett, it is about controlling the clock and establishing a multi-faceted attack. Williams was the highlight-film player for the Bears last year and became one of the game’s most spectacular quarterbacks, but they will not want to get into a shootout with the Rams. If Williams is dropping back to pass on nearly every play, that’s a green light for Donald and Garrett. That would almost certainly turn into a punishing experience for Williams and that is not the way to beat an elite defense. Johnson can come up with the winning plan during the season and unleash it at the proper time in the postseason. articles._body: Scottie Scheffler trailed by multiple strokes heading into the final day of the Tour Championship on Sunday. If there’s one thing anyone who follows golf knows, however, it is to never count the world’s No. 1 player out . Sure enough, Scheffler enjoyed a big round and ultimately won the Tour Championship after shooting a -16 overall for the tournament. The 30-year-old shared his thoughts on the comeback victory following his win on Sunday, via Golf on CBS. “I think that’s something I’m very proud of,” Scheffler said. “I think when you look over the course of the season, especially some of the tough starts… I’m very proud of fighting back and having some good finishes, and even giving myself some chances to win with some of those poor starts. Overall, just continued to battle… It’s a gift to be out here on tour, so each and every day I’m going to give it my best.” Scheffler had a number of tournaments this year where he started slow but ended up either back in contention on Sunday or even winning the overall tournament. He was one of the best weekend players throughout the season. It is something that certainly played a crucial role in his overall success. Scheffler simply never gives up. While Scottie Scheffler would obviously love to be more consistent throughout all four days next season, it is difficult to complain about the success he found this year. articles._body: New Orleans Saints first-round pick Jordyn Tyson suffered a right hamstring injury during training camp this offseason. He hasn’t been available to practice for several weeks, and with the new season around the corner, the club made a move that was widely expected across the league. Reports indicate that the 22-year-old wide receiver was officially placed on the IR , according to Mike Garafolo of the NFL Network. Tyson will be out for at least the first four weeks of the regular season. “The Saints have placed rookie WR Jordyn Tyson on IR,” Garafolo reported. “He’s out at least the first four weeks of the season with a hamstring injury.” A return by the Week 5 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings would be ideal, but not guaranteed. It is deemed a different hamstring issue from his injuries at Arizona State. However, Jordyn Tyson is expected to be out for two months with this current hamstring injury. With Tyson out, the Saints will rely on a wide receiver group consisting of Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele. Rookies Barion Brown and Bryce Lance will have an opportunity to prove themselves right away, while Kevin Austin Jr. rears up at the end of the depth chart. Jordyn Tyson played four years of college football, one with the Colorado Buffaloes and three with the Arizona State Sun Devils. He didn’t emerge as a starter until the 2024-25 campaign, when he broke out with 75 receptions, 1,101 yards, and 10 touchdowns. Injuries derailed his following season, but he was on pace for another spectacular year. articles.title: Warner Bros. axed ‘Coyote vs. Acme’ three years ago to take a tax write off. But it’s finally in theaters after a public outcry—and a box office hit
articles.summary: The Looney Tunes feature film that was given a new lease on life by Ketchup Entertainment and debuted with an estimated $15.5 million in ticket sales over the weekend.
articles._body: Three years after Warner Bros. abruptly canned  “Coyote vs. Acme,”  the Looney Tunes feature film that was  given a new lease on life  by Ketchup Entertainment debuted with an estimated $15.5 million in ticket sales over the weekend. For the fifth weekend in a row,  “Spider-Man: Brand New Day”  topped the North American box office. It grossed $22.2 million in U.S. and Canadian theaters, according to studio estimates Sunday, bringing its worldwide total to $2.33 billion and making it the fourth highest-grossing film of all time. “Coyote vs. Acme,” which had been relegated to the dust heap, fared best of the newcomers, debuting in second place. The Ridley Scott action drama  “The Dog Stars,”  starring Jacob Elordi, flopped. The film, about a pilot and German Shepherd who survive a global pandemic, opened in fifth place with $8 million for 20th Century Studios. It added $11.3 million overseas, a poor result for a film that cost between $70 million and $100 million to make. “Coyote vs. Acme,” however, scored a decent, hard-earned opening. In 2023, Warner Bros. canceled any release of the completed film, preferring to take a tax write off on a movie originally produced for its streaming service, HBO Max. Warner also shelved “Batgirl” and “Scoob! Holiday Haunt,” both of which remain unreleased. “Coyote vs. Acme,” based on an Ian Frazier “Shouts and Murmurs” New Yorker column, is about Wile E. Coyote suing the Acme Corporation for its faulty products. It stars Will Forte, John Cena, Lana Condor and Eric Bauza. The film, a hybrid of live-action and animation directed by Dave Green, cost $70 million to make. But despite good test screening scores, Warner Bros. opted to ax the completed film. After an outcry, the studio put the film up for sale. Early last year, Ketchup Entertainment  acquired worldwide distribution rights  for about $50 million. For the makers of the film, just getting released was a victory. “‘Coyote vs. Acme’ is finally, gloriously, in theaters now,” Green said on social media Friday. “Which means one thing. WE WON.” Reviews and audience scores were also good. Moviegoers gave it an “A” CinemaScore. Critics were just as enthusiastic. On Rotten Tomatoes, it rated 95% fresh. While the result might have counted as a disappointment for some $70 million movies, the opening weekend for “Coyote vs. Acme” was the best ever for Ketchup. The indie distributor’s previous high was 2024’s “The Day the Earth Blew Up” (a $3.1 million opening), another Warner-made Looney Tunes castoff. “The box office numbers are fair, but the reception is excellent and the release should set up good ancillary business for kids’ viewing, where the film should recoup its investment,” said David A. Gross, who publishes the box office newsletter FranchiseRe. “The Odyssey,”  in its seventh weekend, slid to third place with $14.3 million. It remains unusually strong overseas, where the Christopher Nolan movie grossed $48.6 million over the weekend. Altogether, the Universal Pictures release has collected $1.55 billion in global sales. Top 10 movies by domestic box office With final domestic figures being released Monday, this list factors in the estimated ticket sales for Friday through Sunday at U.S. and Canadian theaters, according to Rentrak: 1. “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” $22.2 million. 2. “Coyote vs. Acme,” $15.5 million. 3. “The Odyssey,” $14.3 million. 4. “Insidious: Out of the Further,” $10.1 million. 5. “The Dog Stars,” $8 million. 6. “Buddy,” $5.4 million. 7. “The End of Oak Street,” $5 million. 8. “PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie,” $4.9 million. 9. “Mutiny,” $2.8 million. 10. “Tony,” $2.2 million. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Cardinals’ James Conner to miss at least 4 games after latest injury move

The Cardinals placed James Conner on injured reserved/designated to return, via Tom Pelissero of the R
articles._body: Head coach Mike LaFleur is finalizing his first roster with the Arizona Cardinals . When it comes to the running back position, he knows one option who won’t be available to start the year. The Cardinals placed James Conner on injured reserved/designated to return , via Tom Pelissero of the Ringer. He will now miss at least the first four games of the season. Conner is still working his way back from a serious ankle injury. The Cardinals will closely monitor him as he continues his rehab process. But they clearly felt he wouldn’t be on the field any time soon. When he does return, Arizona is hoping Conner can be a vital resource in the run game. Arizona will now turn to rookie Jeremiyah Love and veteran Tyler Allgeier. Love is dealing with a high ankle sprain of his own, so Allgeier may get a lot of the early season work. But sooner rather than later, Love will become the leader of the Cardinals’ run game. Because of that, it’s fair to wonder how much longer Conner’s tenure will last in Arizona. He re-worked his contract to stay with the franchise , but is set to be a free agent after the season. With Love and Allgeier in place, the running back may be expendable. For now though, the Cardinals are just trying to put up a fight. They’ll have to do so without one extra element of their ground game. All Arizona can look for now is the running back to be ready to roll once those four games are up. If not, Allgeier and Love will only garner more opportunities. articles.summary: Cleveland Guardians star Jose Ramirez underwent surgery for a hamate fracture earlier this season. While Ramirez was able to return in July after missing over one month of action, his numbers have been down overall this season. One has to wonder if the injury issue is still bothering Ramirez. The
articles._body: Cleveland Guardians star Jose Ramirez underwent surgery for a hamate fracture earlier this season . While Ramirez was able to return in July after missing over one month of action, his numbers have been down overall this season. One has to wonder if the injury issue is still bothering Ramirez. The seven-time All-Star often avoids making excuses, but he did make an honest admission about the injury while speaking to reporters after Sunday’s 11-1 win against the Kansas City Royals, per Mason Horodyski. “It’s a blend of dealing with pain, but also recovering the strength. Many times you feel that weakness when you’re hitting, it’s been only two months,” Ramirez said via interpreter. “People forget that that’s a very serious injury. It takes some time to recover, but we want to be in a good spot, trying to find the ways how to get better every day.” Ramirez contributed on Sunday with two hits, one home run and four RBI. He is now hitting .243/.339/.393 across 103 games played. The third baseman has 11 home runs, 24 doubles and 31 stolen bases. Ramirez’s numbers may be below his expectations, but he can still help Cleveland in a crucial manner as the team pushes toward the postseason. The Guardians are currently 3.5 games behind the Chicago White Sox for first place in the American League Central, but they do hold the final AL Wild Card spot at the moment. Jose Ramirez and the Guardians will have an off day on Monday before beginning a three-game series with the Toronto Blue Jays at Progressive Field in Cleveland on Tuesday night.
