Iran’s president admits ‘we have many problems’ and missiles ‘are of no use’ as the U.S. chokes its economy while weakening Tehran’s grip on Hormuz
articles.summary: "People are on the edge now; if I put more pressure on them, they might fall off the edge. We have to be careful that no one falls off."
articles._body: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian acknowledged his country’s economic woes amid pressure from the U.S., which is strangling its trade while protecting other countries’ ships carrying oil through the Strait of Hormuz. Recent weeks have seen Tehran lose leverage over the critical energy chokepoint as traffic picks up, especially via a southern route along Oman’s coast. At the same time, warnings about Iran’s economy from Pezeshkian and the regime’s other relative moderates have been mounting. In an interview with state media on Friday, he signaled defiance in the face of all the economic pressure and credited Iran’s resilience to its unity. “We have many problems,” Pezeshkian said, according to a Google translation. “There’s inflation, economic issues, employment and many other problems, but the people are with us.” Indeed, inflation has soared above 80%, with prices for certain food staples up 100%. The International Monetary Fund said in April Iran’s economy will shrink 6.1% this year, the worst contraction in decades. And a labor ministry official estimated that more than 1 million jobs had been lost by late May. In an apparent dig at Iranian hardliners who reject negotiations with the U.S. and favor continued war, Pezeshkian added that “we may have many things; we may even have missiles and bombs, but they are of no use.” He later noted that imports are not coming into the country, including gasoline. The naval blockade has not only prevented Iran from exporting oil via its ports, it has also kept out imports of refined fuels that Iran needs despite being a major oil producer. That has created shortages and long lines at gas stations, made worse by deep subsidies that encourage excess consumption. In the interview, Pezeshkian described efforts to curb fuel demand and hike prices, but hinted they can’t go too far. “We shouldn’t make someone whose life revolves around gasoline suffer,” he explained. “We shouldn’t put more pressure on those who are already under pressure. People are on the edge now; if I put more pressure on them, they might fall off the edge. We have to be careful that no one falls off.” Pezeshkian estimated that Iranian trade has plunged 25%-35%, with imports down significantly more than exports. In fact, trade intelligence firm Kpler said Iran’s August crude export loadings have collapsed more than 80% compared to a year ago. Since the naval blockade was reimposed, U.S. force have redirected 82 commercial vessels, disabled three and boarded two to ensure compliance, Central Command said on Friday. “Some people say that sanctions have no effect at all,” Pezeshkian said. “I really don’t know what to tell these people. I just want to say this, saying that sanctions have no effect is not consistent with these facts.” While the U.S. military tightens its chokehold, it is simultaneously loosening Iran’s grip on the Strait of Hormuz . Last week, Central Command said U.S. forces completed clearing sea mines from the strait’s international shipping routes. Estimates vary on exactly how much oil is leaking through, but the upshot is the volumes are substantial albeit still well short of normal. According to Goldman Sachs , total exports of crude and oil products from the region have risen to 15 million-16 million barrels a day. And Kpler said oil flows from the Persian Gulf have recovered to around 70% of pre-war levels . U.S. officials told Axios that about 10 million barrels of oil a day are being transported out of the strait through the Omani corridor the U.S. military is defending. A two-week stretch of U.S. bombing last month degraded Iran’s radar and maritime surveillance systems, the report said, making it easier for tankers to sail through undetected at night with their transponders turned off. This has allowed vessels to make shuttle runs in and out , then unload oil to other tankers that deliver the cargo to customers. To be sure, Iran is still attacking ships, but that hasn’t been enough to stop traffic. Meanwhile, the U.S. military continues to weaken Iran’s ability to close the strait. On Sunday, U.S. forces struck Iranian rocket launchers that were preparing to deploy sea mines in the strait. Gregory Brew, an expert on Iran and oil at the Eurasia Group, said on X on Friday that Iran overplayed its hand in July, when it resumed attack on shipping in the strait’s southern route. “The result: the MOU is dead, the blockade is back in place, and the US is succeeding (to a partial, but notable extent) at reopening the strait without another deal,” he added. “Perhaps the status quo swings back in Iran’s favor, but right now this looks like a miscalculation to me.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

As rumors continue around the Steelers and Porter’s potential future contract, the latest move
articles._body: As the contract situation between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Joey Porter Jr. continues, there is a significant move was made as the cornerback was on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list. As rumors continue around the Steelers and Porter’s potential future contract, the latest move could signal that a Week 1 return could be in the cards. According to NFL insider Tom Pelissero, Pittsburgh has activated Porter, as he is being taken off the PUP list. “The Steelers activated CB Joey Porter Jr. from the PUP list,” Pelissero wrote on X, formerly Twitter. While it’s great news for fans to see that Porter is healthy enough to play, there are still other variables at play, which is that he has missed all of training camp and the preseason with the back injury, not to mention the contract situation at hand. Speaking of the contract talks between the Steelers and Porter, there doesn’t appear to be a lot of movement at the moment, as NFL insider Jeremy Fowler called it a “classic stalemate” on Friday’s SportsCenter. “I am told the player has not been happy with the way things have gone because they paid other players,” Fowler said. “They haven’t made him a formal offer that matches his skill set. It feels like he’s been a really good corner for them. It’s a situation where they want him to play out the contract essentially because they haven’t made him an offer. He hasn’t been practicing. He’s listed with a back injury, but really it’s about his contract as well.” Names to watch over the weekend and where things stand with Christian Gonzalez and Joey Porter Jr. @SportsCenter with @KevinNegandhi @itsthebaldgirl pic.twitter.com/vMQBfkog0q — Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) August 28, 2026 At any rate, it remains to be seen when the 26-year-old plays for the Steelers again and also when both sides could agree on a potential contract extension. articles.title: The best non-Sabres Connor Hellebuyck trade destination after Jets demand
articles.summary: The Winnipeg Jets have dealt with Connor Hellebuyck trade rumors throughout the offseason. Winnipeg hoped to resolve the situation privately when a trade to their liking presented itself. However, that hope was dashed recently by their franchise goaltender. Hellebuyck went public with his desire
articles._body: The Winnipeg Jets have dealt with Connor Hellebuyck trade rumors throughout the offseason. Winnipeg hoped to resolve the situation privately when a trade to their liking presented itself. However, that hope was dashed recently by their franchise goaltender. Hellebuyck went public with his desire to be traded out of Winnipeg. The Michigan native released a statement confirming that he had privately requested a trade, and that he would still like to see a move materialize soon . “I have tried to handle the situation quietly and respectfully while giving the organization time to explore its options,” Hellebuyck said in the statement released by his agent, Ray Petkau, via NHL.com. “With training camp approaching, I felt it was important to publicly confirm my request. My position has not changed. I believe moving on is the best path forward for me and my family.” This is the latest in a slew of star players requesting a trade from their current team. Former Ottawa Senators captain Brady Tkachuk wanted out of Ottawa this summer and was traded to the Florida Panthers. Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin also requested a trade . However, his request remains unfulfilled. In saying this, Hellebuyck is the first to go public with his request before a trade. Tkachuk spoke about his request after being moved to Florida. Meanwhile, Larkin had remained quiet on the situation surrounding him. Hellebuyck’s decision certainly puts pressure on the Jets to get something done. Currently, the Buffalo Sabres have been the favorite to land the star netminder , given the trade rumors from earlier in the summer. However, if Buffalo doesn’t land Hellebuyck, another Eastern Conference team could swing a deal for his services. Connor Hellebuyck could be missing piece for Devils Jerome Miron-Imagn Images The New Jersey Devils have sought to contend for the Stanley Cup for some time now. New Jersey has a very talented core that arguably should make it a playoff contender. Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt, and Nico Hischier lead a very impressive team. However, this team has lacked strong goaltending in recent seasons. Veteran Jake Allen has done well in a backup role. But Jacob Markstrom struggled as the primary option, especially this past season. Markstrom is no longer with the Devils. He was traded to the Panthers this summer, reuniting him with the team that initially drafted him. For now, Allen is set to be the starting netminder, with Nico Daws and David Rittich providing cover. As mentioned, Allen has provided strong play for New Jersey. But he is 36 years old and has not carried a starting workload since 2018. It would be a lot to ask him to be the starting netminder this season if the goal is to eventually contend for the Stanley Cup. Adding Hellebuyck gives the Devils an elite goaltender who can bring them to the postseason. His record in the playoffs is certainly spotty, and that does raise some concerns. At the same time, Hellebuyck is a monumental upgrade for the Devils in between the pipes. New Jersey has a new general manager in Sunny Mehta, who could be looking to leave his mark on this team. He comes from the Panthers organization, and Florida is not a stranger to major blockbusters. Mehta could replicate that if he can swoop in and acquire Hellebuyck from the Jets before the puck drops on the 2026-27 season. The Sparks roster moves began late Friday night whe
articles._body: The Los Angeles Sparks’ recent flurry of roster moves continued on Sunday as the team signed former WNBA draft pick Shyanne Sellers to a development contract, head coach Lynne Roberts confirmed prior to the team’s game against the Seattle Storm. The Sparks roster moves began late Friday night when the team signed rookie guard Ndjakalenga Mwenentanda to a development contract as they had one available. Then on Saturday, the Sparks claimed second-year wing Aaliyah Nye off waivers after she cut by the Atlanta Dream, and waiving fan favorite Kate Martin to make room on the roster. And to open up the other development contract in which they signed Shyanne Sellers, the Sparks waived Alissa Pili whom Roberts coached during college at the University of Utah. Sellers most recently played in the inaugural season of UpShot, making an appearance in the league’s championship game with the Jacksonville Waves. She was the No. 17 overall pick in the 2025 WNBA Draft by the Golden State Valkyries, but was one of the team’s cuts before the start of the season. The former Maryland star was claimed off waivers by the Dream, but did not make their final roster either. This season, Sellers was in training camp with the Dallas Wings prior to joining UpShot. Before the Sparks’ game against the Storm, Roberts addressed the team’s recent moves while acknowledging that the team expects the new players to join them during the FIBA break. “It’s hard when the human element of this business is challenging,” Roberts said during her pregame press conference. “But at the end of the day, there’s business decision made.” With Martin and Pili being cut, Roberts was confident that both players would eventually find their footing in the WNBA. “I called both of them after I knew that they had a discussion with the front office, and just expressed my love for them and appreciation,” Roberts continued. “I talked to both of them and just told them I loved them and appreciated them and this isn’t the end of their journey. They’ll be back in the league and I’m grateful for what they gave me and all that they gave their teammates.” Sellers, along with Nye and Mwenentanda, were not available against the Storm, and will join the team amid the World Cup break. articles.summary: The New England Patriots added another offensive lineman ahead of Sunday’s 6 p.m. ET roster deadline, acquiring Walter Rouse from the Minnesota Vikings. New England will send a 2027 sixth-round pick to Minnesota and receive Rouse along with a 2027 seventh-round selection. Rouse, 25, entered
articles._body: The New England Patriots added another offensive lineman ahead of Sunday’s 6 p.m. ET roster deadline, acquiring Walter Rouse from the Minnesota Vikings. New England will send a 2027 sixth-round pick to Minnesota and receive Rouse along with a 2027 seventh-round selection. Rouse, 25, entered the NFL as a sixth-round selection by the Vikings in 2024 after playing his final college season at Oklahoma. He began his collegiate career at Stanford, where he became the starting left tackle during his true freshman season and remained in that role throughout his four seasons. He then used a fifth year of eligibility and transferred to Oklahoma, where he started his final season at left tackle. Standing m at 6-foot-6 and weighing 330 pounds, Rouse started 52 college games at left tackle. During his first two NFL seasons with Minnesota, however, his opportunities were limited. He appeared in eight games overall, including one as a rookie and seven in his second season, without making a start. He accumulated 88 offensive snaps in the NFL, all during his second season. Rouse also brings positional flexibility to the Patriots. Although he primarily played tackle in college and initially worked at right tackle in the NFL, the Vikings moved him inside during the 2026 preseason. All 109 of his preseason snaps this summer came at either left guard or right guard. New England now has additional depth behind their projected starting offensive line of Will Campbell, Alijah Vera-Tucker, Jared Wilson, Mike Onwenu and Morgan Moses. Rouse also joins a group that includes first-round rookie Caleb Lomu, sixth-round rookie Dametrious Crownover and 2025 seventh-round pick Marcus Bryant. Bryant suffered an injury during the second preseason game and is reportedly expected to begin the season on injured reserve. Rouse can also provide depth at guard, where the Patriots have Greg Van Roten and potentially Ben Brown, who has been out since the second week of the preseason with an injury. The acquisition was New England’s second trade before roster cuts after the Patriots acquired running back Corey Kiner from the Arizona Cardinals on Saturday. articles.title: Dolly Parton’s Legacy on the Billboard 200 Chart: 7 Decades of Hit Albums
articles.summary: She scored more top 40-charted sets in the 2020s than in any other decade.
articles._body: For seven straight decades, from the 1960s on through the 2020s, the late Dolly Parton charted an iconic string of 50 albums on the all-genre Billboard 200 chart during her lifetime — including 15 top 40-charted sets. Following her passing on Aug. 25, Parton racked up a 16th top 40 set with Ultimate Dolly Parton . From her debut with Porter Wagoner on Just the Two of Us in 1969, on through her most recent studio album to debut, 2023’s Rockstar , the singer-songwriter left a remarkable impression on Billboard ’s signature album chart. Related Dolly Parton Hit Billboard’s Dance Charts, Too, And Even Earned a No. 1 Hit Dolly Parton’s Manager Details the Business Ventures ‘She Had Yet to Fulfill’ Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library Program Honored by Library of Congress: ‘Titan of Children’s Literacy’ Parton notched four early albums on the Billboard 200 with her former TV co-star and duet partner Wagoner in 1969-71. She charted her first solo entry also in 1969, with My Blue Ridge Mountain Boy . Parton would not reach the top 40 of the all-genre Billboard 200 albums chart until 1978, when Here You Come Again climbed to a No. 20 peak off the strength of its smash title track. The single sailed to No. 3 on the overall Billboard Hot 100 songs chart, and marked her first of eight top 40 hits on the ranking. After the Here You Come Again album, Parton would hit the top 40 again in short order with Heartbreaker (No. 27 in 1978), Great Balls of Fire (No. 40 in 1979) and 9 to 5 and Odd Jobs (No. 11 in 1981). The latter boasted her first Hot 100 No. 1 in “9 to 5,” which also scored Parton her first Academy Award nomination, for best original song (from the film of the same name, in which Parton co-starred with Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin). Parton would hit the top 40 of the Billboard 200 again in late 1984 with her holiday album Once Upon a Christmas , with Kenny Rogers. Just a year before, the pair teamed up on Parton’s second Hot 100 No. 1, “Islands in the Stream.” In 1987, Parton joined Linda Ronstadt and Emmylou Harris for the successful Trio album, which reached No. 6 on the Billboard 200 and granted Parton her first top 10 on the chart. Trio would garner Parton her first, and so far only, Grammy Award nomination for album of the year. In the 1990s, Parton notched two more top 40 albums on the Billboard 200 with Eagle When She Flies (No. 24 in 1991) and Slow Dancing With the Moon (No. 16 in 1993). In the 2000s, she brought Backwoods Barbie to the top 40, hitting No. 17 in 2009. In 2014, Parton achieved her first top 10 on the Billboard 200 unaccompanied by any other acts, as Blue Smoke debuted and peaked at No. 6. She followed it with another top 40 album two years later, Pure & Simple , which hit No. 11. In the 2020s, Parton has claimed four new top 40-charted albums — more than in any other decade. In 2020, she reached No. 16 with A Holly Dolly Christmas and followed it with Run, Rose, Run (No. 34 in 2022) and the best-of compilation Diamonds & Rhinestones: The Greatest Hits Collection (No. 27 in 2022). In 2023, Parton claimed her highest charting Billboard 200 album ever, as the all-star collabrations project Rockstar debuted and peaked at No. 3. The Rockstar project was promoted as Parton’s first rock album, and its recording was sparked by Parton’s induction to the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2022. Through her career, Parton primarily recorded country music, but took detours (via albums and songs) into such genres as Americana/folk, bluegrass, children’s music, Christian, dance/electronic and pop. The 30-song Rockstar album mixed covers and original tunes and included guests such as Pat Benatar, Miley Cyrus, Melissa Etheridge, Joan Jett and The Blackhearts, Elton John, Lynyrd Skynyrd, Paul McCartney, Stevie Nicks, Chris Stapleton, Ringo Starr, Sting and Steven Tyler. In the wake of her death, Parton collected a fourth top 10 — and her second-highest-charted album ever — on the Billboard 200 with her 2003 best-of compilation Ultimate Dolly Parton , when it reentered at No. 5 on the Sept. 5, 2026-dated chart.

articles._body: The NFL roster cutdown deadline is always the best or worst day for a player hoping to see his professional dreams become a reality. On one hand, you see years of hard work finally pay off in the form of making a 53-man roster to officially play on Sundays. On the other, it’s the end of the road for many, with that training camp work just not quite good enough. Others are somewhere in between, waived from their respective rosters, but brought back on practice squads with a shot at a call-up down the road. For the Kentucky Wildcats , there were 30-plus BBNFL alums fighting for spots with varying levels of safety going into the regular season. Some are obvious franchise pieces who slept just fine over the weekend, knowing they were not only locked into the 53, but likely in the starting lineup — hello, Josh Hines-Allen, Wan’Dale Robinson and Maxwell Hairston, among others. How about the fringe guys, though, who were sweating out the Sunday deadline, set for 6 p.m. ET? Some received good news, such as Marques Cox in Miami, while others were surprise cuts and looking for new homes, like Darian Kinnard in Green Bay. KSR has the cutdown tracker rolling for Big Blue Nation to follow along as they find out if their favorite former Wildcats will be sticking around for NFL RedZone viewings in the coming months. articles.title: YSL’s ‘Slime Language 3’: All 41 Tracks Ranked
articles.summary: The 41-song compilation is a peek into the present and future of Young Thug's label.
articles._body: YSL shared the third installment of its popular Slime Language compilation series on Friday (Aug. 28), featuring Future , Travis Scott , Lil Baby and many more. If you asked someone any time between 2022 and 2025 if they thought Young Thug ’s Young Stoner Life label would put out another Slime Language compilation album, they probably would have said no. In that period, Gunna became completely distanced from the group, along with Yak Gotti, Lil Duke, YTB Trench,and FN DaDealer. Additionally, Nine Vicious left in 2025. Related Young Thug’s YSL Records Surprise-Drops ‘Slime Language 3’ Double Album The most important factor of all was Thugger being behind bars for more than two years due to the YSL RICO case . Fortunately, he was able to strike a plea deal and come home, but the damage to his label and Atlanta as a whole felt insurmountable. Many fallings-out occurred as a result of plea deals, betrayal and pride. Thug also had a tough time reorienting himself to the current music landscape, as his comeback album UY SCUTI did not land well for the masses (though it did make the top 10 of the Billboard 200, peaking at No. 6). The beautiful thing about music, though — specifically out of The A — is that there are always new, hungry artists who are ready for the spotlight. Throughout his career, Thugger has gotten stronger an as artist by mentoring up-and-comers and allowing their creative energy to flow through him. Thus, we get Slime Language 3 , which shows that the new era of YSL has the potential to be impactful in its own way. Tezzus, diamond* and 1300SAINT have countless standout moments on this two-disc, 41-song project. And it wouldn’t be a YSL compilation without inviting the extended family. Future, Travis Scott, Lil Baby, Yeat, Quavo and Cash Cobain are among those bringing their flavors to the party. Take a gander at our ranking of the 41-song compilation and get a peek into what the present and future of YSL looks like.

articles._body: The SEC is prepared to let the courts decide whether former NFL players can play in the league, despite the conference passing restrictions on such activity recently. The league released a statement on Sunday to CBS Sports clarifying its intent. In short, the league plans to avail itself of the opportunity to speak in court on Thursday at a hearing in a Louisiana lawsuit. Until then, it will respect the court’s decision compelling the SEC to make way for former professionals under the order. [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] “The order entered against the SEC and Commissioner (Greg) Sankey is a temporary restraining order, not a final ruling on the merits,” the statement provided to Brandon Marcello of CBS Sports read . “The SEC and Commissioner Sankey are prepared to contest the allegations in the plaintiffs’ petition at Thursday morning’s hearing and defend the SEC’s rights as a voluntary association to fulfill its mission to its member institutions. “In the meantime, the SEC and Commissioner Sankey will continue to comply with the Court’s order. Following the hearing, the SEC will carefully review the Court’s decision and determine the appropriate next steps.” The court case in Louisiana, which cleared the way for several class of 2022 athletes to receive an additional year of eligibility, even if they had been on NFL rosters, took a turn late in the week. The SEC and Sankey were added as defendants in the case, putting pressure on the league’s recently adopted policy to disallow former professional players from returning and playing for member schools. The SEC instituted some harsh penalties for programs doing so. Violating the new SEC-pro sports rule will result in a coach suspension of 50% of contests and a hefty fine. The fine will amount for 50% of that sport’s annual operating budget, and the head coach’s suspension will include all coaching, recruiting and administrative duties. The punishment is similar to the one the NCAA has in place for “ghost transfers,” or players who leave one school for another without entering the transfer portal. However, with the SEC now listed as a defendant in the Louisiana lawsuit, the conference has put its enforcement on hold. As noted, the league is prepared to contest the court’s ruling on Thursday. With programs like LSU awaiting a decision ahead of the season’s opening kick — with a handful of players affected by the contested portion of the court battle — the upcoming week’s legal proceedings figure to be closely monitored.

articles._body: The Dallas Cowboys made one of the biggest moves of the late offseason when they signed Von Miller . The future Hall of Famer ranks ninth all-time in sacks with 138.5, and the former Super Bowl MVP still has plenty of quarterback hurries left in the tank to bring to his hometown of Dallas. Last season, Miller had nine sacks with the Washington Commanders, and he brings pass-rushing prowess to a team still trying to navigate life after Micah Parsons. The fact that he lasted so long into free agency was a shock, but Miller’s addition also created more pass-rushing depth on the roster than the Cowboys could fit in 53 spots. One of Dallas’ final cut-down day decisions was to release Sam Williams, whom the team had re-signed to a $2 million deal back in March. Williams’ contract was guaranteed, but the 2022 second-round pick became expendable with a proven commodity like Miller on the roster. Williams showed flashes of greatness early in his career, as he racked up 8.5 sacks through his first two seasons. He missed all of year three with a torn ACL, though, and the defensive end didn’t look like the same player last year when he had just one sack. Miller, Rashan Gary, Malachi Lawrence, Donovan Ezeiruaku, James Houston, and Tyrus Wheat made the team as Dallas’ edge rushers over Williams, who wasn’t the only surprise cut the Cowboys made. Dallas also let go of running back Jayden Blue in one of the most surprising moves of the cut-down deadline. articles.title: Grass Is Latest Issue With Bills’ New Stadium
articles.summary: Gregory Fisher-Imagn Images
articles._body: The Bills are still working out the kinks at their brand new stadium as the NFL regular season approaches, and the latest issue is its grass. The team’s new Highmark Stadium, a $2.2 billion home venue that opened this summer after three years of construction, will have its field re-sodded ahead of Week 2, when Buffalo hosts the Lions on Sept. 17, a representative for the team confirmed to Front Office Sports . The condition of the field came into question because of instances of sod being displaced during the stadium’s first football events, including two August preseason games. Player comments about the field also contributed to the uncertainty; one anonymous player told The Athletic earlier this month “ the field is ass right now. ” The plan to re-sod was first reported on Saturday by the Buffalo News , which said the field passed the NFL’s safety and playability standards earlier this week. “We’re committed to having the best possible playing surface for our players,” a team representative said in a statement shared with FOS . “With a stretch of three consecutive home games early in the season, we decided it was the appropriate time to re-sod our field.” The process will begin on Monday, the statement said, and the full installation of the new surface is expected to be completed by the end of the week. “We will continue to monitor the field and every aspect of our new stadium to ensure it is the best possible experience for our players and fans,” the statement finished. The grass isn’t the only aspect of the stadium that hasn’t necessarily provided fans and players with the best possible experience. The Bills said earlier this month they were “ addressing internal and external feedback ” after a weekend scrimmage generated record attendance but also revealed the presence of some obstructed-view seats, particularly in the upper deck. (Some of the seats that have received criticism online are not being sold for Bills games.) Despite criticism of the obstructed seats, Highmark Stadium has drawn large crowds since opening its doors. Its first fan-facing event, the annual Return of the Blue & Red practice, drew 51,807 fans, beating the event’s prior high by more than 12,000. Buffalo’s first home preseason game—a 29–14 victory over the Panthers—drew 58,528, the team told FOS . The second game, a 28–27 comeback win over the Steelers to close out the preseason, drew 59,001, the team said. Those numbers are all less than the Bills have drawn in recent years. Last year, the one home preseason game they played had 69,835 paid attendees , and in 2024, they averaged about 69,462 attendees over two games, according to The Football Database. The drop can be partially explained by the fact that the new Highmark Stadium simply has fewer available seats than the old Highmark Stadium. The new venue has a total capacity of 60,108, compared to over 71,000 for the old Highmark Stadium. The post Grass Is Latest Issue With Bills’ New Stadium appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: Lions’ Kerby Joseph to start season on PUP, out at least 4 games with knee injury
articles.summary: Veteran safety Kerby Joseph has been working his way back from a knee injury he suffered last year, with the hopes of contributing to the Detroit Lions’ defense. However, he will not be available for the first four games of the 2026-27 season after the club’s latest decision. Reports
articles._body: Veteran safety Kerby Joseph has been working his way back from a knee injury he suffered last year, with the hopes of contributing to the Detroit Lions’ defense. However, he will not be available for the first four games of the 2026-27 season after the club’s latest decision. Reports indicate that the Lions plan to move the 25-year-old to the reserve/PUP , according to Jeremy Fowler of ESPN. That means the Lions will be without Joseph for at least the first four games of the new campaign. “The Lions plan to move safety Kerby Joseph to reserve/PUP, meaning he’ll miss a minimum of four games, per source,” Fowler reported. Joseph initially suffered the knee injury in last year’s training camp. After recovering from the injury, he aggravated his knee again after suffering a bone bruise in Week 4 last season. Kerby Joseph played through the pain before injuring his knee again in Week 6 last year. It’s been a long road to recovery, and the Lions star will need several more weeks to eventually make a full recovery. When healthy, Joseph has proven to be a reliable starter since being drafted in the third round of the 2022 NFL Draft. He’s a turnover machine and consistent defender, as he has recorded 265 combined tackles (196 solo), 20 interceptions, and one fumble recovery in 55 career games played. He’s also managed to return one of those picks for a touchdown in the 2024-25 campaign. The safety’s in Detroit are both going to miss the first four games of the season, as Brian Branch is working his way back from a torn Achilles tendon. That means the Lions will have to rely on Avonte Maddoz and Chuck Clark for the first few games. articles.summary: Valor Christian is looking very strong, and their cross-sectional matchup against Mater Dei this weekend will be one of the biggest games in the country.
articles._body: Valor Christian is looking very strong, and their cross-sectional matchup against Mater Dei this weekend will be one of the biggest games in the country. Cherry Creek will take on Ralston Valley in a rematch of last year’s State Championship Game. Grandview had arguably the most exciting win of the weekend, rallying in the 4th to take down Legend. Another jam-packed slate is on deck as teams continue their quests for a state title. Below are the top 25 Colorado high school football teams, according to the Massey Ratings , as of Aug. 30. 1. Cherry Creek (1-0) The Bruins had their bye over the weekend and will take on Ralston Valley on September 4 in a rematch of last year’s State Championship Game. 2. Valor Christian (2-0) It was the Titus Huard to Jackson Coleman show once again as the Eagles rolled over Las Vegas (Nev.) Faith Lutheran, one of the top 10 teams in the state, 46-9. Huard was 16-24 for 296 yards and three touchdowns while Coleman caught seven passes for 194 yards and all three touchdowns. Roger Garey added 92 yards and two touchdowns on the ground, and the defense was stout all night long with 10 tackles for loss and two interceptions. This Friday, the Eagles hit the road to play perennial national power Santa Ana (Calif.) Mater Dei. A potential fun game-within-the-game matchup to watch is Mater Dei corner and USC commit Danny Lang against Coleman, a Notre Dame commit. 3. Ralston Valley (1-0) The Mustangs opened their season in impressive fashion, pitching a 31-0 shutout against Castle View. Junior wideout Phoenix Tomsick, who was the state 200m champion last year, had several big plays in the game, including an 85-yard touchdown where he took a short hitch and outran the defense. Wyoming commit Levi Rillos excelled on both sides of the ball with an interception and a touchdown run. The Mustangs will play Cherry Creek this weekend, the No. 1 rated team in the state in a rematch of last year’s State Championship Game. 4. Grandview (2-0) In a game matching up a pair of top-10-ranked teams, the Wolves rallied to knock off Legend 28-24. Grandview was comfortably ahead at halftime 21-3, before Legend ripped off 21 straight points in the 3rd quarter to take a 24-21 lead in to the 4th. Grandview junior quarterback Lander Wise connected with Blake Richmeier from 33 yards out for the only score of the 4th quarter and the eventual game-winner. Wise finished the night 16-25 for 211 yards and three touchdowns while Richmeier had six catches for 135 yards and a pair of touchdowns. The Wolves will take on Fountain-Fort Carson on Friday. 5. Mountain Vista (1-1) The Golden Eagles knocked off Arapahoe in a shootout 43-39. Colorado State quarterback commit Marquise Reese had a big night, completing 28-of-39 passes for 316 yards and three touchdowns. He also rushed for 95 yards and the go-ahead touchdown from 11 yards out late in the 4th quarter. Brooklyn Bailey was his favorite target, hauling in 11 passes for 128 yards. The Golden Eagles will have a bye this weekend before hosting Montrose on September 18. 6. Eaglecrest (2-0) The Raptors moved up four spots after their 21-6 win over Regis Jesuit on Friday. Wide receiver JayAnthony Green had seven catches for 108 yards and a touchdown, and running back Clyde Surrell added a late 4th quarter touchdown to seal the deal. The Raptors will play on the road against Gonzaga Prep on Friday. 7. Montrose (1-0) The Red Hawks had a bye over the weekend and will play Palisade on Friday. 8. Fairview (1-0) The Knights opened their season in impressive fashion, with a dominant 45-6 win over Westminster. Quarterback Ki Ellison put on a show, completing 15-of-24 passes for 211 yards and three touchdowns and rushing for 77 yards and one more score. Cashin Fejer was his primary target, catching five passes for 95 yards and a pair of touchdowns. The Knights will play on the road against ThunderRidge on Thursday. 9. Palmer Ridge (2-0) The Bears moved to 2-0 with a solid win over La Cueva, the No. 4-ranked team in New Mexico, 29-10. Running back Micah Nocita was the star of the game, rushing for 180 yards and a touchdown. Quarterback Knox Tinlin threw for 120 yards and a touchdown and rushed for 20 yards on the ground and a score. The Bears will host Mesa Ridge on Friday. 10. Legend (0-1) In one of the most exciting games of the weekend, Legend lost a tough one to No. 4-ranked Grandview 28-24. There were a ton of twists and turns in this one, with Grandview holding a 21-3 lead at halftime before Legend dominated the 3rd quarter, outscoring the Wolves 21-0 to take a 24-21 lead into the final frame. Grandview was able to make one more play and scored the lone touchdown in the 4th to get the win. articles.title: Josh Berry told NASCAR owners to ‘just watch the races’ — then delivered again
articles.summary: Josh Berry backed up his “just watch the races” message to NASCAR owners with a fifth straight Top 10 as his search for a 2027 ride continues.
articles._body: Josh Berry remains on the job hunt after it was announced that he would be replaced in the Wood Brothers No. 21 in 2027 by Jesse Love. He also remains on a heater when he needs it the most. On Saturday night in Daytona, Berry had a late rally and was in contention on the final lap of overtime. Although he was caught up in the wreck coming to the checkered flag, Berry finished P9 in the Coke Zero 400 . The Berry streak continues Saturday night’s finish made it five-in-a-row Top Ten finishes for Berry. An amazing run for a driver who will not be in the Cup Series in 2027, barring another seat opening late in the cycle.   After the news that RCR had signed Austin Hill for the 2027 NASCAR Cup Series season, that reality for Josh Berry set in.  There are no open rides in the Cup Series for next season as of today.   But Berry keeps producing, and keeps marketing himself to potential employers.  Although he was not interviewed after Saturday night’s race, Berry let people know on Twitter .  P9 @DAYTONA . Had a shot at it at the end. #5inarow Thank you @geteero @woodbrothers21 @FordRacing — Josh Berry (@joshberry) August 30, 2026 A week ago at New Hampshire, his P4 finish gave him four straight Top 10 finishes, a first for the Wood Brothers since 1994 when Morgan Shepherd did it.  He’s grown that count to five-in-a-row.  If he hits a sixth Top Ten in a row, he will join some truly rarified air.   A sixth would be a first for Wood Brothers since 1976 when NASCAR Hall of Famer David Pearson did it.   And it feels like with each passing race, Berry is gaining fans. The 35-year-old Tennessee native is an easy one to pull for. And add in the fact that he’s on the verge of not having a seat in 2027, and it’s even easier. An anemic job market At this point, it’s likely O’Reilly or Trucks for Berry.  And that’s despite the fact that he has more Top Tens than one Chase driver and the same amount as two others.  Berry has led more laps than four Chase drivers.  A week ago, Berry gave a banger quote following his finish at New Hampshire.  That quote still resonates today.  “You just watch the races,” said Berry to Dustin Albino . “I don’t know what else you can say. I’ve been pretty honest about my feelings with how this stuff works.   “It just boils down to finding someone that believes in me that I can do this. Unfortunately, most of the time, it comes down to how much money you have to find opportunities.  “Hopefully, something is out there for me.”

articles.summary: The Cleveland Guardians have endured an up and down season. They are still in the American League postseason conversation, as winning the American League Central remains realistic while the ball club is currently in the AL Wild Card picture. Starting pitcher Parker Messick has somewhat quietly em
articles._body: The Cleveland Guardians have endured an up and down season. They are still in the American League postseason conversation, as winning the American League Central remains realistic while the ball club is currently in the AL Wild Card picture. Starting pitcher Parker Messick has somewhat quietly emerged as not just a star rookie, but one of the best pitchers in baseball. Messick perfectly displayed how he’s become a true ace during Cleveland’s Sunday’s 11-1 win against the Kansas City Royals. Cleveland entered its series against the Royals on a seven-game winning streak on Friday. However, the ball club dropped the first two games of the series. The Guardians needed a win on Sunday. While Messick clearly received no shortage of run support, the southpaw also turned in a stellar performance. He turned in six innings of one-run baseball while striking out five hitters. Aces are the guys who either end losing streaks or stop them from happening in the first place, and Messick helped the Guards avoid a three-game sweep at home on Sunday. It should be noted that Messick has not often received much run support this season . Sunday’s game was a nice change in that department. The reality of the situation is that all Messick needed was two runs of support in the contest — but he won’t complain about 11 runs. It seems as if the narrative in the American League is still that either the Detroit Tigers’ Kevin McGonigle or the Chicago White Sox’s Munetaka Murakami will win the AL Rookie of the Year Award. Messick is consistently mentioned right behind those guys, but he deserves far more respect in the conversation. Parker Messick deserves to win the AL Rookie of the Year Award in 2026. Why Guardians’ Parker Messick deserves the 2026 AL Rookie of the Year Award Ken Blaze-Imagn Images McGonigle and Murakami have both enjoyed strong seasons, especially considering the fact that they are rookies. McGonigle is currently hitting .276 to go along with a .795 OPS and 14 home runs. Meanwhile, Murakami is hitting just .218 but he has an .854 OPS and 29 home runs. Neither player will seriously be considered for the AL MVP. They could receive some votes, but they are not true candidates for that award. The AL Rookie of the Year is realistic for both, but they are not having incredibly memorable seasons compared to other superstars in the sport. Messick, however, is having a legitimate Cy Young-caliber campaign. The left-hander holds a 2.46 ERA across 27 starts to go along with 161 strikeouts. He likely won’t win the Cy Young in the AL given the presences of the New York Yankees’ Cam Schlittler and Toronto Blue Jays’ Dylan Cease, but Messick deserves to be a finalist. The Guardians southpaw is currently third in the AL in ERA, fourth in innings pitched, eighth in strikeouts, fourth in WHIP and fourth in opponents batting average. At the very least, Messick should be third in AL Cy Young voting if the season ended today, and one could argue he could be second. Comparing a hitter’s season to a pitcher’s season can present challenges. McGonigle and Murakami have played well, but Messick is having a true Cy Young-caliber season. There is still plenty of baseball left to be played and it will be intriguing to see how Messick holds up over the final month of the ’26 campaign as a rookie. With all of that being said, Parker Messick should win the AL Rookie of the Year Award this season. The post Guardians’ Parker Messick must win AL Rookie of the Year. Aaron Donald Returns to Rams
articles.summary: Tommy Gilligan-USA TODAY Sports
articles._body: Aaron Donald is back. And the Rams, who were already prohibitive Super Bowl favorites, will enter the NFL season with a roster overflowing with talent on both sides of the ball. Donald, 35, ended his retirement Sunday and rejoined the Rams. The defensive tackle has a litany of accomplishments: 10 Pro Bowl selections, eight first-team All-Pro appearances, three NFL Defensive Player of the Year awards, and a Super Bowl title in 10 seasons with the Rams before retiring following the 2023 season. Donald will play for Los Angeles on a one-year contract that is worth $20 million and includes an additional $10 million in potential incentives, his agent Todd France of Athletes First tells Front Office Sports . He comes back to a team that traded this offseason for pass rusher Myles Garrett—a two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year with the Browns—to add to a collection of star players that already included quarterback and reigning league MVP Matthew Stafford and wide receiver Puka Nacua. The Rams, who lost last season’s NFC championship game to the Seahawks, were already widely regarded as the favorite to win the Super Bowl title. They are now cemented even more firmly as the front-runner. At a press conference on Sunday at the Rams’ training facility, Donald said he thinks he still can be the same player that he previously was, adding that the Rams’ eye-catching offseason moves prompted him to contemplate his return and begin discussions with coach Sean McVay. “Seeing what was being done with this team, the pieces that [were] getting brought here… and then you see all the moves they make, and it’s like, ‘Okay, I wish I was still out there playing right about now,’” Donald said. “You have conversations and then kind of start bringing it to fruition, starting to put myself in a position to train and get my body to a certain point where I felt good and seeing how I move and see if I still can do certain things…. Aaron is back playing football again, right?” Earlier in the day, Donald confirmed his comeback in a video posted to social media entitled “The Return.” The team also confirmed it without announcing contract specifics. “I let him out the house y’all,” his wife Erica wrote on X/Twitter . Los Angeles was $15.4 million under the NFL’s salary cap, according to NFL Players Association records. The $20 million that the Rams will pay to Donald before any incentives is reportedly divided into a $10 million base salary and $10 million through per-game 53-man roster bonuses, a structure that helps the team fit Donald’s contract beneath the cap. Donald had one season remaining on his contract with the Rams when he retired. That remained in effect, for approximately $30 million. But the team worked out a revised deal with Donald and France. Los Angeles faces the 49ers in Melbourne on Sept. 10 for its opening game of the season. It was not immediately clear whether Donald will make that trip and play in that game. Donald is known for his rigorous training routine. His on-field preparations for his comeback included two official workouts with the Rams, called “tryouts” on the NFL’s daily personnel notices. “Good to be able to get Aaron back into the mix,” McVay said at a separate news conference. “You guys know how close we are. There’s been a lot of dialogue that we’ve had. Excited to be able to just take it a day at a time. I’m not going to talk about any sort of plans. It’s going to be a day at a time for us… We’ll see what that ramp-up period looks like, whether or not he’s available or whether or not we think it’s best to be able to play him in Australia.” The Rams posted to social media an image of Donald’s letter to NFL commissioner Roger Goodell in which he wrote simply, “I’m Back.” Donald also signed with Jon Rosen’s management team at Envisionary to grow his businesses, brand partnerships, and overall profile in the media and entertainment industries, Rosen confirmed to FOS in early August. In March, the Rams traded first-, fifth-, and sixth-round draft picks this year and a third-rounder next year to the Chiefs for cornerback Trent McDuffie, then signed him to a four-year, $124 million contract extension that includes $100 million in guaranteed money. In June, they dealt pass rusher Jared Verse and three draft choices—a first-rounder next year, a second-rounder in 2028, and a third-rounder in 2029—to the Browns for Garrett, who set the NFL’s single-season sack record with 23 last season. Los Angeles is the first NFL team to have both a quarterback who is the reigning MVP and the previous season’s defensive player of the year. And now the Rams have Donald as well. “Do I feel like I can play at a high level? Yes,” Donald said. “Do I feel like I can still be myself? A hundred percent. If I didn’t feel like that, I wouldn’t be here.” The post Aaron Donald Returns to Rams appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles._body: Head coach Mike McCarthy will have plenty of decisions to make as he finalizes his first roster with the Pittsburgh Steelers . When it comes to the quarterback situation, McCarthy clearly believes the more the merrier. The Steelers are carrying four quarterbacks on the 53-man roster, via Adam Schefter of ESPN. Aaron Rodgers, Mason Rudolph, Will Howard and Drew Allar have all made the cut. Rodgers’ inclusion was inevitable. He is entering what is expected to be his final season in the NFL . Behind them though, there was nothing certain with the Steelers’ quarterback room. But with all three providing value in the franchise’s eyes, they decided not to make any changes. Of all three players, Rudolph offers the most NFL experience. If Rodgers were to suffer an injury that forced him to the sidelines, perhaps he is the player Pittsburgh would call upon. As long as Rodgers is around, it seems unlikely either will see the field. But both will be around the organization, seeing how McCarthy and company operate. That will be crucial experience if either is set to take over as QB in 2027. When it comes to Steelers quarterbacks, all eyes are on Rodgers. articles.title: Guardians’ Parker Messick closing in on franchise record with another gem vs. Royals
articles.summary: Cleveland Guardians starter Parker Messick turned in yet another impressive performance in an 11-1 win over the Kansas City Royals on Sunday. The All-Star left-hander worked six innings, surrendering one run on five hits while finishing with five strikeouts and two walks. By allowing two runs or
articles._body: Cleveland Guardians starter Parker Messick turned in yet another impressive performance in an 11-1 win over the Kansas City Royals on Sunday. The All-Star left-hander worked six innings , surrendering one run on five hits while finishing with five strikeouts and two walks. By allowing two runs or fewer once again, Messick extended his streak to 10 straight starts , tying Bob Lemon’s mark from 1956. One more such outing would put him alongside Gaylord Perry, whose 11-start streak in 1974 remains the Cleveland franchise record. Messick’s current run is therefore the longest by a Guardians pitcher since Perry’s 1974 run. The 25-year-old improved to 11-8 on the season having entered the game with a 2.50 ERA, which ranked second among qualified major league rookies. His six-inning performance lowered his season ERA to 2.46. Through 27 games and 27 starts, Messick has logged 161 strikeouts, 43 walks and a 1.02 WHIP across 161 innings, with his 9.0 strikeouts per nine innings. The outing was particularly impressive considering Kansas City made Messick work early. The Royals forced him to throw 31 pitches in the first inning, and Salvador Perez brought home Kansas City’s only run with an RBI single. Messick escaped the inning by striking out Nick Loftin and then settled down over the remainder of his performance. As Messick kept the Royals under control, Cleveland’s offense exploded for 11 runs. Jose Ramirez homered and collected his 1,000th career single, while driving in four runs. Chase DeLauter went 4-for-4 with two doubles and an RBI, recording his third career four-hit game and raising his August batting average to .329 with a .901 OPS. The Guardians improved to 69-68 and holds the third American League wild-card position. Cleveland gets a breather Monday before opening a three-game series against the Toronto Blue Jays on Tuesday. articles._body: The Arizona Diamondbacks have been embroiled in an off-field saga involving star infielder Ketel Marte. Marte did not show up to one of the team’s games against the Boston Red Sox recently. Since then, he has not played and was also placed on the injured list. Much has been said about this situation. It’s clear that the Diamondbacks organization is frustrated and confused as to what’s going on. It appears that those who are looking for answers will have them soon. “The plan is for Ketel Marte to address his teammates tomorrow afternoon when he arrives to the ballpark before the Diamondbacks begin a crucial home stand against the Philadelphia Phillies,” local radio host John Gambadoro reported on Sunday . Marte is eligible to come off the injured list on Monday before taking on the Phillies. Whether he is activated and plays on Monday remains to be seen. However, it’s clear this is a contentious time for the Diamondbacks organization. It won’t be easy to mend fences, though manager Torey Lovullo will do his best to do so. “It will be my job to make sure when Ketel gets back in that clubhouse it’s smoothed over, and then we get to playing baseball as soon as possible,” Lovullo told MLB Network Radio on Friday. The Diamondbacks are still fighting for a playoff spot at this time. In fact, Arizona currently owns the final Wild Card spot in the National League. Adding Marte to this lineup certainly gives them a chance to cement their claim to this postseason spot. Only time will tell if the tense clubhouse situation can be mended during the season. Meanwhile, Victor Wembanyama has been competing for his native France at the ongoing FIBA World Cup qualifiers in Europ
articles._body: The San Antonio Spurs have had a relatively quiet offseason, running it back with the same core of players who made it to the NBA Finals last year, in addition to Tobias Harris. Meanwhile, Victor Wembanyama has been competing for his native France at the ongoing FIBA World Cup qualifiers in Europe, putting up some impressive performances in the process. Now, Wemby has revealed how strange it is to no longer be on the French national team year-round. “A lot of frustration. I didn’t expect it to be this much, but seeing these guys again, whom I’ve known for so long, feels so good. It’s going to feel strange not being with them anymore,” he said, per L’Equipe, via Hoopshype. However, Spurs fans won’t have to worry about the star’s mind being elsewhere during the upcoming season. “That doesn’t change the fact that I’m still very excited to be back in San Antonio and to get back to work. There’s nowhere else like it to work,” he added. Wembanyama staked his claim as the best basketball player on the planet during the Western Conference Finals against the Oklahoma City Thunder last year, with the Spurs knocking off the defending champs in seven games. However, he largely struggled during his first NBA Finals appearance vs the New York Knicks, with his late-game execution in particular repeatedly coming up short against a veteran opponent. Still, there’s little doubt that Wembanyama will progress even further in his upcoming fourth NBA season, which will be filled with title aspirations for San Antonio. The Spurs are set to kick off their new season on October 20 vs the Thunder. Then LLMs could write them, and lectures could be fixed with code edits instead of v
articles._body: Hi HN, we are Sina Atalay and Abdullah Geduk, co-founders of Academa. We are both PhD students. We thought: what if lecture videos were written as code and compiled into video using computer graphics and TTS? Then LLMs could write them, and lectures could be fixed with code edits instead of video production. On correctness: LLMs may make mistakes. But these videos are code sitting in our repository, and we can maintain them. Every report and review becomes a fix in the source, and everyone who watches after that gets the corrected lecture. Every recorded lecture on the internet is stuck with its mistakes. Ours will continuously improve. Each video also comes with an AI chat that understands everything said and shown in the lecture. articles._body: With the Chicago Bears trading defensive lineman Gervon Dexter to the Atlanta Falcons , the 25-year-old would take the time to send a message to the fanbase and his now-former team. As the Bears received trade interest for Dexter from other teams , the Falcons were the team that won the sweepstakes; while he starts a new chapter in his NFL journey, he would reflect on the team he started it with. Dexter took to X, formerly Twitter, to share his thoughts on the trade, first thanking the city of Chicago “for everything.” Having been in the NFL for the last three seasons with the Bears, he expressed that time “have meant more to me than I can put into words.” “Thank you to the Chicago Bears organization for drafting me, believing in me, and welcoming me and my family with open arms. Chicago will always be a special part of my journey, and I’ll forever appreciate my teammates, coaches, staff, and all of Bears Nation for the love and support,” Dexter wrote. Former Bears defensive tackle Gervon Dexter speaks about the Falcons When it comes to the trade itself, the Falcons dealt a fifth-round pick and corner back Clark Phillips in exchange for Dexter from the Bears, as the defensive tackle looks to take his talents under head coach Kevin Stefanski. Continuing in his farewell to Chicago, he would make sure to say that he is “excited” for his upcoming tenure with Atlanta. “With that being said, I’m excited for this next chapter,” Dexter continued. “Atlanta, I’m ready to get to work! Falcons fans, I’m excited to be here and ready to give everything I have to this team and this city. Looking forward to a great year! Forever grateful for where I’ve been. Excited for where I’m going.” At any rate, while Chicago starts its regular season schedule on Sept. 13 against the Carolina Panthers, the team does have the Falcons for an Oct. 18 matchup that is sure to hold a lot of emotion for Dexter. The Vikings selected McCarthy 10th overall in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft, but he missed his entire rookie season due to a devastating knee injury he suffered in the preseason. articles.summary: Even though he has struggled more than usual at times this season, Scottie Scheffler has still shown time and time again that he is the man to beat in professional golf. On the final Sunday of the PGA Tour season, he rose above the rest one final time in 2026. After starting the final round [R
articles._body: Even though he has struggled more than usual at times this season, Scottie Scheffler has still shown time and time again that he is the man to beat in professional golf. On the final Sunday of the PGA Tour season, he rose above the rest one final time in 2026. After starting the final round of the Tour Championship three shots off the lead, Scheffler found his best golf early and often in tough conditions to run away with a three shot victory and win the FedEx Cup for the second time . Scheffler’s four-under 66 in the final round matched the best round of the day in dry, windy conditions that flummoxed most of the players at the top of the leaderboard. 54-hole leader Viktor Hovland couldn’t find the fairway on Sunday and fired a two-over 72 to finish alone in second place. His 72 was matched by Ryan Gerard in the final group, and the North Carolina native finished in solo-third. Scheffler started the day hot, nearly firing an ace on the par-3 second hole before sinking the easy birdie putt. After birdies on Nos. 8 and 10, he had equaled Hovland for the lead at 15-under par while the Norwegian struggled to find his groove off the tee. The championship-winning moment came on the 16th after Scheffler’s drive found the fairway bunker. He didn’t blink at the challenging approach, sticking it to about 10 feet before sinking the birdie putt to extend his lead. Hovland faltered on the 17th with a chance to close the gap, and the rest was history. Scheffler came into the FedEx Cup Playoffs as the points leader for the season before winning the FedEx St. Jude Championship a few weeks ago in Memphis. Even though the Tour Championship no longer uses the starting strokes format that it did in the past, Scheffler still outpaced the rest of the field with ease over the weekend. This is the third victory of the season for Scheffler, a 2026 that has been defined by near-misses and tough finishes. After his playoff performance, however, it’s clear that he is still head and shoulders above the field heading into the Presidents Cup this fall and will be the favorite to collect more big titles in 2027. articles.title: Next move Packers must make with Josh Jacobs on exempt list after Kaleb Johnson trade
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers have been hit with a haymaker as they prepare for the start of the NFL season. They knew that they had a potential problem on their hands because of Josh Jacobs’ off-the-field difficulties, but there was hope that it would not impact them on the field until Jacobs̵
articles._body: The Green Bay Packers have been hit with a haymaker as they prepare for the start of the NFL season. They knew that they had a potential problem on their hands because of Josh Jacobs’ off-the-field difficulties, but there was hope that it would not impact them on the field until Jacobs’ legal case stemming from an alleged altercation at his home on May 23 was adjudicated. Jacobs was formally charged Thursday with misdemeanor battery and misdemeanor criminal damage to property. There was a thought that the matter would play out through the legal system before the NFL took any action, but he was placed on the commissioner’s exempt list. That means he cannot practice or play with the team but he could possibly go to the team’s facility for rehab, therapy and non-football activities if he makes such a request and the Packers are in agreement. Prior to the announcement of the suspension, the Packers acquired running back Kaleb Johnson from the Pittsburgh Steelers. Johnson was a third-round pick in the 2025 draft after a solid college career at Iowa, but he was never able to gain the confidence of the Steelers coaching staff. He gained 69 yards on 28 carries a year ago and made a notable special teams error in a loss to the Seahawks that result in an easy touchdown for the eventual Super Bowl champions. However, the 6-1, 225-pound Johnson had a monster season for the Hawkeyes in 2024, and the Packers will try to draw that kind of performance out of him. While he does not have game-breaking speed, he gained 1,537 yards on 240 carries for a 6.4 yards per carry average that included 21 rushing touchdowns during his final season with the Hawkeyes. Packers have to turn to MarShawn Lloyd The addition of Johnson gives the Packers some much-needed depth at the running back position, but it will take him some time to get acclimated to the Green Bay system. Head coach Matt LaFleur does not have to force-feed Johnson into the game plan when the Packers face the Minnesota Vikings in Week 1. He will eventually get an opportunity to show what he can do, but it may not be until Week 3 against the Atlanta Falcons or Week 4 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The first option is turning to MarShawn Lloyd. He has had injury issues since he was selected in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft after playing his college football at USC and South Carolina. Lloyd has played just one game in his NFL career because he has had a series of injuries. However, he has been healthy this summer and has looked like the most explosive running back that the Packers have on their roster. Lloyd has shown he can hit the hole quickly, finish his runs with authority and he appears to be very hungry for success. The Packers also have Chris Brooks, but he is more of a third-down back who can also block fairly well. He is a nice option, but he is not the kind of running back the Packers can depend on for big plays. The Packers do not have to panic and sign a running back off the street. They need to build Lloyd up and let him know that he will be the team’s No. 1 running back. If they can increase his confidence just a bit, they may have a running back who can do a decent-to-good job. He is not a star, but he can be a competent running back.   The post Next move Packers must make with Josh Jacobs on exempt list after Kaleb Johnson trade appeared first on ClutchPoints .

Aaron Donald goes full Michael Jordan with Rams return announcement
articles.summary: Michael Jordan is the greatest player in NBA history. He won six championships, five MVP trophies, and 10 scoring titles during his time in the NBA. However, some of those accolades that make for an unmatched resume didn’t happen until after Jordan first retired. His Airness left the Chicag
articles._body: Michael Jordan is the greatest player in NBA history . He won six championships, five MVP trophies, and 10 scoring titles during his time in the NBA. However, some of those accolades that make for an unmatched resume didn’t happen until after Jordan first retired. His Airness left the Chicago Bulls in 1993 in pursuit of a baseball career. Less than two years later, the G.O.A.T. announced his return to the hardwood with a press release that simply said: “I’m Back.” The memo has been repeated by athletes ending a hiatus numerous times since, but it rarely meant as much as it did with Jordan’s return. That was until Aaron Donald wrote “I’m Back” and officially confirmed his return to the Los Angeles Rams. pic.twitter.com/G4Wc6GZVLX — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) August 30, 2026 The defensive tackle hasn’t played since the 2023 season, but he was one of the best defensive players in NFL history during a 10-year career that ended while he was still in his prime. Donald is one of just three players with three Defensive Player of the Year nods to his name. The 10-time Pro Bowler and Super Bowl LVI champion seemingly still has plenty left in the tank, too. Donald is just 35 years old and joins a loaded Rams’ defense that added reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett in the offseason. Trent McDuffie was also acquired via trade , and Jaylen Watson was added in free agency. Along with an offense that features Matthew Stafford, Puka Nacua, and Davante Adams, the former of whom was last year’s MVP, and the Rams seem like clear-cut Super Bowl favorites. Winning three championships post-retirement, as Jordan did, seems unlikely for Donald, but the defensive tackle is officially back. articles.summary: The New York Giants are expected to release veteran offensive lineman Evan Neal, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz. Neal, who played college football at Alabama, has been with the Giants since 2022, when they selected him in the first round of the draft. The release comes as the Giants are fin
articles._body: The New York Giants are expected to release veteran offensive lineman Evan Neal , according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz . Neal, who played college football at Alabama , has been with the Giants since 2022, when they selected him in the first round of the draft. The release comes as the Giants are finalizing their initial 53-man roster for the 2026 season. In March, Neal re-signed with the Giants on a one-year contract after he played out his rookie deal. Ahead of the 2025 season, the Giants declined Neal’s fifth-year option. During his time with the Giants, Evan Neal started 13 games at right tackle before starting in just 14 games in 2023 and 2024. Last year, Neal did not play in a single game, as he was inactive before being placed on injured reserve with a hamstring injury in November. The Giants’ re-signing Neal was a surprise considering how things played out last year. However, a new coaching staff, led by head coach John Harbaugh , wanted to see if Neal would be a fit for the team moving forward. It looked like Neal was going to make the roster based on what offensive line coach Mike Bloomgren said about him earlier this month. Giants OL coach shares thoughts on Evan Neal “Yeah, I’ve seen great growth from Evan in his ability to take coaching and his ability to try to understand not just how things look on paper, but, like, what certain alignments mean to him,” Bloomgren said, per Patricia Traina of Sports Illustrated. “I think he’s seeing more in his stance, and he’s playing with more confidence,” Bloomgren added. “I haven’t been here for those years of questioning, but listening to other people in the building, they feel like he’s taking some good steps.” Before joining the Giants, Neal played at Alabama from 2019 to 2021. He helped the team win a national title in 2020 and was named a consensus All-American in 2021. Ahead of the 2022 draft, Lance Zierlein of NFL.com compared Neal to Jordan Mailata of the Philadelphia Eagles. Mailata was named to the All-Pro Second Team in 2024 and helped the Eagles win the Super Bowl that same year.

Scottie Scheffler Breaks Tiger’s PGA Tour Earnings Record, Wins Second FedEx Cup
articles.summary: Brett Davis-Imagn Images
articles._body: Scottie Scheffler’s 16-under at this weekend’s Tour Championship at the East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta earned him his third PGA Tour win this year. But the massive $10 million winner’s purse also catapulted him past Tiger Woods as the Tour’s all-time earnings leader. To date, he has taken home $130,390,661 in PGA Tour career earnings . Scheffler entered the weekend just $608,505 behind Woods on the career earnings list. He passed Rory McIlroy at No. 2 two weeks ago by winning the FedEx St. Jude Championship in Memphis—the first of three playoff events that culminated with the Tour Championship this weekend. But the golfer was unable to overtake Woods on the money list at last week’s BMW Championship in St. Louis, where he shot 7-under and finished in a tie for 12th place. The 30-year-old American finished the Tour Championship three strokes ahead of Norwegian Viktor Hovland, who earned $5 million for second place. Hovland came into Sunday at 15-under with a one-shot lead over Ryan Gerard—with Scheffler lurking three strokes back along with Chris Gotterup. Then, while Hovland and Gerard struggled slightly, Scheffler got hot, hitting six birdies on the final day to surge into the lead. It has been a strange year for Scheffler. Despite retaining his status as the world’s No. 1–ranked golfer, he went over half a year in between wins. After claiming The American Express trophy in January, he didn’t win another until the FedEx St. Jude Championship. Still, he’s finished in the top five 13 times and has won more than $30 million on the PGA Tour this year. He also earned $23 million in FedExCup bonus money for being in first place following last week’s BMW Championship; the PGA Tour does not count bonus money as career earnings. Scheffler has now led the Tour in prize money for five consecutive seasons. articles.title: Rick Pitino is tired of the NCAA lawsuit mess, too
articles.summary: Injunctions. Stays. Continuances. This summer, Big Blue Nation has had to become amateur legal analysts to interpret news about whether a guy who averaged 18.3 points per game last year will suit up for Kentucky this basketball season. If you’re worn out with all the lawsuits and court filings
articles._body: Injunctions. Stays. Continuances. This summer, Big Blue Nation has had to become amateur legal analysts to interpret news about whether a guy who averaged 18.3 points per game last year will suit up for Kentucky this basketball season. If you’re worn out with all the lawsuits and court filings, the new rules and fresh punishments, then you’re not alone. Everyone is ready for these standoffs to end and play some ball, including Rick Pitino. On Friday, Pitino posted on X : “I’m still puzzled as to why the NCAA didn’t wait until November with these new rules. All of this confusion could have been avoided. I can only imagine how much of our money has been spent on lawyers.” Rick Pitino, X Pitino is referring to the new 5 Years to Play 5 Seasons rule that the NCAA announced in late June, which opened the floodgates to the eligibility chaos for Class of 2022 students. He thinks if they had only waited until November to enact the new rule, then college sports wouldn’t be in this current state of dissarray. The logic tracks. By November, both the basketball and football seasons would be underway, and there likely would not be the time or appetite for legal battles in order to add a player for a handful of games. However, the NCAA gave schools (and attorneys) a few months of the summer to file suits, and they’ve seized it. Think of all the would-be NIL dollars being wasted on attorneys’ hourly rates. Did the NCAA create this mess on purpose? If you would be so kind as to don a tinfoil hat for a moment, there is another theory floating around about the NCAA’s timing of the 5-in-5 announcement. If you don’t have one, you can borrow former Athletic writer Kyle Tucker’s. He quoted Pitino’s post and suggested the timing was on purpose. Whispers: It was on purpose. https://t.co/AJEvS3AJrP — Kyle Tucker (@KyleTuckerCBB) August 29, 2026 Tucker is implying the NCAA knew that announcing the 5-in-5 rule early would generate a plethora of lawsuits and further imbue college sports with pandemonium. This, in their minds, would create urgency within Congress to pass the Protect College Sports Act. This is legislation that, in theory, would return some semblance of normalcy across the collegiate athletic landscape. The bill has been stalled, as lawmakers add amendments and tweaks to appease holdouts. It remains on shaky grounds as it makes its way through the procedural process, but it could come up for a full vote in the Senate in September. Key voices in the House of Representatives, though, have expressed skepticism, so it still has a long way to go before becoming law. Intentionally launching themselves into a slew of lawsuits for the sake of Congressional motivation would be diabolical, even by NCAA standards. Per Tucker , Alabama coach Nate Oats thinks this was the plan. The simplest reading of the situation is that of naivety or not thinking the timing aspect through. However, at this point, it is hard to put anything past the decision-makers within the National Collegiate Athletic Association. Whatever the reasoning, August Madness continues, and much like Rick Pitino, Kentucky fans are exhausted. They just want Mark Mitchell and Alex Afari to play. As for now, though, the waiting for the next judges’ decision continues.
