High School Football: Winners and Losers from Aug. 27-29
articles.summary: Well, well, well. The first few weeks of the 2026 high school football season has been about exciting as riding every roller coaster at a Six Flags multiple times over. Okay, maybe not that exhilarating, but you get what we mean by all this. The upsets, the down to the wire finishes, big plays. It&#
articles._body: Well, well, well. The first few weeks of the 2026 high school football season has been about exciting as riding every roller coaster at a Six Flags multiple times over. Okay, maybe not that exhilarating, but you get what we mean by all this. The upsets, the down to the wire finishes, big plays. It’s all really making us amped up for what’s ahead this fall and we’re all here for it. We’re looking at the players who impressed, the coaches who stood out and the fans who are either celebrating or scratching their heads. This week, we’re highlighting the biggest winners and losers – the people and moments that made the past few days memorable. [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] WINNERS Miami Columbus (Fla.) 5-star ATH A’mir Sears : Sears is him. You’ve heard the saying and as someone that watched this elite high school football player in-person, there’s not many players that really jump out at you the way the future Miami Hurricane does. The 2028 5-star put together a stat line that might be as good as it gets in the high school football world playing against some of the best talent this level has to offer. Sears finished with just under 70 yards receiving and added a couple tuddies and picked off three passes. Og yeah, and he did all that with Miami Hurricanes head coach Mario Cristobal watching from an endzone. Basha Bears (Ariz.): Coming off winning a Arizona Interscholastic Association (AIA) Open Division state championship, the Basha Bears made their 2026 regular season debut at home on national television (ESPN2) against the very team they beat in Chandler, 34-7, in 2025. What ended up ensuing was a strong offensive performance led by 2027 quarterback Jake Rogers (Princeton commit), who threw for over 200 yards and three touchdowns in the victory. If the AIA at some point this season decides to officially approve allowing one of their member teams to play in the Overtime Nationals, this game could have major importance way down the line as they try to repeat as state champs, but this time going undefeated while doing it will be the goal. Mount Carmel Caravan (IL): How many times do you hear of a team trailing 30-0 and coming back and winning without their head coach? Well in the case of Chicago Mount Carmel facing St. Joseph Regional of New Jersey on Friday night, neither team had their respective lead man and played probably the most thrilling game of them all. The Caravan, without head coach Jordan Lynch , who is suspended for the first two games of the regular season, were able to overcome the massive deficit and come away with a thrilling 48-44 victory at home. Total collapse or not by the Green Knights, Mount Carmel wanted it more and dug deep in order to come away with arguably the most exciting finish of the young season. LOSERS Bishop Gorman Gaels (Nev.): Life comes at you fast. One week you’re considered by many as the nation’s top high school football team and the next, everything comes crashing down like a sack of potatoes. Bishop Gorman looked like the favorite to run the table the rest of the way after an impressive 38-28 win against St. John Bosco in Las Vegas. Hold the line there as the Gaels looked listless for a quarter and a half before they woke up just before halftime. Other than a couple late touchdowns in an attempt to climb back into the game, Bishop Gorman might’ve worked themselves effectively out of the national championship picture. St. Frances Academy Panthers (Md.): It was just over a week since head coach Messay Hailemariam went off on social media, seemingly calling out every high school football team in the nation for a game. Then came game numero uno for St. Frances Academy when they traveled to Central Florida to take on one of the region’s better teams and boy did the Bulldogs give the Panthers everything they could want and then some. At times, it looked like the Panthers looked like they were on upset alert as they were trailing in the first half and the Bulldogs hung around for most of the second before pulling away. A game like this causes concern and pauses many on where exactly this team is on a national level. We give them a slight benefit of the doubt, but not by much here. DeSoto Eagles (TX): Sportsmanship ahead of a high school football game always starts right before the coin toss with the ceremonial handshakes. Video footage ahead of DeSoto’s historic meeting with St. Thomas Aquinas showed many for the exception of Texas Tech 4-star running back commit SaRod Baker , not shaking hands with Raiders’ players and the latter took that personally. All St. Thomas Aquinas did was scored 38 unanswered points as they took a 38-0 lead into intermission and most of the second half was played under a running clock. Ouch. Basha and Chandler (Ariz.) opened their season in front of a national audience, in primetime on ESPN. Once again, the Bears had the Wolves number, outlasting Chandler, 37-26, in a contest full of game-changing takeaways that allowed Basha to finally put them away. ACC, Big Ten, Big 12 and SEC commits dotted the field and multiple Navy All-American’s and Polynesian Bowl selections were in action. But it was a rising 2028 playing his first game in almost two years who stole the show, while several of the FCS commits in the game made their own big impression. Rivals Offensive Player of the Game: WR Makai Nelson , 2028 All offseason, we’ve extolled the virtues of Nelson, who shined at every camp and 7v7 tournament we saw him. What he lacked, however, was film. He started his prep career at Chandler then transferred to Mountain Pointe last year, but was forced to sit out the season. Cleared to play this year at Basha, he made his old school pay, with two touchdown receptions and over 100 yards receiving. He set up Basha’s first score with a 47-yard catch to put them inside the red zone. He then had a 24-yard touchdown as the first half expired to give the Bears momentum going in to the half. That, of course, came after he had an 80-yard punt return for a touchdown negated by a penalty. Nelson had offers in the teens, based largely off in-person evals and camps, but this game should see his recruitment skyrocket. Rivals Defensive Player of the Game: LB Marc Duerson , 2027 Duerson was on the Rivals’ All-West FCS Commit Team earlier this month after averaging nearly 10 tackles a game for the Bears a year ago ahead of his commitment to Northern Arizona. He showed no signs of rust whatsoever, with a number of big hits in the game, including three forced fumbles, none bigger than his hit on Jai Jones that Tre Kennard scooped and scored to give the Bears a 27-20 lead they would never relinquish. Mencl finished 27-for-47 for 334 yards and four touchdowns against the two picks and also extended plays with his feet, rushing for 35 yards on seven carries. He took a big hit in the third quarter and went out for a series, but came back and got the Wolves back to within a point. – Sire Stewart , OT, 2027 – The Utah pledge anchored the Wolves offensive line that had to go up against an FBS-across-the-line defense all night, and a lot of depth, and looks like he’s taken a big jump from his junior year as he’s added more strength from a season ago. – Jude Jones , DL, 2027 – The Penn commit has been overshadowed on his own team but he was a bright spot in their defensive line play, getting to the quarterback twice for sacks among his three tackles. Jake Hildebrand Basha – Jake Rogers , QB, 2027 – The Rivals All-West FCS Commit quarterback, who is committed to Princeton, has still yet to lose a start since taking over for Brodie Vehrs last season when Vehrs was injured. His throw to Nelson was followed by a touchdown pass to Jaden Baldwin to tie the game and then his pass as time expired in the first half, again to Nelson, swung momentum the Bears way. While he did have a pick, he finished with 209 yards and three touchdown passes on 21-of-33 passing. – Jake Hildebrand , OT, 2027 – The No. 1 lineman in the state, committed to Arizona State , added a bunch of weight and strength in the offseason, and didn’t sacrifice any agility and looked every bit the best lineman in the state. – Jayden Jamerson , CB, 2029 – We’ve been saying that, like with Nelson, all Jamerson needed was more film – he was behind a loaded secondary a year ago, but he drew Jai Jones in the game and won that battle and he will absolutely be in the discussion for the top prospect in the state in his class when it’s all said and done. He’s physical, he can run, he can cover and he plays the game with an edge that is only going to grow. – Geremiah Grimes , CB, 2027 – Speaking of players overshadowed, it was easy for Grimes to get lost in the shuffle, but after winning DB MVP honors at the Under Armour Next Camp in Phoenix, he came in to this season as one to watch with an opportunity as a starter. Like Duerson, he is headed to Northern Arizona . And while Duerson forced the fumbles, Wilson had his takeaway come via the air, with the other pick of Mencl. – Landen Wade , EDGE, 2028 – One of the premier prospects in the West in his class, Wade showed his quickness and backside pursuit throughout the night, and he had the hit that initially knocked Mencl out. – Noah Roberts , RB, 2027 – The Texas pledge finally looked

articles.title: A 12TB Steam “teraleak” spills more than a decade of lost PC gaming history
articles.summary: Cut content from Portal 2, hints of Half Life 2: Episode 3, and so much more.
articles._body: Here at Ars, we're intimately familiar with data leaks surrounding Valve's games , hardware , and the workings of Steam itself . But nothing could have prepared us for this weekend's "terarelease" encompassing more than 12TB of content related to seemingly every title available on Steam between 2003 to 2013. What's being sold as an "as-complete-as-possible ... content server dump" of Steam's defunct "Steam2" server architecture from that time period is now circulating around via a BitTorrent tracker that Valve seems unlikely to ever completely purge from the Internet. The massive collection includes thousands of "depots" representing what seems to be every version of every game uploaded to those old Steam2 servers. That includes public release builds, of course, but in many cases also covers previously unseen pre-release, prototype, and playtest versions of popular titles published by Valve and third-party Steam publishers. Steam2: Electric Boogaloo The reason this weekend's leaked content cuts off abruptly in 2013 is because that's when Valve updated its content distribution system from "Steam2" to the current SteamPipe system . In moving from a proprietary file distribution format to standard HTTP file trees, the new system removed various update approval bottlenecks on Valve's end and streamlined update and patch downloads so they only reflected file differentials. articles.summary: BTS was the first K-pop act to top the all-genre chart; BLACKPINK was the first female K-pop act to do so.
articles._body: ENHYPHEN ’s THE SIN: BLISS puts K-pop back in a familiar spot — No. 1 on the all-genre Billboard 200 chart. The EP is the 26th album or EP by a K-pop act to reach No. 1 on Billboard’s flagship albums chart in just over eight years. The first was BTS ’ Love Yourself: Tear in June 2018. Stray Kids has amassed nine No. 1 titles on the Billboard 200, which puts them out front among K-pop acts. BTS is second, with seven No. 1 titles. ATEEZ is next in line with three No. 1s. SuperM , BLACKPINK , TOMORROW X TOGETHER , NewJeans , TWICE and ENHYPHEN have all notched one No. 1 to date. In addition, one multi-artist K-pop soundtrack, KPop Demon Hunters , has reached No. 1. Related ENHYPEN Scores First No. 1 Album on Billboard 200 With ‘THE SIN : BLISS’ BLACKPINK was the first female K-pop act to land a No. 1 album on the Billboard 200. They scored with Born Pink in 2022. They were followed by NewJeans and TWICE. K-pop groups tend to be large ensembles. TWICE has nine members, one more than Stray Kids and ATEEZ. Another jam-packed slate is on deck as teams continue their quests for a state title. Below are the top 25 Arizona high school football teams,  according  to the Massey Ratings , as of Aug. 30. 1. Liberty (1-0) The Lions are in search of their third Open Division title in the last four years and started the 2026 off with a bang in a surprising blowout of Mesa, 58-18. Sophomore quarterback Jason Haines finished 18-of-27 for 403 yards and threw four touchdown passes while Carter Rothe was on the receiving end of four of those for 138 yards and a touchdown. Junior linebacker Brecken Garday was all over the field, with 13 tackles and one for loss in the win. Next up is a home contest with Utah’s No. 1 ranked team Corner Canyon, in a game that Liberty lost a year ago. 2. Basha (1-0) The Bears took on Chandler in a rematch of last year’s Open Division title game, and just like in Mountain America Stadium nine months ago, won, albeit this one was much closer, with the Bears using second-half takeaways to take what was a 1-point game into a double-digit win. Princeton quarterback commit Jake Rogers finished 21-for-33 for 209 yards and three touchdowns to just one pick, including a 24-yard touchdown as the first half expired to 2028 receiver Makai Nelson , one of Nelson’s two touchdowns on the night. Northern Arizona linebacker commit Marc Duerson was a machine for the Bears, forcing three Chandler fumbles in the win. They go on the road to play Orange (Calif.) Lutheran, the No. 9 team in California. 3. Hamilton (1-0) The Huskies were without star Roye Oliver , the USC-bound receiver and reining state player of the year, but they didn’t need the offense to churn when the defense was just stout and the special teams scored touchdowns. Kacey Allen had a pick-six in the win. They host the No. 3 team in Nevada, Arbor View, on Friday. 4. Centennial (1-0) Junior quarterback Titus Hill was efficient throughout the night, going 13-for-16 for 186 yards and threw three touchdown passes, all to his twin brother, Torrin Hill , the junior tight end catching seven passes for 147 yards and a trio of touchdowns. Senior running back Damonte Drake rushed for 104 yards on 10 carries and ran in a touchdown in the win. Next up for the Coyotes is a road trip to Southern California to take on Servite, the No. 8 team in California. 5. Chandler (0-1) The Wolves had an opening drive to take an early lead over Basha and battled the Bears throughout, cutting the lead to one in the fourth quarter. But a blocked PAT and too many turnovers made getting over the hump too tall a task and they fell by 11 to the Bears in a rematch of the state title game. Oregon-bound Will Mencl was 27-for-47 for 334 yards and four touchdowns but threw two picks. Mountain View rolled to a 63-0 win in the interstate matchup, allowing just under 200 yards in total offense in the blanking. Junior quarterback Brayden Merwin finished 11-for-14 for 211 yards and threw three touchdown passes while rushing for 45 yards and a score. TJ Gaines and Slade Foster each had a pair of sacks in the shutout. Next for the Toros is Pinnacle, the No. 11 team in Arizona. 7. Red Mountain (1-0) In what may have been the most entertaining game of the weekend, Red Mountain escaped with a 1-point win over defending 6A state champion Casteel in a 35-34. Junior Kaeden Weaver , who moved to Arizona from Washington, did a little bit of everything for the Mountain Lions, throwing a 79-yard touchdown pass to Airreon Windom , while catching three passes for 154 yards and a touchdown. Caleb Joe ran for a touchdown and threw two of them in the win. They face Westwood HS this Friday. 8. Desert Mountain (1-0) The reigning 5A state champions had no problem with former 5A power Saguaro, cruising to a 62-0 win over the Sabercats to begin their title defense. Junior running back Easton Conner reached paydirt four times on five carries, finishing with 95 yards rushing and the four scores. They’ll face No. 35 Arizona College Prep this weekend. 9. Freshman receiver Karter Chamblin was a bright spot in his prep debut, with a team high four catches for 46 yards while Julian Ferrari had a touchdown reception from Stewart. articles.title: Battle for Hormuz: U.S. forces take first military action against Iran in a month, striking rocket launchers being used to deploy sea mines
articles.summary: The U.S. military last week completed clearing sea mines from the strait’s international shipping routes.
articles._body: U.S. forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on the  Strait of Hormuz  in the first military action in a month on Sunday, according to a U.S. official, breaking a lull in fighting during an intermittent war that has lasted more than six months. Forces with the Revolutionary Guard Corps were observed preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into the strait, according to the official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to detail sensitive military movements. The U.S. military last week completed clearing sea mines from the strait’s international shipping routes. Semiofficial news outlets in Iran reported sounds of explosions near Larak island on the strait. The Guard in a statement carried by Iran’s state broadcaster noted “the martyrdom and injury of several of our fighters and compatriots.” The statement said the attack will “result in punishment of the aggressor.” The fighting comes just days after the Trump administration said it would turn its focus to  increasing economic pressure  — rather than military action — to try to end its war with Iran. The shifting strategy centers on threats to punish any country or entity that continues to  conduct business with Tehran . The turn to using sanctions as the cudgel of choice comes as the administration weighs diminished munitions stockpiles after months of war, sparking concerns that the prolonged conflict could  undermine U.S. military readiness in other parts of the globe. As the conflict grinds on, Trump’s talk of finding a quick end to the war also appears to be fading. He stressed last week that he’s “not in a hurry” to get Iran back to the negotiating table , and he continues making the case that the Islamic Republic’s leadership is on the ropes. Trump has consistently emphasized that the U.S. and Israel campaign  has been devastating  for Iran’s navy and air force. Iranian officials have said the  country has suffered  $270 billion in direct and indirect damage. Israeli military strikes in the first weeks of the war wiped out much of the theocratic government’s leadership structure. But Iran has found leverage through its own strikes in the critical Strait of Hormuz where relatively few vessels carrying oil and liquefied natural gas are risking passage. Iran still has enough drones and missiles to fire at vessels transiting the vital energy waterway, through which 20% of the world’s oil normally flows, effectively controlling much of the traffic in the strait. Trump has repeatedly declared that the “Strait of Hormuz is open,” saying 24 vessels passed through last week. But that’s a fraction of the roughly 130 vessels that passed through the vital waterway daily before the war began. Earlier on Sunday, a multinational coalition overseen by the U.S. Navy said commercial traffic through the strait remained at “reduced levels.” And a monitoring agency run by the British military said an unknown projectile struck a tanker ship on Saturday north of Khasab, Oman, in the strait. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Organization said the ship had been moving inbound and no casualties or environmental impact had been reported. It cited unspecified military authorities. There was no immediate claim of responsibility. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: 49ers add interior OL depth immediately after Rams’ Aaron Donald move
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers moved swiftly to prepare for Aaron Donald’s return to the Los Angeles Rams. General manager John Lynch made a call to the Houston Texans to receive some interior offensive lineman help. Now Jarrett Patterson has come on board. NFL insider for The Ringer and Netflix S
articles._body: The San Francisco 49ers moved swiftly to prepare for Aaron Donald’s return to the Los Angeles Rams . General manager John Lynch made a call to the Houston Texans to receive some interior offensive lineman help. Now Jarrett Patterson has come on board. NFL insider for The Ringer and Netflix Sports Tom Pelissero revealed the trade got completed Sunday . Once again, SF pulls this off while the rival Rams celebrate Donald’s retirement coming to a brief end. The longtime 49ers thorn Donald signed for only one-year and $20 million. He launched speculation across the league for a comeback attempt back in June, when LA traded Jared Verse and draft picks to the Cleveland Browns for All-Pro edge rusher Myles Garrett. Donald sparked rumors of wanting to play alongside the reigning 2025 NFL Defensive Player of the Year before summer officially started. So now Donald will join the Rams’ 53-man roster, making him set to face the 49ers on Sept. 10 in Melbourne, Australia. But little did the Rams know, the 49ers had a counterattack in place through adding Patterson. Lynch and head coach Kyle Shanahan gain a versatile veteran who has played center and guard. He allowed zero sacks last season while blocking for Texans Pro Bowl quarterback CJ Stroud. Patterson has started in 21 total games throughout his career, handing SF assurance that it can rely on the veteran to withstand Donald and the Rams’ defensive line if the 49ers call upon him. Of course perennial Pro Bowler Trent Williams leads the SF front line. But depth arrives before that highly-anticipated season opening showdown in the Land Down Under. As the Chargers finalize their 53-man roster, the latest move on offensive guard Branson Taylor
articles._body: With the Los Angeles Chargers preparing for the 2026 season , which is right around the corner, the team’s latest move makes this positional battle clear as to who the winner is to start the year. As t he Chargers finalize their 53-man roster, the latest move on offensive guard Branson Taylor makes the victor of the starting guard competition all too clear. According to insider Ian Rapoport of The NFL Network, Los Angeles is putting Taylor on the injured reserve (IR) “ with a designated for return designation.” He would add that Kayode Awosika is now “in line” to start as the team’s offensive guard. “The Chargers are putting G Branson Taylor on IR with a designated-for-return designation, source said. Sounds like Kayode Awosika is in line to start at guard,” Rapoport wrote on X, formerly Twitter. Taylor would sustain an upper-body injury in the Chargers’ second preseason game against the San Francisco 49ers, which ended in a 41-17 loss. While Taylor’s injury puts Awosika in line to start, there is a case to be made that he was already heading down the path of being Los Angeles’ starting offensive guard. Take what Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said last Sunday, even expressing that Awosika is the “leader right now.” “Kayode Awosika is right there. He’s the leader right now,” Harbaugh said, according to The Chargers Wire. At any rate, it remains to be seen when Taylor will come back to the team and help with Los Angeles’ offensive line depth, as there’s no denying that the unit will be critical to help protect star quarterback Justin Herbert. The Chargers open the regular season with a Week 1 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, Sept. 13, as a new offense looks to be displayed under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. articles._body: Here’s an early look at Purdue’s first opponent of the 2026 season: the Indiana State Sycamores : Date/Time: Friday, September 4, 7 p.m. EDT Location: Ross-Ade Stadium Surface: Bermuda Grass Capacity: 61,441 (tickets) Weather:  High of 88, low of 67 with partly cloudy skies and minimal wind Purdue schedule  |  Purdue roster  | Indiana State schedule  |  Indiana State roster Series notes : Purdue enters this matchup with a 7-0 all-time record in the in-state series. Friday’s contest will mark the sixth meeting between the two since 2006. In the last five meetings, Purdue averages a 32-point margin of victory. This will serve as Barry Odom’s first meeting with Indiana State, but Sycamores head coach Curt Mallory led Indiana State in its trips to Purdue in 2022 and 2024. Mallory’s teams still remain scoreless against Purdue, losing 56-0 in 2022 and 49-0 in 2024. TV: BTN Early line: Purdue -35.5, O/U 56.5 STORYLINES TO WATCH Year two begins Odom begins his second season at the helm, looking to turn the page following a tough debut season. After a 2-0 start, Purdue dropped its final 10 contests to finish 2-10. Purdue gets a somewhat more favorable schedule this year, avoiding four of the top five teams in the unofficial Big Ten preseason media poll. Preseason odds in Las Vegas project Purdue with an over/under win total of 3.5. Previous Purdue coaches often struggle to make a big improvement from year one to year two. Darrell Hazell was the last Boilermaker boss to see growth, winning one game in 2013 and three games in 2014. Before Hazell, Jim Young was the last coach to see a multi-game improvement in his second season. Continuing historical trends? Since the NCAA split Division I football into subdivisions in 1978, Purdue holds a perfect record against I-AA/FCS competition (15-0). Eight of the 18 Big Ten squads cannot say the same. Since the split, Purdue has played Indiana State more than any other FCS opponent. The majority of the matchups between the Boilermakers and Sycamores resulted in a blowout. Purdue will look to continue that trend on Friday night. Not *their* first game While Purdue opens the 2026 season on Friday, the Sycamores already have a game under their belt. Indiana State dropped a 23-21 affair in Terre Haute on Saturday evening against Southeast Missouri. After falling behind 17-7, Indiana State rallied to take a 21-20 lead, but a late field goal lifted SEMO to the victory. Quarterback Elijah Owens threw for 288 yards, but the Sycamore run game struggled. Indiana State took the field as a 2.5-point favorite in the ballgame. Familiar faces On the Purdue side of things, offensive tackle Jude McCoskey came to West Lafayette from Indiana State before the 2025 season. He spent two years as a starter on the Sycamore offensive line, including the 2024 matchup against Purdue at left tackle. McCoskey, a Terre Haute native, projects to start at right tackle for Purdue on Friday night. For Indiana State, former Purdue quarterback Brady Allen is listed as the backup quarterback on the depth chart. He earned Indiana Mr. Football honors as a senior at Gibson Southern HS in 2021 and signed with Purdue. After spending his freshman season with the Boilermakers, he transferred to Louisville, where he played sparingly over the past three years.

articles.title: Aaron Donald return makes 2026 officially Super Bowl or bust for Rams
articles.summary: Star player Aaron Donald has officially ended months of speculation about a potential comeback, agreeing to a one-year, $20 million deal to return to the Los Angeles Rams after more than two years away from the NFL. The three-time Defensive Player of the Year had already sparked expectations with
articles._body: Star player Aaron Donald has officially ended months of speculation about a potential comeback , agreeing to a one-year, $20 million deal to return to the Los Angeles Rams after more than two years away from the NFL. The three-time Defensive Player of the Year had already sparked expectations with multiple workouts at the team facility. His decision now places him alongside Myles Garrett on a defensive front that appears formidable on paper. There was already significant pressure on Los Angeles before Donald reversed his retirement decision, particularly after acquiring Garrett earlier in the offseason. Bringing back one of the greatest defensive players in NFL history changes the expectations dramatically, and the Rams are no longer merely a talented contender hoping to make a deep postseason run because they have constructed a roster whose success will ultimately be judged by whether they can win the Super Bowl. While this may seem unfair in a league where one poor playoff performance can derail an entire season, Los Angeles has willingly embraced these expectations by aggressively prioritizing the present. Trading for Garrett was a move typically made by a franchise that believes its championship window is currently open, and adding Donald for another season reinforces that philosophy. This is clearly not a move aimed at building for 2028 or 2029. Donald is 35 years old and has not played an NFL game since the 2023 season, making it unreasonable to expect him to immediately return to his prime form, but this misses the essence of his comeback. The Rams do not necessarily need Donald to perform at the level where he regularly overwhelmed double teams and competed for Defensive Player of the Year awards because they need him to be dangerous enough that opposing offenses cannot focus all their protection adjustments on Garrett, and even a less dominant version of Donald could significantly change how teams strategize against the Rams. Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images The combination of Garrett and Donald creates a daunting challenge for opponents, as Garrett already demands extraordinary attention, while Donald has built his career on defeating such attention. Together, they present a dilemma for offenses because if teams leave either player isolated too often, the quarterback could face relentless pressure, but continuously committing extra protection to both players would make things easier for everyone else on the Rams’ defense. The larger issue for Los Angeles is that, following Donald’s return, there are almost no acceptable excuses if the season ends quietly. Donald did not come out of retirement just to help the Rams secure a wild-card spot, and the organization did not invest $20 million in a franchise legend for merely another veteran presence in the locker room. His comeback signifies that both the Rams and Donald believe there is something substantial left to pursue, and with the addition of Garrett, that goal can only be described as chasing another Lombardi Trophy. There are legitimate risks involved, particularly regarding how Donald’s body will respond after such a long absence from competitive football. Being physically fit is very different from enduring NFL contact for four quarters and then repeating that week after week, and Los Angeles will need to manage his workload intelligently, especially early in the season, rather than letting nostalgia convince the coaching staff that the old Donald should immediately play every significant defensive snap. Despite this uncertainty, the potential rewards are too great to treat this like an ordinary veteran signing, and coach Sean McVay now has a defensive weapon few coaches could realistically expect to add so close to Week 1. Donald also understands the organization, knows McVay’s standards, and carries enough institutional credibility that his return should require much less adjustment than a typical late-summer acquisition. The Rams have effectively pushed all their chips to the center of the table, first by bringing Garrett to Los Angeles, and now by convincing Donald to postpone retirement. Once a team assembles this level of talent for a single championship run, merely being competitive is no longer sufficient. Winning the division would be nice, another playoff appearance would be respectable, and reaching the NFC Championship Game would typically qualify as a successful season, but 2026 ceased to be an ordinary year the moment Donald signed his contract. For these Rams, the destination must now be the Super Bowl, and anything significantly less than that will feel like a missed opportunity they may never recreate. articles.title: Buccaneers’ Jalon Daniels gets Baker Mayfield stamp of approval after winning QB2 job
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers seem to have found something special at quarterback. Tampa Bay is naming rookie Jalon Daniels from Kansas as the team’s no. 2 quarterback. Buccaneers starter Baker Mayfield is tipping his cap to his new teammate. “I’m proud of Jalon. I thought he took tremendous ste
articles._body: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers seem to have found something special at quarterback. Tampa Bay is naming rookie Jalon Daniels from Kansas as the team’s no. 2 quarterback . Buccaneers starter Baker Mayfield is tipping his cap to his new teammate. “I’m proud of Jalon. I thought he took tremendous steps from the first time I met him in the offseason to now. Played his tail off, worked hard, worked on some of the things the coaches wanted to get done out of him, for him to progress with…yeah, I’m excited for him,” Mayfield said, per ESPN. Baker Mayfield on Jalon Daniels now being the No. 2 quarterback: “I’m proud of Jalon. I thought he took tremendous steps from the first time I met him in the offseason to now. Played his tail off, worked hard, worked on some of the things the coaches wanted to get done out of… pic.twitter.com/cL04gUXcVq — JennaLaineESPN (@JennaLaineESPN) August 30, 2026 Daniels went undrafted in the 2026 NFL Draft, after starting many games at Kansas. He helped turn the Jayhawks into a competitive football program, after spending years in the cellar of the Big 12 conference. He is fitting right in at Tampa Bay. “[Daniels] has shown a lot. He’s shown a lot,” Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said after the team’s preseason finale against the Jacksonville Jaguars, per ESPN. “We’re going to go back and evaluate the film.” It isn’t all peaches and cream for Daniels though. Daniels struggled in the preseason game against Jacksonville. He completed just eight passes, and lost a fumble. “It’s not really the completions,” Bowles said. “It’s the overall operation to make sure he’s fine with that, and then we’ll come back and look at the film because it wasn’t very good offensively tonight.” In his college career, Daniels threw for more than 9,000 passing yards. He completed 67 touchdown passes, while also establishing himself as a dual-threat quarterback. He rushed for 23 touchdowns at Kansas. Time will tell if Daniels can add some more spark to this Buccaneers offense , during the regular season. Tampa Bay finished the 2025 NFL season with a 8-9 record. Tampa Bay opens the 2026 season with a game against the Cincinnati Bengals, on September 13. articles.title: NBA sets record straight on LeBron James’ free agency impacting schedule release
articles.summary: LeBron James’ free agency saga dragged into late July, long past the usual time frame when players agree to free agent deals, and there was growing sentiment that the NBA was starting to get impatient due to the league needing to finalize the 2026-27 schedule release. Even at the ripe old age of
articles._body: LeBron James’ free agency saga dragged into late July, long past the usual time frame when players agree to free agent deals, and there was growing sentiment that the NBA was starting to get impatient due to the league needing to finalize the 2026-27 schedule release. Even at the ripe old age of 41-years-old, LeBron James still plays a major factor when it comes to the NBA’s schedule and potential nationally televised games. With big games such as James’ return to Los Angeles to face off against the Lakers , NBA head of basketball strategy and growth Evan Wasch essentially confirmed that LeBron James’ drawn-out free agency did play a factor in the league delaying the schedule release, as per Jeff Zillgitt of NBA.com. “There is obviously a track record of superstars changing teams in the offseason, and that impacting the schedule … The difference here was just the timing. To my recollection, there had not been an instance of a superstar changing teams, call it in late July,” Wasch said. “It absolutely does drive the overall scheduling picture. And that was the complication while waiting for his decision, knowing what some of those foundational pieces of the schedule were going to look like.” Among the chief scheduling concerns were planning for a potential West Coast road trip when James makes his return to face off against the Lakers. That game will occur on Christmas Day this season, the beginning of a four game West Coast trip with games against the LA Clippers, Sacramento Kings and Phoenix Suns. James and the 76ers will also appear on opening night against the defending champion New York Knicks. articles.title: Insider gives sneak peek into Rams’ Aaron Donald usage that won’t be ‘anywhere near’ his prime
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams finally signed Aaron Donald to a one-year $20 million contract. It’s a move that gives L.A. arguably the best defensive line in the league. But what kind of role will Donald play after sitting out for the past two seasons? Insider James Palmer of “NFL on PrimeR
articles._body: The Los Angeles Rams finally signed Aaron Donald to a one-year $20 million contract. It’s a move that gives L.A. arguably the best defensive line in the league. But what kind of role will Donald play after sitting out for the past two seasons? Insider James Palmer of “NFL on Prime” broke down the 35-year-old’s usage in the last three years he played (2021, 2022, 2023). There was a notable drop in usage in the back end of Donald’s career. He claims that after coming out of retirement, head coach Sean McVay is not going to play Aaron Donald nearly as often as he used to. It sounds like Donald will have specific packages while playing on crucial downs. “In Aaron Donald’s last 3 seasons for the Rams, he played 90%, 89%, and 81% of the snaps on defense,” Palmer said. “He’s not going to play anywhere near that. He knows it, and so do the Rams. They have plenty of depth and have been working on packages, formations, and ways to deploy him for some time, to my understanding.” That means the Rams will likely rotate the defensive line often. The interior will feature Donald, Poona Ford, Kobie Turner, and Braden Fiske. Meanwhile, Tyler Davis and Ty Hamilton are the likely backups. Myles Garrett and Byron Young are listed as the starting edge rushers, with Desjuan Johnson and Josaiah Stewart rotating off the bench. Aaron Donald is a future Hall of Famer going into the 11th season of his career. He enters the 2026-27 campaign as a three-time Defensive Player of the Year, eight-time First-Team All-Pro, 10-time Pro Bowler, 2014 Defensive Rookie of the Year, and Super Bowl winner. He’ll aim to secure his second ring this year after returning to the Rams. articles.title: USC issues statement in response to low attendance vs. San Jose State
articles.summary: USC earned a 42-26 victory over San Jose State in its season opener on Saturday, but the bigger discussion was the lack of attendance at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. In a statement to USA Today, USC responded to fans not showing up for the Week 0 contest. “We understand the factors that impa
articles._body: USC earned a 42-26 victory over San Jose State in its season opener on Saturday, but the bigger discussion was the lack of attendance at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. In a statement to USA Today , USC responded to fans not showing up for the Week 0 contest. “We understand the factors that impacted Saturday’s attendance,” USC said, per Jordan Mendoza of USA Today . “We have high expectations and a premier home schedule this season, and we know the competitive advantage an electric Coliseum atmosphere can provide our program. We thank our fans who showed up Saturday and look forward to seeing increased attendance the rest of the season.” [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] The official attendance was 51,144, the lowest under Trojans head coach Lincoln Riley and the lowest since 2018. Mendoza pointed out that several factors came into play as to why USC didn’t have a big turnout, including the weather. The U.S. National Weather Service issued an extreme heat advisory in the Los Angeles area on Saturday. USC will host Oregon and Ohio State this season When the game kicked off at noon local time, the temperature was 94 degrees with a real feel temperature of 104, per AccuWeather. But that didn’t stop social media from taking aim at the Trojans for their fans’ lack of support. Another reason could have been the opponent USC faced in the opener. San Jose State is a Group of Six School that finished 3-9 last year. Trojan fans who didn’t attend the game figured USC would win by double digits, and that was the case. As the school mentioned, attendance should improve as the season rolls on. On Sept. 26, the Trojans will have a huge home contest against Oregon . Both teams will likely enter the game undefeated, and a win would give that team a leg up in the Big Ten Championship and College Football Playoff race. On Halloween, USC will have another big home game. The Trojans will host Ohio State, a team that is looking to win its second national title in three seasons. That will likely be a primetime game with the entire country watching.

articles.title: Josh Jacobs Put on Paid Leave by NFL
articles.summary: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect
articles._body: The NFL put Packers running back Josh Jacobs on paid administrative leave Sunday via placement on the commissioner’s exempt list, rendering him ineligible to play while he faces misdemeanor charges related to alleged domestic abuse. The league’s decision came as NFL teams faced a 6 p.m. ET deadline Sunday to reduce their rosters to 53 players for the season. On Saturday, the NFL said it would place Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold on the exempt list once his contract was filed with the league office. Jacobs faces misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property. The Brown County (Wis.) District Attorney’s Office announced the charges Thursday after Jacobs was arrested in May on initial charges related to domestic abuse, including felony strangulation and suffocation. “Josh Jacobs has been placed on the Commissioner’s Exempt List, which is an administrative procedure used by the NFL while a matter is being reviewed,” Jacobs’s attorneys David Z. Chesnoff, Richard A. Schonfeld, and Clarence F. Duchac III said in a written statement Sunday provided to Front Office Sports . “It is not a final determination. Josh respects the NFL process, the Packers, and his Coaches and Teammates. He looks forward to his return to the team and the NFL.” He will be paid his salary while on the exempt list but cannot practice with the Packers or attend games. The NFL’s personal conduct policy for players says that “upon request and with the club’s permission,” a player on the exempt list “may be present at the club’s facility on a reasonable basis for meetings, individual workouts, therapy and rehabilitation, and other permitted non-football activities.” Jacobs and the NFL Players Association have three days after Jacobs is formally notified of his placement on the list to appeal the league’s decision. The conduct policy says that a player’s paid leave will “generally last” until a disciplinary ruling is made on a prospective fine or unpaid suspension. That usually comes after the player’s criminal case is completed. Any games that a player misses while on paid leave are ultimately credited toward a possible unpaid suspension, with the player returning pay for the appropriate number of games. The conduct policy says that paid leave may be used when a player is charged with a felony or violent crime, when an investigation leads the commissioner to believe the policy may have been violated in that manner, or when a violent crime has been alleged but further investigation is required. Jacobs is entering the third season of a four-year, $48 million contract with the Packers. He is a three-time Pro Bowl selection over seven NFL seasons with the Raiders and Packers and ran for 929 yards and 13 touchdowns last season. The Packers traded for a running back, the Steelers’ Kaleb Johnson, earlier Sunday. The Seahawks signed Arnold on Saturday after previously agreeing to contract terms with him and after he’d been released by the Lions. Arnold was arrested in Tampa and faces felony charges related to a kidnapping and robbery in February. He has denied the allegations through his representatives. articles.title: Xavier Lewis Wreaks Havoc as ‘All-Down Guy’ in UNC’s Season-Opener
articles.summary: Sophomore defensive lineman Xavier Lewis finished with seven tackles, including 4.5 for loss, on his way to being named the MVP of the Aer Lingus Classic.
articles._body: DUBLIN — Looking along North Carolina’s defensive line, it would be easy for Xavier Lewis to get lost in the shuffle. Standing at 6 feet and 260 pounds, Lewis — who originally signed with Austin Peay before taking a preferred walk-on spot at UNC — may not carry the size or accolades of Melkart Abou Jaoude , who led the ACC in sacks a season ago, or Leroy Jackson , who earned Second-Team Freshman All-America honors from The Athletic in 2025. But Saturday night at Aviva Stadium, Lewis made sure he wouldn’t be overlooked. The sophomore announced his presence in dominant fashion, wreaking havoc in the Horned Frogs’ backfield throughout North Carolina’s season-opening win over TCU. Lewis finished with seven tackles — third among all Tar Heels — while adding two sacks and 4.5 tackles for loss on his way to being named MVP of the Aer Lingus Classic. “For me, my get-off,” Lewis said when asked what worked for him against TCU. “Our coaches put together a great game plan against TCU, so we really stuck with it and it was able to be good for me.” And in a game that turned into a defensive rock fight, it was Lewis’ second tackle for loss that helped set up the two points that ultimately decided Saturday’s contest. With the game deadlocked at 10 and 2:31 remaining in the first half, Lewis burst untouched through the left side of the Horned Frogs’ offensive line on second-and-5. He nearly took the handoff from TCU quarterback Jaden Craig before planting Jeremy Payne in the grass, turning what could have been a manageable third down into third-and-9 — one TCU could not convert. On the ensuing fourth down, the Horned Frogs’ punting unit gifted the Tar Heels a 12-10 lead they would never relinquish. That wasn’t the only big play Lewis made on a night when he seemingly found himself in the right spot at every turn. On UNC’s first fourth-down stand in the red zone during the second half, the Raleigh (N.C.) Rolesville High product was one of the first Tar Heels through the line, joining Isaiah Johnson in meeting Payne in the backfield and keeping TCU from cutting into the Tar Heels’ lead — or taking one of its own. “When it’s fourth-and-1 or something like that, we know what they’re doing and they know what we’re doing,” Lewis said of the play. “So it’s just beat them off the ball and make a play.” Then, on Carolina’s second red-zone stand of the half, Lewis made an impact that won’t show up in the box score. He was the closest Tar Heel in pursuit of Craig, applying the pressure that forced the TCU quarterback into an errant fourth-down throw intended for Jeremy Scott. Despite the numbers attached to his performance, Lewis was quick to credit those around him for helping make it possible. His second sack of the night came on a well-executed stunt with Trey Giddens , who occupied two TCU offensive linemen and opened a path for Lewis to get to Craig. “It was a great team effort from the defensive line,” Lewis said. “Guys like Leroy Jackson, Isaiah Johnson, Trey Giddens, they also had a great game as well. It wasn’t just me, I had a little bit to do with it but they helped me out a lot through their performance as well.” Lewis appeared in all 12 games as a freshman in 2025, finishing with eight tackles. But despite playing in every game, his role was largely limited to rushing the passer, with 130 of his 167 snaps coming against the pass. “Last year was just a start for me, just to get out on the field,” Lewis said. “I was a third down, passing, situational guy last year. (This year I was) able to come out here and have the staff put their trust in me to play on all downs and become an all-down guy.” Saturday night in Dublin offered a glimpse of just how much that role has expanded. Making his first career start, Lewis played 53 of UNC’s 71 defensive snaps, including 28 against the run, and proved capable of making an impact regardless of the situation. According to Pro Football Focus, he was the nation’s highest graded defender in Week 0 with an 88.2 overall mark, including an 89.2 run-defense grade and a 69.2 pass-rush grade. “What I’ve learned is to just attack more, just be more aggressive,” Lewis said. “I didn’t really get a lot of run in short yardage snaps last year, so like I said, the coaching staff put their trust in me for that and I was able to attack their line.”

articles.title: Chargers quarterback Trey Lance beats out DJ Uiagalelei as Justin Herbert’s backup
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers already have an established quarterback as the starter, with Justin Herbert. Herbert could be primed for an MVP-level season, which could decide the fate of the Chargers in 2026. Regardless, every team needs a quality backup quarterback in case the top man goes down. Now,
articles._body: The Los Angeles Chargers already have an established quarterback as the starter, with Justin Herbert. Herbert could be primed for an MVP-level season , which could decide the fate of the Chargers in 2026. Regardless, every team needs a quality backup quarterback in case the top man goes down. Now, the Chargers have decided on who will be backing up Herbert to start the 2026 campaign, per Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports. Trey Lance will be the backup quarterback after beating out DJ Uiagalelei for the job. Uiagalelei will be waived, according to CBS Sports. Uiagalelei was the better quarterback in the final preseason game. Lance played two possessions and did not complete a pass. Meanwhile, Uiagalelei was 11 for 18 for 141 yards in his extended time. Still, the team has decided to move forward with Lance. Lance was the third overall selection of the San Francisco 49ers in the 2021 NFL Draft. He was traded ahead of the 2024 season to the Dallas Cowboys, sitting him behind Dak Prescott. He signed a one-year deal with the Chargers ahead of the 2025 season and was the backup to Herbert, starting the final regular-season game of the year. Overall, he has played in 16 games and six starts in his career, passing for 1,289 yards and five touchdowns with five interceptions. Uiagalelei was undrafted out of Florida State in the 2025 NFL Draft. He was waived as part of the final roster cuts last summer, but signed back on as a member of the practice squad last season. He then signed a reserve/futures contract with the Chargers at the end of the season. Uiagalelei may return to the Chargers roster as a member of the practice squad. Bubba Wallace delivers verdict on NASCAR’s new Daytona package after ominous pre-race warning
articles.summary: Bubba Wallace weighs in on NASCAR’s new superspeedway package after its Daytona debut and reveals whether his pre-race concerns were justified.
articles._body: Ahead of Saturday night’s Coke Zero Sugar 400, Bubba Wallace was one of the most outspoken about the uncertainty of how the cars would race with NASCAR’s new superspeedway rules package . Ahead of the race, Wallace said: “I really hope it’s not a debacle, because it’s gonna look really bad that we didn’t get practice with something so drastic, if it is a debacle.” With no practice and now a full night of racing experience with the new package, Wallace gave his verdict on the changes.  Changes that NASCAR called just the first step in helping make superspeedway racing at Daytona and Talladega better.   Wallace weighs in on new speedway package For Wallace, who finished P20 , the rear spoiler reduction was noticeable.  He did feel that the fuel-saving tactics played out the same as with previous races at Daytona.  “It was okay,” said Wallace. “It was definitely a loss of a little bit of rear downforce; you could feel that. So you just kind of had to be easier with your inputs. “But it kind of played out the same, just saving fuel and riding around quarter percent throttle.” Asked how NASCAR could continue to remedy the mileage racing, Wallace offered to continue to alter stage lengths. Then again, he didn’t have an answer for whether lengthening them or shortening them was the answer.  “Yeah, I mean, I think that’s the only fix is messing with the lengths and which direction. “I have no idea.” The 23XI driver did see the difference in the ability to make runs. He also compared it to the Gen 6 car.  “I thought the runs could get a little bit bigger and you could make some passes. “It kind of felt like the Gen 6 car.” On to the Chase The Chase starts next week at Darlington.  Wallace finished the regular season in P14 of the 16-driver field, locking his spot in the Chase.  While the next running of Saturday night’s updated speedway package isn’t until November at Talladega, Wallace is excited about seeing what the changes will bring at another superspeedway.  “I’m excited for Talladega. I really take a lot of pride in trying to get better each and every speedway race. We just got to- I don’t know if it’s the right way to phrase it, but work backwards. “We fire off really good in the first stage, the first half of the second stage, and then we just kind of finish 20th tonight. Unfortunate circumstances, the way the cards fell. “This stuff is hard, putting yourself in the right spot on the racetrack, putting yourself in the right spot from the pit box and the strategy standpoint. “It’s all hard. There’s nothing easy about this. So we’ve just got to figure out how to be better than the rest.”

articles.title: ENHYPEN Scores First No. 1 Album on Billboard 200 With ‘THE SIN : BLISS’
articles.summary: Plus, Dolly Parton soars into the top five after her passing.
articles._body: ENHYPEN claims its first No. 1 album on the Billboard 200 chart as THE SIN : BLISS debuts atop the ranking (dated Sept. 5). The set earned 98,000 equivalent album units in the United States in its first week (ending Aug. 27), according to Luminate. THE SIN : BLISS marks ENHYPEN’s seventh top 10, all achieved since 2022. The act had previously gone as high as No. 2, twice, with THE SIN : VANISH in January and ROMANCE : UNTOLD in 2024.   Related ENHYPEN Drops Latest Installment in ‘THE SIN’ Series With ‘BLISS’: Stream It Now Here Are All the K-pop Albums That Have Topped the Billboard 200: Full List Forever No. 1: Dolly Parton, ‘9 to 5’ Also in the top 10, Dolly Parton , who died on Aug. 25, tallies her fourth top 10-charted album, as the greatest hits collection Ultimate Dolly Parton reenters the chart at No. 5. The Billboard 200 chart ranks the most popular albums of the week in the U.S. based on multi-metric consumption as measured in equivalent album units, compiled by Luminate. Units comprise album sales, track equivalent albums (TEA) and streaming equivalent albums (SEA). Each unit equals one album sale, or 10 individual tracks sold from an album, or 2,500 ad-supported or 1,000 paid/subscription on-demand official audio and video streams generated by songs from an album. The new Sept. 5, 2026-dated chart will be posted in full on  Billboard ‘s website on Sept. 1. For all chart news, follow @billboard and @billboardcharts on both X, formerly known as Twitter, and Instagram. Of THE SIN : BLISS ’ 98,000 first-week equivalent album units, album sales comprise 92,000 (it debuts at No. 1 on the Top Album Sales chart), SEA units comprise 6,000 (equaling 6.91 million on-demand official streams of the set’s songs) and TEA units comprise a negligible sum. THE SIN : BLISS ’ album sales were largely driven by its availability across more than 30 CD and vinyl variants (all containing collectible items such as photocards, stickers and posters, with some items randomized). Three former No. 1s follow ENHYPEN, as Ella Langley’s Dandelion rises 5-2 (70,000 equivalent album units, down less than 1%), Olivia Rodrigo’s you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love climbs 4-3 (67,000, down 4%) and Morgan Wallen’s I’m the Problem moves 6-4 (63,000, down 6%). Dolly Parton’s best-of collection Ultimate Dolly Parton reenters the Billboard 200 at No. 5, marking the late icon’s fourth top 10-charted set, and her second-highest-charted album ever. Parton died on Aug. 25 at age 80 after a short battle with cancer . The entertainer previously visited the top 10 of the chart with the all-star collaborations project Rockstar (No. 3 in 2023, her highest-charted album), Blue Smoke (No. 6 in 2014) and the collaborative album Trio (No. 6 in 1987) with Linda Ronstadt and Emmylou Harris. Ultimate Dolly Parton was released in 2003 and originally peaked at No. 112 in 2019. Until this week, it hadn’t been on the chart since 2020. In the Aug. 21-27 tracking week, which reflects less than three days of impact following the announcement of Parton’s death, Ultimate Dolly Parton earned 59,000 equivalent album units (up from a negligible sum in the previous week), largely driven by streaming activity of the songs on the album. The 20-track Ultimate Dolly Parton includes familiar Parton favorites such as “Jolene,” “I Will Always Love You,” “Here You Come Again,” “9 to 5” and “Islands In the Stream” (with Kenny Rogers). Many of the songs on this album are shared among other Parton projects — hits compilations and studio albums. For chart purposes, songs shared across an artist’s albums have their SEA and TEA assigned to whichever of those albums sells the most, by pure album sales, in a given week. In the latest tracking week, Ultimate Dolly Parton was the legend’s best-selling album, with 7,000 copies sold. The rest of the top 10 on the latest Billboard 200 comprises former leaders. KATSEYE’s WILD falls 1-6 in its second week (55,000 equivalent album units earned, down 68%), Noah Kahan’s The Great Divide is a non-mover at No. 7 (54,000, down 4%), Stray Kids’ THIS & THAT drops 3-8 (48,000, down 42%), Drake’s ICEMAN is stationary at No. 9 (41,000, down 6%) and Ariana Grande’s Petal dips 8-10 (41,000, down 20%). Luminate, the independent data provider to the  Billboard  charts, completes a thorough review of all data submissions used in compiling the weekly chart rankings. Luminate reviews and authenticates data. In partnership with  Billboard , data deemed suspicious or unverifiable is removed, using established criteria, before final chart calculations are made and published.

articles._body: Toronto Blue Jays starter Max Scherzer has had plenty of ups and downs throughout the 2026 campaign. But on Sunday, he put together a vintage performance that further etched his name in MLB’s history books. Scherzer pitched seven innings of scoreless baseball against the Seattle Mariners, allowing one hit and one walk while striking out 10. He joined Nolan Ryan as the only two pitchers in MLB history to record 10+ Ks and allow one or less hits and 42-years-old or older. Scherzer – who is 42 – is now the oldest player to accomplish the feat since Ryan did back in 1991, via Sarah Langs of MLB.com. At 42 years and 34 days old, Max Scherzer is the oldest pitcher with 10+ strikeouts and 1 or no hits allowed in a game since Nolan Ryan on 5/1/91 (44y 90d, no-hitter) Scherzer and Ryan (6x) are the only pitchers with such an outing at age 42+ in MLB history https://t.co/UHwaO1m1vi — Sarah Langs (@SlangsOnSports) August 30, 2026 Earning a 7-0 victory, the Blue Jays are now 68-70 on the season. While they’re out of the AL East race, Toronto sits just one game back of a Wild Card spot. The franchise will make a fierce push down the stretch. If Scherzer keeps pitching like this, he will become an even more valuable asset. Through his 13 starts this season, Scherzer now holds a 6.16 ERA and a 46/26 K/BB ratio. While those numbers don’t jump off the page, he has allowed two or fewer runs in seven of his last eight starts. The one outlier was a seven-run blow up, that supremely inflated the ERA mark. The Blue Jays will now hope Scherzer is fully back on track. Injuries have hampered his abilities throughout his time in Toronto. But on Sunday, he proved he had plenty of gas left in the tank. All eyes will be on Scherzer next time he’s on the mound to see if he can replicate the performance. articles.title: Packers officially delay Micah Parsons return until at least Week 5 with injury move
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers defensive superstar Micah Parsons has issued a warning to the rest of the NFL regarding his return from a torn ACL. He told reporters, via Ryan Wood, that people should focus less on his knee and more on the anger and frustration he plans to unleash on the field. Despite Parsons
articles._body: Green Bay Packers defensive superstar Micah Parsons has issued a warning to the rest of the NFL regarding his return from a torn ACL. He told reporters, via Ryan Wood, that people should focus less on his knee and more on the anger and frustration he plans to unleash on the field. Despite Parsons’ confident remarks and impressive rehabilitation milestones, the Packers are taking a cautious approach to ensure his long-term health. Rather than rushing their prized pass rusher back onto the field for the start of the regular season, the organization made a significant roster decision ahead of Tuesday’s 53-man deadline. ESPN senior NFL insider Adam Schefter confirmed the anticipated change in timeline on X, stating, “The Packers have officially moved Micah Parsons to Reserve/PUP, ruling him out for this season’s first four games.” By placing Parsons on the Reserve/Physically Unable to Perform list, Green Bay is ensuring that his 2026 debut will be delayed until at least Week 5, allowing him extra recovery time before testing his surgically repaired knee in a live regular-season game. While the defense works to replace the 12.5 sacks Parsons recorded last year during his initial weeks on the sidelines, the star defender has full confidence in the offense to keep Green Bay competitive. Speaking with Bleacher Report, Parsons praised franchise quarterback Jordan Love , boldly predicting, “I think Jordan is going to be a top 5 quarterback this year, and I think he is going to show the world how great he really can be.” With Love’s emerging leadership and an offense poised for significant improvement, Green Bay aims to build early momentum while waiting for Parsons to return at full strength. articles.title: Pitt great Aaron Donald ditching retirement, rejoining Rams
articles.summary: Aaron Donald is coming out of retirement to rejoin the Los Angeles Rams and play beside Myles Garrett.
articles._body: Aaron Donald is back. The Pitt graduate and Los Angeles Rams great has decided to make an NFL return after two seasons in retirement. According to multiple reports, he’s decided to rejoin Sean McVay’s team, which added reigning Associated Press NFL Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett via a trade this offseason. Donald, 35, has spent the entirety of his 10-season NFL career with the Rams, who selected him No. 13 overall in the 2014 NFL Draft. A nine-time first-team AP All-Pro, Donald has also collected three AP NFL Defensive Player of the Year awards. By sticking him on the same defensive front as Garrett, the Rams should have a wrecking crew. Aaron Donald left the Rams offices at noon PT today, without notifying team officials of his plans. Some doubts about his return were starting to creep into the organization’s thoughts. And then Donald announced that he is, in fact, returning. The Rams are loaded. https://t.co/G4955Pa0kw — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 30, 2026 “Aaron Donald left the Rams offices at noon PT today, without notifying team officials of his plans,” ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter wrote on X. “Some doubts about his return were starting to creep into the organization’s thoughts. And then Donald announced that he is, in fact, returning.” Donald compiled 66 tackles for loss during his career at Pitt, the most by an FBS interior defensive lineman since the NCAA began tracking that statistic. As a senior with the Panthers, he was a unanimous first-team All-American and won the Bronko Nagurski Trophy, Chuck Bendarik Award, Outland Trophy and Rotary Lombardi Award.

articles._body: The Green Bay Packers are set to begin their 2026 season without one of their star players. According to a report from ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter , the team has placed pass-rusher Micah Parsons on the reserve/physically unable to perform list, ruling him out of for the first four games of the season. Parsons is working to recover from a torn ACL that he suffered in a game against the Denver Broncos on Dec. 14. He’s not quite ready for a return to the playing field at this point. [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] The hope is for Micah Parsons to be ready by Week 6, but that will obviously depend on his ongoing recovery. Parsons recently addressed that on The Edge with Micah Parsons . “I think the people really want Week 6,” he said on the podcast. “I just want to come back when I’m feeling like myself again. I’d say Week 6 would be optimistic. Window opens the first week of October and two, three weeks of practice. But the reality is you’ve got to feel like yourself. You’ve got to be moving again. I don’t want to go out there and embarrass myself. That’s a real feeling.” Parsons is obviously a huge piece for the Packers defense. He was obtained via a trade with the Dallas Cowboys last season and instantly had an impact. The talented pass-rusher played in 14 games, starting 13 of them. He logged 41 tackles, 12.0 tackles for a loss, 12.5 sacks, two forced fumbles and a pass defended. Now the goal is to get him back on the field. And healthy. A healthy Micah Parsons is a dangerous, dangerous pass rush. “I’m not going to lie, the rehab is going really good,” Parsons said. “We’re getting stronger. We’re moving a little bit now. We’re running. We’re starting change of direction. It’s coming along, bro.” Josh Jacobs sent to commissioner’s exempt list While Micah Parsons will miss the first four games, running back Josh Jacobs has been placed on the commissioner exempt list by the NFL, the league announced Sunday. The decision comes in light of formal charges related to his May arrest, which came down earlier this week. Earlier this week, Jacobs was formally charged with misdemeanor battery and misdemeanor criminal damage to property in connection with the arrest. If convicted, Jacobs is facing a fine of not more than $10,000 or not more than nine months in prison, or both, according to ESPN. He has a court date scheduled for Nov. 17. In light of the arrest, there were questions about what type of action the NFL could take against Jacobs. By going on the commissioner exempt list, Jacobs cannot practice or play for the Packers, according to league rules. “The National Football League today placed Josh Jacobs of the Green Bay Packers on the Commissioner Exempt List,” the NFL announced Sunday afternoon. “Jacobs may not practice or attend games while on the list.”

articles.title: Kaleb Johnson trade with Steelers labeled ‘good gamble’ for Packers by ESPN
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers added depth to their running back room, by trading with the Pittsburgh Steelers for rusher Kaleb Johnson. In return, Pittsburgh picked up a 2028 NFL Draft pick. Green Bay is getting applauded for that move, in a new ESPN report. “The most likely outcome is still that J
articles._body: The Green Bay Packers added depth to their running back room , by trading with the Pittsburgh Steelers for rusher Kaleb Johnson. In return, Pittsburgh picked up a 2028 NFL Draft pick. Green Bay is getting applauded for that move , in a new ESPN report. “The most likely outcome is still that Johnson is too limited of a player to be an impactful NFL back. But getting an ex-third rounder for the cost of a future sixth, especially when the Steelers were clearly done with Johnson outright, is a good gamble,” Ben Solak wrote for ESPN. The Packers have questions at running back right now. Josh Jacobs is facing misdemeanor charges , and was placed on the commissioner’s exempt list. That means Jacobs can’t practice or even attend Packers games. He will still be paid. Johnson adds a body to the running back room, who can help make up for the loss of Jacobs. “Johnson is the right sort of player to take a trade flier on. A wide zone running back at Iowa, Johnson was drafted early (pick 83) in the 2025 NFL draft relative to his skillset as a scheme-specific back, and he never found a great foothold in Pittsburgh as a rookie,” Solak wrote. During the 2025 season, Johnson rushed for just 69 yards with the Steelers. “A fresh start might do Johnson well, and the Packers project as a team moving to more outside zone given the smaller, quicker players they’re currently playing along the offensive line. In Jacobs’ absence, Johnson can earn some early-down ball-carrying work in his preferred blocking style. Even if he’s stuck behind MarShawn Lloyd to start the year, Lloyd’s rough injury history creates even more opportunity for Johnson to see the field,” Solak added. Green Bay made the NFL Playoffs in 2025, losing a close game to the Chicago Bears. The Packers have expectations to compete this season for a Super Bowl. articles.summary: Week 0 of the college football season may be in the books, but with just eight FBS games, many fantasy leagues are still drafting. Finding a quarterback in college fantasy football to lead the charge can be easy, but finding tight ends that bring value is much more difficult. Even more, of the to
articles._body: Week 0 of the college football season may be in the books, but with just eight FBS games, many fantasy leagues are still drafting. Finding a quarterback in college fantasy football to lead the charge can be easy, but finding tight ends that bring value is much more difficult. Even more, of the top six tight ends in fantasy last season, five of them are now in the NFL. There is plenty of turnover at the tight end position, but some great value to find at the position. With some tight ends in new places, some working with new offensive coordinators, and others returning to great spots, these are the top ten college fantasy tight ends in 2026. 1. Trey’Dez Green | LSU Maria Lysaker-Imagn Images Trey’Dez Green finished 2025 at TE10 in fantasy, despite playing just eight games. Green played in the first game for LSU against Clemson, but left the game with an injury and would not return until facing South Carolina in October. Overall, he had 33 receptions for 433 yards and seven touchdowns. Green scored touchdowns in six of the eight gams he played, and was a common red zone target. Green was impressive in fall camp, and expects to be a bigger part of Lane Kiffin’s offense in 2026 at LSU. Sam Leavitt could be a top college quarterback this year , and a solid red zone target in Green could bring up both of their values. 2. Jamari Johnson | Oregon Jamari Johnson is coming off a solid season in 2025. The tight end brought in 32 receptions for 510 yards and three touchdowns. While not numbers normally worth drafting early in fantasy, the fact that he was the second tight end on the team last year makes his future bright. Johnson was only used in two tight end sets, with Kenyon Sadiq on the roster. Sadiq finished as TE4 in 2025 , after 560 yards and eight touchdowns. He went on to be a first-round pick of the New York Jets, which opens up Johnson for more opportunities. With a solid receiving corps on the outside, the passing lanes in the middle should open, which is where Johnson thrives. He could be in line for over 600 yards and at least five touchdowns in 2026. 3. DJ Vonnahme | Iowa DJ Vonnahme is in an interesting situation in Iowa. Iowa was one of the worst in the nation in Pass Success Rate and offensive Predicted Points Added. The Iowa offense is known to struggle, and the passing offense has not been good for some time. Regardless, Vonnahme could have a massive season for the Hawkeyes, despite the bad offense around him. Vonnahme had 29 receptions for 434 yards and three touchdowns. He led the team in receptions, yards, and touchdowns. Further, Vonnahme averaged 15 yards per reception. With a new quarterback getting broken in at Iowa, and the need for some sort of passing game, the Iowa tight end will see plenty of targets. If the team can move the ball into the red zone some, he will be the primary target in the end zone, which will give him great value. 4. Terrance Carter Jr. | Texas Tech NATHAN GIESE/AVALANCHE-JOURNAL / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Terrance Carter Jr. is coming off a 55-reception year in 2025 for Texas Tech. He ended up with 624 yards and five touchdown receptions as well. Carter is in an interesting situation because of the quarterback situation for the Red Raiders. With Brendan Sorsby not eligible, the expectation was Will Hammond would be QB1 for the Red Raiders. Hammond is coming off a torn ACL in 2025, and if Hammond does not come back to form, it could be an issue for Carter. Further, the Red Raiders brought in Tommy Castellanos as a transfer . If Castellanos ends up as the starter, Texas Tech could move to more of a run-first offense, which could hurt the value of Carter. 5. Grant Hollier | Georgia State Grant Hollier comes in as the only non-Power Four conference tight end on the list. Hollier played in just eight games in 2025, bringing in 21 receptions for 288 yards and four touchdowns. Regardless, Hollier is the top returning receiver for Georgia State. Ted Hurst took 27.9 percent of the target share, but he is off to the NFL. Meanwhile, Cameran Brown is back at quarterback, and he has a great connection with Hollier. Hollier averaged 13.7 yards per catch last year, and the offense should improve under Hue Jackson, who is in his second year as the offensive coordinator. This should lead to a solid season for the tight end. 6. Dylan Wade | UCF Dylan Wade is coming off a solid season at UCF. He hauled in 43 receptions for 523 yards and five touchdowns in 2025. Wade also comes in as one of the most reliable tight end options in fantasy for 2026. He had just two games last year under four receptions. He also had 897 yards since the start of 2024, which is the highest total among returning Power Four tight ends. Wade has a low floor, which makes him attractive. He does not have the same ceiling as some of the other tight ends, but with a thin tight end group in 2026, Wade could be a smart selection. 7. Benjamin Brahmer | Penn State Matthew O’Haren-Imagn Images Benjamin Brahmer is joining quarterback Rocco Becht and head coach Matt Campbell at Penn State in 2026. Expectations are high for Penn State in this first season under Campbell . Brahmer brought in 37 receptions for 446 yards and six touchdowns last year. He was the primary red-zone target for Becht in 2025, and should continue to be that again in 2026. Brahmer also was a major player out ofthe slot in 2025, taking over 40 percent of his snaps out of the slot, which should continue in 2026. He has better value in PPR leagues due to his volume, but regardless, he is a top option this year. 8. Patrick Overmyer | Houston Patrick Overmyer is coming off back-to-back solid years at UTSA. In his freshman season, he hauled in 31 receptions for 283 yards and three scores. Then, last year he hauled in 27 receptions for 344 yards and five touchdowns. articles.summary: During cut-down day every year, teams make surprising roster cuts as they trim their teams down to 53 players. This year, the Dallas Cowboys are responsible for arguably the most surprising cut league-wide. The Cowboys waived running back Jaydon Blue, according to Adam Schefter.  The second-year
articles._body: During cut-down day every year, teams make surprising roster cuts as they trim their teams down to 53 players. This year, the Dallas Cowboys are responsible for arguably the most surprising cut league-wide. The Cowboys waived running back Jaydon Blue, according to Adam Schefter. The second-year player from Texas was a fifth-round pick last year. Many thought he could take on a large role right away in a thin Dallas backfield, but he was instead limited to 38 carries and 129 yards as a rookie. Reports suggested that Blue improved in a big way in the offseason, though, and he was even the favorite to earn the RB2 gig at one point. Instead, Blue was supplanted by Malik Davis on the depth chart after he had an impressive training camp and preseason run. Even so, Blue was still expected to make the team. When the Cowboys released their unofficial depth chart, Blue was listed as Javonte Williams’ top backup. Just behind him as RB3 was Phil Mafah, who was also just cut by the team. Mafah was a seventh-round selection the same year as Blue was drafted. That leaves Davis, Israel Abanikanda, and Jashaun Corbin as the options to back up Williams. Most teams roster three to four running backs, so it will be interesting to see who ends up making the 53-man roster in Dallas. While the Cowboys are known for their aerial attack , they need depth at the running back position in order to balance out the offense and create insurance for Williams, who has an injury history of his own. Blue immediately becomes one of the most coveted players on the open market now. The post Cowboys waive Jaydon Blue in surprise cutdown day roster move appeared first on ClutchPoints .
