Top 10 games to watch Week 1 of college football season
articles.summary: Ole Miss-Louisville and LSU-Clemson top our list of the 10 best college football games for Week 1 of the 2026 season.
articles._body: The 2026 college football season has kicked off, and Week 1 begins Thursday night. The slate doesn’t pack as much of a punch as some years past with only one ranked matchup and eight games between power conference teams. But it’s college football nonetheless, and we’re happy to have it back. There will be games from Thursday to Monday. Some feature coaches making their debuts at new schools, such as LSU’s Lane Kiffin and Auburn’s Alex Golesh . Others include coaches trying to save their jobs with an early win. Here’s a breakdown of the top 10 games in Week 1. 1. Clemson at LSU Location: Baton Rouge, Louisiana Time: Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET Channel: ABC Kiffin will make his debut as No. 11 LSU’s coach in primetime against Clemson, one of the most anticipated season-opening home games in program history. It marks the first chance to see Arizona State transfer quarterback Sam Leavitt and the rest of a $40 million-plus roster after an offseason filled with drama. Meanwhile, Clemson coach Dabo Swinney has a chance to prove his team can rebound after posting its worst record in the past 15 years. LSU is currently a 9.5-point favorite, according to Polymarket odds. 2. Ole Miss – Louisville Location: Nashville Time: Sunday at 7:30 p.m. ET Channel: ABC This is the only Week 1 matchup between ranked teams in the AP Poll. After making a run to the College Football Playoff semifinals, No. 9 Ole Miss brought back quarterback Trinidad Chambliss and running back Kewan Lacy . Their returns gave Pete Golding some star power in his first full season as the head coach. Louisville slipped down the stretch last season, but the No. 24 Cardinals might contend for the ACC title after signing Ohio State transfer quarterback Lincoln Kienholz . Ole Miss is currently a 6.5-point favorite, according to Polymarket odds. 3. SMU at Florida State Location: Tallahassee, Florida Time: Monday at 7:30 p.m. ET Channel: ESPN An early conference game will help show whether or not No. 19 SMU can contend for the ACC championship and Florida State coach Mike Norvell can keep his job. SMU is coming off a 9-4 season in which three losses came by a combined seven points. Rhett Lashlee ‘s squad will try to return to the ACC title game for the second time in three years with quarterback Kevin Jennings , who dealt with a finger injury early in camp. Florida State struggled early against New Mexico State in Week 0, and a third straight losing season would likely spell the end for Norvell. SMU is currently a 2.5-point favorite on Polymarket. 4. Baylor – Auburn Location: Atlanta Time: Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET Channel: ABC This matchup will feature new quarterbacks for both teams. Baylor signed Florida transfer DJ Lagway entering a critical seventh season for head coach Dave Aranda , who needs a win to alleviate some pressure. Can Lagway, a former five-star recruit, improve after a disappointing sophomore year? Golesh brought quarterback Byrum Brown and 12 other players with him from South Florida as he remade the Auburn roster. Brown posted huge numbers last season with the Bulls. Auburn is a 7.5-point favorite, per Polymarket. 5. UCLA at Cal Location: Berkeley, California Time: Saturday at 10:30 p.m. ET Channel: ESPN UCLA and Cal both made head coaching changes in the offseason. UCLA hired Bob Chesney after he led James Madison to the CFP, and Cal brought back former Oregon defensive coordinator Tosh Lupoi to his alma mater. The quarterbacks make this game particularly intriguing. Former five-star recruit Nico Iamaleava is in his second season with the Bruins, and Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele could be one of the best quarterbacks in the country after showing a lot of upside as a true freshman. Polymarket currently has UCLA as a 1.5-point favorite. 6. Notre Dame – Wisconsin Location: Green Bay, Wisconsin Time: Sunday at 7:30 p.m. ET Channel: NBC Notre Dame has national championship expectations after missing the CFP last season. The No. 4 Fighting Irish had to replace two first-round draft picks at running back, but otherwise, Marcus Freeman brought back most of his team. Redshirt sophomore CJ Carr is leading the way, and he could be one of the nation’s best quarterbacks. Wisconsin signed Old Dominion quarterback Colton Joseph as head coach Luke Fickell fights to save his job. There are currently no odds on the game at Polymarket. 7. Colorado at Georgia Tech Location: Atlanta Time: Thursday at 8 p.m. ET Channel: ESPN Georgia Tech head coach Brent Key had to find a new quarterback, offensive coordinator and defensive coordinator after a 9-4 season. Indiana transfer quarterback Alberto Mendoza will make his first career start, and Michigan transfer running back Justice Haynes is expected to be a big part of the Yellow Jackets’ offense. The shine wore off the Deion Sanders era at Colorado during a 3-9 season, so he could use an upset win. It’ll be a homecoming for sophomore quarterback Julian Lewis , a Georgia native. Georgia Tech is currently a 6.5-point favorite, per Polymarket. 8. UNLV at Hawai’i Location: Honolulu, Hawaii Time: Saturday at 10 p.m. ET Channel: CW This is an early matchup for supremacy in the Mountain West and a potential CFP elimination game for two teams that entered the season with hopes of snagging the Group of 6 bid. UNLV and Hawai’i both lost their Week 0 games to Memphis and Stanford, respectively. UNLV’s offense stalled in the second half, while Hawai’i couldn’t complete a fourth-quarter comeback. UNLV is favored by 2.5 points, per Polymarket. 9. Tulane at Duke Location: Durham, North Carolina Time: Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET Channel: ACC Network Tulane beat Duke last season. Both went on to win their respective conference championships, and Tulane reached the CFP. A lot has changed since then. Tulane has a new head coach after choosing offensive assistant Will Hall as the replacement for Jon Sumrall. The Green Wave will start Houston transfer quarterback Zeon Chriss-Gremil

articles.title: Timberwolves’ Jonathan Kuminga’s agent already eyeing Kings, Bulls for big payday next summer
articles.summary: With Jonathan Kuminga moving to the Minnesota Timberwolves, much of the NBA offseason buzz is now at peace. Kuminga arrived at the Timberwolves on a two-year, $13 million deal that also includes a player option. While the deal on paper did not look as appealing as what the Golden State Warriors r
articles._body: With Jonathan Kuminga moving to the Minnesota Timberwolves , much of the NBA offseason buzz is now at peace. Kuminga arrived at the Timberwolves on a two-year, $13 million deal that also includes a player option. While the deal on paper did not look as appealing as what the Golden State Warriors reportedly offered initially, Kuminga’s agent, Aaron Turner, said his client now has more control over his future, which was not the case with the more valuable previous offers. During a recent conversation on Run It Back on FanDuel TV, Turner explained two teams he is eyeing for a potential move next summer . “I would say on paper, next year for Jonathan Kuminga is a way better free-agency year for him,” Turner told Chandler Parsons. “There are a lot of teams with money, and if you have paid attention to the JK’s recruiting saga over the last few years, those teams that have been trying to sign and trade from (are) Sacramento and Chicago.” Jonathan Kuminga's agent, Aaron Turner, explains why he didn't sign a 3-year, $75M extension with the Warriors: "Money coming before basketball is not how you continue to make more and more money. … Next year is a way better free agency year for him…teams that have been… pic.twitter.com/tpeJMrHym0 — Run It Back (@RunItBackFDTV) August 29, 2026 While he did not confirm that his agent will eventually move out of Minnesota, he did name the Sacramento Kings and the Chicago Bulls as the two teams that he would be looking at in the free agency that comes before the next season. “These teams have a lot of money next year. Now I’m not saying that will necessarily (offer a trade, but) who knows. But the game board is set very, very well for JK for 2027, but you have to be able to get into that market,” he further added. “And if you have a team option, you could have as good a year as you want; you can’t get into that market. So with a player option now, you decide if you want to be in that market, and that is a big, big deal in controlling your future earnings.” Additionally, the roster fit for Kuminga is itself intriguing , given he will be starting alongside franchise icon Anthony Edwards, the newly signed LaMelo Ball, and Jaden McDaniels. And for all the speculation to come to fruition, the 2021 first-round pick will have to let his stats speak on his behalf. A good production season with the Timberwolves means a better chance of striking a deal, while a subpar performance year will create a situation similar to the current one. articles.title: Recapping Week 0 around the ACC
articles.summary: Boston College got to sit back and watch some of its ACC brethren kick off the season on Saturday as five conference foes kicked off their seasons. Here's what you may have missed around the country (and in Ireland) during Week 0 action.
articles._body: Six days to go. Boston College and its fan base got to sit back and get a little taste of ACC action on Saturday as Week 0 officially kicked off. Five ACC teams were in action, but only of them is on the BC schedule later this season. Here’s what you may have missed around the country (and in Ireland) on Saturday: UNC 15, TCU 10 (Ireland) Bill Belichick’s Tar Heels got off on a much better foot this season, grinding out a win over former Harvard QB Jaden Craig and TCU. The defense held the Horned Frogs to under 300 yards of offense (281) and stopped four of five fourth down attempts. The Bill Belichick vs. Bill O’Brien dream matchup (as a writer at least) unfortunately isn’t scheduled for this season. Belichick is however set to be back in New England when the Tar Heels face UConn on November 7. Virginia 34, NC State 8 The Cavs led 17-0 at the half but it was never really all that close. UVA out-gained the Wolfpack 413-168 and put up 258 yards rushing. Beau Pribula led the way with 110 yards on 15 carries. UVA plays Norfolk State while NC State plays Richmond in two weeks. Both teams have a bye week next week. Neither team is on the Eagles’ schedule, but UVA could be a team to watch that makes serious noise in the conference this season. Stanford 37, Hawaii 27 The Cardinal scored 20 points in a wild fourth quarter (34 points combined) to hang on. Davis Warren had 310 yards through the air with a touchdown. Micah Ford had 25 carries for 99 yards and three touchdowns. Stanford led 7-0 after one, 14-7 at the half and 23-7 heading to the fourth beofe the explosion of points. Stanford and BC won’t get to see each other in 2026 after the Eagles’ meltdown before halftime last year. The Cardinal host No. 7 Miami this Friday night. Florida State 34, New Mexicto State 17 It wasn’t pretty, but the Seminoles found a way. Ashton Daniels was 17-27 for 202 yards a touchdown and an interception. Ousmane Kromah had 14 carries for 115 yards and a TD. Samuel Singleton Jr. led the FSU receivers (4/54/1 TD). It was just 3-0 Florida State after one, but the Seminoles gradually built a 17-7 halftime lead and pushed it to 24-10 heading to the fourth quarter. FSU will be here at Alumni on November 7.

articles._body: The Oklahoma high school football season is officially underway, and with a bang. With a rematch of the state championship from 2025 taking place on Friday Night, between state title holders Bixby (Okla.) and Owasso (Okla.), Jenks (Okla.) was also in big game action, in a massive game against Southlake Carroll (Texas) at the Cotton Bowl. With all of the state’s top teams in action, Bixby opens up the season at No. 1 in the Massey Ratings to the surprise of nobody, taking their first step toward defending its state title. Here’s how Massey ranked the best Oklahoma high school football teams in one of the nation’s most competitive states as teams head into Week 2 of the season. [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] The Massey Ratings , officially used during the BCS era, is a model that ranks sports teams by analyzing game outcomes, strength of schedule, and margin of victory. 1. Bixby Spartans As expected, the defending state champions Bixby kick off the season as they ended 2025 as the number one team in all of Oklahoma high school football, after coming out on top in a blockbuster clash with Owasso. With four-star tight end Connor Arrant opening the scoring for the Spartans, the 6A-I state champions took an early 14-0 start as Isaiah Butcher ran one in on his first start. Transferring from Jenks (Okla.), the 2028 signal caller finished the night with three rushing scores. Predicted to once again repeat as 6A-I state champions, Bixby finished week one as the number one. 2. Jenks Trojans It should have been a perfect start to the year for the Jenks Trojans. After going up 27-0 over one of the best teams in Texas high school football at the Cotton Bowl, despite finishing the week as the number two team in Oklahoma high school football, it won’t be much consolation for Jenks after its loss. Despite that, the Trojans still look on pace to make another deep playoff run after falling in the 6A semifinals to the No. 3-ranked Owasso last year, returning a significant amount of senior talent to their roster, headlined by three-star safety Kalib Dillard . 3. Owasso Rams Despite a standout performance from one of the best talents in Oklahoma high school football, four-star athlete Kamieon Compton-Nero , who hauled in two touchdowns on the night, Owasso was still unable to close the gap with Bixby. Despite that, the Rams still showcased why they’re one of the top teams in the state, despite the sheer number of seniors who graduated in 2025. Starting the season with a 0-1 record, Owasso is predicted to finish the rest of the year undefeated. 4. articles._body: The Boston Red Sox are seeing a resurgence this season , under interim manager Chad Tracy. Boston is closing in on naming Tracy as a full-time replacement to Alex Cora, per USA Today. “Chad Tracy may be the interim Boton Red Sox manager, but that job could become permanent once the season ends. He took a team that was going nowhere and morphed into a powerful playoff contender that will be a force in October,” Major League Baseball insider and columnist Bob Nightengale wrote. Tracy is also expected to get attention from other clubs looking for managers. At one point this summer, Tracy managed Boston to a stunning 15-game win streak. “The Red Sox also realize that if they wait too long before extending him, he’ll be the hottest managerial free agent – behind only his predecessor, Alex Cora,” Nightengale added. Boston is currently in a key four-game series against the New York Yankees. The two clubs are battling for position in the American League East. The Red Sox are currently third in the division , with a 74-62 record. That is a remarkable turnaround from the beginning of the year. Under Cora, the Red Sox were floundering with a losing record. Boston seemed destined to finish last in the AL East and miss the MLB Playoffs. Tracy is hoping to pick up as many wins as possible before the regular season ends. He wants the Red Sox to host a playoff series . “That’s important, I won’t shy away from that,” Tracy said during this series with the Yankees, per The Athletic. “I think if you get a short series, you’re able to play in your home ballpark, that stuff matters for sure.” Boston and New York play Sunday. Roman Anthony and Trevor Story are expected to re-join the Red Sox , after missing months due to injuries. articles._body: The Miami Dolphins were in need of a new backup quarterback for Malik Willis this year. The Dolphins just traded Quinn Ewers to the Jacksonville Jaguars , leading to a need at quarterback for Miami. Now, the Green Bay Packers are providing the Dolphins with a backup QB. The Packers are trading Kyle McCord to the Dolphins, per Adam Schefter of ESPN. “Trade: Packers are sending QB Kyle McCord to the Miami Dolphins in exchange for a 2028 6th-round pick, per sources. After trading Quinn Ewers to the Jaguars, the Dolphins needed a new backup for Malik Willis. Now the Dolphins have two former Packers QBs,” Schefter posted on X, formerly Twitter. The Packers have Jordan Love as the established starting quarterback. Last season, Malik Willis was the backup, but he is now with the Dolphins as the starter. McCord signed a reserve/futures contract with the Packers in January 2026, but the team also brought in Tyrod Taylor to compete for the job. Taylor has been the backup with the New York Jets the last two seasons, and has been in the league since 2011. He won the backup job, making McCord expendable. McCord was a three-year player at Ohio State, starting for the team in 2023. He then transferred to Syracuse in 2024, starting 13 games for the team. He was then drafted by the Philadelphia Eagles in the sixth round of the 2025 NFL Draft. McCord was waived in final cuts by the team, but signed back on with the practice squad. McCord will be the backup this year for Willis , with no other quarterbacks currently on the roster. My goals wi
articles._body: I've just released Piqt, an on-device photo/video curator. For years I've wanted to get my Apple Photos library under control, but there just aren't enough hours in the day. I started out in Jupyter notebooks to see how much I can use AI models to automate it and Piqt is the result. My goals with Piqt: - Fully on device: I use a number of ML models, Apple Vision API, clustering algorithms to rank and sort your photos. Everything runs on device. - Private and Safe: Piqt has no accounts, no cloud services, no personal identifiers. Images or personal information never leave the device. Piqt also CAN'T delete your photos. I have a test and validation step in the release process to ensure no delete APIs exist in the code. Instead, Piqt stages things you want to clear out in an album, which you can delete when you're ready. - A library you can use. I didn't just want to clean out images or clear up space. There are plenty of apps for this. My ultimate goal is to make your (and my) photos easier to navigate I'm just looking for feedback on the app and the approach. I'd love to chat about the vision models I'm using and hear from you about any research or techniques I've missed. App Store Link: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/piqt-photo-video-curator/id677... articles.title: Coco Gauff gets honest about fame ahead of US Open first round
articles.summary: Coco Gauff is sharing how she feels about how people have treated her amid her success ahead of her first-round match at the US Open this week. During the US Open media day on Friday, Aug. 28, Gauff shared that she has to lean on her discernment when it comes to making decisions on who […]<
articles._body: Coco Gauff is sharing how she feels about how people have treated her amid her success ahead of her first-round match at the US Open this week. During the US Open media day on Friday, Aug. 28, Gauff shared that she has to lean on her discernment when it comes to making decisions on who is genuinely in her corner. “Honestly it is tough, because you’ve got to navigate who is there to genuinely support and who is there for the ride,” Gauff said. “I feel like I have been blessed with good discernment to kind of know who is there for the right reasons.” Her mother, Candi Gauff, recently went viral for her message on social media regarding people contacting her for tickets to the US Open. The tennis tournament began on August 23 and will conclude on September 13, 2026 at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in Flushing Meadows, Queens, New York. “Dear Family and friends, I apologize in advance for this blunt, but necessary statement,” Candi wrote in her post alongside a photo of Coco celebrating her 2026 Cincinnati Open victory. “I know you are very excited about Coco playing in the US Open. Me too!!! Coco’s guest ticket request have already been accounted for.” She continued, “Unfortunately, I will not be able to hook you up with a ticket. Please make arrangements to purchase a ticket. Side note, never ask for more than 2 tickets. Coco is grown now and she has her own friends that she is honoring tickets for the match.Thank you for your continued support.” View this post on Instagram Coco agreed with her mom’s message and says that her parents have received a lot of requests from people asking for multiple tickets. “I have seen some of the requests my parents have gotten, and it’s people they probably went to elementary school [with] and they’ll literally ask for five, six tickets,” she said. “I would never ask someone for more than two.” “But yeah, it’s okay. You know, some people just don’t know any better, and I guess my mom wanted to post that because she is going to stop responding,” she continued. “At least they know why.” Coco is entering the tournament as the No. 4 seed is one of the top favorites to win. She previously won the 2023 US Open against Aryna Sabalenka. She will face Turkey’s Zeynep Sönmez in the first round of the US Open on Tuesday, Sept. 1 at 7 pm ET. articles.title: The Malik Willis backup Dolphins must acquire after Quinn Ewers trade, Cam Miller release
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins are in the midst of a youth movement as they rebuild the organization in Jeff Hafley’s image. Miami is starting over at quarterback with Malik Willis set to start on offense during the 2026 season. The Dolphins just made a handful of surprising quarterback moves that have
articles._body: The Miami Dolphins are in the midst of a youth movement as they rebuild the organization in Jeff Hafley’s image. Miami is starting over at quarterback with Malik Willis set to start on offense during the 2026 season. The Dolphins just made a handful of surprising quarterback moves that have the depth chart behind Willis looking like a complete mystery. Miami decided to trade backup QB Quinn Ewers to the Jaguars on Saturday in exchange for a late-round pick swap. The Dolphins are destined to draft a new quarterback in the near future, so Ewers had almost no realistic path to playing time. Perhaps more surprisingly, the Dolphins plan to waive Cam Willer before the roster deadline. That means the QB2 spot behind Willis is currently up for grabs. The only other quarterback currently on the roster is rookie Mark Gronowski from Iowa. At this point it looks like he’ll make the final roster. However, he does not look ready to fulfill backup duties behind Willis. So what will the Dolphins do to find their backup quarterback? One veteran quarterback stands out as the perfect one-year rental for the Dolphins. Could Jimmy Garoppolo be the ideal backup for Malik Willis in 2026? Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images One veteran quarterback is still sitting on the free agent market and could be an ideal backup for Willis. Garoppolo boasts 12 years of NFL experience and has played for some of the best franchises in the league. He spent time under Bill Belichick, Kyle Shanahan, and most recently Sean McVay. Jimmy G briefly crossed paths with Hafley for two seasons when both were on the 49ers from 2017-18. That doesn’t immediately make him the favorite to land the job. Instead, it simply shows that both player and coach may see the game the same way given their similar background. Garoppolo’s years of veteran experience make him an ideal mentor for Willis. He could be the prototypical “coach on the field” with Willis during practices and while on the sideline during games. Plus Garoppolo is still talented enough to provide backup-level starts if his number is called. The last time Garoppolo played in the regular season was in 2024. He looked great, going 27-of-41 for 334 passing yards with two touchdowns and an interception. The Dolphins did bring in Kyle McCord on Sunday, but that shouldn’t stop them from exploring the veteran free agent market too. Ultimately, the expectations are not high in Miami in 2026. That means player development and building a new culture are more important than simply winning now. Garoppolo would be an ideal backup who checks all of those boxes. It will be fascinating to see what Miami’s quarterback room looks like when the regular season kicks off in a few weeks. articles._body: College football fans were focused on the excitement of a new season. TCU and North Carolina kicked off the FBS season with a game in Ireland. While most fans were focused on the first week of FBS play, tragedy struck at the Division II level. William Jewell College was facing Fort Lewis College in Liberty, Missouri, when a player collapsed on the sideline. The player, Micah Jo Barnett, passed away, per a statement from the school . “William Jewell College and the Liberty, Missouri community mourn the passing of Micah Jo Barnett, a junior business administration and member of Jewell Cardinal football program and former Liberty North Eagle. Our thoughts and prayers are with Micah Jo’s family, our students, the Cardinal Football family, and the rest of our community during this time of loss. Students and staff are encouraged to connect with Counseling Services and/or the office of the Chaplain who are ready to provide support to those who need it,” the statement read. Barnett scored the first touchdown of the game, rushing in a one-yard touchdown with 5:25 left in the first quarter. The game was stopped with 4:32 left in the quarter after Barnett collapsed on the sideline. His teammates spoke about Barnett after the game . “It’s an honor to play for him, you know,” said sophomore wide receiver Tatum Bethany. “He’s always going to be with us regardless. So we know he would want us to keep moving and keep pushing and play as hard as he would every day.” “At this point, it’s not really thinking about the [rest of the] season. This is bigger than football,” sophomore wide receiver Kaleb Mays said. “He was bigger than football.” Barnett was a junior who went to high school at nearby Liberty North High School. Every Song That Topped the U.K. Chart for 8 or More Weeks, But Didn’t Make the Top 10 on the Hot 100
articles.summary: "Rein Me In” by Sam Fender and Olivia Dean is the first single to log 23 weeks at No. 1 in the U.K. It hasn't even made the top 40 on the Hot 100, but it's closing in.
articles._body: UPDATE (Aug. 30): “Rein Me In” by Sam Fender and Olivia Dean logs its 23rd nonconsecutive week at No. 1 on the U.K.’s Official Singles Chart on the tally that was published on Friday (Aug. 28). The song hasn’t been nearly as big a hit in the U.S., though it isn’t done yet. It jumps from No. 50 to No. 45 in its 22nd week on the Billboard Hot 100 dated Aug. 29, its highest ranking to date. “Rein Me In” is the first single to log 23 weeks at No. 1 in the U.K., but it has yet to reach the top 10 (or even the top 40) on the Hot 100. In the 68 years that the Hot 100 has been in place, music fans in the U.S. and the U.K. have never been so far apart in their reactions to a song. Here’s an essay on how “Rein Me In” became the U.K.’s longest-running No. 1 single ever. And here’s a look at the song that previously held the record, Frankie Laine ‘s “I Believe.” PREVIOUSLY (April 23): Music fans in the United States and the United Kingdom often agree on big hits. Six songs have logged 10 or more weeks at No. 1 on both the Billboard Hot 100, the flagship chart for success in the U.S., and the Official Singles Chart in the U.K. Whitney Houston ’s “I Will Always Love You” from The Bodyguard (1992-93) became the first song to reach double digits in weeks at No. 1 on both sides of the Atlantic. Alex Warren ’s “Ordinary” (2025) marked the most recent. In between those two megahits, four other singles achieved the feat: Drake ‘s “One Dance,” featuring WizKid & Kyla (2016), Ed Sheeran ’s “Shape of You” (2017), Luis Fonsi & Daddy Yankee ‘s “Despacito,” featuring Justin Bieber (2017) and Harry Styles ’ “As It Was” (2022). But music fans in our two countries don’t always agree. “Rein Me In” by Sam Fender and Olivia Dean is currently in its eighth week at No. 1 on the Official Singles Chart in the U.K., but it hasn’t broken through in nearly the same way on the Hot 100. This week, it drops from its No. 64 high point to No. 73. Part of the problem is that two other Dean hits simply refuse to yield: “Man I Need” (which holds at its No. 2 peak) and “So Easy (to Fall in Love)” (which keeps at its No. 6 high). Both are catchier and closer to the core sound in pop music right now. And while Fender is an established star in the U.K., with four top 10 hits, this is his first Hot 100 hit. “Rein Me In” is the ninth song since 1958 (when the Hot 100 originated) to log eight or more weeks at No. 1 on the Official Singles Chart in the U.K. but fall short of the top 10 on the Hot 100. Here’s a complete list of those songs, in chronological order:

articles.title: Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields Donation Reaches $20 Million After Melinda French Gates Match
articles.summary: "What Daisy Chain Fields sets in motion will last far beyond a single night," the philanthropist said.
articles._body: Olivia Rodrigo ’s Daisy Chain Fields received a major financial boost thanks to a multimillion-dollar donation from Melinda French Gates. After the inaugural all-women music festival announced Friday (Aug. 28) that it had raised $10 million for women’s charities, French Gates doubled that amount, bringing the total to $20 million. Related Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields Music Festival Proves There Is Hope For Us All: 13 Best Moments Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields Festival Raises $10 Million for Women’s Charities Olivia Rodrigo Recruits Alanis Morissette for a Surprise ‘Ironic’ Duet “What @daisychainfields set in motion will last far beyond a single night,” French Gates wrote on Instagram alongside a photo of herself with Rodrigo. “I was so inspired by @oliviarodrigo’s vision, which is why I couldn’t be prouder to contribute $10 million through @pivotaldotcom, doubling the amount this extraordinary community already raised for organizations supporting women & girls.” During her Daisy Chain Fields headlining set Saturday night (Aug. 29) at Great Park in Irvine, California, the 23-year-old pop star welcomed French Gates onstage to announce the philanthropist’s massive donation. “Melinda is one of the most inspiring women I’ve ever met. She’s devoted her life to empowering women and girls that might have otherwise been forgotten,” Rodrigo told the crowd. “She’s generous and brave and has done so much good in this world, and I’m totally floored because as well as being in attendance here tonight, she’s pledged to double every dollar that we made here today to a grand total of funds being donated to $20 million. I’m so grateful!” The partner organizations benefiting from the festival’s initial $10 million include Baby2Baby, Black Mamas Matter Alliance, Center for Reproductive Rights, FreeFrom, Jhpiego, Johns Hopkins Center for Indigenous Health, National Domestic Workers Alliance, National Institute for Reproductive Health, National Women’s Law Center and Planned Parenthood. Rodrigo revealed during a press conference Friday that the one-day festival had raised $10 million for its beneficiary organizations. During the show, she also thanked the artists on the lineup for performing their sets for free. Rodrigo personally curated the lineup, which included Chappell Roan, Doechii, Mitski, Garbage, The Breeders and Bikini Kill, as well as “special guests” Stevie Nicks and Sarah McLachlan.

articles.title: Dolphins shockingly cut former starter after 129-tackle season
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins were arguably the most active team in the offseason, as they began a rebuild that was highlighted by the departures of Tua Tagovailoa, Jaylen Waddle, Tyreek Hill, and Bradley Chubb. The team is still seemingly fast-tracking losing this year, as they surprisingly moved off of ye
articles._body: The Miami Dolphins were arguably the most active team in the offseason, as they began a rebuild that was highlighted by the departures of Tua Tagovailoa , Jaylen Waddle, Tyreek Hill, and Bradley Chubb. The team is still seemingly fast-tracking losing this year, as they surprisingly moved off of yet another talented player. Hours before the cut-down deadline passes, the Dolphins released Tyrel Dodson in a shocking move that has some fans claiming the team is tanking. The linebacker was a 16-game starter last season who racked up 129 tackles. That was the 14th-best mark in the NFL, although Dodson’s teammate, Jordyn Brooks, did lead the NFL with 183 tackles . Dodson was on the final year of a two-year, $6,250,000 deal. Dodson was an undrafted player in 2019 who had played for the Buffalo Bills and Seattle Seahawks before he joined the Dolphins. Now, he will be one of the most coveted players on the open market. The Dodson release comes just one day after the Dolphins traded Quinn Ewers, who started three games at quarterback for the team last year. While Miami is all in on Malik Willis at quarterback, they’ve stripped the rest of the roster down to the bones. The team looks a whole lot different than they did last season, when they went 7-10. Miami’s busyness leading up to the cut-down deadline proves that they aren’t done rebuilding. More big-name departures, both through the trade market and via cuts, are likely to come in Miami. The cut-down deadline is officially at 6 p.m. ET on Sunday, Aug. 30. The post Dolphins shockingly cut former starter after 129-tackle season appeared first on ClutchPoints .

A quick funny story about this game's history:

articles._body: Hi HN, I just completed a rewrite of Snaketron, a competitive multiplayer Snake game. (Yes, yes, in Rust) A quick funny story about this game's history: Back in 2012 I had (poorly) implemented the first version of Snaketron. The issue with it was that I was keeping game state on the client, and while I did realize that it was insecure, I also had no idea what to do about it without increasing latency to unplayable levels. I was still in school, never worked on games, and haven't even heard of the term "netcode" before. The excitement of releasing my first pet project got the better of me, and I placed this security concern in the "theoretical issues" bucket, and shipped it. No one would even notice, and if they did, they wouldn't take the time to break into my little Snake game project, right? WRONG! Hacker News absolutely lived up to its name. While I was busy with my first experience of handling a traffic surge, scaling up my database and fixing bugs, several players found the security holes and were beginning their Snake rampage. Reports were coming in of unkillable snakes so I decided to start up a game to see if I could catch it. I loaded a 1v1 and my opponent was ... space invaders. My snake was a snake. Their "snake" was a rendering of the game Space Invaders. Needless to say they were also moving around and were invincible. I really wish I had taken a video of that, but I was floored that HN not just played, but hacked, my project is such an epic way. I always wanted to rebuild it properly, so here's V2! The architecture and motivations are quite different this time around. First, the state is server authoritative and lag is compensated for by client-state prediction. The game engine is written in Rust and compiled to WASM for the client side library. To minimize the ops burden, I also imposed a strict resiliency requirement on this project: it must be auto-scalable. So a node can join the cluster and live games will rebalance to it without disrupting gameplay. I also tried to make the new Snaketron a little more fun. The core mechanic is still, like classic Snake, collecting food without crashing. But now team matches have an objective to make competitive games more structured. There's also a Bronze to Grand Master ranking sub system (if enough people play, calibrating this will be interesting) and some fun features like boosting, combos, skins, and Play Of The Game detection. On Rust: One of my original goals for doing this in Rust was so that I could learn the language. That didn't work out as well as I thought it would. Usually I learn by building stuff, but AI got so good that I stopped writing code by hand and preferred to spend my nights & weekends working on what was more intereting to me than borrow checking errors: game design and the high availability stuff. On AI: Who knows if this would have gotten done without AI. Probably not, what with my day job and other things going on in life. It's 200k LOC (most of that is tests don't worry) but still. Anyway, here are the project links. Thank you for reading, I hope you enjoy the game and any feedback is very much appreciated! A massive triple-layer CloudTec® midsole powered by Helion™ superfoam delivers plush, springy impact absorption with every step, grounded by a durable rubber outsole built to put in actual miles. articles.title: Connor Meadows ready to take center stage for UCF
articles.summary: Connor Meadows' versatility helped him earn a starting role late last season. Now the veteran offensive lineman is preparing to take over at center for UCF in 2026.
articles._body: A year ago, Connor Meadows was willing to line up just about anywhere UCF needed him. Guard. Tackle. Even tight end. Now, after carving out a bigger role late last season, Meadows enters 2026 poised to take on arguably his most important assignment yet: starting center. The former Tennessee State and Tennessee lineman appeared in eight games during his first season at UCF, eventually starting at right guard in each of the Knights’ final three games. But his path to the lineup required patience after arriving at UCF in May 2025 as a post-spring portal addition. “That was a sprint to try to learn new terminology, learn what we’re trying to do and the style of play that we wanted to have,” Meadows said. “Maybe I didn’t start in the role I wanted to, but I just put my head down and went to work every day, got on the grind. That’s all we can do, and I think it’s paid off.” That persistence ultimately made Meadows one of UCF’s more valuable offensive linemen. He played 187 snaps at right guard last season, along with 33 at right tackle and four at left tackle. His first start actually came as an extra tight end against Baylor before he moved into the starting lineup at guard over the final three games. This year, he’s moving again. Taking over in the middle Center wasn’t completely foreign to Meadows. He had practiced there at both of his previous college stops, and the possibility of eventually moving to the position had been discussed before. But there’s a difference between taking occasional practice snaps and preparing to handle the position full-time. “I feel like I got to a place at guard where I can play really fast without thinking too much about it,” Meadows said. “Obviously, with the new position, there’s more reps and more thinking, and every rep’s slowing down for me. “I just have to keep trusting that process.” His experience across the offensive line may actually be helping now. Meadows believes playing tackle, guard and even tight end has given him a better understanding of how all the pieces fit together, something that’s particularly valuable at center, where identifying the defense before the snap becomes a major responsibility. “I think playing tackle and playing guard and even tight end, that’s already given me a wide view of what happens within a defense and what goes on within our offense,” Meadows said. “It gives more of an understanding, and that’s assisted me with this move to center.” The biggest adjustment? “Pre-snap is the biggest difference,” Meadows said. “Learning how to ID things fast and seeing things move on the run, but also letting yourself play fast. “Again, with more reps, it becomes easier. Things start slowing down.” Impressed by Alonza The move also puts Meadows directly in front of quarterback Alonza Barnett III. Barnett missed spring practice but spent the summer working with UCF’s offense, giving Meadows an opportunity to build chemistry with the James Madison transfer. One characteristic has stood out. “There’s just a real calmness to him and poise in the huddle,” Meadows said. “You can feel that radiate off the other 10 in the huddle.” Meadows had already watched Barnett play at James Madison, but seeing him up close has reinforced what he saw on film. “He’s really, really good on schedule,” Meadows said. “And even when things get off schedule and he has to extend the play out of the pocket, that calmness that I spoke of is still there. He makes plays.” That has shown up during preseason camp, particularly when Barnett has been forced to escape pressure. “There’s no panic in his body language or eyes at all,” Meadows said. “He’ll deliver a dart to one of our plethora of receivers we have. “It’s been really fun to watch his eye progressions and how he moves in the pocket. He just looks so natural.” Small town roots Football was a major part of life growing up in Trenton, Tenn. Located about 30 minutes northwest of Jackson in West Tennessee, Trenton is the type of place where, as Meadows puts it, everybody knows everybody. “Small town. Everybody kind of knows each other,” Meadows said. “Football is the biggest thing we had.” Just how small? “We have one stoplight in town,” Meadows said. “I think that describes everything you need to know.” Meadows grew up fishing and playing just about every sport available, but football was always the constant. He also grew up alongside many of the same kids he eventually played with in high school at Peabody. “Because everybody knew each other, I grew up with the same kids,” Meadows said. “We played in high school together and won a lot of games, won a lot of championships. I think that was the fun part of growing up in a small town.” There’s plenty of football talent in that part of Tennessee, too. Meadows pointed to nearby Humboldt, the hometown of Kansas City Chiefs offensive lineman Trey Smith , who also played at Tennessee. Meadows hopes to do his part to represent his corner of the state. “There’s a lot of underdogs coming out of there,” Meadows said. “Try to put them on the map, you know?” One last run Now, after spending much of his career adapting to different teams and different positions, Meadows has some lofty goals for his final season of college football. “I want to be the best player I can be for this team and contribute to this O-line,” Meadows said. “I want every guy individually to be as great as they can be. I want us as an O-line to win the Joe Moore Award.” And his goals don’t stop there. “I want to win a Big 12 championship. I want to win a national championship,” Meadows said. “Again, that starts one week at a time, one day at a time. I believe the individual results, individual goals, which I have, will take care of themselves.” The first opportunity arrives Thursday against Bethune-Cookman.

articles.title: The moment LSU coach Lane Kiffin saw Bo Nix in Sam Leavitt
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin is preparing for his first season at LSU. After controversially leaving Ole Miss, then bringing plenty of transfers, and now trying to add former NFL players to the roster, Kiffin has become a villain in college football. Kiffin brought multiple players with him from Ole Miss, but was
articles._body: Lane Kiffin is preparing for his first season at LSU. After controversially leaving Ole Miss, then bringing plenty of transfers, and now trying to add former NFL players to the roster, Kiffin has become a villain in college football . Kiffin brought multiple players with him from Ole Miss, but was not able to bring his quarterback, Trinidad Chambliss. Kiffin instead will be working with former Arizona State quarterback Sam Leavitt. Now, Kiffin is speaking out about his new quarterback, per DJ Siddiqi of Covers. “He’s had great intensity about how he’s gone about this, wanting to chase greatness, and that’s really what I talk about. Really what I try to do in life is relentless pursuit of chasing greatness, and that’s part of sometimes moving jobs that aren’t popular decisions for everybody. But Sam’s done that, and so I’m really excited to see him play,” Kiffin said. Kiffin will not have to wait much longer to see his quarterback play as LSU will host Clemson on September 5. While the two prepare for the season, Kiffin also is reminded of a different quarterback he faced when watching Leavitt. “There’s a lot of movement similar to Bo Nix. He was making some plays on the run the other day, and I said, ‘Man, he kind of looks like Bo right there.'” Kiffin added. The former Ole Miss coach saw Bo Nix on the other sideline twice. In 2020, Auburn beat Ole Miss 35-28 on a game-winning touchdown pass from Nix. The next year, Auburn won again, with Nix making multiple big plays. When Nix entered the transfer portal, Kiffin attempted to bring him to Ole Miss, but the quarterback decided on Oregon instead. Kiffin has been effusive with his praise for Leavitt this offseason , and now they hope to start the season strong with a win on national television. The post The moment LSU coach Lane Kiffin saw Bo Nix in Sam Leavitt appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: This baby boomer vs. Gen X Senate race emerges as key test of generational change in U.S. politics and what age is too old for Congress
articles.summary: Sen. Ed Markey is 80, while his rival, Rep. Seth Moulton, is 47.
articles._body: In a race that has centered on whether  Ed Markey , 80, is too old for another U.S. Senate term, the Massachusetts Democrat’s answer to a recent debate question was especially striking. When asked whether he uses AI platforms like Claude or ChatGPT in his work, Markey seemed unclear on the topic. He responded that he uses “whatever is inside of my iPhone or my iPad — whatever comes up” and added that he doesn’t know “what companies my iPad may be using.” For Arsen Bagdassarian, an 18-year-old supporter of Markey’s rival, 47-year-old U.S. Rep.  Seth Moulton , the answer reinforced a concern that has become central to Moulton’s campaign to unseat the incumbent in Tuesday’s party primary: that Markey, who would be 86 at the end of another term, is too old to represent a generation confronting problems that didn’t exist when Markey entered Congress 50 years ago. “To be frank, I didn’t expect him to be as clueless as he really was on that topic,” said Bagdassarian, an incoming freshman at Boston’s Northeastern University. Artificial intelligence is “a major concern,” he said, and the country needs leaders “who understand what they’re being asked to regulate.” The 2026 midterms have brought a number of generational challenges like the one Moulton is waging against Markey, with younger Democrats taking on — and in some cases unseating — longtime incumbents. There are signs that Democratic voters, especially, are looking for change , and some young voters argue older politicians can’t truly understand a world transformed by artificial intelligence, rising housing costs and student debt. But that hasn’t been the case for all young people voting for the Senate nominee in a heavily Democratic state where the primary often decides who wins office. Markey has a strong following of young supporters, some of whom say that the internal party debate is more over policy than age. He’s won the endorsement of the High School Democrats of America and the College Democrats of America, as well as the backing of popular progressives such as U.S. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani. Among those younger supporters is Matt Kelly, president of the UMass Lowell College Democrats. Kelly doesn’t dispute that Markey stumbled when asked about his use of AI, saying, “I’ll admit it wasn’t a good answer.” But Kelly said he cares less about whether Markey knows how to use the latest technology than whether he understands how to govern it. Moulton’s relative youth, Kelly said, doesn’t necessarily make his views more representative of young voters. “Just because he has a younger face doesn’t mean that he has younger ideas,” he said. For young Markey supporters, longevity can be an asset Many of Markey’s younger supporters turn Moulton’s argument about the senator’s 50-year political career on its head. To them, longevity provides a record they can judge — one that shows whether politicians held the same positions before they became popular with younger voters. One example is Markey’s vote in 2002 against the creation of the Department of Homeland Security, which later led to the creation of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Milan van Dam, a 17-year-old who serves as national chair of the High School Democrats of America, said generational leadership is “less about an age on a Wikipedia page” than the ideas a candidate represents and their consistency through time. Abby Shadden, a 21-year-old Emmanuel College student, similarly pointed to Markey’s co-authorship of the Green New Deal and his early support for Medicare for All. “There is this idea that younger people are just automatically more progressive when, in this case, it is very much not true,” she said. For Kelly, the debate over AI is already playing out close to home. A  proposed data center  in Lowell, where he attends college, has generated opposition from some residents over its potential impact on the community. Kelly said Markey’s push for greater regulation of data centers matters more to him than the senator’s awkward answer about AI. Kelly said his generation will be graduating into an economy increasingly shaped by artificial intelligence while facing a cost of living that has made it harder to achieve the same financial security as previous generations. “Yes, Ed Markey’s answer rhetorically didn’t come off well, optically didn’t look well,” Kelly said. But when it comes to who will be good for “the group that’s graduating into this new economy,” he said, Markey’s record matters more. Moulton says it’s time for a new generation of Democratic leaders Moulton seized on Markey’s debate answer, telling him: “Senator, if you don’t even know what you’re using on your phone or your iPad, like this is why we need a new generation of leaders to regulate these technologies.” Moulton called Markey’s loose grasp of the technology “potentially disqualifying.” Markey pushed back, saying, “It doesn’t make any difference whether it’s called Siri or it’s called Claude,” and emphasizing that familiarity with individual AI products was less important than putting safeguards around the technology. He pointed to legislation he has introduced to regulate AI’s effects on children, workers, civil rights, and the environment. articles.summary: The NC State football team got smacked around by Virginia on Saturday. Virginia defeated the Wolfpack, 34-8. NC State quarterback CJ Bailey had a tough game. He opened up postgame about what went wrong for his squad. “It happens…I just have to re-gather myself and get my feet back set
articles._body: The NC State football team got smacked around by Virginia on Saturday. Virginia defeated the Wolfpack, 34-8. NC State quarterback CJ Bailey had a tough game . He opened up postgame about what went wrong for his squad. “It happens…I just have to re-gather myself and get my feet back set right,” Bailey said, per Carolina Blitz. “….it was just bad luck. We had tips at the line of scrimmage.” CJ Bailey on his performance in NC State’s season-opening loss to UVA. pic.twitter.com/KcpxuY6guN — Carolina Blitz (@KeepBlitzin) August 30, 2026 NC State struggled to move the football in the first half, and the team also couldn’t protect the football. Bailey finished his day with 12 completions and an interception. He posted just 84 passing yards, and also had a red zone fumble . “The world’s not going to end, but it was disappointing as hell, to say the least, to see how we played today,” North Carolina State coach Dave Doeren said, per the Associated Press. “I own that. That’s on me. Everybody can blame the head coach. That’s great. I’m going to go in there and work my (backside) off for these guys and help them.” Virginia’s defense was extremely effective. The Cavaliers had Bailey scrambling for most of the day. That pressure led to Bailey making some bad decisions on offense. Virginia football meanwhile was led by transfer quarterback Beau Pribula . Pribula took to the air and to the ground to lead Virginia’s offense to a powerful victory. The Cavaliers had a stunning drive at one point that lasted a whopping 23 plays. “I thought he was very decisive, very efficient with the ball,” Virginia coach Tony Elliott said. “He protected it, didn’t put it in jeopardy for the most part. He was looking for checkdowns. If it wasn’t there, he was pulling it down, keeping us ahead of the chains. It was fun to watch him play.” NC State will next play FCS Richmond, on September 11. articles.title: Broncos’ Sean Payton absolutely crushes FOX Sports analyst over Bo Nix hate
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos face some difficult roster decisions now that the preseason is in the rearview mirror. Denver is preparing for a bounce-back campaign in 2026 as QB Bo Nix gets healthy following last year’s ankle injury. Head coach Sean Payton does not want to hear Nix slander just before
articles._body: The Denver Broncos face some difficult roster decisions now that the preseason is in the rearview mirror. Denver is preparing for a bounce-back campaign in 2026 as QB Bo Nix gets healthy following last year’s ankle injury. Head coach Sean Payton does not want to hear Nix slander just before the regular season. Payton was not shy sharing his opinion about FOX Sports analyst Geoff Schwartz on social media recently. He took issue with Schwartz’s assessment of Nix during a recent segment on FS1. Schwartz said he sees Nix as the same player that he was during his college career at Oregon. “I do think he just is what he is at this point. He looks like the same quarterback he was in college,” Schwartz said on August 26th. “He’s consistent. He’s not gonna make mistakes. But he’s not gonna push the ball down the field all that often.” Payton posted a dismissive message in reply to Schwartz’s analysis, quipping “always easy to tell who works at it and who doesn’t.” Denver’s head coach broke down that comments in further details after Friday’s big preseason win . “That was crazy wasn’t it? I can’t help myself though. When I see something like that, I’m sorry. It’s just, I have a pause and then it’s like, ‘What are you watching?’ Just watch the tape,” Payton said during his postgame press conference. “Here’s the thing though. I think—and this is for any player—sometimes when you’re on the East Coast, you don’t see, whatever, but when you get to see… I remember the first time I ever saw a Percy Harvin or Adrian Peterson, it was completely different than… So to see someone live and to actually watch them is…” Payton also made a reference to “the basement podcast with the beer logo” when talking about the variations of takes on the NFL. Schwartz does not fall into that category, especially as an eight-year NFL veteran. Ultimately, Payton once again showed his devotion to Nix ahead of a crucial 2026 season for the organization. Denver kicks off the regular season with a road game against Kansas City on Monday Night Football. articles.title: Hearts2Hearts’ ‘ICONIC HEART’ Records Highest First-Week Sales Among 5th-Gen K-Pop Girl Group Japanese Debuts
articles.summary: The title track "ICONIC HEART" also entered the Billboard Japan Hot 100 at No. 2.
articles._body: Hearts2Hearts’ ICONIC HEART debuted at No. 2 on Billboard Japan’s weekly Top Singles Sales chart released Aug. 19 — tracking the week from Aug. 10 to 16 — with first-week sales of 65,176 copies. Hearts2Hearts is an eight-member K-pop girl group consisting of JIWOO, CARMEN, YUHA, STELLA, JUUN, A-NA, IAN and YE-ON. The group debuted in South Korea in February 2025 and swept nine rookie awards, making them the most-awarded rookie act among K-pop artists who debuted that year. ICONIC HEART , released Aug. 12, marks the group’s milestone Japanese debut single. It was issued in six formats — a regular edition, first press limited edition A with a photobook, first press limited edition B with member profile sheets, first press limited edition C with postcards, first press limited edition D with initial beads, and a UNIVERSAL MUSIC STORE exclusive edition — each containing three tracks including “RUDE! (Japanese Ver.).” The title track “ICONIC HEART” also entered the Billboard Japan Hot 100 at No. 2 on the chart released the same day for the same tracking period, while topping the radio airplay metric — a strong start for a debut single. Related Hearts2Hearts on Turning Up the Brightness With ‘Lemon Tang’ & The Art of Shining Together KATSEYE Makes Brief Daisy Chain Fields Festival Appearance After Canceling Performance Kacey Musgraves Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton With 'Rainbow' & 'Here You Come Again' Live in Boston Using SoundScan Japan sales data, we examined first-week sales trends for debut releases by 5th-generation K-pop girl groups that have made their Japan debut with a physical release.  According to the sales data, ICONIC HEART sold 65,176 copies in its first week, compared with 54,187 and 5,764 copies for the other two Japanese debut releases examined. This marks the highest first-week sales figure among the three releases compared, reflecting strong fan interest in Hearts2Hearts. Beyond the group’s own appeal, their vigorous activity in Japan ahead of the release clearly paid off in building an audience before their debut even arrived — from performing “STYLE” at the Tokyo stop of the SM ENTERTAINMENT 30th anniversary world tour (SMTOWN LIVE 2025 in TOKYO, August 2025), to a release event at DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (December 2025), the early digital release of “RUDE! (Japanese Ver.)” (March 2026), and appearances on Japanese terrestrial TV (April–June 2026). Around the timing of their Japan debut, the group’s momentum and drive have been further underscored by three TOKYO GIRLS COLLECTION appearances, their first appearance on THE FIRST TAKE YouTube channel, festival and TV appearances, and being named August 2026’s Monthly Artist on TikTok and Spotify’s artist support program “Buzz Tracker.” Hearts2Hearts is also drawing global attention, having been selected for NME’s annual NME100: Essential Emerging Artists For 2026 list spotlighting rising artists from around the world, and having held solo showcases in North America. With each member bringing her own distinct charm and personality, Hearts2Hearts looks set to further establish themselves as icons of the Z-alpha generation.

articles.title: Will Stein prepares for first game week as a head coach: ‘Let the results speak for themselves.’
articles.summary: "You never know when your last day on this earth is going to be. So why not spend it at Kroger Field on September 5th, being so loud and proud of this team?"
articles._body: Fall camp is over for Will Stein and the Kentucky Wildcats. Game week is here. They’ve worked through roster battles and nursed injuries to get the best possible group out there, ready to take on Youngstown State in Week 1. Now, it’s about all of their work since the coaching change with portal and high school recruiting, spring ball, summer workouts and camp, turning into results. Stein sat down with Keith Farmer of BBN Gameday to talk about those months finally becoming days ahead of his debut on September 5, when he’ll get to coach in front of Big Blue Nation for the very first time. What did he learn about the roster he built over the offseason that now must prove itself as a team? “Well, I think more importantly than anything, I think we have a tough team. I do,” Stein said. “I think we’ve established that throughout spring ball, through fall camp, through summer. That’s what I’m looking forward to, seeing these guys play tough on Saturdays. I let the results speak for themselves — you know the old John Wooden adage, ‘The score will take care of itself.’ That’s really what we live by. I’m excited for these guys to go out and perform at Kroger Field in front of our fans.” That’s only part of the equation: the players on the field. What about Stein as a coach? This is his first shot as a head coach, too, after years of calling plays and working underneath other program leads. Now, he’s leading his own, with records attached to his name, not anyone else’s. It’s extra sweet for him, knowing he used to be a fan in those stands, cheering on his Cats. This time around, it’ll be tens of thousands cheering on the product he puts on the field — well, that’s the hope anyway. “I think it’s just going to — it’ll bring back some memories, I think, for sure,” Stein told Farmer. “I’m just excited about doing the job in that stadium here very soon and being really laser-focused, watching our guys go play and perform. And me being at my best, to be the best head coach I can be for our team on Saturdays. “It’s going to mean a lot. To sit here and say it’s not going to mean much — I mean, it’s going to be a lot. I’m representing not just me, my team, my family, but the entire state of Kentucky, you know? I think it’s such an important thing to our fans, to the state. That’s what I’m most proud of, I get to represent them.” His only request to BBN as we enter the very first game week of the Will Stein era in Lexington? Fill up Kroger Field for the players who trusted his vision and have put in the work since he arrived on campus. They get to decide just how impactful Kentucky’s home-field advantage will be this season, with countless big-time opponents coming to town, including Alabama in Week 2. “They are as big a reason that we win as our play on the field. When they’re loud, when they show up, when they tailgate the way that they do, that only makes us better as a team. I urge them to be here — which I know they will — to be loud, to be proud and to be really present in the moment,” Stein said. “Just like anybody, you never know when your last day on this earth is going to be. So why not spend it at Kroger Field on September 5th, being so loud and proud of this team? We owe it to them as a team to play well. And then they owe it to our players to come and show up and be the best fans in America.” Six days, BBN. Kentucky football is back.

Bears better be right about bet on rookie ‘beast’ after Gervon Dexter trade
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears have made one of the most consequential defensive decisions of their summer. They traded Gervon Dexter to the Atlanta Falcons for cornerback Clark Phillips III and a fifth-round pick. It immediately reshapes Chicago’s interior defensive line and places an enormous spotlight on r
articles._body: The Chicago Bears have made one of the most consequential defensive decisions of their summer. They traded Gervon Dexter to the Atlanta Falcons for cornerback Clark Phillips III and a fifth-round pick. It immediately reshapes Chicago’s interior defensive line and places an enormous spotlight on rookie Jordan van den Berg . Dexter was a productive contributor who started all 17 games last season. He recorded six sacks, making his departure a legitimate gamble rather than a routine roster move. Now, Chicago is betting that van den Berg’s unusual athletic profile and rapid development can help justify the decision. Setting the stage In Chicago’s preseason games, the coaching staff watched starting units solidify. A significant philosophical shift was also clearly taking place in the defensive tackle room. The Dexter trade opened the door for a new era along the defensive line. The timing matters here. Van den Berg had already begun receiving first-team work alongside veteran Grady Jarrett during Dexter’s absence. That seemingly gave the Bears an early look at what their post-Dexter interior could become. Unusual athletic profile At the center of this gamble stands van den Berg. He is a 6-foot-3, 310-pound defensive lineman whose athleticism has quickly become one of the most intriguing stories around Halas Hall. Chicago selected him 213th overall after he recorded 93 tackles, 20 tackles for loss and 6.5 sacks during his college career. His background makes the physical profile even more fascinating. Born and raised in South Africa, van den Berg grew up playing rugby and cricket. That rugby foundation remains evident in his playing style. He looks explosive off the snap and comfortable attacking gaps with leverage. Van den Berg does not need to become Dexter this season. He can become something different. Sure, Dexter provided a powerful interior presence. However, van den Berg offers the potential for more immediate penetration and disruption. His quickness could give the Bears defense another weapon for generating interior pressure. Behind the gamble This is where the Bears better be right, though. Dexter started every game last season and was quite effective. His career totals already stood at 13.5 sacks and 42 quarterback hits. Replacing that production is no small assignment. Van den Berg’s impact can come through disruption that creates opportunities for teammates. Still, Chicago needs its defensive tackle rotation to remain reliable throughout a 17-game season. The reward, however, could be substantial. If van den Berg develops into the disruptive interior presence his athletic profile suggests, Chicago could eventually view Dexter’s departure as a calculated personnel win rather than a costly gamble. Betting on upside The name to watch for the #Bears is 6th-round rookie DT Jordan van den Berg, who has been off the charts in camp and even earned reps with the starters. His emergence was part of the reason Chicago felt comfortable trading Gervon Dexter, who has wanted a new contract. https://t.co/IeZM84h3lT pic.twitter.com/FMLyFDmE8B — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) August 30, 2026 Phillips addresses a need in the secondary , while van den Berg gives Chicago another athletic interior piece. Now, the responsibility falls on the young defensive lineman to make the gamble look smart. If van den Berg’s athleticism translates into consistent disruption, the Bears may eventually look back at Dexter’s departure as the moment they found the next piece of their defensive puzzle. If it does not, Chicago will have willingly weakened an established position without an immediate replacement of comparable production. That is the gamble. And after making it, the Bears better be right about their young defensive “beast.” The post Bears better be right about bet on rookie ‘beast’ after Gervon Dexter trade appeared first on ClutchPoints .

Show HN: Murmell – Collaborative cloud canvas for coding agents
articles.summary:
Hey HN!

I'm Moss'Ab. Murmell (https://murmell.com) is an infinite canvas where coding agents run together in the cloud instead of on your laptop.

It's like Google Docs, except the other editors are you, your teammates, and a set of agents all w
articles._body: Hey HN! I'm Moss'Ab. Murmell ( https://murmell.com ) is an infinite canvas where coding agents run together in the cloud instead of on your laptop. It's like Google Docs, except the other editors are you, your teammates, and a set of agents all working in the same canvas. Short demo: https://app.murmell.com/demo The idea came out of a YC hackathon. We were trying to build the thing under extrem pressure, deploying at the very last minute, but with several agents working in parallel, all the branches collided. Everything broke at the worst possible moment and we spent the end of it untangling instead of building. We didn't win. Murmell is the thing I wished we'd had that day: one place where the agents and the people can see each other work, on machines that don't belong to any one laptop. Each canvas gets its own machine in the cloud. Close your laptop and the agents keep going; open it again anywhere, or have a teammate open the same canvas by sending him the link, and you're inside the same session rather than a copy of it. The work stays exactly where you left it : same branches, same dev server still running, so an agent picks up mid-task instead of starting from scratch. And you can literally collaborate with your team like google docs, it's se same system, read of edit link, they connect they can type on your terminal, you can see their mouse, wich terminal they're typing in. And you can interact wich each other sessions, it's pretty useful instead of sharing a screen, copying a prompt, etc. The hardest part was building the cloud infrastructure, trying to make it scalable, and to manage the sessions to make the best experience possible: when the VM shuts down, it snapshots everything and restores everything when you come back, even the conversation with your terminal, it's stored with a system that i built like obsidian wich also make you save a little bit of tokens. So the answer to that hackathon is file claiming. Before an agent works on something, it claims the paths, it's an exclusive lease with a TTL, so nothing stays locked forever because an agent died mid-task. And if another agent asking for the same file gets denied, the denial tells it who holds it, how long is left, and to either pick other work in its scope or message the holder (the agents can communicate through the board) A watcher classifies every write, so if anything writes inside someone else's claim it shows up on the canvas as a collision right then, instead of as a merge conflict you discover an hour later. And when an agent is done, it can hand its claim to the next one. And agents never hold your provider keys either, they get a token, and a proxy on the container's loopback swaps it for the real key on the way out, which makes a leaked token worthless outside that container. Murmell is paid. I've put prices at 50% off for now, because it's still not where I want to take it yet. It is fully usable though: I develop Murmell with Murmell, every day (and tbh it's save soooo much time to us with my cofounder) And to be fully transparent with the actual prices it costs us much than we are earning but the goal is to collect feedback to make Murmell as good as possible For context: I'm 19, a 4th year computer engineering student, and I've been on this for about three and a half months, day and night. I discovered claude code after my father showed me first Windsurf (today Devin) for a python homework in 2024, and i think i never went somewhere without my laptop since then lol. So feel free to comment or to give feedback, or even subscribe to support the project :) Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49499167 Points: 7 # Comments: 2

articles._body: Florida State head coach Mike Norvell is under significant pressure as he heads into the 2026 season . Despite the scrutiny, he remains focused on his preparations, stating at ACC Media Days that he fears only regret, not failure. The intensity surrounding Norvell’s position increased after Florida State’s inconsistent performance in its Week 0 season opener. Fans and analysts quickly expressed their frustration over the team’s repeated execution errors. In response, national college football analyst and former Seminoles quarterback Danny Kanell stepped in to provide a more measured perspective. On social media platform X, Kanell shared his thoughts on FSU’s performance: “Some thoughts on FSU. I’m not surprised by the overreaction to the performance. However, I saw a team that did some good things. There’s clearly a lot to improve, but that’s normal for a team with significant turnover and no true preseason. 1-0 is all that matters.” He highlighted that with major offseason roster changes and no traditional exhibition games, it is common to experience growing pains. Kanell emphasized that securing the win is the ultimate goal. The situation at quarterback is also evolving as the program moves forward with new starting quarterback Ashton Daniels. Former Florida State quarterback Thomas Castellanos has recently received a temporary court injunction granting him a fifth year of eligibility, allowing for a one-week portal window to transfer to a new program. With Castellanos departing and Daniels stepping in, Norvell and the Seminoles aim to correct their mistakes and build momentum to silence their critics. articles.title: Olivia Rodrigo and philanthropist Melinda French Gates raise $20 million for women’s well-being with a benefit show recalling ’90s feminist push
articles.summary: Melinda French Gates pledged $10 million through her Pivotal Ventures in a surprise appearance at the start of Rodrigo's set, praising her for "showing a new generation how much their voices matter."
articles._body: Evoking the same do-it-yourself pop-rock feminism of her ’90s musical influences,  Olivia Rodrigo  raised $20 million for women’s well-being with a benefit show that activated her young audience. Daisy Chain Fields united a women-led lineup boasting queer pop star Chappell Roan , breakout rapper Doechii and riot grrrl pioneers Bikini Kill behind issues of women’s health, workplace protections and legal rights. Ahead of Saturday’s festival in Irvine, California, Rodrigo announced the show had already raised enough to make a $10 million donation to 10 nonprofit partners including Planned Parenthood, National Women’s Law Center and Black Mamas Matter Alliance. Philanthropist  Melinda French Gates  pledged another $10 million through her Pivotal Ventures in a surprise appearance at the start of Rodrigo’s set, praising her for “showing a new generation how much their voices matter.” Rodrigo said the festival’s artists and activists give her hope despite the “regression of women’s rights” today. “That’s actually why I fell in love with the name ‘Daisy Chain,’” she said Friday. “It served as a reminder of how individual parts can come together to create something strong and unbreakable.” Rodrigo, 23, has made a name channeling the rage and dissatisfaction of modern romance into chart-topping songs that are equal parts Taylor Swift and Alanis Morissette. Now, she looks to bridge the gap between Gen Z and nonprofits, which have  struggled to build relationships with younger donors  who tend to prefer informal ways of giving. The connection is not lost on Daisy Chain Fields attendees. “People don’t join together and mobilize unless they feel connected to the group that is mobilizing,” said Grace Slevin, 24. “What’s better than music?” All-star benefit concerts have proven popular for driving millions of dollars toward everything from  refugee relief  to  pandemic response .  But it’s been decades since a young artist with Rodrigo’s following brought her peers together for gender justice. That focus comes as President Donald Trump attempts to overhaul family planning grants that reproductive health clinics use to provide birth control and treat sexually transmitted infections. His administration  paused $27.5 million last year  for such organizations, including some Planned Parenthood affiliates, before  officials agreed to restore the money . For Slevin, an Orange County, California, resident who does anti-sex-trafficking advocacy, Daisy Chain Fields embodies the sentiment of “be who you needed when you were younger.” She loves that attendees are welcome to learn about the beneficiaries’ work in addition to donating. Nonprofit partners engaged with fans in Daisy Chain Fields’ “philanthropy village.” Festivalgoers collected pins from booths as they learned about health services from Planned Parenthood or pay tribute to caregivers through the National Domestic Workers Alliance. An art installation by the Guerilla Girls, anonymous artist activists, invited fans to air their grievances on chalkboards. Handwritten responses included “PROTECT QUEER KIDS!” and “Put women in charge and pay us more!!!” as well as “ICE OUT!” and “ABORTION RIGHTS 4 ALL.” Younger generations expect a level of authenticity beyond a “pseudo-sort-of-progressiveness,” Slevin said. “They can see just how deeply intertwined the music is with the cause,” she said. “It’s not just, like, a second thought.” Do you get déjà vu? Rodrigo’s effort recalls ’90s feminist push Rodrigo took inspiration from  Lilith Fair , the all-women festival that raised $10 million for charity from 1997 to 1999.  Sarah McLachlan , who founded the show to dispel the music industry’s notion they couldn’t book women consecutively, performed with Rodrigo Saturday. Planned Parenthood National Director of Arts and Entertainment Caren Spruch recalled working on Lilith Fair, adding that concert outreach is an important tool to reach people “where they are.” That culture-shifting work grows more important during times like this, she acknowledged, when  abortion clinics are closing in restrictive states and anti-abortion groups are  pushing the courts to limit access  to drugs most commonly used in abortion. Rodrigo, Spruch said, talks about those topics with “no shame or stigma.” As she did with other nonprofits, the  three-time Grammy winner appeared in informational videos on Planned Parenthood’s social media. “All of that does so much to help us normalize the whole range of reproductive health and rights,” Spruch said. Intergenerational change Melissa Shaw, 33, drove to the festival from Tucson, Arizona, with her 8-year-old daughter. They didn’t plan to spend the day camped out for close-up views. Shaw wanted to let her daughter ask questions as they explored the nonprofits and visited art installations. She appreciates that Rodrigo is not only promoting well-known organizations such as Planned Parenthood, but also groups focused specifically on Black maternal health or baby formula access. “It’s really important for me as a parent to expose my daughter to celebrities who set that example,” Shaw said. To her, the lineup seemed intentionally curated to attract multiple generations. Her daughter loves Rodrigo and Roan, and she herself grew up listening to Bikini Kill and fellow performer Santigold. She saw many mother-daughter duos sharing their festival plans online. The festival’s nonprofit partners were eager to join that multigenerational community of women, too. “At a time when decisions about our bodies, our health, our safety and our futures are being made for us not by us, a day built around care and community is its own kind of statement,” FreeFrom founder Sonya Passi said i
