articles._body: The Chicago Bears have been shopping young defensive tackle Gervon Dexter for a while now, looking for a trade. On Sunday, the Bears finally made a deal, sending Dexter to the Atlanta Falcons for a cornerback and a 2027 fifth-round pick . “The #Bears are trading DT Gervon Dexter Sr to the #Falcons, as they add a player who started 17 games last season, per me and @AdamSchefter,” NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported. “The Bears are getting back Clark Phillips and 5th rounder.” Dexter is still just 24 years old. The former Florida Gator was a second-round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft. However, he was surplus to requirements in Chicago, so at least the Bears got something in return with this Falcons trade. Phillips, the corner coming back, is also 24 and was a 2023 fourth-round selection out of Utah. The young Bears DT, who is now a Falcon , started all 17 games last season and 15-of-15 in the season before that. He has 13.5 career sacks and 42 QB hits, which is impressive from an interior defensive line position. Grady Jarrett and Shemar Turner are expected to be the starting DTs on the Bears’ D, although the former is 33 and the latter is recovering from an ACL tear and isn’t expected back for a few more weeks at minimum. Offseason free agent additions Neville Gallimore and Kentavious Street will fill Dexter’s vacated position in the meantime. As for Phillips, he will be a depth corner for the Bears after missing most of the 2025 season with a torn triceps. articles._body: A schedule can make or break a season. Ask any coach. Purdue’s 2026 slate is filled with challenges and opportunities. This series is a breakdown of what’s ahead for the Boilermakers this fall. Next up: Who Purdue doesn’t play. • Toughest non-conference game: Notre Dame, Sept. 26 • Toughest conference: at Indiana, Nov. 28 • Who they don’t play: Michigan, Ohio State, Rutgers, USC, Oregon, Northwestern, Nebraska, Michigan State • Easiest game: Indiana State, Sept. 4 • Best chance to be upset: • Best chance to pull an upset : • Toughest stretch: The logic:  Look, Purdue probably will be favored in only one game this season: The opener vs. Indiana State. But–and it’s a big but–Purdue could be a slight favorite when Wake Forest visits in Week Two. But know this: Wake is led by second-year coach Jake Dickert , who is a rising star. The 42-year-old forged a 9-4 mark in his debut in Winston-Salem in 2025, capped by a bowl win. The nine victories were more than Wake had had in its previous two seasons combined. Prior to that, Dickert went 23-20 in four seasons at Washington State. The history: The last time the Demon Deacons came to Ross-Ade Stadium, they stunned Purdue: 24-21 in 2002. The Boilers were done in by five turnovers and three missed Berin Lacevic fourth quarter field goals (46, 40 and 44 yards)–-the final miss coming with 21 seconds left in the game. The teams last met in 2003 in Winston-Salem, with Purdue winning 16-10. The lowdown: Wake is picked to finish 12th in the 17-team ACC by Athlon. The Deacons should have a good defense. And there is experience, speed, depth and size. A big key: QB play by Gio Lopez . The bottom line: It may be an overstatement to say the second game of a season could make or break Purdue. But, it’s the truth. Following the visit from the Deacs, Purdue plays at UCLA and then comes home to play Notre Dame. You get the picture. Could the Boilermakers toppled Wake AND UCLA to be 3-0 when the Fighting Irish invade Ross-Ade Stadium? But a loss to the Demon Deacons could set up a 1-2 start prior to ND’s visit–and who knows where the season could tumble to. 2026 Purdue schedule Date Opponent Sept. 4 (Friday) Indiana State Sept. 12 Wake Forest Sept. 19 at UCLA Sept. 26 Notre Dame Oct. 3 at Illinois Oct. 10 Minnesota Oct. 16 (Friday) Washington Oct. 24 OFF Oct. 31 at Penn State Nov. 7 Maryland Nov. 14 at Iowa Nov. 21 Wisconsin Nov. 28 at Indiana More:  Join the discussion on Knucklehead Central  | Subscribe to GoldandBlack.com for 75% off  |  Subscribe to GoldandBlack.com’s YouTube channel

articles.summary: NC State’s defense didn’t have an answer for Virginia quarterback Beau Pribula, especially on the ground, as Virginia raced to a 34-8 win on Saturday afternoon at Scott Stadium. The result is likely to send the defense back to the drawing board for the next two weeks before its home open
articles._body: NC State’s defense didn’t have an answer for Virginia quarterback Beau Pribula , especially on the ground, as Virginia raced to a 34-8 win on Saturday afternoon at Scott Stadium. The result is likely to send the defense back to the drawing board for the next two weeks before its home opener against Richmond. Senior linebacker Popo Aguirre led the unit with 18 total tackles, while defensive backs Ronnie Royal III and King Mack added seven each. Royal accounted for the lone pass breakup, while the defense only logged three tackles for a loss as Virginia picked up positive yardage on nearly every play it ran. Sophomore linebacker LaCorian Hodge was the unit’s highest-graded player at 77.5, while sophomore defensive lineman Adrian Farrow and Mack were right behind him at 77.1 and 72.1, respectively. Sophomore nose guard Josiah Victor was the team’s lowest-rated defender at 49.9. Let’s take a look at NC State’s full list of initial PFF grades and snap counts with notes to put some of the data into context. NC State snap counts and PFF grades: Defense at Virginia Defensive line Name Snap count Pass Run Grade Adrian Farrow 3 0 3 77.1 Omarian Abraham 8 1 7 68.9 Isaiah Shirley 27 3 24 64.4 KaTron Evans 29 3 26 63.3 Chase Bond 32 6 26 62.7 Joseph Adedire 33 8 25 59.8 AJ Prim 35 7 28 59.7 Colby Cronk 8 4 4 59.7 Josiah Victor 28 6 22 49.9 Inside linebacker Name Snap count Pass Run Grade LaCorian Hodge 17 3 14 77.5 Popo Aguirre 62 11 51 61.7 AJ Richardson 55 14 41 58.6 Outside linebacker Name Snap count Pass Run Grade Ke’Von Carter 34 5 29 69.4 Josh Warren 3 2 1 67.7 Elijah Satchell 8 2 6 60.9 Sterling Dixon 2 2 0 57.6 Harvey Dyson 48 12 36 56.9 Cornerback Name Snap count Pass Run Grade Brian Nelson II 66 14 52 66.7 Jaren Sensabaugh 35 9 26 60.5 Ty White 22 4 18 57.3 Jackson Vick 35 5 30 56.2 Safety Name Snap count Pass Run Grade King Mack 43 12 31 72.1 Ronnie Royal III 37 8 29 68.2 Tristan Teasdell 25 2 23 64.3 Brody Barnhardt 31 6 25 62.7 Asaad Brown 22 5 17 60.3 Takeaways from NC State’s snap counts and PFF grades — NC State didn’t have many opportunities to rush the passer since Virginia only threw the ball 11 times, but it still only generated three quarterback pressures. Dyson and Hodge teamed up for the only sack, which PFF logged as two pressures, while Carter also posted one in the game. — For it being the first game, missed tackles weren’t as bad as they could have been. The Wolfpack was credited with six across six different defenders: Teasdell, Prim, Royal, Sensabaugh, Barnhardt and Richardson. Aguirre, meanwhile, didn’t miss a stop and totaled 18 tackles in his Wolfpack debut. — NC State accumulated 31 “stops,” which PFF dubs a tackle that resulted in a failure for the offense. Aguirre led the team with five such plays, while Carter had four, and Bond, Dyson and Evans had three each to pace the Wolfpack. Victor had two, while 11 others logged one in the defeat. — The unit’s pass coverage wasn’t tested often, but when it was, Virginia found success. Every player that was targeted in the game gave up at least one reception as Beau Pribula was 9-of-11 passing for 155 yards and two touchdowns. Aguirre was the only defender to allow multiple receptions, conceding 58 yards, including 36 after the catch. Vick was labeled as the primary defender on the ‘Hoos 47-yard passing touchdown, his only target of the afternoon.

articles.title: Rooster Reads: A history of Gamecock athletics in 10 titles
articles.summary: Alan Piercy is the author of A Gamecock Odyssey: University of South Carolina Sports in the Independent Era (1971-1991). Dusting off the shelf to delve into a few recent works, and a bevy of deep cuts There was a time when the University of South Carolina first stepped into the bracing waters of Sou
articles._body: Alan Piercy is the author of A Gamecock Odyssey: University of South Carolina Sports in the Independent Era (1971-1991) . Dusting off the shelf to delve into a few recent works, and a bevy of deep cuts There was a time when the University of South Carolina first stepped into the bracing waters of Southeastern Conference membership, that fans fretted about the Gamecocks’ perceived lack of history. It was a shared sense that maybe Carolina didn’t quite measure up to the storied programs like Alabama, LSU, and Tennessee, among others. Perhaps, we thought to ourselves in moments of quiet reflection, or in confessional tones whispered to fellow fans, we were just lucky to be there. We were in the throes of “new guy syndrome,” adjusting to our newfound identity after twenty years of independent status, a winless bowl record, and a conspicuously lonely trophy case. As Carolina charted its course through the choppy waters of those early SEC years, insecurities abounded. But thirty-five years into our alliance with the greatest conference in the land, Gamecock fans can gaze into the middle distance through eyes of chipped granite and proclaim with a confident sniff, “ Damn right we belong here! ”  Admittedly, the University of South Carolina took an unorthodox and often rocky path to this point. A founding member of the ACC, Carolina left that conference in a huff in 1971, arguably the greatest self-inflicted setback in the history of Division I sports. While the ACC thrived thanks to lucrative television deals during a golden age of men’s basketball, the period is mostly remembered by Gamecock fans as “ The Wilderness .” Those decades of the 1970’s and 80’s were a struggle on many fronts, though the period was not without highlights and fun times, as detailed in my own 2023 book, A Gamecock Odyssey. But beyond the Wilderness years, the history of USC sports is deep and rich, and finely detailed in a growing list of books that should be required reading for any serious Gamecock fan. What follows is a list of ten additional histories that shed light on a broad swath of programs, coaches, players, and eras across more than a century of Carolina athletics. At the end I’ll include a brand new release, and a forthcoming book I think you’ll be excited about. So, grab your readers, settle into your favorite chair, and let’s dive in:  The author’s library of Gamecock (or Gamecock adjacent) titles The Carolina-Clemson Game – 1896-1966 , Don Barton (The State Printing Company, Columbia, 1967) – A 1949 USC graduate, Barton served as Sports Information Director at Carolina from 1950 to 1959, and even doubled as Gamecock tennis coach in 1954 and 1955. Barton published a number of books on Carolina sports, including “They Wore Garnet & Black” and “Frank McGuire: The Life and Times of a Basketball Legend” (both highlighted below). His first volume, covering the Carolina-Clemson rivalry, is a tough find, but a delight if you can get your hands on a copy. It details every game in the legendary series, from the inaugural contest in 1896 through Paul Dietzel’s first season in 1966. Detailed with fast-paced narratives from all seventy games, the summaries of each contest include full rosters and box scores. Barton’s compelling prose and wry humor bring the legendary clashes of the bygone Big Thursday era to life. This book is a treasure for anyone interested in the history of this great rivalry and fans of both programs. The Cadillac , Mike Chibbaro (Thirty-Seven Publishing, 2014) – Chibbaro cut his teeth in the publishing world as sports editor of The Gamecock student newspaper during his time at USC. A 1981 Carolina grad, Chibbaro went on to a successful business career before retiring in 2012. Since, he has devoted his time to leadership development consulting and, fortunately for Gamecock fans, chronicling the exploits of USC football legend Steve “The Cadillac” Wadiak. The gold standard of Gamecock rushers before a guy named George Rogers arrived on campus in the late ‘70’s, Wadiak starred for Carolina from 1948-1951, and still holds the program record for longest run from scrimmage (96 yards vs George Washington on October 27, 1950). The Chicago-born son of Ukrainian immigrants still ranks fourth on the all-time rushing list at USC with 2,878 career yards. Wadiak tragically died in an automobile accident shortly after his senior season. His #37 was the first number or jersey retired by USC in any sport. Wadiak was elected to the USC Athletics Hall of Fame as a member of the inaugural class in 1967. Roundball Culture , Dan Klores (A.M. Press, 1980) – Another hard-to-find volume (a paperback version currently lists on Amazon for $2,999, though eBay has offerings in the $100 to $200 range), Klores’ Roundball Culture documents Frank McGuire’s iconic 16-year run as head men’s basketball coach at the University of South Carolina between 1964 and 1980. This book has developed somewhat of a cult following among Gamecock fans of a certain age, and provides an insider’s perspective on the program from someone who cultivated close friendships with many players and coaches of that era. A Peabody Award-winning documentary filmmaker, Klores attended USC during McGuire’s heyday in the late 1960s and early 1970s. The New York City-based Klores is a guy who knew where the bodies were buried during that era of Gamecock hoops, and he wrote this book with trademark wit and uncompromising honesty. For anyone who remembers those halcyon days, or is curious to learn more about this drama-filled era when USC men’s basketball was the hottest ticket around, this book is indispensable. Frank McGuire: The Life and Times of a Basketball Legend , Don Barton and Bob Fulton (Summerhouse Press, 1995) – Before Dawn Staley and Ray Tanner brought multiple national championships to Columbia for their respective programs, the dominant figure in the history of Gamecock athletics was Frank J. McGuire. Clos

Recap: No. 1 Stanford Women’s Soccer dominates No. 17 UCLA
articles.summary: On Thursday, No. 1 Stanford women’s soccer defeated No. 17 UCLA 3-0.
articles._body: Credit: Fausto Ibarra/ISI Photos On Thursday, No. 1 Stanford women’s soccer defeated No. 17 UCLA 3-0. Bella Winn (20:58), Brooke Holden (23:45), and Charlotte Kohler (81:38) scored for the Cardinal. Rhiannon Stewart was the winning goalkeeper for the Cardinal with two saves, playing all 90 minutes while Daphne Nakfoor was the losing goalkeeper for UCLA with eight saves and three goals allowed in 90 minutes played. Stanford improves to 4-0-0 overall while UCLA falls to 1-2-1. BOX SCORE: UCLA at Stanford-Thursday, August 27 th “Yeah, I thought it was an incredible team performance,” Stanford head coach Paul Ratcliffe said after the match. “Every player that played tonight stepped up and played at a really high level. So I couldn’t be more proud of the entire group.” Stanford got off to a hot start with corner kicks at 3:43 and 5:08. At 13:58, UCLA’s Asa Yamazaki g ot called for a yellow card while Stanford also got their third corner kick of the match. Stanford would get corner kicks at 19:17 and 20:29 before Bella Winn had an absolutely sensational self-volley goal to make it 1-0 at 23:45, finding the top right of the goal off her left foot as Sadie Leal-Schuman got the assist. “Yeah, I mean, I think I just trusted myself, trusted our preparation,” Winn said of her goal. “We work a lot on shooting and finishing and just trying to have composure. I knew my teammates trusted me and so when the ball came in, I just really tried to take a touch and hit it as hard as I could. Aim low and hard, just like the coaches always tells us. We practice volleys a lot and definitely pays off.” Shortly thereafter at 23:45, Leal-Schuman would get a free kick from the corner area. She would place the ball perfectly to Brooke Holden, who headed the ball into the top left of the goal making 2-0. Stanford was now in firm control. “I think our energy coming into the game,” Winn said of the key to their early goal scoring. “Coming out of the locker room, winning the warmup is something we always say and I think that’s super important setting the tone early. We have a lot of energy coming from the bench and everyone knows, since we have a lot of depth, there’s competition and we need to start strong. We know we have a target on our back. And so coming out and trying to put one in early definitely helps set the tone and shows other teams we’re not scared and we’re here to play.” UCLA would get corner kicks at 35:58 and 38:29, unable to get on the scoreboard before halftime. 2-0 Stanford led going into the tent. UCLA needed to flip the script in the second half. To UCLA’s credit, they wouldn’t make things easy on Stanford in the second half. UCLA would get a corner kick at 46:18, applying immediate pressure on Stanford. UCLA also didn’t allow Stanford to get a single corner kick the entire second half. It wasn’t until 81:38 that Stanford found their third goal of the match as Charlotte Kohler found the bottom right of the goal off her left foot thanks to an assist from Bella Winn and Peyton Marinos . The ball squeezed past Nakfoor, who wasn’t quite able to block the shot. “Yeah, Bella scored an incredible goal,” Ratclife said. “One of the best goals I’ve seen in a while. And then Charlotte to end with that goal was fantastic and then Brooke had another goal I believe it was. So yeah, just three outstanding goals and could have had a few more, but three is pretty impressive…She’s gotten better in all aspects of her game [Kohler]. But definitely goal scoring. I mean, she’s scoring every game right now. She’s on pace to score almost every game, which is remarkable. But yeah, she’s such good player and wants to learn, wants to grow, wants to get better. She’s very professional about all of her performances and how she prepares, so I’m not surprised to see her getting so much success. She definitely earns it and deserves it.” From there, Stanford would win 3-0 as UCLA was unable to get on the board. It was a strong, convincing win for Stanford. Especially given they were down multiple players due to the U-20 World Cup. “Yeah, it showed the quality of our squad,” Ratcliffe said of winning handily with six players away. “I thought players stepped in, Rhiannon in goal was amazing. Her first full match. I thought she was incredible. And then Sadie in midfield was incredible.  I think she had two assists. So, so many big performances from everyone, kind of moving up as a few players leave. So yeah, couldn’t be more proud of the whole group. “It’s really important [to get that third goal]. Yeah, it’s really important because you’re up 2-0, if they score one, momentum can change on you and then you’re in trouble. It could be 2-2. So, to get the third really solidifies the victory and I thought Charlotte did a great, really a nice pass. It was Bella and Peyton. Good little weighted pass in the space and Charlotte can’t stop scoring. She keeps scoring for every game for us, so she’s been incredible.” “Yeah, I mean, it’s a great win,” Winn echoed. “Like, we talk about making statement wins and protecting our home field and I think today it was a full-team effort and we really showed ourselves and everyone watching we have all we need right here and obviously, we’re missing some players and we love them, but every single person on the team today gave their all and put everything into this full 90 minute game and it really paid off and it’s great to see how much depth we have going into season.” Like other matches this season, Stanford spread the scoring around, not getting goals from just one or two people. They continue to show an ability to score from a variety of places. That makes them extremely dangerous. Especially when you combine that with a tough back row on defense. “Yeah, the whole back four: Sammy, Lily, London, and Aniya. I thought they had a really strong performance,” Ratcliffe said. “To get a shutout against a team of the caliber of UCLA is not easy. So, I was really proud of them. And then Milly p

articles.title: Keenan Allen arrested on 2 DWI charges literally hours after making Colts debut
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts wrapped up their preseason on Saturday. Indy lost 25-16 against Detroit with final roster cuts on the horizon. One Colts player just got into some legal troubles right before those decisions need to happen. And mere hours following his debut in a Colts uniform. Colts wide r
articles._body: The Indianapolis Colts wrapped up their preseason on Saturday. Indy lost 25-16 against Detroit with final roster cuts on the horizon . One Colts player just got into some legal troubles right before those decisions need to happen. And mere hours following his debut in a Colts uniform. Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen was arrested for DUI on early Sunday morning, per Nathan Brown of IndyStar. Allen was arrested on two preliminary misdemeanor charges : DWI with a blood alcohol content of 0.08 or more and DWI endangering a person. Indy released a short statement after news of Allen’s arrest broke. “We are aware of the incident involving Keenan Allen last night,” the Colts said in a statement. “We are in the process of gathering more information and have no further comment at this time.” The Colts signed Allen to a one-year contract worth $8.32 million on August 17th. Allen’s arrest came just hours after the 14-year veteran made his debut in a Colts uniform on Saturday. He hauled in one reception for 24 yards against the Lions. Indianapolis had big plans for Allen after signing him, especially with Alec Pierce still injured and his Week 1 status still up in the air. It is currently unclear how the Colts, or the NFL, will respond to Allen’s arrest ahead of the regular season. Allen proved over the past two seasons that he is still capable of playing at a high level. He went over 70 receptions, 700 receiving yards, and four touchdowns with the Bears in 2024 and Chargers in 2025. If the Colts got that level of production from Allen in 2026, then their offense should be in great shape. Colts fans should keep their eyes peeled for further updates as this story develops. The Colts open the regular season with a home game against the Ravens. That contest kicks off at 1PM ET on September 13th from Lucas Oil Stadium in Indy. Eight college football games kicked off Saturday during Week 0, beginning with second-year North Carolina head coach Bill Belichick securing the biggest win of his short collegiate tenure with a 15-10 victory over TCU in Dublin, Ireland. And while the rest of the college football world kicks off later this week with Week 1 action beginning Thursday, ESPN still updated its weekly Football Power Index (FPI) rankings following those eight Week 0 games. That included just one team in the preseason Top 25 — No. 14 USC , which easily dispatched San Jose State , 42-26, in Los Angeles. Despite the victory, the Trojans held pat at No. 18 in ESPN’s FPI ranking. Ohio State (28.7) Despite ending 2025 on a two-game losing streak, the Buckeyes opens the 2026 season as the consensus No. 1-ranked team in both the AP and USA Today Top 25 polls. And ESPN’s FPI agrees. Featuring a loaded roster that includes 2025 Heisman Trophy finalist Julian Sayin at quarterback and superstar Jeremiah Smith at receiver, Ohio State is once again expected to be among the leading contenders to win this season’s College Football Playoff national championship. 2. Texas Longhorns (26.9) Much like Ohio State, which it plays in Week 2, the Longhorns feature one of college football’s most talent-rich rosters, led by star quarterback Arch Manning . Sixth-year head coach Steve Sarkisian dove into the transfer portal this offseason and came away with No. 1 receiver Cam Coleman . But whether Texas continues to climb this ranking or drop like it did last season will depend on how it fares Sept. 12 against the Buckeyes. Thankfully, this year’s game is in Austin, providing the Longhorns a welcomed home field advantage after last year’s road loss in Columbus. 3. Notre Dame Fighting Irish (25.9) Notre Dame enters 2026 with a boulder-sized chip on its shoulder after the Irish were notoriously snubbed at the end of last season and missed out on the 2025 College Football Playoff. This year, though, Marcus Freeman returns with a loaded roster, led by a rising star at quarterback in CJ Carr . But while Carr is already garnering some preseason Heisman Trophy buzz, he’s not alone. Notre Dame also returns an experienced defense, which is anchored by lockdown cornerback Leonard Moore . 4. Oregon Ducks (25.3) The Ducks land at No. 4 in ESPN’s FPI despite returning what is considered the most experienced roster in college football in 2026. That effort was aided by the somewhat surprising return of star quarterback Dante Moore, who opted to forgo the 2026 NFL Draft in favor of running it back in Eugene. As usual, Oregon head coach Dan Lanning still made a splash in the transfer portal by landing safety Koi Perich from Minnesota to strengthen an already strong Ducks secondary. Oregon also returns its entire starting defensive line, led by seniors A’Mauri Washington and Matayo Uiagalelei . 5. But while Georgia’s offense will have some new faces in 2026, especially at receiver, the Bulldogs’ defense is considered among the most talented in the game this season. That’s in large part to an elite secondary led by junior safety KJ Bolden and junior cornerback Ellis Robinson IV . 6. Indiana Hoosiers (23.1) The reigning national champion Hoosiers begin the 2026 season flying a little under the radar after being ranked No. 6 in both the AP and USA Today polls. Of course, ESPN FPI’s rankings is of the same mind. That’s likely due to head coach Curt Cignetti ‘s complete roster overhaul this offseason, beginning with the arrival of senior quarterback Josh Hoover from TCU to replace 2025 Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza . Despite all that change, the Hoosiers have established themselves as perennial title contenders. 7. articles.summary: With the official 53-man roster deadline hours away, the Dallas Cowboys recently acquired Broderick Jones from the Pittsburgh Steelers. The trade came in the wake of the Cowboys’ attempt to strengthen their offensive line. Soon after the transaction, sports analyst Skip Bayless weighed in on the
articles._body: With the official 53-man roster deadline hours away, the Dallas Cowboys recently acquired Broderick Jones from the Pittsburgh Steelers. The trade came in the wake of the Cowboys’ attempt to strengthen their offensive line. Soon after the transaction, sports analyst Skip Bayless weighed in on the decision. Bayless dropped a skeptical take on the Jones trade while suggesting Dallas is not sure about their starting tackles . “Cowboys trade for Steelers’ Broderick Jones because the Cowboys are not sure about either of their starting tackles. Neither am I,” he tweeted. In addition to Jones, the Steelers are also sending their fourth-round pick in return for two draft picks, namely the third and sixth picks, to the Cowboys. However, as Bayless questioned, the Cowboys have been struggling on the tackle front given Tyler Guyton and Terence Steele’s performance slump. There hasn’t been much noise during the preseason action or training camp, and the Cowboys were looking for another option. Though the trade comes with its complications as well. Only last season, Jones dealt with a concerning neck injury after colliding with linebacker Dominique Robinson during the Chicago Bears game. The injury required neck fusion surgery followed by a long rehab timeline. He was shut down for the season and missed out on what could have been his last six games of the season. Jones now arrives in Dallas fresh off his training camp clearance. Though he has said to have lost significant weight, fans are hoping for a healthy stretch once the season kicks off on September 9. articles.title: Previewing ACC preseason favorite Miami with CaneSport
articles.summary: CaneSport publisher Gary Ferman breaks down the Miami Hurricanes, the preseason favorite to win the ACC.
articles._body: CaneSport publisher Gary Ferman breaks down the Miami Hurricanes, the preseason favorite to win the ACC. Will SMU face Mario Cristobal’s team in the ACC Championship? 1. Can you describe the overall state of the program coming off the 2025 season, considering Miami reached the National Championship? Miami has the best state of the program in more than two decades. The Hurricanes really have it all going right now. They have a top shelf roster and are recruiting as well as anybody in the country. They have a quarterback in Darian Mensah that they feel is good enough to win a national championship. They have solid depth on both sides of the ball and are loaded at the skill positions. Coaches always want more, but it’s very difficult to poke holes in this Miami roster. The university is funding NIL at the highest level. The institutional commitment is unprecedented. So the State of The U is pretty darn good right now. 2. Heading into season, what are the biggest questions or concerns for each side of the ball? I think the biggest concern on offense is breaking in a new offensive line. The talent is there, the chemistry is probably not. The running back room is loaded and there will be times that Miami wants to lean on that group. So the line is obviously critical in that regard. Freshman left tackle Jackson Cantwell , the nation’s top recruit, has the size and ability to be great, but he is still a true freshman. Right tackle Matt McCoy is making the switch from guard. Samson Okunlola at left guard is being asked to be a full-time starter for the first time. Max Buchanan is a new starter at right guard. Ryan Rodriguez is regaining a starting spot at center after losing the job to portal additions the past two seasons. A lot of people would say linebacker is the biggest concern on defense but both starters are back there. Even though Miami signed end Damon Wilson out of Missouri and he had nine sacks in the SEC last season, I’ll say pass rush is the biggest defensive concern just because Rueben Bain and Akheem Mesidor are first round talents that have to be replaced. That seems easy when you look at Wilson and former 5 stars Marquise Lightfoot and Armondo Blount , but it really is not something that should be taken for granted because they have not done it in games yet. 3. What are the strengths or areas in the best place heading into the 2026 season for the Hurricanes? Quarterback, running back and receiver on offense for sure. Miami should be able to score points in bunches.  That’s why they invested in Mensah. It makes no sense to have all the talent at the skill positions and not have a QB to pull it all together.  4. Who are the players who could step up in these roles and/or surprise some people? I think Nickel will win the backup QB battle pretty easily. Mark Fletcher won the starting RB job with his postseason efforts for Miami but let’s not forget that Jordan Lyle was the starter at the beginning of last season and Girard Pringle played great when he was on the field. I am expecting Josh Moore to step up and claim the starting wr job alongside Malachi Toney and Duke transfer Cooper Barkate . And on the defensive line I am expecting Ahmad Moten to be a steady guy at tackle with Justin Scott and Wilson and Lightfoot to win starting honors at end. 5. Who’s a key transfer that you expect to be a household name in the 2026 season other than Darian Mensah? Damon Wilson for sure. NIne sacks in the SEC is impressive and suggests he could get more during an ACC schedule.  Going off that, can you share your impressions of Mensah so far? Mensah is the real deal. He walked right in and became an instant leader. On the field he is poised, accurate and consistent. He also throws a nice deep ball.  6. Can you list a couple of significant losses from 2025 and a couple of key returners for 2026?  The biggest losses are the three first rounders at the line of scrimmage. Bain and Mesidor at defensive end  and Francis Mauigoa at left tackle. There are an enormous number of key returners but none bigger than Toney, who could emerge as a Heisman candidate.  7. What are your expectations for this season and can Miami live up to the lofty goals it has set? The Canes should contend for the national title but first they have to prove that they have grown up and can avoid bad losses and lulls during a four-month season.  In  2024 it was Georgia Tech and Syracuse. Last season it was Louisville and SMU. With Notre Dame on the schedule this year in a night game on the road, the team won’t be playing out the season with a large margin of error.

articles.summary: Hi HN, I'm Bor Shev, a composer and developer. Over the past two years I've been developing ShevtoneAudio Orchestrator. The idea is simple: instead of generating a finished piece of music and replacing the composer, Orchestrator takes the composer's own MIDI and develops it into a full orchestrat
articles._body: Hi HN, I'm Bor Shev, a composer and developer. Over the past two years I've been developing ShevtoneAudio Orchestrator. The idea is simple: instead of generating a finished piece of music and replacing the composer, Orchestrator takes the composer's own MIDI and develops it into a full orchestration. It analyzes the musical material — harmony, melody, rhythm, dynamics, structure and orchestral density — and creates an arrangement across strings, brass, percussion and other sections. The important part is that the result remains editable MIDI. The composer keeps control and can continue working with everything inside their DAW. I believe this approach could be a breakthrough in AI-assisted composition: AI as an orchestration tool rather than a replacement for the musician. I'm especially interested in feedback from developers, composers and people working with music technology. Feel free to tear the idea apart — I'd genuinely like to know what you think. I'm also running a limited launch offer for Orchestrator at $149. Demo / product: orchestra.shevtoneaudio.com Thanks for taking a look! — Bor Shev ShevtoneAudio Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49497791 Points: 4 # Comments: 1

articles.summary: I built a tool (https://1mil.app/hn) to help me test my intuition about various weird business ideas that were on my mind. Initially, I wanted to create a database with 1 million business ideas (hence the name - "1 million opportunities"). But turn
articles._body: I built a tool ( https://1mil.app/hn ) to help me test my intuition about various weird business ideas that were on my mind. Initially, I wanted to create a database with 1 million business ideas (hence the name - "1 million opportunities"). But turned out to be a dumb idea already. So instead I built this tool that returns only 10 ideas. It's all based on your input, market + your background. The first release scored on demand only and it gave false confidence. So I rebuilt the the scoring around "winnability": can a solo founder with a specific background "win" against what already exists? Heres what still bugs me: since winnability went live in June, it has scored 500+ ideas, and none reached 7/10. The best was 6.3 and the median is 1.3. That includes every scan I ran for myself. My preliminary conclusion: most business ideas are improbable to win. Well, go ahead and try the scanner, and let me know what you think. A free scan without an account is included. Each scan costs Vertex tokens, which is why the tool isn't free. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49497779 Points: 2 # Comments: 0

Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields Music Festival Proves There Is Hope For Us All: 13 Best Moments
articles.summary: Inside the inaugural all-women festival founded and headlined by the pop superstar.
articles._body: It was scorching, and nearly every artist commented on the intense heat — from Rachel Chinouriri stating, “it’s f—ing hot, Jesus…the U.K. ain’t like this” during her 12:30 p.m. set to Chappell Roan introducing her hit “HOT TO GO!” near the end of her 7 p.m. set by saying, “this next song is very fitting, I feel.” Bikini Kill’s Kathleen Hanna, Mitski and Doechii were among those who reminded fans to hydrate – with Hanna herself taking long sips from her reusable bottle boasting an“F–k Ice” sticker. Such was the ethos of the day: Stand for something, and look out for one another.  Related Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields Donation Reaches $20 Million After Melinda French Gates Match It was just two months ago that Olivia Rodrigo announced Daisy Chain Fields, her very own music festival, along with its Daisy Chain Fields Fund. “Truly never felt more excited to share a piece of news with you all,” Rodrigo wrote on Instagram at the time. “I’ve had a dream of doing this festival for years and I am so ecstatic it’s finally coming true!!” Today, Saturday (Aug. 29), fans felt firsthand how Daisy Chain Fields was always meant so much more than just a festival — and in fact, it could even change how such events operate going forward. Boasting an all-women lineup of Olivia’s “heroes and friends,” and with 100% of the net proceeds going to charities dedicated to advancing and advocating for women and girls, Rodrigo created something much greater than a day of music: She amplified a mission and supercharged a movement. The day before fans flocked to Irvine, Calif. for the one-day festival (on Friday, Aug. 28), Rodrigo held a press conference to share a sizeable piece of news: Ticket sales alone brought in $10 million for the fest’s 10 nonprofit partners. (Partners include Baby2Baby, Black Mamas Matter Alliance, Center for Reproductive Rights, FreeFrom, Jhpiego, Johns Hopkins Center for Indigenous Health, National Domestic Workers Alliance, National Institute for Reproductive Health, National Women’s Law Center and Planned Parenthood.) While speaking at the presser, Rodrigo also name-checked the iconic Lilith Fair tour, saying its founder, Sarah McLachlan, was one of the first people she called while in the early stages of making her dream a reality. Tonight, to cap off her own historic first fest, Rodrigo welcomed McLachlan – along with Alanis Morissette and Stevie Nicks – on stage during her stellar headlining set. Prior to performing, Rodrigo first brought Melinda French Gates to the stage to announce that the philanthropist had doubled the $10 million in funds raised – bringing Daisy Chain Fields’ total donation amount to $20 million .  In Rodrigo’s same Instagram caption from two months ago, she had ended it by saying: “I firmly believe that joy, community and music can be the drivers of meaningful change and I’m hopeful this festival will be just that.” In its first year, it already was. And thankfully, as Rodrigo revealed at the end of her set, it will continue to be ahe enthusiastically declared, “See you next year!” Until then, read on for the best moments from the inaugural Daisy Chain Fields music festival.

Inside Meta’s push to put robots to work in data centers
articles.summary: The company is testing robots on tasks that can performed by technicians.
articles._body: Meta is testing robots that can plug in cables, reset servers, and handle other tasks inside its data centers , according to several current and former workers familiar with the projects. The ongoing effort, which has not been previously reported, may eventually allow Meta to operate its rapidly expanding data center footprint with fewer humans, keeping labor costs in check as its spending on AI infrastructure soars . Meta is using robots and related hardware from several different vendors, including Watney Robotics, Kinova, and ABB, according to the same workers, who asked to remain anonymous because they weren’t authorized to speak to the media. Kinova and ABB declined to comment. Watney didn’t respond to requests for comment. In one experiment, Meta is evaluating whether a Kinova Gen3 robotic arm could be used for power cycling or cutting off electricity to servers. The company is also testing a different robot to swap networking cables. One Meta data center worker estimates that if it’s successful, the bot could replace up to 80 percent of some people’s workloads. “We thought those of us performing the physical tasks were safe for a while, but not anymore,” says the worker. “It’s coming for us all, unfortunately.” Read full article Comments

articles.title: How Alex Eala Turned the Philippines Into a Tennis Nation
articles.summary: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images
articles._body: NEW YORK — Alex Eala has been filling tennis stadiums all over the world this past year, buoyed by more than 11 million overseas Filipinos. Packed crowds in Australia , Dubai , Toronto , and this week, New York , have felt “Eala Mania,” decorating relatively docile tennis crowds with Philippine flags and “Laban Alex!” signs. Eala is a complete anomaly for her country. No other Filipina had even made the top 250 before her, and she’s already cracked the top 20 before the year’s final major following her maiden WTA title at the DC Open earlier this month. The 21-year-old even has current stars already labeling her the future of the sport . Her unprecedented ascent has led Filipino fans to fly across the country to see her play. One group even planned their college reunion around her first appearance at the Cincinnati Open a few weeks ago. But because of the nomadic nature of tennis, Eala is barely able to witness how she’s impacting the other 117 million Filipinos in her home country. “I think because I’m always traveling and I’m on tour, I’m quite out of touch sometimes with what my impact is back home, for the good and the bad. I think that’s why I said a couple of times that when I went back home, it really opened my eyes,” Eala said in response to a question from FOS at the Cincinnati Open. The last time she played in the Philippines was the Philippine Women’s Open in January, a WTA 125 event that was the first in the country’s history. She easily sold out the 2,000-seat stadium in Manila for the tournament earlier this year. Fans in the country have even held watch parties of her WTA Tour matches in stadiums. They will finally be able to watch her in-person again after Tatler Philippines announced Friday that she will play an exhibition match against Indonesian pro Janice Tjen in December. The exhibition will take place at the Philippine Arena, a 55,000-seat venue that could smash the record attendance for a tennis match. “A lot of my matches are overseas—no, 99% of my matches are overseas. So for me to be back home and playing in front of the people in the Philippines, it’s going to be super special,” Eala said Friday during her US Open press conference. Philippine Tennis Association executive director Tonette Mendoza tells FOS that Eala’s impact goes far beyond selling out stadiums. According to Mendoza, she’s completely changed the Philippine government’s view on the sport. “It’s easier to ask the government for funding for facilities, like if we’d like to build or refurbish a tennis center or build a regional tennis center,” Mendoza tells FOS . “At least it’s there now because they can see na pwede pala (that it’s possible). Because before, it really felt like a very, very far dream.” Mendoza said that COVID-19 the pandemic accelerated the sport’s growth; lockdowns in the country lasted more than a year, and for a while, tennis was one of the only sports the government allowed citizens to play. But Eala has allowed the government to believe Filipinos can compete globally in the sport. PhilTA estimates there are less than 1,000 courts in the country, most of which are now packed, pushing local governments to build more. Late last year, the organization acquired nearly 25 acres of land where it plans to construct a Philippine Tennis Center that will be a central hub to train its future tennis stars. She also said Eala’s rise has helped push PhilTA’s grassroots agendas, from working with World Tennis (formerly the International Tennis Federation) to certify more coaches to trying to bring tennis, known as a sport for the elite, into the country’s public school system. “The more people play, of course, the better it is for everyone’s health,” Mendoza said. “But also, there are more people to choose from, di ba? (right?) You will get more good people, more people who will have potential, rather than you just have like 100 people playing.” Bee Go, founder of Atleta Filipina who has covered Eala since she was 13 , tells FOS that fully booked tennis courts are often filled with young girls hoping to become the next Filipina star. “Alex has really impacted the rise of the sport among young girls,” Go said. “You’ll see videos now of kids saying: ‘I really want to be Alex Eala,’ so that’s why a lot of kids take up tennis.’” And yet, the young star consistently defers when asked about her impact. “I think that every single WTA player and every single ATP player has contributed to the world of tennis and its history just by being here and by putting in the work every single day. Although there are certain things … that make me stand out, I think that I’m a drop in the ocean when it comes to these things,” Eala said Friday. The post How Alex Eala Turned the Philippines Into a Tennis Nation appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: South Korea may be getting too old to take advantage of its AI boom
articles.summary: Korea could keep getting richer from AI while elderly households become reluctant or unable to spend those gains
articles._body: South Korea is one of the biggest winners of the AI boom. It’s home to Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, the two largest manufacturers of memory chips. Chip workers are flashing bonuses of around $400,000. The KOSPI, Korea’s benchmark index, is up almost 60% for the year so far. Yet a report from Goldman Sachs suggests that all that wealth might not make it to ordinary households.  Even as demand for chips has sent Korean exports and factory investment surging, retail sales are still close to whether they were in 2019. Goldman calls it a “K-shaped cycle” where corporate balance sheets thrive while private consumption remains soft. Goldman’s economists have an explanation: South Korea is getting too old, too quickly.   The East Asian country has one of the world’s lowest fertility rates, reporting 0.8 births per woman last year , far below the 2.1 rate to keep population levels relatively stable. (The U.S., by comparison, reported 1.6 births per woman ). Twenty percent of Korea’s population is now over the age of 65. The country’s postwar baby boomers are retiring just as its fertility rate remains below replacement level, leading to a shrinking pool of working-age Koreans supporting the elderly.  The United Nations projects Korea’s “dependency ratio”—the number of children and elderly people relative to the working-age population—will increase by 1.5 percentage points a year over the next decade. That’s the fastest pace among the 70 large and midsized economies Goldman analyzed, surpassing even Japan during its most intense period of aging from 2000 to 2015. Korea’s retirement problem To make matters worse, older Koreans behave unusually when they retire: They don’t spend. In Japan, Taiwan and the U.S., people tend to draw down their savings once they retire, but Koreans don’t. Goldman found Koreans in their sixties save more than any other age group, retaining 37% of their income. Even those in their seventies save at rates similar to those in their forties. The wealth elderly Koreans do have is difficult to spend.  More than 60% of Korean household net worth is tied up in non-financial assets like real estate, the highest share among the advanced economies Goldman studied. Financial assets held by Korean households are only worth 100% of the country’s 2024 GDP, the lowest level in Goldman’s sample. That leaves Korean retirees asset-rich, but cash poor. “Even among elderly households that have accumulated retirement savings, fewer than one-fourth could cover consumption needs with financial assets,” Goldman researchers wrote. When incomes decline, Koreans are more likely to cut their spending or work more than to liquidate their assets. Koreans are wary of methods to turn housing wealth into cash. Reverse mortgages cover just 1.8% of homeowners older than 75, which Goldman observed partly reflects a strong desire among retirees to leave assets to their heirs. In contrast, Goldman found that Taiwan, another AI boom winne r, has stronger consumption from older consumers, despite just as severe aging pressures. (The island’s government projects the population could halve in size by 2075). Taiwanese households have a much larger financial cushion than their Korean counterparts, with net financial assets totaling five times GDP, compared to just one times GDP in Korea.  Why too much saving could be bad for Korea’s economy As more Koreans age, that propensity to save could become a drag on spending. Among the major economies Goldman studied, a one percentage point increase in the dependency ratio reduces real private consumption growth by around 3 basis points a year. Yet in Korea, the hit to growth is between 10 and 17 basis points. One of Goldman’s models suggests that Korea’s fast aging population could shave as much as 25 basis points from annual consumption growth over the next decade.  Even if Korea can maintain 2% economic growth over the next two decades, consumption growth gradually weakens and eventually turns negative, according to Goldman’s long-term modeling.  Korean officials have tried a variety of national- and local-level approaches to reverse falling birth rates. The national government announced a “marriage support grant” of up to 1 million won ($725) to couples who get married and an extra 20 million won ($14,500) per newborn. Local governments are also hosting matchmaking events for Korean singles, even dangling monetary rewards for couples who marry after meeting at the event. Birth rates are increasing very slightly, but even a radical increase in fertility won’t solve Korea’s problem in the near-term, as any babies born now won’t be of working age for at least two decades. Instead, Goldman economists suggest that Seoul try some more immediate solutions, like helping elderly Koreans unlock their housing wealth, and better distributing the windfall from the country’s super-profitable tech firms. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Carson Hocevar delivers surprising verdict on NASCAR’s new Daytona package after massive wreck
articles.summary: Carson Hocevar explains his massive late Daytona wreck and offers a surprising assessment of NASCAR’s new superspeedway rules package.
articles._body: The Carson Hocevar experience continued on Saturday night in Daytona.  Following a hard wreck with six laps remaining in the Coke Zero Sugar 400, Hocevar tried to make sense of his race.  With six laps remaining in Saturday night’s race, Hocevar ducked out of high groove to his left to attempt to make a pass.  His car got loose, broke further left before rocketing back up the track and hard into the wall .   Trouble at the front of the field! @CarsonHocevar goes for a slide and gets into the wall. pic.twitter.com/aBCUAfXnOq — NASCAR (@NASCAR) August 30, 2026 ‘It just kept going’ Following his release from the infield care center to get checked by doctors, Hocevar relived the incident, which ultimately sent the race to overtime and was eventually won by Ryan Preece .  “I was always super tight behind people, it seemed,” said Hocevar of the incident, which ended up collecting Erick Jones as well. “I just changed from top to bottom there. “And that’s the first time I got a ton of air on my nose into Turn 3. I just lost it.  It just kept going.  “I had the wheel straight and just kept going with all the air sent down on the nose. Oh well, it just kept going.  I’m shocked.” Hocevar comments on new superspeedway rules package Heading into Saturday night, all of the talk was about NASCAR’s new superspeedway rules package. With no practice with the package ahead of time, the first real test was when the green flag dropped. Hocevar was asked about his thoughts on the package.  His response ?  “I thought it was fun.” “Yeah, it was fine. I thought it was fun, and I just felt like dirty air mattered more or was more difficult. I don’t know if it was better or not, but I didn’t complain.  “We were up front, so same contenders were kind of up front no matter what, either package.” Despite the wreck, Hocevar felt good about the performance Hocevar was asked how he felt about his and his team’s performance following the race. He walked away (with a bit of limp), feeling pretty good about the night.  “It was nice to ride around all day like we kind of planned and then gave ourselves a shot to win one of these things up front, having track position again, and leading these things at the end.  “I feel like that’s all I can really ask for from a team standpoint. So, I thought we did a pretty good job there.”  The last four races have seen Hocevar fall from fifth in the Chase standings to 12th in the final regular season standings.  Now, he moves forward, looking to recapture the momentum he had just over a month ago.

articles.title: Show HN: Train 300M/32-Layer Model in 1.5GB RAM on Base M1 Mac
articles.summary: Hello again! Since my last post about Ullis, the project has gone through several changes as I was searching for the right architecture. As it turned out, KAN and Hyena were quite resource-heavy, and I couldn't get anything viable out of them. Then I tried RWKV, specifically the latest RWKV-8 Her
articles._body: Hello again! Since my last post about Ullis, the project has gone through several changes as I was searching for the right architecture. As it turned out, KAN and Hyena were quite resource-heavy, and I couldn't get anything viable out of them. Then I tried RWKV, specifically the latest RWKV-8 Heron version with 1-bit ROSA activation. This ultimately proved to be the most viable architecture of all. As an example: on my 2020 MacBook Pro M1 with 8GB RAM and a 68GB/s memory bandwidth, I managed to start training a model with ~272 million parameters, a 2048 context length, and 32 layers—all within a 1.5GB memory footprint. On my specific hardware, this is still a highly taxing task. Due to the low bandwidth, the total latency per step is around half a minute, and the throughput drops to about 70 tokens per second. To be clear right away: I had to keep ROSA SAM on the CPU because it proved to be more efficient for these tasks than the GPU. Here are the logs as proof: cargo run --release -- train \ --data data/ullis_dataset.jsonl \ --run runs/hard \ --config train_config.json \ --steps 20000 \ --learning-rate 0.005 \ --checkpoint-every 500 \ --bpe-train-mib 150 ullis: token stream compacted to u16 (156 MiB) ullis: compiling Metal shaders ullis: Metal ready in 0.2s ullis: Metal train: LN/QKV/CMix/head on GPU; ROSA SAM on CPU (~603979776 bytes idx+y+out/step) ullis: starting loop after 379.0s of setup ullis: clipped SGD lr=0.005 rosa_grad=StopGradBits (QKV frozen; window-mean CE on FP16, token-sum STE on BinaryConnect; |w0|=0.01) step 1/20000 loss=7.9256 ema=7.9256 p10=5.218 p50=8.193 p90=10.197 unigram=5.958 unique=597 n=1389 flips=0/0/0 (head/cmix/o) embed_grms=6.40e-5 scale_grms=8.09e-3 cmix_vrms=0.013 |w|=0.010 dw=4.37e-6 bias_rms=2.033 resid=3.21e-8 rss=1643MiB 27881ms 73 tok/s ullis: step 1 phases embed=8ms fwd_ln=370ms fwd_rosa=7220ms fwd_cmix=5897ms head=1070ms bwd_ln=625ms bwd_cmix=9754ms bwd_rosa=2678ms embed_sgd=57ms step 2/20000 loss=7.0537 ema=7.8384 p10=1.670 p50=7.518 p90=9.969 unigram=5.564 unique=590 n=1520 flips=0/0/0 (head/cmix/o) embed_grms=6.46e-5 scale_grms=1.06e-2 cmix_vrms=0.013 |w|=0.010 dw=4.68e-6 bias_rms=2.033 resid=5.67e-8 rss=1628MiB 27997ms 73 tok/s ullis: step 2 phases embed=8ms fwd_ln=314ms fwd_rosa=5717ms fwd_cmix=4738ms head=1231ms bwd_ln=786ms bwd_cmix=11755ms bwd_rosa=3180ms embed_sgd=60ms With scaled-down settings, training runs with pretty satisfactory performance. Here is an example: since a multi-stage training pipeline with pre-training is not implemented yet, I trained it on a large Claude Opus distillation dataset. After 5500 steps, here is the result: cargo run --release -- generate \ --checkpoint runs/ullis_b1_32m/checkpoint.safetensors \ --prompt "2+2" \ --temperature 0.4 \ --top-p 0.8 Finished `release` profile [optimized] target(s) in 0.60s Running `target/release/ullis generate --checkpoint runs/ullis_b1_32m/checkpoint.safetensors --prompt 2+2 --temperature 0.4 --top-p 0.8` - *No a single = = = = = = i [b_t + 1 + 3-c)$ - The correct answer is a list of the number of the first n > 0 As you can see, the model is capable of learning, but since I cannot afford to keep my main work laptop running training tasks 24/7, I had to stop at this relatively modest result. There is, of course, a possibility that some training algorithms might have implementation bugs, but this is the current outcome. I hope you find this project interesting. Honestly, pulling off a project like this entirely on your own is quite tough, especially considering I'm developing it alongside an LLM assistant (which constantly tries to break things). I'm not deeply experienced in this field yet, so I'd be incredibly glad to find testers, people with domain expertise, or anyone willing to share any kind of feedback. Thank you! Link: https://github.com/Vladislav-Kalinkin/ullis Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49497451 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

Women’s professional soccer has a champagne problem: A packed calendar around the World Cup that will test the sustainability of its mega growth
articles.summary: “That schedule was intentionally designed to position the NWSL at the center of one of the biggest years in the history of women's soccer,” Commissioner Jessica Berman said.
articles._body: The National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) insists that too much of a good thing is just a myth, at least in the context of the sport. Earlier this month, the league announced its 2027 calendar, which will start one month earlier than usual to account for a two-month mid-season break when many of its athletes will swap club jerseys for country ones at the FIFA Women’s World Cup. It will be the NWSL’s longest season in its 14-year history. The global tournament comes at a critical time for the NWSL, which has doubled in size over the last decade. As of its 2026 season mid-point, the league saw an average of more than 11,000 fans at each match, a 10% year-over-year increase, and its social media following grew 24% year-over-year to 3.1 million followers across major platforms, according to NWSL data . With 138 NWSL players expected to join national rosters for the Women’s World Cup, the league is preparing to capitalize on an influx of fans. “That schedule was intentionally designed to position the NWSL at the center of one of the biggest years in the history of women’s soccer,” NWSL Commissioner Jessica Berman told reporters this month. “By maintaining our spring to fall calendar, which we decided earlier this year, we’ve created the best possible environment for our players, clubs, partners, and fans to maximize the extraordinary opportunity presented by the FIFA Women’s World Cup.  “We know that major tournaments inspire millions of people to follow the sport,” she added. “And our schedule allows us to be part of the lead-in and the lead-out of that big moment.” But in order for the NWSL to make the most of a jam-packed calendar, it will have to overcome a number of logistical obstacles, from cold climates to maintaining the health of players. Its executives believe the league is ready to meet the moment. “It means that we can then come back to our regular season on the heels of the Women’s World Cup and ride that momentum,” Sarah Jones Simmer, chief operating officer of the NWSL, told Fortune . “And we will have so many players coming back to our league that will have had success in the Women’s World Cup, and that’s going to be a massive fan acquisition opportunity for us. It’s going to really contribute to the growth of the league.” How the NWSL is meeting the moment For the league, preparing to take advantage of the 2027 World Cup has meant pushing up its regular season start by more than a month to Feb. 11, meaning its preseason will begin in the first week of January, just six weeks after the 2026 championship, the shortest offseason in the league’s history. The regular season will end on Decision Day on Oct. 31, and the 2027 championship will be on Nov. 20. The league will pause play for the World Cup, which falls from June 24 to July 25. The early start will necessitate navigating the weather, particularly for teams in colder markets, such as Chicago, Denver, and Boston. NWSL players have previously expressed concern about playing in cold weather. The league’s player’s association tabled a vote on a fall-to-spring calendar, with many opposing the measure , citing the climate. “I think there’s way too many locations that are way too cold. I don’t think we’ve fully thought through what that looks like,” Washington Spirit forward Trinity Rodman said in April. “If we have snowed-out games—or just the conditions in general—what are the backup plans? Where are the fields we can play at? “And just fans in general (and) getting to games, I think that would decrease the attendance for games in cold climates. So, for me, I just think we have to be fully prepared and have backup plans if we do potentially decide to do that.” Simmer said there’s enough geographic diversity in the league to hold games in February because warm weather markets are able to accommodate them. The MLS season typically starts in late February, and front-loads away matches for teams in colder climates, as well as schedules later kickoffs when temperatures peak for the day. For 2027, it will flip its schedule to a summer-to-spring model to better align with the international calendar and sign and retail top talent. Then there’s the health of the athletes, who will not only have to play in their 30-game schedule, but also compete in the World Cups matches in the middle of their regular season. A study published in the Journal of the American Osteopathic Academy of Orthopedics in 2025 found that when the 2022 FIFA World Cup was held in the winter instead of its usual summer time, injuries in the Premier League and Bundesliga significantly increased. “A midseason slot may not be the best time to schedule a World Cup,” the study authors wrote. The NWSL’s collective bargaining agreement mandates an offseason , and league officials said the league works hard to add policies to accommodate playing conditions, such as adding hydration breaks during hot-weather games. The league, as it continues to grow, is used to adapting and making game-time decisions. Eleven of the NWSL’s 16 teams share venues with MLS clubs and coordinate schedules to use the facilities that can accommodate more fans. Only the Kansas City Current have their own stadium , financed by co-owners Angie and Chris Long, as well as Patrick and Brittany Mahomes. As more teams look to build out their own infrastructure, the league facilitates how to give its clubs the best possible venues under the constraints.  “We’re working even closer, with not just our clubs and the venues, but also with MLS directly to continue to understand their plans heading into a newer year for them,” Carlin Hudson, NWSL’s vice President of strategy, told Fortune . “We work very hand in hand with our venues that have responsibilities to both MLS and NWSL clubs.” The high stakes of women’s soccer Historically, professional soccer in the U.S. has benefitted from the World Cup. articles.title: 2026 LA Tech Football  Preview and Predictions
articles.summary: After 13 up-and-down seasons in Conference USA, the Bulldogs will finally be reunited with classic in-state rivals, UL-Monroe and UL-Lafayette.
articles._body: Welcome Home After 13 up-and-down seasons in Conference USA, the Bulldogs will finally be reunited with classic in-state rivals, UL-Monroe and UL-Lafayette. Tech’s transition from the disbanded WAC to the well-regarded C-USA was a decision that seemed to appropriate for 2013. However, the conference suffered the mass exodus of several universities, including Tulane, Southern Miss, Marshall, UTSA, North Texas, Rice, and others. This diluted the quality of the play week-to-week, as respected G5 schools were mostly being replaced with FCS call-ups. Despite the lack of flashy competition, the Bulldogs were never able to grab a conference title in their most valuable sport, football. Skip Holtz led excellent units from 2014-2016, but close losses and inconsistencies put a lid on their potential. 2019 was supposed to be the year Tech finally broke through, but we all know what happened instead. Holtz was let go at the end of the 2021 season, and OC Sonny Cumbie from Texas Tech was hired to spark new life into the program. Cumbie’s teams certainly fell short of expectations during his first two seasons, but 2024 was a year of good and bad luck, encapsulated by the Jax State homecoming game fiasco. The 5-7 Bulldogs backed their way into the Indy Bowl after Marshall’s entire team entered the transfer portal, and although Tech was handled by an imposing Army squad, it was nice to see the Bulldogs back in bowl mania for the first time since 2020. After swapping from Trey Kukuk to Blake Baker early in the 2025 season, Tech’s offense showed genuine promise with the return of OC Tony Franklin. Unfortunately, starting LB Kolbe Fields and QB Blake Baker would battle injuries, leading to the former being out for the season and the latter eventually being shut down for the season. Tech’s losing streak was salvaged by a mind-boggling comeback against Liberty, an impressive win at Missouri State, and an ugly but winning effort over Coastal in the Indy Bowl. With Tech soon to play its first games as a member of the Sun Belt Conference, it is hard to express how much pressure will be on the administration, coaches, and players due to who they will be competing against. Only true diehards suffered through late-weekday CUSA games like the multiple overtime loss to NMSU two years ago and stayed up until 2 am to listen to the BTB postgame show. Now, the spotlight will be much more central for Tech alumni and students, as we will get to witness clashes with local schools for years to come. The rewards for winning are enormous, but the cost of losing? Forever damaging. Below, I will be providing a concise breakdown of each game and predict the result of all 12 contests. Week 1 vs Northwestern State Since the infamous firework display following the Dawgs’ shocking upset loss to the Demons in 2014, Tech has handled business in both season openers against the school from Natchitoches, winning comfortably in both 2017 and 2023. Since the Bulldogs’ 30-point defeat of NSU in 2023, the Demons have won just 1 game. Tech should pound the rock with ease and allow Baker and Kukuk to reestablish themselves in this new season. Prediction: Bulldogs 55 Demons 7 Week 2 @ #11 LSU This game was a late addition to the ’26 schedule and will make Tech students show who their favorite team really is once again. Luke Olson’s defense played admirably against the #3 Tigers from last season, limiting Joe Sloan’s unit to just 23 points. Throughout the rest of the season, it became evident that LSU’s offense was simply atrocious, and keeping them out of the end zone wasn’t nearly as impressive as it seemed at the time. With Lane Kiffin and a $50 million roster this year, the offense should be more explosive. However, Tech plays LSU at the perfect time, after a likely hard-fought Clemson game, and Kiffin’s must-see return to Oxford. LSU will win, but the Dawgs don’t go down without some fight. Prediction: Tigers 34 Bulldogs 13 Week 3 @ Baylor This will be a fun matchup that was initially on the 2022 schedule before being swapped for Missouri. Tech fans in Louisiana and graduates in the DFW area can enjoy a nice day trip to McLane Stadium in Waco. After Dave Aranda surprisingly kept his job while sitting on the hottest of seats, former 5-star+ recruit DJ Lagway transfers in to the school where his father played, trying to prove that he still is an elite quarterback. The Bears lose a tremendous amount of production on offense, but retained OC Jake Spavital, who returned an exciting brand of football to Baylor. Tech should be formidable against the rushing attack, but the Bulldogs losing nearly their entire secondary this offseason gives me reasonable doubt about how they can stop Lagway and the offense. Prediction: Bears 30 Bulldogs 14 Week 4 vs Army This was another excellent addition to the schedule by the athletic department and a rematch of the 2024 Independence Bowl. Thankfully, the Joe Award-winning offensive line graduated along with QB Bryson Daily, but the Black Knights still won’t be a cakewalk in 2026. Army fell back down to earth last season, going 7-6 and experiencing drastic variability to begin the year, dropping the opener to Tarleton State and coming back the following week and taking down Kansas State in Manhattan. As Ben previously discussed, this game could truly be one of the season’s most meaningful, as it’ll serve as an early indicator of how the Dawgs will perform against similarly talented rosters. Kolbe Fields, as well as the trio of young linebackers, will be key in stopping Army’s option attack. West Florida transfer NT Juice Williams will also need to make a huge impact if the Bulldogs want to earn this statement win. articles.title: 100 Days of Georgia’s Greatest Plays—Day 6
articles.summary: On Day 6, we look back at the 6-yard David Greene-to-Verron Haynes “Hobnail Boot” touchdown that crushed Tennessee in Knoxville a quarter-century ago.
articles._body: UGASports continues its 100-day countdown to the Bulldogs’ 2026 season opener with the “100 Days of Georgia’s Greatest Plays” series. Today, on Day 6 , we revisit one of the greatest plays in Georgia football history involving the number 6. On Day 6, we look back at the 6-yard David Greene-to-Verron Haynes “Hobnail Boot” touchdown that crushed Tennessee in Knoxville a quarter-century ago. The Game: Georgia (2-1 record under first-year head coach Mark Richt ) vs. No. 6 Tennessee (3-0 record under head coach Phillip Fulmer ) at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tennessee, on October 6, 2001. Under first-year head coach Richt, Georgia sought its first win in Knoxville since 1980, having lost five straight to the Volunteers on the road. Tennessee had defeated 38 consecutive unranked opponents at Neyland Stadium and was an overwhelming 11-point favorite over the Bulldogs. “Get the Picture”: With less than a minute remaining in the game, Tennessee appeared to have delivered the decisive blow when Casey Clausen connected with Travis Stephens on a 62-yard touchdown pass, giving the Volunteers a 24-20 lead. Following the ensuing kickoff, Georgia took possession at its own 41-yard line with 42 seconds left. Freshman quarterback David Greene immediately went to work, completing three of four passes for 53 yards—13 yards to Damien Gary , followed by gains of 26 and 14 yards to Randy McMichael —to move the Bulldogs to the Tennessee 6. With 10 seconds remaining, Georgia called its final timeout while Richt and company dialed up the play “P-44-Haynes.” The Play From the 6-yard line, Greene faked a handoff to the tailback as fullback Verron Haynes initially appeared to block blitzing middle linebacker Dominique Stevenson before slipping unnoticed into the end zone. Stevenson bit on the play-action, leaving Haynes without a defender within five yards of him. Greene calmly floated the ball to the wide-open Haynes for a 6-yard touchdown. Georgia had retaken the lead, 26-24, with only five seconds remaining. Tennessee fumbled the ensuing kickoff, sealing a stunning road victory for the Bulldogs over the nation’s sixth-ranked team and a double-digit favorite. Following the game, Haynes said he was surprised when “P-44-Haynes” was called from the sideline—so much so that he said a quick prayer before lining up at fullback. At the line of scrimmage, Greene was instructed to check Tennessee’s defensive alignment. If the Volunteers showed one safety, he was to throw the ball away; if they showed two, the play should work as designed. Tennessee lined up with two safeties—and Haynes’ prayer was answered. The touchdown immediately became one of the most celebrated plays in Georgia football history, forever remembered as the “Hobnail Boot.” “We just stepped on their face with a hobnail boot and broke their nose! We just crushed their face!” 22 years ago… 10/6/2001 #UGA executes P-44-Haynes for a touchdown and steps on Tennessee's face "with a hobnail boot and broke their nose…” The 26-24 win over the Vols, which entered as 11-point favorites, remains the Bulldogs' 4th biggest upset of the modern era. pic.twitter.com/JVxghKSCFt — Patrick Garbin (@patrickgarbin) October 6, 2023

articles.title: Why the AI economy is like a bad dating app — drowning in decks, pilot purgatory — and it’s playing out like the dotcom bubble, except worse
articles.summary: Amy Webb is a futurist who called the rise of AI — and a U.S./China tech Cold War — years ago. She wishes she were happier with what she's seeing.
articles._body: Amy Webb was on her long Sunday bike ride, the one she takes when she’s not training for a race, when the thought arrived fully formed. As she posted on LinkedIn recently: every CEO she talks to is buying abundance, and none are budgeting for the cost of abundance. And she talks to CEOs every day for a living. Webb, 51, runs the Future Today Strategy Group, the foresight and consulting firm she founded in 2006 after a career in data journalism that led to her subsequent interest in machine learning. Webb, who also teaches at NYU’s Stern School of Business, published The Big Nine , which named nine American and Chinese tech giants as forces that would dominate in a world marked by artificial intelligence and a full-scale tech cold war, so she’s used to being ahead of her time, and she’s used to being frustrated by the world being behind the schedule she sees in her head. So when Webb told Fortune that she sees something like a bust coming for corporate AI spending, it’s worth pausing on the precise dynamic she’s describing. “AI is making production cheap,” she said, “but it’s making everything else in companies much more expensive.” The corporate world, she added, is going through something like what millennials and Gen Zers experienced as dating-app fatigue. “The best thing [for a dating app] is to never get married,” Webb said, adding that she sees the same thing playing out in the endless series of generative AI pilots. She said executives tell her they’re in “pilot purgatory”: dealing with unending pilots and “enormous productivity but [they’re] not sure what to do with that.” Venture capitalist Marc Andreessen , meanwhile, said in March that large companies are overstaffed by as much as 75% and were using AI as a “silver bullet excuse” for cuts that reflect pandemic-era overhiring. A separate analysis by Oxford Economics found AI-cited layoffs accounted for a mere 4.5% of total U.S. job losses despite outsized headlines. ‘It feels like you’re buying abundance’ Webb, who speaks with between 100 and 150 CEOs a year, said she’s most focused on a bubble that sits apart from what’s happening on Wall Street: the strange way that AI is deforming work without actually changing it much at all. “It feels like you’re getting a lot when you invest in AI,” Webb said, “it feels like you’re buying abundance. But that abundance ends up costing much more down the road.” It’s not a question of long-term investment versus short-term gains, an old business trade-off. “This is immediate satisfaction, followed by: can I productize this? Can I put it in a workflow?” AI is making companies feel like they’re winning, a sensation of “I’m getting away with it,” and that’s driving a lot of enthusiasm and adoption. At the same time, she said she can count on one hand the number of companies that have figured out a sustainable way to pull off this kind of experimentation. One of her clients had run 14 or 15 generative AI/agent pilots since the start of the year and used Amazon’s famous two-pizza rule, in which no team was big enough that it would take more than two pizzas to feed them. None of them scaled. “They’ve gone through a lot of pizza.” Part of the issue is that pilots often run without integration into legal and IT, and so executives don’t embed the pilots into their infrastructure, but restart from zero each time. “That costs a lot of money,” she said. The pattern shows up in the data: A Bain & Company survey of 951 global companies published in June found that nearly 40% of companies that measured their AI cost savings landed below 10%, despite having targeted returns of 11% to 20%. But to Webb’s point, the shortfall hadn’t slowed spending, as 90% of companies surveyed said they’re increasing their AI budget anyway. Drowning in decks Outside of pilot purgatory, there’s the drowning-in-decks issue. Webb recalled an executive who recently shared that their direct reports were experiencing something like decision paralysis, not because they had too little information, but because they were being buried in too much analysis to process. Another described the problem to Webb as “insta-decks”: presentations that used to take a week to build now take a day, but the same team is receiving five times as many of them. It doesn’t help, she added, that “Claude has a little bit of a verbosity problem,” producing 10 pages when you only need one. “The more a company uses these tools,” Webb added, “the more generic ideas are spit out.” This isn’t the same thing as AI slop, she said — it’s something different. “It’s fine with me if something was not written necessarily by a person, if the rest of the information is useful.” Webb said she asks nearly every CEO she meets: if AI freed up 10% of your total capacity tomorrow, where would you deploy it? “So far, I haven’t gotten an answer.” Of all the time being saved, she said, nobody seems to have the job of harvesting all these productivity gains. “I’d bet at most companies, people are prioritizing speed over creating new ways of thinking. And then you’re not learning anything.” Psychologists have begun studying the phenomenon of “cognitive offloading”—delegating mental work to a tool rather than doing it yourself—and recent research finds that when AI takes over core reasoning tasks, people’s sense of ownership over the resulting work declines.
