Why Gen X should stop planning around an inheritance that may never arrive
articles.summary: Gen X has been handed a hard set of facts. Less saved than the generation before it, no pension underneath, and obligations pointing in both directions.
articles._body: There is a line item in a lot of Gen X retirement plans that nobody writes down. It does not appear on a spreadsheet. It rarely comes up with an advisor. But it sits in the back of the mind of millions of people in their 50s: Eventually, there will be my parents’ house. Eventually, there will be whatever is left in their accounts. It will not solve everything. It will help. I understand the instinct. I have spent a career building businesses around finance and how long people live, and this assumption turns up everywhere. It is seldom stated out loud. It is almost never stress-tested. And it is getting less reliable every year. Start with the number everyone has heard. Something close to $124 trillion in American wealth is projected to change hands by 2048, and Gen X is first in line. About $14 trillion of it is expected to reach Gen X households over the next ten years. Set against a generation that saved a fraction of what the boomers had at the same age, that sounds like a rescue arriving. It is not. Three things get in the way. The average is a mirage Averages do real damage in retirement planning, and inheritance is where they do the most. Only about one in three American households ever receives an inheritance at all. Across all households, Federal Reserve data puts the average received at roughly $46,200. That figure is performing a magic trick. Households in the top one percent average close to $719,000. The bottom half average about $9,700. The transfer is real. It is also concentrated. The money is not spreading evenly across a generation. It is pooling where wealth already sits. For a median Gen X household, a realistic inheritance is not a retirement plan. It is a good year of saving, if it comes at all. There is also a gap between what families expect and what shows up. Households that inherit almost always expect more than they receive. The estimate forms early, when parents look healthy and the house is worth what it is worth today. It seldom gets revised downward, even as the years that will consume it pile up. It arrives too late to do the work The second problem is timing, and longevity is rewriting it in real time. The median American who inherits is about 58 years old. Sit with that for a second. The money shows up after the tuition is paid, after most of the mortgage is gone, after the decades when capital could have compounded into something larger. Inherited money in the hands of a 40-year-old buys a house or starts a business. In the hands of a 60-year-old, it retires a mortgage balance and moves into a conservative portfolio. Same dollars. A different life. That median age keeps climbing, because parents keep living longer. Longer life is the achievement of our era, not a problem to be solved. But it means the transfer Gen X has half-planned around arrives later every year, at a point in their own lives when it can do less. Most people set this expectation once, in their forties, and never touch it again. The number in your head is probably a decade old. It formed when your parents were younger, healthier, and far cheaper to care for. Care gets paid first Here is the piece that reshapes the whole calculation, and the piece almost nobody has modeled. Before an estate passes to anyone, it pays for care. A private room in a nursing home now runs a national median of about $129,575 a year. Assisted living runs about $74,400. Most families assume Medicare covers this. Medicare does not cover custodial care, and custodial care is the bulk of what a long stay involves. Run it on an ordinary estate. A paid-off house worth $400,000 and $200,000 in savings looks like a meaningful inheritance to a Gen X child doing mental math. Three years of nursing care for one parent takes more than half of it. Add a second parent, or a longer stay, and there is nothing left to pass down. For most middle-class families, the estate is not a portfolio. It is a house. That matters, because a house cannot be spent in pieces. When care costs land, families sell the home or borrow against it. The asset a Gen X child had mentally earmarked becomes the funding source for a parent’s final years. That is the right use of it. It is also the end of it. Nobody in that family made a mistake. This is the arithmetic of a long life meeting the price of care in America. The wealth transfer still happens. It transfers to care providers. What to do instead None of this is an argument for pessimism. It is an argument for building on ground that will hold. Take the inheritance out and see whether the plan still stands. Whatever number is sitting in the back of your mind, set it to zero and run the plan again. If it fails, you have found the real gap, and you have found it while there is still time to close it. Have the conversation now, and make it about care rather than money. Families avoid this because it sounds like asking about the will. It is a different conversation. What is the plan if you need help at 84? Is there coverage for care, and what does it cover? Who manages it when it happens? Families who answer those questions early protect both generations. Families who wait find out during a crisis, at the worst possible price. Treat whatever arrives as acceleration, not foundation. An inheritance that lands on top of a plan you built yourself is a gift. An inheritance that was holding the plan up, and never comes, is a crisis with no time left to fix it. Gen X has been handed a hard set of facts. Less saved than the generation before it, no pension underneath, and obligations pointing in both directions at once. The honest response is not to hope the math gets rescued from above. It is to build something that does not need rescuing. articles.title: America’s Mediterranean lunch bowl is booming as NAYA races toward 200 restaurants
articles.summary: Mediterranean fast casual grew 16% last year, and NAYA’s founder is betting the boom can carry his Lebanese chain from 48 locations to 200.
articles._body: When Hady Kfoury opened his first restaurant in Manhattan in 2008, he was already out of money. He had raised cash from friends and family to bring the Lebanese food he grew up eating to New York, but construction had cost more than he expected. He still owed money to his general contractor and resorted to buying equipment on eBay just to get the 54-seat restaurant open. “It was a nightmare,” Kfoury told Fortune. The nightmare eventually turned into 48 restaurants and counting. NAYA now employs more than 1,000 people, with average annual sales of roughly $3 million per restaurant and same-store sales growth above 10% yearly. Its footprint has grown more than 40% in each of the past four years, just as Mediterranean bowls have become a fast-casual lunch staple. Kfoury’s next target is 200 NAYAs by 2030. The fast-casual restaurant he couldn’t open Kfoury was born in Lebanon in 1981, during the country’s civil war. He remembers some days going to school and other days having to take shelter in basements as bombs fell nearby. After studying hospitality in Switzerland and working in New York with chef Daniel Boulud, Kfoury returned to Lebanon, only to live through another war in 2006. “I’m like, all right, that’s not going to work,” he recalled. “I have to move to the U.S., start a restaurant, and take the flavors that I was raised on and do it over there.” By 2007, he was back in New York looking for space for a fast-casual Lebanese concept in the city’s office-heavy neighborhoods. But landlords wouldn’t lease to him. Kfoury had no track record as a restaurant owner, and after months of searching Midtown and Wall Street, he took a space on East 56th Street and Second Avenue. It happened to sit across the street from the aunt he’d stayed with during childhood trips to New York. The location wasn’t busy enough for the high-volume concept he envisioned, so Kfoury opened NAYA as a fine-dining Lebanese restaurant instead. His mother and aunt became what he calls the “culinary mastermind” behind it. His mother was a talented cook who didn’t measure ingredients, so Kfoury convinced her to turn the food he had grown up eating—chicken kebabs, falafel, rice with vermicelli, baba ghanoush and hummus—into written recipes. The restaurant attracted attention, but Kfoury hadn’t abandoned his original idea. In 2010, he finally shifted NAYA to fast casual. The challenge was figuring out how to reproduce his family’s food quickly and cheaply enough to serve hundreds of customers without stripping away what made it Lebanese. “The most difficult part is how do you do it at scale,” Kfoury said. Ingredients weren’t necessarily the problem. Lebanese cooking is labor intensive, he said, so NAYA introduced equipment, preparation techniques and systems designed to make that labor more efficient. The fast-casual model also depended on higher volumes at smaller margins. But being early didn’t mean customers immediately understood the concept. “The first two years were very hard at the fast casual,” Kfoury said. “People didn’t get it.” America catches up to the Mediterranean bowl Kfoury spent nearly a decade refining the model. By 2019, NAYA had just seven restaurants. Since then, the category around it has changed dramatically. Mediterranean and Middle Eastern flavors have become increasingly common across grocery stores and restaurant menus, while the customizable bowl has become a fixture of the American workday lunch. Fast-casual Mediterranean chains generated just under $2.5 billion in sales last year, according to Technomic data provided to Fortune . Sales across the category jumped 16% in 2025, significantly outpacing the 6% growth of the broader fast-casual segment. Technomic tracks about 30 leading Mediterranean fast-casual chains with a combined footprint of roughly 1,500 restaurants. The biggest player offers a glimpse of just how large the category can get. Publicly traded Cava ended its latest quarter with 476 restaurants , nearly 10 times NAYA’s total, yet the two chains generate similar sales per location. Cava reported average unit volume of $3.1 million in the second quarter, compared with roughly $3 million at NAYA. Cava’s same-store sales rose 9% during the quarter, driven in part by a 5.3% increase in traffic. That growth has come alongside a broader familiarity with foods that Kfoury once had to introduce to customers. “Ten years ago, you would say shawarma to someone, maybe you would get three out of 10 people who would know what it is,” he said. “Today, eight, nine out of 10 would know what shawarma is.” Kfoury thinks Americans are also becoming more discerning about what “Mediterranean” actually means. As the label can encompass cuisines from Lebanon and Turkey to Greece, Italy and Morocco, he compares it to the way Americans once broadly categorized distinct cuisines as “Asian food.” Over time, diners learned to distinguish Japanese food from Korean, Taiwanese or Sichuan cuisine. Kfoury expects something similar to happen with Mediterranean food. “I think the same thing is about to happen in the Mediterranean,” he said. For now, he doesn’t mind NAYA falling under the broader umbrella, even as the company emphasizes its Lebanese roots. From seven restaurants to 50 By 2019, Kfoury believed he’d finally refined NAYA’s model enough to scale. After years without institutional backing, he brought on restaurant-focused private equity firm TriSpan in 2020. Then COVID hit. NAYA’s seven restaurants were concentrated in Midtown and the Financial District, leaving the company particularly exposed when office workers disappeared. The restaurants shut down for months before gradually reopening, and Kfoury said TriSpan’s arrival helped give NAYA the financial backing to survive the disruption. What followed was a dramatically faster period of expansion. NAYA’s unit count grew 55.6% in 2022, 42.9% in 2023

articles.title: adidas Put the Superstar On Ozempic
articles.summary: The adidas Originals Superstar Lo Pro Aurora Coffee/Cream White strips away the 1970s cupsole in favor of an ultra-flat, low-profile footprint.
articles._body: After giving the slim-sole makeover to court staples like the Samba, Gazelle, and Stan Smith, the Three Stripes is officially taking a razor to its most famous basketball icon. The adidas Originals Superstar Lo Pro Aurora Coffee/Cream White strips away the silhouette's chunky 1970s cupsole in favor of an ultra-flat, low-profile footprint. Beyond being the latest drop, we can’t help feeling that this release raises a bigger question about adidas' current design strategy. The brand's archive is undeniably deep, but the speed at which it is pulling apart its most revered icons to fit hyper-specific trends—in this case, the wave of low-slung, ballet-adjacent footwear—feels relentless. While reshaping a heavy-set hardwood classic like the Superstar into a razor-thin flat is a fun design experiment, running through iconic silhouettes to satisfy fast-moving aesthetics begs the question: is this rapid deconstruction strategy long-term sustainable, or is it over-saturating the brand's core pillars? For now, the appetite remains high. With a barely-there sole unit, the Superstar Lo Pro transforms from a big classic into something daintier that slots into contemporary trends. The upper retains its DNA, crafted from supple Aurora Coffee brown leather and anchored by the iconic rubber shell toe at the forefoot. Contrasting Cream White serrated 3-Stripes and heel tabs cut through the deep brown upper, while gold foil lettering provides classic framing along the lateral panel. Underfoot is where the transformation takes center stage. Gone is the thick, traditional rubber cupsole, replaced by an ultra-thin, low-profile rubber outsole that sits nearly flush to the ground. It feels incongruous with the chunky upper, but maybe we’re just resistant to change, clinging on to the glory days of an iconic silhouette, unwilling to evolve… Highsnobiety has affiliate marketing partnerships, which means we may receive a commission from your purchase. articles.title: Olivia Rodrigo Recruits Alanis Morissette for a Surprise ‘Ironic’ Duet
articles.summary: Rodrigo welcomed Morissette, and the two launched into "Ironic," the enduring single from Morissette's 1995 landmark Jagged Little Pill.
articles._body: Olivia Rodrigo turned a last-minute lineup shakeup into one of the defining moments of her inaugural Daisy Chain Fields festival on Saturday (Aug. 29), calling Alanis Morissette to the stage after Yeah Yeah Yeahs frontwoman Karen O pulled out of the all-women event at Great Park in Irvine, Calif. Related Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields Donation Reaches $20 Million After Melinda French Gates Match Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields Music Festival Proves There Is Hope For Us All: 13 Best Moments Harry Styles Jokes About Taylor Swift's MSG Wedding During Residency Show Rodrigo delivered the news of the cancellation to the crowd herself, framing it gently before revealing the silver lining. “The bad news is Karen O is not able to make it tonight, she was one of the first people who said yes to Daisy Chain but she has a personal matter that requires her to be elsewhere,” Rodrigo said. The good news walked out moments later. Rodrigo welcomed Morissette as the fill-in, and the two launched into “Ironic,” the enduring single from Morissette’s 1995 landmark Jagged Little Pill . Then came the twist worth talking about: partway through, they reworked the song’s most-quoted scenario, flipping its “beautiful wife” to a “beautiful husband” — a small rewrite with a pointed wink at a festival built on an all-women, queer-inclusive bill that also features Chappell Roan and Doechii. The duet doubled as a full-circle moment for Rodrigo, who has long named Jagged Little Pill as a cornerstone of her own songwriting. She inducted Morissette into the Canadian Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2022, and the pair previously shared a stage on Rodrigo’s Sour tour, trading verses on “You Oughta Know” in Los Angeles. Rodrigo staged Daisy Chain Fields at a career high. Her third album, You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love , debuted atop the Billboard 200 in June with 485,000 equivalent album units — the biggest week of her career and the largest week of 2026 for any solo artist. Lead single “drop dead” bowed at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, her fourth chart-topping debut. With the release, she became just the second artist ever, after Beyoncé, to send each of her first three studio albums to No. 1 on the Billboard 200 while landing at least one Hot 100 leader from each. The one-day festival, which raised $10 million for nonprofits supporting women and girls, arrives just weeks before Rodrigo launches her Unraveled Tour.

articles.title: UNLV QB Jackson Arnold showcases cannon with textbook touchdown vs. Memphis
articles.summary: UNLV opened its 2026 season with a 27-21 loss to Memphis on Saturday, but quarterback Jackson Arnold provided plenty of positives with his passing accuracy and impact in the running game. The Auburn transfer completed 25 of 37 attempts for 291 yards and two touchdowns, while also leading the Rebe
articles._body: UNLV opened its 2026 season with a 27-21 loss to Memphis on Saturday, but quarterback Jackson Arnold provided plenty of positives with his passing accuracy and impact in the running game. The Auburn transfer completed 25 of 37 attempts for 291 yards and two touchdowns, while also leading the Rebels on the ground with 54 yards on 21 carries. Arnold accounted for all three of UNLV’s touchdowns, throwing two and running for another. Arnold helped the Rebels build a 14-7 halftime advantage by connecting with Tavian McNair for a 38-yard touchdown and scoring himself on a 6-yard rushing touchdown. UNLV had won its previous 11 games when holding a halftime lead, with its last such loss coming against Syracuse back on Oct. 4, 2024. Tavian McNair gets into the end zone for the UNLV touchdown pic.twitter.com/JlHGJGrreB — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 30, 2026 After the Tigers tied the game early in the third quarter on Marcus Stokes’ 48-yard touchdown pass to Stonka Burnside, Arnold responded with another big scoring play. He found Kayden McGee for a 22-yard touchdown, putting UNLV back in front. Memphis eventually erased the deficit and took control late. Jaylin Carter’s 36-yard rushing touchdown tied the game at 21, while Philippe Laforge converted field goals from 32 and 36 yards to give the Tigers a 27-21 lead. The Rebels had an opportunity to respond midway through the fourth quarter after reaching the Memphis 18-yard line. However, Arnold was sacked on fourth-and-7 with 6:08 remaining, ending the possession. The Tigers finished with six sacks and 11 tackles for loss while applying pressure throughout the closing stages. UNLV coach Dan Mullen had said earlier in the week that Arnold and Alex Orji would both play against Memphis. However, Arnold’s performance limited Orji’s involvement, as Orji did not attempt a pass. The Rebels will look to rebound next Saturday against Hawaii. The post UNLV QB Jackson Arnold showcases cannon with textbook touchdown vs. Memphis appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Dodgers’ Tyler Glasnow breaks down 99th percentile extension
articles.summary: Tyler Glasnow spends a concerning amount of time on the injured list, but when he is on the mound, he can mystify spectators with just his presence. Yes, the veteran right-handed starting pitcher is an impressive talent who can bewilder some of the best hitters in the game when he is at his best.
articles._body: Tyler Glasnow spends a concerning amount of time on the injured list, but when he is on the mound, he can mystify spectators with just his presence. Yes, the veteran right-handed starting pitcher is an impressive talent who can bewilder some of the best hitters in the game when he is at his best. Last year’s playoff showing strongly supports that notion. However, he is also a physical force who can do things that others simply cannot. Glasnow ranks in the 99th percentile with a 7.5-foot extension, per the MLB Network X account. Big-leaguers pride themselves on their approach, but it is extremely difficult to brace oneself for such a phenomenon. Although the 2024 All-Star has always been able to utilize his 6-foot-8 frame to some degree, he is much more disciplined in how he moves during his windup. Glasnow admitted that he used to focus on quickly releasing his pitches with optimal force. The mindset has changed a bit , however. “If I can work properly and have my spine and everything working well, I don’t necessarily need to use a lot of force,” the 33-year-old told “MLB Tonight.” “My extension, just being as long as I am, is always going to be pretty long. I think the only time I get into trouble is if I’m not rotating properly, and then I’m compensating with my back as opposed to moving from my hips.” Tyler Glasnow is 99th percentile in extension at 7.5 feet The 11-season veteran joins #MLBTonight to talk about what he's learned about his mechanics over the years. pic.twitter.com/zTuF4gEMeM — MLB Network (@MLBNetwork) August 30, 2026 Even though the Dodgers already have a fantastic rotation that consists of World Series MVP Yoshinobu Yamamoto, two-time Cy Young Tarik Skubal and two-time Cy Young Blake Snell, a healthy Tyler Glasnow can make an enormous difference in a five or seven-game series. He just needs to keep tightening up his mechanics. The imposing hurler pitched five innings of three-run ball with seven strikeouts and zero walks in Tuesday’s 4-3 loss versus the Atlanta Braves. Glasnow showed some rust after missing more than two and a half months with back spasms, but he still has time to perfect his execution before the playoffs begin. No. 31 will get back at it for Sunday’s series finale against the Detroit Tigers. The post Dodgers’ Tyler Glasnow breaks down 99th percentile extension appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Bears’ Zavion Thomas torches Titans defender in his postgame interview too
articles.summary: Chicago Bears rookie wide receiver Zavion Thomas made his long-awaited preseason debut in a 24-15 win over the Tennessee Titans on Saturday. The 22-year-old caught all five passes thrown his way for 140 yards and a touchdown. Thomas needed only one offensive play to make his impact. With the Bear
articles._body: Chicago Bears rookie wide receiver Zavion Thomas made his long-awaited preseason debut in a 24-15 win over the Tennessee Titans on Saturday. The 22-year-old caught all five passes thrown his way for 140 yards and a touchdown. Thomas needed only one offensive play to make his impact. With the Bears backed up at their own 3-yard line, backup quarterback Tyson Bagent quickly looked toward Thomas after Roschon Johnson picked up a blitz. Titans cornerback Keydrain Calligan stumbled during the route, leaving Thomas with separation. Thomas caught the pass at Chicago’s 33-yard line and raced 97 yards for the score, while safety Jerrick Reed II could only chase him and swipe at his leg. After the game, Thomas was asked whether the Titans defender had any chance of stopping him . His response was blunt: “Nahhh. He didn’t have a chance.” #Bears rookie WR Zavion Thomas on whether the #Titans defender had any shot against him tonight: “Nahhh. He didn’t have a chance.” https://t.co/XjqroW2tNV pic.twitter.com/q2j0Vs9cRN — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) August 30, 2026 The rookie third-round pick out of LSU continued producing after the long touchdown. He averaged 28 yards per reception and added a 39-yard punt return and a 22-yard kickoff return. His punt return nearly resulted in another touchdown and further showcased his ability to create explosive plays in the return game. Thomas had missed the Bears’ first two preseason games because of a knee injury. He remained on the field into the third quarter and finished the night as Chicago’s leading receiver by yardage. Thomas did have one mistake, fumbling an attempted fly-sweep exchange in the first quarter, with Titans defensive end Jacob Martin recovering. Bagent also put together an efficient performance while Caleb Williams watched from the sideline. He completed 16 of 17 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns, while the Bears converted four of five fourth-down attempts with him directing the offense. Bagent’s other touchdown came on a fourth-and-goal play from Tennessee’s 2-yard line, when he escaped pressure before finding Maurice Alexander in the back of the end zone. NFL teams are required to reach the 53-player roster limit by 5 p.m. Sunday. Thomas is projected to compete for a potential No. 4 receiver role while also serving as the Bears’ likely primary returner. Chicago opens the regular season Sept. 13 against the Carolina Panthers in Charlotte, N.C. articles.title: Harry Styles Jokes About Taylor Swift’s MSG Wedding During Residency Show
articles.summary: The singer name-checked the Knicks' championship and his ex's wedding in the same breath at his third Madison Square Garden date.
articles._body: Harry Styles gave a cheeky nod to ex-girlfriend Taylor Swift’s wedding during night three of his Madison Square Garden residency on Saturday (Aug. 29). Toward the end of the set, he hyped up the venue’s recent history before pivoting to the joke: “We’re at Madison Square Garden, home of the world champion New York Knicks!” he told the crowd, before adding, “And they also do weddings.” The line, referencing Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce ‘s July 3 wedding at the arena, drew loud cheers. Styles and Swift dated from November 2012 to January 2013, a relationship widely understood to have inspired Swift’s 2014 hit “Style.” He reportedly received an invitation to the Swift-Kelce wedding but didn’t attend; sources told Variety at the time he was “currently on tour and will not make it to MSG.” His fiancée, Zoë Kravitz, went to the ceremony without him. Styles was performing the London leg of his own Together, Together tour that same night, and fan footage from the July 3 Wembley show captured him singing 2017 track “Two Ghosts” — long rumored to be his response to “Style” — including the lines “Same lips red, same eyes blue / Same white shirt, couple more tattoos.” The joke landed three days into a residency already drawing outsized attention. Styles’ 30-show MSG run — which makes up the entirety of his 2026 U.S. tour dates and continues through Halloween — opened Aug. 26 to 11.5 million presale ticket registrations in January, which Ticketmaster called the highest volume ever recorded for an artist presale. It’s Styles’ first run of live shows since 2023, in support of his new album Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally , released in March. Opening night carried its own emotional weight. Styles completely overhauled his usual setlist — a departure from the largely unchanged show he’d played across 33 prior tour dates — and paused late in the set to honor Dolly Parton, who had died the day before. “I just wanna give a proper thank you to all the musicians who have inspired me over the years,” he told the crowd. “Dolly, we love you. Thank you so much.” Her 1974 recording of “I Will Always Love You” then played over the PA as the crowd sang along, with Zoë Kravitz, Gayle King and Drew Barrymore among those in attendance. Styles closed that show with “Sign of the Times” and set-closer “Aperture.”

articles.summary:
Hi HN — I built VelocityNote, a compact, Markdown cross-platform notebook.

The desktop app is under 100 MB. It starts quickly and remains responsive under memory pressure.

VelocityNote has a built-in, pluggable AI system that can run local models:

- It is a local LLM app: you can use a llam
articles._body: Hi HN — I built VelocityNote, a compact, Markdown cross-platform notebook. The desktop app is under 100 MB. It starts quickly and remains responsive under memory pressure. VelocityNote has a built-in, pluggable AI system that can run local models: - It is a local LLM app: you can use a llama.cpp-based local agent to summarize notes and tasks. More features, including translation, are coming. - It is an intelligent screenshot app: built-in OCR extracts text, while vision models can describe your images. - It is a dictation app: with Silero VAD and speech-to-text, you can record and transcribe hours-long meetings entirely on your device. - It is an app for managing documents: it supports importing a variety of file formats, including PDF and Word, and migrating data from other notebook databases. With local models, your data always stays on your device, with no external provider or per-token limits. Under the hood, notes are stored in SQLite. Full-text search makes searching large notebooks fast. Everything remains available offline and can be exported as standard Markdown. VelocityNote also exposes an MCP server and a command-line interface, allowing it to serve as a local second brain for both you and your AI agents. Agents can use ultra-fast full-text search to find notes, then read, create, and update them through explicit tools instead of scraping the UI or directly modifying the database. VelocityNote is cross-platform and currently available for Windows and macOS. articles.title: Titans HC Robert Saleh reveals how many 53-man roster spots are up in the air
articles.summary: Robert Saleh isn’t ready to close the book on the Tennessee Titans’ 53-man roster just yet. With the Titans coming off their preseason finale against the Chicago Bears, Saleh and his coaching staff have a quick turnaround to make their final roster decisions. While some players have s
articles._body: Robert Saleh isn’t ready to close the book on the Tennessee Titans’ 53-man roster just yet . With the Titans coming off their preseason finale against the Chicago Bears, Saleh and his coaching staff have a quick turnaround to make their final roster decisions. While some players have seemingly secured their spots, the head coach made it clear that several battles remain unsettled . Saleh explained that performances in the preseason finale could still change the team’s evaluation of players who are competing for roster spots. “Yeah, absolutely they can,” Saleh said when asked if players could make a final push . “There’s going to be stuff that shows up on tape, where if it was neck and neck, someone can take a leap ahead, or if it was, I mean, someone could have had the inside track and lost it, you know what I’m saying?” Robert Saleh said there are about 10 spots on the Titans 53-man roster that are still up in the air. Tonight’s preseason finale could have moved the needle for some. pic.twitter.com/xbtxfeFvPX — Blaine Kellar (@sports_bk) August 30, 2026 That means players who entered the final game with an advantage aren’t necessarily guaranteed a place on the initial 53-man roster. Saleh, however, emphasized that the Titans won’t make those decisions based solely on what happened in the preseason finale. The first-year Tennessee head coach wants his staff to consider the full body of work from throughout the offseason. “But the discipline in it is to make sure that we’re taking the entire body of work, from the entire, from all the way back to OTAs and the improvement,” Saleh said. That approach could make the final roster decisions particularly difficult for Tennessee. The Titans have spent the offseason reshaping the roster under Saleh , and several position groups have featured competitions for backup and depth roles. The preseason finale provided one final opportunity for those players to strengthen their cases, but Saleh isn’t allowing one performance to completely override everything that came before it. The Titans now have little time to finalize their initial 53-man roster, with the NFL’s deadline arriving Sunday. Teams around the league are already beginning the process of making cuts as they prepare for the regular season. “Again, like I said, it’s a quick turnaround, a lot of decisions to be made, but we feel good about it,” Saleh said. articles.summary: D’Ernest Johnson paid tribute to franchise legend Chris Johnson with a quality touchdown celebration during the Tennessee Titans’ preseason finale against the Chicago Bears on Saturday night. D’Ernest is going through the ninth season of his NFL career, his first with the Titans
articles._body: D’Ernest Johnson paid tribute to franchise legend Chris Johnson with a quality touchdown celebration during the Tennessee Titans’ preseason finale against the Chicago Bears on Saturday night. D’Ernest is going through the ninth season of his NFL career, his first with the Titans. He looks to secure a place in the rushing attack, seeking great opportunities to be productive on the team. Chris Johnson is a player Tennessee fans remember fondly. He represented them for six seasons, shining as one of the top rushers in the league. He earned NFL Offensive Player of the Year in 2009, landed on the First-team All-Pro in 2009, and made three Pro Bowls from 2008 to 2010. D’Ernest was well aware of Chris’ impact on the Titans. Which is why it was only fair for him to pay tribute to the franchise legend with the Choppa City Juke celebration after scoring the touchdown against Chicago. Tennessee was nine yards away from the end zone as D’Ernest pulled off the highlight in convincing fashion. D'Ernest Johnson scores the TD and hits the Choppa City Juke in honor of Chris Johnson CHIvsTEN on @NFLNetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/sYmEAhp7bC — NFL (@NFL) August 30, 2026 How D’Ernest Johnson, Titans played against Bears D’Ernest Johnson brought Titans fans a memorable touchdown with the Chris Johnson tribute before the preseason drew to a close. Tennessee ended the preseason with a 2-1 record, falling to the Bears by a 24-15 score. Both teams traded blows, but the visitors had bigger plays with the touchdown highlights to gain the upper hand. Will Levis played in the game as he completed 14 out of 22 passes for 143 yards. D’Ernest led the rushing attack with six carries for 29 yards and a touchdown. Meanwhile, Xavier Restrepo caught four passes for 71 yards. The Titans will seek to improve upon their record of 3–14 from the past two seasons. They also intend to end their four-year drought of both a playoff appearance and an AFC South title. Tennessee sees its 2026 campaign begin at home, hosting the New York Jets. That matchup will commence on Sept. 13 as kickoff takes place at 1 p.m. ET. Yankees’ Max Fried breaks down 1st start since returning from IL
articles.summary: Max Fried was happy to be back on the mound, but more importantly, the New York Yankees left Saturday’s game with exactly what they wanted from his return. Fried made his first start since returning from the injured list in Game 3 of the series on Saturday. The Yankees had opened the series
articles._body: Max Fried was happy to be back on the mound, but more importantly, the New York Yankees left Saturday’s game with exactly what they wanted from his return. Fried made his first start since returning from the injured list in Game 3 of the series on Saturday. The Yankees had opened the series with a 1-0 win before Boston responded with a 6-0 victory earlier Saturday . New York then bounced back in the nightcap, with Fried making his return to the mound. The left-hander threw 63 pitches over 3⅔ innings , allowing one run on two hits while striking out four. While Fried acknowledged that he was sharper earlier in the outing, he was pleased to get back into competitive action and finish the game feeling healthy. “Definitely a lot sharper earlier than late, but nice to get back out there,” Fried told reporters after the game . “Competitive juices going, and at the end of the day, just us being able to win the game was really big. So I’m just happy that we were able to do that.” Max Fried on his 63-pitch outing vs Boston in his first start off the injured list. #YANKSonYES pic.twitter.com/YdbVn4QsFo — YES Network (@YESNetwork) August 30, 2026 Fried said he felt strong before his latest stint on the injured list, explaining that one pitch had irritated his elbow. After getting through his return without another issue, the Yankees starter was encouraged by how he felt. “I was feeling really strong going before this IL stint,” Fried said. “And I was feeling good in the game. It just kind of was just like one little pitch that irritated it.” The Yankees also needed the victory after being shut out by Boston earlier in the day. New York’s offense responded in a big way in Game 3, scoring nine runs to give Fried plenty of support in his return. The 32-year-old also emphasized how important it was for the Yankees to answer after the Game 2 loss and put themselves in position to win the series. “Anytime you have a doubleheader, you want to make sure to try to win both,” he said. “But coming out there and not coming off the win, you’re a little bit more focused. And you want to make sure that you don’t drop too straight.” “Now we’re up 2-1 going into tomorrow,” Fried added. “And I’m excited to sit and watch and hopefully come out with a series win.” The post Yankees’ Max Fried breaks down 1st start since returning from IL appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Three thoughts after Texas Southern’s huge upset over North Carolina Central
articles.summary: Texas Southern pulled off a huge upset over North Carolina Central on Saturday evening, with the win serving as a proof of concept for Cris Dishman and the success he wants to bring to the Tigers. North Carolina Central is one of the most decorated programs in the FCS over the past few years, par
articles._body: Texas Southern pulled off a huge upset over North Carolina Central on Saturday evening, with the win serving as a proof of concept for Cris Dishman and the success he wants to bring to the Tigers. North Carolina Central is one of the most decorated programs in the FCS over the past few years, particularly in HBCU football. Texas Southern authored a resounding comeback victory after trailing 24-14 at halftime, winning 42-30. Here are three thoughts about both teams. Cam’Ron McCoy is the perfect QB1 for Texas Southern Cam’Ron McCoy has had a very interesting journey in HBCU football over the past couple of seasons, transferring from Eastern Michigan to Jackson State in the 2024 season, then from Jackson State to Southern University, where he was highly regarded by Terrence Graves before Graves’s ultimate dismissal from the program midway through the season. Now he’s on his third HBCU program, and he was able to showcase his talent in Dishman’s dynamic offense. He finished the game 8 of 19 passing for 185 yards and three touchdowns with one interception, also adding 8 carries for 30 yards, including a 22-yard run, to his stat line. McCoy has a tall task replacing KJ Cooper, who was the starter for the Tigers before transferring to the University of South Florida this offseason. Cooper emerged as one of the best quarterbacks in the SWAC last season, and with his consistency, Texas Southern finished the season 6-5 overall and 5-3 in conference. It’s yet to be seen if McCoy can remain as consistent, but his first game under center for Texas Southern went as well as it possibly could. Can Texas Southern really be a SWAC West contender? Texas Southern can seriously be a player in the SWAC West after going 5-3 in conference last season. It’s clear that Dishman and his vision for the program are finally paying off. A win against one of the best teams in the MEAC and a perennial Celebration Bowl contender should definitely have HBCU football fans paying attention to what’s happening in Houston. Alongside McCoy, running back Athean Renfro Jr. finished the game with 163 yards and one touchdown on 18 carries. Receiver Jaquan McGee was on the receiving end of two touchdowns among his four receptions for 115 yards, with Roriyon Richardson netting one touchdown of his own, his lone catch going for a 45-yard touchdown reception. The defense for Texas Southern also stepped up against North Carolina Central, notching three sacks and eight tackles for loss, and Jaquavius Holman pulled in an interception. Prairie View A&M, with their performance against Tarleton State, will clearly be a contender in the SWAC West once again. But between Southern under Marshall Faulk, Grambling State under Mickey Joseph, and an improved Texas Southern, it’s going to be a fight to the finish to see who ultimately clashes with the Panthers to decide who represents the West in the SWAC championship game. North Carolina Central will be good again, but how good? North Carolina Central had a strong start, leading 24-14 at halftime, but they scored only 6 points in the second half and ultimately allowed 28 points after the break. They didn’t necessarily look bad. Former Eagles offensive coordinator Matt Leone’s absence was certainly felt, as the offense didn’t look as inspired as it did with him at the helm, but North Carolina Central looked competitive throughout the game. North Carolina Central under new OC Chris Barnette looked good, per usual, with a nice offensive attack predicated on a strong running game, where the running back room finished with 190 yards and 2 touchdowns. Nelson Layne also had a respectable performance, throwing for 131 yards, one touchdown, and one interception on 16 of 31 passes. Chance Peterson, shockingly, had a quiet evening; the reigning preseason MEAC Offensive Player of the Year only had 4 receptions for 23 yards. North Carolina Central in the Trei Oliver era will always be a Celebration Bowl or FCS playoff-caliber team. They’re always going to be good, but how good will they be? Will they show improvement on their schedule and win seven to nine games but lose to South Carolina State at the end of the season, or will they break through and ultimately represent the MEAC in the Celebration Bowl the same way they did in 2016 and 2022? Likewise, will they find a way into the FCS playoffs if they don’t make the Celebration Bowl, and compete there? It’s never a question whether the Eagles under Oliver will be a solid squad. But the question has to be: how good can they be, and can they break through the same way they did just four seasons ago, when they pulled off a resounding win over Deion Sanders and Jackson State in the Celebration Bowl? articles.title: Titans’ Will Levis thanks Tennessee fans for support amid uncertain future
articles.summary: Will Levis is not ready to speculate about what comes next, but the Tennessee Titans quarterback made it clear that he remains grateful for his time in Nashville. Levis addressed his uncertain future with the Titans following Tennessee’s preseason finale against the Chicago Bears. Rather th
articles._body: Will Levis is not ready to speculate about what comes next, but the Tennessee Titans quarterback made it clear that he remains grateful for his time in Nashville. Levis addressed his uncertain future with the Titans following Tennessee’s preseason finale against the Chicago Bears. Rather than look ahead to a potential departure, the quarterback chose to reflect on the support he has received since arriving in Tennessee. “I don’t want to predict or talk about things that haven’t happened yet, so I don’t know. We’ll get there when we get there,” Levis told reporters . How does Will Levis reflect on his time here if it’s over after tonight: pic.twitter.com/3CpBskfcOf — Buck Reising (@BuckReising) August 30, 2026 Levis was then asked how he would reflect on his time with the Titans regardless of whether he remains with the team. “Very thankful. Very, very thankful,” he said. The Titans selected Levis in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft, and he entered the organization with plenty of expectations. His tenure in Tennessee, however, has been marked by inconsistency and injuries, while the franchise’s decision to select Cam Ward with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft fundamentally changed the quarterback situation. Ward is entrenched as Tennessee’s starter, leaving Levis facing an uncertain path with the franchise . ClutchPoints recently projected the Titans’ 53-man roster with Ward and Mitchell Trubisky as the team’s quarterbacks while suggesting Levis’ time in Nashville could be coming to an end. Still, the 27-year-old’s comments showed that his connection to Tennessee goes beyond his position on the depth chart. He specifically thanked the people who welcomed him when he arrived, as well as the Nashville community and everyone within the organization. “Sandy brought me in here and welcomed me with open arms, as well as everyone else here in Nashville and the team,” Levis said. Levis previously made his confidence in his ability clear , saying he believes he is “100%” an NFL starting quarterback and that there are not 32 quarterbacks better than him. Whether that next opportunity comes in Tennessee or elsewhere remains to be seen. For now, he is choosing not to look beyond what has actually happened. His message to Titans fans, however, was unmistakable: regardless of where his NFL career goes next, he will remain thankful for the support he received in Tennessee. Shane van Gisbergen opens up on late Daytona pit stop as Ryan Preece steals Chase berth
articles.summary: Shane van Gisbergen opens up about a crucial late pit call at Daytona after Ryan Preece’s dramatic win cost him the final NASCAR Chase berth.
articles._body: A clearly disappointed Shane van Gisbergen met with the media on pit road following the Coke Zero Sugar 400. Entering the race at Dayton with a 31-point lead over Ryan Preece, the one thing van Gisbergen couldn’t afford was a Preece win. Preece did notch the win and despite van Gisbergen winning Stage 1, the 20-point race win bonus for Preece did make the difference. Preece grabbed the 16th and final spot in the Chase. Shane van Gisbergen was left out of the Chase field . The late pit stop strategy for van Gisbergen With six laps remaining in the race, Carson Hocevar spun and made hard contact with the wall. The caution set up an overtime finish . Van Gisbergen was told to pit to top off gas and took four tires. The leaders stayed out. SVG came out of the pits 28th on the overtime restart.  And that’s where he finished in the race.  Freshly out of his Red Bull Chevy, van Gisbergen was asked about the decision to pit there .  “I don’t know, they obviously have more information on how much fuel we had left, and maybe I didn’t do a good enough job early,” said van Gisbergen with fireworks exploding in the background for Preece’s win. “I was trying, but I guess conservative at that point, but yeah, it is what it is. “I don’t know, I don’t get emotional about that stuff, just trust what they say and pit it because they told me to.” SVG congratulated Ryan Preece In his USA Network interview, van Gisbergen congratulated Preece.  He was asked if he was hoping Preece would run out of gas.  He said no. SVG said he missed the Chase because of the points left on the table all season, not because of tonight. “I never hope for the misfortune of others, but yeah, I don’t put down him winning tonight; it’s not a one-night loss. “It’s, you know, I haven’t done a good enough job throughout the year; we’ve lost points in various places, we didn’t just lose it tonight, yeah, it is what it is.” Not all bad for van Gisbergen SVG did like the new rules package and the racing it produced tonight.  And he was also stoked to win his first stage on an oval in his NASCAR Cup Series career.  “Yeah, I thought it was awesome. The racing when we were flat out was really good, and where you could move around, and the cars were getting kind of loose, so yeah, it definitely was more fun than previous times. “I was pretty stoked; I have never won, I don’t think I’ve ever won a stage run on ovals, so we got within one corner at North Wilkesboro, so that was pretty awesome.” Moving forward, SVG said the season isn’t over. He’s proud of the strides he’s made, particularly on ovals this season. “The season’s not over yet, but for sure, I’m proud that I’m closer to my teammates on ovals, and you know, managed to have a pretty good year. “Obviously I want to do better as a team; as a team we’re not quite there, but I think we’ve made good improvement on the ovals compared to my teammates. “I guess we can try things now; we can take a bit more risk, and just have some fun, low stress, and have a crack.”

Federer, widely regarded as one of the greatest players in tennis history, used the moment to highlight t
articles._body: Roger Federer delivered an emotional speech during his Hall of Fame induction , with the tennis legend fighting back tears as he reflected on the people who helped shape his remarkable career. Federer, widely regarded as one of the greatest players in tennis history, used the moment to highlight the role his family played throughout his journey. The 20-time Grand Slam champion became particularly emotional when speaking about his wife, Mirka Federer. “I need tissues and sunglasses. I need everything to protect me right now,” Federer said during his speech. There's no one quite like Roger An iconic speech from one of our greatest sporting ambassadors pic.twitter.com/1TPj6jTRdJ — Tennis Channel (@TennisChannel) August 30, 2026 Federer then turned his attention to Mirka, whom he credited with being far more than just his wife throughout his career. “As you know, Mirka’s my wife. Duh. Which is the greatest understatement I can make, because she’s also been my coach, my hitting partner before matches, and my reality check,” he said. The Swiss icon also jokingly called Mirka his stylist, admitting that he “definitely needed one at the time.” Behind the humor, however, Federer offered a heartfelt look at how much his wife meant to both his career and his life away from the court. Federer said Mirka helped him become more focused on tennis while also teaching him to find joy outside of the sport. He also praised her as a mother to their four children and emphasized how the family navigated the demands of his professional career together. “She and I grab each other’s hands, and we run through walls,” he said. Federer’s induction into the International Tennis Hall of Fame adds another milestone to a career that already includes 20 Grand Slam singles titles, 103 ATP singles titles and 310 weeks ranked No. 1 in the world. The 42-year-old retired from professional tennis in 2022 , closing the chapter on a career defined by his elegant playing style, longevity and fierce rivalry with Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic. While Federer’s achievements on the court have cemented his place among tennis’ all-time greats, his Hall of Fame speech offered a reminder that his journey was never his alone. After thanking Mirka for everything she contributed to his career and family, Federer summed up what his wife and loved ones ultimately mean to him. “She’s all of these things, and that’s my hall of fame,” he said. [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] Pittsburgh 3-star running back commitment Tyler Reid opened the game up with a 57-yard touchdown run and the Raiders never looked back as they cruised past the Eagles in a 38-14 rout at the Broward County Classic High School Football Showcase finale. Though St. Thomas Aquinas didn’t score another touchdown after halftime, they really didn’t need to against the defending UIL Class 6A, Division II state champions. For DeSoto one miscue turned a domino effect of others as the night wore on as quarterback Jayden Shaw never got into any sort of groove throwing the ball as the Raiders effectively shut down Texas Tech 4-star running back commitment SaRod Baker . St. Thomas Aquinas next touchdown would come off an interception returned for a touchdown as Ohio State 3-star cornerback commitment Jaden Carey returned it to the endzone to give the Raiders a 14-0 lead. The Raiders scored touchdowns on offense, defense and special teams, when Notre Dame 4-star safety edge Zayden Gamble picked up a punt and returned it 50-plus yards to pay dirt. The Raiders (2-0) closed out their scoring when 2028 quarterback Blake Calixte connected with Notre Dame 4-star wide receiver commitment Julius Jones on a touchdown pass to give St. Thomas Aquinas a 38-0 lead heading into intermission. DeSoto would score twice in the second half, which was played under a running clock. As it did so, it offered a heartwarming moment for linebacker Ethan Pritchard and the thousands of fans supporting his recovery from a gunshot wound. Ethan Pritchard’s story is well known at this point, and the entire Seminoles fanbase has been pulling for him at every step. “One of the most remarkable experiences I’ve ever been a part of,” coach Mike Norvell said after the game . “He’s our walking miracle. Seeing him, being able to take part in that with him is something I’ll never forget.” Ethan Pritchard walks out with his team nearly a year after surviving a gunshot wound to the head @FSUFootball pic.twitter.com/xTO54ukaih — ACC Network (@accnetwork) August 29, 2026 Perhaps motivated by Ethan Pritchard’s presence, Florida State put together a winning effort against New Mexico State. More on Ethan Pritchard shooting Ethan Pritchard, a former three-star recruit who arrived at Florida State in 2025, was the victim in a shooting while he was in his car on the night of Aug. 30, 2025, after a season-opening win for the ‘Noles over Alabama, while visiting family in Havana, Florida. articles.title: How Fever star Caitlin Clark winning MVP could create a huge problem for Indiana
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark winning the WNBA MVP award would be a dream scenario for the Indiana Fever. But it could also create a difficult financial question for the franchise sooner than expected. The Fever have built one of the league’s most promising cores around Clark, Aliyah Boston and Kelsey Mitc
articles._body: Caitlin Clark winning the WNBA MVP award would be a dream scenario for the Indiana Fever. But it could also create a difficult financial question for the franchise sooner than expected. The Fever have built one of the league’s most promising cores around Clark, Aliyah Boston and Kelsey Mitchell. But the WNBA’s new collective bargaining agreement has changed the financial landscape considerably, creating an expedited path to maximum-level contracts for standout players still on rookie deals. Clark is already eligible to renegotiate the final year of her rookie contract under the CBA’s Exceptional Performance on Initial Contract provision because of her previous All-WNBA honors. The Fever exercised her fourth-year option, keeping her under contract through 2027, but the new rules allow her to negotiate a higher salary and an extension. An MVP award would only raise the stakes further. “If we want to just quickly talk about the salary situation with the Indiana Fever, so Aliyah Boston is on her epic contract,” WNBA analyst Rachel DeMita said on her Courtside Club podcast . “Now, Caitlin Clark will also be eligible for a max contract next season because of this provision.” IF Caitlin Clark does win MVP, thanks to the new CBA it will trigger an option to renegotiate out of the final year of her rookie deal and she’ll be able to command a new 3 year super max contract. The Fever may have to pass the collection plate to keep their Big 3. #WNBA https://t.co/Fg6BWqNdru — Cindy Brunson (@CindyBrunsonAZ) August 30, 2026 Boston already represents an example of how quickly the Fever’s financial picture can change. Her new contract was made possible through the same accelerated pathway for players who earn major league honors while on their initial contracts. Meanwhile, Mitchell is already playing on a maximum-level deal , meaning Indiana could soon have three players commanding a significant portion of its salary cap. “If she wins MVP this season, Kelsey Mitchell is also on a max contract deal,” DeMita continued. “So you have three super max eligible players, or at least max eligible players for the squad next year.” That is where a potential problem emerges for Indiana. The Fever would undoubtedly want to keep their core intact, especially considering what Clark, Mitchell and Boston have accomplished together. But building a complete roster around multiple maximum-level contracts becomes considerably more challenging. The irony is that the Fever’s success could accelerate that challenge. Clark winning MVP would be another sign that Indiana’s investment in its young superstar has paid off, while simultaneously strengthening her leverage to command a significantly larger deal. The Fever have already seen their offense reach another level with Clark and Mitchell leading the way. For now, the organization can enjoy having one of the WNBA’s most talented cores. articles._body: Stanford football turned back its personal clock in hiring Tavita Pritchard as head coach . General manager Andrew Luck made the hire happen during Dec. 2025, bringing a former Cardinal home. Now Luck and Pritchard celebrated their first win together as GM and HC, defeating Hawai’i 37-27. Luck was all smiles on the sidelines during the game, despite how warm it got on the field. “It’s too hot out here, but I love it,” Luck said, adding what he loves about his role. “You get to run around and supporting everyone including the coaching staff.” Luck feels more hands on with the Cardinal compared to even when he lined up at quarterback. He even helped off an injured Cardinal player during the game too. Stanford GM Andrew Luck helped injured center Aidan Kilstrom off the field pic.twitter.com/upx3vbpJJ3 — Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) August 30, 2026 Perhaps he watched a new quarterback star emerge at The Farm. Davis Warren handled the QB1 reins and looked efficient: 22-of-34 passing for 310 yards and tossed one touchdown. Luck watched Pritchard turn to a familiar blueprint of Cardinal past: Pounding the ball with the running attack. Micah Ford answered the bell there, tallying 25 carries for 99 yards and scoring three touchdowns. Sedrick Irvin added some balance too in the ground game, spelling Ford with eight carries for 43 yards. Warren produced six wide receivers who caught between two to five passes, with Benjamin Blackburn leading the way with five receptions. JonAnthony Hall led the way with 81 receiving yards. Matt Rose led Stanford in piling nine tackles. Lonnie McAllister III delivered six tackles. So Pritchard and Luck got a glimpse of who the immediate contributors will be for this revamped Cardinal team. articles.summary: Southern University head coach Marshall Faulk sounded off on his team’s effort against Alabama State in the 30-17 loss on Saturday afternoon. Faulk told the media in attendance that he’s looking for better from his team and that they’ll look for other options if mistakes continu
articles._body: Southern University head coach Marshall Faulk sounded off on his team’s effort against Alabama State in the 30-17 loss on Saturday afternoon. Faulk told the media in attendance that he’s looking for better from his team and that they’ll look for other options if mistakes continue. “You cannot do that. And the reality is this, we’re gonna work with those guys on those things and try to get them to fix it. If not, we’re gonna find guys to play that might not be as talented, that might not be the best in that department, but at least they won’t beat themselves. You just cannot have the mistakes and the penalties and the things that we did to put ourselves in the position that we were in.” Faulk pinpointed penalties as what cost Southern the game. “Some costly holding penalties, just different things that we always talk about that are drive killers, and they’re hard to come back from. We have to get better at just being disciplined in the arena of how to play smart football. And how to do the number one thing that I told you guys we can’t do, which is beat yourself.” But despite his criticism and ultimate ultimatum for the team, he still believed that there were right spots, such as the defense. “I challenged them, like the last drive that they had in our end zone after we turned it over on downs, let them know it’s drives like that that you start to build your character. You don’t build character when things are good. We’re down two scores, and it’s like, right now you get a stop, we have a chance. And they went out there and they forced a field goal. He continued, “It’s so easy for me to sit here and pick out what they did wrong, but it’s something like that. In the moments when it may seem like you don’t really have a reason to play for, they went out there and they got a stop, man. They got a stop, and I’m proud of what they were able to do.” And he also articulated that he was pleased with the majority of his players. “For the majority of the guys, I was pleased with their effort. The guys played hard. We just have to finish plays, we gotta finish drives. As good a job as Alabama State did, we really put ourselves in some bad situations.” The post Marshall Faulk sends stern message after Southern loss to Alabama State appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles._body: The Seattle Storm have one game remaining on their schedule, a matchup at home against the Los Angeles Sparks before the WNBA goes on temporary hiatus for the FIBA World Cup. The Storm have been without veteran guard Natisha Hiedeman for the past three games due to a shoulder injury, and that will continue into Sunday. Natisha Hiedeman was officially ruled out on the Storm’s injury report for their game against the Sparks with said shoulder injury. It will be her fourth straight game sidelined, and the next opportunity she will have to get back on the court will be after the FIBA break on Sept. 17 against the Las Vegas Aces. The eight-year veteran was in the midst of a career season after signing with the Storm as a free agent . She had appeared in 36 games prior to her injury, at a little over 29 minutes per game. Hiedeman had been averaging a career-best 15.4 points, 2.7 rebounds, 4.8 assists and 1.1 steals with splits of 44.4 percent shooting from the field, 33.7 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 85.8 percent shooting from the free-throw line. The No. 18 overall pick in the 2019 WNBA Draft, Hiedeman began her career with the Connecticut Sun where she played for the first five seasons of her career before being traded to the Minnesota Lynx in exchange for Tiffany Mitchell and a future draft pick. The former Marquette standout played two seasons with the Lynx before joining the Storm. As for the team, the Storm have already been eliminated from playoff contention with a handful of games remaining in the regular season. But they have one of the most promising young cores in the league with Dominque Malonga, Awa Fam and Flau’jae Johnson. Drinkwi
articles._body: Missouri football head coach Eli Drinkwitz showed his vocal side one month ago. Drinkwitz called out the rival conference to the SEC, the Big Ten, over the belief his conference is more superior. But did drop an ’embarrassing’ take on the NCAA one month after his Big Ten rant. Drinkwitz got asked his true thoughts on the institution that oversees every Division I to III university. But focusing mainly on the Football Bowl Subdivision (FBS) side of things. “It’s embarrassing, man,” Drinkwitz said to reporters Saturday. “I’ve been saying this for three years that college football and college athletics are not in a great place.” He’s not zeroing in only on undrafted NFL players attempting to return to college either. Which the SEC prohibited ahead of Week 0 . Or even the College Football Transfer Portal in general. “I said this several years ago when we had the announcement of conference changes,” Drinkwitz added, referring to conference realignment. “This stuff is not good for any student athlete. And it’s a direct reflection of our inability as leaders to come up with a plan. Now you see the results. Mizzou jammed from the Big 12 during the first realignment cycle of the early 2010s. The Tigers linked up with Texas A&M to bolt from the conference and land in the SEC. So Mizzou handed the SEC its first-ever St. Louis television market in the process. But realignment continued with Texas and Oklahoma defecting the Big 12 for the SEC in 2023. “For us to complete operating like this is a complete clown show,” Drinkwitz added. He claims complaints and suggestions have been ignored. And now it must come down to administrators and court room to figure out how to fix this growing problem. articles.title: Watch Giants officially retire Jeff Kent’s No. 21
articles.summary: The San Francisco Giants officially retired Jeff Kent’s No. 21 on Saturday at Oracle Park, honoring the former second baseman between games of their day-night doubleheader against the Arizona Diamondbacks. Jon Miller opened the ceremony by sharing memories of Kent, including his first walk-
articles._body: The San Francisco Giants officially retired Jeff Kent’s No. 21 on Saturday at Oracle Park, honoring the former second baseman between games of their day-night doubleheader against the Arizona Diamondbacks. Jon Miller opened the ceremony by sharing memories of Kent, including his first walk-off home run at Oracle Park, then known as Pacific Bell Park. Giants figures including Dusty Baker, Juan Marichal, Barry Bonds, Will Clark and current President of Baseball Operations Buster Posey joined Kent’s family on the field . Jeff Kent officially gets his No. 21 jersey retired by the Giants pic.twitter.com/pD1VF7LJv4 — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 30, 2026   Kent later walked out of the dugout to AC/DC’s “Back in Black” and embraced Bonds, his former teammate. Following the ceremony, Kent delivered the ceremonial first pitch to his father, Alan Kent, before celebrating on the field in a truck while being chased by mascot Lou Seal. Kent, 58, became the 15th player honored by San Francisco in this manner, while No. 21 became the organization’s 13th officially retired number. Christy Mathewson and John McGraw are included among the 15 honorees, although neither played during the era when MLB players wore uniform numbers. The ceremony had originally been scheduled before Saturday’s single game, but the Giants’ schedule changed after a rainout makeup game in Atlanta forced Sunday’s series finale against the Diamondbacks to become a Saturday doubleheader. The Kent ceremony was consequently moved to the period between the two games. Kent spent six of his 17 major-league seasons with San Francisco, appearing in 900 games and producing 175 home runs, 689 RBIs and a .290 batting average. His most decorated season with the Giants came in 2000, when he won the National League MVP award after recording a career-best .334 average, 1.021 OPS and 33 homers. While playing for San Francisco, he also collected three of his four career Silver Slugger Awards and made three All-Star teams. Kent spent time with the Toronto Blue Jays, New York Mets, Cleveland Indians, Houston Astros and Los Angeles Dodgers during his 17-year career, hitting 377 home runs — the most ever by an MLB second baseman — and accumulating 1,518 RBIs, third-most among players at the position. Ward has experienced his share of growing pains as he continues to develop under a new coaching staff and of
articles._body: Robert Saleh is not just optimistic about Cam Ward’s future with the Tennessee Titans . The head coach is willing to put his own reputation behind his belief in the young quarterback. Ward has experienced his share of growing pains as he continues to develop under a new coaching staff and offensive system. But Saleh has consistently maintained that the Titans quarterback has the tools to succeed , even as the team works through mistakes during the preseason. “Yeah, he’s not stubborn. He’s not stuck. He wants to learn, he wants to evolve, he wants to grow, not just football-wise, but as a man, as a person,” Saleh told reporters . “This kid’s not gonna fail” Robert Saleh plants his flag on Cam Ward and what he’s learned about his young QB this August pic.twitter.com/1e1uus5wrK — AtoZ Sports Nashville (@AtoZSports) August 30, 2026 After spending August around Ward, Saleh explained what has stood out most about the quarterback beyond what he can do on the field. After spending August around Ward, Saleh pointed to the 24-year-old’s willingness to keep learning and the maturity he has shown in his interactions throughout the organization. The Titans coach cited the way his quarterback carries himself around teammates and others as evidence of qualities that may not always show up on the stat sheet. “The way he handles himself with you guys, the way he handles himself with his teammates, the conversations he has are very mature for his age,” Saleh said. “He’s much deeper than you would think for a young, hotshot quarterback.” The head tactician’s confidence is particularly notable given the pressure surrounding Ward’s development. The quarterback is entering his second NFL season after Tennessee selected him with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, and his ability to develop into a franchise quarterback remains central to the Titans’ long-term plans. While Ward’s preseason performances have featured missed opportunities , Saleh has repeatedly emphasized that growth takes time and that live repetitions are part of the process. His latest assessment, however, went beyond patience. “So he’s, this kid’s not going to fail,” Saleh said. “Obviously, I put my job on that one, but he’s not going to fail. He’s special.” It is a bold declaration from a coach who has only recently begun working with Ward, but Saleh’s comments make clear that his belief is rooted in what he has seen every day. The Titans still have plenty to prove entering the regular season, and Ward’s development will remain under a microscope. articles._body: Riley Leonard and Anthony Richardson are on great terms as the competition for the Indianapolis Colts’ secondary quarterback role remains up for grabs ahead of the 2026 NFL season. Leonard is gearing up for Year 2 of his career, while Richardson goes through Year 4. Leonard played in five games as a rookie following Daniel Jones’ season-ending injury, splitting time with Philip Rivers. Richardson was the starter in 2023 and 2024 before losing his job to Jones. Jones has successfully undergone Achilles rehab, on pace to be the Colts’ starter. The focus is now the backup role, seeing Leonard and Richardson duke it out for the spot . “My best is good enough to win, and Anthony (Richardson Sr.’s) best is good enough to win. You never want to win a competition because maybe you both played bad and you just didn’t play as bad. … Who can reach their full potential?” Leonard said, per reporter James Boyd. Riley Leonard on trying to be the #Colts ’ QB2: “My best is good enough to win, and Anthony (Richardson Sr.’s) best is good enough to win. You never want to win a competition because maybe you both played bad and you just didn’t play as bad. … Who can reach their full potential?” pic.twitter.com/DxGk5ITOOD — James Boyd (@RomeovilleKid) August 29, 2026 What lies ahead for Riley Leonard, Colts this season The Colts have promising talent that can allow them to be in the playoff mix once again. However, they need to do their best to protect Daniel Jones at quarterback while Riley Leonard and Anthony Richardson handle backup duties. Leonard made five appearances that featured one start throughout the 2025 season. He completed 39 passes for 415 yards and two touchdowns and three interceptions while racking up six rushes for 27 yards and two touchdowns. As for Richardson, he seeks the healthiest of his career after suffering season-ending injuries in his first three seasons. 2024 marks his best as he threw for 1,814 yards and eight touchdowns and 12 interceptions while recording 86 rushes for 499 yards and six touchdowns. The Colts will seek to improve upon their 8–9 record from the previous two seasons, make the playoffs after a five-year absence and win the AFC South for the first time since 2014. Indianapolis’ campaign will get underway at home. They host the Baltimore Ravens as kickoff commences on Sept. 13 at 1 p.m. ET. RBs Kromah, Singleton power Florida State to 34-17 win in season opener
articles.summary: The Florida State football team gets big days from running backs Ousmane Kromah and Samuel Singleton in season-opening victory over New Mexico State.
articles._body: If Mike Norvell was hoping this Week Zero game against New Mexico State was going to give his Florida State football team some confidence and momentum heading into its big Labor Day showdown with SMU, he could not have gone home very happy Saturday night. The Seminoles’ fan base undoubtedly feels the same way. Despite being favored by more than 30 points in its season opener against a team expected to finish in the bottom half of Conference USA, Florida State struggled to generate much separation before salting away a 34-17 victory. The game was never really in doubt, but late in the third quarter, Florida State actually led the Aggies by only seven points. The Seminoles then went on a 12-play, 51-yard drive, capped off by a 2-yard touchdown run by Samuel Singleton Jr., to push their advantage to 24-10. And a 41-yard field goal from Gabe Panikowski extended the lead to 17 points early in the fourth quarter. New Mexico State then scored on a 34-yard touchdown strike midway through the fourth quarter to make things interesting, but the Seminoles responded with another TD drive to make it 34-17. Running back Ousmane Kromah capped off that eight-play march with a 1-yard plunge to give FSU its third rushing touchdown of the night. While the Seminoles’ offense was choppy, the stars of the night were the running backs. Kromah rushed for 115 yards on 14 carries, Singleton scored twice and racked up 96 yards of offense (54 receiving, 42 rushing), and Florida State out-rushed New Mexico State by nearly 200 yards. The Seminoles’ passing attack, however, was uneven for most of the night. Quarterback Ashton Daniels, making his first start for Florida State, completed 17 of 27 passes for 202 yards with one touchdown and one interception. Florida State took a 17-7 lead into halftime after Daniels found Singleton in the end zone for a 4-yard touchdown pass with 36 seconds left in the second quarter. The Seminoles scored their first touchdown on a 4-yard keeper by Daniels earlier in the second quarter, and their first points of the year came on a 43-yard first-quarter field goal by Panikowski. Daniels finished the half with 144 yards on 9-of-14 passing with one interception. The Seminoles had a 220-140 advantage in total yardage. New Mexico State’s lone score in the first half came on a 33-yard touchdown pass from Trey Hedden to Brodie Malone-Bradford after the receiver beat FSU cornerback Ja’Bril Rawls with a double-move. articles.title: Giants HC John Harbaugh tells fans what to expect from trade addition CJ Okoye
articles.summary: The New York Giants addressed a clear need on the interior defensive line on Saturday, acquiring defensive tackle CJ Okoye from the Baltimore Ravens for a 2028 seventh-round pick. The move reunites Okoye with head coach John Harbaugh, who coached him in Baltimore this past season. The 24-year-old
articles._body: The New York Giants addressed a clear need on the interior defensive line on Saturday, acquiring defensive tackle CJ Okoye from the Baltimore Ravens for a 2028 seventh-round pick. The move reunites Okoye with head coach John Harbaugh, who coached him in Baltimore this past season. The 24-year-old Okoye stands at 6-foot-6 and weighs 365 pounds, giving New York a sizable interior option. He appeared in 13 games for the Ravens last season and finished with 15 tackles, including one tackle for loss. He was considered to be on the roster bubble in Baltimore heading into Sunday’s 53-man roster deadline. Harbaugh explained why the Giants were interested in bringing Okoye to New York, saying : “He’s a guy that we got to know recently last year, came in, was with the Chargers actually with my brother [Jim] for a couple years in the international program. So a guy who had been developmental type guy, learning the game and tremendous physical skills, hard worker, has really dedicated himself over the last few years to learning the game really because he didn’t play it growing up and made great strides, made great strides with Dennis Johnson, our defensive line coach last year. That’s where he kind of broke through and had a really good season.” John Harbaugh talks about what the Giants are getting in C. J. Okoye pic.twitter.com/qLWsHfZl6A — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) August 29, 2026 Okoye is viewed primarily as an interior defender capable of playing both the A and B gaps with New York. “We see him as an inside defender, a defensive tackle, A gap, B gap player, run stopper, pocket pusher in terms of the past game and just a really a real big physical player,” said Harbaugh. “So kind of a type of guy we’ve been looking for and we’re really excited to get him up here.” The Giants were looking for more interior defensive line depth, and Okoye provides familiarity with Harbaugh’s coaching staff. He joins several other former Ravens in New York, including tight end Isaiah Likely, punter Jordan Stout, defensive back Ar’Darius Washington and fullback Patrick Ricard. New York was able to use a 2028 seventh-round selection acquired earlier in the week from the Kansas City Chiefs in the Joshua Ezeudu trade to complete the deal for Okoye. Harbaugh also indicated that the Giants have not stopped searching for defensive tackle help. He said the team is still looking and is making and receiving calls as part of its normal roster evaluation process. NFL teams must reach the 53-man regular-season roster limit by 6 p.m. ET Sunday.
