articles._body: Amid Jonathan Kuminga’s move to join the Minnesota Timberwolves , many have wondered about his position on the ascendant, young Western Conference team. But in an interview with Run It Back , Kuminga’s agent laid out how his client will fit with the team. "Melo, Ant, Jaden, JK, Rudy… Chris Finch did a great job of explaining the role that he envisions." Aaron Turner says that Jonathan Kuminga will be starting for the Timberwolves this season (via @RunItBackFDTV ) pic.twitter.com/SkCtsgyrp3 — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 30, 2026 Aaron Turner explained that Kuminga was brought in with a clearly defined starting role from the jump. “Yeah, this was a clear-cut… you’re coming in here to start at the four, with Melo, Ant, Jaden, JK, Rudy. Obviously they have great young guys coming in too. You got Ayo, you got Terrence Shannon Jr., Donte when he comes back.” Turner then explained how the Timberwolves are viewing Kuminga’s role heading into camp, given how stacked the roster is. “I think on paper, this is obviously one of the most stacked teams. Going into camp, going into preseason, how are they viewing JK? Is he a starter? Is he more of an energy guy? What are they looking to use him for, playing with Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball? Obviously he’s 23 years old.” He pointed out that this is the first time in Kuminga’s six-year career he’s entered a season already knowing he’d start. “So they pitched a great, clear role. And for JK going into year six, which it’s crazy it’s year six now, but he’s never got to come into the season going, ‘I know I’m the starter.’ That tailwind of just clear, ‘Hey man, you’re coming in here to start.’ Chris Finch did a great job explaining the role to him that he envisions and how they wanna play.” The post Jonathan Kuminga’s agent reveals his role in Minnesota’s lineup appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles._body: The long-scrutinized Connor Hellebuyck proved he could meet the moment when he helped Team USA capture its first Olympics men’s ice hockey gold medal in 46 years. Now, he wants another chance to do it in the NHL. The Winnipeg Jets star goaltender requested a trade earlier this week, triggering a frenzy around the league. There are plenty of good teams whose biggest obstacle to an eventful run in the Stanley Cup Playoffs is a shaky netminder. Although the 2024-25 Hart Memorial Trophy winner and three-time Vezina Trophy recipient can significantly raise a squad’s ceiling, he is quite expensive. There are two franchises who often make noise in the spring and consistently find ways to overcome seemingly daunting salary cap issues, but believe it or not, they are considered the most improbable landing spots for Hellebuyck. “Florida and Vegas are the least-likely destinations,” Lyle Richardson of Spectors Hockey writes. “If those clubs can’t afford to acquire {Dylan} Larkin ($8.7 million AAV), they can’t afford Hellebuyck, and even if they could, they lack the tradeable assets to entice the Jets, unless they can somehow get a third team involved in the deal to send them the necessary assets to make it happen.” Hellebuyck’s contract carries a steep average annual value of $8.5 million for the next five seasons. The Florida Panthers and Vegas Golden Knights already have stout rosters that contain hefty financial commitments. Absorbing another one would be difficult. Imagine what fans would say, though. They might combust. If either of these polarizing squads is able to complete a deal with the Jets, they would probably morph into a full-fledged villain. They would also improve their already solid Stanley Cup prospects . Connor Hellebuyck posted a 2.86 goals against average and .895 save percentage in 57 games for Winnipeg last season. Perhaps he can recapture his elite form in a new environment. Wherever he winds up, the lights will be even brighter. Such is the case when a player demands out. articles.title: Colts’ Blake Grupe gets 100% real on the uncertainty players face before cut day
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts’ kicking competition has come down to Blake Grupe and Spencer Shrader, and now the team must decide who gets the job after Saturday’s preseason finale against the Detroit Lions. Grupe made two field goals in Indianapolis’ 25-16 loss, connecting from 46 and
articles._body: The Indianapolis Colts’ kicking competition has come down to Blake Grupe and Spencer Shrader , and now the team must decide who gets the job after Saturday’s preseason finale against the Detroit Lions. Grupe made two field goals in Indianapolis’ 25-16 loss, connecting from 46 and 36 yards during the first half. Shrader had one opportunity after halftime and converted from 60 yards. Following the game, Grupe acknowledged that the next step is simply waiting to find out who earned the roster spot . “I definitely feel confident that I put my best foot forward, and now you just sit and wait,” said Grupe via WISH-TV News. "Now you just sit and wait" A big decision for #Colts head coach Shane Steichen as Blake Grupe and Spencer Shrader each hope to be named the team's starting kicker. Which player do you think should earn the spot? pic.twitter.com/nzb0nIBOph — WISH-TV News (@WISHNews8) August 29, 2026 The competition had remained very close throughout the preseason . Shrader entered the Lions game with a perfect 4-for-4 record on preseason field-goal attempts, including three successful kicks from at least 48 yards. Grupe had shown stronger stretches during practices, keeping the battle undecided. Special teams coordinator Brian Mason previously said the Colts “can’t go wrong” with either kicker, while also explaining that performance during games would carry the greatest importance in the final evaluation. Grupe brings plenty of NFL experience into the competition. As a rookie with the New Orleans Saints in 2023, he made all 40 extra-point attempts and converted 30 of 37 field goals. In 2024, he made 27 of 31 field goals and 31 of 33 extra points. His 2025 season was more difficult, as he missed a league-high eight field-goal attempts through Week 12 and converted only five of 11 attempts beyond 40 yards. The Saints released him on November 25, 2025, before he joined Indianapolis’ practice squad on December 2. Grupe later made a 60-yard go-ahead field goal against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 15, surpassing the Colts’ previous franchise record of 58 yards set by Dan Miller in 1982. He re-signed with Indianapolis on a one-year, $1.4 million contract on March 16, 2026. Now, after weeks of competition, Grupe and Shrader can only wait for the Colts to make their choice. articles.title: Broderick Jones trade grades for Cowboys, Steelers
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers looked at Broderick Jones as a powerful offensive lineman who could solidify their offensive line when they moved up in the 2023 NFL Draft to select the Georgia product. However, a neck injury sustained against the Chicago Bears last year have led the Steelers to move on f
articles._body: The Pittsburgh Steelers looked at Broderick Jones as a powerful offensive lineman who could solidify their offensive line when they moved up in the 2023 NFL Draft to select the Georgia product. However, a neck injury sustained against the Chicago Bears last year have led the Steelers to move on from the former first-round pick. The Steelers traded Jones and a fourth-round pick to the Dallas Cowboy for a future third- and sixth-round pick. The trade was first reported by ESPN NFL Insider Adam Schefter. Jones had to endure spinal fusion surgery and that led to a long rehab process. He was finally allowed to resume football activities at the start of training camp, but it was difficult for Jones to return to form. It seemed likely that the Steelers would move on from Jones in the offseason because they drafted tackle Max Iheanachor with their first-round pick. They also moved Troy Fautanu from right tackle to left tackle. Jones seemed to be having issues with both his strength and technique after returning to practice this summer. He explained that it was taking time for him to find his form. “I’m still working through it,” Jones said . “I wouldn’t say I’m where I want to be at. Just trying to get back in shape and putting the weight back on in the right places.” Cowboys unhappy with their offensive line performance The Cowboys are making the trade because they have significant concerns about their offensive line play. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones, who also serves as the team’s general manager, said the team was going to be very aggressive making moves prior to the start of the season because they wanted to upgrade their overall depth and play along the offensive line. The Cowboys have Terrence Steele as their right tackle, but head coach Brian Schottenheimer has not been overly complimentary to the 6-6, 320-pound, 7-year veteran. Steele struggled with his pass protection last year. As a result, if Jones can work himself back to a respectable level of strength and technique, he should have a good chance of getting significant playing time at some point in the season. The Steelers are making a statement in trading a player who was still on his initial contract. They are telling the rest of the NFL that they don’t believe that Jones can get close to top form after suffering a serious injury. While they could be right, a neck injury could take longer to recover from and they could be getting rid of a player who just might need a bit longer to recover. If that is the case, they are making a significant mistake. Trade grades The Cowboys have not given up much to get a player who could be a key contributor to their offensive line depth if he can make a full recovery from his neck injury. He has done enough to participate in training camp activities for the Steelers, but he still has more distance to travel. If the Cowboys have patience with him and given him the time to regain his strength and technique, it could be a winning move. Grade: B-plus The Steelers are giving up on a player that has been a contributor in the past. They don’t believe he will be able to recover, so they decided to take two future picks for him. There is nothing inspiring about this trade from the Pittsburgh perspective. Grade: C-minus The post Broderick Jones trade grades for Cowboys, Steelers appeared first on ClutchPoints .

Five things to look for going into the 2026 Stanford Football season
articles.summary: Here are five things to look for as the Stanford Cardinal begin the Tavita Pritchard era.
articles._body: With Stanford football beginning their season against Hawaii today, it’s time for me to write five things to look for going into the 2026 season. Ok, let’s dive in! #1. Can Davis Warren bring the upgrade needed at quarterback? Michigan grad transfer Davis Warren by all accounts has looked the part in the spring and in the fall. Everyone you talk to on the team will tell you how great of a leader he is and how much faith they have in him. The vibe is certainly that he’s a much better quarterback than what Stanford had last season. But vibes and seeing it in the game aren’t the same thing. The first thing to look for with Stanford is how Warren is looking and whether or not he truly is the upgrade that they say he is. READ: What can Stanford expect from quarterback Davis Warren? #2. Can the offensive line give Warren the help he needs? Offensive line has been a major thorn in Stanford’s side these past few seasons. It’s really been a struggle. Last year was a bit better, but still nowhere near where it needs to be. With Keli’i Kekuewa and Tavita Thompson as the two offensive line coaches, there is a hope that the offensive line will be better this season. The biggest thing right now is they need offensive tackle Niki Prongos and offensive guard Simione Pale to get healthy. With those two in the lineup, the offensive line should be better than what it was last year. #3. Can Kris Richard’s defense deliver the goods? With inside linebacker Matt Rose as the anchor, Stanford has a new defensive scheme, a 4-3 scheme, under defensive coordinator Kris Richard . With his experience having been a defensive coordinator with the Seahawks during the Legion of Boom era, Stanford should have a better defense this season. It was already decent last year. If they can take another step forward, forcing more takeaways, and getting more tackles for loss, that would be big. #4. Can Benji Blackburn become the new franchise tight end? Junior tight end Benji Blackburn is coming off a season in which he had nine receptions for 109 yards and one touchdown. With Sam Roush now with the Chicago Bears, it’s on Blackburn to be the new face of “Tight End U”. If Blackburn can rise to the occasion, that will give the offense a lot more versatility. #5. How does Tavita Pritchard handle the play calling? Given it’s his first season as head coach, a big thing to look for this season is how does head coach Tavita Pritchard go about calling the plays? When he was offensives coordinator under David Shaw , Shaw was the one who called the plays. Now it’s Pritchard’s chance to spread his wings and show what he can do as a play caller. articles.summary: Spencer Rattler’s time on the New Orleans Saints may look to continue ahead of the 2026 NFL season. Rattler is approaching the third season of his career in the league with the Saints. The team selected him in the fifth round of the 2024 draft, having garnered several starts throughout his
articles._body: Spencer Rattler’s time on the New Orleans Saints may look to continue ahead of the 2026 NFL season. Rattler is approaching the third season of his career in the league with the Saints. The team selected him in the fifth round of the 2024 draft, having garnered several starts throughout his first two campaigns. New Orleans seeks to make strides as a rebuilding squad. NFL insiders Jeremy Fowler and Adam Schefter provided updates on the team . Fowler reported on Rattler’s situation, while Schefter listed roster updates regarding cuts . “The Saints received trade interest in QB Spencer Rattler but plan to keep him, per sources. Rattler will serve as quality depth behind Tyler Shough, barring a change,” Fowler wrote. “Saints waived WR Ronnie Bell, S Elliott Davison, QB Hunter Dekkers, WR Bub Means, TE Zaire Mitchell-Paden, Edge Garrett Nelson, DL Kahlil Saunders, DL Brien Taylor, OL Xavier Truss and Edge Malakai Williams,” Schefter reported. The Saints received trade interest in QB Spencer Rattler but plan to keep him, per sources. Rattler will serve as quality depth behind Tyler Shough, barring a change. pic.twitter.com/1kmZcWzSHb — Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) August 30, 2026 What lies ahead for Spencer Rattler, Saints this season Spencer Rattler and the Saints anticipate for great things going into the 2026 season. For Rattler’s case, he wants his individual stats to improve in a significant manner. Rattler has appeared in 16 games that features 14 starts, going 1-13 in those chances. He has completed 2,904 yards and 12 touchdowns and 10 interceptions. He also racked up 49 rushes for 313 yards on the ground. The 2025 season saw him go 1-7 in his eight starts, throwing for 1,586 yards and eight touchdowns and five interceptions. The Saints will seek to improve upon their 6-11 record from the previous season. They also intend to end their five-year drought of both a playoff appearance and an NFC South title. New Orleans’ regular season will get underway on the road. They take on the Detroit Lions as kickoff commences on Sept. 13 at 1 p.m. ET. articles.title: Timberwolves officially waive John Konchar after Josh Green trade
articles.summary: The Minnesota Timberwolves needed to pull off a trade to help clear salary for the pending signing of free agent forward Jonathan Kuminga, and they did so on Friday by sending Josh Green to the Utah Jazz in a three-team trade that also saw them acquire veteran wing John Konchar in return. The Tim
articles._body: The Minnesota Timberwolves needed to pull off a trade to help clear salary for the pending signing of free agent forward Jonathan Kuminga , and they did so on Friday by sending Josh Green to the Utah Jazz in a three-team trade that also saw them acquire veteran wing John Konchar in return. The Timberwolves were then expected to waive and stretch Konchar’s contract to free salary cap room, and they executed that move over the weekend, as per ClutchPoints’ NBA insider Brett Siegel. John Konchar was under contract with the Timberwolves for one more season at slightly over $6 million after the trade, and he was set to hit unrestricted free agency next offseason. He now gets to potentially choose a new team in time for training camp in a little over one month. The former Purdue Fort Wayne star went undrafted in the 2019 NBA Draft and began his career with the Memphis Grizzlies via two-way contract. He played the first seven and half seasons of his career with the Grizzlies before being traded to the Jazz via the Jaren Jackson Jr. deal this past deadline. He appeared in a total of 56 games, including eight starts, at a little over 19 minutes per game splitting time between the Grizzlies and Jazz this past season. He averaged 4.4 points, 4.3 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.5 steals with splits of 47.2 percent shooting from the field, 28.3 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 72.7 percent shooting from the free-throw line. The Wolves will now be able to commence with the Kuminga signing amid getting under the second apron. In addition to Konchar, the Wolves also received Cody Williams in the trade, and he is expected to remain on the roster. articles.title: Mets’ Juan Soto drops honest admission on returning from injury
articles.summary: Juan Soto is glad to be back out on the field after recovering from his injury before the New York Mets’ matchup against the Houston Astros on Saturday night. Soto returned to the last-place Mets after missing 31 games with a grade 2 strain of his left calf. It was the second IL stint of [&
articles._body: Juan Soto is glad to be back out on the field after recovering from his injury before the New York Mets’ matchup against the Houston Astros on Saturday night. Soto returned to the last-place Mets after missing 31 games with a grade 2 strain of his left calf. It was the second IL stint of the season for Soto. Soto’s first game back ended up seeing him go 1-for-4 in his at-bats. He got an RBI in the fifth inning with a single to right field, driving home Francisco Lindor. The star hitter reflected on his performance after the game, having relief to be playing alongside his teammates again after a long absence. “It’s really frustrating to be down and not being able to help your team…to not perform out there, have fun with the boys. That keeps me motivated to be out there again,” Soto said. "It's really frustrating to be down and not being able to help your team…to not perform out there, have fun with the boys. That keeps me motivated to be out there again." – Juan Soto on his return pic.twitter.com/xqVEUezhp4 — SNY Mets (@SNY_Mets) August 29, 2026 How Juan Soto, Mets played against Astros Juan Soto got to enjoy having a decent night in his first game back, seeing the Mets beat the Astros 6-2 in Game 2. They bounced back from a 3-1 loss in Game 1 on Friday. Both teams took a while to get going, being even at one run apiece after four innings. It wasn’t until the fifth frame when the Mets bloomed with three runs. Houston tried to fight back in the eighth inning, but New York sealed the deal with a three-run homer from Francisco Alvarez. The bullpen had a solid night on the mound. Nolan McLean earned the win after serving for seven innings, striking out four batters while conceding two hits. New York improved to a 61-75 record on the season but remain at the bottom of the NL East Division standings. They are under the Washington Nationals and the Miami Marlins at the moment. The Mets will look forward to Game 3 of their series against the Astros. That game will commence on Aug. 30 as first pitch takes place at 3:10 p.m. ET. articles.title: Colts HC Shane Steichen gives final take on Anthony Richardson, Riley Leonard QB battle
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts finished the preseason with a 25-16 loss to the Detroit Lions, but head coach Shane Steichen still has not made a final decision on Daniel Jones’ backup. With roster cutdown day approaching, Steichen said both Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard showed positive signs
articles._body: The Indianapolis Colts finished the preseason with a 25-16 loss to the Detroit Lions, but head coach Shane Steichen still has not made a final decision on Daniel Jones’ backup. With roster cutdown day approaching, Steichen said both Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard showed positive signs during Saturday’s game. “I thought Anthony had some good drives for sure and did some good things,” said Steichen. “I think Riley did some good things as well, I just obviously don’t want to turn it over in the redzone.” Indianapolis Colts' Shane Steichen On Anthony Richardson Sr., Riley Leonard After Preseason Finale pic.twitter.com/1XpJKGdUGs — Jake Arthur (@JakeArthurNFL) August 29, 2026 Richardson handled most of the quarterback snaps during the preseason and completed 21 of 33 passes for 249 yards across three games. Against the Lions, he went 7-for-10 for 80 yards. He also finished the preseason with one rushing touchdown, while throwing no touchdown passes, along with one fumble and one interception. Leonard completed 20 of 42 passes for 199 yards during the preseason. On Saturday, the 2025 sixth-round pick went 3-for-7 for 48 yards. His afternoon included a scoring drive in which he connected on a couple of important passes before DJ Giddens scored on a 6-yard touchdown run. Leonard later threw an interception on a drive that began just outside the red zone. He said afterward that the bigger issue was his inability to get his teammates properly positioned before the snap, which prevented him from creating more time to throw. The pass itself went where he intended, but he acknowledged that he missed the opportunity. The competition has produced little separation statistically. Richardson’s 21 completions on 33 attempts compare with Leonard’s 20 completions on 42 attempts, while neither quarterback threw a preseason touchdown. Leonard had two interceptions. Steichen previously said he had no timeline for naming Jones’ backup before the Colts open the regular season against the Baltimore Ravens on Sept. 13, and he would not commit to the decision being permanent once made. Despite competing for the same job throughout the offseason, Richardson and Leonard have continued supporting each other . Richardson was among those celebrating Leonard after the touchdown drive, demonstrating the relationship between the two quarterbacks even as the competition reaches its final stage. Skinner earns 500th career win as No. 3 Kentucky VB sweeps USF
articles.summary: Kentucky volleyball gets sweeps on back-to-back nights, as head coach Craig Skinner earned his 500th career victory.
articles._body: A shaky start ends in a sweet surprise. Head coach Craig Skinner earned his 500th career win as No. 3 Kentucky grinded out a sweep over USF (25-18, 25-16, 25-19) on Saturday in Memorial Coliseum, leaving the court with a face smothered in blue icing. 500 career wins for Craig Skinner! pic.twitter.com/1ehNRRlXzL — SterlingVision (@sterlingvis1) August 29, 2026 “It’s such an honor to get to play for this program and for him and for someone who is just such a great figure who cares so much about us as people,” said middle blocker Lizzie Carr. “That’s not found everywhere in college sports.” The first set was flat-out sloppy. By the end of the opening frame, the teams had eight attack errors each and eight service errors combined. UK finished with a .067 hit rate that actually climbed throughout, and USF was in the red at -.077. The match started as a game of runs with the Bulls going up 3-0 and the Cats immediately responded with a 6-0 run. The game would settle at an ongoing stalemate before UK wrapped up the set on a 9-1 run, winning it 25-18. Kentucky came out of the second set playing more like themselves, bouncing back with a set hit rate of .429 en route to a 25-16 triumph. Lizzie Carr emerged as UK’s star with five kills in the set. Carr finished with 10 kills in total on a .421 hit percentage and six blocks, utilizing her height to her advantage. The Cats broke open a tie at 9-all with a 5-0 run and from there coasted to the second-frame victory, with 16 kills to four errors. The final set was a similar story, except this time it favored USF. It was the Bulls who forged a 5-0 run mid-way through the set to take a 14-10 lead (their first since the opening frame). But the HMC crowd was too loud, too rowdy, as Kentucky reclaimed the momentum and snapped back with a 9-1 run, including three Carr kills and two Kassie O’Brien aces in this span. From there, the Cats handled business to a 25-19 final set victory, earning a sweep in back-to-back evenings at the Bluegrass Battle. Asia Thigpen and Kennedy Washington took on the role of unsung heroes. Thigpen played an all-around match, tallying a Kentucky third-best seven kills on a .455 hit rate, eight digs, a block, and an assist each. Washington had an even more efficient six kills on a .625 hit percentage and three blocks. She didn’t register an attack error until the final set. “Defensively we were really good,” said Skinner. “Great teams have to find ways to win when everything’s not clicking.” USF closes out the showcase with a Sunday noon game against Utah State. The Bulls should have some blue behind them, though, as Rajon Rondo’s daughter — Ryelle Rondo — plays for them. Rondo is listed as a libero, but mainly played in the back row on Saturday evening, registering two digs in the match.

articles.summary: New Philadelphia 76ers guard Kentavious Caldwell-Pope dealt with an unfortunate incident that occurred at his new residence in Philadelphia. According to a TikTok post by Caldwell-Pope’s wife, McKenzie, the couple’s penthouse was struck by lightning, forcing her to descend 14 flights
articles._body: New Philadelphia 76ers guard Kentavious Caldwell-Pope dealt with an unfortunate incident that occurred at his new residence in Philadelphia. According to a TikTok post by Caldwell-Pope’s wife, McKenzie, the couple’s penthouse was struck by lightning , forcing her to descend 14 flights of stairs to evacuate. @mckenziecaldwellpope First day in Philly #storytime ♬ original sound – McKenzie Caldwell-Pope “You guys, it’s our first day in Philly, and our condo got struck by lightning. I’m in a hotel right now because I’m homeless,” She said in the TikTok video explaining what occurred. She then gave a backstory about why they moved and what happened. “I flew in yesterday, so I arrived around 10 a.m. The movers had already started moving things in about 9 a.m., right? I get here, I meet my moving coordinator, everything’s going smoothly. Literally, I’m here for maybe 30 minutes after I sign the lease. You guys, I hear the loudest bang I’ve ever heard in my life. Mind you, we’re on the penthouse floor, the highest floor. I hear the loudest bang. All of a sudden, sh*t starts shooting out of the ceiling, and water is pouring and dumping in.” She then showed a video of the water pouring into the penthouse. “So everyone just starts screaming, and we’re like, ‘We have to get out of here.’ When I say ‘was coming,’ it was like there was at least 2-3 inches of water in there before we even got out. We were like, ‘We have to go,’ so we just grabbed our valuables and got the f*ck…then we got out, and there was water coming from the elevators. All of the elevators are broken, so we had to climb down 14 floors to get to safety.” McKenzie then said the front desk at the penthouse didn’t believe her at first, and they initially thought the sprinklers might have gone off by mistake. The movers who were helping them place their stuff in the penthouse and the electrician confirmed her suspicions that something was amiss. “And they say you guys, after everyone was denying that, I heard what I heard. Why did the electrician say, ‘Yeah, you got struck by lightning, and there’s a one-in-400-million chance of a unit getting struck the way this unit got struck.’ What?” According to her video, it appears everyone made it out of the penthouse safely, and she joked that her survival might prove she has superpowers. “The only bright side in this is that I might have superpowers because the way our unit got struck…” The post Kentavious Caldwell-Pope’s new Philly penthouse struck by lightning, flooded appeared first on ClutchPoints .

Chrys Black Jr. Powers Pittsburgh Central Catholic to Marquee Win in Season Opener
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Central Catholic, the Class-6A favorites in the WPIAL, opened its season up with a statement win over nationally-ranked Bergen Catholic on Friday night. One player that made the “upset” possible was one of the Vikings’ more under-the-radar stars, Chrys Black Jr., a junio
articles._body: Pittsburgh Central Catholic, the Class-6A favorites in the WPIAL, opened its season up with a statement win over nationally-ranked Bergen Catholic on Friday night. One player that made the “upset” possible was one of the Vikings’ more under-the-radar stars, Chrys Black Jr. , a junior running back. Black saw decent playing time when healthy a season ago, scoring nine total touchdowns across five playoff games, but he often is overlooked by some for some of older players on the roster, such as four-star prospects Jimmy Kalis and James Halter , along with running back/linebacker Roman Thompson . Time and time again though, Black has proved to teams that he has just as much of an impact on the Vikings’ team as some of his more nationally-known peers and he proved it again in his team’s victory over Bergen Catholic as he rushed for 153 yards and scored three second-half touchdowns. “I knew it was going to be a physical game,” Black said after the game. “I knew what I was going to have to do. They’re a great team. I knew what it was going to be like. I knew it wasn’t going to be easy, but Pittsburgh ball better than Jersey ball so I just had to show them that.” Black did not only make his presence known on the ground on Friday as he made plays in all three phases of the game. On top of his monster rushing game, Black had two field-flipping punt returns, a punt return touchdown that was called back due to a penalty and a couple of big-time hits on defense. “I do whatever they want me to do,” Black said. “I’ll play any position they want me to play. I’m a team player. I just know what time it is and when it’s my turn, I ain’t taking it for granted. I’m going to ball out every time.” Black is just a junior but his recruitment has been steadily catching fire since last year. He mentioned to Pittsburgh Sports Now following his Week One takeover that Maryland is currently the program sticking out the most to him but he also has offers from schools such as Cal, Colorado, Florida State, Indiana, Kentucky, West Virginia among many others. With more games like the one he had against nationally-ranked Bergen Catholic, and a full-time starting job likely available to him as a senior next season, more offers and interest will continue to roll in for Black. Sabrina Ionescu reaches new low never seen before in WNBA history
articles.summary: The New York Liberty have been mired in an inconsistent season despite already clinching a playoff berth, and part of it has been due to the up and down season from All-Star guard Sabrina Ionescu. The former Oregon star dealt with injury issues early this season, and she’s yet to find a consisten
articles._body: The New York Liberty have been mired in an inconsistent season despite already clinching a playoff berth, and part of it has been due to the up and down season from All-Star guard Sabrina Ionescu. The former Oregon star dealt with injury issues early this season , and she’s yet to find a consistent rhythm offensively with only a handful of games remaining before the playoffs. Amid the Liberty’s win against the Chicago Sky on Saturday, Sabrina Ionescu reached an unenviable mark in the WNBA record books, setting the worst percentage from the 3-point line in an eight game span with at least 50 attempts, as per Jack Maloney of CBS Sports. Against the Sky, Ionescu shot 0-of-3 from the 3-point line. In the past eight games, she is 8-of-53, or 15.1 percent. That surpasses the previous low mark set by Phoenix Mercury guard Kahleah Copper who went 9-of-51, 17.6 percent, earlier this season. Before that, the mark was held by Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark and Toronto Tempo guard Marina Mabrey who went 9-of-58 and 9-of-51, respectively, last season. Ionescu has always been one of the most dead-eye shooters in the game, going back to her college days with the Ducks. She held an average of 42.2 percent shooting from 3-point range across four seasons at Oregon, with only one year shooting under 40 percent. Since beginning her WNBA career, she’s connected on an average of 34.5 percent from distance in seven seasons. Her 3-point shooting percentages haven’t been as prolific as her college days, but following Sunday’s game, she’s shooting a career-worst 29.5 percent from deep. Her previous career-low was 29.9 percent which she shot last season. The post Sabrina Ionescu reaches new low never seen before in WNBA history appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Ken Rosenthal shares big Aaron Judge injury return timeline update
articles.summary: The New York Yankees have been waiting to get superstar Aaron Judge back in the lineup since the end of May after suffering a rib fracture after diving for a ball. As the Yankees get ready for the final month of the season, it appears that Judge is coming close to the end of his […]
articles._body: The New York Yankees have been waiting to get superstar Aaron Judge back in the lineup since the end of May after suffering a rib fracture after diving for a ball. As the Yankees get ready for the final month of the season, it appears that Judge is coming close to the end of his rehab and could return in the second week of September. Aaron Judge hasn't played since May 31. @Ken_Rosenthal has the latest on when we might see him back with the Yankees again: pic.twitter.com/jeHjs7aapE — FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) August 29, 2026 Fox MLB insider Ken Rosenthal indicated that Judge would accompany the Yankees when they go on a West Coast road trip to play the Los Angeles Angels and San Diego Padres. He will be working on baseball-related drills throughout the road trip. When the road trip ends and the Yankees return home to play the Colorado Rockies in a three-game series, Judge could possibly return to the lineup. Judge had said previously that when he feels ready to play again that he did not want to go on a rehab assignment — he just wanted to return to major league competition. However, as he gets closer to a return, he could decide to take a brief trip to the minor leagues before returning. While the Yankees have the second-best record in the American League at 76-59, their offense has struggled to put runs on the board without Judge in the middle of the lineup. The 3-time Most Valuable Player was slashing .248/.375/.533 with 17 home runs and 38 runs batted in at the time of the injury. Ben Rice has taken over as the Yankees leading slugger with 35 home runs and 83 RBI. Jazz Chisholm Jr. and Trent Grisham are far behind Rice with 18 home runs each. articles.title: Yankees’ Anthony Volpe minor league move hints at new role
articles.summary: New York Yankees infielder Anthony Volpe’s latest assignment with the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders could point toward the franchise exploring greater defensive versatility for the 25-year-old. On Saturday afternoon, Volpe was listed as the RailRiders’ starting third baseman and wa
articles._body: New York Yankees infielder Anthony Volpe’s latest assignment with the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders could point toward the franchise exploring greater defensive versatility for the 25-year-old. On Saturday afternoon, Volpe was listed as the RailRiders’ starting third baseman and was batting second against the Worcester Red Sox. The move stood out because shortstop has been his primary position throughout his professional career, while he has also spent time at second base since being optioned to Triple-A earlier this month. Saturday’s appearance was only the fourth time Volpe had played third base. His previous appearance at the position came with Single-A Tampa on June 3, 2021. Volpe also started at shortstop and hit leadoff for the RailRiders on Friday against Worcester. He went 1-for-4 with one RBI as Scranton/Wilkes-Barre secured a 2-0 win. The shift around the infield raises the possibility of Volpe developing into a utility option capable of handling shortstop, second base and third base. Before being optioned to Triple-A, Volpe was hitting .240 with 41 hits, one home run, 19 RBIs, 20 runs and seven stolen bases through 56 games. He has spent all four seasons of his career in the Yankees organization after being selected in the first round of the 2019 MLB Draft. The move comes with the Yankees sitting second in the American League East at 76-59 after 135 games. New York split Saturday’s doubleheader opener against Boston, losing 6-0 after winning Friday’s series opener 1-0. For now, Volpe’s move to third base provides another indication that the Yankees are testing his defensive flexibility as he continues working in Triple-A. articles.title: Lincoln Riley calls out 1 quarter after USC 42-26 win over San Jose State
articles.summary: USC football entered Saturday as the only top 15 team in action. Fans who basked in the near 90 degree heat inside Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum saw a dominating three quarters. But head coach Lincoln Riley called out one quarter that didn’t live up to USC’s standards against San Jose
articles._body: USC football entered Saturday as the only top 15 team in action. Fans who basked in the near 90 degree heat inside Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum saw a dominating three quarters. But head coach Lincoln Riley called out one quarter that didn’t live up to USC’s standards against San Jose State. The Trojans prevailed to a 42-26 romp to kickoff the season, winning without key wide receiver Tanook Hines . But again, Riley became blunt about the end. “First three quarters, a lot of really good football out there. Fourth quarter, not up to our standards,” Riley told reporters after the win. Yet that wasn’t Riley’s strongest take. He revealed who’s the most upset about that final quarter: Gary Patterson, who made his USC defensive coordinator debut after a lengthy run with TCU. “He’s pissed right now about the fourth quarter,” Riley added. Patterson turned heads early by playing two true freshman on that side of the ball. Five-star edge rusher Luke Wafle impressed early in nearly getting a sack for the safety. But ultimately forced an errant incomplete throw. Wafle even bulldozed past two different blockers to pressure quarterback Luke Weaver of the Spartans. Patterson also played four-star cornerback Elbert Hill IV in USC’s new-look five-man defensive back scheme. USC allowed 336 total yards against the Mountain West Conference foe. But 234 came through the air. And SJSU outscored USC with an astonishing 23-7 run. So USC’s head coach and defensive coordinator left unpleased by the final opening result. This despite showing the nation that it can be a dominating force for three quarters. Now USC faces an upset-minded Fresno State team on a short week, with that contest set for Sept. 4 inside the Coliseum. Courtney Williams on track for injury return amid Dream clash
articles.summary: Minnesota Lynx All-Star guard Courtney Williams missed her first game of the season this past week during the team’s win against the Washington Mystics, snapping her streak of 196 consecutive games played. That streak began during the 2022 season, and saw Williams play in every single game for th
articles._body: Minnesota Lynx All-Star guard Courtney Williams missed her first game of the season this past week during the team’s win against the Washington Mystics, snapping her streak of 196 consecutive games played . That streak began during the 2022 season, and saw Williams play in every single game for three straight years from 2023-2025. And now, she’s on track to make her return to the lineup. Courtney Williams was officially listed as probable on the Lynx’s injury report for the team’s upcoming game against the Atlanta Dream. The 11-year veteran sustained a foot injury during the team’s win against the Washington Mystics back on Aug. 21, and was ruled out amid their loss to the Golden State Valkyries this past Monday. Fifth-year guard Maya Caldwell started in place of the injured Williams in the loss to the Valkyries, finishing with nine points and two rebounds while shooting 3-of-5 from 3-point range in a little over 25 minutes of play. Williams’ return is a much welcome one for the Lynx as they square off against another playoff team in the Dream on Sunday. Atlanta features an All-Star guard/wing duo of their own in Allisha Gray and Rhyne Howard. The former USF star has appeared in 38 games for the Lynx this season at a little over 30 minutes per game. She’s been averaging 14.4 points, 5.1 rebounds, 4.3 assists and 1.1 steals with splits of 45.4 percent shooting from the field, 36.1 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 82 percent shooting from the free-throw line. Williams is in her third season with the Lynx, and re-signed on a two-year max contract this past offseason. articles.title: UVa dominates NC State in 34-8 rout to start 2026 season
articles.summary: The Wahoos rolled up 413 yards of total offense and stifled NC State on the way to a dominant 34-8 win over the Wolfpack.
articles._body: Entering its season opener with plenty of questions surrounding its new roster, Virginia left no doubt in a dominating 34-8 win over NC State in front of a sell-out crowd of 62,779 at Scott Stadium, the venue’s eighth largest ever, and its highest-ever student attendance. Missouri transfer Beau Pribula impressed in his UVa debut, finishing 9-for-11 (82%) passing for 155 yards and two touchdowns while also leading the Cavaliers in rushing with 110 yards on 15 attempts. All five of UVa’s available running backs also walked away with yardage, with Jekail Middlebrook gaining 64 yards on 15 attempts, and Xavier Brown , playing in his first game since going out with a season-ending injury against Washington State in October, rushed for 40 yards and a touchdown on eight attempts. He also led the Hoos in receiving yards with 58 and another score on two receptions. UVa’s offense started out modestly. Its opening drive ended in a punt after just four plays. But the Cavaliers got their first points on the board on the following drive, when Will Bettridge hit a 47-yard field goal, tying his career-high, to cap off a seven-play, 31 yard-drive. But the Hoos truly took hold of the momentum on the Pack’s ensuing possession. On just the second play from scrimmage, CJ Bailey’s pass was broken up by Fisher Camac before being intercepted by Michigan transfer Brandyn Hillman , setting the Cavaliers up at State’s 32. Pribula started, as he did each of the first four drives, with a keeper, rushing for 22 yards to put UVa in the red zone. Brown punched it in from one-yard out just three plays later. The Wolfpack got their first 1st down of the game on the following drive with 2:01 left in the first quarter, but stalled out shortly thereafter. The Cavaliers then drove to their 48 before Pribula, who had just one pass attempt up to that point, connected with Connor Cox for a 7-yard reception. He then threw a 45-yard touchdown pass to Brown for his second score of the day. NC State’s offense continued to struggle, but got a pair of good breaks after a 29-yard punt return from Victor Snow set the Pack up at the 50. A pass interference call on Hillman then put NC State at UVa’s 35. Yet just as Bailey had NC State in the red zone, Hillman forced a fumble out of him at the 7 at the end of a 12-yard rush. Landon Danley recovered it and the Pack’s best drive to that point ended with nothing. UVa’s defense, even without linebacker standout Kam Robinson , kept Bailey contained all game. He finished 12-for-23 (52%) passing for 84 yards and an interception while rushing for just 33 yards, which still led the Wolfpack on 10 attempts. The score remained 17-0 at halftime, but after not connecting with a single wideout in the first half, Pribula opened the drive with three straight completions to his receivers. The last of those was a 47-yard pitch and catch to Da’Shawn Martin for a touchdown, putting UVa up 24-0. NC State finally got on the board with a nine-play, 60-yard touchdown drive with just under five to go in the third. Backup quarterback Will Wilson got the score with a 1-yard keeper before Bailey connected with Deandre Desinor for the two-point conversion. UVa responded with one of its most impressive drives not just of the game but of all time: The 23-play, 75-yard touchdown drive that took 12:15 off the clock not only featured four 4th-down conversions but set school records for both time elapsed and plays. If there was any doubt about the outcome, that drive officially put the evening’s festivities to bed for good. All-in-all, UVa outgained NC State 413-168 in total net yards, 258-76 in rushing and 155-92 in passing. The Cavaliers added one last field goal late in the fourth, but both sides had their backups in by the end, and not only did UVa walk away with a statement win but also snapped a four-game losing streak against the Wolfpack.

articles.title: Jelani Thurman Announces His Arrival as Featured UNC Weapon
articles.summary: Ohio State transfer tight end Jelani Thurman led the Tar Heels in receiving on Saturday in his first game in Carolina blue.
articles._body: On the first play of North Carolina’s 2026 season, Billy Edwards Jr. faked a draw handoff to Benjamin Hall and looked to his right after taking a quick drop. There sat Jelani Thurman , the Ohio State transfer, rocking the No. 45, wide open in the flat.  In Bill Belichick ’s initial season at the helm, the passing attack was subpar. But from a production standpoint, the tight end position might have been worse. The longest play from a Carolina tight end in 2025 was a 19-yard reception by the Tar Heels’ top tight end Jake Johnson . Johnson finished with 149 yards last season. After lining up next to right tackle Shaq McRoy , Thurman faked a block and slipped towards the sideline. Edwards Jr. didn’t hesitate in finding Thurman on that opening down, and the redshirt junior erupted for a 20-yard catch-and-run in his first snap in Carolina blue. In other words, Thurman eclipsed the longest tight end reception in all of 2025 in the first play of this season. That was just the start, though. Thurman led UNC in receiving with 94 yards on four grabs in the season-opening win over TCU, dominating the target share along with Jordan Shipp , who were both thrown to eight times. And just as Thurman flashed on the opening drive, his 25-yard catch and run on the game-sealing drive sent North Carolina back to the states with a victory. “Jelani gave us some explosive plays, especially early in the game, to kind of get us started there,” Belichick said. “And then the pass and on the naked in the flat was a big first down there at the end on the last drive.” Thurman followed up his first grab with a 35-yard reception directly through the teeth of the defense just a minute later. This was no catch-and-run, as the 6-foot-6, 245-pounder flashed up the seam and Edwards Jr. placed the ball on the money to punch the Tar Heels into the redzone in three plays — with two of them going to Thurman. Carolina would settle for three points on that drive after a third-and-goal pass to Thurman fell incomplete. That wouldn’t be the first time UNC’s offense stalled in scoring position, which is one of the many things the Tar Heels will look to improve on moving forward. But regardless of the sloppiness of the Week 0 matchup, the resurgence of the tight end position in game one — albeit only through Thurman — reemphasized the main takeaway from the trip to Ireland: it’s going to be better than it was a year ago.  “The tight end position is just a great position overall,” Thurman said. “Carolina just brought me in and they showed everybody how the tight ends can work. This year, we’re just executing. The whole team is executing. The offense is executing. It should be a good year.” Thurman had seven catches for 84 yards last season as a Buckeye. He surpassed that total on North Carolina’s final drive of the game when Belichick, Edwards Jr. and offensive coordinator Bobby Petrino called his number again.  The Tar Heels, backed up in their own territory, led by five and faced a 2nd-and-12 just before the two minute warning. Instead of keeping the ball on the ground, once again, Edwards Jr. faked the handoff and found his tight end who was crossing into empty space behind the line of scrimmage. Thurman did the rest. “After getting the ball, it was really green grass,” Thurman said. “But I saw my two blockers out in front of me. I was really just trying to stay in bounds so we can keep the clock running and keep the game going.” That catch-and-run of 25 yards completely changed the calculus for Carolina. Near midfield, all UNC needed was one more first down to secure the underdog win, which they got when the Horned Frogs jumped offsides on fourth down. Aside from the all-important victory, the Tar Heels might’ve found another offensive star, too. Even though Thurman only caught four balls, he played 55 of the 58 offensive snaps for North Carolina and was the top target for Edwards Jr., who entered with a lot of question marks. More and more of those uncertainties will be answered for UNC’s quarterback — and entire offense — if Thurman keeps making plays like he did Saturday. “I’m truly grateful,” Thurman said. “Being able to come in here and fit the offense, be a key player in the offense, be a highlighted player in the offense, and be able to catch some balls from Billy. And to be coached by one of some of the best coaches in the game, I mean, I can’t complain. It’s good football. I’m ready to play.”

articles.title: Padres’ Luis Rengifo exits Rays game with knee sprain
articles.summary: The San Diego Padres suffered a tough 7-6 loss to the Tampa Bay Rays on Saturday. But the organization might be a bit more concerned about Luis Rengifo, as he was forced to exit the contest early with a knee injury. The Padres announced on social media that the 29-year-old infielder is dealing wi
articles._body: The San Diego Padres suffered a tough 7-6 loss to the Tampa Bay Rays on Saturday. But the organization might be a bit more concerned about Luis Rengifo, as he was forced to exit the contest early with a knee injury. The Padres announced on social media that the 29-year-old infielder is dealing with a knee sprain . After being carted off the field, Rengifo will fly back to San Diego for more testing on his injured knee. “Update from the Padres clubhouse: Luis Rengifo exited today’s game with a right knee sprain,” The Padres said. “He’s receiving treatment and will fly back to San Diego for further evaluation.” Rengifo left the contest with two at-bats, generating a walk and recording one of the club’s six runs. Manager Craig Stammen moved Jake Cronenworth from shortstop to second base, then subbed Xander Bogaerts to shortstop to replace Rengifo in the lineup on Saturday. For now, we’ll have to wait and see how serious the injury actually is. The Padres will likely provide an update for the eight-year veteran within the next couple of days. In the meantime, the team will focus on Sunday’s matchup against the Rays, which will be the final contest of a three-game series. Luis Rengifo only played 38 games for the Padres this season before sustaining the knee injury. Through 127 at-bats so far, the Venezuelan native has recorded 37 hits, four home runs, and 17 RBIs, giving him a .296 batting average and .376 OBP. He’s been much more productive in San Diego than he was in his 57 games with the Milwaukee Brewers earlier this year. Singapore has overhauled its baby bonus scheme. Will it work to boost birth rates this time?
articles.summary: Probably not.
articles._body: Singapore is overhauling its landmark baby bonus scheme, first introduced in 2001, as the city’s fertility rate and number of births fall to record lows.  In 2025, births in the Southeast Asian country fell below 30,000 for the first time in its post-independence history, while the fertility rate dropped to just 0.87 per woman, a record low. That’s a dangerous prospect for any country, but especially for Singapore, crammed into a space smaller than New York City. “The country does not have the natural resources to finance the costs of supporting an aged society, including both care and medical expenditures,” Tan Poh Lin, a senior research fellow at the National University of Singapore (NUS)’s Institute for Policy Studies explains. Immigration, in his view, won’t be enough to solve the problem: “Boosting the fertility rate is crucial to slow down the rate of change and allow society to adjust economically as well as institutionally.” At the country’s National Day Rally on Aug. 23, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong unveiled the “SG Child Support Package,” boasting measures like expanded childcare leave, strong financial support for parents, more affordable caregiving options, and extra chances to get subsidized housing. In total, the support is equal to almost 70,000 Singapore dollars ($55,000) by the time a child is 17. Demographic experts are cautiously optimistic about the new scheme, which appears to offer more sustained and holistic support for families.  “Singapore’s family policies had become increasingly complicated, with benefits varying by birth order and across different schemes ,” says Bussarawan Teerawichitchainan, a social demographer and sociologist from NUS. With the new package, “support is attached more clearly to each child and is provided over a longer period of childhood rather than being concentrated primarily around birth.” But previous policies to give parents more money, both in Singapore and elsewhere in Asia, haven’t been able to reverse falling birth rates. “Singapore has progressively expanded financial support for marriage and parenthood over many years, yet fertility has continued to decline,” Teerawichitchainan admits. “Concerns voiced by parents increasingly involve not just money but time, work-family pressures, childcare, housing and other demands associated with raising children.” Economic impact of low birth rates Persistently low birth rates could threaten a country’s ability to sustain its economy . “Smaller younger cohorts enter the workforce while the older population continues to grow…over time, that places greater pressure on labor supply and the tax base,” says Chua Yeow Hwee, an economist at Singapore’s Nanyang Technological University (NTU). “For businesses, an aging and shrinking workforce also makes labor constraints more acute.” Singapore has long turned to foreign workers to make up for a dwindling domestic workforce. As of 2025, Singapore is home to nearly 1.6 million foreign workers, making up 40% of the country’s total labor force, the highest in Asia outside of countries in the Middle East, according to the Migration Policy Institute, a U.S. think tank. The country is also placing its hopes on automation, with the government committing 1 billion Singapore dollars ($787 million) to public AI research from 2026 to 2030 .  “The relationship between demography and economic growth is complicated,” Teerawichitchainan explains. “Economies can adapt through productivity growth, technology, longer and healthier working lives, higher labor force participation and immigration.” The role of companies Singapore’s new scheme shifts from merely encouraging births to focus on family well-being over the long term, which might help change how potential parents think about children. “Cash gifts have a positive impact on births, but the effect tends to be short-lived as many beneficiaries do not increase their final family size,” Tan of NUS explains. “Tangible change can only be achieved by adjusting parenting expectations, including the notion that parenthood involves sacrificing personal wellbeing.” Some of the responsibility for changing these expectations lies with companies. “There is a limit to what government policy can do directly, and employers have an important role,” Chua says. “A generous leave entitlement has less value if employees believe that using it will make them appear less committed or affect their advancement.” (Singaporeans get 16 weeks of paid maternity leave and four weeks of paternity leave, as well as 10 weeks of parental leave, shared between both parents, that must be used within a year of birth). But there may be little anyone–government or corporate–can do to persuade people to have children amid greater economic uncertainty.  “These days, folks will have children only if they are confident that they could ease their children’s journey ahead and help them access a good life in the future,” says Tan Ern Ser, an adjunct principal research fellow at Singapore’s Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy. “Unfortunately, the world we live in today does not leave much room for optimism, notwithstanding the government’s relentless efforts.” Singapore’s government, too, acknowledges that there are limits to its ability to influence its populace to have kids. “The decision to have children is a deeply personal one. Policies alone cannot make this happen,” Wong, Singapore’s Prime Minister, said during his speech. “But what we can do is make it easier for Singaporeans who want children to start and raise a family.” Ultimately, Singapore may just need to accept that it’ll have to live with fewer people. “The economic challenge is not simply to restore some particular fertility level,” Teerawichitchainan concludes. “It is also to build institutions, labor markets, and technologies that allow Singapore to prosper under a demographic reality that may remain one of low fertility and population aging.” This story was originall

articles.title: New study ranks most vulgar college football fanbases (and Louisville is near the top)
articles.summary: Covers.com ranked every college football fanbase by Vulgarity Score. Louisville was at the top while Kentucky was at the bottom.
articles._body: A new study ranked the most vulgar college football fanbases in the country. Kentucky graded out quite low, but Louisville came in near the very top. Andy Whiteoak of Covers.com dropped a study this week identifying which fanbases are the meanest, most negative, and angriest in the entire sport. His analysis tracked thousands of online posts to create a Vulgarity Score for every single college football team in the FBS. How is this all tracked? Whiteoak and his team “evaluated thousands of college football posts on Reddit across every FBS college football program.” They primarily used four factors to build the scores: Frequency of profanity per 10,000 words Average number of swear words per comment Density of angry and vulgar emojis Overall negative sentiment of the fan text Vulgarity Scores were ranked on a scale of 1-10. Louisville checked in at No. 3 in the entire country with a score of 9.79, trailing only a couple of SEC schools: No. 1 Mississippi State (10.00) and No. 2 Arkansas (9.97). See for yourself. Vulgarity Score | Covers.com Louisville is the only ACC school that ranked among the top 10. Meanwhile, the least vulgar college football fanbases featured four other ACC schools in the bottom 10: Clemson (2.00), Syracuse (2.35), NC State (2.74), and Boston College (2.82). Sacramento State fans are apparently the nicest in the country, coming in at the bottom with a score of 1.00. As for the SEC schools, Kentucky checked in all the way down at 15th (4.54), ahead of only the Ole Miss Rebels (3.96). UK, Ole Miss, and Texas (4.83) were the lone schools that ranked below the national average. Every other SEC school would be considered vulgar by this study. Below is how the entire SEC graded out. SEC Vulgarity Score | Covers.com So what does this all mean? Probably nothing. But if you’ve been on the Internet as a Kentucky fan before, you’ve probably run into an unfriendly Louisville fan along the way — so the study makes sense. Let’s just be grateful this study only covered college football and not men’s college basketball…

articles.title: KATSEYE Makes Brief Daisy Chain Fields Festival Appearance After Canceling Performance
articles.summary: Three members of KATSEYE appeared on stage on Saturday (Aug. 29) even though Megan's injury forced the group to exit the fest's official lineup.
articles._body: KATSEYE made it to Olivia Rodrigo ‘s Daisy Chain Fields festival after all, though their appearance was short. Related Megan Speaks Out After Sprained Ankle Prompts KATSEYE Daisy Chain Fields Fest Cancellation: ‘Sending All My Love to Olivia’ Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields Festival Raises $10 Million for Women’s Charities How Did KATSEYE’s ‘WILD’ Manage Such a Record-Setting First Week for the Group? Three of the group’s current active members — Yoonchae, Lara and Megan, who sustained an ankle injury during rehearsal that led to KATSEYE pulling out of performing this weekend — unexpectedly showed up on stage Saturday (Aug. 29) just before Devon Again, the act booked to fill in for what would’ve been KATSEYE’s time slot. The trio said they were honored to introduce nonprofit Baby2Baby, an organization that provides children in poverty with diapers, clothing and other necessities, ahead of Devon Again’s performance. Addressing their last-minute exit from the lineup, Megan expressed, “We’re so disappointed that we can’t perform today on stage, but my ankle is on hiatus.” “But our hearts are definitely not,” she added. “We’re sending all of our love to Olivia and this beautiful community that she built at Daisy Chain Fields. We’re so happy to be here and show as much support as we can. We love you, Olivia. Thank you for letting us be a small part of this.” (Check out a video clip that was captured of the moment here .) KATSEYE announced on Thursday that Megan had sprained her ankle, and that they’d no longer be performing at Rodrigo’s inaugural charity festival. “My doctors have advised me to stay off it and let it heal so I can be ready for tour,” Megan said on Friday. KATSEYE’s scheduled appearance at the Irvine, Calif., music festival curated by Rodrigo came just after the group earned its first No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with the EP WILD . KATSEYE’s active lineup presently consists of Yoonchae, Lara, Megan and Daniela, who wasn’t seen on stage Saturday. Fellow members Manon and Sophia are on hiatus, with Manon focusing on her wellness and Sophia focusing on her mental health. On Friday, Rodrigo announced that ticket sales for Saturday’s day-long music event had brought in $10 million that will go directly to 10 nonprofit organizations supporting women: Planned Parenthood, Center for Reproductive Rights, Baby2Baby, Black Mamas Matter Alliance, FreeFrom, Jhpiego, Johns Hopkins Center for Indigenous Health, National Domestic Workers Alliance, National Institute for Reproductive Health and National Women’s Law Center.

articles.summary: The Washington Commanders invested a good chunk of change in their defense, which seems quite rational given the injury and age-related questions surrounding the offense. They intend to be a more well-rounded football team than the one that gave up an NFL-worst 384.0 yards per game last season. B
articles._body: The Washington Commanders invested a good chunk of change in their defense, which seems quite rational given the injury and age-related questions surrounding the offense . They intend to be a more well-rounded football team than the one that gave up an NFL-worst 384.0 yards per game last season. Boogie Basham will not get the chance to help them complete that objective. Management is releasing the 28-year-old outside linebacker, per Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network. Basham, a 2021 second-round draft pick who began his career with the Buffalo Bills, did not get much time to impress the Dan Quinn-led coaching staff. He was only on the Commanders for a few days before the organization made its decision. Basham logged 36 snaps for the squad in Friday’s 41-3 preseason loss versus the Baltimore Ravens, per Pro Football Focus. He posted two stops and two missed tackles, a mixed outing that apparently did little to persuade Washington. The former Wake Forest playmaker now finds himself at a crossroads. He spent two seasons each with Buffalo and the New York Giants and played three games for the Carolina Panthers in 2025. He owns four and a half sacks, 61 combined tackles, one interception and one fumble recovery in 43 NFL games. What does the future have in store for him? Although Boogie Basham has not had the career that he hoped for after landing in Orchard Park, he undoubtedly lays claim to one of the coolest names around. Obviously, the Virginia native would love to see it plastered on another roster sheet. Stay tuned. The post Commanders release ex-Bills 2nd round defender appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Edgardo Henriquez makes jaw-dropping Dodgers history vs. Tigers
articles.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers reliever Edgardo Henriquez reached a historic milestone in a 2-1 loss against the Detroit Tigers on Saturday. To open the bottom of the eighth, Henriquez unleashed a 103.6 mph front-door sinker that nicked the outside corner and froze Detroit Tigers hitter Dillon Dingler for t
articles._body: Los Angeles Dodgers reliever Edgardo Henriquez reached a historic milestone in a 2-1 loss against the Detroit Tigers on Saturday. To open the bottom of the eighth, Henriquez unleashed a 103.6 mph front-door sinker that nicked the outside corner and froze Detroit Tigers hitter Dillon Dingler for the first out. The 103.6 mph throw officially was the fastest strikeout pitch by a Dodger in the Statcast Era, according to tracking metrics dating back to 2008. That tied Henriquez’s own previous organizational velocity record of 103.6 mph, which he initially set earlier in the 2026 season on June 2 against the Arizona Diamondbacks. Entering the game, the 24-year-old right-handed pitcher already held 22 of the fastest pitches ever recorded by a Dodgers player under Statcast tracking. Furthermore, he commands 14 of the top 16 spots specifically for fastest strikeout pitches in franchise history. In 55 appearances this season, Henriquez has logged 55.1 innings and gone 4-1 with a 2.77 ERA. He has struck out 63 batters, posted a 0.98 WHIP and limited opposing hitters to a .164 batting average. Henriquez relies heavily on a hard-throwing repertoire, averaging 100.6 mph on his primary fastballs. His 2026 pitch utilization includes a four-seam fastball (33.1%), a sinker (25.5%), a slider (22.4%), a cutter (14.3%), and a curveball (4.8%). This pitch combination has generated a 25.1% strikeout rate and limited opposing lineups to a 2.4% barrel percentage and a 26.2% hard-hit percentage. Through 80 career regular-season appearances since his MLB debut on September 24, 2024, Henriquez holds a 6-2 record, a 2.67 ERA, and 86 strikeouts over 77.2 total innings pitched. articles.title: Jimmie Johnson’s final NASCAR Cup Series car scheme has been revealed, and it’s perfect
articles.summary: Jimmie Johnson revealed the No. 48 he’ll drive in his final NASCAR Cup Series race, complete with a fitting nod to longtime partner Lowe’s.
articles._body: Jimmie Johnson’s final Cup Series race will be the 2027 Daytona 500. For the race, he will use his iconic number 48 that he won 7 NASCAR Cup Series Championships with on the side of his car. On Saturday night in Daytona, he revealed the paint scheme for it. Lowe’s officially entered the chat earlier this month.  A week after Jimmie Johnson said that adding Lowe’s as a sponsor to his final NASCAR Cup Series car would be highly unlikely, things may be changing. Tonight, on the track where the final race will happen,  Johnson unveiled the car , which does in fact include Lowe’s, the perfect addition for his No. 48 car for the night.  An iconic final ride. pic.twitter.com/HnBBH94hMB — LEGACY MOTOR CLUB (@LEGACYMotorClub) August 29, 2026 The car on track: pic.twitter.com/7fQVDd0jcm — Jeff Gluck (@jeff_gluck) August 29, 2026 How we got here Rick Hendrick announced on the TNT Sports pre-race set before the Brickyard 400 that it had been approved by NASCAR for Jimmie Johnson to drive his final Cup Series race with the iconic No. 48.  The first question fans had was whether it would be Lowe’s as the sponsor of Jimmie Johnson’s car when unloaded off the trailer at the 2027 Daytona 500.  Johnson, who won 7 NASCAR Cup Series Championships in the 48, appeared on SiriusXM NASCAR Radio this week .  He talked about Rick Hendrick getting this done and the chances that Lowe’s would be on board for his final drive in the Cup Series.  The origin of the 48 idea Johnson said he proposed the idea to Hendrick, and immediately, Mr. H. was on board with the idea.  There were hurdles, however.  All parties wanted Alex Bowman on board.  There was also the issue of the primary car sponsor of Bowman’s car, Ally.   And of course, there was NASCAR itself needing to approve it.   “It was an idea that I had, and I knew that it was far-fetched, and it’d be complicated and many layers to it, but I gave Rick a call and proposed the idea,” said Johnson. “And he’s like, ‘Yeah, I love it. Let me get to work.’  “And so with NASCAR and Ally, Alex and all the other important layers, we were able to get that part done and thrilled to have announced it. “We have some other layers to come as the race grows closer and we can put more of this together, but just so excited to know that I’ll be back in that 48 car one last time.” ‘Only one man that could pull that off’ Not many could have done, according to Johnson.  In fact, it was only Rick Hendrick that had the pull to convince all parties to make this a reality for his former star driver.  “And, you know, it also speaks to the relationships he has far and wide to be able to pull this off with different manufacturers, obviously title sponsors, you know, we had a conversation with NASCAR and, you know, the variety of layers that are there, there’s only one man that could pull that off, and it’s him.”

articles._body: NC State coach Dave Doeren walked into a cramped postgame press conference room inside Virginia’s Scott Stadium and moved the chair that both senior linebacker Popo Aguirre and junior quarterback CJ Bailey occupied in the minutes before him. It was soaked with sweat, and he chose to sit in the dry one. But before Doeren started his opening statement, he made a dejected off-handed comment: “That’s probably what I deserve, though.” Why? Well, the 14th-year coach was ready to shoulder the blame for how his team played in a 34-8 loss at Virginia on Saturday afternoon.

articles.summary: The New York Giants made several cuts on Saturday, as the coaching staff must bring the roster size down to 53 players before the start of the new season. However, one notable release was wideout Isaiah Hodgins, as the club is going in a different direction with the wide receiver room. Hodgins wa
articles._body: The New York Giants made several cuts on Saturday, as the coaching staff must bring the roster size down to 53 players before the start of the new season. However, one notable release was wideout Isaiah Hodgins , as the club is going in a different direction with the wide receiver room. Hodgins was cut alongside seven other players , according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. After over three years with the Giants, Hodgins’ time in New York has ended. “Giants released: CB Ugo Amadi, RB Damon Bankston, TE Josiah Deguara, DL Leki Fotu, WR Isaiah Hodgins, OL Brenden Jaimes, LB Anfernee Orji, [and] WR Kobe Prentice,” Schefter reported. Hodgins first entered the league as a sixth-round pick in the 2020 NFL Draft with the Buffalo Bills. He didn’t make his NFL debut, however, until the 2021-22 campaign, appearing in just one game with the Bills. He eventually joined the Giants in the middle of the 2022-23 season, where he remained until being cut on Saturday. In his 35 total games in New York, Isaiah Hodgins hauled in 66 receptions for 708 yards, and eight touchdowns. He mainly served as a rotational option in the Giants’ wide receiver room . With Hodgins out of the picture, head coach John Harbaugh is seemingly narrowing down his roster. Malik Nabers, Darius Slayton, and Darnell Mooney are expected to work as the top three wide receivers. Odell Beckham Jr. is in the mix for a final spot on the roster, and rookie Malachi Fields is expected to have some kind of role with the club, too. articles.summary: The Houston Texans have a potentially historic defense and a talented yet inconsistent quarterback who is coming off an abysmal playoff performance. That combination is producing heaps of scrutiny. After seeing CJ Stroud throw four interceptions in an AFC Divisional Round loss to the New England
articles._body: The Houston Texans have a potentially historic defense and a talented yet inconsistent quarterback who is coming off an abysmal playoff performance. That combination is producing heaps of scrutiny. After seeing CJ Stroud throw four interceptions in an AFC Divisional Round loss to the New England Patriots in January, fans will be quick to call for a replacement if he struggles again this season. Brett Rypien will not be one of the names they potentially shout, however. Houston is releasing the veteran QB , according to Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports. The Texans picked up the former Boise State star after Graham Mertz suffered a torn ACL in the team’s preseason opener versus the Los Angeles Chargers, but he had little chance of jumping backup Davis Mills on the depth chart. Rypien completed 19-of-33 passes for 145 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions across the last two preseason matchups. Unfortunately, the 30-year-old is on the move once again. He has played for the Denver Broncos, Los Angeles Rams and Cincinnati Bengals in parts of five NFL seasons, while also spending brief stints with the Seattle Seahawks, New York Jets, Chicago Bears, Minnesota Vikings and Indianapolis Colts. The 2018 Mountain West Offensive Player of the Year has four career starts under his belt. Stroud and Mills are currently the only signal-callers on the Texans’ roster. Perhaps the front office will scoop up another one to keep on the practice squad in case of emergency. Regardless of who occupies the QB room, an unrelenting defense will continue to serve as the identity of this franchise. articles._body: FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla.- After several weather delays and horns going off left and right, No. 3 nationally ranked Las Vegas (Nev.) Bishop Gorman and Miami (Fla.) Columbus were finally able to take to the field at Saturday afternoon’s Broward County Classic High School Football Showcase at St. Thomas Aquinas. One team was able to take advantage of the multiple layoffs. [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] Columbus shrugged off the delays and was able to come away with a 33-28 victory over Bishop Gorman at Brian Piccolo Memorial Stadium. It was a standout performance for Miami 5-star athlete commit A’mir Sears , who scored twice and intercepted three passes on defense for the Explorers. The Gaels, which was coming off an 38-28 win over St. John Bosco (Calif.) last week, entered the game as the country’s third ranked team, according to the latest Rivals National 2026 High School Football Composite Rankings. It was the Explorers that came out of the gates hot as they scored on a Kai Moore (Northern Illinois commit) to running back Cecil Smith on a 47-yard touchdown to take a 7-0 lead. After a Sears interception, the future Hurricane hauled in a 28-yard touchdown pass from Moore to put the Explorers ahead 14-0. Columbus would end up taking a 20-0 lead on an 11-yard strike from Moore to Sears with less than six minutes before halftime. Bishop Gorman would finally answer with a couple touchdowns of their own as 2028 4-star quarterback Ace Amina connected with tight end Trent Walker and freshman wide receiver Michael Blackmond to put the Gaels within 23-15 at intermission. Moore wasn’t finished with his day as he hit on Tony Brown III on a 29-yard touchdown pass to go ahead at 30-15. Columbus got the ball back after a Bishop Gorman fumble and added a field goal to take a 33-15 lead with 7:58 left. Bishop Gorman (1-1) scored two touchdowns in the final few minutes in a comeback attempt, recovering one of two onside kick tries, but couldn’t get one more shot offensively in the final minutes. With an enrollment of about 1500 students, Bishop Gorman is the oldest Catholic High School in Southern Nevada. Bishop Gorman is the home of the Gaels and has a rich tradition of athletic excellence with over 100 State Championships in our 65+ year history. The Class of 2023 also had 47 seniors receiving athletic scholarships to play at the college level.” More about Columbus High School “Columbus High School, located in Miami, Florida, is recognized for its strong commitment to academic excellence, community service, and athletic achievement. Serving a diverse and vibrant student population, Columbus High School offers a comprehensive educational experience that prepares students for college, careers, and leadership roles in society.”
