articles.title: Two thoughts on Alabama State’s win over Marshall Faulk, Southern
articles.summary: Alabama State pulled off a comeback victory over Marshall Faulk and the Southern University Jaguars in the Birmingham Football Classic on Saturday afternoon to kick off the football season. Southern University looked impressive in Faulk’s first game as head coach, pulling out a 14-3 lead ea
articles._body: Alabama State pulled off a comeback victory over Marshall Faulk and the Southern University Jaguars in the Birmingham Football Classic on Saturday afternoon to kick off the football season. Southern University looked impressive in Faulk’s first game as head coach, pulling out a 14-3 lead early in the second quarter, but Alabama State quickly fought to regain control of the game and ultimately prevailed. Here are two thoughts on the game regarding both Alabama State and Southern University. Southern looked better than expected Southern University looks way better than I thought they would. At the beginning of the year, coming out of Media Day, I was concerned that Faulk’s start to his tenure with Southern would be strenuous. Given the fact that Marshall Faulk seemingly hadn’t settled on a starting quarterback, as well as how vague he was in media availabilities, it seemed like Southern was going to be a team in disarray. It looked like a team with a first-year head coach in a new system, one that might be a little better than the Terrence Graves era but still bound to have its struggles. Instead, they came out of the gate swinging, with Christian Johnson as the starting quarterback. Johnson transferred to Southern University from Hutchinson Community College, where he was part of the 2024 NJCAA Division I national championship team. He put up impressive numbers at Hutchinson, throwing for 3,103 passing yards and rushing for 907 yards, with 42 total touchdowns across his two seasons there. His resume heading into the game made it clear he earned the nod. Johnson proved to be a solid QB1 for Southern, helping them secure a 14-3 lead early in the game. He showed his ability to run the ball and his ability as a passer, and I think that dual-threat ability is going to be essential for the up-tempo offense Marshall Faulk is looking to build. We saw other names step up in the offense outside of Trey Holly, such as Daejawn Smith. Holly didn’t put up the eye-popping numbers he normally does, but he was still a productive part of the offense, both on the ground and through the air, getting the majority of the snaps at running back. Southern is going to be way better than I thought they would be, and it’s going to be interesting to see how they measure up in the SWAC under Marshall Faulk, especially with some tough matchups still on their schedule. Alabama State started off rough but stuck the landing Alabama State’s offense returns several key contributors, such as Andrew Body and Jamarie Hoytzclaw To start the game, it looked like the offense wasn’t firing on all cylinders. Eddie Robinson Jr. and his coaching staff appeared to be really conservative in how he was running the offense, and it wasn’t as free-flowing as we saw a year ago. I believe that allowed Southern to stake out an early advantage. But we saw the lights flicker on for Alabama State’s offense once Southern went up 14-3, as they immediately answered with a touchdown, and we saw Andrew Body featured more in the attack. The two-headed monster of Body and Hostzclaw in the backfield is going to be pivotal. Hostzclaw is one of the better running backs in the SWAC and has proven his ability to make plays, so much so that in certain stretches Southern simply wasn’t able to contain him. And Andrew Body is still electric in the run game, even breaking off an 18-yard run early in the contest. The threat of Hostzclaw breaking off a big run, combined with Andrew Body keeping the ball and navigating his way down the field, is a real problem for opposing defenses, and it validates their ranking as the projected top team in the SWAC East out of SWAC Media Day. But as the season goes on, I want to see a little more consistency from their offensive unit. And I believe we will, because this is week zero, and it appears that programs around the HBCU nation are still trying to figure out both their rosters and their winning formula. The Alabama State we saw today is not the Alabama State we’ll see play Jackson State and Prairie View A&M in back-to-back weeks leading into Thanksgiving weekend. I still believe they’re championship contenders, but there are certainly some things they’ll need to work on. articles.title: Eli Drinkwitz on SEC, player eligibility saga: ‘For us to be operating like this is a complete clown show’
articles.summary: It was reported Saturday morning that the SEC and commissioner Greg Sankey plan on complying with all new applicable court orders (including the ones in Louisiana), which will allow schools to roster former NFL players despite the original threat of punishment. Originally, the SE
articles._body: It was reported Saturday morning that the SEC and commissioner  Greg Sankey  plan on complying with all new applicable court orders (including the ones in Louisiana), which will allow schools to roster former NFL players despite the original threat of punishment. Originally, the SEC  revealed rules and punishments  for schools that violated their new professional sports rule. This was meant to prevent NFL rostered players from returning to the conference, but that no longer seems to be the case. Ahead of his Missouri ‘s season opener next week, head coach Eli Drinkwitz commented on the chaos surrounding college football and the SEC. Essentially, he revealed he plans on doing whatever he needs to do to ‘help the University of Missouri win.’ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage “This is the second-biggest sport in the United States, most-watched sport in the United States, and for us to be operating like this is a complete clown show. And it’s disappointing,” Drinkwitz said, via Missouri reporter Killian Wright . “Coaches have been on the forefront of saying this, and it’s been ignored. It’s been ignored. “And you know I would say now the, this is what they get. That’s what they’ve got. So, you know administrators and courtrooms have got to figure out what the rules are now. And we’ve been saying this for years and years and years. “So, you know, I’m going to focus on my team. If I’m told that I can add players, then then I’ll look to add players. I’m going to do whatever I’m supposed to do to help the University of Missouri win. That’s my job. That’s what the president, the board, and the fans expect out of me.” Eli Drinkwitz calls out NCAA, SEC for not passing a bill to prevent eligibility chaos Violating the new SEC-pro sports rule was set to result in a coach suspension of 50% of contests and a hefty fine. The fine would have amounted for 50% of that sport’s annual operating budget, and the head coach’s suspension would include all coaching, recruiting and administrative duties. The punishment was similar to the one the NCAA has in place for ‘ghost transfers’. Those are players who leave one school for another without entering the transfer portal. “Whatever the rules are, we’ll try to play by those rules,” Drinkwitz continued. “It would just be nice if those rules weren’t adjusted by tweet on social media or by courtrooms or lawyers. But that’s our fault because we didn’t pass a bill to get it done.” Amid the chaos around the sport and conference, Drinkwitz heads into his seventh season at Missouri. In his previous six seasons, Drink has led the Tigers to a 46-29 (26-24) record and two top-25 finishes (No. 8 in 2023 and No. 22 in 2024).

articles._body: MicahJo Barnett, a college football running back from William Jewell College, which is located in Liberty, Missouri, died during the team’s season opener on Saturday, the school announced. First responders were called to the field to treat Barnett at 12:20 p.m. local time. The paramedics attended to Barnett for a few minutes before taking him to a local hospital, where he was pronounced dead. “William Jewell College and the Liberty, Missouri community mourn the passing of Micah Jo Barnett, a junior business administration and member of Jewell Cardinal football program and former Liberty North Eagle,” William Jewel said in a statement . “Our thoughts and prayers are with Micah Jo’s family, our students, the Cardinal Football family, and the rest of our community during this time of loss.” Forever a Cardinal William Jewell & the Liberty community mourn the passing of junior MicahJo Barnett. Our thoughts & prayers are with MicahJo’s family, teammates, friends, & coaches. A vigil will be held tonight on the Jewell quad at 8 p.m. in honor of MicahJo & family. pic.twitter.com/SXAXSGcdD4 — William Jewell Athletics (@JewellCardinals) August 29, 2026 William Jewell, a Division II program, also announced a vigil will be held on campus Saturday at 8 p.m. At the time of the incident, the team was facing Fort Lewis College, and the game was suspended before being canceled. William Jewell president reacts to MichaJo Barnett’s death “We appreciate the response that we’ve received from the sheriff’s office, the police department, the EMS department, the physician for the team,” William Jewell president Dr. Dave Van Horn said during a press conference via Harold R. Kuntz of FOX 4 . “Everybody responded so quickly, so well. We want to thank them along with the Liberty Hospital System for being there with us. “Our partners have been reaching out to us and have given us great support during this time. …Our hearts are heavy, and we just appreciate all the support that we have received from the greater community.” In 2025, MicahJo Barnett started five games before suffering a season-ending injury. In those five games, Barnett recorded 366 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 71 carries. During his freshman season in 2024, Barnett played in eight games and tallied 91 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 37 attempts. Barnett was from Liberty, Missouri, and played high school football at Liberty North High School. During his senior season, Barnett led the team to a state championship and was named to the All-State team after posting 1,450 all-purpose yards and 20 touchdowns.

In addition to Martin, the Sparks also cut third-year forward Alissa Pili who had been on one of the WNBA’s new development contracts. To replace Kate Martin on the active roster, the Sparks were awarded second-year forward Aaliyah Nye off waivers. Nye had played for the Atlanta Dream this season, but was waived by the team to make room for veteran DeWanna Bonner. Prior to the multiple cuts, the Sparks started off the weekend by signing rookie guard Ndjakalanga Mwenentanda to a development contract . The team had one development spot open after converting rookie guard Tonie Morgan to standard deal. Now with Pili being cut, the Sparks are back to having one developmental contract spot open. When it comes to standard contracts, however, the waiving of Martin and acquisition of Nye brings the team to a full 12. Martin had begun the 2026 season on a development contract with the Sparks after being cut by the Golden State Valkyries. She eventually had her deal converted to standard, but she was on the outs of the main rotation for most of the year. In total, Martin appeared in 17 games with the Sparks at a little over seven minutes per game. She was averaging 2.3 points and 1.1 rebounds with splits of 37.1 percent shooting from the field, 30.8 percent shooting from 3-point range and 62.5 percent shooting from the free-throw line. The No. 18 overall pick in the 2024 WNBA Draft, Martin began her career with the Las Vegas Aces before being claimed by the Valkyries in the 2025 expansion draft. As far as the Sparks newest active roster player, Nye was selected by the Aces as well with the No. 13 overall pick in the 2025 WNBA Draft. She played her rookie year with the Aces before also being claimed via expansion draft by the Toronto Tempo this year. The former Alabama standout had found her way to the Dream after being cut by the Tempo before the start of the year. She had appeared in 19 games at only a little over two minutes per game while shooting 33.3 percent from the 3-point line and 100 percent from the free-throw line. Her season high in scoring was six point back on Aug. 13 during the Dream’s win against the Connecticut Sun. The Sparks have already been mathematically eliminated from playoff contention , and head coach Lynne Roberts acknowledged that young player development is a primary focus during the final stretch of the year. articles.title: What to know about Kentucky’s preseason opponent, the UCF Knights
articles.summary: Kentucky will close out the preseason schedule against UCF on Oct. 28. Here's what you need to know about the Knights.
articles._body: Kentucky men’s basketball’s 2026-27 schedule has been finalized with the addition of the third and final preseason game. The Wildcats will take on the Central Florida Knights on Wednesday, Oct. 28, inside Rupp Arena. It’ll be the final exhibition before UK’s season-opener the following week against Manhattan. Similar to last season, head coach Mark Pope is taking advantage of the preseason. He’s now allowed three exhibitions, which he filled with UCF and Texas Tech as high-major opponents. Travis Ford’s Little Rock program rounds out the three preseason games for a nostalgic touch. Texas Tech will likely begin the season as a top 25 team in the nation, but just how good is fellow Big 12 program UCF? That’s what we’re here to figure out. Let’s get to know more about UCF before the Knights come to Lexington this fall. What to know about UCF Former Duke standout Johnny Dawkins is entering his 11th season as head coach at UCF. He was previously at Stanford for eight seasons (2008-16) before making the move to the Sunshine State. With the Knights, Dawkins has posted an overall record of 189-132. He’s helped the program win at least 20 games four times and has made the NCAA Tournament twice, including last season as a 10-seed (former UK forward Jordan Burks was on that roster). Since UCF joined the Big 12 three seasons ago, Dawkins has gone 58-45. Entering the 2026-27 season, Dawkins saw plenty of roster turnover from last season’s NCAA Tournament team. Burks is gone, as is most of the team’s best scorers, including the top four. Only five players return from last season: Carmelo Pacheco (4.6 PPG), John Bol (5.9 PPG), Elijah Hulsewe (1.1 PPG), Arturo Dean , and Tanner Jones . Dean and Jones did not play, but Dean is expected to see a major role after sitting out due to NCAA rules. UCF brought in a trio of high school recruits, two of them considered three-star talents. But the real moves came in the transfer portal. Dawkins added seven new players in the offseason: Isaiah Malone (FCGU), Cayden Vasko (Wofford), Lewis Walker (North Carolina A&T), Mister Dean (Charleston), Churchill Abass (New Orleans), Jason Asemota (Boston College), and most notably, Dior Johnson (Tarleton State). Johnson, who played for UCF during the 2024-25 season, was an All-WAC Second Team member last season at Tarleton State while averaging 24 points per outing. He’s likely to be a starter in the backcourt alongside Arturo Dean. Walker comes to the Big 12 after averaging 18.9 points per game at NC A&T, while Malone led the A-Sun in blocks per game last season (1.9) as a 6-foot-8 forward. The 7-foot-2 Bol will likely round out the starting five after a productive 2025-26 season in limited minutes. Unlike Texas Tech, UCF is not projected to finish near the top of the Big 12. Johnson and Walker are going to be asked to score a ton. Bol needs to prove he can upgrade his production. There is hope the Knights can be an impactful defensive unit, but scoring could be tough to come by if one of Johnson and Walker has an off night. Regardless, this will still be a quality Power 4 test for Kentucky as the Wildcats prepare for the regular season. Kentucky’s history with the Knights The history between these two programs is nearly non-existent. In fact, Kentucky and UCF have only faced each other once — 20 years ago. Per BigBlueHistory.net , an unranked UCF team almost came out on top in that game back in January 2006, losing 59-57 inside Rupp Arena against Tubby Smith ‘s Wildcats. Ramel Bradley dropped 16 points while Rajon Rondo added 13 points and six assists. UK nearly coughed up an 11-point lead down the stretch in front of the Big Blue Nation, but Rondo came up clutch, hitting the go-ahead game-winner in the lane with 1.5 seconds left to gift Kentucky a tight victory.

articles._body: It’s cut weekend in the NFL, as each team must bring the roster down to 53 players. The New York Jets made a final decision on one player who was part of the deal that sent Quinnen Williams to the Dallas Cowboys . Reports indicate that former first-round pick Mazi Smith is being released by the Jets, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. After initially playing as the backup defensive tackle, the organization decided to go in a different direction before the start of the new season. “Jets are releasing defensive tackle Mazi Smith, who was included in last season’s trade with Dallas for Quinnen Williams,” Schefter reported. The deal that sent Smith to New York was a mid-season move last year. He appeared in eight total games last season, three of which were with the Jets . Mazi Smith finished the 2025-26 campaign with just three combined tackles, as it was a notable drop-off from his first two years in the league. Smith was initially viewed as the replacement defensive tackle in New York once the club dealt Quinnen Williams away. Instead, the 25-year-old interior defensive lineman became a cut candidate after just three years in the NFL. He should have a chance to sign elsewhere, or even sign back with the Jets to join the practice squad. Considering his youth and the fact that he was drafted in the first round of the 2023 NFL Draft, Smith could land on his feet somewhere. With Mazi Smith out of the picture, Harrison Phillips will likely serve as the club’s starting defensive tackle. Meanwhile, T’Vondre Sweat will play the nose tackle position. Rookie Darrell Jackson Jr. has an opportunity to serve as an immediate backup for both positions. articles.summary: The New York Mets acquired Luis Robert Jr. this past offseason in hopes that he would give the lineup a boost. Instead, injuries and underperformance have defined Robert’s 2026 season with the Mets. On Saturday, Anthony DiComo of MLB.com reported that the ball club is placing Robert on waiv
articles._body: The New York Mets acquired Luis Robert Jr. this past offseason in hopes that he would give the lineup a boost. Instead, injuries and underperformance have defined Robert’s 2026 season with the Mets. On Saturday, Anthony DiComo of MLB.com reported that the ball club is placing Robert on waivers, meaning teams can claim him. Teams will have 48 hours to claim Robert once the Mets officially make the waiver move. He is a former All-Star so teams in need of offensive and/or outfield help may have interest in adding him. The Mets did not move him before the trade deadline despite swirling rumors, but now potentially interested teams will have another opportunity to add him to their rosters. Through 56 games played this season, the outfielder is hitting .229 to go along with a .719 OPS and 10 home runs. Those numbers obviously do not jump off the page, but he could offer right-handed power for a contender down the stretch. It will be interesting to see if teams take a chance on Robert. In all reality, it would be a low-risk move. Robert’s contract includes a club option for the 2027 season, so any team that acquires him would not have to keep him for another season. If they want to keep him on their roster, however, that also remains an option. Either way, the underperforming Mets will attempt to finish the season strong. They earned a 6-2 victory against the Houston Astros on Saturday. They will play the Astros once again on Sunday afternoon at 3:10 PM ET. The mayor of this desert city likens the U.S. West’s water crisis to planning for a meteor. ‘You can see it coming, but you can’t get out of the way’
articles.summary: Under the Bureau of Reclamation’s plan, California, Nevada and Arizona will collectively reduce water use by 1.25 million acre-feet.
articles._body: On the outskirts of Phoenix, a small town with a huge reliance on the Colorado River has capped growth, revived old wells and struck water deals. But Cave Creek Mayor Robert Morris can’t shake the real possibility that it’s not enough to keep the desert community of about 5,000 people afloat well into the future. And a recent  federal plan  to address a deepening crisis in the river basin won’t help. Cave Creek gets nearly all of its water from the river, which serves 40 million people across the U.S. West and has been dwindling because of climate change, demand and overuse. The town already was forced to make cuts this year and it stands to lose more under a new federal plan. Morris likened the situation to planning for a meteor strike. “You can see it coming, but you can’t get out of the way and you don’t know what the damage is going to be,” he said. The uncertainty stretches across seven U.S. states, tribal nations and Mexico. Farmers are deciding which crops are worth the investment. Phoenix could lose some municipal and industrial water for the first time and turn to backup supplies. And residents could face even more costly water. Nevada raised the stakes this week by suing the Interior Department and the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, saying basic needs in the Las Vegas region will go unmet if the area has to absorb  planned reductions  of up to 70% of its Colorado River water in the next decade. The bureau said Thursday it does not comment on litigation. “The uncertainty is going to continue to build in the wrong direction,” said Tom Buschatzke, director of the Arizona Department of Water Resources. Western reservoirs see record lows In the U.S. West, water is stored primarily in reservoirs, aquifers and snowpacks. But a  record snow drought  means there’s far less water to recharge those sources. The two largest reservoirs in the country serve as barometers of health for the Colorado River system:  Lake Mead and Lake Powell . Both hit record lows this month. Eight other reservoirs operated by the  Bureau of Reclamation  recently recorded the lowest levels in at least the last 30 years. Among them is Elephant Butte Lake in New Mexico that’s critical for supplying water for crops in southern New Mexico, Texas and Mexico. The Green Mountain Reservoir serves the western part of Colorado, and the Guernsey Reservoir in Wyoming funnels water to farmers in the eastern part of the state and western Nebraska. Under the Bureau of Reclamation’s plan, California, Nevada and Arizona will collectively reduce water use by 1.25 million acre-feet (about 1.54 billion cubic meters) — enough to fill over 600,000 Olympic-sized swimming pools — annually in the next two years, with the possibility of larger cuts depending on conditions. Colorado, Utah, Wyoming and New Mexico are not required to make cuts for now but could voluntarily reduce water. While  El Niño  could bring intense moisture to the northern Rockies and the Southwest in the coming months, it won’t erase decades of drought. “Drought is a slow-moving phenomena and it can take some time to come into it and also come out of it,” said David Mocko, senior research scientist who authored a recent U.S. Drought Monitor map. Farmers are reluctant to plant John Boelts grows vegetables, melons, durum wheat and other crops in Yuma, Arizona — a region that produces about 90% of leafy greens eaten in North America during the winter. Farmers there have high-priority rights and may avoid cuts to their Colorado River supply over the next two years but, Boelts said, the reprieve isn’t enough to make longer-term plans. That makes farmers reluctant to plant new acreage. Citrus, date and other orchard crops that thrive in the region take years to become commercially productive, he said. “There’s no food that we grow in a hurry,” said Boelts, the Arizona Farm Bureau president. “Beef takes years to produce. The lettuce you eat today? A farmer was working on how they would grow that crop six plus months ago.” Ray Martinez grows alfalfa on a reservation that’s home to the  Colorado River Indian Tribes . The tribe holds some of the river’s oldest rights, and while its Arizona allocation is huge, an old irrigation system and the lack of infrastructure have kept much of the water out of reach. Martinez and the water department are concerned about having enough water to finish this growing season. He has left some fields unplanted for years to help prop up Lake Mead. If the reservoir keeps dropping, he said, surface water coming to him and neighboring farms will be further limited. “Unfortunately, Mother Nature has its own way of doing things, and we have no control of that,” he added. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: How Sammy Sosa predicted Pete Crow-Armstrong on his 3-home run day for Cubs
articles.summary: The Chicago Cubs were bound and determined to get back on the winning track after losing three painful games in a row to the Arizona Diamondbacks and the Cincinnati Reds. Their offense woke up Saturday against the Reds, and MVP candidate Pete Crow-Armstrong was the fuse behind a 17-5 blowout win.
articles._body: The Chicago Cubs were bound and determined to get back on the winning track after losing three painful games in a row to the Arizona Diamondbacks and the Cincinnati Reds. Their offense woke up Saturday against the Reds, and MVP candidate Pete Crow-Armstrong was the fuse behind a 17-5 blowout win. Pete Crow-Armstrong on his 3-homer day: "Sammy did say I was gonna hit 3 today. Sammy Sosa told me I was gonna hit 3 and I hit 3. Put that on the record." Consider this officially on the record pic.twitter.com/y2srQInvOV — Marquee Sports Network (@WatchMarquee) August 29, 2026 Crow-Armstong blasted three home runs against the Reds and has 36 home runs this season. He had four hits in six at bats and he also drove in six runs in the one-sided triumph. Prior to the start of the game, he had a conversation with former Cubs superstar Sammy Sosa, and the record-setting slugger predicted that Crow-Armstrong would have a big day. “He told me I was going to hit three home runs today,” Crow-Armstrong said. “So, let’s put it on the record.” The Cubs’ All-Star centerfielder led off the bottom of the first inning with a home run to right center field, and red-hot Alex Bregman added a two-run homer before the inning was over. Crow-Armstrong is competing for the National League MVP award with Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani. The Cubs outfielder made his case even stronger when he added a two-run homer in the bottom of the second. He hit his third home run of the game when he blasted a three-run shot in the seventh inning. The Cubs pummeled six home runs in the win. In addition to Crow-Armstrong’s heroics, Bregman, Seiya Suzuki and Carson Kelly also delivered long balls for the Cubs. The Reds were unable to keep up with the barrage, but they did get two home runs from Sal Stewart and Eugenio Suarez. The Cubs will send Shota Imanaga to the mound Sunday night to close out the series against Reds fireballer Chase Burns. articles.summary: With the Chicago Bears facing the Tennessee Titans in the preseason finale, the team made its mark immediately in the first drive, thanks to rookie wide receiver Zavion Thomas. As the Bears prepare for Week 1 of the 2026 NFL regular season, any type of positive momentum is needed, which is just w
articles._body: With the Chicago Bears facing the Tennessee Titans in the preseason finale , the team made its mark immediately in the first drive, thanks to rookie wide receiver Zavion Thomas. As the Bears prepare for Week 1 of the 2026 NFL regular season , any type of positive momentum is needed, which is just what Thomas provided. On the very first drive of the contest for Chicago, the team was backed up on their own three-yard line. However, quarterback Tyson Bagent didn’t waste any time finding Thomas free on the right as he got open on his route and took it to the house for a 96-yard touchdown. ZAVION THOMAS BREAKS FREE FOR A 96-YARD TD pic.twitter.com/Gag399Cpma — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 29, 2026 While this play occurring at any point of the game would’ve been impressive, it happened on the Bears’ first play of the game as Bagent and Thomas made the most of the situation with the last game of the preseason. Not to mention that it was also Thomas’ first catch in an NFL game, as there is no denying that it will be one to remember for the rookie. Thomas was selected with the 89th overall pick in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft by Chicago, coming out of LSU. The 22-year-old is looking to separate himself from the rest as the Bears’ wide receiver room is filled with other players like Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III, Kalif Raymond, and others. At any rate, it remains to be seen how Thomas can progress in his first season with the Bears, as after the preseason finale, the Week 1 opener takes place on Sept. 13 against the Carolina Panthers. articles.title: Chiefs release linebacker who successfully sued NCAA for eligibility
articles.summary: Wesley Bissainthe enjoyed a fairly satisfying ending to his college career, as he helped Miami upset Ohio State and advance to the national championship for the first time in 24 years. Though, in this day and age, one writes their final chapter in pencil, not pen. Sensing that his NFL opportuniti
articles._body: Wesley Bissainthe enjoyed a fairly satisfying ending to his college career, as he helped Miami upset Ohio State and advance to the national championship for the first time in 24 years. Though, in this day and age, one writes their final chapter in pencil, not pen. Sensing that his NFL opportunities could be slim for 2026, the Third-Team All-ACC selection sought a fifth year of NCAA eligibility. He received a temporary restraining order from a Texas judge on Friday, and the Kansas City Chiefs are making his decision quite easy on Saturday. KC is releasing the undrafted rookie linebacker , per ESPN’s Adam Schefter. The likelihood of Bissainthe going back to school just spiked. Unless another NFL team wishes to give him a shot, he will probably try to sharpen his skills and expand his bank account in college. Fans may not like it, but this move is perfectly understandable given what has recently been put into action. The NCAA changed its eligibility requirements in June, allowing all of its athletes to play five seasons over the course of a five-year span. But it forbid outgoing seniors from receiving the same privilege , which, naturally, has unleashed a deluge of lawsuits. Bissainthe is one of 100-plus people to formally dispute the ruling. Perhaps a Miami reunion is imminent. He did grow up there, after all. The 22-year-old totaled five sacks, two interceptions, 121 solo tackles and 14.5 tackles for loss in 54 games for the Hurricanes. Wesley Bissainthe will presumably look to boost those career numbers. One thing is clear, he will not play for the Chiefs to begin the 2026 NFL campaign. articles.title: Kacey Musgraves Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton With ‘Rainbow’ & ‘Here You Come Again’ Live in Boston
articles.summary: She remembered the beloved icon as "someone always looking out for someone else, looking out for the underdog, even when it probably wasn't easy, even when it didn't benefit her career."
articles._body: Kacey Musgraves dedicated her emotional Golden Hour ballad “Rainbow,” as well as a cover of “Here You Come Again,” to Dolly Parton in Boston on Friday (Aug. 28). Related Nashville Airport to Be Renamed for Dolly Parton, Tennessee Governor Announces Dolly Parton’s Legacy on the Billboard 200 Chart: 7 Decades of Hit Albums Dolly Parton, One of Country Music’s Biggest & Brightest Icons, Dies at 80 Musgraves, who’s on tour in support of her Middle of Nowhere album, took a moment on the TD Garden stage Friday to point out it’s not just Parton’s Grammys, or countless other career accolades, that people are talking about in the wake of the country trailblazer’s death . “It’s what a humanitarian [she was],” Musgraves said. “Someone always looking out for someone else, looking out for the underdog, even when it probably wasn’t easy, even when it didn’t benefit her career. We can all learn a lot from someone like that.” “She’s woven into the fabric of who we’ve always been, so it just feels extra sad. Let’s all sing this together for her memory, OK?” she suggested, leading the arena crowd in a sweet sing-along of “Rainbow,” the closing track from Musgraves’ Grammy Award-winning 2018 album, Golden Hour . Photos of Parton, who passed away on Aug. 25 after a brief battle with cancer , were displayed on the big screen behind Musgraves as the room paid tribute to her, singing, “There’s always been a rainbow hangin’ over your head.” The next song on Musgraves’ set list at Friday’s show was a performance of “Here You Come Again,” off of Parton’s 1977 studio album of the same name. “Here You Come Again” was Parton’s earliest pop crossover hit, peaking at No. 3 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1978. In fact, just two other recordings from Dolly have topped its success on the all-genre ranking: “9 to 5” and her Kenny Rogers duet “Islands in the Stream,” which both became Hot 100 No. 1s in the early 1980s. Though Parton was a prolific songwriter, “Here You Come Again” was penned by Barry Mann and Cynthia Weil. Musgraves’ song choice is a callback to when she performed “Here You Come Again” alongside Parton in 2019, during a special segment featuring a medley of Parton’s hits at the Grammys. That year, she also sang the tune in Parton’s honor — as a duet with pop star Katy Perry , in a reprise of their CMT Crossroads performance several years prior — at the MusiCares Person of the Year gala. Musgraves has had a solo cover of “Here You Come Again” in rotation at concerts dating back to 2014. “She’s an earth angel,” she said of Parton in a red carpet interview at the 2019 Grammys. “She really is. She’s so cool. She’s so present. What I like about her is she has a keen attention to detail, and that’s obviously why she’s had such a long, amazing career. She really cares about those things, she can put her stamp on things without apology … She paved the way for a lot of us, especially in country music. We wouldn’t really be able to do what we do without her. She’s the first who had all of it together. The sex appeal, the brains, the humor, the songwriting, the outfits, the hair.” Watch the clips Musgraves shared from her Friday night show in Boston below. articles._body: With the Kansas City Chiefs ready for Week 1 of the 2026 regular season, the team is not done adding players to the team ahead of their opener, this time strengthening their offensive line depth. As the Chiefs are always looking to protect star quarterback Patrick Mahomes , the team did address that once again in a trade for a Baltimore Ravens rookie. According to NFL insider Mike Garafolo, Kansas City is trading for offensive lineman Diego Pounds, as the undrafted free agent was deemed to be “pound for pound” one of the highest-rated rookies in the preseason by Pro Football Focus (PFF). “The Ravens are trading OT Diego Pounds to the #Chiefs, sources tell me and [Ian Rapoport],” Garafolo wrote on X, formerly Twitter. “The undrafted free agent from Ole Miss, who weighs 330, was … pound-for-pound … one of [Pro Football Focus]’s highest-graded rookies this preseason.” Where PFF has new Chiefs player at in their rankings Looking at PFF’s latest rookie rankings after Week 2 of the preseason, Pounds was rated third with a 90.9 rating , with the Ole Miss product showing off in his limited opportunity. The rating made him the third-highest rookie and the top rookie offensive lineman in the rankings. “Pounds is the highest-graded offensive lineman in the NFL so far this preseason. He has been on the field for 15 pass-blocking snaps and has yet to allow a sack hit or hurry. He’s also produced a 91.1 PFF run-blocking grade on 19 run-blocking snaps,” Gordon McGuinness wrote. To get Pounds, Adam Schefter would say that it’s “contingent on the picks that KC has available at the end of the season,” which could be Day three of the 2027 NFL Draft or a Day three pick in 2028. It remains to be seen if Pounds will have a role for Kansas City this season, as Week 1 takes place on Sept. 14 against the Denver Broncos. NFL, NFLPA negotiating terms for player particpation in flag football at 2028 Olympics
articles.summary: The NFL and the NFL Players Association are in talks to finalize the terms by which players would be allowed to compete in flag football at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles, according to Mark Maske of Front Office Sports. Both parties are currently attempting to remove the final obstacles for NFL pl
articles._body: The NFL and the NFL Players Association are in talks to finalize the terms by which players would be allowed to compete in flag football at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles, according to Mark Maske of Front Office Sports . Both parties are currently attempting to remove the final obstacles for NFL players to compete in the Summer Games. In 2025, NFL team owners approved a resolution in support of players being allowed to play in the Olympics. But the resolution permitted the NFL’s management council and other league committees to negotiate arrangements with the NFLPA, Olympic authorities, and national governing bodies for player participation. Maske said the NFL must reach agreements on standards for field surfaces and medical care for the players, per the resolution. Additionally, the schedule could not “unreasonably conflict” with team and league commitments, and if a player gets injured while competing in flag football, the NFL team would receive salary-cap credit. It’s not clear when the talks will end, but they are ongoing. Once the terms are finalized, NFL players will likely take part in flag football practices and preparations ahead of the Olympics. This means players and teams would like to know the policies as soon as possible. Which NFL players will compete in flag football at the Olympics? The 2028 Olympics will have flag football from July 15-22. The games will be played at BMO Stadium, home to Los Angeles FC of Major League Soccer and Angel City FC of the National Women’s Soccer League. “There’s a lot of flag [football] content that’s going to be out there … including that weekend in Los Angeles and moving forward as we head towards the Olympics,” NFL’s executive vice president of club business, international and league events Peter O’Reilly said this week. “But separating the [Pro Bowl] honor from the flag [game] and the competitive piece of it was the key to it.” NFL officials told Front Office Sports that over 200 NFL players have expressed interest in competing in flag football at the Olympics. Some of the players who have expressed interest are QB Josh Allen of the Buffalo Bills, QB Joe Burrow of the Cincinnati Bengals, and WR Justin Jefferson of the Minnesota Vikings. However, the players on the U.S. flag football team said they want to be on the Olympic roster. Earlier this year, Team USA defeated two teams that included current and former NFL players in a round-robin tournament in Los Angeles.

articles.title: Eagles’ most agonizing roster decision looming on 2026 cutdown day
articles.summary: With their preseason finale against the Cincinnati Bengals officially in the books, the Philadelphia Eagles have already begun the process of trimming down their 90-man roster to a 53. Carson Steele, the owner of Crocky J and basically every offensive highlight of the preseason? Gone. Quez Watkin
articles._body: With their preseason finale against the Cincinnati Bengals officially in the books, the Philadelphia Eagles have already begun the process of trimming down their 90-man roster to a 53 . Carson Steele, the owner of Crocky J and basically every offensive highlight of the preseason? Gone . Quez Watkins? Gabe Hall? Zion Wilson? Ambry Thomas? Gone, gone, gone, and gone , though the last one shouldn’t be too surprising, considering how poorly he played against the Bengals. And yet, as dozens of dreams come to an end at the Jefferson Health Training Complex in South Philadelphia, there’s one major question that will likely go right up to the wire: who will be Jalen Hurts’ primary backup in Week 1? Heading into the summer, it looked like the Eagles had assembled a very deep and talented quarterback room, with 38-year-old veteran Andy Dalton joining incumbent reserve Tanner McKee and rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton out of North Dakota, but when the team actually took the field? Goodness, those expectations did not meet reality. Maybe it’s the loss of AJ Brown, which stung even more as top receivers like DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon missed much of the summer with injuries? Or maybe Sean Mannion’s scheme really is a radical departure from what Nick Sirianni has relied on over the last five years, with players like McKee, who have shined over the last two seasons, struggling to make the transition during the preseason? Either way, with Hurts the unquestioned Week 1 starter – with any suggestions of a reserve having a better chance to run Mannion’s offense firmly put to bed on Friday – and Payton likely safe as a developmental QB3 who showed more than 2025 sixth-round pick Kyle McCord, eventually, the Eagles will have to make a decision on which QB2 to keep heading into Week 1. Fortunately, it shouldn’t be much of a decision at all, as despite Philadelphia’s best effort to make it work, one of their quarterbacks simply doesn’t deserve a spot on the 53-man roster no matter how much veteran leadership he brings to the table. Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The Eagles have to finally say goodbye to Andy Dalton On paper, acquiring Andy Dalton for a 2027 seventh-round pick made all the sense in the world for Howie Roseman. A 15-year veteran with 183 games under his belt, including the playoffs, Dalton appeared in 13 games over the last three years for the Panthers, and while he only won one of the seven games he started, he completed an average of 64.7 percent of his passes and threw 10 touchdowns versus seven interceptions. Factor in his experience playing in a Sean McVay-style system, the same basic framework Mannion was expected to bring to Philadelphia as their offensive coordinator, and rolling with Dalton for the next two years as Payton developed looked like the play. And yet, even if McKee had shined in the preseason, forcing an opposing team to overpay in a trade to bring him to town – which didn’t happen – Dalton simply didn’t show he could do anything on the field but struggle, to the point where another team might not even pick him up if he gets released. Splitting time fairly evenly with McKee during the Birds’ three preseason games, Dalton struggled to get much going through the air, completing 18 of his 25 pass attempts for 168 yards, with the majority of that production coming in Game 3 against the Bengals’ deep reserves. Philadelphia’s offense was largely limited to quick screen passes and halfback checkdowns with Dalton running the show, and even when bigger plays were open, he struggled to get the ball where it needed to be. Now granted, McKee hasn’t been much better, to the point where if the Eagles were to make a trade involving a quarterback, it would likely be to bring in an arm like Dillon Gabriel, Spencer Rattler, or Will Howard, completing 34 of his 54 pass attempts for 263 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception that was really more Lemon’s fault than his own, but at least there were some highlights. Who knows, maybe McKee simply doesn’t have enough reps with the Eagles’ new players. Maybe Mannion’s vanilla offense was so bland that it didn’t allow the fourth-year quarterback to let it fly. But where Philadelphia once looked like they had two starting-caliber quarterbacks on their roster, they now might need a better option behind Hurts should anything happen to QB1. But there’s no two ways about it: McKee is better than Dalton in 2026, and at the end of the day, that’s all that matters. Would it have been a great bit of business for Roseman to land a quality backup for a seventh-round pick? Yes, that’s a good value for a position teams have increasingly begun to prioritize, and it would have freed up Payton to learn without a microscope on his day-to-day development as a rookie. But at this point, the experiment has failed, and that’s okay; better to move on now and start planning for the future than have to play Dalton when it matters, especially considering the rest of the roster around him is Super Bowl caliber. With ‘virtual speed bumps,’ these cities have reduced crashes by rewarding slower drivers with fewer red lights
articles.summary: "If you come to Albuquerque right now and you’re driving that corridor, you will learn pretty quickly that if you are speeding, you stop.”
articles._body: Officials struggled for years to curb  high-speed crashes  along a residential corridor cutting through Albuquerque, New Mexico, but simply  punishing the lead-footed drivers  didn’t seem to work. What ultimately did was rewarding the law-abiding ones with fewer  red lights . The solution, which the city credits for a dramatic drop in crashes and injuries along one busy stretch of road, is a relatively novel version of a longstanding  traffic safety  concept commonly known as “rest in red,” in which traffic signals default to red until a vehicle approaches. But Albuquerque and Portland, Oregon, took it a step further by adding speed sensors that grant a much earlier green light to drivers traveling at or below the  posted limit. “We’re finding that the technology itself is kind of its best advertisement,” Jennifer Turner, Albuquerque’s director of municipal development, said of the strategy the city deployed on Lead and Coal avenues, parallel one-way streets. “If you come to Albuquerque right now and you’re driving that corridor, you will learn pretty quickly that if you are speeding, you stop.” Isaac Romero, who lives along the corridor, said he has noticed a big difference. Before rest in red, he would sometimes wake up in the middle of the night to the sound of drivers racing to beat the traffic lights or one another. He saw  cars that had crashed and flipped , including one that ended up in his neighbor’s yard. “We had one accident where it’s even shaken the whole house because some guy slammed into a tree,” Romero said. “It’s a lot of change because now you don’t get as many people flying through there.” Portland credits its ‘virtual speed bumps’ Portland recently rolled out the concept during the late-night hours on Southeast Powell Boulevard, a busy state highway with a long history of crashes, including  fatal ones . Peter Koonce, who manages signals and street lighting for the city, calls the new approach a “virtual speed bump” and said the early results are promising. At the first intersection tested, rest in red was able to lower the average speed from 39 mph (63 kph) to 30 mph (48 kph), which is the speed limit, he said. Oregon State University researchers helped Portland choose its vehicle detection system for monitoring speeds, and now they’re assessing its performance. David Hurwitz, a professor of transportation engineering who leads the study, said it’s too early to draw sweeping conclusions. “This choice that we are making to try to increase speed compliance seems like it’s working really well — seems like it has potential,” said Hurwitz, who stressed that further research is needed to ensure those gains aren’t offset by more drivers running red lights or other negative consequences. Cities try to change driver behavior but avoid other problems Potential negative consequences are also a primary concern of Jay Beeber, chief government affairs and policy officer for the National Motorists Association, a drivers advocacy group. Although he acknowledges that rest in red could be effective in certain places at specific times, he questions whether driver behavior can really change without a broad education campaign and believes there are simpler, less-intrusive solutions. “I think it’s wishful thinking that drivers are aware enough and pay attention enough to really learn to change their speeds based on whether the light is gonna be red or not,” Beeber said. “I think people are going to end up at the light and just be frustrated. I don’t think they’re gonna know why.” Many U.S. cities, including Albuquerque and Portland, have long used  speed cameras  to successfully prevent speeding. In fact, Albuquerque set up three near where it also deploys the rest in red approach, which has made that approach even stronger, according to officials. LA briefly tried rest in red, but most cities haven’t A few other cities including Boulder, Colorado, and Long Beach, California, implemented smaller targeted efforts to use the threat of more red lights to force speeders to slow down. Rebecca Sanders, a national safety practice leader at the transportation consulting firm Fehr & Peers, led a 2019 report at Arizona State University and Toole Design looking at various strategies used across the country to manage speed. Of the cities surveyed, only Los Angeles was trying rest in red at the time, and it briefly experimented with using feedback signs to trigger a red light when a driver traveling too fast was detected. Sanders said the concept seems to work best on roads built for high-capacity traffic during the day but much less congested — and therefore more conducive to speeding — at night. A 2023 study on five rural and urban roads in North Carolina found a 43% reduction in total crashes after rest in red was implemented around the clock, said Aaron Moody, spokesperson for the North Carolina Department of Transportation. Unlike the systems being used in Albuquerque and Portland, this and other versions of the rest in red approach didn’t use speed sensors to turn lights green for law-abiding drivers, but instead kept lights red by default until vehicles approached, slowing them. Despite their apparent effectiveness at deterring speeding, cities have been slow to embrace rest in red. Romero said he’s visited enough neighborhoods through his home security business to know that the approach could work in many other places in Albuquerque and beyond. But it’ll take all drivers buying in, as the presence of just one speeder can trigger a red light. “If everybody cruises to 30 calmly, I can promise you, you can get every single green light all the way down,” Romero said. “But the moment that one person is there, it changes that whole route for everybody.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

Zappe was hoping to earn a backup QB role , but now he will need to look for a new opportunity. With Geno Smith leading the way and Cade Klubnik also on the roster, the Jets will move forward without Zappe. Zappe, 27, made his NFL debut during the 2022 season with the New England Patriots. He displayed signs of promise but only appeared in four total games and made two starts. Zappe received more playing time the following season, as he made 10 appearances and started six contests. Zappe has made just one appearance since the ’23 campaign, however, as he started one game for the Cleveland Browns in 2024. The quarterback is trying to find an opportunity, but he likely won’t receive much playing time with any team even if he signs elsewhere soon. Still, Zappe could serve as a reliable backup QB. In the 2026 NFL preseason with the Jets, Zappe completed 14 of his 21 passing attempts. He did throw two interceptions and failed to record a touchdown. Nevertheless, the QB recorded 135 passing yards through the air. Zappe’s respectable NFL experience and the fact that he had some quality moments this preseason could make him an intriguing backup quarterback candidate for a few teams around the league. Meanwhile, the Jets will move forward as they continue to prepare for the upcoming regular season. articles.summary: LOS ANGELES – When the Los Angeles Sparks first signed Tonie Morgan to a developmental contract earlier this season, head coach Lynne Roberts was eager to see two things from her. articles._body: LOS ANGELES – When the Los Angeles Sparks first signed Tonie Morgan to a developmental contract earlier this season, head coach Lynne Roberts was eager to see two things from her. One, her skill as a natural point guard, and two, her ability to put pressure on the rim . Before the Kelsey Plum trade, the All-Star guard had been the only guard on the roster who could consistently put the ball on the floor, get to the basket and finish while simultaneously drawing contact. But with a full 12-player roster, there just wasn’t any room for Tonie Morgan to get on the court for the Sparks. That all changed this month. The Sparks attempted to sign guard Ashlon Jackson away from the Connecticut Sun, and waived veteran Kiana Williams in the process. The Sun ended up matching the Sparks’ offer sheet, leaving them with an open roster spot. The team chose to convert Morgan’s development contract to a standard deal to round out the roster. And now with a consistent spot in the rotation, she’s been able to take advantage of her off the dribble game. “Getting downhill really opens up the 3-point shot for your teammates, opens up pocket passes, being able to make decisions in tight spaces helps,” Morgan said following the Sparks’ loss to the Atlanta Dream on Aug. 20. “Teams are kind of, I guess, still adjusting. Being a quick guard, that’s really hard to guard … But just being able to make the right read every time, be a playmaker is really the main goal.” Morgan took a hard fall during the Sparks’ most recent game, this past Monday against the Dream, and exited early to the locker room. Postgame, Roberts acknowledged she was in the process of getting imaging done and was in a lot of pain, but was up and walking around. She was not listed on the team’s injury report for Friday’s matchup against the Washington Mystics, a sigh of relief for a team that has battled shuffling lineups this year. Prior to signing the standard contract, Morgan had appeared in only one game with the Sparks. But since having her deal converted, she’s played in six games, including one start, and has been averaging a little over 14 minutes per game. In her lone start against the Connecticut Sun on Aug. 18, she had arguably her best performance of her young WNBA career, finishing with eight points and three steals while shooting 4-of-5 from the field. She followed that up with another eight point effort on Aug. 20 against the Atlanta Dream to go along with one rebound, three assists and two steals while again missing only one shot (4-of-5). In the first game she played after signing a standard deal, back on Aug. 15 against the Washington Mystics, she responded with seven points and six assists while knocking down the only two shots she took. She’s firmly established herself as a WNBA rotation caliber player, and is boosted by the recent contract reward. “Obviously it’s a positive thing, so I was very grateful, very excited,” Morgan said. “But I just want to show up every day, do my job and try and help the team.” The post Sparks’ Tonie Morgan opens up on ‘main goal’ during rookie season appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles._body: The Dallas Cowboys feature players on the roster bubble ahead of NFL roster cutoff day. But the franchise added offensive line help beforehand. Dallas and owner/general manager Jerry Jones struck a deal with the Pittsburgh Steelers to land Broderick Jones. ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter broke the Saturday news , adding that Dallas gains a former 2023 first rounder through Jones. Dallas quarterback Dak Prescott gains help up front here. The Cowboys are sending third and sixth round picks to Pittsburgh. Plus gains a future fourth rounder for the 2027 class. The Cowboys have endured trouble with protecting Prescott over the years. So this moves arrives late to address that flaw ahead of the regular season. Yet Jones’ arrival likely will push out some aspiring rookies and veterans who aimed to land on the 53-man roster. Names like Sebastian Guiterrez come to mind. Same with Marcellus Johnson, who like the former New England Patriots tackle Guiterrez only has one season of league experience in tow. Dallas brought in two rookies in former Kentucky Wildcat Shiyazh Pete and ex-Penn State standout Drew Shelton. The Cowboys still feature Tyler Guyton as the blindside protector in this room. Jones, however, knows the blindside well and can rise as a critical depth piece for this offensive line room. The 25-year-old still heads to Dallas with inconsistency concerns. He’s delivered trouble becoming a consistent starter and has fought through some notable injuries in his career. Perhaps the change in scenery can benefit Jones in the long run while at his new surroundings. The post Cowboys acquires Broderick Jones in trade with Steelers appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Even Cubs’ Craig Counsell can’t believe what Pete Crow-Armstrong
articles.summary: As Chicago Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong has been in NL MVP talks along with Los Angeles Dodgers sensation Shohei Ohtani, Saturday’s 17-5 win was a display of why the 24-year-old why he believes the award is for him to win. Crow-Armstrong would lead the Cubs with his first three-home-run ga
articles._body: As Chicago Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong has been in NL MVP talks along with Los Angeles Dodgers sensation Shohei Ohtani, Saturday’s 17-5 win was a display of why the 24-year-old why he believes the award is for him to win. Crow-Armstrong would lead the Cubs with his first three-home-run game on Saturday, garnering the attention of manager Craig Counsell. Bringing him now to 39 home runs on the season, the outfielder is having a fantastic season that has everybody within Chicago and the entire MLB amazed. Speaking after the win over Cincinnati, Counsell expressed how “lucky” he feels, along with everybody else, to be a part of the magical season from the star, according to Marquee Sports Network. “I think Pete’s having a wonderful season. It’s a lot of fun to watch,” Counsell said. “You see guys do this, and it doesn’t happen a lot, but it’s the seasons that you remember somebody having, and we’re lucky to be a part of it. I think as a fan in the stands, as teammates, for coaching staff, it’s watching somebody perform like this is something special.” “Pete’s done some things this year, done a couple things this year that really haven’t been done in a long time, and that’s why we’re talking about him a lot,” Counsell continued. “There’s a lot of things that have just changed tremendously, and it’s a credit to his continued work. I think his talent, he’s got himself in a good place, and his baseball IQ, and that’s a credit to a lot of people. It’s a credit to his teammates, his coaches, has gone quickly to another level.” "I think Pete's having a wonderful season. It's a lot of fun to watch … we're lucky to be a part of it … Pete's done a couple things this year that haven't been done in a long time." Craig Counsell on PCA's incredible season pic.twitter.com/kl2JOI1Kkb — Marquee Sports Network (@WatchMarquee) August 29, 2026 PETE CROW-ARMSTRONG HAS HIS FIRST CAREER 3-HOMER GAME! pic.twitter.com/XEfKhUYs9S — MLB (@MLB) August 29, 2026 At any rate, Crow-Armstrong looks to continue his incredible season with the series finale against the Reds on Sunday. Georgia Amoore’s locker room celebration goes viral after career game for Mystics
articles.summary: After scoring a career-high 25 points on Friday night, Georgia Amoore and her head coach broke out the dance moves.
articles._body: Georgia Amoore quickly became a fan favorite during her lone season in Lexington. She’s doing the same in the WNBA. After missing her entire rookie season with the Washington Mystics due to a torn ACL, Amoore made her professional debut earlier this summer. The former All-American point guard at Kentucky has started all 40 games for the Mystics, which sit at a 24-16 record, good enough for sixth in the standings. But up until this week, Amoore hadn’t been putting up the numbers she was as a Wildcat — that changed on Friday night. Amoore had her best outing yet as a pro in an 80-73 win over the Phoenix Mercury, going for 25 points and four assists in 30 minutes. She shot 9-16 from the field and 6-11 from deep, both setting new season-highs for makes. It was her first time scoring more than 14 points all season long. But no one was more excited about her performance than her head coach, Sydney Johnson. After Amoore’s career night, Johnson charged into the locker room and began celebrating with Amoore and the rest of the team. What happened next was an excellent use of social media. Start your day celebrating Georgia pic.twitter.com/OysLOjqtzw — Washington Mystics (@WashMystics) August 28, 2026 Amoore, who was taken 6th overall in the 2025 WNBA Draft before going down with her knee injury, has taken some time to get back to the same speed we saw in college. For the season, she’s averaged just 6.6 points and 3.5 assists in 23 minutes per outing as the starting point guard. She’s shot only 35.7 percent from the field and 32.6 percent from deep. She followed up Friday’s performance with a nine-point, five-assist outing on Saturday night in a loss to the Los Angeles Sparks. But Amoore is slowly finding her groove. She’s scored at least nine points in five of her last six games. The Mystics have gone 12-4 over the last 16 games with Amoore shooting the ball at a much-improved clip: 41.4 percent from the field and 42.5 percent from deep. She also signed a deal with the Australian league’s Perth Lynx on Friday , where she’ll play after the WNBA season wraps up. Amoore was always a fun presence with the Wildcats. The WNBA is beginning to see the same thing.

Report: Pittsburgh Steelers trade OT Broderick Jones to Dallas Cowboys
articles.summary: According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the Pittsburgh Steelers have traded offensive tackle Broderick Jones to the Dallas Cowboys. Jones is a former first-round pick of the Steelers, playing on both the left and right sides for them. But he is set to have a new home in Dallas, joining an offensive
articles._body: According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter , the Pittsburgh Steelers have traded offensive tackle Broderick Jones to the Dallas Cowboys. Jones is a former first-round pick of the Steelers, playing on both the left and right sides for them. But he is set to have a new home in Dallas, joining an offensive line already full of high draft selections. The Cowboys will also be receiving a fourth-round pick in the deal, per ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler . Going back to the Steelers will be a third a sixth-round pick. So, Dallas comes away with a new offensive tackle and an early Day 3 selection, while Pittsburgh adds extra draft capital. Going into the 2026 season, two tackles capable of filling starting roles appear to be on the roster for the Cowboys. Tyler Guyton , who is also a former first-rounder, should be back out on the left. Right tackle might be where Jones can make a push once arriving in Dallas. Right now, Terence Steele has the position held down. Brian Schottenheimer has to feel good about the interior. Tyler Smith and Tyler Booker are as good as it gets at guard. Cooper Beebe returns at center, combining for what’s one of the league’s top trios. If nothing else, Jones provides solid depth for the Cowboys on the outside. Some work has been put in this offseason to improve his game. New Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy brought out something Jones has never done before. “Coach McCarthy’s big on putting your hand down in the ground if it’s 1st and 10,” Jones recently said . “I’ve always been out of like a two-point, so putting my hand in the dirt, playing out of a three is a little bit different for me. But it’s something to learn from.” More on Broderick Jones, time with Pittsburgh Steelers Jones was a first-round pick of the organization and deemed the long-term plan on the blindside. His presence had been a constant one until the neck injury popped up. In three seasons, Jones played in 43 games and started 38 of those. Of the offensive snaps the Steelers had in 2025, he was out there for 97% of them. However, things have changed back in late April. Not only is the neck problem something to consider. But Pittsburgh also used its 2026 first-rounder on an offensive tackle. Max Iheanachor out of Arizona State is somebody they might be putting faith in moving forward. At the time, plenty of people were wondering what the Steelers would do. Flash forward to late August, and a trade came together.

The Earth is sizzling, but ‘climate hushing’ is hot right now among Democrats. ‘People are increasingly freaked out about other issues’
articles.summary: The Searchlight Institute, a Democratic think tank, urged the party to stop mentioning climate change because it is not a priority for voters.
articles._body: Climate change has been the backdrop to Charles Hughes’ entire life, from kindergarten lessons about disappearing habitats to wildfire smoke billowing through the air he breathed while growing up in Colorado. But now that he’s a college student in Massachusetts, he said global warming is rarely a top issue. “Honestly, it doesn’t come up as much,” said Hughes, who chairs the state’s chapter of the College Democrats. What a difference six years makes. During  President Donald Trump’s first term  and especially during the Democratic primaries to determine who would run against him in 2020, Democrats spoke constantly about climate change. They used it to rally young voters such as Hughes, fueling protests and sweeping demands to remake the economy with proposals like the  Green New Deal . But there has been a national shift in the conversation that is sharp enough for some researchers to coin the term “climate hushing” to describe it. The Searchlight Institute, a Democratic think tank, urged the party to stop mentioning climate change because it is not a priority for voters. The Sunrise Movement, a left-wing group that pushed global warming as a top issue for young people, switched its mission last fall to a broader mandate of fighting the Republican president. The shift is encapsulated by the  Democratic primary for U.S. Senate in Massachusetts  on Tuesday as the incumbent, Ed Markey, 80, tries to fend off a challenge from U.S. Rep. Seth Moulton, 47. Although Markey still talks about sponsoring the Green New Deal, his campaign is more focused on other issues to burnish his left-wing bona fides and prove to voters that he is not too old for the job. It is the latest example of how climate change has been eclipsed by issues such as affordability, U.S. support for Israel and, above all, how to confront Trump. “Six years ago, Green New Deal was every phrase out of Ed Markey’s mouth every chance he got. That is not the case now,” said Mary Anne Marsh, a veteran Democratic strategist in Massachusetts. “It’s about who’s best to fight. Period, full stop. Everything falls under that.” ‘People are increasingly freaked out about other issues’ Even if the political discussion on climate change has quieted, the planet has not. Scientists say there is an increasing chance that by the end of the year,  2026 could be the hottest year on record , or at least come close. A strengthening El Nino is forecast to be off the charts, spiking global temperatures. Some advocates expect the issue to return to center stage if Democrats retake the U.S. House in November and climate-sparked disasters dominate the winter. U.S. Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island, a prominent Democratic voice on climate change, said in an interview that ignoring the issue is a major strategic “blunder.” “Climate change has moved from the science department into the economics department,” he said. “It’s now battering people’s home insurance, property values, pocketbook concerns. So I think it’s a very powerful argument.” Trump has falsely claimed climate change is “a hoax,” and his party has regularly scoffed at Democratic proposals such as the Green New Deal. The Sunrise Movement, founded in 2017 to mobilize young voters over climate issues, announced in October that it was shifting to a broader fight against “fascism.” The group’s executive director, Aru Shiney-Ajay, said that was a prescient move because of reports that federal agents infiltrated protest meetings during Trump’s immigration raids in Minneapolis. “We just live in a significantly more authoritarian country. Because of that, a lot of the Democratic primaries are about more existential questions,” Shiney-Ajay, whose network generally backs left-wing Democrats, said in an interview. “It has felt less like people care less about climate and more like people are increasingly freaked out about other issues.” About 6 in 10 Democrats say climate change is “a very big problem” for the country, according to a  Pew Research Center poll  from April. That is roughly the same as in 2016. Still, climate has often taken a back seat to other issues in Democratic voters’ priorities, such as inflation, healthcare affordability and the role of money in politics. Affordability concerns have dominated the political debate this year. McKenzie Wilson of Blue Rose Research, a Democratic data firm, said voters have called for sweeping changes in response to economic discontent, demonstrating a level of anger not seen in years. “In that kind of environment it’s hard to think about long-term, existential problems,” Wilson said. “If we don’t talk and focus our attention on the number one thing the electorate wants to talk about, as we saw in 2024, we’re not going to be connecting with the electorate.” ‘Don’t say climate change’ That view was summed up by the Searchlight Institute, a Democratic think tank that last year released a provocative suggestion: “The First Rule About Solving Climate Change: Don’t Say Climate Change.” It contended that voters saw it as such an intimidating, complex issue that Democrats were more likely to win by focusing on other subjects — thus enabling them to regain power and tackle the crisis that they were not talking about. Leah Stokes, a political scientist at the University of California, Santa Barbara and author of “The Carbon Wave,” a book about Democratic President Joe Biden’s domestic agenda, said it was “galling” when politicians made the issue less of a priority. “The climate crisis is accelerating and we can’t really not talk about it for like a decade, because the planet will be even more on fire if we do that,” she said. Breaking down the 2026 Stanford Football schedule
articles.summary: Stanford football begins their 2026 season at home against Hawaii on Saturday, August 29th at 4:00 PM PT on ACCN.
articles._body: Sep 13, 2025; Stanford, California, USA; Stanford Cardinal linebacker Matt Rose (35) is congratulated by safety Jay Green (5) after a tackle against the Boston College Eagles during the third quarter at Stanford Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images Stanford football begins their 2026 season at home against Hawaii on Saturday, August 29 th at 4:00 PM PT on ACCN. Stanford is coming off a season in which they went 4-8 overall and 3-5 in the ACC. This is Tavita Pritchard ’s first season as head coach with Michigan grad transfer Davis Warren as the starting quarterback. Ok, let’s dive in! GoStanford.com: 2026 Stanford Football Schedule VIDEO: Andrew Luck punching out footballs before Hawaii Starting with the Hawaii game, Stanford narrowly fell to the Rainbow Warriors in the opener last year on the road, losing by just three points 23-20. Stanford had a legit chance to win that game, but due to some costly interceptions and some boneheaded penalties, they booted the game. The fact that they still only lost by three points is something that should give them some confidence going into this game. Hawaii went 9-4 overall and 5-3 in the Mountain West last season, defeating Cal in the Hawaii Bowl 35-31. Hawaii put up 29.0 points per game last season while giving up 24.1 points per game. Hawaii sophomore quarterback Micah Alejado is coming off an impressive campaign in which he went 285-430 (66.3%) for 3106 yards, 24 touchdowns, and nine interceptions. He also rushed for 105 yards and one touchdown, so he can move. They like to play a fast paced offense that gets the ball out quickly. Alejado’s favorite target, senior wide receiver Pofele Ashlock is out for this week zero matchup against the Cardinal per multiple reports . He had 76 receptions for 827 yards and eight touchdowns last season. Without him, that’s a major blow to the Rainbow Warriors’ offense. Especially since they lost wide receiver Jackson Harris (49 receptions for 963 yards and 12 touchdowns) to the transfer portal (LSU). Stanford will be missing a couple of keys pieces on offense as well in offensive tackle Niki Prongos , wide receiver Caden High , and wide receiver Nico Brown . For a full breakdown of who is out, I have more updates on the Cardinal Sports Report message boards , but those three guys I wanted to highlight. It’ll be crucial for Stanford’s offensive line and wide receivers to pick up the slack. As we saw last season, Stanford was able to move the ball pretty well against Hawaii, but they committed far too many mistakes with their turnovers and costly penalties. If Davis Warren can take good care of the ball and get a good rushing performance from Micah Ford and the rest of the running backs, Stanford should be in a good spot assuming Kris Richard ’s defense does its job. Following their game against Hawaii, Stanford will welcome No. 7 Miami (FL) to The Farm on Friday, September 4 th at 6:00 PM PT on ESPN. Miami went 13-3 overall and 6-2 in the ACC last season, reaching the national championship game despite not playing in the ACC championship game. Stanford was the first to score last year at Miami, leading 7-0 at the end of the 1 st quarter and being tied 7-7 at halftime. However, Miami broke it open in the second half, going on to win 42-7. This will be a tough game for the Cardinal, but one that hopefully will bring a good crowd and a lot of excitement. If they can take care of business against Hawaii, they’ll at least be going into this game with a win under their belts. That’s why the Hawaii game is so important. Stanford will then have a bye week the weekend of September 12 th . Stanford will return to action on Saturday, September 19 th at Duke. Kickoff is set for 1:00 PM PT on The CW. Duke went 9-5 overall and 6-2 in the ACC last season, winning the ACC championship game. A lot of people kinda seem to have dismissed the fact that they were ACC champions. The fact of the matter is they handled their business on their schedule, played in the championship game against Virginia and won the game. They were the champs. Simple as that. This should be a good road test for Stanford to kinda see where they’re at. It’ll also help Stanford I think that they’ll be coming off a bye. Especially since it’s going to be a road game. After their duel with the Blue Devils, the Cardinal will return home to face Georgia Tech on Saturday, September 26 th at 7:30 PM PT on ESPN. The Yellow Jackets are receiving votes in the AP Top 25 and are coming off a season in which they went 9-4 overall and 6-2 in the ACC. This should prove to be a legit challenge for Stanford. Thankfully, it’s a night game on the West Coast, which tends to give Stanford at bit of an edge against East Coast opponents. This is a game that could really affect the direction of the season given it’s at home and Georgia Tech is a quality opponent. This is the kind of game you win if you are a program on the upward trajectory. After facing the Yellow Jackets, Stanford will hit the road to face Wake Forest on Saturday, October 3 rd . Wake Forest went 9-4 overall and 4-4 in the ACC last season. They’re a decent team, but on paper one of the more winnable road games Stanford has this season. Another litmus test game. This is the kind of game you win if you are on the up and up. Stanford will then head to South Bend for a non-conference game against No. 4 Notre Dame. Kickoff is 12:30 PM PT on NBC. Notre Dame defeated Stanford 49-20 last season in The Legends Trophy game. Notre Dame on paper should win this game handily, but a few years back, Stanford stunned Notre Dame on the road, so you never know. Still, I think everyone would be shocked if the Cardinal pull off the upset. Stanford will finally return home for their homecoming game against Elon on Saturday, October 17 th . articles.title: 49ers release QB right before 2026 regular season
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers face one of the most difficult assignments of any team in the NFL this season. They have high hopes of making a run at the NFC West title, but if they are going to do that, they are going to have to beat out the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks […]
articles._body: The San Francisco 49ers face one of the most difficult assignments of any team in the NFL this season. They have high hopes of making a run at the NFC West title, but if they are going to do that, they are going to have to beat out the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks and the heavily favored Los Angeles Rams. Perhaps no team in the league will have a greater challenge, but as head coach Kyle Shanahan finalizes his roster, he knows that quarterbacks Brock Purdy and Mac Jones will attempt to drive the Niners past their two primary competitors. Purdy, of course is the team’s QB1, and Jones is a proven backup. The No. 3 quarterback position came down to a battle between former Indiana quarterback Kurtis Rourke and Adrian Martinez. Shanahan has decided that Rourke will man the No. 3 QB position and that Martinez does not have a place on the San Francisco roster, per NFL insider Ian Rapoport. Martinez played in one game for the 49ers last season, but that was not enough to convince the head coach that he deserved another spot on the team in 2026. Purdy had to split time at quarterback last year with Jones, but he hopes to remain healthy and start 17 games this season. Purdy completed 197 of 284 passes for 2,167 yards with 20 TDs and 10 interceptions. Jones was solid as his backup, completing 201 of 289 passes for 2,151 yards with 13 TDs and 6 interceptions. Martinez did not get a chance to throw the ball in the one game that he played last season, registering one carry on a kneel down on the final play of the game in a 34-24 victory over the New York Giants.
