articles.title: Why Dodgers’ Blake Snell wasn’t satisfied by almost perfect outing vs. Tigers
articles.summary: Though Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani had his pitching return delayed, Blake Snell is a pitcher on the team who is currently in the groove of making his mark on the season, with Saturday’s start being his fourth of the season. As the playoffs are near for the Dodgers, Snell looks to
articles._body: Though Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani had his pitching return delayed , Blake Snell is a pitcher on the team who is currently in the groove of making his mark on the season, with Saturday’s start being his fourth of the season. As the p layoffs are near for the Dodgers , Snell looks to ramp up for the postseason, with Saturday’s outing a good start in the right direction, though there was one area that he wants to be better in. Though Los Angeles would fall 2-1 to Detroit, Snell turned in an impressive outing, recording 10 strikeouts while only giving up one earned run to go along wth allowing three hits and three walks in five innings and 99 pitches. However, the main goal that Snell is “chasing” is to “give up zero runs.” “The goal is to give up zero runs, so that’s what I’m chasing,” Snell said, via SportsNet LA. “My goal is, ‘don’t give up any runs and give us a good chance to win.'” "The goal is to give up zero runs. That's what I'm chasing." Blake Snell (5.0 IP, 3 H, 1 ER, 3 BB, 10 K, 99 P) recaps his outing in the #Dodgers 2-1 loss to the Tigers. pic.twitter.com/HDs0HSpyRW — SportsNet LA (@SportsNetLA) August 29, 2026 While Snell would analyze his start positively, he expressed that he felt “more passive today than aggressive” against Detroit, even stating that preparing for the afternoon contest was “tough” “Just more passive today than aggressive,” Snell said. “I don’t know for what reason, but getting ready for a day game today was tough. I don’t know why that was. Locking in was a little tougher, but yeah, overall, happy with the way I competed with runners on base. Happy with the way I continue to just learn and develop throughout the at-bats on what I should do, what I don’t like, what I like. But yeah, overall, didn’t give in and made pitches when I needed to.” At any rate, Snell looks to continue to chase his goal of allowing zero runs in his next start, likely to be on Saturday, Sept. 5 against the Washington Nationals. articles.title: Countdown to kickoff prediction series: Mason Love will be even better as a sophomore
articles.summary: Continuing the countdown to kickoff prediction series: Sophomore Mason Love will an even better year as South Carolina's punter and holder.
articles._body: In May, when the calendar revealed that it was 100 days until South Carolina kicked off the season, I posted a story on GamecockCentral entitled “100 predictions for the 2026 Gamecocks.” Now, that countdown is down to just seven days. The prediction paired with day seven read, “In year two of Mason Love starting, South Carolina will continue its streak of punting excellence. Love will also have another good year as the team’s holder, assuming he doesn’t win the placekicking job.” Let’s break down that prognostication. Have a question for the GamecockCentral staff? Ask it now on The Insiders Forum. 2025 Mason Love joined the South Carolina football program in the class of 2024. He was a five-star punter and a five-star kicker but was the nation’s top punter in the ’24 cycle. He then redshirted behind All-American Kai Kroeger. As a redshirt freshman last year, Love was very good in the starting punter role. He averaged over 45 yards per punt, earning Freshman All-SEC recognition. He also had a smooth year as the Gamecocks’ holder. In fact, Love’s freshman campaign was so good that only one other freshman had a better per-punt average, and he was a 29-year-old former professional Australian Rules football player. Love booted 13 punts for more than 50 yards, and he pinned 16 punts inside the 20-yard line, while allowing just four touchbacks. The Ray Guy Award picked Love as one of its weekly “Ray’s 8” twice in 2025, against LSU and against Alabama. Love’s freshman year was a continuation of the punting excellence that South Carolina experienced under Kroeger and Joseph Charlton. Punting from 2017-2024, those two own most of the punting records in Gamecock history. If he continues to get better, Love could challenge some of his predecessors’ marks. What does this mean for the Gamecocks? Fellow subscribers are discussing it now on The Insiders Forum. 2026 Perhaps working in Love’s favor, it felt at times in 2025 that he wasn’t performing his best. Even with strong averages and a good overall body of work, Love looked like he mishit several of his punts. That should be an encouraging thing, as it means he was among the SEC’s best punters, despite having room for personal improvement. In other words, he had a strong season but has even more left in the tank. That, combined with another offseason of getting stronger and more experienced, could indicate that Mason Love is in line for a big redshirt sophomore campaign. Plus, Love has not been nearly as involved in the placekicking job as he was in 2025. Last year, he was the team’s (lightly used) long option. This summer, head coach Shane Beamer revealed Love was primarily focused on punting and holding. While South Carolina fans hope they see him with his knee on the ground as a holder much more than standing up as a punter, special teams coordinator Matthew Smiley will be counting on him to excel in both spots this fall. What’s your prediction? Share it with fellow subscribers on The Insiders Forum.

articles._body: <a href="https://www.on3.com/sites/asu-devils/join/?utm_source=publisher&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=subscriber_referral&ref=1035347"> <img src="https://on3static.com/cdn-cgi/image/quality=95,format=jpg/uploads/dev/assets/cms/2026/08/28182555/Devils-Digest-KS.png"> </a> <a href="https://www.SanTanFord.com"> <img src="https://on3static.com/cdn-cgi/image/quality=95,format=jpg/uploads/dev/assets/cms/2025/07/25180034/2024-San-Tan-Ford-Banner-3.jpg"> </a> Saturday morning reports started trickling in that third-year Kentucky transfer Cutter Boley was named Arizona State’s starting quarterback. Following today’s practice, ASU head coach Kenny Dillingham revealed that Boley’s play over the course of the preseason practices won him the job. Boley had been the frontrunner for the role ever since committing to the program in January, but he wasn’t able to secure that niche when spring practices ended. The competition for that coveted job pitted Boley against sixth-year QB Mikey Keene, second-year QB Cameron Dyer and first-year QB Jake Fette, continued.  Dillingham whittled the battle down to Boley and Keene on Aug. 17, following the Sun Devils’ trip to Camp Tontozona. Since then, despite Dillingham’s reluctance to name a starter, Boley consistently commanded the first team offense. Now, with Week 1 just around the corner, Dillingham didn’t delay the inevitable with his announcement.  “We felt like he (Boley) had a great camp, did a good job taking care of the football,” Dillingham said. “We felt like there’s a lot of guys that had a great camp. We feel really good about Mikey. We feel really good about Cam. We feel really good about Jake. We feel good about that room; we thought they all got better. We think Cutter’s the best opportunity for us to go win football games. “He has comfort in the system (since spring), understanding what we are trying to accomplish.” Boley’s arm talent has long been lauded, and Dillingham has praised his underrated athleticism. Accuracy, however, was a question that the third-year player had to answer.  Boley recorded 12 interceptions to 15 touchdowns a season ago, and 16 interceptions to 17 touchdowns across his entire two-year tenure at Kentucky. During the fall, Boley and the coaching staff emphasized taking care of the ball, and the quarterback delivered, as the defense picking him off was a rare sight.  “We’ve been coaching him pretty hard on when to take chances and when to not,” Dillingham expressed. “If it’s fourth down and you throw a pick 25 yards down the field in the fourth quarter of a game, I’m not going to be too upset. If it’s third and eight on our minus 25 in the first quarter, and you scramble out and throw an errant throw for an interception, you just cost us a minimum of three points. That can’t happen. “Part of being a quarterback is understanding how not to take negatives, and not put the ball in jeopardy  and I think he has grown in that.” Although Boley’s play in the vaunted SEC wasn’t earth-shattering, he proved himself to be a capable quarterback. He was named to the SEC All-Freshman team and showcased his potential with a 330-yard, 5 touchdown to 1 interception game against Tennessee.  Boley has continued to grow under the tutelage of Dillingham and offensive coordinator Marcus Arroyo, and his already established experience should help the Sun Devils against a gauntlet of No. 8 Texas A&M, No. 12 Texas Tech and No. 14 BYU — not to mention ASU’s trip to London, taking on Kansas at Wembley Stadium in the Union Jack Classic. “The experience to play at a high level is huge because the lights aren’t going to be too bright for him,” Dillingham said. “He understands what the biggest atmospheres in college football look like. We play three games versus top-15 opponents on the road this year. We’re going to play under a lot of bright lights.” *** Fourth-year running back Kyson Brown is one of the Sun Devils’ veteran leaders, serving on the Pat Tillman Leadership Council. During his time in Tempe, Brown has shared the backfield with five different quarterbacks, giving him a good understanding of how a college QB should operate.  Brown believes Boley fits the billing.  “He really knows how to communicate with the guys around him,” Brown revealed. “I think that’s one of the biggest jobs as far as the quarterback, commanding the offense, getting guys lined up, knowing where guys are. He definitely helps us.”  The aid isn’t a one-way street; when Boley first arrived in the Valley of the Sun, Brown helped him understand the offense and learn ASU-specific terminology. Over time, the two have grown closer on a personal level as well. The pair share a similar Southern background, with Boley hailing from Hodgenville, Kentucky, and Brown from Lancaster, Texas, which gives them something to bond over and fosters their friendship. “He’s a good human being,” Brown expressed. “Cool dude, chill, laid back. We kick it all the time, go out to eat, do activities together. We’ve definitely grown since the time he’s been here.”  Boley’s abilities go beyond commanding the offense and being a good hang, however. Like Dillingham, Brown, who’s played the majority of first-team running back reps alongside Boley, sees him as a multifaceted quarterback.  Boley’s playstyle has kept Brown on his toes throughout the fall, as even when positive gains seem implausible, Boley can make something work.  “He has a lot of different capabilities,” Brown said. “Knowing that he can do whatever with the ball, just know I got to be alert at all times. Scramble, he might make some miraculous plays. He’s done some flips off the script, so got to make me aware of those off-the-script plays.”   *** Dillingham confirming that Boley will start for the Sun Devils wasn’t the only announcement he made Saturday morning, revealing that Boley,

articles._body: The Baltimore Ravens are making another change to their quarterback group before the 2026 NFL season. The Ravens have officially released quarterback Austin Reed, according to ESPN reporter Jeremy Fowler. Fowler shared the news on Saturday. Baltimore keeps making key roster decisions before the regular season begins. Reed joined the Ravens earlier this month after the team put quarterback Skylar Thompson on injured reserve . Baltimore signed Reed on August 12. The former UFL standout for the Dallas Renegades had a chance to compete for a spot behind Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. The 26-year-old quarterback played for the Dallas Renegades in the 2026 UFL season and had an impressive year. Reed was second in the league with 1,923 passing yards. He set a UFL single-season record with 21 touchdown passes. He also threw for 376 yards in the season opener. That was a UFL single-game record at the time. Reed did not get many chances with Baltimore but made a quick, noticeable impact in the preseason. He completed both of his passes and ran for a 14-yard touchdown in his Ravens debut against the Philadelphia Eagles. Still, the Ravens ultimately chose to let Reed go on Saturday as they finish building their roster for the 2026 season. Rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano also competed for the third-string spot. He had a strong preseason, going 22-for-28 for 224 yards and a touchdown against the Philadelphia Eagles. Now, Baltimore will move forward with Jackson, Huntley, and Fagnano as its quarterbacks as the team prepares for its regular season opener at home. articles.title: TCU football getting roasted on social media after loss to North Carolina
articles.summary: Four years ago, TCU football enjoyed one of its greatest campaigns ever. Last year, the Horned Frogs pummeled North Carolina in their opener and posted nine wins for the second straight season, a feat they had not accomplished since 2015. On Saturday, Sonny Dykes’ squad fell to Bill Belichi
articles._body: Four years ago, TCU football enjoyed one of its greatest campaigns ever. Last year, the Horned Frogs pummeled North Carolina in their opener and posted nine wins for the second straight season, a feat they had not accomplished since 2015. On Saturday, Sonny Dykes’ squad fell to Bill Belichick and the Tar Heels in an ugly iteration of the Aer Lingus College Football Classic. This is not your slightly older brother’s TCU. And it is certainly not your father’s TCU. Although Belichick is the man of the hour after coaching his team to a much-needed 15-10 victory in Dublin, Ireland, many are focusing on what the Horned Frogs did wrong instead of what Carolina did right. Considering what transpired on the field, dwelling on the negative is quite easy to do. Just look at social media. “The fall of TCU from making the National Championship in 2022 to whatever the hell this is now needs to be studied,” On3’s Blain Crain posted on X . “You can talk up UNC after this if you want idc but idk how you don’t come away from this 60 minutes of football just being disgusted by the product TCU put on display,” Barstool’s Liam Blutman opined . He has a point. The Frogs committed an inexcusable 11 penalties for 89 yards and were 1-of-5 on fourth-down conversions, which included their failed attempt on the Tar Heels’ 10-yard line on their final drive of the game. Jaden Craig completed 20-of-32 passes for a modest 175 yards with no touchdowns and no interceptions. This team had its opportunities but will leave the Emerald Isle with an 0-1 record and much to work on moving forward. “Fitting way for that to end for TCU,” Dan Wolken of Yahoo Sports stated . “So sloppy. North Carolina gets the upset.” Whatever his faults, Bill Belichick is one of the greatest defensive minds the sport has ever known and can certainly shut down a quarterback who has never competed in a Power Four program before. One should be able to see why Sonny Dykes and company were unable to break through in this one, but the execution gives TCU football fans good reason for concern. The Horned Frogs have two weeks to digest and learn from this outcome before facing Grambling in Fort Worth. Someone better make sure they do not venture off to the pub on their way back to the plane, because these guys will be in some kind of a mood after enduring such a bitter start to the season. articles.title: NFL, NFLPA Negotiating Terms for Olympic Flag Football Participation
articles.summary: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images
articles._body: The NFL and the NFL Players Association are engaged in discussions to finalize the terms by which interested players would be permitted to participate in flag football at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles. The final policy details have not yet been determined but the talks are ongoing, a source familiar with the state of the negotiations told Front Office Sports . The league and union have been able to work cooperatively on a series of recent measures. They’re now attempting to remove the final obstacles to NFL players competing for an Olympic gold medal. NFL team owners unanimously approved a resolution last year in support of players being allowed to play at the Olympics. That was not the final step, however. The owners’ resolution authorized the NFL’s management council and other league committees to negotiate suitable arrangements with the NFLPA, Olympic authorities, and national governing bodies for player participation. The resolution said the NFL must reach agreements on standards for field surfaces and medical care for players. The participation schedule for players, it said, could not “unreasonably conflict” with team and league commitments. Other issues include establishing injury protections for players via insurance policies and ensuring that an NFL team would receive salary-cap credit if any of its players is injured while participating. The owners’ resolution proposed limiting Olympic participation to one player per NFL team on a single country’s roster, along with permitting any player in a team’s international program to participate for his country. It’s not clear when the talks might conclude. Players and teams will likely want to know the policies well in advance of the run-up to the Games. Participating NFL players will presumably have to participate in flag football practices and preparations ahead of the Olympic competition. The flag football competition at the 2028 Games is scheduled for July 15–22. That creates limited—if any— conflict with NFL training camps, at least under the current offseason structure. The competition includes men’s and women’s tournaments consisting of six teams each. Games will be played at BMO Stadium, home to Los Angeles FC of MLS and Angel City FC of the NWSL. NFL officials have said recently that more than 200 players have expressed interest in participating. “They’re very serious about the Olympic opportunity,” Peter O’Reilly, the NFL’s executive vice president of club business, international and league events, said at the league meeting Wednesday in Atlanta. NFL commissioner Roger Goodell and other league leaders began endorsing the participation of NFL players in Olympic flag football soon after the International Olympic Committee’s 2023 decision to add five sports, including men’s and women’s flag football, to the 2028 Games. The NFL has leaned heavily into the growth of flag football, believing that the flag version of the sport expands the fan base, boosts youth participation, and furthers the league’s goal of broadening its global appeal. The NFL is involved in launching professional flag football leagues for men and women. It established an ambitious youth flag football tournament and has promoted the growth of the non-tackle version of the sport at the high school and collegiate levels. It played its Pro Bowl as a flag football game in recent years before announcing Wednesday that it was eliminating the postseason all-star game . The league said that 88 players still will be selected as Pro Bowl players for this season and honored next year at an event in Los Angeles. “There’s a lot of flag [football] content that’s going to be out there … including that weekend in Los Angeles and moving forward as we head towards the Olympics,” O’Reilly said Wednesday. “But separating the [Pro Bowl] honor from the flag [game] and the competitive piece of it was the key to it.” Troy Vincent, the NFL’s executive vice president of football operations, said in Atlanta that players “understand the importance of football being a global sport. And what’s our entry point globally? It’s through flag. And if that’s an important part of growing popularity, we should be doing everything to make sure that the game is being open to all.” Star quarterbacks Josh Allen of the Bills and Joe Burrow of the Bengals are among the NFL players to have expressed interest publicly in playing in the Olympic flag football competition. Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson attended the announcement of the owners’ resolution in May 2025—during a league meeting held at a hotel next to the Vikings’ training facility in Eagan, Minnesota—and said he’d consider playing. Meanwhile, veteran U.S. flag football players have said they want a fair chance to vie for roster spots. The NFLPA said the week before that 2025 owners’ meeting that it fully supported “our player members participating in the Olympics and taking this opportunity to represent their country on the highest international stage.” The union added then that it looked forward to discussing the players’ participation with the NFL “to ensure players who choose to compete can do so without detrimental impacts to their health, safety and job.” The league and NFLPA have a sometimes-combative history, but have been able to work together well in recent months, early in JC Tretter’s tenure as the union’s new executive director. They jointly announced a new player-accountability system Wednesday, by which any player who violates specified player-safety rules three times this season faces an automatic one-game suspension, while any player who has only one such infraction will have half his fine money refunded to him at season’s end. The deliberations on that system occurred over “the last several months,” the NFL and NFLPA said in their joint statement. The same day, the league and union jointly announced the Sept. 1 launch of a Behavioral Health Network, which they described as an enhancement to the NFL player insurance plan exp

articles.title: New U.S. sanctions will hit ordinary Iranians hard. That may be the whole point as the crashing economy stirs fresh protests
articles.summary: "Digital assets and gold are how ordinary Iranians protect their savings from inflation."
articles._body: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent laid out plans for an “economic D-Day” against Iran on Monday, seeking to further isolate the regime from the rest of the world. The U.S. will expand its use of secondary sanctions against entities and countries that engage with Iran. Bessent also said any country that helps Iran will be removed from the dollar-based financial system. In addition, he targeted five of Iran’s “most vital lifelines”: digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, and shipping. But Esfandyar Batmanghelidj, founder and CEO of the Bourse & Bazaar Foundation think tank, said those are actually lifelines for the Iranian people, not the regime. “Digital assets and gold are how ordinary Iranians protect their savings from inflation,” he explained in a post on X . “Technology keeps Iranians connected with the world. Aviation keeps Iranian families connected with loved ones across borders. Shipping is how essential goods, including food and medicine, reach Iran.” The sanctions come as the Trump administration has pivoted away from resuming all-out war, hoping that economic warfare will accomplish what bombs and missiles couldn’t. The Treasury Department didn’t respond to a request for comment. To be sure, crypto currencies, technology and front companies in shipping are also ways the Iranian regime skirts Western sanctions, allowing it to continue earning valuable revenue. But the United Arab Emirates also shut down all trade and transactions with Iran earlier this month, cutting off a vital for engagement with the global economy. Meanwhile, the U.S. war and naval blockade have inflicted a catastrophic toll on Iran’s economy, which was already in shambles before the conflict started. Inflation has soared above 80%, with prices for certain food staples up 100%. The currency, which triggered nationwide protests late last year after it collapsed, has lost a further 30% of its value this year. The International Monetary Fund said in April Iran’s economy will shrink 6.1% this year, the worst contraction in decades. And a labor ministry official estimated that more than 1 million jobs had been lost by late May. The naval blockade has not only prevented Iran from exporting oil via its ports, it has also kept out imports of refined fuels that Iran needs despite being a major oil producer. That has created shortages and long lines at gas stations, made worse by deep subsidies that encourage excess consumption. But the government is reluctant to hike prices and slow demand, fearing more public anger over inflation. Amid the growing stress, some moderate officials have signaled that time is running out to obtain some economic relief as the U.S. and Iran remain in limbo with no sign of diplomatic progress. “No matter how strong we are militarily, if the people are hungry and we do not have financial circulation, economic growth and domestic production, we will not endure,” parliamentary speaker and Iran’s chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said while visiting Iraq earlier this month. In fact, some protests have started breaking out, though not at the massive scale that was seen in January, when the government slaughtered thousands in a brutal crackdown. On Monday, oil and gas workers in Asaluyeh staged a protest, saying they shouldn’t have to suffer a cost-of-living crisis while keeping oil production online, state media said, according to the Wall Street Journal . Earlier, about 100 laid-off workers protested at the Shadegan steel complex in western Iran, petrochemical workers in costal city of Bandar-e Mahshahr protested their layoffs, and teachers union members have publicly complained about not getting paid. Experts have cautioned that Iran’s repressive regime is unlikely to be swayed by the suffering of ordinary citizens and is prepared to wait out economic hardship longer than Americans can endure high gas prices. Still, officials continue to acknowledge the strains ordinary Iranians face, while clashing with hardliners who oppose any negotiations with the U.S. “The country today faces great, complex, and multiple open and hidden challenges,” Ghalibaf said on Wednesday. “Our duty at this moment is to devote all our time and energy to resolving the people’s problems, increasing Iran’s economic power, and preserving the achievements of resistance.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles._body: Pete Crow-Armstrong is a man possessed this season. He played a huge part in leading the Chicago Cubs to a 17-5 win over the Cincinnati Reds on Saturday after hitting three home runs in the contest. That just so happens to be the first three-home-run game in the 24-year-old’s MLB career. His third dinger of the day came in the bottom of the seventh inning, as he launched the ball to deep left-center field. The ball landed well in the stands at Wrigley Field. CUBS' PETE CROW-ARMSTRONG MAKES HISTORY WITH HIS FIRST CAREER THREE-HOMER GAME pic.twitter.com/091f8Nne7t — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 29, 2026 On top of going yard three times, one of his home runs happened as a leadoff homer. Pete Crow-Armstrong tied for the second-most leadoff home runs in a single season in Cubs’ franchise history. He needs four more to tie Alfonso Soriano, who recorded 12 leadoff dingers in the 2007 campaign. The four-year veteran ended Saturday’s game with an impressive statline. He totaled four hits, three of which were blasted for home runs, and six RBIs through six at-bats. Crow-Armstrong also scored four runs himself in the Cubs’ win. His home run totals are now up to 36 on the season. That’s good enough to put him tied for third most with Yordan Alvarez and Hunter Goodman (assuming they hit no home runs on Saturday). Either way, the two-time All-Star is certainly making a name for himself in the best year of his career so far. Pete Crow-Armstrong is firmly in the mix for the NL MVP race. Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani is also a top candidate for the award. However, Crow-Armstrong’s availability, defensive ability, and wildly impressive league-high 7.9 WAR makes him a standout amongst the crowd. articles._body: The Las Vegas Raiders may be delaying their official announcement regarding their starting quarterback, but reports are making the expected outcome increasingly clear. According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, there is a growing consensus within the organization and across the league that Kirk Cousins will secure the starting role for Week 1. As the regular season opener approaches, the Raiders are preparing to rely on veteran leadership in their offense. CBS Sports national reporter Matt Zenitz confirmed on X that the Raiders are expected to name Cousins as their starting quarterback, citing sources. This decision firmly establishes Cousins as the primary quarterback over rookie Fernando Mendoza, providing head coach Klint Kubiak’s team with experienced stability at the position as they begin the 2026 campaign. The #Raiders are expected to name Kirk Cousins as their starting quarterback, sources tell @CBSSports pic.twitter.com/U1DlIY9u19 — Matt Zenitz (@mzenitz) August 29, 2026 Choosing the seasoned four-time Pro Bowler over the developing rookie is a sensible strategy aimed at protecting Mendoza as he adjusts to the speed of the NFL. During Las Vegas’ exhibition finale against the San Francisco 49ers, Mendoza entered the game after Cousins played two series. He faced significant pressure behind a reconstructed offensive line, completing only seven of 14 passes for 51 yards and throwing an interception. Pro Football Focus ranks the Raiders’ offensive line 18th in the league. While newly signed center Tyler Linderbaum has improved their run blocking, the line is still working to improve its pass protection. Thus, putting a rookie in such a challenging situation carries substantial risks. For Cousins, taking on this role is about setting a standard and executing his responsibilities with humility. In a statement on the team’s official YouTube channel, Cousins highlighted his mindset : “I think it’s just up to Coach. You do the best you can with the opportunities you’re given. Lead as well as you can. Compete. You’re never a finished product.” Allowing Mendoza the opportunity to observe and learn from Cousins positions the young quarterback for greater long-term success. articles.title: Yankees’ Aaron Boone says quiet part out loud after lackluster loss to Red Sox
articles.summary: NEW YORK– Saturday’s daytime portion of a doubleheader against the Boston Red Sox did not feature any real offensive production from the home team. The New York Yankees only recorded four hits as they suffered a 6-0 defeat to their division rival. Red Sox starter Jake Bennett tossed six sco
articles._body: NEW YORK– Saturday’s daytime portion of a doubleheader against the Boston Red Sox did not feature any real offensive production from the home team. The New York Yankees only recorded four hits as they suffered a 6-0 defeat to their division rival. Red Sox starter Jake Bennett tossed six scoreless innings and struck out seven batters en route to his ninth win of the campaign. Yankees manager Aaron Boone did not mince words after the game and acknowledged that his lineup has struggled to remain a consistent threat. “We’ve scored one run in two games, so we have to be better than that. Today we just were on the heels of a night where we didn’t score and played really well; we played poorly today. You know, simple as that,” Boone said. “So we’ve got to turn the page in a hurry here and go out and try and grab one of these doubleheader games today. But we need to play better, and part of that is offense.” Wilyer Abreu helped the Red Sox strike first when he launched a first-inning home run off Yankees southpaw Carlos Rodon, who lasted only 4.2 innings and permitted two runs and three hits while striking out five batters. New York had multiple chances to change the complexion of the contest. After Amed Rosario reached first on a throwing error in the fourth and advanced to second on a passed ball, Heliot Ramos belted a double just past center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela. Despite the extra-base hit, Rafaela and Boston’s defense recovered to complete a solid relay and gun down Rosario at the plate. “I think Rosie got stuck a little bit where it looked like he was going to scamper back and catch the ball, but got himself stuck in a position where his momentum wasn’t good, and with one out, we’ve got to be in a better position to score more seamlessly there,” Boone said. “It took two perfect throws. That’s a tough one in the moment.” Boston’s lineup earned another run in the fifth when catcher Ali Sanchez let a ball get behind him, and they proceeded to tally four more in the top of the ninth against Ryan Yarbrough. New York could not scratch across anything in the bottom half against Jovani Moran as it suffered its eighth shutout loss of the year. The Yankees and Red Sox are separated by less than three games in the American League Wild Card standings. With two games between them remaining and their season series separated by one game in the loss column, a tiebreaker would be decided by how the pair of contests shake out. articles._body: Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken is faced with important decisions regarding the team’s depth chart following Dillon Gabriel’s impressive performance in the preseason finale against the New England Patriots. The Browns concluded their exhibition schedule with a decisive 37-13 victory over New England, highlighted by an outstanding performance from second-year quarterback Dillon Gabriel. The former third-round pick completed 12 of 15 passes for 186 yards and threw three touchdowns without any turnovers. Both Gabriel and rookie dual-threat quarterback Taylen Green made strong cases to remain on the final 53-man roster. However, Monken noted, as reported by The Athletic’s Zac Jackson, that he and general manager Andrew Berry have yet to determine how many quarterbacks the team will ultimately carry behind their top passers. Navigating the challenges of trimming the roster down to 53 players reveals the difficult reality for coaches. Regarding the upcoming deadline for roster cuts, Monken expressed his empathy for the emotional toll it takes to release players who have dedicated themselves throughout training camp. News 5 Cleveland reporter Camryn Justice captured Monken’s candid remarks at the podium : “Asked about roster cutdowns due tomorrow, #Browns HC Todd Monken said, ‘It is hard to make those decisions and to let guys go, but it’s the nature of the beast. We can’t keep everybody. And I’ve been really proud of the way our guys have practiced since I got here.'” Monken emphasized that while making roster cuts can be painful, constructing a competitive and balanced team requires making difficult sacrifices across multiple deep position groups. In addition to finalizing the bottom of the roster, Monken has taken decisive control over the team’s most significant personnel decision at quarterback. Following the announcement that Deshaun Watson will start in Week 1 over rookie sensation Shedeur Sanders, longtime ESPN Cleveland insider Tony Grossi reported that Monken was solely responsible for that decision. Grossi suggested that if ownership had intervened, Sanders might have been the preferred choice due to his fan appeal, indicating that Monken has complete autonomy to make decisions based purely on football considerations. articles.title: UNC Overcomes Preseason Drama As Bill Belichick Earns Signature Win
articles.summary: Laszlo Geczo-Imagn Images
articles._body: As was the case a year ago, North Carolina began its 2026 season by scoring first against TCU. But this time, that wasn’t the only highlight for the Tar Heels in their season opener. UNC opened Year 2 of the Bill Belichick era in Dublin, Ireland, on Saturday, picking up an upset 15–10 victory over the Horned Frogs in the Aer Lingus College Football Classic. The Tar Heels’ victory stood in stark contrast to a year ago, when TCU beat UNC 48–14 in Belichick’s highly anticipated Chapel Hill debut. Starting the season 1-0 is no small feat for the Tar Heels, who entered the 2026 campaign with less buzz and more baggage than a year ago. Most notably, the program placed general manager Michael Lombardi on paid administrative leave in late July as the university investigated a personnel complaint against the longtime Belichick associate. Meanwhile, UNC defensive coordinator Steve Belichick—Bill’s son—has been out on medical leave since Aug. 6 and didn’t coach against TCU on Saturday. In his place, Bill Belichick himself took over defensive play-calling duties, the first time he’s called plays full-time since his final season with the Patriots in 2019. Yet despite the preseason distractions, the Tar Heels looked much improved from the UNC team that amassed a disappointing 4–8 record (2–6 in the ACC) during Belichick’s debut season in 2025. That’s not to say the Tar Heels are now a College Football Playoff—or even ACC—contender, or that the program’s unique NFL-centric approach has been validated. Still, the six-time Super Bowl champion head coach now has his first signature win at the college level. Among the encouraging signs for the Tar Heels on Saturday was the play of quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. under new UNC offensive coordinator Bobby Petrino. The Wisconsin transfer, who carries a nearly $1.3 million NIL valuation according to The NIL Standard database, threw for 232 yards against the Horned Frogs, more than any Tar Heels quarterback amassed in a single game last season. The UNC defense also looked vastly improved after ranking 66th nationally in points allowed per game in 2025. While some of the Horned Frogs’ struggles on Saturday were self-inflicted, the Tar Heels took advantage of their opportunities, limiting TCU to 281 total yards and 1-for-5 on fourth-down conversion attempts. But regardless of how they got there, it’s already easy to sense a newfound optimism surrounding the UNC program—especially considering that the win came in the national spotlight of the first FBS game of the 2026 season. The Tar Heels entered Saturday’s contest as a 9.5-point underdog at some sportsbooks, a point spread indicative of the public’s expectations (or lack thereof) for the 74-year-old Belichick’s second UNC season. Of course, it’s just one game and plenty can still change for a Tar Heels program that the ACC media voted to finish 15th out of 17 teams in its preseason poll . It’s also worth noting that the Lombardi situation remains unresolved and it remains to be seen when Steve Belichick will return as the team’s defensive coordinator. In other words, it’s far too early to point to Saturday’s win as evidence that UNC is now the NFL’s “33rd team ,” as Lombardi once dubbed it in an effort to distinguish the Tar Heels as a pro-level program. But should Saturday’s victory be a sign of things to come for UNC, the Tar Heels’ success would undoubtedly become one of the biggest storylines of the college football season. That would, in turn, have significant implications for the ACC’s primary media rights holder, ESPN, as well as the program’s own NIL efforts. With a game against East Tennessee State on Sept. 12 to follow UNC’s upcoming bye week, a 2–0 start to the 2026 season appears to be all but a foregone conclusion in Chapel Hill. That could also set up a high-profile matchup against ACC rival Clemson on Sept. 19, as Belichick tries to make good on the buzz that accompanied his move to the college level a year ago. The post UNC Overcomes Preseason Drama As Bill Belichick Earns Signature Win appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles._body: The adidas Handball Spezial loafer has gone viral on social media for being essentially the perfect sneaker-loafer (as it should). The brand just made its killer dress shoe even better. adidas has introduced two new exclusive colorways for its Handball Spezial Loafer, which transform the model into an even more dressy flex. The newest pairs feature grainy leather uppers and suede Stripes, all dressed in either all-black or chocolate brown schemes. It's not just that they're classic color options, but the colorways themselves really bring out the classy textures of the new adidas loafer. We've seen the dressy Handball Spezial model in buttery leather and smooth suede before. This pair flexes both in an absurdly luxe manner. adidas' Handball Spezial loafer debuted earlier this year, but it wasn't until this summer that the world realized the brand had a seriously good sneaker-loafer on its hands. And that's the thing: the Handball Spezial is honestly more loafer than sneaker. It's really a sporty dress shoe with rubber soles and Three Stripes. It sounds like a crazy combination, but the Handball Spezial loafer pulls it off with ease. It helps that adidas has kept the model looking quite sharp with many stylish options, including animal-print designs and classic leather renditions. And adidas continues to perfect its already good loafer. Now, it's getting two more nice colorways, which are currently up for grabs on Billy's website for ¥17,600, or around $110. articles.title: Nike’s Red-Hot Air Force 1 Is Wearable Hip-Hop History
articles.summary: The Terror Squad x Nike Air Force 1 Low sneaker finally releases in the classic red & white colorways. Here's how to cop this piece of wearable hip-hop history.
articles._body: It's wild to think the Terror Squad x Nike Air Force 1s were among the rarest sneakers in the world at one point. Now, Fat Joe and Nike are making grail dreams come true with wider releases. They already blessed the streets with two drops back in 2023. Now, they've returned to release the red Terror Squad x Nike Air Force 1 sneakers. Expect the usual AF1 details, this time dressed in red and white leather and, of course, those unmistakable Terror Squad stamps. There's an embroidered "TS" on the heel, referencing the hip-hop group founded by Fat Joe in the late 1990s. Meanwhile, "JC" strikes the heel tab, calling back to the musician's nickname, Joey Crack. The first wave of Terror Squad Air Forces came out in the early 2000s, but they were limited to Fat Joe and his crew. Essentially, they were mega-exclusive "Friends and Family" shoes that fetched thousands on resale sites and even famous auctions . Fat Joe is a well-documented sneakerhead, known not only for possessing an insane collection but also for licking the soles of brand-new sneakers on camera. He's flexed just about every new hot release, ranging from Nigel Sylvester's Air Jordan 4s to Kith's Air Max 95s to, naturally, his very own Air Forces, which he calls "the greatest story never told." See, the Terror Squad Forces aren't just wearable sneaker history but a hip-hop legacy you can lace up in. The brands are making the once-rare sneakers available to everyone now. Well, those who can successfully cop them, that is. Again, Nike and Fat released two Terror Squad x Air Force 1s, which sold out. We're expecting the same outcome for the red-hot pairs. Mark your calendars and set your alarms. The red Terror Squad x Nike Air Force 1 sneakers are slated to finally release on September 9 on Nike's website, retailing for $150. Now TIED for the lead.” With that last birdie, McIlroy completed a big comeback. Instead of trailing by several shots, he is now right at the top of the leaderboard. The atmosphere around East Lake has become electric as spectators watch his charge unfold. Meanwhile, many hope to witness a memorable finish. McIlroy started the tournament six shots behind Min Woo Lee, who shot an impressive 8-under 62. Catching up to the leader After struggling to get going in the first round, McIlroy’s strong second round stands out even more. Furthermore, his improved rhythm and accuracy have made a clear difference. McIlroy’s bold play has worked, as he keeps giving himself chances to score. Moreover, his run of birdies has helped him catch up fast and put pressure on the other players. As the leaderboard gets closer, McIlroy is back in the hunt for the Tour Championship. If he keeps making birdies like this, his comeback could be one of the tournament’s biggest stories. Ultimately, his determination may pay off. The final holes will be crucial. All eyes are on McIlroy as he attempts to secure another major victory and add to his already impressive career. articles.title: Cale Makar, Avalanche grades for record-breaking $163.2 million contract extension
articles.summary: Cale Makar has been bringing fans out of their seats since he made his debut with the Colorado Avalanche in the 2019-20 season. He looked like a boy scout stepping onto the ice, but that timid look quickly gave way to that of a game-changing superstar. All it took was a few strides for NHL [̷
articles._body: Cale Makar has been bringing fans out of their seats since he made his debut with the Colorado Avalanche in the 2019-20 season . He looked like a boy scout stepping onto the ice, but that timid look quickly gave way to that of a game-changing superstar. All it took was a few strides for NHL observers to realize they were looking at an elite skater, a player who could dominate with the puck on his stick and turn the game in the Avalanche’s favor in a matter of moments. Makar has played seven seasons with the Avs, and he quickly became the best defenseman in the NHL. He has the ability to dominate the game with his skating, stickhandling, playmaking and shooting. This is a wonderful era for NHL defensemen with Quinn Hughes, Zach Werenski, Miro Heiskanen, Lane Hutson and Charley McAvoy — to name just a few. Makar has the edge on all of them, particularly when it comes to turning it up a gear or two and providing the extra speed when it is needed. That is why the Avalanche have made him the highest paid player in the sport, giving him an eight-year contract extension that will pay him $163.2 million . His average salary is $20.4 million and that is also the top number in the league. He passed Kirill Kaprizov of the Minnesota Wild to become the highest paid player in the league. Perhaps Quinn Hughes of the Wild can approach the salary that Makar just signed for as he prepares for his next contract, but Makar is the better player and he deserves more. Some may say that Connor McDavid is the best player in the league and he should eventually get a contract that pays more than the Avs defenseman, but that may be a year or two away. Makar ranks with many of the NHL’s all-time best blue liners Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images As long as Makar stays healthy, he will be the top defenseman in the NHL and he will rank with the best defensemen who have ever played the game. The names are familiar: Nicklas Lidstrom, Ray Bourque, Denis Potvin, Paul Coffey, Larry Robinson, Chris Pronger, Brad Park and Doug Harvey. The belief is that Makar has a chance to be equal to or better than all of them. The only name he won’t be able to exceed is the legendary Bobby Orr, the Bruins defenseman who changed the game and regularly challenges Wayne Gretzky in the on-going debate concerning the greatest player in NHL history. Makar showed off his offensive skill in his first year when he scored 12 goals and 38 assists for 50 points while playing 57 games. He was limited to 44 games in his second year — he averaged a point a game — but outdistanced the competition in his third season. Makar had a remarkable 2021-22 season with 28 goals and 58 assists for 86 points. However, the other notable numbers were his 9 power play goals that season and his remarkable plus-48 rating. That figure helped bring about some of the comparisons to the best defensemen in league history and was comparable to Orr and Robinson’s performances. Since then, Makar had a 90-point season in 2023-24 and a 92-point season in 2024-25. He has the ability to dominate play every time he is on the ice, and he creates pressure when he is on the bench between shifts. Opposing teams know they must produce when Makar is resting because they know he is likely to have the puck on his stick during the 25-plus minutes he is on the ice. Makar wants to help Avs to bring home multiple Stanley Cups There are similarities to the way Makar and Orr have played and also interact with their teammates. Makar does not look for the accolades or demand the recognition he has earned to this point. He only wants to help the Avs win championships. That certainly was the case in 2022, when the powerful Avs won their third Stanley Cup in team history and Makar won the Conn Smythe Award as the playoff MVP with 8 goals and 21 assists for 29 points while averaging more than 27 minutes per game. The Avs had a pair of 4-game sweeps over the Nashville Predators in the opening round and the Edmonton Oilers in the Western Conference Final. They needed six games to get by the St. Louis Blue in the second round and six games to win the Stanley Cup over the back-to-back champion Tampa Bay Lightning. Makar had 3 goals and 4 assists in the championship series. While he did not score in the sixth and decisive game, he played sensational defense and was on the ice for more than 24 minutes in that game before he had a chance to skate around the ice with the Stanley Cup. Makar has not been able to lift the Stanley Cup since, but the 27-year-old is in the prime of his career, and he should have multiple opportunities to help his team win additional titles. Any team with Mark, Nathan MacKinnon, Martin Necas, Brock Nelson and Devon Toews should always have a shot at bringing home hockey’s elite chalice. The Av have paid full price for the best defenseman in the game. He may be the best overall player, and they deserve a grade of A for making sure that Makar will be with the team for another eight seasons. Bubba Wallace issues ominous warning about new NASCAR Daytona package: ‘I really hope it’s not a debacle’
articles.summary: Bubba Wallace warns NASCAR could “look really bad” if its new Daytona superspeedway package turns into a debacle without any practice.
articles._body: Count Bubba Wallace among those who have more questions than answers about the superspeedway package installed by NASCAR entering tonight’s Coke Zero Sugar 400 at Daytona. He has one sincere hope: it’s not a debacle. On Friday evening, Wallace covered several topics with the media . One thing kept coming back around: how will the cars react when the green flag waves? Wallace: ‘I really hope it’s not a debacle’ With no practice allowed by NASCAR this week, and the package in place, everyone has questions.  Wallace, who currently sits in 14th in the points entering this regular season finale before the Chase, hopes NASCAR doesn’t face scrutiny after the checkered flag waves.  “I think it’s whoever’s aero group did the best research, and think we brought the best package,” said Wallace. “I don’t know, I really hope it’s not a debacle, because it’s gonna look really bad that we didn’t get practice with something so drastic, if it is a debacle.” Pressed on what would be considered ‘a debacle,’ Wallace painted the worst-case scenario. “We all just go in a crash lap one, because we can’t drive these things. We don’t know what it’s gonna drive like. You cannot tell anything from qualifying. “So before we start asking those questions, this is apples to oranges. So I hope it goes well for that sake.  “It’s gonna be a long week of press coverage if it’s not.” Wallace is hoping for ‘Atlanta-esque’ racing Who wouldn’t love Atlanta-like racing at Daytona? Wallace was asked what he thought NASCAR’s intentions are with the rules package change on superspeedways. “I mean, I’m not exactly sure what they’re trying to chase,” said Wallace. “Maybe like an Atlanta-esque, right? But I don’t know.  “I mean, in the 500, we were riding around quarter throttle, controlling the race, and not doing much. So get away from that, get away from the fuel-saving stuff, get it to where you can create runs and make passes while you’re driving hard.  “We’ll see. I think the intent’s there.” How to watch the Coke Zero Sugar 400 On Saturday, August 29th, NASCAR makes its return to Daytona International Speedway for the Coke Zero Sugar 400. This will be the fourth race on USA Sports, which will carry NASCAR coverage through the end of the season.  The race begins at 7:30 p.m. ET.  It will be televised on NBC, while carrying the USA Sports branding.  And it’s the final race of the regular season before the start of the Chase.  When the checkered flag waves, the field of 16 drivers for the NASCAR postseason will be set.  It will also be the first race using the new superspeedway rules package .   “The rear spoiler will be shortened from 7 inches to 4 inches, the same height as intermediate tracks, in an effort to reduce drag, along with a slight reduction in horsepower from 510 to 465 to adjust for the reduced downforce,” wrote Zach Sturniolo on NASCAR.com. “NASCAR officials anticipate single-car runs to be approximately 3 mph faster than the current package, but cars in a pack are expected to run about the same speeds.” A brief breakdown of the rules package and the expectations: Superspeedway Package Update: 14” spoiler and wide splitter stuffers (same as intermediate) Safety equipment remains the same as current SSW Engine tapered spacer reduced to 27/32” ~ 465 HP New spoiler braces Spoiler deflection device redesigned to accommodate 4” spoiler Performance Aspects: Single-car speeds estimated at 2-3 mph faster than current qualifying. Maximum pack speeds estimated in the same range as current. Dynamic passing maneuver CFD indicates completion of a pass with a 5-mph run is more likely with new package. Expect fireworks on and off the track at Daytona.

articles.title: Terrion Arnold to be placed on commissioner’s exempt list after Seahawks signing
articles.summary: With the Seattle Seahawks preparing for the start of the 2026 season, the focus around the team now centers on the signing of cornerback Terrion Arnold. As the Seahawks are signing Arnold, despite his recent arrest on kidnapping and robbery charges, the NFL has made an expected move with the play
articles._body: With the Seattle Seahawks preparing for the start of the 2026 season , the focus around the team now centers on the signing of cornerback Terrion Arnold. As the Seahawks are signing Arnold , despite his recent arrest on kidnapping and robbery charges, the NFL has made an expected move with the player. According to NFL insider Adam Schefter of ESPN, the league is placing Arnold on the “commissioner’s exempt list” as soon as they get his contract. “New Seahawks CB Terrion Arnold will be placed on the commissioner’s exempt list once the league receives his contract, per the NFL,” Schefter wrote on X, formerly Twitter. More on the Seahawks signing Terrion Arnold As mentioned, this move was expected, as the move for Seattle to sign Arnold was a process to be had, as NFL insider Ian Rapoport said on Aug. 18 that the Seahawks are “still planning to sign” the 23-year-old. “The Seahawks are still planning to sign CB Terrion Arnold but are working through the timing, and it will take a while, sources tell me and [Mike Garafolo],” Rapoport wrote on X, formerly Twitter. “Arnold will be placed on the commissioner’s exempt list when he signs, meaning he’d be ineligible to play or practice.” With the signing made official on Saturday, it remains to be seen what will happen in the future with Arnold, as being put on the commissioner’s exempt list means he can’t practice or play with the team, though he’ll still be paid and can attend team meetings , via The Athletic. The incident with Arnold was in February, and he was arrested in June, leading to the Detroit Lions cutting him shortly after; now Seattle is waiting to see what Arnold’s punishment will be, as a potential sentence could be life in prison. Why TCU football’s Sonny Dykes must be on hot seat after brutal loss to North Carolina
articles.summary: TCU football absorbed the first upset of the 2026 college football season in falling to North Carolina. The loss to Bill Belichick and company comes one year after the Horned Frogs thrashed his Tar Heels. And now, looks like Sonny Dykes is sitting on the hotter seat compared to Belichick. One TCU
articles._body: TCU football absorbed the first upset of the 2026 college football season in falling to North Carolina . The loss to Bill Belichick and company comes one year after the Horned Frogs thrashed his Tar Heels. And now, looks like Sonny Dykes is sitting on the hotter seat compared to Belichick. One TCU alumnus in King 5 Seattle sports anchor Dusty Baker is one already believing the temperature’s hot for Dykes. But there are external factors that now force the belief that Dykes could get removed sooner than expected. Loss adds to tumultuous week for TCU The Horned Frogs traveled to Dublin, Ireland revoking the credentials of one beat reporter. Steven M. Johnson from the Fort Worth Star-Telegram had his access removed. TCU’s decision stemmed from the fallout behind former safety Jacob Fields getting kicked off the team for a locker room assault on a teammate. That assault victim Dozie Ezukanma later posted an Instagram video detailing the account , which Johnson reported on. Looks like both rose as major distractions for Dykes and TCU. Many local and even national reporters took the side of Johnson. So that applied pressure on Dykes and TCU to reconsider their ban on the reporter. Both Fields’ actions, followed by the treatment handed to the TCU beat reporter, carried into TCU’s overseas road trip. Clearly both rose as a distraction. But this mess falls on Dykes’ hands. The veteran head coach never did a thorough job of navigating through the distractions and now, TCU may have internal problems. TCU loses to an underachieving foe The counterargument of facing Belichick gets ruled out here. Yes the coach won six Super Bowls in the NFL and brought a Hall of Fame resume to Ireland. But Belichick entered fresh off a disastrous CFB start and dealt with his own distraction: General manager Michael Lombardi going on administrative leave. Many wondered if Belichick himself would feel distracted. Turns out he was more locked in compared to Dykes. Schedule gets tougher from here TCU lightens up with Grambling State and Arkansas State next. Then UCF in the Big 12 opener, so there’s a chance they can get to 3-1. But BYU arrives as the home conference opener. The Arizona, Utah and Texas Tech close out the regular season. Dykes must get TCU to 9-3 to save his job. An 8-4 finish or worse may not guarantee job security here, especially with Dykes dealing with new distractions. articles.title: ‘The Asylum’ Gets an Upgrade: Miami Hurricanes To Unveil New Hard Rock Stadium Game-Day Features In 2026
articles.summary: The Miami Hurricanes open on the road this season, but the Event Experience team at The U is hard at work getting ready to put on a show September 10 when Miami returns home to play Florida A&M under the lights.
articles._body: The Miami Hurricanes open on the road this season, but the Event Experience team at The U is hard at work getting ready to put on a show September 10 when Miami returns home to play Florida A&M under the lights. A new DJ host. A Band that has grown 50% in size. A revamped pre-game with a newer, grander entrance for Sebastian’s run-out moment, a new fan participation chant and the return of the Canes Siren. An expanded stadium light package. Special Fan Mobile Phone light shows that will be controlled by QR codes on the scoreboards. It’s  an understatement to say that Game Days at Hard Rock Stadium this season are being amped up. “Our goal is for our stadium to be one of the toughest environments in the country for visiting teams to come play. We want them to dread it,” said Rob Roselli, Miami’s Associate AD for Marketing and Event Experience. “To get there, it takes everyone – the team, the fans, the production staff, the student section, the band all buying in and doing their part, adopting the mindset of `I can impact this game with my voice.’ “When 65,000 people do that, we’ll be an unstoppable force. We know our fans already have a swagger and a chip on their shoulder, and we expect to see that carry into the noise level this season, especially coming off of last season’s run. Let’s just say I wouldn’t want to be an opposing quarterback or offensive lineman coming to Hard Rock Stadium this season.” Miami DJ M Dot The new hype man will be M-DOT, who some may be familiar with from Miami Heat games where he serves as the DJ and Hype Man. He will take charge of crowd pump-ups, full stadium chants, and handle in-venue MC/hosting with his infectious energy, big booming voice and swagger.  M Dot, whose real name is Michael Hankerson, has been a South Florida sports event fixture for a long time. He launched his career  back in 2007 as the official DJ for the Florida Marlins and joined the Miami Heat in 2008 and replaced DJ Irie as the team’s official DJ in 2020. He also has worked with FIU football and basketball. Beyond the arena, M Dot has toured with platinum-selling artists including Jamie Foxx and Grammy Award-winner Kelly Rowland. He is deeply committed to giving back and supports organizations such as the Leukemia and Lymphoma Society, Big Brothers Big Sisters of Miami, and the Overtown Youth Center. In 2024, he founded the Dotted Line Foundation, a nonprofit empowering underserved communities through music education, health and wellness, and mentorship. His community impact earned him the Miami-Dade Public Schools Alumni Achievement Award in 2025, honoring his dedication to inspiring the next generation. Roselli keeps pushing to max out the team entrance onto the field. A huge focus has gone into the band pre-game show all the way to increasing the size of the band, which has been a bit of a liability for many years. Frost Band of The Hour Leadership Craig McKenzie, Sheldon McLean and Charles Damon have been working tirelessly to grow the band in size, travelling the country to attend various recruitment events. The band will grow about 50% in size this season. “They will be bigger, louder and rowdier,” Roselli said. The enhanced pre-game show will feature new elements intending to build the hype to a climax right before the team enters the field. Fans can expect to see the addition of an official Sebastian entrance/run-out moment, the addition of a full stadium crowd participation chant and more. Fans are being asked to leave their tailgates a few minutes earlier and be in their seats for the team entrance into the stadium. Lighting inside stadiums has been a big focus around the country the past few years to enhance the game day environment. This year, Miami is bringing in spotlights and additional uplighting that will allow Roselli’s team to transform the environment at Hard Rock Stadium. They will be able to spotlight special elements during the pre-game show and during timeouts such as mascot spellouts, the team run-out, special ceremonies and more. During fun or hype moments, they will be able to program the lights in a way that they enhance the vibe inside the stadium to create a big event, Miami flair. Phone Light Shows have become a staple around the country and Miami is adding a special phone light show. Fans will be able to scan a QR code on the videoboard, which will take them right into the light show. The phone lights will then be programmed for the now-famous Michael Irvin 4 th  quarter video, followed by Thunderstruck, creating an electric environment for that moment. The Ringing of The Hurricane Siren was unveiled last season. This year, it’s back. The celebrity Siren Ringers will be announced a couple days before each home game this year. “We think fans are going to be really excited about the first ringer, or in this case, should I say `ringers,’” Roselli said. “We are so excited to see the passion and energy our fans will bring to the stadium this year. “Last year was awesome, and “The Asylum” was officially born. The Notre Dame and Florida crowds were two of the louder crowds I’ve ever heard in my career in sports. We’ve all heard the stories of the legendary crowds at The Orange Bowl, and we’re pumped to continue to see that energy and rowdiness continue to make its way into Hard Rock Stadium.”

articles._body: Former Detroit Lions cornerback Terrion Arnold has officially signed with the Seattle Seahawks, according to a report from ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter . The move has been reported as likely for weeks. Schefter also reports that the former Detroit cornerback will be placed on the commissioner’s exempt list once the league receives his contract. The commissioner’s exempt list allows a player not to count against the 53-man roster limit due to special circumstances. [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] Arnold was released by the Lions this offseason after he was arrested on felony charges in connection with an incident in February. Arnold has strongly denied the charges against him through his management team. “Terrion Arnold categorically denies any involvement in the matters underlying the allegations made against him and maintains his innocence,” a statement from Arnold’s management group read. “There is no credible evidence linking Mr. Arnold to these allegations. “Instead, the government appears to be relying on testimony from multiple convicted felons who have admitted their own involvement and may have substantial incentives to shift blame in an effort to lessen their sentences. Mr. Arnold looks forward to his day in court and is confident that the judicial process will lead to his ultimate vindication.” Terrior Arnold visited multiple NFL teams as he looked for a new home following his release. He visited with the New Orleans Saints, New York Giants and Houston Texans, in addition to the Seahawks. Eventually, Seattle made the decision to bring him in. Arnold is coming off a season in which he saw action in eight games, recording 31 tackles, eight passes defended and one interception. He was a first-round NFL Draft pick by the Lions in 2024. More on Terrion Arnold’s arrest Terrion Arnold was arrested in June in connection with a February robbery and kidnapping in Florida. He was charged with kidnapping and armed robbery, the Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Department announced, although he denied the allegations after turning himself in to police. Arnold was granted bond after a court hearing in which the judge said the former Alabama star was able to leave his residence for work, including practices and games. He added he did not want to interfere with Arnold’s ability to earn a living, which led to the decision. However, shortly thereafter, the Lions announced his release. Arnold’s name appeared in a court order in February, which had details of an alleged armed robbery and kidnapping that took place in Tampa. In the order, Judge J. Logan Murphy granted a motion from the state for a pre-trial detention against Boakai Hilton . Hilton allegedly planned a kidnapping and robberies while riding in a car with Arnold as part of a retaliation for two robberies, the Detroit News reported at the time. The alleged incidents occurred at Arnold’s rental home in Largo, Fla. On3’s Nick Schultz also contributed to this report.

articles.title: This isn’t your Grandma’s Band of the Hour: New look band ready for a innovative season
articles.summary: The Band of the Hour is taking on a fresh look this season
articles._body: As respectfully as I can say this, I remember attending Miami Hurricanes games as a kid at the Orange Bowl. When halftime approached and the Band of the Hour was preparing to take the field, I remember asking my parents a question that probably tells you everything you need to know: “Is halftime an hour?” Because, as a kid, it genuinely felt like it. Again, I say that as respectfully as possible. The band was a tradition, but I never really felt like it represented  me  or the Miami I knew. Growing up in South Florida, Miami had a sound. It had a personality. It had swagger. It was a melting pot of cultures, neighborhoods and musical influences. And whenever bands from Historically Black Colleges and Universities—like Florida A&M or Bethune-Cookman—came to town with their football teams to play Miami, I would watch them and wonder: “Why doesn’t our band sound like that?” Why didn’t the University of Miami’s band have that same energy? That same movement? That same connection to the culture surrounding the university? Fast-forward to early August 2026. The Frost Band of the Hour released a video on Instagram, and I was stunned. This wasn’t the band I remembered. There was  swag. There was  energy. There was  movement. And most importantly, there was a sound that felt current. It was  dope. So naturally, I made a video responding to what I saw. And something happened that I didn’t expect. Band members and faculty started flocking to my page, inviting me to come check them out at  Preview the U. So I did. And what I saw in person confirmed everything I had seen on Instagram. The band played with energy and enthusiasm. But it wasn’t just the execution that caught my attention. It was the  identity. I heard Richmond Heights. I heard Hialeah. I heard the neighborhoods, cultures and communities that make Miami what it is. The melting pot that is Miami was reflected in the arrangements. And the band wasn’t afraid to have fun. They seamlessly transitioned from traditional pieces into Drake’s  “Nokia.” There were smiles. There was dancing. There was personality. And before long, that energy wasn’t just coming from the band—it was spreading through the audience. It was infectious. After the performance, I had the opportunity to catch up with Associate Director Dr. Craig McKenzie and Dr. Sheldon McLean. And what they told me helped put everything I had just witnessed into perspective. They said that one of their goals was to infuse the personality of the  City of Miami  into the Frost Band of the Hour. Because, in their view, something was missing. Miami was missing. And they made it their purpose to change that. That resonated with me because that’s exactly what I felt as a kid sitting in the Orange Bowl. The issue wasn’t that the band needed to abandon its tradition. It was that the tradition needed to evolve in a way that reflected the community it represented. Because Miami isn’t one sound. It’s Little Haiti. It’s Hialeah. It’s Overtown. It’s Liberty City. It’s Richmond Heights. It’s Caribbean culture, Latin culture, Black culture, immigrant culture and generations of people who have all contributed something to the city’s identity. It’s old school and new school. It’s tradition and innovation. And now, maybe, it’s the sound coming from the Frost Band of the Hour. What I saw at  Preview the U  wasn’t simply a band performing halftime entertainment. I saw a band stepping into its identity. And for the first time, I looked at the Band of the Hour and thought: “I hope their performance lasts an hour.”

2027 NFL Draft offensive line rankings: Top 10 before 2026 college football season
articles.summary: The 2026 college football season is upon us, with Week 0 kicking off Saturday. For pro football fans, that means getting our next looks at the prospects who will enter the 2027 NFL Draft. You know about Arch Manning and the quarterbacks, Jeremiah Smith and the wide receivers, and maybe even Colin
articles._body: The 2026 college football season is upon us, with Week 0 kicking off Saturday. For pro football fans, that means getting our next looks at the prospects who will enter the 2027 NFL Draf t. You know about Arch Manning and the quarterbacks, Jeremiah Smith and the wide receivers, and maybe even Colin Simmons and the pass rushers. However, there will be just as many (if not more) offensive linemen in Round 1 as any of these other positions, so let’s look at the top-10 2027 NFL Draft offensive line rankings as it stands right now. 1. OT Trevor Goosby, Texas Longhorns left tackle Trevor Goosby looks like an NFL bookend at 6-foot-7, 312 pounds. He considered coming out in 2026, but decided to go back for another year to protect Arch Manning’s blindside. Scouts will love that, as the biggest knock on him last draft was that he was inecpereinced as a starter. And despite that, he would have been a first-round pick anyway. Goosby should be the first tackle off the board and a likely top-10 , if not top-five, pick, depending on how many elite quarterbacks come out in the 2027 NFL Draft. 2. OT Jordan Seaton, LSU Jordan Seaton is making a jump in competition this season, moving from Colorado in the Big 12 to LSU in the SEC. The 6-foot-5, 311-pound Seaton has been a top tackle since high school. He was a five-star recruit, a two-year starter for Deion Sanders, and now a highly-regarded transfer to one of the best teams in college football this season. Right now, it does seem like Seaton is slightly behind Goosby for the No. 1 offensive lineman in the 2027 NFL Draft, but a dominant season for the Bayou Bengals, and there’s a real chance he vaults ahead of the Texas LT. 3. OT Cayden Green, Missouri Gossby and Seaton are NFL-ready left tackles, so they should come off the board first. After that, we get into the college/pro G/T tweeners, who aren’t quite as valuable, but can still become NFL stars. Whether these players stay at left tackle, flip to the right side, or move inside to guard, they can be key players on winning teams. Cayden Green has played guard and tackle in college, and that versatility alone is valuable. His best fit may be inside in the NFL, but he’s an incredible pass blocker, an emerging run blocker at 6-foot-5, 324 pounds, and will be a Week 1 starter on someone’s offensive line in 2027. 4. OT Niki Prongos, Stanford Stanford tackle Niki Prongos was a basketball player in high school who started playing football in his senior year. But his 6-foot-7, 311-pound frame and basketball athleticism have NFL scouts drooling. It would be nice if he showed a little more polish in this upcoming college football season, but even if he doesn’t, his size and skill will remind people of 2026 21st overall pick Max Iheanachor. 5. OT Trevor Lauk, Iowa Trevor Lauck is 6-foot-5, 310 pounds, and compares favorably to NFL starters like Grey Zabel and Graham Barton. Like those two players, he will also slide inside to guard in the pros, but having that tackle background can help a team construct an offensive line and deal with injury situations as they come up throughout the season. It would be nice if Lauck got a little stronger this season, but either way, he should be a mid-first-round pick in 2027. And there is a chance he could be as high as the third offensive tackle off the board. That said, he could also slip to six or seven, depending on how the next opponent looks. 6. OT Carter Smith, Indiana Indiana’s Carter Smith has a championship pedigree now and will have another valuable year of experience after flirting with the 2026 NFL Draft. He does have the dreaded short arms label, so the combine will be crucial. But Smith is obviously an NFL-caliber lineman, so no matter how his arms measure, a team should take him with the right plan and watch him make Pro Bowls. 7. C Kade Pieper, Iowa Is Kade Pieper a guard or is he a center? He’s shown he can be a standout right guard, but most Hawkeyes observers thought he would replace Logan Jones this year. That may not be the case, though , as the Iowa line is not quite set ahead of their opener. No matter where Pieper ends up, he will be an All-American and a likely late first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. That said, he will have a little more positional value if he can play center or guard at the next level. If he loses the center battle at Iowa this season, he may “just” be a guard. 8. OG Greg Johnson, Minnesota At 6-foot-6, 330 pounds, Greg Johnson has played tackle and guard for the Golden Gophers, and looks like a perfect big guard in the league. Johnson can even play center in a pinch, which gives him even more value. He may not quite fit into the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft, but right now, he should be a high second-rounder at worst. 9. OT P.J. Williams, SMU P.J. Williams may not be as exciting as some of the other players on this 2027 NFL Draft offensive line rankings list, but he is just incredibly experienced and solid. He started his college career as a defensive lineman, but morphed into a longtime starter and captain on the line. His best position is at right tackle, so for a team that needs an RT and doesn’t want to gamble on an LT making the switch, Williams could be a perfect fit. 10. OT Lance Heard, Kentucky This LSU transfer is 6-foot-6, 330 pounds, and can move like a man much smaller. Lance Heard doesn’t have a ton of experience, but he has all the tools and traits to become an NFL LT. This year will be big for him, as he stays in the SEC but moves to Kentucky, where he will be the man at left tackle instead of the guy forced out of position by Seaton. Heard is just too big, strong, and fluid to pass up, but to stay at No. 10 or even move up this season, he needs to play well. articles._body: The North Carolina Tar Heels earned a 15-10 Week 0 win over the TCU Horned Frogs on Saturday, marking the program’s first win of the new season. It was a big victory, as it’s the first step for Bill Belichick and his team to leave the ugly 2025-26 campaign in the rearview mirror. Nearly the entire college football world shared their reaction to the win on social media. Many patted Belichick on the back, giving the 74-year-old head coach credit for leading North Carolina to an upset win over TCU. “Honestly, good for Bill Belichick. Young fella just needed a year in college football to get his feet wet. Hopefully he will have a long and storied CFB career,” Brandon Walker of Barstool Sports said. Josh Pate claimed , “Bill Belichick is ACC COY right now.” “And just like that, Bill Belichick has flipped college football on its head,” Will Compton stated . Bill Belichick emotion! pic.twitter.com/O75pIqp8yj — Ross Martin (@RossMartinNC) August 29, 2026 Nicole Auberback said , “Bill Belichick gets the win over TCU in Ireland. That was not always pretty, but that’s a big win for UNC.” “Some really aggressive Belichick takes out there probably needed to be walked back this week. They’re much improved and well coached. Having said that…TCU, woof,” Dan Wolken explained . Michael Casagrande asked , “Bill Belichick might have figured out how to coach college football? A bad day [for] the rest of college football?” Winning completely changes any narrative, especially in college football. This might be a completely different Tar Heels team this year, as North Carolina appeared to be the better team against TCU throughout. Belichick and his Tar Heels will get a bye week for Week 1. They’ll return in Week 2 when North Carolina takes on the East Tennessee State Buccaneers for the season opener.
