articles.title: Kentucky is prepared for fair catch kick rule in 2026
articles.summary: An interesting rule is coming to college football.
articles._body: Some significant kicking game changes are coming to college football in 2026. The new punt rules will be felt early when games begin in Week Zero. Another rule change might not occur very often but it could swing a game or two down the road. The fair catch kick rule is coming to college football . What does that mean? Let KSR explain. This new rule will allow a receiving team on punt or kickoff to attempt an uncontested field goal attempt and add three points to the board. The team will align in a kickoff formation when this is declared. The other team can line up to receive and return the ball but points are added to the scoreboard if the football splits the uprights. That is the basic explanation. Let’s break it down into more detail. This selection for a Fair Catch Kick must come from the head coach before the dead ball is put into play and spotted. The decision is irrevocable. Penalty yards do count if there is a pass catch interference, illegal formation, etc. by the kicking team. The ball is spotted after the penalty yards and that is where the offense will attempt the fair catch kick. The ball will automatically be marked on the hash mark if the fair catch occurs outside the hash. There will be a play clock like normal. This free kick must occur before that expires. The defense must align 10 yards away from the kick just like a normal kickoff play. A holder with no tee is required on a fair catch kick. If the kick is unsuccessful, then kickoff rules are immediately put into place. There could be a touchback, return, or fair catch by the receiving team. If the free kick is unsuccessful and not touched by the return team, the other team will then get the ball at the previous spot which is the location of the free kick. This is not a rule that will occur very often. You will only seen this done at the end of the first half or second half. Whenever there is not enough time for a play, teams can select this free kick option to attempt to steal points. It was used in the NFL last year by the Los Angeles Chargers in a Thursday Night Football game against the Denver Broncos. It could now swing a college football game. Kentucky is ready for it. We have it prepared because it’s an opportunity to take advantage of the rules, get three points. But that’s a unique one, too. It happened in the NFL, happens in high school, and so now we got it,” Kentucky special teams coordinator Parker Fleming said.

articles.title: Reds slugger Sal Stewart can’t stop strengthening Rookie of the Year case
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Reds watched rookie slugger Sal Stewart strengthen his National League Rookie of the Year case Saturday with his 30th home run of the season. His two-run homer against Chicago Cubs starter Kevin Gausman raised his RBI total to 104. Elly De La Cruz scored on the third-inning drive,
articles._body: The Cincinnati Reds watched rookie slugger Sal Stewart strengthen his National League Rookie of the Year case Saturday with his 30th home run of the season. His two-run homer against Chicago Cubs starter Kevin Gausman raised his RBI total to 104. Elly De La Cruz scored on the third-inning drive, cutting Chicago’s lead to 6-4. The Cubs currently lead 7-5 in the bottom of the fifth at Wrigley Field. Stewart entered Saturday as baseball’s RBI leader. The homer also extended the franchise rookie RBI record he established during Friday’s series opener at Wrigley Field. Barstool Baseball took to its official X account, formerly Twitter, and posted the clip of Stewart’s latest blast . “Sal Stewart is coming for that Rookie of the Year” Sal Stewart is coming for that Rookie of the Year pic.twitter.com/gy81IxvROb — Barstool Baseball (@StoolBaseball) August 29, 2026 MLB.com’s Sarah Langs followed up minutes later on the platform with a post providing historical context behind the rookie slugger’s latest milestone. “Sal Stewart is the 14th rookie in MLB history with 30+ homers and 100+ RBI in a season the 9 previous players to do it since the rookie of the year award began (1947) all won it” Stewart became the 14th rookie in MLB history to produce 30 homers and 100 RBIs in one season. He is the first Reds rookie to reach both marks. The 22-year-old turned on an 84.2 mph splitter from Gausman. The drive traveled a projected 431 feet to left-center field with a 105.9 mph exit velocity and 28-degree launch angle. Stewart hit his 29th homer Friday before adding an RBI single that moved him past Jim Greengrass for Cincinnati’s modern rookie RBI record. The Reds won the series opener 10-8. Frank Robinson, who hit 38 homers in 1956, remains the only Cincinnati rookie with more home runs in one season. Stewart has already surpassed Joey Votto’s 24-homer rookie total. The historical pattern does not determine the award. However, Stewart’s power, major league-leading run production , and growing collection of franchise records continue strengthening his Rookie of the Year candidacy. articles.title: ‘It’s pretty wild’ … FSU’s Duce Robinson squares off with best friend Myles Libman for 3rd time
articles.summary: Childhood friends Duce Robinson and Myles Libman will play against each other for the third time in college when Florida State hosts New Mexico State in Doak Campbell Stadium
articles._body: The odds seem so extraordinary that they have to be closer to impossible than simply improbable. When the Florida State football team opens its 2026 season tonight against visiting New Mexico State, Duce Robinson will be in the starting lineup at wide receiver for the Seminoles. In the starting lineup for the Aggies at wide receiver will be Myles Libman. The two former high school teammates have not only been best friends for half their lives, but they somehow have squared off against each other during three of their four years in college football — despite playing for numerous different teams in numerous different conferences. “It is so hard to even comprehend how rare that has to be,” said Duce’s father, Dominic Robinson, a former Florida State player who coached both of the receivers in high school. “I’ve tried to express it to so many people how rare it is to even get to play your buddy one time in college. And the fact that they’ve gone against each other almost every single year … it’s pretty wild.” It’s very wild. After starring together at Phoenix’s Pinnacle High School, Robinson went on to be a Southern Cal Trojan while Libman became a Stanford Cardinal. With both schools being members of the Pac-12 at the time, they played against each other early in that 2023 season. One year later, USC bolted for the Big Ten, so Libman and Robinson didn’t get to play. But when the Cardinal moved to the ACC in 2025 and Robinson transferred to Florida State, the friendly rivalry continued; the Seminoles and Stanford squared off as conference foes for the first time last October. Tonight, thanks to Libman transferring to New Mexico State in the offseason, they will meet one more time. At 7 p.m. ET inside Doak Campbell Stadium. “I can’t wait,” Duce Robinson said earlier this week. “We were just texting the other day. … It’s a really full-circle moment. We’re both at different schools, but we’re playing each other in the first game of the season. Like, that’s what we used to dream about.” In some ways, the wide receivers’ friendship is as unlikely as the number of times they’ve faced each other in college. When they first met, Libman and Robinson played for rival middle schools in the Phoenix area. They were going head-to-head each year in flag football, and they both had very different personalities. While Libman loves fashion and likes to wear his hair longer, Robinson goes with a more clean-cut look and spends much less time focusing on clothes and style. “He’s super swaggy and has all the drip,” Dominic Robinson said of Libman. “And Duce is as dry as they come. He’s not worried or concerned with any of those things and having all the shiny things and looking good. He goes out there on the field with all team-issued gear. He’s not having a towel hanging down or seven different wristbands or any of that. So I think they both admire in each other the contrast of their personalities. “It’s one of those things where the opposites … like magnets, the positive and the negative polarity just pulls them together.” Florida State WR Duce Robinson and former Stanford/current New Mexico State WR Myles Libman. (Courtesy of Dominic Robinson) Even though they wouldn’t play on the same high school team until much later, Robinson and Libman wasted no time becoming the best of friends. They respected each others’ physical talents immediately, and they soon came to realize they shared many of the same goals and priorities. They both were driven to not only be exceptional athletes, but also very high-achievers in academics. They also both starred in multiple sports — Libman in football, track and basketball, and Robinson in football, basketball and baseball. “They realized they’re both high-character, high-integrity guys,” Dominic Robinson said. “To find a guy who’s the best player on the team plus has a 4.0-plus (grade-point average), wants to be part of the National Junior Honor Society and is social but wants to do the right things, I think that can be a lonely place for a lot of athletes. They don’t really find that until college. … I think they got lucky and found each other in the seventh or eighth grade, and pretty much knew right away those guys are gonna be in each others’ weddings.” Said Duce: “From there, it sparked into a friendship, and very quickly we became like best friends. You could ask anyone, we were inseparable. He pushed me to be the best version of myself, and I hope I did the same for him.” Now, all these years later, they will be in the starting lineups for their respective teams again tonight — Libman with the Aggies and Robinson with the Florida State Seminoles. Before the game, they will spend some time talking on the Doak Campbell Stadium grass. They have been exchanging texts all week. But as soon as the opening kickoff sails into the Tallahassee sky and the game begins, they will go back to being rivals once again — for a good three hours. The same as they were back in middle school. The same as they’ve been two other times in college. “Being able to to play at two big-time programs and being able to, you know, dap each other up on the sideline before and after the game … the 5-year-old me would be in awe,” Robinson said. “I truly can’t wait. I’m so blessed to to be able to play him.” And then once the game ends, they will really be inseparable. “I think the thing that kind of drew them together was their differences,” Dominic Robinson said. “They have very different personalities, but when you put them together, it’s cookies and cream. It’s just a perfect mix.” Talk about this story with other die-ha

Trump cannot deport students for criticizing Israel, judge rules, saying speech and press freedoms are ‘foundational to America’s enduring democracy’
articles.summary: “Freedom of speech is illusory if we are only ‘free’ to express complementary views about the government and its leaders,” the judge wrote.
articles._body: Citing the importance of the First Amendment, a federal judge in California says the U.S. government is unconstitutionally silencing critics of  Israel’s war in Gaza  and others as part of the  Trump administration  ‘s quest to deport noncitizens who it says disrupted college campuses while expressing their views. Judge Noël Wise, in a ruling Friday, delivered a victory for The Stanford Daily, the student newspaper at Stanford University, which has said some international students were afraid to speak out because of the deportation threat. “Freedom of speech is illusory if we are only ‘free’ to express complementary views about the government and its leaders,” the judge wrote. The decision largely piggybacks on findings from nearly a year ago by a U.S. district judge in Boston, who ruled that the Trump administration violated the Constitution when it targeted people who are not citizens for deportation solely for supporting Palestinians and criticizing Israel. Wise wrote that the freedoms of speech and the press are “foundational to America’s enduring democracy.” The judge cited free-speech and vagueness flaws that violate the First Amendment and Fifth Amendment as she struck down portions of the provisions that the federal government follows regarding deportations. Wise cited retaliation in March 2025 by U.S. immigration authorities against people who engaged in speech supporting the Palestinians and against Israel’s actions — which a growing number of experts, including those commissioned by a U.N. body, have said amount to genocide . The judge also cited retaliation against people who were critical of Charlie Kirk after the Turning Point USA co-founder was assassinated last September . “Tomorrow, or perhaps even today, targets may include anyone in the United States who exercises their freedom of speech to simply express opinions the government does not like,” the judge in San Jose said. “This downward spiral is antithetical to our Constitution that recognizes our right to speak freely,” she added. “Here you can simultaneously hate the content of a person’s speech and love the country that cherishes the freedom to allow it. Zealous protection of our Constitutional right to free speech is a provocative demonstration of our country’s powerful lack of fear.” The Justice Department did not respond Saturday to a message seeking comment on the decision. George Porteous, the editor-in-chief of The Stanford Daily, responded to the ruling by saying on X: “The reporters in our newsroom shouldn’t have to fear that writing a story will result in their deportation. Today’s victory means they won’t have to.” Conor Fitzpatrick, an attorney with the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression, which brought the lawsuit, praised the ruling. “In America, free speech doesn’t just belong to the people who say things the government agrees with,” Fitzpatrick said in a release. In her decision, Wise said it was clear that the government’s tactics has had an effect on college campuses. “The government has offered a chilling message regarding protected speech — speak out against Israel or in support of Palestinians and we will revoke your visa and deport you. Behave. Noncitizen students heard the warning and heeded. And, as the idiom goes, the silence is deafening,” the judge wrote. At The Stanford Daily, lawfully present noncitizens at the paper have quit, withheld articles, refused assignments, requested articles be taken down, and asked for anonymity due to fear of adverse immigration consequences, Wise noted. She said noncitizens have the same First Amendment rights as citizens and yet were left to guess what the U.S. foreign policy was at any given moment and on any given subject. “This is an incomprehensible standard,” she said. “While the Court understands that the government has been granted considerable discretion on foreign policy and immigration matters, that discretion must nevertheless still ensure that ordinary people can understand what the law permits and prohibits.” Wise added: “Our Constitutional right to freedom of speech guarantees people the right to express — through their words, actions, or assembly — opinions that may be repugnant, views that run counter to prevailing political norms, or beliefs that otherwise challenge the country’s domestic or foreign policy, military engagement, or war.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: ‘Long after President Trump is gone, it will still be called Lake Ontario’ — Premier Doug Ford fires back at ‘Lake America’ decree with giant sign
articles.summary: Wearing a Team Canada soccer jersey, Ford unveiled the sign near Grimsby, Ontario.
articles._body: Ontario Premier Doug Ford answered President Donald Trump’s  “Lake America” decree  Saturday with a billboard-sized message on the Canadian shoreline: “Lake Ontario. Now and Always.” Wearing a Team Canada soccer jersey, Ford unveiled the sign near Grimsby, Ontario, and posed for photographs. The 24-by-12-foot (7.3-by-3.6 meter) sign stands on 6-foot (1.8-meter) legs, putting its top about 18 feet (5.5 meters) above the ground — roughly two stories high. The message is repeated in French. It was the latest show of defiance after Trump signed an executive order directing U.S. federal agencies to call Lake Ontario “Lake America.” After months of  tariffs , threats to make Canada the  51st U.S. state  and personal  attacks on its leaders , the move has been met in Canada largely with ridicule. Ford said Trump was trying to rename the lake because Ontario and Canada were “standing up for ourselves” and argued the name would outlast the president. “Long after President Trump is gone, it will still be called Lake Ontario,” Ford said in a video posted on social media. Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew compared Trump to an aging rock band trying to revive an old hit “You know when a rock band is really over the hill and you see them like in a casino playing some song from like 50 years ago. I think that’s the part of Donald Trump’s presidency we’re at now, Like he thought they had a real hit, a real golden oldie, with the  Gulf of Mexico ,” Kinew said, referring to Trump’s executive order renaming the Gulf of Mexico the Gulf of America. “And he’s trying to bring back that, and he’s trying to play the hits for his base. But I think everybody here thinks it’s a little sad and it’s not his best work.” The mockery was not limited to politicians. Canadian historian Robert Bothwell was even more scathing. “The greatest country on earth takes this moron seriously?” Bothwell said. But Bothwell said the dispute was more serious than the jokes, arguing Trump’s broader aim was “to subordinate Canada and at best make it a colony, at worst absorb it into the United States.” Nelson Wiseman, professor emeritus at the University of Toronto, said Trump “would like Canada to act like a vassal state, but it refuses to do so. That irritates him.” The dispute comes as relations between the longtime allies worsen over trade. Negotiations collapsed last week, both governments accused the other of making late demands, and Canada announced retaliatory tariffs set to take effect next month. Trump’s order also came amid an escalating war of words with Ford. In an interview with The Associated Press earlier this week, Ford said Ronald Reagan would be “throwing up” over Trump’s tariff policies and “disgusted with President Trump.” Trump fired back by dismissing Ford’s comments as “bluster,” calling him Prime Minister Mark Carney’s “flunky” and mocking him as the “less charismatic, intelligent, and overall unimpressive brother” of the late Toronto Mayor Rob Ford. Trump continued promoting the new name Saturday, reposting a meme showing Canada geese with Trump-like blond hair firing rifles as they “protected” Lake America. Trump has repeatedly used maps to make political points. A “Gulf of America” map was displayed for a time beside the Resolute Desk in the Oval Office, and Trump has posted images depicting Canada as part of the United States or as the 51st state. The name Lake Ontario  comes from the Huron Indigenous people’s word “oniatarí:io,” which means “lake of shining waters.” The Canadian province of Ontario, founded in 1867, took its name from the lake. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney rejected the move, noting the lake’s Indigenous roots and that the name predates both Canadian Confederation and the U.S. Declaration of Independence. Trump cannot require Canada to adopt the new name. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles._body: Billy Edwards tipped his cap to the UNC defense, led by head coach Bill Belichick , for the Tar Heels’ win over TCU in Dublin, Ireland Saturday. UNC opened up with a 15-10 win overseas to kickoff Year 2 under Belichick. The veteran and transfer quarterback played well in his own right, but holding the Horned Frogs to 10 points was the biggest key. Edwards said he could practically relax during some points of the game due to the knowledge that the entire defensive unit could pick up any slack. $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage “It feels great,” Edwards said postgame on the ESPN broadcast. “You know, first game of the season, I don’t think I played my best football, but hats off to the defense. They kept us into the whole game. Big time stops in the fourth quarter. Multiple turnovers. And shout out to the offensive line. “I think we got the ball with four minutes, or maybe a little under four minutes, and that’s how you go finish the game. So, really happy to come out here and start the season off on the right note. We got a lot of stuff to clean up, but at least we can do it in the victory column.” As far as the defense is concerned, Belichick was the man in charge. Not that he wasn’t coming into the game, but the long time head coach had to relay the play calls without Steve Belichick currently with the program. Edwards knew he saw a solid performance. “They got they got high-end motors. You know, going against them every day in practice, it obviously makes you better,” Edwards said. “Iron sharpens iron. So, honestly, as a quarterback, you can sit back and kind of have a little bit more relaxation knowing that guys like that are out on your defense, and they’re going to put up a hell in a fight like they did tonight.” Bill Belichick’s defense comes to play vs. TCU Edwards finished the game 16-of-28 passing for 232 yards, but did not throw a touchdown. Tight end Jelani Thurman reeled in four passes for 94 yards to lead the Tar Heels on offense. Bill Belichick’s defense ended up loggin three sacks, kept TCU to 7-of-16 on third down and forced a fumble. Coming into the game, Belichick was honest about the approach to take on TCU’s new-look offense. Led by new OC Gordon Sammis , who came from UConn , promised to shake things up. But the Tar Heels were clearly ready. “It’s an unknown,” Belichick said this week leading up . “We can look at UConn’s offense (where TCU offensive coordinator Gordon Sammis came from). We can look at what TCU did against us last year, which I’m sure they felt like was successful. Sonny’s here, the offensive line coach is here, they have several coaches on their staff (that returned), so it could be a combination of what they did here last year and what’s coming in. “That’s opening day. You never really know that. Even if it was the same coaches, which I was in that situation for many, many years, where it was our same staff, you still make changes from year to year. You change things based on trends, what you’re seeing, your personnel, and so forth.”

articles.title: Lane Kiffin, Reggie Bush, Jameis Winston poke fun at controversies in new DoorDash campaign
articles.summary: Buckle up for this one. With college football returning, some of the sport’s top stars of past and present, like Lane Kiffin, Reggie Bush and Jameis Winston, are having some fun with its past in a new DoorDash campaign. The three prominent figures are starring in DoorDash’s new season-lo
articles._body: Buckle up for this one. With college football returning, some of the sport’s top stars of past and present, like Lane Kiffin , Reggie Bush and Jameis Winston , are having some fun with its past in a new DoorDash campaign. The three prominent figures are starring in DoorDash’s new season-long “Don’t Fan for Free” campaign , according to Kristi Dosh of Forbes . The advertisements play off the dramatic changes to college athletics since athletes were permitted to profit from their name, image and likeness beginning in 2021. $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage #LSU coach @Lane_Kiffin is featured in another major TV commercial alongside Jameis Winston and Reggie Bush for @DoorDash . The commercial poke jabs at Winston’s crab leg incident and Bush’s house incident at USC that cost him his Heisman for a few years. pic.twitter.com/0oGkhJf8Vy — Preston Guy (@PGuy77) August 29, 2026 Of course, Bush and Winston provide particularly fitting examples of how different the college sports landscape once was, perfect for the campaign.. Bush had his 2005 Heisman Trophy taken away following an NCAA investigation that found his family received impermissible benefits, including rent-free housing and cash from prospective sports agents. His Heisman was eventually reinstated in 2024 following significant changes to college athletics. Meanwhile, Winston, was suspended from Florida State’s baseball team for five days in 2014 after receiving a civil citation for stealing crab legs from a Tallahassee grocery store. “The idea started with NIL and just how dramatically it has changed the culture of college football in recent years,” DoorDash Vice President of Brand, Creative and Consumer Marketing Gina Igwe told Forbes. “Reggie, Jameis and Lane were the perfect people to bring that idea to life because each has a distinct personality and very real ties to the pre-NIL era and the rules that defined it.” The campaign allows all three to poke fun at their respective college football histories while highlighting how much the sport has changed: “There’s a fun and cheeky irony in having them be the ones telling fans that now it’s finally their turn to get a deal,” Igwe added . “They immediately understood the joke, leaned into it and brought the kind of self-awareness that made the idea feel authentic rather than forced.” Moreover, DoorDash also worked several references to Bush and Winston’s past into the campaign. Fans participating in DoorDash Streaks can earn weekly deals and monthly prizes by ordering on Saturdays throughout the season. Among the prizes is $757,500 toward a home. According to Forbes , the specific amount is a reference to the purchase price of the home Bush’s family lived in rent-free, which became part of the NCAA’s investigation into the former USC star. More on Lane Kiffin, LSU Tigers The most polarizing figure is of course Kiffin, who’s become no stranger to poking fun at himself in commercials. The LSU head coach is also starring in a new Dr. Pepper advertisement alongside former Oklahoma star Brian Bosworth . Kiffin gets pulled over by Bosworth, who reprises his role as the Fansville sheriff, for making an “illegal ‘Lane’ change.” The joke comes after Kiffin made another major coaching move, leaving Ole Miss for LSU following the 2025 regular season. Kiffin has remained at the center of college football’s rapidly changing landscape since arriving in Baton Rouge. Most recently, he has been outspoken about former NFL players attempting to return to college after receiving additional eligibility through court rulings. Now, Kiffin is also leaning into his reputation away from the field. DoorDash’s campaign will run throughout the college football season, with the company also bringing its National Tailgate Tour to campuses around the country. “We hope fans have fun with it and appreciate the hidden references, nostalgic callbacks, and Easter eggs woven throughout the campaign, particularly the playful nods to Jameis and Reggie’s pre-NIL days,” Igwe said.

articles.title: Lil Nas X Reveals Mother’s Death Amid Sobriety Journey: ‘This One’s Gonna Hurt’
articles.summary: “RIP TO THE BADDEST EVER!" the rapper and singer wrote.
articles._body: Lil Nas X is mourning the death of his mother, Tameka Hill. On Saturday (Aug. 29), the 27-year-old rapper and singer took to social media to pay tribute to his late mom. Related Lil Nas X Says Fans Are Being ‘OD Nice’ to Him Since He Got Out of Rehab Olivia Rodrigo Recruits Alanis Morissette for a Surprise 'Ironic' Duet Harry Styles Jokes About Taylor Swift's MSG Wedding During Residency Show “RIP TO THE BADDEST EVER! LOVE U FOREVER MOMMY,” Nas wrote on Instagram alongside throwback photos. “This one’s gonna hurt.” Hill’s age and cause of death were unknown at press time. Billboard has reached out to Nas’ representatives for further information. The “Old Town Road” hitmaker had a complicated relationship with his mother but revealed in 2020 that she struggled with addiction. “I never really talk about my mom,” the Grammy winner told Variety at the time. “She’s an addict, so we don’t have the closest relationship. Even trying to get her better — things didn’t quite work out. But there’s still love.” The news of Hill’s passing comes days after Lil Nas X — who recently revealed that he had been diagnosed with bipolar disorder and had entered rehab for mental health support — celebrated his “10,000th day alive.” “So, tomorrow is my 10,000th day alive and I made it,” he said in a video shared to his Instagram Stories. “A lot of you won’t make it, but I made it.” In mid-June, he revealed on Instagram that he had been in rehab “for a few months.” He later spent time with family in Atlanta and friends in Los Angeles to “ground myself down to Earth and get out of my head.” He added, “I have a therapist now and a psychiatrist, which is really helpful.” Nas, whose real name is Montero Hill, has also faced legal trouble . In August 2025, he was charged with four felonies after allegedly attacking police officers while walking naked through the streets of Los Angeles. The charges will be dismissed if he continues with mental health treatment, Variety reports .

articles.summary: The Texas Tech Red Raiders added a quarterback to the roster at the last minute after signing Thomas Castellanos in the transfer portal. On Saturday, head coach Joey McGuire opened up about bringing Castellanos onto the roster and what kind of role the fifth-year senior could play this season. Mc
articles._body: The Texas Tech Red Raiders added a quarterback to the roster at the last minute after signing Thomas Castellanos in the transfer portal. On Saturday, head coach Joey McGuire opened up about bringing Castellanos onto the roster and what kind of role the fifth-year senior could play this season. McGuire admitted that his goal this offseason was to enter the 2026-27 campaign with six quarterbacks on the roster , according to Pete Nakos of On3 Sports. The 55-year-old claimed that he believes Castallenos’ athleticism and experience are something that can help expand the Red Raiders’ offense. “It has been our intention since this past December to carry six quarterbacks on our roster this season,” McGuire said. “With Tommy, we have an experienced quarterback who we believe can come in and help us win games, if needed. His athleticism is also a great trait and will let us continue to expand our offense.” That means Castellanos could have some designed packages in the offense this season, as Will Hammond will serve as the starting quarterback for Texas Tech. So if Thomas Castellanos gets some looks, his playing time could be sporadic. Castellanos joins Texas Tech with four years of college experience under his belt. He began his collegiate career with the UCF Knights. He then transferred to Boston College, where he played for two seasons before transferring to Florida State for the 2025-26 season. Thomas Castellanos ended last year with 2.760 passing yards (career-high), 557 rushing yards, and 24 total touchdowns (15 passing, 9 rushing). His dual-threat ability could provide a big boost to Texas Tech’s run game this year. articles.title: Riley Herbst out for Daytona, Harrison Burton to replace him in 23XI Toyota
articles.summary: Riley Herbst will not race at Daytona after experiencing lingering effects from last weekend’s incident. Harrison Burton will drive the No. 35.
articles._body: 23XI has announced a driver change for tonight’s Coke Zero Sugar 400 at Daytona. Riley Hebrst will be replaced by Harrison Burton, the team announced on Saturday afternoon. Herbst was involved in a wreck last weekend at New Hampshire with Michael McDowell. After extremely hard contact into the wall, Connor Zilisch missed his downshift and locked up his brakes, sliding directly into an already wrecked Herbst. 23XI announces Riley Herbst out of Coke Zero 400 “After a strong effort in qualifying yesterday, Riley Herbst woke up with lingering effects from last weekend’s incident and, along with the team, decided it was in his best interest to step out of the car for tonight’s race at Daytona International Speedway,” the statement read. “He will be replaced in the No. 35 Toyota for tonight’s NASCAR Cup Series race at Daytona International Speedway by Harrison Burton.” An update on today’s race. A driver change for the No. 35 team. pic.twitter.com/w0blYPsjAe — 23XI Racing (@23XIRacing) August 29, 2026 Herbst was among the Top 10 qualifiers on Friday , advancing to the second round of qualifying. He was set to start P5 in tonight’s race at Daytona. How to watch the Coke Zero Sugar 400 On Saturday, August 29th, NASCAR makes its return to Daytona International Speedway for the Coke Zero Sugar 400. This will be the fourth race on USA Sports, which will carry NASCAR coverage through the end of the season.  The race begins at 7:30 p.m. ET.  It will be televised on NBC, while carrying the USA Sports branding.  And it’s the final race of the regular season before the start of the Chase.  When the checkered flag waves, the field of 16 drivers for the NASCAR postseason will be set.  It will also be the first race using the new superspeedway rules package .   “The rear spoiler will be shortened from 7 inches to 4 inches, the same height as intermediate tracks, in an effort to reduce drag, along with a slight reduction in horsepower from 510 to 465 to adjust for the reduced downforce,” wrote Zach Sturniolo on NASCAR.com. “NASCAR officials anticipate single-car runs to be approximately 3 mph faster than the current package, but cars in a pack are expected to run about the same speeds.” A brief breakdown of the rules package and the expectations: Superspeedway Package Update: 14” spoiler and wide splitter stuffers (same as intermediate) Safety equipment remains the same as current SSW Engine tapered spacer reduced to 27/32” ~ 465 HP New spoiler braces Spoiler deflection device redesigned to accommodate 4” spoiler Performance Aspects: Single-car speeds estimated at 2-3 mph faster than current qualifying. Maximum pack speeds estimated in the same range as current. Dynamic passing maneuver CFD indicates completion of a pass with a 5-mph run is more likely with new package. Expect fireworks on and off the track at Daytona.

articles._body: CHARLOTTESVILLE, Va. — After waiting 253 days since knocking off Memphis in the Gasparilla Bowl to cap the 2025 campaign, NC State is ready to kick off the new season in a Week 0 clash at Virginia. The Wolfpack enters the opener at nearly full strength across its offense and defense, and will be led by junior quarterback CJ Bailey in his 23rd career start at the helm the program. Follow along here with all of the live updates. By: Noah Fleischman Pack gets a sack 08/29/2026 03:41:27 PM NC State’s defense comes up with a much-needed sack on third down. LaCorian Hodge and Harvey Dyson team up to bring down Beau Pribula. Victor Snow’s quality punt return of 29 yards has the Wolfpack on its own 49. Virginia 17, NC State 0. 2Q 5:45. Jackson Waller’s third punt of the afternoon will have Virginia start its next drive from its own 23. Virginia 10, NC State 0. 1Q 0:44. Virginia 10, NC State 0. 1Q 2:37. By: Noah Fleischman Bailey throws an INT 08/29/2026 03:04:33 PM NC State QB CJ Bailey tried to throw a pass over the middle, but it was tipped at the line of scrimmage. It was picked off by Virginia’s Brandyn Hillman at the NC State 32. Virginia 3, NC State 0. 1Q 4:43. By: Noah Fleischman Virginia strikes first 08/29/2026 02:59:47 PM It looked like Virginia was building a touchdown drive, but Josh Warren had a game-changing stop on Beau Pribula. articles.summary: North Carolina took down TCU 15-10 inside Aviva Stadium on Saturday night to avenge last season's loss on Labor Day night.
articles._body: DUBLIN — Behind a gutsy defensive performance, the second year of the Bill Belichick era got off to a much different start inside Aviva Stadium on Saturday night. In a rematch of last year’s season opener, UNC took down TCU 15-10 on a rainy, gray Dublin evening. ** After falling behind 10-3 in the first quarter, 12 unanswered points and two second half fourth-down stops inside the red zone helped the Tar Heels avenge last season’s season-opening loss. ** In his first start as a Tar Heel, Billy Edwards Jr. completed 16 of 28 passes for 232 yards with no touchdowns and no interceptions. ** Jelani Thurman paced the UNC passing attack with 94 yards on four receptions, while Jordan Shipp tallied 71 yards on five catches. **On the ground, Benjamin Hall led the Tar Heels with 36 yards on 11 carries. UNC totaled 90 rushing yards for the game. ** On the defensive side of the ball, Derek McDonald led UNC with 11 tackles in his first game as a Tar Heel. Along the defensive line, sophomore Xavier Lewis turned in a standout performance with seven total tackles, including two sacks and 4.5 tackles for loss. ** TCU did not score after the first quarter and totaled 312 yards for the game against UNC’s defense. ** Play of the Game: Hanging onto a 15-10 lead with TCU at the UNC 10-yard line and facing fourth-and-2 with 4:05 to play, the Tar Heel defense bowed up for its second red-zone fourth-down stand of the second half. Horned Frogs quarterback Jaden Craig overthrew Jeremy Scott on the left side of the end zone, allowing UNC to take over on downs. ** With Demon June in at running back, North Carolina picked up three first downs, including a 25-yarder to Thurman then drawing an offsides on fourth down, to run out the clock to secure the victory.

US Open Unveils Record Player Pay but Resists Revenue Share
articles.summary: REUTERS/Loren Elliott
articles._body: NEW YORK — There will be no prize money protests from the players at the 2026 US Open after the tournament announced record-setting player compensation alongside a new player support program and new Grand Slam Player Advisory Council. But that doesn’t mean all issues are solved. Speaking at a press conference Saturday at the US Open, USTA CEO Craig Tiley, who officially took over last month , said the tournament does not use revenue as a form of measuring the players’ prize money. “We don’t use that number as a form of calculating how we compensate, because it can be fairly arbitrary from one event to another,” Tiley said. “I believe the tours use profit, so we look at it very differently. We say, what’s a fair share that the players need to be compensated on, and what can we do, because even outside of just the compensation package, what other things can we do to help support the players, not just during the event but also year-round.” Tiley’s comments come one day after world No. 3 Jessica Pegula, a member of the WTA Players’ Council and one of the more outspoken voices for player compensation on both tours, told Front Office Sports that revenue share will be a key topic of discussion of the new Grand Slam Player Advisory Council. “That’s something we’re still pushing for, and so I think hopefully with this council, that we’ll be able to continue those discussions because I know from our side, we still do believe that a revenue share is the best way, and now we’ll just have much more open communication,” Pegula said. There is currently no structure in place that gives players a fixed share of revenue from the Grand Slams. Tournament organizers generally allocate about 15% of revenue to players, but the players are aiming to get to 22% by 2030. Tiley, known for elevating the Australian Open as the CEO of Tennis Australia, reiterated that he is a “player-focused” leader and that he will continue to push for an improved package at the US Open. “You will see the US Open continue to be a very player-friendly event. I think our desire to increase the amount that we put on the table was driven really within the organization, the sense that we need to give the players a fair share,” Tiley said. Pegula commended the USTA on Friday for taking the lead in discussions with players, particularly in creating the new council. There is still little known about the council, Pegula said, with a USTA spokesperson telling FOS that more plans are expected to be laid out in the weeks after the tournament. But Tiley said Saturday that around 10 players have already come forward to express their interest in joining the council. “We think, again, the voice of the players, we believe, is important,” Tiley said. “Many of us have been spending a lot of time and energy individually talking to the players. Not just the last week—it’s been going on for years. The Slams having a close player relationship is critical to the success of the Slams and the success of the relationship that we have with the fans, as well.” Ticket Prices Tiley was also asked about the tournament’s rising ticket prices, which have led to significant complaints from fans. As of Saturday, the day before the main draw, the average US Open get-in price for the next two weeks is $289 on the secondary, up 14% from this point last year, per TicketData . Tiley made sure to mention that entrance is free during fan week, and for eight of the 22 total days of the tournament. But he admitted that the resale market is one of the tournament’s “biggest challenges” in tempering ticket prices. “$65 for a grounds pass gets moved pretty quickly when it goes to market and at some years we’ll keep looking at, because one thing that’s critically important to us as an event is we want kids to be able to experience,” Tiley said. articles.title: Kasen Carpenter back healthy, learning new system at center
articles.summary: After missing some practice time in fall camp Kasen Carpenter is back and healthy. He talked about his transition from Oklahoma State.
articles._body: Kasen Carpenter arrived at Kansas before spring football after transferring from Oklahoma State , giving him time to get comfortable with a new position group and offensive system. The center has blended in and most importantly picked up on a new offensive scheme. Carpenter has spent much of fall camp running with the first-team offensive line. Since the spring the extra has allowed him to continue learning the offense and develop chemistry with the other players up front. He said offensive line coach Daryl Agpalsa and the Kansas staff have emphasized finding something specific to improve each day. “Yeah, it’s been great,” Carpenter said. “You know, we’ve taken it day by day. Coach Agpalsa has done a great job, and the whole coaching staff, of challenging us to 1% goals. I think that the biggest part of our offense so far is 1% better daily.” That approach has given Carpenter and the offense something to focus on. The word from the coaching staff has been to continue to improve through practice and focus on the growth. “We’ve been challenged to pick out something each day that we can focus on, and I think that’s just the small things that we can get through that,” Carpenter said. “And finding something like that to work on every day is just—I think it’s caused our offense to exponentially grow.” Carpenter has missed time through fall camp with the bumps and bruises that are common. But he’s been back and taking a lot of snaps. “You know, obviously, you have good days, you have bad days, you have mediocre days,” he said. “Just finding ways to work through those and continue getting better.” Adjusting to new offense A big part Carpenter’s transition has been learning offensive coordinator Andy Kotelnicki ‘s system. Having played college football at Oklahoma State before coming to Kansas has helped him adjust to different language, “Especially just football in general, as you play it for a while, it gets easier to learn,” Carpenter said. “There’s definitely different terminology and little things, but it’s been great.” “There’s a lot that we’ve installed, but he’s done a great job teaching us why, like, what it is, why it is, and how we do it.” Carpenter had heard about the complexity of Kotelnicki’s offense before arriving at Kansas. After going through spring practices and fall camp, he has seen how the system continues to evolve and the new plays that are added daily. “We’ve been installing since January, so we’ve had new stuff, new wrinkles,” he said. “You have your base plays and stuff, but there’s new wrinkles that he adds in all the time, so it’s been great to learn.” There has also been movement throughout the offensive line during fall camp. Agpalsa has cross-trained players at different spots, which has created competition while giving players experience are other positions. “Oh, it’s awesome,” Carpenter said. “They’ve done a great job keeping us competing. That’s the biggest thing from it is we’re always competing at all times. They’re shifting us around.” The goal for Agpalsa is to build enough depth that Kansas can adjust for different situations. If there is an injury and a player needs to move positions it might create a new opportunity for someone else. He wants them to be ready for what can come up during a season. “We’re working together and finding ways to work together with different people, because things happen in games and people got to come in,” Carpenter said. “And so, Coach A’s thing is, you know, I need to find somebody that I can put in, and the level doesn’t drop who I play. So, it’s been great, guys coming in and competing.” 75% OFF: Season Kickoff sale through Labor Day Our new and final 75% off promo for the year is underway and will go through Labor Day. articles.title: Eagles’ release running back after strong preseason game vs. Bengals
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are reportedly letting go of running back Carson Steele, even though he played well in the team’s preseason finale against the Cincinnati Bengals. NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports that the Eagles plan to release Steele as they finalize their 53-man roster. Schultz posted
articles._body: The Philadelphia Eagles are reportedly letting go of running back Carson Steele, even though he played well in the team’s preseason finale against the Cincinnati Bengals. NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports that the Eagles plan to release Steele as they finalize their 53-man roster . Schultz posted on X that Philadelphia will let go of the former undrafted free agent. He also pointed out Steele’s strong game against Cincinnati, where he had eight catches for 52 yards and a touchdown. The Eagles lost their preseason finale 30-13 to the Bengals on Friday night, but Steele was one of the team’s bright spots. He showed his versatility by making plays as both a runner and a receiver as the regular season neared. Steele ended the game with 24 rushing yards on eight carries and caught eight passes for 52 yards. He also scored on a five-yard touchdown catch from veteran quarterback Andy Dalton. Steele’s performance stood out because he spent the offseason fighting for a spot in a crowded Eagles running back group. Saquon Barkley is still the clear starter, while Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley are also competing for backup roles. Even with his strong game against Cincinnati, Steele did not make Philadelphia’s initial 53-man roster. If he clears waivers, the Eagles could still bring him back on the practice squad. The decision on Steele is surprising , considering how well he finished the preseason. His showing against the Bengals might also catch the attention of other teams needing running back depth. As the Eagles get ready for the regular season, they still have several key roster decisions ahead. Steele’s release is one of the bigger stories after Friday’s preseason finale. Cody Bellinger’s ‘tennis’ admission will catch Yankees fans’ attention
articles.summary: New York Yankees outfielder Cody Bellinger is a World Series champion, National League Championship Series MVP, regular season MVP, three-time All-Star and Gold Glove winner. One does not collect all that hardware without becoming a master of preparation. Yes, his career took a nosedive for a cou
articles._body: New York Yankees outfielder Cody Bellinger is a World Series champion, National League Championship Series MVP, regular season MVP, three-time All-Star and Gold Glove winner. One does not collect all that hardware without becoming a master of preparation. Yes, his career took a nosedive for a couple of years due to prolonged injury problems and offensive shortcomings, but the veteran ballplayer’s commitment to evolving allowed him to retain and maintain his productivity. This adaptable mindset has been visible to those following him in 2026, and it was especially noticeable in Friday night’s 1-0 win over the Boston Red Sox . Bellinger made a perfect throw to prevent the speedy Ceddanne Rafaela from tying the game in the seventh inning. With runs at a premium, the 31-year-old’s pinpoint precision saved the day and expanded the Yankees’ lead in the American League Wild Card standings. This was no one-night triumph, however. Bellinger has been among the best defensive left fielders in MLB this season, thriving in all the advanced metrics that are used to determine such a standard. Again, it goes back to preparation. He has 20 defensive runs saved, +6 outs above average and an +8 fielding run value at the position, per FanGraphs. The 2013 fourth-round draft pick and his Yankees teammates have looked to another sport to improve their efficiency . “We actually got it from tennis,” Bellinger said, per Gary Phillips of the New York Daily News. “When these guys are getting serves at them 115 mph, you’ll see this little pre-step that they do, and we’ve taken that on defense, and it’s been good for me.” Will this new Yankees approach show up when it matters most? Having a keen attention to detail and displaying top-notch instincts are instrumental to enjoying a successful tennis career. Timing can be the difference between a consistently good player and a multi-time Grand Slam winner. The Yankees understand how narrow that gap can be. Opportune, heads-up plays decide playoff series, and Aaron Boone’s squad has failed to produce the requisite amount during the last few Octobers. Defensive sloppiness ended the Yanks’ World Series quest in 2025, and if they get the chance to avenge that brutal outcome in 2026, those brain freezes cannot pop up. A mentally-sharp Cody Bellinger is trying to help them solve this issue. New York (76-58) will conclude an important four-game series versus the Red Sox (73-61) on Sunday afternoon and then head West to begin a six-game road trip. Perhaps the team can find time to check out the opening round of the US Open along the way. With the incident between the Sky guard, Cloud, and Kanter Freedo
articles._body: After Chicago Sky star Natasha Cloud confronted Enes Kanter Freedom during the team’s 113-90 loss to the Indiana Fever last Sunday, it amplified the conversation running rampant around the WNBA regarding transgender athletes. With the incident between the Sky guard , Cloud, and Kanter Freedom the talk of the sports world, Cloud has moved on from the event, claiming the former NBA player to be unimportant. Before Chicago took on the New York Liberty on Saturday, Cloud made sure to mention how she won’t be talking about that “irrelevant person.” Cloud wants to focus more on issues that impact women and children currently, like domestic violence, sexual assault, and food insecurity, according to ESPN. “I will not talk about an irrelevant threat to our lives, because that’s exactly what it is,” Cloud continued. “I want to talk about real issues that face women, and it’s not our trans human beings, and it’s not our drag queens. It’s not our gay community. There is a certain demographic of people that you can generally search. It’s a simple Google search of what is the greatest threat to women and children currently in 2026 in the United States of America.” More on Sky’s Natasha Cloud and incident with Enes Kanter Freedom During the confrontation, Kanter Freedom was sitting baseline wearing a shirt that read “WOMAN noun. adult human female,” as he believes in stopping transgender athletes from playing in women’s sports, though not a single one plays in the WNBA. During a timeout towards the end of the game last Sunday, Cloud approached Kanter Freedom while yelling at him , as the former player egged it on, leading to people separating the two. ENES KANTER AND NATASHA CLOUD GOING AT IT. pic.twitter.com/Qov6x500re — Hoop Central (@TheHoopCentral) August 24, 2026 Kanter Freedom has since been banned from Sky games by owner Michael Alter, as Cloud applauded the move. Cloud would say that the players “won’t allow our league to be used as a pawn for any political or cultural wars that the right wants.” “This league has always stood on principle and on our humanitarian efforts,” Cloud continued. It remains to be seen how the conversation around transgender athletes continues in the WNBA. articles.title: Panthers give defense a boost with latest signing
articles.summary: The Carolina Panthers added veteran experience to their defense Saturday, agreeing to a one-year contract with linebacker Bobby Okereke. The move addresses uncertainty at inside linebacker as the Panthers prepare to finalize their 53-man roster. Okereke, 30, has started 95 games across seven NFL
articles._body: The Carolina Panthers added veteran experience to their defense Saturday, agreeing to a one-year contract with linebacker Bobby Okereke. The move addresses uncertainty at inside linebacker as the Panthers prepare to finalize their 53-man roster. Okereke, 30, has started 95 games across seven NFL seasons and gives defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero another proven option in the middle of the defense. The agreement came one day after the Panthers defeated the Houston Texans 16-13 in their preseason finale. NFL teams must reduce their rosters to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET Sunday. The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero took to X, formerly Twitter, on Saturday to report on the latest addition to the Panthers’ defense. “Veteran LB Bobby Okereke agreed to terms with the Panthers, per source.” Okereke played every defensive snap during his first season with the Giants in 2023, totaling 149 tackles, 11 tackles for loss, four forced fumbles, and 10 passes defended. The veteran linebacker also spent his first four seasons with the Indianapolis Colts before signing with the New York Giants in 2023. The Giants released him in March, a move that freed about $9 million in salary-cap space. He started all 17 games last season and led New York with 143 tackles. Okereke also recorded two interceptions and earned NFC Defensive Player of the Week honors following his two-takeaway performance in Week 18. Across 110 career games, Okereke has totaled 805 tackles, seven interceptions, 11 forced fumbles and 7.5 sacks. His experience and production expand Carolina’s choices alongside Devin Lloyd, whose recent knee soreness required additional treatment. Lloyd remains on track for Week 1, while Trevin Wallace and Claudin Cherelus had been competing for the other starting inside linebacker job. Okereke now joins that mix as the Panthers evaluate their personnel before the regular season. The short-term agreement gives general manager Dan Morgan flexibility without a long-term commitment. Okereke’s eventual role will depend on his health, performance, and the Panthers’ final roster decisions. The post Panthers give defense a boost with latest signing appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles._body: I wanted to try using the larger models on my computer (32GB RAM, RTX 5080, Gen5 NVMe), but the best I could do was around 30B. So I started with the idea that it might be possible by taking advantage of the fact that MoE models use only some of the experts rather than all of them. MoE-Direct essentially uses the three layers of SSD, RAM, and VRAM instead of residing entirely in memory, caching only the necessary experts in RAM and making the model usable even with resources far smaller than required. In my environment, I obtained the following decode results: Kimi K2.6: 1.03 tok/s. Qwen3.5-122B: 5.59–5.69 tok/s, with decode performance about 2.3 times better than plain mmap for the same binary. The current project is still far from the intended stage of practical use, and there are still many problems that need to be addressed. Since MoE-Direct is still in its early stages and external usability reviews and testing have not yet been conducted, I am very interested in feedback on my project and participation in testing. articles.title: Wall Street used to worry that too much U.S. debt would crowd out the private sector. But AI hyperscalers are ‘reverse crowding’ the Treasury
articles.summary: "Capital flowing into corporate bonds is capital not flowing into Treasuries, and Treasury yields have had to rise to clear the market."
articles._body: Among the many potential downsides for letting the national debt get too high was that the federal government would suck up so much capital that businesses wouldn’t be left with enough. Today, U.S. debt is at $40 trillion, the federal budget deficit is on track to reach $2 trillion this fiscal year, and debt servicing costs alone are $1 trillion a year. That’s a lot money that the Treasury Department has to raise from the bond market, which is also a key source of financing for corporate giants. But AI hyperscalers, so far, are still able to issue plenty of their own debt in the mad dash to buy chips, build data centers and lay down other infrastructure. In fact, even Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who has billed himself as America’s top bond salesman, has noted the eagerness with which AI companies are offering debt—no matter the cost of borrowing. “We are also seeing big corporate issuance. And a lot of that corporate issuance, I would say, is almost yield-agnostic, because the build-out for AI, the returns on that, the companies believe they’re going to be so high. They don’t really care what they’re paying,” he said recently. U.S. investment-grade corporate bond issuance totaled about $1.7 trillion in the year to date through July, about 27% above last year’s pace and on track to exceed $2 trillion for the first time, according to Wall Street veteran Ed Yardeni. A flood of corporate debt that massive would typically require yields to offer a bigger premium over risk-free bonds in order to attract enough buyers. But in the case of AI-related bonds, demand has been so high that the yield spread has remained compressed, barely widening for an additional premium, he pointed out in a note on Monday. “As a result, the market has adjusted not through higher corporate borrowing costs relative to Treasuries but through higher Treasury yields themselves. Capital flowing into corporate bonds is capital not flowing into Treasuries, and Treasury yields have had to rise to clear the market,” Yardeni explained. “In short, the AI revolution is producing a classic crowding-out effect, causing Treasury yields to rise.” Higher yields could eventually fuel a feedback loop where rising debt-servicing costs expand deficits further and further add on to the pile of U.S. debt, which in turn pushes yields up further. To be sure, the rise in Treasury yields has been attributed to a variety factors, in addition to the AI debt orgy. They include massive federal budget deficits with no end in sight, higher oil prices due to the Iran war, and a robust U.S. economy continuing to put upward pressure on inflation. But Yardeni noted that international capital-flow data show that net purchases of U.S. corporate bonds by private-sector foreign buyers have exceeded their purchases of Treasury debt over the past year. Jurrien Timmer, director of global macro at Fidelity Investments, said on X that “The reverse crowding out in the corporate bond market has even gotten the Treasury Secretary’s attention.” It has gotten Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh’s attention too. In his speech as the Jackson Hole conference on Friday, he nodded to the debt boom, saying “Ever-expanding pools of capital are pouring into AI-related infrastructure of all sorts.” That’s as private credit is financing the AI boom as well, while chipmaker Nvidia is even leveraging its balance sheet to back AI deals. So-called hidden borrowing has also exploded, with one tally putting it at $1.65 trillion. But markets are showing some signs of fatigue, after absorbing the flood of debt in such a short time, S&P Global warned last month, pointing out that hyperscalers are paying a higher premium compared with yields on risk-free bonds. “Market participants are growing leery of quickly rising leverage from issuers previously characterized by strong and reliable cash flow,” the report said. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Cubs’ Pete Crow-Armstrong adds even more fuel to MVP argument with latest leadoff home run
articles.summary: The Chicago Cubs are taking on the Cincinnati Reds on Saturday, as the team continues its push for the playoffs. Pete Crow-Armstrong launched an impressive leadoff home run in the contest, which only strengthens his MVP case. The 24-year-old slugger sent the ball toward right-center field. Cincin
articles._body: The Chicago Cubs are taking on the Cincinnati Reds on Saturday, as the team continues its push for the playoffs. Pete Crow-Armstrong launched an impressive leadoff home run in the contest, which only strengthens his MVP case. The 24-year-old slugger sent the ball toward right-center field . Cincinnati’s outfielders had no chance of getting to the ball, as it soared well into the stands at Wrigley Field. The home run gave the Cubs an early 1-0 lead to begin the contest. Pete Crow-Armstrong leads off the day for the @Cubs with a TANK pic.twitter.com/4eLqSBgNi1 — MLB (@MLB) August 29, 2026 That leadoff home run put Crow-Armstrong in the Cubs’ history books. It was the eighth leadoff blast this season, which ties him for second most in a single campaign in franchise history with Rick Monday, according to MLB reporter Sara Langs. Alfonso Soriano holds the record with 12. “Most leadoff home runs in a season, Cubs history,” Langs said. “2007 Alfonso Soriano: 12. 2026 Pete Crow-Armstrong: 8. 1976 Rick Monday: 8.” The NL MVP race appears to be between Pete Crow-Armstrong and Shohei Ohtani . Both players have put on strong performances throughout this season. However, the Cubs’ four-year pro has taken his offensive production to a new level while maintaining his impressive defensive skills. Crow-Armstrong entered Saturday’s contest against the Reds with a .277 batting average and .374 OBP. He leads MLB with a highly impressive 7.9 WAR. He’s managed to hit two home runs in the first three innings against Cincinnati, so his home run totals have reached 35 on the season. Chicago has just 26 games remaining on the schedule (after Saturday’s game vs. the Reds). Crow-Armstrong has a few weeks to put together his case for the MVP Award before the start of the playoffs in October. articles.title: Is USC football’s Tanook Hines playing vs. San Jose State?
articles.summary: With the USC football program preparing for the 2026 season, the first game comes on Saturday afternoon against San Jose State in a Week 0 contest to get the year started. However, there has been concern surrounding USC football quarterback Jayden Maiava’s top target for the Week 0 contest
articles._body: With the USC football program preparing for the 2026 season , the first game comes on Saturday afternoon against San Jose State in a Week 0 contest to get the year started. However, there has been concern surrounding U SC football quarterback Jayden Maiava’s top target for the Week 0 contest and whether he was going to play, as the latest update confirms his status. All eyes are on Trojans wide receiver Tanook Hines, who is slated to be the top pass-catcher on the roster, though it looks like he won’t play in the Week 0 game on Saturday against San Jose State. According to Ryan Kartje of The Los Angeles Times, Hines is “not dressed” for the outing, which he considers to be “no surprise.” “USC’s presumptive No. 1 receiver Tanook Hines is not dressed today, due to injury,” Kartje wrote on X, formerly Twitter. “No surprise. But expect a lot of freshmen receiver action today.” Hines is likely to be the top target in the offense for the USC football team after leading receivers from the 2025 season, Makai Lemon and Ja’Kobi Lane, are currently in the NFL with the Philadelphia Eagles and Baltimore Ravens, respectively. USC football’s Lincoln Riley on Tanook Hines’ injury progress In 2025, Hines recorded 561 yards on 34 catches with two touchdowns, averaging 16.5 yards per reception, but an offseason surgery in the spring, which is undisclosed, put a dent in offseason training. For a majority of the fall camp sessions, Hines was a non-participant, though following practice on Thursday, head coach Lincoln Riley said the sophomore had an “increase in activity the past 10 to 14 days,” via Sports Illustrated. “He’s definitely progressed enough to kind of look like himself, which has been great,” Riley said about Hines. “He’s close, there’s no question. I mean, if he plays this game, that’s great, and if he doesn’t, he’s certainly not far away.” At any rate, it remains to be seen when Hines is back on the field for the Trojans, as the next opportunity comes on Friday, Sept. 4, against the Fresno State Bulldogs. articles.title: Cardinals DFA veteran reliever with latest roster move
articles.summary: The St. Louis Cardinals made a bullpen-related roster change Saturday, promoting left-hander Brycen Mautz from Triple-A Memphis while designating veteran reliever Caleb Ferguson for assignment ahead of their matchup with the Pittsburgh Pirates. Mautz, 25, returns to the majors after spending most
articles._body: The St. Louis Cardinals made a bullpen-related roster change Saturday, promoting left-hander Brycen Mautz from Triple-A Memphis while designating veteran reliever Caleb Ferguson for assignment ahead of their matchup with the Pittsburgh Pirates. Mautz, 25, returns to the majors after spending most of the 2026 season with Memphis. The Cardinals’ 2025 Minor League Pitcher of the Year owns a 1-6 record and 3.78 ERA across 31 Triple-A appearances, including 16 starts. He has worked 85 2/3 innings and recorded 89 strikeouts against 65 walks. Although Mautz began the season as a starter, Memphis has gradually shifted him toward relief work. His most recent 15 appearances have all come from the bullpen, a transition that could help St. Louis manage its pitching workload. The Cardinals plan to use Mautz in a piggyback role behind Kyle Leahy against the Pirates as they attempt to control Leahy’s innings after he surpassed his previous career high. Mautz previously reached the majors on May 25 against the Milwaukee Brewers. In that appearance, he allowed two runs over three innings. The roster spot previously belonged to Ferguson, whom St. Louis acquired from the Cincinnati Reds at the 2026 trade deadline . The Cardinals sent Cincinnati $250,000 in international bonus space in the transaction, but Ferguson never settled in during his short tenure with St. Louis. The 30-year-old lefty appeared in nine games for the Cardinals, covering 8 1/3 innings while logging an 8.64 ERA. He surrendered at least one earned run in five of those nine appearances. Ferguson finished his St. Louis stint with nine strikeouts and eight walks and had pitched in three of the previous four days before being designated. His downturn was a far cry from the level of production he had maintained with the Reds, where he finished with a 4.01 ERA, 20.2% strikeout rate and 10.2% walk rate over 24 2/3 innings across 26 appearances. Because the trade deadline has passed, Ferguson can now only move to another organization through the waiver process. If he clears waivers, he has enough MLB service time to reject a minor-league assignment and become a free agent. Mautz’s promotion also leaves the Cardinals with an open spot on their 40-man roster because he was already a member of that roster. articles.title: Jarred Kelenic lands contract with Yankees, but there’s a catch
articles.summary: The New York Yankees added experienced outfield depth Saturday by signing Jarred Kelenic to a minor league contract. However, the former top prospect will not receive an immediate major league roster spot. Kelenic will report to the Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders, making the agreement
articles._body: The New York Yankees added experienced outfield depth Saturday by signing Jarred Kelenic to a minor league contract. However, the former top prospect will not receive an immediate major league roster spot. Kelenic will report to the Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders, making the agreement an organizational depth move rather than a direct promotion to Yankee Stadium. The Yankees’ outfield currently includes Cody Bellinger, Trent Grisham, Spencer Jones, and Heliot Ramos. Meanwhile, Aaron Judge continues recovering from a right rib stress fracture. MLB.com’s Bryan Hoch took to X, formerly Twitter, on Saturday to confirm the signing and assignment by the organization. “The Yankees have signed Jarred Kelenic to a Minor League contract. Reporting to Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre.” Kelenic became available after the Texas Rangers designated him for assignment last Sunday. He cleared waivers and elected free agency earlier this week rather than accepting an outright assignment. The 27-year-old batted .219 with a .313 on-base percentage and a .288 slugging percentage across 83 major league plate appearances this season. He recorded one home run and six RBIs. Kelenic produced stronger results in the minors, batting .310 with a .408 on-base percentage and a .584 slugging percentage across 63 games. He added 13 home runs and 17 stolen bases. The New York Mets selected Kelenic sixth overall in the 2018 MLB Draft before trading him to the Seattle Mariners that December. Robinson Cano and Edwin Diaz were included in the package sent to New York. Kelenic later played for the Atlanta Braves, Chicago White Sox, and Rangers. He owns a career .211/.283/.371 major league slash line across 1,571 plate appearances. The Yankees did not add Kelenic to their 40-man roster and have not announced a September promotion plan. Kelenic’s assignment gives him another opportunity to show that his minor league production can translate against major league pitching. For now, at least, he is heading to Scranton rather than the Bronx. The post Jarred Kelenic lands contract with Yankees, but there’s a catch appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles._body: Hello Everyone, I have been working on Rysh (Apache 2.0 licence), a new AI harnessing tool that lets you have the followings 1. Dominick Giudice “Being named captain is definitely one of the greatest honors of my liftime,” Giudice said. “Honestly, it just shows how the team and the coaches see me. And I think he really found a position where he can stick at. He’s just been getting better every day. And Jack (Lange) , me and him been working side by side all summer. Just being part of a team and being captain means a lot to me.” Nicholas Rodriguez “I’m grateful for the opportunity,” Rodriguez said. “It was a blessing. I’m not the only one though, we have a team. We all try to lead together and go toward our common goal together. articles.title: Tim McGraw Pokes Fun at Himself After Onstage Fall at Cincinnati Concert
articles.summary: “Cincinnati, you started our weekend off on the right foot even if I couldn’t stay on mine,” the country star joked.
articles._body: Tim McGraw is laughing off a tumble he took onstage during his Pawn Shop Guitar Tour. In fan-captured footage from his concert at Cincinnati’s Riverbend Music Center on Thursday (Aug. 27), the 59-year-old country star took a spill while belting out his 1995 hit “I Like It, I Love It.” Related Watch Lainey Wilson & Tim McGraw Team Up for a Striking Duet During CMA Fest TV Special Nashville Airport to Be Renamed for Dolly Parton, Tennessee Governor Announces Tim McGraw To Join Hulu Show ‘Southern Bastards’ In the clip, McGraw’s cowboy boot appears to get caught in a crevice onstage, sending him to the ground. But the “Humble and Kind” singer quickly got back on his feet and continued singing without missing a beat. McGraw later poked fun at the onstage mishap in a social media post. “Cincinnati, you started our weekend off on the right foot even if I couldn’t stay on mine,” he captioned a photo gallery from the show on Instagram . “We appreciate you coming out and singing along! Detroit, you’re up!” Fans quickly took to the comments section to playfully react to the fall. “I bet your daughters blew up the family group chat,” one person wrote. Another joked, “bubble wrap him for tonight.” A third commended the singer for his professionalism, writing, “SO GLAD YOU DIDN’T HURT YOURSELF! YOU ARE A REAL PRO YOU JUMPED RIGHT UP AND DIDN’T EVEN MISS A BEAT.” The Grammy-winning superstar launched his Pawn Shop Guitar Tour in mid-July. The North American trek — featuring support from The Chicks, Lady A, 49 Winchester and Timothy Wayne on select dates — is scheduled to wrap Sept. 29 in West Palm Beach, Florida. From there, he’ll head to Las Vegas in October for a five-night residency at The Colosseum at Caesars Palace. McGraw did not address the death of iconic country singer Dolly Parton during Thursday’s Cincinnati concert, but he paid tribute to her earlier in the week on social media. “She was an icon and showed us all what was possible, not only as a human but as an entertainer,” McGraw wrote on Instagram . “She was the blueprint, head and shoulders above anyone that came before her and all those of us that have come after.” Parton died on Aug. 25 following a “brief battle with cancer,” according to her team.

articles.title: North Carolina’s halftime lead over TCU snaps embarrassing Bill Belichick streak
articles.summary: The North Carolina Tar Heels ended the first half of their Week 0 matchup against the TCU Horned Frogs with a narrow 12-10 lead. It just so happens that UNC’s lead managed to snap a rather embarrassing streak in the Bill Belichick era. The 12-10 lead over TCU on Saturday marks the first tim
articles._body: The North Carolina Tar Heels ended the first half of their Week 0 matchup against the TCU Horned Frogs with a narrow 12-10 lead. It just so happens that UNC’s lead managed to snap a rather embarrassing streak in the Bill Belichick era . The 12-10 lead over TCU on Saturday marks the first time North Carolina has held a halftime lead over a Power Conference opponent with Belichick as head coach, according to Bleacher Report CFB. That means the Tar Heels never once held a lead going into halftime during the 74-year-old’s first year with the program. “North Carolina’s first halftime lead vs a Power Conference opponent under Bill Belichick,” Bleacher Report posted. “Can the Tar Heels hold on in Ireland?” Perhaps it’s a sign of good things to come for Belichick and the Tar Heels. His first year as head coach was a bit of a disaster, as the program ended the 2024-25 campaign with a 4-8 record. But changes were made to the coaching staff this offseason, as Belichick hired longtime coach Bobby Petrino to step in as the new offensive coordinator. The first half against TCU on Saturday was close. North Carolina’s offense looked a bit more productive under Petrino, as the Tar Heels ended the first two quarters with 197 total yards (152 passing, 45 rushing). Meanwhile, the defense allowed 160 total yards, but limited the Horned Frogs to just 80 passing yards. It’s just the first game of the new campaign in his second year as head coach, but Bill Belichick very well could be on the hot seat . College football is a win-now league, and that’s what the six-time Super Bowl-winning head coach (has an additiona two as a defensive coordinator) hopes to do this season. articles.summary: With the Cleveland Guardians surging in the AL Central race, the team is looking to be fully healthy by the time the postseason comes around, as the team has been without slugger Rhys Hoskins. As the Guardians prepare for the playoffs, the latest injury update on Hoskins has been revealed. Hoskin
articles._body: With the Cleveland Guardians surging in the AL Central race , the team is looking to be fully healthy by the time the postseason comes around, as the team has been without slugger Rhys Hoskins. As the Guardians prepare for the playoffs , the latest injury update on Hoskins has been revealed. Hoskins has not played for Cleveland since Aug 18.’s game against the San Francisco Giants, where he went on the 10-day injured list (IL), as he’s dealing with lower back inflammation. While he’s reportedly “feeling better,” the 33-year-old “has not resumed baseball activities.” According to Tim Stebbins at MLB.com, manager Stephen Vogt said Hoskins had felt lingering lower back tightness during the series against the Chicago White Sox from Aug. 7 to Aug. 9. Also feeling it during that Aug. 18 game against San Francisco, he would go through an MRI the next day, leading to the IL stint. “He felt like he just wasn’t himself, and so we felt like it was time for him to go on IL,” Vogt said at the time. More on the injury to Guardians’ Rhys Hoskins So far this season with the Guardians, Hoskins has recorded a .179 batting average to go along with 13 home runs and 38 RBIs in 95 games and 263 at-bats. Hoskins’ role was taking a lot of at-bats against left-handed pitchers, as Vogt said after Cleveland put the veteran on the IL that the hope is that the stint away could have him “feeling good for the home stretch” ahead. “We haven’t had a whole lot of versatility on our roster the last few weeks,” Vogt said. “Unfortunate news on Rhys, obviously. We’re hoping that this stint can get him back to feeling good for the home stretch. But good to have David and his versatility back.” At any rate, the next nine games are at home, with the hope that he could come back during that time, though the latest update on not resuming baseball activities could put a dent in the plans. The Guardians are currently 68-67, which puts them second in the AL Central, three-and-a-half games back of first. articles._body: I needed to make a tiny webapp backend to upload to shared LAMP hosting (they still exist, and I think they're fun despite us being well beyond 2005), but I couldn't face waiting for FTP to sync down however thousands files Laravel or similar frameworks need. So I made a tiny PHP framework that gets packaged into a single file. I'm using it for my own shady purposes, but I decided to put it on GitHub in case anyone else finds the approach useful.
