articles.title: Michigan OL Nathan Efobi is meaner, leaner and ready to seize his opportunity
articles.summary: Michigan Wolverines football senior Nathan Efobi redshirt while being a part of a national championship-winning offensive line his freshman year in 2023. The Wolverines held up against SEC power Alabama in the CFP semifinal, then bludgeoned Washington to the tune of 303 rushing yards in the title ga
articles._body: Michigan Wolverines football senior Nathan Efobi redshirt while being a part of a national championship-winning offensive line his freshman year in 2023. The Wolverines held up against SEC power Alabama in the CFP semifinal, then bludgeoned Washington to the tune of 303 rushing yards in the title game victory over Washington. Over the last two seasons, Michigan offensive linemen have spoken about the need for the group to be as cohesive as it was in 2023. Last year, a big emphasis was spending time together off the field. Now, Michigan has most of its offensive line back, and a much more experienced group is continuing to bond while learning from Jim Harding , one of the best to coach the position at the college level. I think it’s a brotherhood,” Efobi said. “We hang out every single day, so just keeping that strong-knit, closeness together of what an O-line should have and how we had it in 2023 is just a big part of this game. “[I’m close with] really all of them. [Junior center] Jake [Guarnera is] my roommate. [Senior Evan] Link , [junior Andrew] Sprague , [junior] Blake [Frazier ], all of them. Really cool guys.” From 2024-25, Michigan’s offensive line was coached by Grant Newsome , a former U-M offensive lineman that went into coaching after medically retiring. Newsome, now an assistant offensive line coach for the New York Giants, is on the rise in coaching, but he had much less experience than Harding, who’s been an offfensive line coach in college since 2009. “It’s just experience — years of experience,” Efobi said of Harding. “Hall of Famer at Toledo. I don’t think I’ve ever heard anyone say anything bad about Coach Harding since I’ve been here and known him. He had two first-round picks [this spring at Utah], so it’s just having his knowledge, his confidence, just learning new techniques have been great. “I think just the way he vocalizes things. He’s going to tell you the truth, and that’s all you really need as an offensive line. You’re not going to be able to sugarcoat stuff on the field. You let up a sack, and he’s going to be mad, but he’s going to always want you to get better.” The line has taken his lessons to heart, including the most important thing that the group is focused on. “Just physicality, really,” Efobi revealed. “Just letting your actions speak louder than your words, because we don’t really need to talk a lot. You’re going to see it on the field regardless of what we say.” The 6-foot-4, 303-pound Efobi has repped at both left and right guard this offseason. With the assumption that Link will take the starting left guard job, Efobi is most likely to start on the right side. However, as of his conversation with the media Thursday, he was unsure of where he’ll end up and if he’ll start. “Anywhere, as long as I get to see the field,” Efobi said. Michigan’s coaches have a good idea of what the starting offensive line will be, but the players didn’t know as of that time. “[I’d like to know] ss soon as possible, but it is what it is,” Efobi noted. “I’m going to keep working like I’m a starter just to see it happen. “I don’t know anything. I’m just keeping my head down to work, and I don’t really know anything.” Efobi was a backup last season but made some spot starts while others were injured. He appeared in al 13 games, opening five of them at left guard. He took 315 snaps on the left side of the line and 37 on the right. An Atlanta, Ga., native, Efobi feels much more prepared now, revealing that he’s only 19 percent body fat now compared to 23 at this time last year. “The biggest differences are mentality and strength,” Efobi said. “I feel a lot stronger, just built around leaner, faster. I just feel more ready for the season than last year.” The biggest competitor to Efobi this offseason is one of his good friends, senior Brady Norton , a 6-foot-4, 310-pounder who transferred to Michigan from Cal Poly ahead of the 2025 campaign. Norton played in seven games last season, starting at right guard against Oklahoma and Texas. “That’s my dawg. We’re always here to compete, always here to push ourselves to the next level,” Efobi said of Norton. “Just knowing that he’s there to have my back, anytime he’s got questions, I’ve got questions. We’re just here to help each other. It’s just still love at the end of the day.” Whoever’s out there, the 2026 Michigan Wolverines are looking to prove doubters wrong. “People have us as underdogs, and that’s how we like it,” Efobi said. “We’re very hungry. We know what we want to do. We know what our angle is, and we’re just trying to win.”

articles.title: Red Sox make big Garrett Whitlock roster move during Yankees series
articles.summary: The Boston Red Sox are trying to overtake the New York Yankees for second place in the American League East. Amidst a key series between the clubs this weekend, Boston is making a pivotal roster move. The Red Sox are reinstating pitcher Garrett Whitlock from the injured list, per the team. Whitlo
articles._body: The Boston Red Sox are trying to overtake the New York Yankees for second place in the American League East. Amidst a key series between the clubs this weekend, Boston is making a pivotal roster move. The Red Sox are reinstating pitcher Garrett Whitlock from the injured list, per the team. Whitlock has been bothered by an elbow injury. “The 30-year-old reliever never made any rehab appearances in the minors but still figures to immediately slot back in as the Red Sox’s top setup man for closer Aroldis Chapman. Wyatt Olds was optioned to Triple-A in a corresponding move,” CBS Sports reported. New York is currently second in the AL East. The Yankees defeated the Red Sox on Friday, 1-0. Boston is third in the division and hopes to win out the remainder of games in this series. It has truly been a wild season for Boston. The Red Sox struggled out of the gate , and ended up firing manager Alex Cora. After Cora’s firing, the team has found success. Boston went on a 15-game win streak over the summer, to catch up in the standings. Boston knows how important it is to win games against the Yankees at this point in the campaign. The Red Sox could host a postseason series against New York, if they can catch up. “That’s important,” Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy said, per MLB.com. “I won’t shy away from that. It’s a home-field advantage when you’re playing at home for most people. It wasn’t for us for a while, but it has been lately. So, yeah, I think if you get a short series, and you’re able to play in your home ballpark, that stuff matters for sure.” The two teams are in action again on Saturday. articles._body: The Chicago Sky could be without veteran guard Natasha Cloud when they face the New York Liberty on Saturday afternoon. Chicago listed Cloud as questionable with a right knee injury on its latest injury report ahead of Saturday’s matchup. The Sky (15-24) will look to snap a two-game losing streak against the Liberty (23-16) at 1 p.m. ET on CBS and Paramount+. Cloud joins DiJonai Carrington on the injury report, with Carrington also listed as questionable because of a left foot injury. Chicago remains without veteran guard Skylar Diggins, who has been sidelined since July 7 with a right knee injury. Cloud played 16 minutes in the Sky’s 87-81 loss to the Connecticut Sun on Tuesday. The 34-year-old guard finished with three points, four assists, one steal and one block while shooting 1-for-3 from the field. Watch WNBA games LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Despite the injury concern, Cloud has provided Chicago with consistent production during her first season with the organization. She is averaging 11.3 points, 5.0 assists, 3.5 rebounds and 1.1 steals per game while shooting 48.3% from the field and 35.2% from 3-point range. Cloud has appeared in 38 games, including 25 starts, while averaging 28.7 minutes per contest. Her status will be worth monitoring as Chicago attempts to get back into the win column against a Liberty team that enters Saturday with a 23-16 record. Following Saturday’s game, the Sky will return home Thursday to host the Washington Mystics (24-16) at 8 p.m. ET on MNMT. The post Is Natasha Cloud playing today? articles.title: Giants’ John Harbaugh makes huge Odell Beckham Jr. roster declaration
articles.summary: Just like at the end of every preseason, the New York Giants are faced with the same question heading into the regular season: who will make it to the 53-man roster and who will not. One name that keeps popping up is Odell Beckham Jr. The speculation around the veteran wide receiver’s roster stat
articles._body: Just like at the end of every preseason, the New York Giants are faced with the same question heading into the regular season: who will make it to the 53-man roster and who will not. One name that keeps popping up is Odell Beckham Jr. The speculation around the veteran wide receiver’s roster status gained traction after the Giants’ 23-6 victory over the New York Jets in the preseason finale. However, coach John Harbaugh recently addressed the situation but did not give away too much . “I think he has done enough to make an NFL roster for sure. He’s played well. He’s gotten better as camp’s gone along, and I think he deserves credit for that,” Harbaugh said, via the SNY Giants’ X, formerly Twitter, account. John Harbaugh is asked if Odell Beckham Jr. has done enough to make the Giants: "Yes, he has done enough to make an NFL roster – he's played well." pic.twitter.com/bEz4WnV0yE — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) August 29, 2026 While the final 53-man roster decision will only be official at 6 p.m. on Sunday, there’s a good chance Beckham will make it . Two of the Giants’ wide receiver candidates have been struggling with injuries. Malik Nabers is nursing a knee injury, and his roster inclusion remains unclear, while Calvin Austin III has been dealing with a season-ending injury. Though this is not the ideal outlook for the Giants, the situation might play in favor of Beckham. Additionally, he also shared the dream of making it to the roster . “It would mean everything. It would be my dream. This is where I started. There’s no place I want to give my whole heart to, more than anything else in the world, is this place right here,” Beckham said. "Super grateful for the opportunity. At this point, it's in God's hands. I know that I have a good feeling about myself – there's ball to be played, plays to be made." – Odell Beckham Jr. pic.twitter.com/aLCY7LCHgA — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) August 29, 2026 As for his stats, Beckham did not play last season due to the league’s six-game suspension. He remained an unsigned free agent for violating the NFL’s PED policy. However, during the 2024 NFL regular season, Beckham was with the Miami Dolphins, where he caught nine passes for 55 yards without any touchdowns in the nine games he played for the franchise. articles.title: Buccaneers GM ‘very optimistic’ about Baker Mayfield’s future despite contract drama
articles.summary: Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is entering the final year of his contract, but ESPN’s Dan Graziano projects he will lead Tampa Bay back to the NFC South title and ultimately secure a lucrative long-term extension before hitting unrestricted free agency. The future of Tampa Bay’s pass
articles._body: Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is entering the final year of his contract, but ESPN’s Dan Graziano projects he will lead Tampa Bay back to the NFC South title and ultimately secure a lucrative long-term extension before hitting unrestricted free agency. The future of Tampa Bay’s passing attack is a key storyline, especially since contract discussions were put on hold ahead of the 2026 season. After feeling undervalued and disrespected by the initial offseason extension offers from the organization, Mayfield decided to pause all contract negotiations when he arrived at training camp, choosing instead to bet on himself and play out the last year of his deal. Despite this standoff and the ongoing drama, the Buccaneers’ front office remains confident that their relationship with the Pro Bowl quarterback will extend beyond the current season. General manager Jason Licht spoke about the situation during an appearance on WFLA’s broadcast of Friday night’s preseason finale, stating that he expects Mayfield to stay in Tampa long term. “I’m very optimistic about it,” Licht said, via Jenna Laine of ESPN.com. “He wants to play. He wants to prove to us that he is the franchise quarterback that we said he was. We’ll just have to see how it plays out. I’ll never close the door on anything in the short term, but right now, he’s focused on football.” With the franchise tag available for 2027, Tampa Bay maintains control over the situation, allowing both sides time to navigate the season before revisiting financial terms. For Mayfield, the immediate focus is on raising the team’s operational and competitive standards ahead of Week 1. After a sluggish joint practice session against the Jacksonville Jaguars, he called out his teammates for a lack of physical intensity, admitting that the Jaguars “played with their hair on fire” and emphasizing that the Buccaneers must improve their toughness as shown in film. articles.title: Will Jets have more kicking competition after rough Jason Sanders preseason showing?
articles.summary: The New York Jets may have another decision to make at kicker after Jason Sanders struggled during Friday night’s 23-6 preseason loss to the New York Giants. New York appeared to settle its kicking competition earlier in the week by releasing Cade York, leaving Sanders as the expected optio
articles._body: The New York Jets may have another decision to make at kicker after Jason Sanders struggled during Friday night’s 23-6 preseason loss to the New York Giants . New York appeared to settle its kicking competition earlier in the week by releasing Cade York , leaving Sanders as the expected option entering the 2026 regular season. However, Sanders missed an extra point following a first-quarter touchdown and later missed a field goal in the fourth quarter. Pro Football Talk’s Josh Alper questioned whether Sanders’ performance could push the Jets to explore other options before their Week 1 matchup against the Tennessee Titans . “The Jets appeared to end their kicking competition this week when they released Cade York, but Jason Sanders’s performance on Friday night may have opened things back up,” Alper wrote. Jets head coach Aaron Glenn acknowledged the misses but said the organization will not rush into a decision. “Am I worried about it? I didn’t like the fact that we missed these field goals, but the thing is we’re not going to panic and we’re going to make sure that we make the right decision to make sure we either fix those issues or we get the right person in here,” Glenn said. “But Jason has been good for us. He’s been good in practice. I’m going to evaluate that and see exactly what direction we’ll go.” Jason Sanders faces uncertainty ahead of Jets’ Week 1 matchup Sanders brings significant experience to New York after spending seven seasons as the Miami Dolphins’ kicker. However, he missed the entire 2025 season because of a hip injury before joining the Jets. His preseason finale now gives New York another factor to evaluate before finalizing its plans at kicker. The Jets will open the regular season on the road against the Titans on Sunday, Sept. 13, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS, giving Glenn and his staff two weeks to determine whether Sanders remains their answer at the position. articles.title: Casey’s quietly became America’s fifth-largest pizza chain. Meet the Fortune 500 gas station Gen Z can’t stop posting about
articles.summary: Have you heard of the fifth-largest pizza chain in the U.S., famous for its red roof, its taco pizza and its sausage gravy-base, breakfast slices?
articles._body: Drive through Iowa, Missouri or Illinois, and you’ll pass a Casey’s roughly every few exits. Midwesterners have come to know the red-roofed convenience store and gas station where people buy diesel, a bag of ice, a lottery ticket and, increasingly, a hot pizza. Maybe it’s one of their distinctive creations, like the taco pizza or the breakfast pizza. Casey’s is closing in on 3,000 stores, nearly half of which sit in towns of 5,000 people or fewer and about two-thirds in towns under 20,000. The Fortune 500 company’s stock price is surging as America wakes up to the stealth pizza empire sitting under its nose: it’s up more than 50% in the past 12 months for a market capitalization of $28 billion. Bank of America Research recently ran the numbers and concluded that Casey’s pizza business ranks as the fifth-largest pizza chain in the entire U.S., when measured by prepared food and dispensed beverage sales. Tom Brennan, Casey’s chief merchandising officer, confirmed to Fortune that it is the fifth-largest pizza chain and the fourth-largest liquor license holder in the U.S., not to mention third-largest convenience store. “You don’t hear the other big pizza players talk about Casey’s,” he added, “but at the same time, it’s evident from our growth … we’re taking share as we continue to grow.” Ask Brennan whether “stealth” is a fair word for his company and he laughs a little at an out-of-touch, coastal way of thinking. “Certainly stealthy for, I think, a lot of the U.S.,” but ask anyone in its 19 states, and they’ll know Casey’s. That’s starting to change a bit online. TikTok and YouTube have built a small, oddly durable genre around “ gas-station pizza ” — creators bracing for something left under a heat lamp then wowed by something genuinely good. Casey’s turns up constantly in the genre, praised for its scratch-made dough and on-site pizza ovens, and Brennan said he welcomes it. Casey’s social team found its penetration with Gen Z has climbed 600 basis points over the past three years based on engagement. “What underpins all of this is just this incredible fandom and brand love that we’ve generated.” It all comes down to something an algorithm can’t fake, he added, an authenticity so beloved in the age of AI backlash and analog fever. “It’s really built on decades of delivering high-quality pizza and food, a great experience.” Brennan argued that Casey’s is the “gathering spot” for its communities, and it keeps adding new features, like its Sauced Wings, which began as a pilot in January 2025 and have now grown to almost 900 stores, gradually rolling out across the chain over the next two years. courtesy of Casey’s A moat across small-town America Casey’s origin traces back to 1968, when Donald Lamberti opened a converted service station in Boone, Iowa. Brennan said he’s talked to Lamberti about his strategy, describing it as, “Hey, this will probably work in the next small town.” He described a gradual, slow-and-steady, now explosive growth: “Literally, they just went from small town to small town, building Casey’s.” Over time, this became what Wall Street calls a “defensible moat,” because most other brands simply aren’t looking “to develop sites in towns that small.” The company is still chasing the same bet that small is beautiful: build where the population is too small for anyone else to bother, and eventually you’re outcompeting Big Pizza on turf it never thought to conquer. Pizza joined the menu in 1984, and breakfast pizza about two decades later, what Brennan calls an “iconic” mix of sausage gravy, egg and cheese. This strategy also means Casey’s is fighting a different war than its pizza competitors — if you consider them competitors. The roughly $31 billion quick-service pizza category turned negative in 2025, per Technomic, after barely growing the year before. The Wall Street Journal reported in January 2026 that America appeared to be “falling out of love with pizza.” Brennan said Casey’s was watching the trend closely, but the company has a different view. “About half of our stores don’t have a national pizza competitor within what we consider a competitive rating,” he said. And when Casey’s does come to a nearby town, “we’re bringing something that hasn’t been really on offer there. And it’s resonating.” Brennan added that Casey’s works to keep pizza and other key items priced slightly below the prevailing market rate. Citing inflation data, he noted that over the past three years, food away-from-home prices are up about 14%, while Casey’s prepared food and dispensed beverage business is only up 5%. “We can leverage the other parts of the business to make the total P&L work while we invest, essentially, to grow food.” BofA noted the unglamorous math: prepared food and beverages carried an estimated 58% gross margin in fiscal 2025, more than double Casey’s overall margin of roughly 23.5%. Brennan calls the Casey’s model “three legs of the stool,” as food, convenience and merchandise combine to prop up one another. Pizza is the “crown jewel” of the food business, he said, but to him, Casey’s is a “category of one,” with “the magic of the brand [being] when we have all three legs of the stool working together.” Math points to Casey’s next frontier: Texas. Iowa has about 3 million people and 550 Casey’s stores, he notes, while Texas has roughly 30 million people and room to run. “We see that as Casey’s country,” Brennan said, pointing to the small towns along the

articles.title: Blue Jays ace Dylan Cease accomplishes feat not seen since Randy Johnson 25 years ago
articles.summary: Toronto Blue Jays right-hander Dylan Cease extended one of baseball’s longest modern strikeout streaks Friday, becoming the first pitcher since Randy Johnson in 2001 to record at least seven strikeouts in 19 consecutive starts. Cease struck out eight across six innings in Toronto’s 8-1 victory ov
articles._body: Toronto Blue Jays right-hander Dylan Cease extended one of baseball’s longest modern strikeout streaks Friday, becoming the first pitcher since Randy Johnson in 2001 to record at least seven strikeouts in 19 consecutive starts. Cease struck out eight across six innings in Toronto’s 8-1 victory over the Seattle Mariners at Rogers Centre. He allowed four hits, one run, and one walk across 92 pitches, improving to 9-5 and lowering his ERA to 2.33. Sportsnet shared a graphic Saturday through its official account on X, formerly Twitter, following the Blue Jays’ dominant seven-run win, pointing out the importance of the 2026 All-Star pitcher’s hot stretch. “Dylan Cease, strikeout machine ” Dylan Cease, strikeout machine pic.twitter.com/zO7PkuQfUY — Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) August 29, 2026 The streak began May 2 and now spans four months. Friday’s outing increased Cease’s season total to an American League-leading 217 strikeouts through 150 1/3 innings. He also owns a 1.05 WHIP as the regular season enters its final month. Those totals place him among the league’s most productive starters. Dominic Canzone opened the scoring with a first-inning solo homer, but Cease quickly settled. He struck out the side in the second inning and retired nine consecutive hitters while keeping Seattle from adding another run. Toronto supported him with 11 hits and three home runs. George Springer went 4-for-4 with a homer and three runs scored, while Nathan Lukes and Kazuma Okamoto also went deep. Okamoto’s sixth-inning shot was his 27th of the season, extending the Blue Jays’ rookie home run record. The victory improved the Blue Jays to 66-70 on the season, moving the club within 2 1/2 games of the Cleveland Guardians for the third and final American League wild-card position. Cease’s consistency has also strengthened his case in the AL Cy Young Award race. His 19-start run demonstrates sustained swing-and-miss production while Toronto remains within reach of a postseason berth. With 26 games remaining after Friday’s victory, the Blue Jays need their ace to continue providing dependable innings and strikeouts. His next start offers another opportunity to extend a streak unmatched in a single season for 25 years. articles._body: The Buffalo Bills are moving forward with rookie punter Tommy Doman Jr. after deciding to release veteran Mitch Wishnowsky as part of their roster cuts ahead of the 2026 NFL season. NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reported the decision Saturday morning via X, formerly known as Twitter. “The Bills informed veteran punter Mitch Wishnowsky they plan to release him, per source. Rookie seventh-round pick Tommy Doman Jr. is now in line to punt for Buffalo.” The move comes after Buffalo completed a perfect 3-0 preseason with a 28-27 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday night. Buffalo selected Doman with the No. 239 overall pick in the seventh round of the 2026 NFL Draft. The 23-year-old entered training camp competing with Wishnowsky for the punting job and has now emerged as the Bills’ expected option heading into the regular season. Wishnowsky brought significant NFL experience to the competition after spending several seasons in the league, but Buffalo ultimately elected to go with the younger, cheaper option at the position. The punter decision is one of several roster moves the Bills have made following the conclusion of the preseason. Buffalo is also releasing veteran wide receiver Mecole Hardman Jr. , a three-time Super Bowl champion who appeared in two regular-season games for the Bills during the 2025 campaign. Buffalo will continue reducing its roster as the regular season approaches. The Bills will open their 2026 schedule on the road against the Houston Texans on Sunday, Sept. 13, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS, with Doman now positioned to handle punting duties in Week 1. articles.summary: Time is running out for Major League Baseball teams to keep themselves in the race for a postseason spot in 2026. Some clubs are truly struggling, while others are separating themselves from the pack. According to a new column by MLB.com’s Travis Sawchik, there are five potential playoff da
articles._body: Time is running out for Major League Baseball teams to keep themselves in the race for a postseason spot in 2026. Some clubs are truly struggling, while others are separating themselves from the pack. According to a new column by MLB.com’s Travis Sawchik, there are five potential playoff dark horses . Those teams are: Cleveland Guardians, Houston Astros, Seattle Mariners, Baltimore Orioles and Pittsburgh Pirates. Sawchik argues these clubs have a solid mix of starting pitching, bullpen strength, and powerful bats in their respective lineups. Four of these teams are in the American League, which has been somewhat of a mess this season. Nearly every team in the AL is still in the race for a postseason berth, due to the relative weakness of the American League this season. Pittsburgh is the only NL team on the writer’s list. It appears highly unlikely that the Pirates will be able to reach the postseason, for a big reason. That is because the National League has a plethora of teams with winning records, while the Pirates are currently at 65-71 on the season. The Guardians and the Astros are the two clubs on this list that currently have winning records, heading into Saturday. Both Cleveland and Houston are 68-67 overall on the campaign. The Astros actually lead the American League West , with that mark. “The Astros have been in a gentle decline from their peak years last decade, but they still have a chance to do damage in October if they enter. One big reason? They enjoy an improving bullpen,” Sawchik wrote. Seattle and Baltimore meanwhile both have losing records this season. The Orioles are 66-69, and currently fourth in the AL East. Baltimore would need to go on a huge run to climb back in the standings and catch up with Boston, New York and Tampa Bay. The Mariners meanwhile sit at 64-71 on the season. Seattle is currently third in the AL West. The post MLB rumors: The 5 potential playoff dark horses, per reporter appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.summary: Do you remember the great Banana Man controversy of summer 2026? At the Baltimore hardcore band End It’s Toronto show in early June, frontman Akil Godsey called out a guy in the pi
articles._body: Do you remember the great Banana Man controversy of summer 2026? At the Baltimore hardcore band End It’s Toronto show in early June, frontman Akil Godsey called out a guy in the pit for “[wanting] attention” with his banana costume. "You don't get rewarded for doing that shit," he told the crowd. "He wanted the attention, and now he has it." Godsey offered the setlist to whoever stripped off the costume. “People have been trying to dim my sparkle my entire life,” a distraught Banana Man wrote on Instagram after. “I was an unwilling participant, attacked and clothing removed at the direction of a band I paid to see.” Tons of online commenters, many of whom had never heard of End It or been to a hardcore show, had strong opinions about the incident. Godsey became the target of racism and death threats before addressing the situation on his own Instagram. “We’re a hardcore band,” he explained. “We do hardcore things.” Finally, three weeks after the incident, End It called a truce with banana-costumed concertgoers when Godsey hugged it out with a different Banana Man at Jera On Air . He was also handed a banana that he promptly tossed into the crowd. “Who woulda thought doing something stupid at a show would get me a month of attention?” Godsey said. Now the great End It Vs. Banana Man Feud Of 2026 has our attention again. Yesterday Godsey showed off new No Banana Man ink he got at Baltimore’s Red Thorn Tattoo, posting the reveal on his Instagram Stories. articles.title: Charli xcx Makes a Striking Statement With Reading Festival Headline Set: 5 Best Moments
articles.summary: Charli gave her first U.K. performance since the release of her eighth studio album Music, Fashion, Film.
articles._body: Earlier this week, Charli xcx took a trip down memory lane. Sitting with BBC Radio 1’s Jack Saunders, she reflected on her previous appearances as a performer at Reading Festival over the years. She was hard on herself in the way you can be when confronted with your younger, more idealistic, carefree self. “It’s cringing me out, if I’m honest,” she said of her 2017 performance. Her review of her 2019 show? She didn’t like her fringe much, she added. “This is a collection of some of the worst hairstyles and hair dyes ever throughout Reading & Leeds, it seems.” This is typical Charli, though. Few acts in modern times are as achingly aware of their presentation, their overarching narrative as a creator, or how their music or eras are received. This mindset fueled Brat , an unapologetic riposte that had, indeed, buckets of intentionality behind it. Music, Fashion, Film , her new LP, finds her ruminating deeply on the direction of her career and if being a recording artist is even something she wants to do anymore, particularly as her head is turned by acting roles.  So how will Charli xcx look back on her headline set at Reading Festival on Friday (Aug. 28)? It seems safe to say she will look back on the set with bullish pride. This set is loaded with additional subtext: It’s the first U.K. performance since the release of Music, Fashion, Film , her second No. 1 on the Official Albums Chart in 2026 following Wuthering Heights soundtrack in February 2026. It was also her first time headlining the iconic festival she grew up attending, as mentioned in her BBC Radio 1 interview. The stakes were high, not least because of Charli’s own expectations. The striking new stage production — first debuted at Lollapalooza last month — brings a thrilling edge to Charli’s performance and the songs sound fuller, less bitty than they do on record. She commanded the stage with a singular focus and was bolstered by a live band in places and a group of dancers; the result was a statement of epic proportions.  These were the five best moments from Charli’s headline debut at Reading Festival.

articles.title: Broncos coach Sean Payton provides hopeful Marvin Mims update after preseason injury
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos appear to have avoided a significant injury to Marvin Mims Jr. after the wide receiver exited Friday night’s 34-6 preseason win over the Minnesota Vikings. Broncos head coach Sean Payton provided an encouraging update on Mims after the game, describing the injury as a bru
articles._body: The Denver Broncos appear to have avoided a significant injury to Marvin Mims Jr. after the wide receiver exited Friday night’s 34-6 preseason win over the Minnesota Vikings. Broncos head coach Sean Payton provided an encouraging update on Mims after the game, describing the injury as a bruise and indicating the team exercised caution with one of its key offensive weapons. “With Mims, he’s going to be fine. It’s a bruise,” Payton said, via Pro Football Talk. “We were really more just cautious with him. There were a few guys that we were going to get some snaps with that may have been — certainly front-line guys for us and he was one of those players.” Mims suffered the injury on a third-down play when he went up for an overthrown pass from quarterback Jarrett Stidham. Mims collided with Vikings safety Jacob Thomas out of bounds before immediately grabbing his right foot after hitting the ground. Marvin Mims injury appears minor ahead of Broncos’ Week 1 opener The 24-year-old initially attempted to jog toward the sideline but was visibly limping. Medical personnel accompanied Mims as he left the field, and he threw his helmet down in frustration before sitting near the Broncos’ bench. He eventually entered the team’s medical tent before heading to the locker room. The injury created another concern for Mims after he previously missed time this summer with a separate lower-body issue. He did not appear in Denver’s first two preseason games, leading the Broncos to give him snaps Friday despite holding several other key players out of the finale. Payton’s update, however, suggests Mims avoided an injury that could threaten his availability for the beginning of the regular season. Denver will now turn its attention toward Week 1 and its AFC West matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday , Sept. 14, at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN and ABC. articles.summary: The show was the first of two headline performances at London's All Points East festival
articles._body: Tyler, The Creator opened his All Points East headline set in London by expressing gratitude that Theresa May is no longer Prime Minister — with a few expletives thrown in. Beef between the pair goes way back: May famously barred the L.A. native from the U.K. back in 2015 for allegedly “posing a threat to public order.” A lot has changed in the decade-plus since, not least the fact that Tyler is a rather different person to who he might have been deemed by some back then. His music is just as different too. Tyler’s career has, in fact, been marked by constant reinvention. Ever since his early, button-pushing days in rap troupe Odd Future, his music and artistry has blossomed to mercurial levels, weaving between the sun-kissed neo-soul of Flower Boy and iconoclastic pop-funk of IGOR to the high-energy experimentation of 2025’s Don’t Tap the Glass . Fittingly, the bill for the first of his two nights headlining Victoria Park on Friday (Aug. 28) followed that same genre-blurring instinct, a line-up reflecting not just the variation in Tyler’s own sound, but in his fans’ tastes too. On the rap front, Vince Staples brought potent, sardonic West Coast hip-hop, alongside Clipse ’s laser-sharp technicality, Sexyy Red’s club-ready Southern bangers, the Spanish drill of BB Trickz and fakemink repping the U.K. underground. For the more melodic crowd, there was Rex Orange County — a key Flower Boy collaborator making a rare recent U.K. festival appearance — along with Mariah the Scientist’s atmospheric R&B, Houston dream-pop act Love Spells, the introspective tones of Memphis singer Yebba and supermodel*’s lo-fi shoegaze, each echoing a different soulful corner of Tyler’s catalogue. Turnstile , meanwhile, held down the harsher end, as did Melbourne’s Ecca Vandal, Sydney’s Shady Nasty and the Brockhampton-approved Jean Dawson — hardcore and rock acts all mirroring Tyler’s own push-and-pull between hard and melodic sounds. As Tyler kicked off his first day at All Points East, these were the seven best moments.

articles.title: For his latest tariffs, Trump used a statute so obscure many lawyers didn’t even know it still existed. ‘This law is literally a blank canvas’
articles.summary: Trump invoked Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 to slap a 50% tax on $20 billion worth of Canadian imports.
articles._body: In firing up a trade war with Canada, President Donald Trump turned to a 96-year-old statute so obscure that many trade lawyers didn’t even know it was still on the books. A week ago, Trump invoked Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 to slap a 50% tax on $20 billion worth of Canadian imports. The move prompted dollar-for-dollar  retaliation from Ottawa  and strained already-tense relations between the neighbors and longtime allies. The president’s Section 338 tariff authority has never been used, let alone tested in court. “This law is literally a blank canvas because it’s never been litigated,’’ said Ryan Majerus, a partner at King & Spalding and a former U.S. trade official. So it’s unclear whether Trump’s latest Canada tariffs could survive a legal challenge, and some lawyers argue that the Depression-era law has been rendered obsolete by more recent trade laws. Trump raises Section 338 from the dead To sanction Canada for allegedly discriminating against U.S. dairy, auto and alcoholic beverage exports this summer, the Trump administration reached back to the Great Depression. The 1930 tariff legislation is known as the  Smoot-Hawley Act  after its congressional sponsors. With the U.S. and world economies in collapse, Congress raised tariffs on hundreds of imports in an attempt to protect American farmers and manufacturers. The tariffs are notorious among economists and historians for shutting down world commerce and making the Great Depression worse. (Trump, who proudly calls himself “Tariff Man,’’  has a different view , arguing that the Smoot-Hawley levies simply came too late to rescue the American economy.) In addition to raising tariffs themselves, lawmakers in 1930 gave the president new power to impose them himself: Section 338 authorizes presidential tariffs of up to 50% on imports from countries that have discriminated against U.S. businesses. Before Trump, no president had actually used the statute. “Until Trump’s second term, few trade lawyers were aware that Section 338 remained on the books or understood what it did,” legal scholars Peter Harrell and Jennifer Hillman of Georgetown University wrote earlier this month in the libertarian magazine Reason. They cite State Department records to show that the U.S. considered using Section 338 in trade disputes – against Spain in 1932 and against newly Communist China in 1949 – but never did. After the Depression, U.S. policy focused more on using negotiations — rather than sanctions — to open foreign markets. So Section 338 sat moldering in the law books. Other laws take hold As the years went by, the United States passed new trade laws. Some of them ceded to the president tariff power, which the U.S. Constitution originally granted to Congress. But the new laws also limited the president’s authority to certain circumstances — including dealing with national security threats and foreign currency crises — and required the government to carry out investigations and meet other procedural requirements beforehand. “There is a very strong argument that (Section 338) was superseded,’’ said Sara Albrecht, CEO of the Liberty Justice Center, a libertarian advocacy group that represented businesses that successfully challenged the earlier Trump tariffs with the Supreme Court. If Congress wanted the president to retain Section 338 power, Albrecht asks, why did lawmakers pass the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, which allowed for national security tariffs? And the Trade Act of 1974, which gives the president power to go after other countries’ unfair trade practices? Battling over Canada’s dairy market Legal experts see other weaknesses in the Section 338 tariffs. Harrell and Hillman, for instance, write in Reason that Section 338 only authorizes tariffs that “offset’’ the harm that a foreign country’s trade practices do to American companies. But in targeting Canada, they note, the Trump administration made no attempt to calculate the dollar amount of damage arising from discrimination against U.S. farmers, automakers and marketers of alcoholic beverages. And the U.S. went after Canadian imports unconnected to those trouble spots, including hockey sticks and cement. Harrell and Hillman also say that Canada’s protection of its dairy market does not single out U.S. farmers for discrimination; the rules apply to many other Canadian trading partners as well. Moreover, the United States agreed to the Canadian system – in which Canada imposes stiff tariffs on dairy imports that exceed a quota — in a North America trade pact Trump himself negotiated with Canada and Mexico in his first term. Harrell and Hillman write that it is “incongruous, to say the least, for the United States to denounce as discriminatory the very terms it agreed to.’’ But John Veroneau, former general counsel for the U.S. Trade Representative, said the Section 338 tariffs are straightforward: They are justified when another country discriminates against U.S. imports by taxing them more than it taxes imports from other countries. And in a “perverse irony,’’ Veroneau said, Canada did just that when it responded to tariffs Trump imposed on Canadian products last year with its own retaliatory tariffs on U.S. imports. “Courts will rightly feel obliged in the face of any challenge (to decide): Are the statutory requirements met or are they not met, however ludicrous the broader context might be,’’ said Veroneau, adjunct professor at the University of Maine Law School. Plaintiffs are so far hard to find Trump’s other tools to impose his protectionist agenda have already floundered in court. The  Supreme Court in February threw out  his boldest gambit: invoking a 1977 national security law to hit almost every country on Earth last year with double-digit tariffs. He made the trip, but has been bat
articles._body: The TCU football team is in Ireland, to play Bill Belichick’s North Carolina squad. TCU is without a key player for that contest, per ESPN. “Sources: TCU will be without leading returning receiver Jordan Dwyer against North Carolina in Ireland today. He made the trip, but has been battling a foot injury and will not play. He caught 54 balls for 730 yards last year and 7 TD passes,” Pete Thamel posted to X, formerly Twitter. TCU defeated North Carolina to start the 2025 season. This game is a key matchup for both teams. TCU is trying to regain the top spot in the Big 12, and a win over North Carolina would help the team’s resumé for the College Football Playoff. North Carolina meanwhile is trying to avenge a lousy 2025 season, under Belichick. Belichick’s squad went 4-8, and the sour notes of the campaign were set by a bad loss to the Horned Frogs to start the year. TCU football is breaking in a new quarterback The Horned Frogs enter the North Carolina game with a new play caller under center. That is Jaden Craig, a transfer from Harvard . Craig is getting praised ahead of the campaign. “I liked that he was experienced,” TCU head coach Sonny Dykes said about Craig, per The Athletic. “I liked that he played in an offense that was similar to what we were going to run. The biggest difference to me, though, was his presence in the pocket, his ability to shuffle, not panic and not put the ball in jeopardy.” Craig threw for 2,869 passing yards at Harvard in 2025. He also posted 25 touchdown passes, with seven interceptions. He now steps into the role of leading a power 4 college football program. “I felt there was another level of development and attention in college that I wouldn’t be able to get in the NFL,” Craig said. “That’s what drove my decision to enter the portal.” TCU plays North Carolina at 12:00 ET on Saturday. articles.title: ‘What is that saying about the applicant pool?’ The FBI will no longer treat experience with prostitution as an automatic bar against hiring
articles.summary: The shift is being made at a time when current and former officials worry that the FBI, and the Justice Department more generally, have eased recruitment requirements.
articles._body: The FBI is dropping a categorical hiring ban on applicants who have had sexual encounters with prostitutes and will instead consider in a more holistic manner at least some candidates who have engaged in the practice in the past, according to people familiar with the matter. The move away from an automatic disqualification falls along a continuum of evolving recruitment standards within federal law enforcement and at the buttoned-up bureau, which several years ago relaxed its approach to candidates’ past marijuana use and has drawn more recent concern among some current and former agents  about a perceived loosening of recruitment requirements  as it seeks to replenish its ranks. The bureau still intends to dismiss applicants who are revealed during the vetting process to have engaged in prostitution within the last 10 years, three or more times overall or while in a position of trust such as public safety, according to guidance issued this past spring and described by a person familiar with the matter who was not authorized to discuss internal decision-making and spoke on condition of anonymity. For others, it will allow for consideration of the context of the conduct rather than treat it as grounds for an automatic rejection from the FBI’s hiring process. The practical impact is not immediately clear since many who have engaged in prostitution may still be either immediately disqualified or weeded out upon further scrutiny from FBI polygraphers and security officials. The FBI said the change was meant to account for the fact that some otherwise suitable candidates, including service members, may have engaged in the practice in places where it is legal and to accommodate applicants who may done so as a young child or have themselves been victims of sexual abuse. “It is false to suggest criminal behavior like this is no longer disqualifying at the FBI. Any applicant who has engaged in criminal sexual acts like those referenced would of course not be eligible for employment, and it is ridiculous to suggest otherwise,” the FBI said in a statement that described the background check process as “wide-ranging and extensive.” “The FBI has and always will maintain some of the highest suitability standards for its applicants and employees in the US Government,” the statement added. Justice Department is easing recruitment requirements in general Even so, the shift is being made at a time when current and former officials worry that the FBI, and the Justice Department more generally, have eased recruitment requirements while facing a mass personnel exodus brought on by retirements, voluntary resignations and firings. The bureau, for instance, has taken steps to make it easier for its own professional staff to become agents and has offered a truncated training academy for applicants from other federal law enforcement agencies. “If they’re moving the bar for sexual encounters to include prostitution, what is that saying about the applicant pool? They’re trying to bring in more people, which to me indicates that the applicant pool is extremely shallow right now,” said Daniel Brunner, a retired FBI agent who spent two decades in the bureau. In 2015, then-Attorney General Eric Holder issued a memo reiterating that all Justice Department employees were prohibited from soliciting or accepting prostitution, including in places where it was legal. But both before and since that directive, the FBI and other federal law enforcement agencies have confronted periodic episodes in which agents serving abroad have been accused of sexual encounters with prostitutes. As recently as last year, for instance,  the Justice Department inspector general substantiated allegations  that a supervisory special agent solicited and used prostitutes on multiple occasions while overseas and used a bureau-issued cellphone for the transactions. Chris Piehota, a retired top FBI executive, said he would be more troubled if the bureau were to loosen its standards for current employees who require periodic renewals of their security clearances. But he said he could understand the FBI leaning “toward leniency” for actions taken as a teenager or college student. “I don’t think you get a better or worse candidate from something you did in your college years,” Piehota said. “That’s why they have the screening process, that’s why they have the vetting process. And the people who do the recruiting and hiring, they look at all those things.” Background checks, polygraph tests and more Applicants to the FBI undergo a multistep application and vetting process that includes, among other things, a background check, a detailed questionnaire, credit checks, interviews with neighbors and colleagues and a polygraph test. The comprehensive regimen is meant to uncover any prior criminal conduct in an applicant’s past as well as embarrassing personal information that could make an employee vulnerable to blackmail. Felony convictions, domestic violence convictions, failure of a urinalysis and the bureau’s drug policies are among factors treated as automatic disqualifiers. Though the new guidance will allow for a broader and more contextual evaluation of applicants who disclose past experience with prostitution during their polygraph admission, such an admission has historically been typically regarded as a “death knell” for potential employees at agencies including the FBI, CIA and NSA, said Daniel Meyer, a Washington lawyer with the Tully Rinckey law firm who specializes in the background check and the security clearance process. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles._body: My company stopped allowing Navicat because of compliance policy. DBeaver worked, but I don't like it. I kept running into two recurring issues. First, production investigations often require several queries across different databases. I would query one table, copy an ID into another query, wait for the result, and repeat the process several times. I started wondering if there was a way to handle this without writing a separate script for every case. What if I had a simple form where I could enter the query parameters I already knew, and then run a sequence of SQL statements? Following that line of thought, I ended up building Workflow. Superset is a great tool, but as a developer who mostly needed to put together a few reports for my boss, deploying and maintaining a full Superset stack felt like overkill. So I ended up building a simple Dashboards feature for saved SQL queries and reports. When Navicat stopped being an option at work, I started looking for an open-source alternative. I also wanted to solve the two recurring problems described above. That eventually led me to build DataZen, a GPLv3-licensed desktop database client built with Tauri v2, Rust, React, and TypeScript. It also includes: - A SQL editor and schema browser - Natural-language SQL using the current schema as context - SQL error diagnosis and EXPLAIN analysis - Charts from query results - MCP server/client support - An extensible database driver API - Schema diff, data sync, and data transfer tools The core database workflow works without AI. Once an AI provider is configured, it extends that same workflow with access to the active schema, query errors, execution plans, and workflow context. It can draft SQL, diagnose failures, explain plans, and automate parts of a multi-step workflow. When AI is enabled, it uses the provider configured by the user and the database context already available in DataZen. This is an early v0.1.0 release and there are still rough edges. I would especially like feedback on: - Whether YAML is a good interface for cross-database workflows - How read-only access and write approvals should work - Whether database driver extensibility is useful in practice - Which everyday database tasks are still unnecessarily repetitive GitHub: https://github.com/flyxl/datazen Downloads: https://github.com/flyxl/datazen/releases Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49490148 Points: 3 # Comments: 0

articles.title: Greensboro Grimsley rolls to 33rd straight victory
articles.summary: GREENSBORO — Clemmons (N.C.) West Forsyth went down the field and tacked on a early field goal on its first possession, and then Greensboro (N.C.) Grimsley just dominated Friday.
articles._body: GREENSBORO — Clemmons (N.C.) West Forsyth went down the field and tacked on a early field goal on its first possession, and then Greensboro (N.C.) Grimsley just dominated Friday. Grimsley scored 39 unanswered points to win 39-3 and extend its winning streak to 33 straight games. The Whirlies last loss was in the NCHSAA playoffs to Matthews (N.C.) Weddington on Nov. 24, 2023. The game Junior running back Ty Shoemake went 76 yards for a touchdown for Grimsley on the next possession after the West Forsyth field goal. Sophomore quarterback Brody Lowe threw a 22-yard touchdown pass to junior receiver Zakai Milton , and later Lowe hit Milton on a slant route for a about a 75-yard score to make it 22-3. A backward pass led to Milton’s third touchdown of the game, from 23 yards out to stretch the lead to 32-3. Milton tackled on his fourth touchdown catch on a 11-yard flanker screen from Lowe. NC State targets NC State has offered Grimsley junior defensive lineman Guy Vann and West Forsyth junior wide receiver Tylan Grimes . Vann was solid in the middle and helped slow down West Forsyth’s running game, with two particular plays that stood out. The 6-foot-3, 265-pounder was offered by NC State defensive tackles/nose tackle coach Elisha Shaw on June 18, and last went to NC State for Alpha Wolf on June 21. Vann has Power Four offers from NC State, Boston College and Louisville, along with Appalachian State, East Carolina, Georgia Souther and Samford. His father is a NC State graduate. Grimes had a few early catches but like most of the West Forsyth offense, it became tough sledding to move the ball. He was offered by NC State on Aug. 3, following attending Alpha Wolf. Grimes has Power Four offers from NC State, Boston College, Colorado, Missouri, North Carolina, South Carolina, Virginia Tech and Wake Forest, plus Delaware, East Carolina and Liberty. Potential targets The lefty Lowe is going to get heavily evaluated by colleges, and he attended NC State’s camp last June. At a listed 6-0, 195-pounder, he hasn’t lost a game yet, winning nine games as a freshman and two this season. Lowe isn’t a runner, but he makes sound decisions, has been remarkably consistent and throws with good touch and to spots where his receiver can run to and make a play. He has thrown just three interceptions in his prep career. Shoemake has proven in the past he can bust open a big run, just like he did Friday. He tallied 1,082 yareds and 16 touchdowns his sophomore year. The 5-11, 210-pounder has Power Four offers from Boston College, Duke, Louisville, Virginia and Virginia Tech. He also has been offered by Appalachian State, Connecticut, East Carolina, Liberty, Gardner-Webb and Samford. Other committted players Grimsley senior left tackle Gavin Milton is committed to Duke and both of the Whirlies senior cornerbacks have picked colleges. Evander Davis , who had an impressive interception, is head to James Madison, and Ramir Harris-Dupree has picked reigning national champions Indiana. Senior edge rusher Andrew Rogers is headed to East Carolina, but was out with an injury. articles.title: High School Football: Paramus Catholic upsets No. 1 La Salle College (Pa.)
articles.summary: Paramus Catholic (N.J.) has heard all off-season about all of the teams in North Jersey being on the come up and not be included in the conversation of best teams when it comes to high school football was taken personally. Friday night against Pennsylvania’s No. 1 ranked La Salle College (Pa.)
articles._body: Paramus Catholic (N.J.) has heard all off-season about all of the teams in North Jersey being on the come up and not be included in the conversation of best teams when it comes to high school football was taken personally. Friday night against Pennsylvania’s No. 1 ranked La Salle College (Pa.) at the Battle at the Beach Classic in Ocean City, New Jersey, the Paladins made the ultimate statement. [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] The Paladins scored 35 unanswered points en route to defeating the Explorers, 35-14, upsetting the top ranked team out of the Keystone State. 2027 3-star running back Chukwuma Odoh (Penn State commit) scored two touchdowns to lead the way offensively for Paramus Catholic. From the looks of it in the early going, it looked like La Salle College (0-1) was going to take full control of the contest as running back Ahzir Nelson scored two first quarter touchdowns to hand the Explorers a 14-0 advantage. Everything from there on out changed dramatically in the final three quarters of play. 2029 quarterback Walker Snee got the scoring going for the Paladins in the second quarter when the signal caller exploded for a 63-yard touchdown run to cut the lead to 14-7. Game got tied up at 14-all when Xavier Weems went 55 yards to the endzone with 5:02 before halftime. Odoh made his presence felt just before the halftime buzzer sounded as the future Nittany Lion raced down to the endzone on a 79-yard run to go up 21-14. Both Snee and Odoh would added touchdowns in the second half to end the scoring for Paramus Catholic as they move to 1-0 on the season and next week take on Virginia’s No. 1 ranked The St. James Academy . More about La Salle College High School “La Salle College High School in Glenside, PA, is an all-boys Catholic preparatory school dedicated to academic, spiritual, and personal growth. It offers a challenging curriculum, extensive extracurricular activities, and a strong athletics program. Emphasizing community service and leadership, La Salle prepares students for college and beyond, embodying values of integrity and perseverance. The school fosters a brotherhood of learners and leaders driven by a commitment to excellence.” More about Paramus Catholic High School “Paramus Catholic High School, located in Paramus, New Jersey, is a private, coeducational Roman Catholic college preparatory school serving students in grades 9–12. Known for its strong academic curriculum, championship athletic teams, and vibrant student life, PC fosters spiritual, intellectual, and personal growth. With a commitment to excellence and service, Paramus Catholic prepares students to lead with integrity and faith in a diverse, global society.”

articles.title: After 6 months of war, hardliners consolidate power in Iran, but there are ‘serious differences over the future path of the country’
articles.summary: President Masoud Pezeshkian is one of the most prominent voices still calling for a negotiated solution.
articles._body: After  six months of war , Iran’s leadership has coalesced around a hard core of military generals and clerics long entrenched in the ruling theocracy. They are ready for a potentially long confrontation with the U.S. and determined to prevent any unrest at home. It’s a far cry from U.S. President  Donald Trump’s  initial hopes of  toppling the Islamic Republic  and his subsequent claims that “regime change” had brought more compromising officials to the fore. Iran’s new leaders evince little faith in any agreement with Trump — after coming under attack twice while holding talks — and they may be bracing for another assault once the U.S.  replenishes its supplies of interceptors . They have also threatened to escalate the war as a continuing American blockade and Trump’s  plans for new sanctions  threaten to suffocate Iran’s already worsening economy. “If (Trump) wants to do something, we will retaliate in a seismic manner,” the new secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, said last weekend. In a post on X, he said that “if the economic war continues, not a single drop of oil will be exported” from the Persian Gulf. Iran is determined to smother any internal unrest Rezaei’s appointment came in a recent set of decrees by the supreme leader, Ayatollah  Mojtaba Khamenei , that formally set Iran’s new senior leadership, including top military posts. Khamenei’s father and much of the highest echelons were killed in the bombing campaign launched by the U.S. and Israel on Feb. 28. Perhaps most telling was the newly named head of the Basij, the Revolutionary Guard’s  volunteer street force , which played a major role in crushing  January’s nationwide protests , when thousands were killed. That post went to Hossein Taeb, a hard-line cleric and longtime intelligence chief who led one of the first major crackdowns on protests, in 2009. His appointment is seen as a sign that the leadership is intent on preventing any new unrest as discontent over the economy spreads. The 56-year-old Khamenei has not been seen in public, or even appeared in video or audio, since Israeli strikes killed his father, Ayatollah  Ali Khamenei , who had been Iran’s supreme leader for some 37 years. The younger Khamenei is believed to have been wounded in the strikes. His public absence could reflect the depth of security surrounding him, since he is likely in Israel’s sights, or the extent of his wounds. The supreme leader surrounds himself with hard-line allies With the appointments announced Aug. 11 and 12, he has surrounded himself with longtime personal allies, like Rezaei and Taeb. They are “a clique of older senior officers who’ve served together over the last decades,” said Sascha Bruchmann, an analyst with the International Institute for Strategic Studies’ Middle East office in Bahrain. Rezaei, 71, led the paramilitary Revolutionary Guard during its formative years, through the entire 1980-1988 war with Iraq and until 1997. He has run for president as a hard-line candidate multiple times since 2009. Brig. Gen. Ahmad Vahidi, 68, was confirmed as head of the Guard, where he has been acting commander since his predecessor was killed along with the elder Khamenei. Also confirmed in their posts were the acting commander of the Guard’s naval forces, Gen. Ali Ozmaei, and the military chief of staff, Gen. Ali Abdollahi. Bruchmann, who pointed out that Rezaei was Vahidi’s commander for many years, said the emphasis appears to be on ensuring unity. “It looks like internal cohesion, as in hard core people are being pulled into the inner circle,” he said. Moderates urge restraint over economic concerns Homayoun Falakshahi, the top oil analyst for the global commerce information firm Kpler, wrote that the appointments of Rezaei and Vahidi show “greater influence for officials associated with a tougher stance.” Still, escalation is not inevitable, and Iran could find it difficult to “escalate enough to restore deterrence without triggering retaliation that leaves it worse off,” he said. A ceasefire deal reached in June  quickly fell apart  amid exchanges of strikes. Iran has demanded the release of billions in frozen assets as called for under the deal — as well as formal authority over the  Strait of Hormuz . President Masoud Pezeshkian is one of the most prominent voices still calling for a negotiated solution. His allies argue Iran risks overplaying its hand by continuing the war as its economy suffers. “It would be better to bring the war to an end, since today we enjoy power and dignity and the entire world approved our victory, and the U.S. is hated,” Pezeshkian said last week. He has also defended the June ceasefire deal against hard-liners’ accusations that it conceded too much. In contrast to ultra-hard-liners who reject any talks, Rezaei has held out the possibility of a deal — if the U.S. backs down. On Monday, he told Pakistani mediator Gen. Asim Munir that the U.S. should “change its attitude and take practical action about implementing the conditions” of the ceasefire deal. Tehran-based political analyst Ahmad Zeidabadi said there are “serious differences over the future path of the country.” Hard-liners oppose normalization with the U.S. because “their survival depends on the existence of conflict and hostility,” he wrote in the newspaper Hammihan, which backs Pezeshkian. Amid worries over unrest, a strong figure leads the Basij So far there has been no sign of new protests even as Iranians find it harder to afford basic staples. Taeb’s appointment as head of the Basij is a sign the leadership wants to preempt any potential unrest “before it even manifests,” Bruchmann said. “Putting someone from an intelligence background in charge of the people that would do the crackdown makes sense,” he said. articles.title: Having entered the ‘transfer portal’ exactly one year ago today, college football remains as captivating as ever
articles.summary: Time flies when you’re having fun. Today marks my one-year anniversary with On3, and I’ve always said I have the best job in the world covering college football, but it doesn’t get any better than this past year with my new (and growing) team as I approach 40 years in the sports media business, the
articles._body: Time flies when you’re having fun. Today marks my one-year anniversary with On3, and I’ve always said I have the best job in the world covering college football, but it doesn’t get any better than this past year with my new (and growing) team as I approach 40 years in the sports media business, the only business I’ve ever known. I wanted to go inside the curtain over the past year, re-visiting the sights and sounds of the best sport on the planet, the memorable moments, insightful conversations with coaches and players and where it all leads to as we kick off the 2026 season today. Cream and Crimson If you asked me for one defining image from the 2025 season, it would be the glow on the face of Fernando Mendoza ’s mom as she looked up at her oldest son from her wheelchair on the field at Miami’s Hard Rock Stadium following Indiana’s 27-21 win over Miami to win the national championship and cap a perfect 16-0 season. It was also a perfect moment, with family surrounding both. Elsa Mendoza has battled multiple sclerosis for nearly two decades, and Fernando has said several times that his mom was his inspiration with the way she fought the degenerative disease with such courage, grace and fortitude. Fernando bent over several times to hug his mom and tell her that he loved her, and each time, her face lit up the way Fernando lit up Miami linebacker Wesley Bissainthe just inside the 5-yard line before diving into the end zone on a fourth-down touchdown run that will live for eternity in IU football lore. I had an Indiana staffer tell me that night that Mendoza’s secret sauce was his ability to get his teammates to believe, as much with his actions as his words. That was never more apparent than sacrificing his body and slamming his way into the end zone on a 12-yard quarterback draw that gave the Hoosiers the breathing room they needed to get past the Hurricanes. Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti initially was going to kick the short field goal, but he called a timeout to think about it. “That’s who he is, who we are. We go for it,” Indiana center Pat Coogan said on the field after the game. “It was like, ‘Hell yeah, we’re going for it.’ ” Being Curt Cignetti This time three years ago, Cignetti was anything but a household name in football circles. Most fans couldn’t have picked him out of a lineup, and he certainly wasn’t showing up on national television commercials with Jake from State Farm. Now that he’s won on the biggest stage and orchestrated the greatest two-year turnaround in college football history (and talked a little smack and/or offered some brutally honest sound bites along the way), he’s the go-to interview for everybody. While some have referred to Cignetti as smug and others as brilliant, he hasn’t changed from his days on the Alabama staff under Nick Saban. Jim McElwain was the offensive coordinator at Alabama when Cignetti was the receivers coach and told me, “It’s not a put-on. That’s who he is. If he thought something, and it was usually well thought out, he said it. Sometimes Coach (Saban) wanted to hear it. Sometimes he didn’t. Timing was everything.” Saban told me he was “hard as shit” on Cignetti, but there’s usually one assistant on Saban’s staff that takes on the role of being the main punching bag. It didn’t help that Cignetti coached receivers, and Saban will always be a defensive backs coach at heart. Cignetti was hardly the only receivers coach Saban was hard on over the years. Longtime Alabama head trainer Jeff Allen said he sat right behind Cignetti in meetings and joked, “Sometimes I caught some of the shrapnel flying off him.” Through it all, Cignetti said his time with Saban prepared him to be a head coach even though his exit from Alabama, referred to as the “grand finale” by Cignetti when he and Saban engaged in a heated exchange in the office after a practice, wasn’t the rosiest of sendoffs. There’s a lot of mutual respect there, though, and Saban told me this summer, “He was cocky as hell then too. I don’t mean that in a bad way, but whether it was cocky or just confidence in who he was, he wasn’t afraid to speak his mind. But I think that absolutely helped him turn things around at Indiana because he got those people to believe. He created a new horizon for that place by having some swag and saying we can do things that they had never done before. The most important thing is that he backed it up and did what he said he was going to do. You can’t fool the kids. They believed it. You can see that from the way they played from the time he got there. Being positive, cocky, or whatever you want to call it, enhances confidence. You see that all throughout his program.” Here’s perhaps the most important part going forward for the Hoosiers: Cignetti is numb to what’s behind him or what happened a year ago. He told me this summer, “There’s nothing that happened last year that is going to matter one bit in what we do this year. Other teams may look at us a little differently, and that’s OK. We’ll prepare, practice and work the same way. The margin is in doing the little things and doing them right all the time. What people expect out of us or say about us outside our building doesn’t matter. It didn’t help us win one game last year and won’t help us win one this year.” Sound familiar? Lane Train pulling out This one gets a little crazier, a little weirder and a lot more volitle by the day now that Lane Kiffin is on the Bayou and doing what he does best — stirring it up. It seems like only yesterday in talking to him the week of the Egg Bowl last season that I was going back and forth on whether he would stay at Ole Miss or leave for LSU. At one point, he told his offensive staff that his intentions were to stay. Still, others closer to him as the week wore on felt like the LSU job would be too enticing for him to pass up. The Verdict: Scars of 2024 will guide the way in 2025
articles.summary: South Carolina football superfan Chris Paschal writes a weekly column during the season for GamecockCentral called “The Verdict.” Chris is a lawyer at Goings Law Firm in Columbia.
articles._body: South Carolina football superfan Chris Paschal writes a weekly column during the season for GamecockCentral called “The Verdict.” Chris is a lawyer at Goings Law Firm in Columbia . Andy Griffith knew nothing about football when he stumbled upon what was his first ever football game back in 1953. As he recalled in his classic stand-up bit “What It Was, Was Football,” there was a little pumpkin that these fellas would fight over, and he couldn’t make heads or tails out of any part of it. At the end of the bit, Andy said, “I don’t know what it was, but I know one thing: I ain’t never going back to another one.” Is there a better way to describe the 2025 Gamecock Football season? “I don’t know what it was, but I know one thing: I ain’t never going back to another one.” The only thing is we always come back for the next one. The agony of 2025 wasn’t due to a lack of talent. This program has some ball players. The cupboard is not bare. In fact, you could probably argue Shane Beamer has built the talent profile of this program into one you would maybe see in Athens or Tuscaloosa or Columbus ( see: Jordan Reid’s piece on ESPN ). Last year, that talent was supposed to culminate with Beamer’s established culture of finishing each game strong, and in turn, finishing the season strong. Only it didn’t happen.  We didn’t get blown out. We didn’t look like a program devoid of SEC-caliber athletes. Heck, we either led or were within one possession in 10 of our 12 contests last season. But time and time again, that Gamecock lost its fight. I think I did this math correctly, but we averaged less than 3.2 points per game in the fourth quarter. There were only four FBS programs (remember, there are now 136 of them) that averaged fewer. Whether it was a 31–30 heartbreak in College Station, late-game stumbles against Missouri, Ole Miss, Alabama and LSU, or offensive drives grinding to a halt due to sacks, penalties, or any other host of problems, the Gamecocks repeatedly hit an invisible wall. They weren’t just outclassed; they were outlasted. 2025 was in many ways a disaster.  So naturally, everyone left, right? Obviously, that is a rhetorical question. In the modern landscape of college football, player retention after a 4–8 gut-punch of a season is almost unheard of. The transfer portal offers an instant escape hatch, a quick reset button for players looking for fresh NIL guarantees or a softer landing spot. Yes, it was impressive LaNorris Sellers, and Nyck Harbor, and Dylan Stewart all stayed. But how about guys like David Bucey? How about guys like Mazeo Bennet? How about guys like Mo Brown? That’s what makes the foundation of the 2026 roster so intriguing. There is some scar tissue on this roster. And I think the good kind. This season’s team and in many ways this program will be defined by guys who decided they would rather fix the house than move into a new one. Much like the 2024 team that rallied after a tough 2023 season, this 2026 team has some guys on it who won’t need the coaches shouting to get them going. Instead, all they have to remember is what it felt like to walk off the field in College Station last season. Luke Day can motivate until his blue in the face, but Peyton Williams knows what it was like watching Alabama rip victory from Gamecock jaws last October. So, we kept most everyone on board after last season. But did they improve at all? How did this 2026 team attack the summer with this scar tissue? How did they get better? There was a line Coach Beamer used in his press conference at SEC Media Days that caught my attention. “Let’s empty the tank.” He had been asked about any changes made to offseason, summer workout training, and Coach Beamer said, “probably just ‘Let’s empty the tank,’ in other words — where if you’re a guy, and we’re doing some sort of conditioning, there’s not a necessarily a set ending point to this conditioning drill. It’s more, ‘Let’s see how far you can go in this allotted time.’” That’s not just physical. That’s mental. Don’t anticipate the whistle. Don’t expect the drill to end. Just keep working. Whether this sprint or this rep is the final one or just the halfway mark, keep working. Keep grinding. That mentality goes hand in hand with a bunch of veteran guys who have decided to stick things out in Columbia and fight together.  Shane Beamer didn’t rewrite his program’s summer protocol because his players lacked effort. He rewrote it because in the modern SEC, the difference between 4–8 and 10-2 isn’t a 50-point offensive explosion. It is three converted third downs on offense. It is one clean pocket on a two-minute drive. It is that one extra stop when the defense has been on the field for 35 minutes. Resilience is a word thrown around lightly in August hype videos and on the message boards. Heck, every team in America claims to be tough when the record sits at 0–0. True resilience and true toughness aren’t motivational bumper stickers. It’s a physical standard paid for with summer sandlapper sweat. The 2025 season gave South Carolina the painful proof of what happens when the tank runs dry. This summer, Luke Day and this Gamecock locker room intentionally emptied it on their own terms.  But now comes the test. The Verdict on this offseason won’t be delivered in August practice reports. It will be rendered in the final seven minutes of fourth-quarter ball games in Columbia, Tuscaloosa, Gainesville, Clemson, and many other places. The hope is that this time South Carolina won’t be playing on empty. What do you think? Join the South Carolina discussion on The Insiders Forum.

articles.title: Former White House teleprompter operator must turn over more than $100,000 in profits and pay a $65,000 fine in insider trading settlement
articles.summary: The settlement with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, announced Friday, also dealt Gabriel Perez a three-year trading ban.
articles._body: A former White House teleprompter operator  accused of using inside knowledge  to make bets on the prediction market Kalshi has been ordered to turn over more than $100,000 in profits and pay a $65,000 fine as part of a settlement with federal authorities. The settlement with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, announced Friday, also dealt Gabriel Perez a three-year trading ban. Perez was placed on unpaid leave from his job at the White House after reports emerged that he  used his position  to make bets on what President Donald Trump would say in speeches. The White House did not immediately comment on the settlement. A White House official said in July that Perez was no longer in his position but did not say if he had been fired or resigned. The commission found that Perez made $107,500 on prediction markets by betting on words and phrases that would appear in Trump’s speeches between December 2025 and February 2026. “In his position, Perez had access to presidential speeches prior to those speeches being delivered and Perez misappropriated that information — in breach of his duty of trust and confidence,” according to a release from the commission. Perez was ordered to repay his profits in full, along with the $65,000 civil penalty, which the commission said was a reduction because of his “exemplary cooperation.” As details emerged July 16, White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said it was “unfortunate” and “a disgrace.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com
