articles.title: Kyle Larson trolls Denny Hamlin, embraces potential chaos with NASCAR’s new Daytona package
articles.summary: Kyle Larson trolls Denny Hamlin over his “absolute chaos” Daytona warning while embracing the unknown surrounding NASCAR’s new package.
articles._body: The new NASCAR superspeedway package has had people talking since it was announced in July. Tonight in the Coke Zero Sugar 400 it is on display for the first time. Denny Hamlin predicted chaos . Kyle Larson threw a jab at Hamlin and offered his thoughts ahead of tonight’s race at Daytona. On his podcast this week, Hamlin offered this ominous warning: “I think this weekend has potential to be absolute chaos. Just from the words I’m getting and the data I’m seeing on this new package, I think the cars could be far more out of control when they’re trying to push each other, which could cause smoke.  “And when there’s smoke, there’s a wreck.”  Larson takes funny jab at Hamlin Kyle Larson was asked on Friday what his expectations are with the new rules package. In addition to trolling Hamlin, Larson offered what he’s hearing from Hendrick Motorsports engineers. “Well, I don’t really know because I’m not a physics engineer, so I’m not sure how it affects it,” said Larson. “You listen to Denny and other guys who probably do understand the race car better than I would.  “And maybe, you know, Denny’s a media member now, so maybe he’s just making it sound crazier than it could be. But it also could be.  “I went into our engineering room, and I was like, ‘Hey, tell me how crazy it’s going to be this week.’ And they were like, ‘It’s less downforce, but then you just raise the front of your car, and you get all that downforce back.’ “Or a lot of it back. So I’m not sure. I mean, I hope it’s a lot different. “I think on the drag perspective, I think it will be different. Hopefully, runs are easier to make on that side of things. But as far as handling, I don’t know. “Maybe, I don’t think it could be too different than what we’re used to, potentially.” ‘We want the chaos’ While there are questions about the new package, Larson is definitely excited about the unknown.  He’s looking to break the monotonous cycle of the Next Gen era.   “I feel like it’s weird because a lot of us complain that Daytona and Talladega and tracks are, like, too chaotic and there’s crashing and all this stuff, but then it’s like it got so boring it’s like we want the chaos,” said Larson. “So that’s why we’re at this point of changing the package.  “But I don’t know. I’m just excited to try something new. I feel like so long in the NextGen era, it’s just every track we go to, it’s just, like, the same thing.  “So I’m happy for a change. I would be open to changing packages at other tracks just to, like, spice things up because it just gets kind of repetitive each year.  “I mean, you see Ryan Blaney win Loudon . He won Loudon last year. “It’s like the same guys run up front every week that did the year previous.”  Larson predicts what Stage 1 will look like With so many unknowns heading into Saturday night, Larson said to expect drivers feeling out their cars for the first 20 or so laps.  He then expects things to ramp up.  “Yeah, I think you’re just going to, at least for me, and I think for most, you’re not going to know what to expect in Turn 1 as far as what your car feels like. “So I think a bit of the first 20 laps is probably going to be just feeling the car, feeling how it changes as the tires get hot. And if that’s all good and comfortable, then I think, yeah, you’ll see people trying to make lanes work or moves happen. And a lot of that happens organically. “It’s not like you’re really trying. So I don’t think it’s, in that sense, I don’t think it’s going to be as chaotic as what people think, because I think we’re all going to be kind of going at a similar pace.  “But yeah, the unknown is always fun. But like any other race, you get through that first stage, and then the second stage looks a lot different.”

articles.summary: Following the news that Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs faces misdemeanor charges, Packers head coach Matt LaFleur is addressing the issue. LaFleur expects Jacobs to continue to have a role with the team, per ESPN. “Well, I fully anticipate him being a member of our team,”
articles._body: Following the news that Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs faces misdemeanor charges , Packers head coach Matt LaFleur is addressing the issue. LaFleur expects Jacobs to continue to have a role with the team, per ESPN. “Well, I fully anticipate him being a member of our team,” LaFleur said. LaFleur wants the legal process to play out. Jacobs was charged with battery and criminal damage to property, the outlet reported. “You’ve got to let everything play out,” LaFleur said. “But I anticipate him being a member of our football team.” Jacobs is facing some serious allegations, regarding events that allegedly occurred earlier this year. “Jacobs was originally arrested May 26 on five counts, including one felony, but formal charges were not filed until Thursday. According to the criminal complaint, Jacobs grabbed a woman and threw her to the ground and she struck her head. The alleged incident happened at Jacobs’ home near Green Bay on May 23,” ESPN reported. The NFL can choose to slap a suspension on Jacobs, or other penalties. The league doesn’t have to wait for the legal process to play out, in order to implement those measures. “I can’t really comment on that because I don’t know,” LaFleur said. League officials have yet to hand down any punishment. “We have been closely monitoring all developments in the matter, which remains under review,” NFL spokesperson Brian McCarthy said Thursday, per ESPN. Jacobs didn’t appear in the team’s final NFL preseason game, against the Arizona Cardinals . He was scheduled to rest, as were most of Green Bay’s starters. Green Bay starts their regular season games against the Minnesota Vikings, on September 13. During the 2025 season, Jacobs rushed for 929 yards and 13 touchdowns. Juanes, Alejandro Sanz & More Launch Marea Viva to Rebuild Chocó After Earthquake & More Uplifting Moments
articles.summary: Plus, Amazon Music honors Juan Gabriel’s legacy, and Eladio Carrión earns the Hispanic Heritage Foundation’s Inspira Award.
articles._body: From career milestones to new releases to major announcements and those little important moments,  Billboard  editors highlight  uplifting moments  in Latin music. Here’s what happened in the Latin music world this week. Juanes, Nicky Jam, Goyo, and Leaders Across Sports and Business Launch Marea Viva for Chocó A new relief effort is uniting some of Colombia’s most recognizable folks in support of communities affected by the Aug. 10 earthquake. Marea Viva, for the Chocó of Tomorrow brings together Juanes, James Rodríguez, Mariana Pajón, Rigoberto Urán, David Ospina, Goyo, Manuel Medrano, Juan Luis Guerra, Alejandro Sanz, Nicky Jam, Altafulla and more to help fund safe, earthquake-resistant housing and essential rebuilding efforts in Chocó. Led by Progresa Chocó, Fundación Mi Sangre, Fundación Bancolombia, Grupo Argos and other partners, the initiative seeks to address both the immediate emergency and long-term housing needs in a region where heavy rainfall and limited road access present unique challenges. Grupo Argos, Fundación Bancolombia, RedPro and Juanes have already pledged $3.2 million, with the campaign aiming to raise at least another $5 million. Click here to donate. View this post on Instagram Amazon Music Honors Juan Gabriel’s Legacy 10 Years After His Death A decade after Juan Gabriel’s passing, Amazon Music is honoring El Divo de Juárez with a multifaceted tribute that includes curated playlists, a collectible vinyl release and a new interpretation of his classic “Así Fue” by Arthur Hanlon featuring Thalía. Fans can now stream the Amazon Music Original and pre-order the 10th Anniversary Commemorative Amazon Exclusive Vinyl Edition of Juan Gabriel en el Palacio de Bellas Artes, due Sept. 11. “Juan Gabriel is not only one of the greatest ambassadors of Mexican music around the world, he is the heart and soul of Spanish-language music,” Rocío Guerrero, Amazon Music’s director of Latin-Iberia, said in a statement. The tribute arrives as his catalog continues to find new audiences: Over the past year, his music was streamed in 47 countries on Amazon Music, with more than half a million listeners becoming new fans. Hispanic Heritage Awards Set to Honor Eladio Carrión, Mon Laferte, Oscar D’León & More The 39th annual Hispanic Heritage Awards are set for Sept. 10 at Orchestra Hall in Minneapolis, honoring artists and leaders whose work has shaped culture and community. Eladio Carrión will receive the Inspira Award, while Mon Laferte will be recognized with the Social Justice Award, salsa icon Oscar D’León will receive the Legend Award, and Rep. Joaquín Castro will be honored with the Public Service Award. “I’m really grateful to receive the Inspira Award from the Hispanic Heritage Foundation,” said Carrión in a press release. “I’ve always believed in betting on yourself, staying true to where you come from and using your platform to open doors for the next generation. I’m proud to represent Puerto Rico and our Latino community, and I’m thankful for everyone who’s been part of this journey.” View this post on Instagram Mon Laferte Celebrates Sold-Out Radio City Music Hall Show and New Live Video Mon Laferte continues her banner Femme Fatale era with multiple sold-out dates across her North American tour. The Chilean-Mexican artist has been packing venues in support of Femme Fatale, Vol. 2 , which expands her theatrical, alternative world through blues, folk, punk and alt-rock influences. To mark the tour’s momentum, Laferte also released a live performance video for “Femme Fatale,” filmed during one of her three sold-out shows at Mexico City’s Palacio de los Deportes, where she played to a combined crowd of 40,000 fans. The run comes as she prepares to receive the 2026 Social Justice Award at the Hispanic Heritage Awards, recognizing her work using music and art to advocate for equality, human rights and marginalized communities. articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles rookie receiver Makai Lemon received support from DeVonta Smith after mishandling a punt during Friday’s 30-13 preseason loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. Lemon made his NFL debut after missing two preseason games and much of training camp with a hamstring injury. He caught thre
articles._body: Philadelphia Eagles rookie receiver Makai Lemon received support from DeVonta Smith after mishandling a punt during Friday’s 30-13 preseason loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. Lemon made his NFL debut after missing two preseason games and much of training camp with a hamstring injury. He caught three passes for three yards on five targets. Another pass went through his hands and became an interception. His difficult night continued when he mishandled a bouncing punt. Lemon recovered it immediately, preventing Cincinnati from taking possession. PHLY Sports’ EJ Smith shared a clip of the interaction Friday on X, formerly Twitter, from Lincoln Financial Field. “DeVonta Smith just came over to chat with Makai Lemon after the muffed punt:” DeVonta Smith just came over to chat with Makai Lemon after the muffed punt: pic.twitter.com/OV1VKX1BX3 — EJ Smith (@EJSmith94) August 29, 2026 The clip contains no public audio, leaving Smith’s exact message unknown. His approach continued a mentorship that began before the rookie’s debut. Lemon previously identified Smith as his biggest mentor, while the veteran said he would remain available whenever Lemon sought advice. Smith did not play against Cincinnati because the Eagles rested their starters. He remained involved from the sideline as Lemon navigated his first professional action after the interrupted summer. Lemon’s first reception gained three yards on Philadelphia’s opening offensive snap. His other two catches netted zero yards, while the interception and punt mistake contributed to an uneven performance. Philadelphia now has only 15 days before the team’s 2026 regular-season opener vs. the Washington Commanders. That window gives Lemon additional practice time to rebuild timing and prepare for a Week 1 role. Smith’s sideline approach did not establish what the Eagles have planned for Lemon ahead of the season. It showed the veteran supporting his rookie teammate after a public mistake. articles._body: This project was born out of a desire to convert my mineral and rock collection into a virtual 3D archive that I can carry around and share. The concept is simple: I take one or more photos of my stones and crystals, and the app generates an HD 3D model while also classifying the rock using a local model (HF-CLIP WASM) directly in the browser. articles._body: The Carolina Panthers are making some tough choices regarding their roster , as the 2026 NFL season is set to begin. Panthers head coach Dave Canales says the roster will be trimmed in the days ahead. The goal is to make sure Carolina has the best possible group together for Week 1 of the season. “They’ll be in waves. We’ll start tomorrow (Saturday) with some guys,” Canales said, per ESPN. “….the trickiest part with the practice squad is that you are limited to how many veteran players you can keep.” Dave Canales on timeline for roster moves this weekend: pic.twitter.com/47Cqwt38O5 — John Ellis (@1PantherPlace) August 29, 2026 Carolina defeated the Houston Texans in a preseason game on Friday, 16-13. The Panthers now await the start of the regular season. Carolina’s first regular season game is against the Chicago Bears on September 13. Carolina is now expected to make some tough decisions , regarding several key areas. “(Quarterback is) another decision. You talk about (running back) AJ Dillon, who had a great camp. Do you keep three quarterbacks? Four running backs?” Canales said, per The Athletic. “How do you keep all these numbers — seven receivers, eight receivers that we’re talking about? The loaded tight end room of guys that we trust. “So yeah, we got our work cut out for us in the next couple days.” The Panthers had a successful 2025 season under Canales . Carolina won just eight games, but that was enough for the team to make the NFL Playoffs. That was a success for the Panthers who had been struggling before Canales took over the team. Time will tell how these Panthers fare in 2026. Canales has coached the team since 2024. Carolina is still looking for its first Super Bowl title as a NFL franchise. Ravens’ Jesse Minter talks Tyler Loop’s future after 2 missed kicks vs. Commanders
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens closed the preseason with a 3-0 record after a 41-3 victory over the Washington Commanders in the finale. While there was much to celebrate, Tyler Loop received boos and chants against him after missing two kicks on game night. However, Ravens coach Jesse Minter made his feel
articles._body: The Baltimore Ravens closed the preseason with a 3-0 record after a 41-3 victory over the Washington Commanders in the finale. While there was much to celebrate, Tyler Loop received boos and chants against him after missing two kicks on game night. However, Ravens coach Jesse Minter made his feelings clear while talking about his confidence level in the young kicker. “You want to see makes in games,” Minter said via ESPN’s Ravens reporter Jamison Hensley. “And so, it’s something we’ll continue to look at. We’ll continue to look at what the best situation is there. He has had a good camp overall, but again, it comes down to making the kicks and the pressure situations in the game. So, that’s something I think that we’ll always be looking at to make sure that we’re doing what’s best for the team.” Ravens coach Jesse Minter on his confidence level in Tyler Loop, who missed two kicks tonight: pic.twitter.com/KN35rn1bzl — Jamison Hensley (@jamisonhensley) August 29, 2026 While initially, the Ravens did not bring in another competition for the kicker role, things might not be the same forever. Coming next season, rookie coach Minter may explore options before the September 13 regular-season kickoff. Loop himself accepted high expectations from him. The Arizona alum also mentioned he keeps himself in check for any such shortcomings . “It’s my job to transfer that to the game. I know the expectation is to make kicks, and the expectations I have for myself are higher than anyone else going to have. And tonight is not good enough,” Loop said after the game via ESPN. However, while bringing in another kicker has not been dismissed completely, Loop showed confidence in his ball-kicking abilities, something that he could channel as motivation to bounce back and forget the recent slump. “I’m confident in my ball-striking. When I’m striking the ball good, it’s really good, and that has to carry over, and that’s all we’re focused on,” he added. We will wait to see if or when the Ravens bring on another reliable name for the kicker role. With the regular season kicking off next month, the Ravens play the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, September 13. articles.title: IBM’s CEO disagrees with JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon’s disdain for texting in meetings: ‘Telling people they can’t use their technology would be weird’
articles.summary: Jamie Dimon calls checking your email during a meeting disrespectful—but IBM’s CEO says he doesn’t care, depending on the number of people in the room.
articles._body: As more employees return to the office , some CEOs are finding they need to reteach basic meeting etiquette —including one surprisingly divisive topic: checking your devices. JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has been especially blunt about it. At Fortune’s Most Powerful Women summit in fall 2025, he said he expects full attention from everyone in the room. “If you have an iPad in front of me and it looks like you’re reading your email or getting notifications, I tell you to close the damn thing,” he told Fortune Editor-in-Chief Alyson Shontell . “It’s disrespectful.” IBM CEO Arvind Krishna , however, sees it a bit differently. He argued it would be “weird” for a tech company to tell its employees not to use their technology—especially in larger meetings where devices can be a useful tool rather than a distraction. “I distinguish between one-to-10-person meetings and very large meetings. If it’s a very large meeting, I’m sorry. It’s not really a meeting. It’s a communication vehicle. You’re just informing people,” Krishna told CNN in October 2025. At the same time, the 64-year-old said that smaller, more intimate meetings should be treated attentively. “If it’s a small meeting, I would really frown upon if somebody is sitting opposite my desk and lost in their phone,” he said. “I would tell them: ‘Why don’t you come back when you have time?’” Dimon’s long-standing frustration with meetings Behavior in the conference room is something Dimon has long lamented. In fact, in his annual letter to shareholders released in spring 2025, he mentioned the word “meetings” six times—urging employees to only schedule them when necessary and to make them count. “I see people in meetings all the time who are getting notifications and personal texts or who are reading emails,” Dimon wrote . “This has to stop. It’s disrespectful. It wastes time.” While Dimon hasn’t drawn clear lines around meeting size like Krishna has, his frustration appears to extend well beyond small gatherings.  During a conversation at Stanford University in March 2025, Dimon recalled joining a Zoom meeting where attention was clearly divided. “There were 12 people in the room and four people on the screen and all four people on the screen were on their phone,” he recalled. “And people say, and you think you’re focusing and learning?” Dimon’s disdain for distracted meetings comes as he’s led one of the most aggressive return-to-office mandates on Wall Street. Most JPMorgan employees are now required to work in the office five days a week—at least in part, to see a return on the company’s real-estate investments. In late 2025, JPMorgan officially opened its new $3 billion global headquarters in Manhattan, a 60-story skyscraper equipped with 19 restaurants, a company store, and gym. Putting the devices down might catch your boss’s attention With a growing reliance on technology in the workplace, multitasking during a meeting has become easier than ever—especially when an AI assistant can generate a post-meeting summary and allow you to zone out. However, multitasking in person is especially disrespectful and a bad habit, according to Gary Rich, founder of executive coaching firm Rich Leadership. “Are manners ‘old fashioned?’ Is listening to what’s happening in a meeting ‘old school?’” Rich previously told Fortune . “When people are multitasking during a meeting, the distraction creates a ripple effect—the speaker feels disrespected, other attendees lose motivation, and the meeting becomes less productive.” Taking the high-road—and practicing good meeting etiquette—can ultimately be an effective way to earn recognition, show genuine commitment, and build credibility. A version of this story originally published on  Fortune.com  on November 4, 2025. More on productivity Like Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, Siemens’ CEO has no recurring meetings with direct reports to save time—he also replies to emails with just ‘OK’ or ‘No’ Forget RTO: Fully remote workers report the highest well-being —and are less likely to quit, new study of 7,700 employees finds Meetings are not work, says Southwest Airlines CEO —and he’s taking action by blocking his calendar every afternoon from Wednesday to Friday This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

Dolly Parton once turned down a song request from Elvis Presley. That was just one business decision that helped build her $650 million empire
articles.summary: Parton established her own publishing company in 1966, which helped her hold on to nearly all of her publishing rights.
articles._body: Country music superstar Dolly Parton had a very early start to her career when she began singing at her local church at age 6. By age 13, she had recorded her first single, “Puppy Love,” which she co-wrote at age 11 with her uncle—and had even appeared on the Grand Ole Opry stage by that time, too, introduced by none other than music legend Johnny Cash.  After high school, Parton immediately moved to Nashville to continue building momentum in her music career. It was there she wrote both hit singles “Jolene” and “I Will Always Love You”—on the same day, no less—two songs that were later cemented as country classics. Her partnership with singer and television star Porter Wagoner in 1967 also helped her gain national recognition.  But what also made Parton so prominent in the music industry was her business savvy. She always retained ownership of her songs, a rare move that helped balloon her wealth to an estimated $650 million . It was especially helpful that she chose to do that when Whitney Houston’s version of “I Will Always Love You” became a global hit in the 1990s.  Notably, Parton, whose family announced her death earlier this week, even turned down Elvis Presley’s request in 1974 to record the song after his manager Colonel Tom Parker demanded half the publishing rights. “I said, ‘I’m sorry, but I can’t give you the publishing.’ I wanted to hear Elvis sing it, and it broke my heart—I cried all night,” Parton told W Magazine in 2021. “But I had to keep that copyright in my pocket. You have to take care of your business.” Dolly Parton onstage with an acoustic guitar circa 1974. Getty Images/Michael Ochs Archives Parton had established her own publishing company in 1966, which helped her hold on to nearly all of her publishing rights. This meant she got paid a larger royalty whenever one of her songs was played or covered. And she wasn’t about to let even The King slide past those rules.  “Everybody’s going to use you if they can,” she added. “These are my songs—they’re like my children. And I expect them to support me when I’m old.” How Dolly Parton grew her wealth Parton built a legendary career in entertainment from her music, acting roles, and her theme park, Dollywood, in Tennessee. While a large portion of Parton’s wealth (an estimated $150 million ) came from her music catalog, she also earned millions in royalties and co-owns Dollywood, which reportedly generates hundreds of millions in revenue each year from roughly 3 million visitors . Parton was also a dedicated philanthropist, having founded the Dollywood Foundation in 1988. Her foundation focuses on supporting children in her hometown of Sevierville, Tenn., through educational programs. She also made multimillion-dollar donations to disaster relief, medical research, and scholarships. In 2022, she received the Carnegie Medal of Philanthropy , joining the ranks of other major philanthropists like Bill and Melinda Gates, Michael Bloomberg, Paul Allen, and the Rockefeller family. Tech billionaires and executives like Evan Spiegel and Peter Thiel are publicly shielding their children from the products that made them rich
articles.summary: As governments race to restrict minors’ social media use, the tech billionaires who built the platforms are imposing strict screen limits at home.
articles._body: Despite building an increasingly screen-focused world, tech billionaires and executives are keeping their own children away from the tech they helped create. As far back as 2010, Apple cofounder Steve Jobs told a New York Times reporter his kids had never used an iPad and that “we limit how much technology our kids use at home.”  Since then, excessive device use among children has grown more common, especially as busy parents turn to screens to find some temporary peace. The trend has accelerated so much that some young children accustomed to extensive screen time have been dubbed “iPad kids.” On average, children in the U.S. ages 8 to 18 spend 7.5 hours per day watching or using screens, according to the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry. At the same time, Silicon Valley billionaires and executives have increasingly sought to limit how their own families use technology and for how long, partly in response to the rise of time sucking social media and short-form video. YouTube CEO Neal Mohan is among those taking a cautious approach. Mohan, who has three children, said he and his wife try to limit the time his children spend on platforms like YouTube. “We do limit their time on YouTube and other platforms and other forms of media. On weekdays we tend to be more strict, on weekends we tend to be less so. We’re not perfect by any stretch,” he said in a December interview with Time . YouTube cofounder Steve Chen also said at a talk at the Stanford Graduate School of Business last year he wouldn’t want his kids consuming only short-form content, noting it might be better to limit kids to videos longer than 15 minutes. “Shorter-form content equates to shorter attention spans,” he said. Different approaches When it comes to how parents control their children’s screen time, some of the most important people in Silicon Valley have surprisingly different approaches. Instagram CEO Adam Mosseri, who has three children, said in an interview last year he controls his kids’ weekend screen and video game time by starting at a baseline of zero minutes. His kids can earn earn up to 90-minutes of screen time or video game time on the weekend by during by completing three 30-minute homework sessions during the week, he said. Still, he said he avoids taking away screen time that his kids have earned, because he said that caused them to act out more. There is one exception to the rule, he said: “When really all barriers go out the window is on planes.” Much like Mosseri, early Facebook investor and billionaire Peter Thiel previously said he lets his two young children use screens for only an hour and a half per week, a revelation that prompted audible gasps from the audience at the 2024 Aspen Ideas Festival. Other tech leaders are a little more adaptable. That includes Snap CEO Evan Spiegel, who said he and his wife, Miranda Kerr, adapt their approach to screen time based on the child because their four boys, ages two, six, seven, and 15, vary so much in age. Spiegel said the two-year-old gets almost zero screen time, unless he is getting a haircut, when his parents allow him to watch videos of Bobcat tractors, because “he really struggles with getting his haircut,” he told Lenny’s Podcast in June. Spiegel said the four and six-year-olds also don’t use screens often, and “we don’t give them phones or anything like that,” he added. They do watch movies occasionally and play video games on ModRetro’s Chromatic handheld video game device, which he got them last Christmas, he said. Meanwhile, Spiegel’s oldest son, Flynn, is “all in on on technology, whether he’s using it for school or whether he’s using it to talk with his friends or using Snapchat,” he said. Much like Facebook investor and billionaire PayPal cofounder Peter Thiel has put said he lets his two young children use screens for only an hour and a half per week, a revelation that prompted audible gasps from the audience. Other tech founders, including Microsoft’s Bill Gates and Tesla’s Elon Musk, have also spoken about limiting their children’s access to devices. Gates has said he did not give his children smartphones until age 14 and banned phones at the dinner table entirely. While Musk, who bought the social media company X, formerly Twitter, in 2022, said it “might’ve been a mistake ” to not set any rules on social media for his children.  Social media backlash is growing Scientific research increasingly backs up tech leaders’ instinct to rein in screen time. A 2025 study of nearly 100,000 people found short-form video use was consistently associated with poorer cognition and a decline in many aspects of mental health across both younger and older social media users. As young people increasingly spend most of their waking moments online, the backlash against social media, and especially minors’ use of social media, has reached a breaking point. Australia, Indonesia, and Malaysia have all banned adolescents under 16 from using social media over the past year. Several other countries, including Spain, Denmark, and the United Kingdom, are considering similar legislation. To be sure, its unclear how effective such legislation has been. A study by a team that advised the Australian government on the rollout of its social media ban found in a July study that some test accounts for fake 16 year-olds weren’t prompted to verify their age. Plus, several social media CEOs have publicly pushed back on claims their platforms are harmful. Mosseri testified earlier this year in a trial against its parent company, Meta , social media overuse does not constitute “clinical addiction.” Meta this week reached a $17 billion settlement in the suit brought against it by 47 states and the District of Columbia and agreed to change its platforms to limit how long teenagers can use them for and to ban certain features. The AI boom hasn’t stopped U.S. companies from hiring cheap offshore labor, and overseas call center employment is still skyrocketing
articles.summary: “The technology that was supposed to shrink the industry is fueling its expansion,” said Apollo chief economist Torsten Slok.
articles._body: In September 2025, Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff said the company slashed 4,000 customer service roles :“I need less heads,” Benioff said at the time. But as more companies adopt agentic AI in hopes of replacing or making human workers more efficient, one top economist has noted customer service roles—particularly those overseas—are only growing. Citing data from the IT & Business Process Association of the Philippines, Apollo chief economist Torsten Slok noted in a recent blog post that from 2016 through 2025, call center employment in the Philippines has risen each year, nearly doubling to 2 million over the 10-year span. He also found from 2021 to July 2026, unemployment rates in the Philippines have decreased from 9% to about 5%, and in India decreased from around 7% to 6%, suggesting AI has not displaced offshore workers. “If AI were displacing white-collar work at scale, you would expect to see it first in the Philippines and India, where business process outsourcing (call centers, IT support, back-office processing) accounts for a large share of employment,” Slok wrote last week. “Instead, the unemployment rate in both countries has continued to trend lower.” The Philippines dethroned India as the largest call center employer about 15 years ago. Offshore call center jobs began booming in the late 1990s and early 2000s as a cost-cutting measure. The labor is considerably cheaper overseas than in the U.S., with Filipino call center workers earning wages of 15,000 to over 120,000 Philippine pesos per month, or about $243 to $1,948. In the U.S., the average monthly wage for call center workers is about $2,866 , according to Indeed. But these jobs are also among the most susceptible to AI displacement. The Brookings Institution estimated 86% of customer service representative tasks had high automation potential. The apparent contradiction of the job’s potential to be automated alongside rising employment points to a centuries-old economic paradox reflected across labor more broadly, according to Slok. “This is Jevons paradox in action,” he wrote. “As AI makes call center work cheaper and faster, companies are buying more of it, not less.” Jevons paradox in the 21st century Jevons paradox refers to an observation made by English economist William Stanley Jevons in 1865: The invention of the Watt steam engine made coal a more efficient energy source. But instead of coal consumption decreasing because of increased efficiency, consumption skyrocketed as energy became cheaper. In the age of AI, Jevons paradox has been resurrected and applied to how the technology may be impacting the labor market: While tech leaders like Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei initially predicted AI will replace white-collar workers , Slok instead posits the cost of professional work will fall as AI boosts task efficiency, increasing demand for certain roles and ultimately expanding available jobs. “Lower cost per interaction does not mean fewer interactions,” he said. “It means more customers served, more channels opened and more markets worth reaching. The technology that was supposed to shrink the industry is fueling its expansion.” This is already being seen in some professions previously predicted to be replaced by AI. A decade ago, “godfather of AI” Geoffrey Hinton declared radiology would one day no longer need to be performed by humans because of its potential to be automated. Instead, Christoph Herpfer, an economist and business administration professor at the University of Virginia’s Darden School of Business, said the number of radiologists in the U.S. has actually increased by 10% over the past decade. “We actually have a huge shortage of radiologists. So the exact opposite of this prediction has happened,” he told Fortune . The future of call centers and automation Labor economists are already seeing evidence of AI increasing the productivity of call center workers, which could bolster the role’s demand. A 2023 study led by Erik Brynjolfsson, director of the Stanford Digital Economy Lab, found that for more than 5,000 customer support agents, an AI-based conversational assistant tool increased productivity by an average of 14% per hour. His research from a decade ago similarly found that an early AI feature able to translate listings on eBay increased international exports by 17.5%. Emma Harrington, an economics professor at the University of Virginia, believes this principle could be applied to today’s AI boom. “What we’re now seeing in the data might be a modern version of the same phenomenon,” she told Fortune . “We can trade labor more easily across countries when language can be traded more seamlessly.” While some economists expect AI’s strengths to bolster productivity and subsequent employment, others argue the technology’s weaknesses will sustain the call center industry. Benjamin Shestakofsky, a sociologist and information science professor at Cornell University, told Fortune AI may not yet be sufficiently trained to navigate the complexities of certain problems. Moreover, humans experience something akin to “ AI brain fry ” if inundated with an increased case load; AI may be able to increase how many customers agents can serve, but humans still have limitations in how much they are able to process. In other cases, some companies may explicitly seek out human customer service agents simply because of their brand, according to Shestakofsky. As the world becomes more automated, it’s sometimes a relief to talk to a human on the other line. “Even if the LLMs get so good that eventually they can deal with those complex issues—which I don’t think they can do now—I would still expect that you would see some companies seeing the value and offering more human interactions that help customers feel seen, feel like they’re more than just a number on a spreadsheet,” he said. A version of this story was published on Fortune.com on May 17, 2026. More on AI and labor: New York

articles.title: This Stealthy Nike Windbreaker Takes Performance Off-Duty
articles.summary: Nike’s Dri-FIT Woven Full-Zip Color-Block Windrunner Jacket is a low-key performance layer that works just as well beyond the track.
articles._body: This transitional time of year calls for a reliable windbreaker. It’s not exactly chilly yet but the rain is looming and, frankly, the forecast can’t be trusted. You need something to chuck on when a T-shirt feels like a gamble but a proper coat would be wildly premature. Enter Nike’s Tech Windrunner. In a sleek, techy, all-black colorway , it’s got just enough going on without making a song and dance about it. We’re particularly into the subtle color blocking, which stops things from feeling too plain without veering into “look at me” territory. Plus, it’s discreet enough to be worn beyond the track too. Seriously, pair it with a smart pant and a solid Nike sneaker and voilà. Sure, a windbreaker isn’t the most exciting thing you’ll buy this fall. But that’s sort of the point. This is the jacket you’ll be happy to have in your back pocket, whether you’ve got a chockablock day planned or just need something reliable when the weather turns, it’s an easy layer to reach for. Not every purchase needs to change your life. Sometimes you just need a decent jacket. This is a decent jacket. The Dri-FIT Woven Full-Zip Color-Block Windrunner Jacket is currently $82 on Nike’s website , nearly 50% off. A pretty good time to make it yours. articles.title: Saints HC Kellen Moore reveals who called plays in preseason win over Cowboys
articles.summary: New Orleans Saints coach Kellen Moore called the offense during Friday’s 27-24 preseason victory over the Dallas Cowboys, taking back the duties after delegating them earlier in the exhibition schedule. The win at AT&T Stadium completed New Orleans’ preseason and gave Moore another live evalu
articles._body: New Orleans Saints coach Kellen Moore called the offense during Friday’s 27-24 preseason victory over the Dallas Cowboys, taking back the duties after delegating them earlier in the exhibition schedule. The win at AT&T Stadium completed New Orleans’ preseason and gave Moore another live evaluation before final roster reductions Sunday. Starting quarterback Tyler Shough sat while Spencer Rattler and Zach Wilson split the work. Rattler completed 8 of 10 passes for 79 yards, while Wilson went 9-for-12 for 93 yards. WDSU News’s Farrah Yvette shared a clip from Moore’s postgame availability Friday on X, formerly Twitter, following the Saints’ preseason finale. “Two very important details from tonight’s #Saints win: Kellen Moore was calling the plays He also didn’t wear a hat today. As a superstitious person, let’s keep that up and see what happens Week 1.” Two very important details from tonight’s #Saints win: 1. Kellen Moore was calling the plays 2. He also didn’t wear a hat today. As a superstitious person, let’s keep that up and see what happens Week 1. pic.twitter.com/px250PbTAe — Farrah Yvette (@farrah_yvette) August 29, 2026 Moore allowed offensive coordinator Doug Nussmeier to call the offense during the preseason opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Terry Joseph handled the defensive calls in that game. Moore returned to his customary offensive role Friday as New Orleans generated 169 rushing yards on 32 carries. The production helped the Saints finish without committing a turnover. Barion Brown, Rattler, and Zamir White each scored on the ground. Rattler’s touchdown covered eight yards, while White reached the end zone from 11 yards out. Daniel Carlson converted a 53-yard field goal with 1:55 remaining after Dallas completed a fourth-quarter rally. The kick secured the Saints’ only victory of the preseason. The outing provided Moore with live play-calling work before the regular season. New Orleans opens September 13 vs. the Detroit Lions at Ford Field, when Moore will begin his second season as the Saints’ head coach. articles.title: Ravens player on roster bubble with most at stake in 2026 NFL preseason finale
articles.summary: Joe Fagnano entered Baltimore’s preseason finale against Washington facing the strangest kind of pressure in football: the better he played, the more complicated his path to the 53-man roster became. The undrafted rookie quarterback out of Connecticut delivered his best performance of camp
articles._body: Joe Fagnano entered Baltimore’s preseason finale against Washington facing the strangest kind of pressure in football: the better he played, the more complicated his path to the 53-man roster became. The undrafted rookie quarterback out of Connecticut delivered his best performance of camp in the Ravens’ 41-3 rout of the Commanders, completing 19 of 27 passes for 162 yards and a touchdown, and finished the preseason 56-of-75 for 489 yards, three touchdowns and just one interception. Yet that very efficiency is what makes his roster case so precarious. A Preseason Too Good to Ignore Mandatory Credit: Mitch Stringer-Imagn Images Fagnano’s body of work over three preseason games left little doubt about his ability. He was described as “poised in the pocket and accurate” by Baltimore’s own team site, capping a stretch that included a strong showing against Minnesota in Week 2 before Friday’s finale against Washington. Against the Commanders, he scored on a 1-yard quarterback sneak after Washington fumbled the ball away, then connected with LaJohntay Wester on a acrobatic 10-yard touchdown grab that pushed Baltimore’s lead to 24-0 before halftime. Joe Fagnano takes it in himself to add 6️⃣ more to the board! WASvsBAL on @NFLNetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/vhNJHZRt0V — NFL (@NFL) August 28, 2026 The problem for Fagnano isn’t talent evaluation. It’s roster math. Baltimore already carries Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley as its top two quarterbacks, and coach Jesse Minter’s staff must decide whether the team can justify a rare third quarterback spot or whether Fagnano’s caliber of play makes him too valuable to risk exposing to waivers en route to the practice squad. The Roster Numbers Game Baltimore’s broader roster crunch adds intrigue to Fagnano’s situation. The Ravens dominated across the board Friday night, piling up a 456-177 total-yardage advantage and a 26-7 edge in first downs, but coaches were watching individual battles far more closely than the scoreboard. Running back Rasheen Ali, another player squarely on the bubble, managed just 28 yards on nine carries while working through an undisclosed injury that limited him earlier in camp, leaving his status behind Derrick Henry, Justice Hill and rookie Adam Randall very much unresolved. Randall, by contrast, strengthened his own case with 25 yards on five carries plus three catches for 45 yards, complicating the numbers at running back in a way that indirectly affects how many bodies Baltimore can afford to keep elsewhere on the roster. That crowded numbers game is exactly why Fagnano’s excellence creates a paradox. If Baltimore views him as a legitimate NFL backup rather than a developmental arm, the smarter long-term move might be trying to sneak him through waivers onto the practice squad, banking on 31 other teams passing on a quarterback with a 101.8 preseason passer rating. If any team believes he can start in a pinch, though, that gamble becomes far riskier, and Fagnano could force Baltimore’s hand into carrying three quarterbacks for the first time in years just to protect an asset they can’t risk losing for nothing. Baltimore must trim its roster to 53 players by Sunday at 6 p.m. ET, and few decisions will be scrutinized more than what the coaching staff does at the bottom of the quarterback depth chart. Fagnano did everything within his control by closing the preseason with a touchdown pass, a rushing score and a 70.4% completion rate in the finale alone, but his fate ultimately rests on a roster-construction debate rather than a talent evaluation, proof that sometimes the biggest obstacle for a bubble player isn’t performing well enough, but performing too well for his own roster spot’s convenience. articles.title: Texans player on roster bubble with most at stake in 2026 NFL preseason finale
articles.summary: Solomon Byrd entered Friday night’s preseason finale against the Carolina Panthers with the highest stakes of any Houston Texans player fighting for a spot on the 53-man roster, and left Charlotte with his fate more uncertain than when he arrived. The third-year defensive end, a former prac
articles._body: Solomon Byrd entered Friday night’s preseason finale against the Carolina Panthers with the highest stakes of any Houston Texans player fighting for a spot on the 53-man roster, and left Charlotte with his fate more uncertain than when he arrived. The third-year defensive end, a former practice-squad fixture in DeMeco Ryans’ system, had positioned himself as the clearest beneficiary of Houston’s edge-rusher injury crisis, only to suffer an ankle injury of his own in the fourth quarter of a 16-13 loss that dropped the Texans to 0-3 in the preseason. Byrd’s Opportunity Born From Misfortune David Butler II-Imagn Images Byrd’s path onto the bubble was shaped almost entirely by circumstances outside his control. With Dylan Horton and Ali Gaye both landing on injured reserve for what’s expected to be the entire 2026 season, Houston’s depth chart at edge rusher thinned dramatically in the days before the finale, turning Byrd from a longshot into arguably the frontrunner for the final edge spot behind Will Anderson Jr., Danielle Hunter and the rest of the room. It marked a stunning reversal for a player who had spent his first two NFL seasons entirely on the practice squad after going undrafted, never appearing in a regular-season game until late in 2024. Entering Friday, analysts framed the game as a referendum on whether Byrd could finally translate camp flashes into a locked roster spot. Texans Wire went further, calling him the biggest beneficiary of the injury attrition at his position and noting this represented his best and possibly last chance to prove he belongs on a 53-man roster after years of practice-squad limbo. A Strong Showing Cut Short For three quarters, Byrd delivered exactly the performance he needed. He notched four total tackles, including two solo stops, and broke up a pass, showing the disruptive edge presence that made him intriguing to Ryans’ staff in the first place. He also produced one of the highlight defensive plays of the night, sacking Panthers backup quarterback Jack Plummer for an 11-yard loss near Carolina’s own goal line, a play that nearly resulted in a safety for Houston. Then, on just the second play of the fourth quarter, everything changed. Byrd suffered an ankle injury and had to be helped off the field, his night ending before he could add to a resume that had otherwise been building momentum all evening. The injury adds a layer of uncertainty that no amount of tape study can resolve: Houston’s medical staff will need the next 48 hours to determine severity before Sunday’s league-wide deadline to trim rosters from 90 to 53 players. Solomon Byrd back to tent, under own power, and some encouragement for gritty #Texans edge from DeMeco Ryans, Will Anderson Jr. https://t.co/TwWZ22vJyq pic.twitter.com/Vth6nmszop — Aaron Wilson (@AaronWilson_NFL) August 29, 2026 What Comes Next for Houston’s Bubble The broader context makes Byrd’s situation even more precarious. The Texans finished their preseason winless, falling to the Panthers after Carolina’s Miles Davis scored the go-ahead touchdown and Jeremy Moon sealed it with a strip-sack of quarterback Brett Rypien in the final minute. Houston did answer briefly, with Zay Jones, one of the wide receivers also fighting for a roster spot, hauling in a fourth-quarter touchdown from Rypien to make it a three-point game, but it wasn’t enough. For Byrd specifically, the calculus now shifts from performance evaluation to medical evaluation. If the ankle injury is minor, his strong three-quarter showing combined with the season-ending injuries to Horton and Gaye should be enough to secure him a spot, since Houston will almost certainly need every healthy edge rusher it can find heading into Week 1. If the injury lingers, however, the Texans could look to other roster mechanisms, including a return trip to injured reserve or a practice-squad stash, options that would extend Byrd’s audition into the regular season rather than resolve it outright. Either way, no player on Houston’s roster bubble had more riding on Friday night’s finale, and few storylines captured the brutal unpredictability of NFL cutdown week quite like a career-defining opportunity ending in a trip to the medical tent. articles.title: CFB Week 0 Opens With Bill Belichick Watch
articles.summary: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images
articles._body: UNC will kick off its second season under beleaguered head coach Bill Belichick, whose program is looking to make a comeback after a season marred in scandal off the field and a lack of success on it. When Belichick was hired in December 2024, the six-time Super Bowl–winning head coach came in with plenty of fanfare—as well as a hefty five-year, $50 million contract . He had already faced controversy over his then-24-year-old girlfriend Jordon Hudson, who was also acting as his business partner and had become a presence around the football team—and who made waves during a cringey CBS interview . But hopes were high that Belichick could bring his NFL magic to college football. Belichick’s debut couldn’t have gone worse, however, when the Tar Heels suffered a 48–14 smackdown by TCU. On the field, things went downhill from there. UNC went 4–8 overall, finding itself toward the bottom of the ACC and without bowl-game eligibility. Off the field, controversies mounted, from questions around Hudson’s continued involvement and behavior, to a disputed trip to Saudi Arabia in search of funding . This past offseason, the drama appeared to cool. Belichick, with the help of GM Michael Lombardi, put together a top-15 recruiting class for the 2026–27 season. But then, earlier this summer, controversy reared its head again: Lombardi was put on administrative leave as the university investigated a personnel complaint against him. UNC defensive coordinator and Bill’s son Steve Belichick has also been out on indefinite medical leave since early August. On Saturday, against the same team that blew out the Tar Heels during last year’s season opener, Chapel Bill has a chance to start the season with redemption—or continue his debut campaign’s disappointing trend. articles.title: Everything Joe Harasymiak said ahead of the UMass / Rutgers game
articles.summary: Here's a look at everything UMass Football head coach Joe Harasymiak said ahead of his upcoming matchup versus Rutgers.
articles._body: UMass Football head coach Joe Harasymiak met with the media earlier this week ahead of the season opener matchup against Rutgers inside of SHI Stadium next Thursday night and here’s what he had to say. For a limited time, new members get their first year of exclusive Scarlet Knights coverage for just $30 – that’s 75% off. Don’t miss the sale of the season. Full Press Conference Transcript JOE HARASYMIAK: “All right, well, I appreciate everyone being here. Just super excited about, you know, starting the second year and getting into this. We’ve worked really hard over camp and the summer and last year, so hopefully this isn’t the last time we’ve been in a very good mood. That wouldn’t be the plan, so, but just super excited for us to get out there and go play. It’s kind of, you watch all the games last night. You know, the FBS games will start tomorrow, so just really excited.” Coach, how does it feel preparing against the team you were trying to help win just a couple years ago? JOE HARASYMIAK: “Yeah, it’s obviously, you know, part of this game. You know, I credit Coach Schiano for a lot of things that have gotten me to this point. All the guys I work with from Coach Ciarrocca to Dave Brock, you know, all those guys that are over there. I could name them all, but it’s certainly special for me. It was my first chance to coordinate in the Big Ten. Coach gave me that opportunity. You know, I’m really happy about a lot of the things we accomplished together. You know, back-to-back bowl games, you know, we took over a defense at a time of struggle, and that’s why, obviously, I got the opportunity, and, you know, in two years, we got it to a top 15, or we were 16th in total defense, and, you know, those are the good things. I certainly want some things back. Not happy with kind of the way it ended defensively there. You know, a lot of things go into that last year. We were playing a lot of the guys that are probably going to line up against us now as young guys, but, you know, kind of some things I want back. I went back to that UCLA game. I went back to the USC game, and I want back my Illinois call, zero-blitz standard game, so I’ve got to execute them, but ultimately, those, unfortunately, you remember the negative a little bit, but I try and focus on the positive in my relationship with Coach. You know, we’re still close. It’ll be great to see him and just great to see all those guys because I know how hard they work, and certainly that’s rubbed off on me.” Is it easier a little bit to prepare for this opening game compared to most opening games because you at least have an idea of what they do on offense and defense? JOE HARASYMIAK: “Yeah, I think maybe with the identity part, like, this is going to be a very physical, violent game. They’re going to play extremely hard. That’s what coach Schiano teams do, so wouldn’t expect anything less, so maybe from that standpoint, I could tell you from being there for three years, I know how he works. I know how they work. I know how physical it’s going to be. I mean, it’s a Big Ten opponent, but from the X’s and O’s standpoint, I mean, certainly working there with Kirk and all those kinds of things and going against him before, right, when I was at Rutgers and he was at Minnesota, but off seasons, you have new studies. You do a lot of things, and then certainly, their whole defense is brand new, so that’ll be kind of the unknown we have to handle. I think in first games, regardless of what you think you know, there’s a level of unknown that comes out that you got to be able to handle.” You didn’t practice at night at all leading up to the game? JOE HARASYMIAK: “No, we did that in camp, so the way we structured camp is we had some night practices, and then our two scrimmages were on Thursday at 6 o’clock, so I’ve tried to do, you know, us and our staff have tried to put this together so that, you know, we give every opportunity for our guys not to be caught off guard by the moment because it’s a special moment. I mean, opening day at Rutgers is special. There’ll be a lot of people there. They’re the Thursday night game. It’s the Big Ten Network game. I’ve coached in it before, and the level of excitement’s really cool in terms of the game day atmosphere they create, so we’ve tried to give our guys that, which I thought something that’s what our team struggled with last year, just those environments, the anxiety that goes with that, so yeah, we scrimmaged at 6. We went underneath the lights. We did everything from a pregame routine. I brought them back in the locker room, gave them the amount of time they’re going to be in the locker room. We did game simulations. We had iPads. We tried to do everything we could do to put this team in a situation for when they get out there. It’s just 120 by 53 and a third. You know, I talked to them the other day. It’s like the movie Hoosiers. Go out and measure it. Like, it’s the same field, no matter who you play over these 12 games, but we got to stick to us and go out and be us.” Talk about the familiarity. The other end, is there anything you need to do to guard, considering they know you pretty well as well, and obviously a lot of you guys? JOE HARASYMIAK: “Yeah, I think certainly from a game plan perspective, you know, I would say more of the UMass defense and Rutgers offense from working together. I think there’s some familiarity there. But I think, you know, when you have off-season studies and, you know, I don’t know what they believe, obviously, what the strength of their team is. Obviously, KJ Duff and Antwan Raymond, I’m sure they’re excited about their O-line. I know their young receiver core is good. S

articles.title: Timberwolves, Jazz trade grades for Josh Green-Cody Williams swap
articles.summary: The Minnesota Timberwolves addressed their need for another power forward with their recent signing of Jonathan Kuminga to a two-year, $12.4 million contract in free agency. However, the Timberwolves needed to pull the trigger on a trade to clear some space under the second apron so they could us
articles._body: The Minnesota Timberwolves addressed their need for another power forward with their recent signing of Jonathan Kuminga to a two-year, $12.4 million contract in free agency. However, the Timberwolves needed to pull the trigger on a trade to clear some space under the second apron so they could use their taxpayer mid-level exception. That’s what they did on Friday when they sent Josh Green, a piece they received from the Charlotte Hornets in the LaMelo Ball trade, to the Utah Jazz in exchange for Cody Williams and John Konchar. The Timberwolves promptly waived and stretched the remaining $6.2 million in Konchar’s expiring contract. By doing so, they opened up a roster spot and created even more space under the second apron (around $4.5 million) to use on another signing moving forward. It was obvious right from the moment Green arrived in Minnesota that he wasn’t long for the team, and the Timberwolves already found the right trade that they believe could help them moving forward. As for the Jazz, they are getting a solid wing who can contribute on defense as well as contribute some playmaking. But this was a rather painful admission from the franchise in the end that drafting Williams in 2024 wasn’t the best use of resources. Here are the grades for the Timberwolves and Jazz after completing their swap on Friday. Timberwolves do what they must while banking on Cody Williams’ untapped potential Peter Creveling-Imagn Images It was a surprise win for the Timberwolves that Kuminga chose to sign with them in free agency. After all, the Los Angeles Lakers were hot on Kuminga’s tail, and they actually could have offered a contract that doubled the 23-year-old’s commitment with the Timberwolves. But with Minnesota, Kuminga’s path to playing time is clear. The Timberwolves will need him, period. It looked like Jaden McDaniels was going to have to slide over to the four to cover for Julius Randle and Naz Reid’s departures, and they were so thin at power forward that Trey Lyles, who was out of the NBA last season, looked like he would need to play a huge role. This trade at least clears the hurdle for the Timberwolves to sign Kuminga. It is an important factor to consider in the evaluation of this trade. The Timberwolves needed to clear space, and they did so while acquiring Williams from the Jazz — giving the roster an additional X-factor on a team that’s already full of them. The Jazz selected Williams with the 10th overall pick of the 2024 NBA Draft, and the Timberwolves essentially got him as a throw-in. Williams is still on his rookie contract, and the Timberwolves badly needed players with size on the wing. The 21-year-old forward has that in spades. Standing at 6-foot-8 with a 7-foot-1 wingspan, Williams has all the measurables in the world to make a talent evaluator salivate over him. Alas, this has not yet translated to many meaningful contributions on the hardwood. Through his two seasons thus far in the NBA, he’s averaging 7.0 points on 42/24/71 shooting splits, all while not being a factor on the glass. His lack of three-point shooting is especially backbreaking. It’s difficult to justify minutes for any player who cannot throw a stone into the ocean, and Williams commands virtually no respect from opposing defenses. His feel for the game has lacked considerably, and at this point, it’s difficult to characterize him as anything other than a bust. But he’s only 21 years of age. For reference, he’s two years younger than 2026 lottery pick Yaxel Lendeborg. The Timberwolves believe that there could very well be some untapped potential left in him. Konchar would have been the better player to keep. He at least has a history of being a serviceable rotation player for a winning Memphis Grizzlies team. But the Timberwolves are banking on Williams’ upside. Perhaps he could turn into a weapon under head coach Chris Finch as they look to play at 150 miles per hour with Ball, Anthony Edwards, and Ayo Dosunmu at the controls. Grade: B+ Jazz give up on former lottery pick, strengthen for potential playoff push Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images It’s no secret that the Jazz believe that the time for tanking is over . They traded for Jaren Jackson Jr. back in February, and that is not a move Utah would have made if they intended to keep on playing for lottery balls. For the first time in years, there could very well be meaningful basketball in Salt Lake City to be had for Lauri Markkanen and company. With that said, Williams was on a short leash for the Jazz, and Utah evidently believed that there’s no more use in keeping him around now that their intention is to win games. But did Utah pull the plug on the Williams experiment far too soon? Perhaps not. Williams was also clogging up the team’s cap sheet, as he has a team option worth $7.7 million for the 2027-28 season, and Utah believed that getting something of value for him now was better than keeping him and then running into a roster crunch later down the line that would require them to give up on him anyway. Williams did average over 20 points during Summer League, and he did so on 46/34/72 shooting splits. The improved three-point shooting, in particular, was very promising — as he ramped up his volume while increasing his efficiency. However, Green is more of a surefire rotation player for a team with winning aspirations. Green did fall in the Hornets’ rotation last year, but that was due to Kon Knueppel’s emergence, not his poor play. Green shot 42 percent from three last year, was a stout defensive presence and a diligent runner on the court, and he’s a smart player who knows his role and doesn’t try to do too much. articles.title: College Football Cheat Sheet: ACC takes center stage in Week Zero
articles.summary: College football has returned. It feels so good to be back. Adam Luckett's College Football Cheat Sheet sets the table for Saturday.
articles._body: The long wait is officially over. FCS teams got things warmed up on Thursday. Now FBS football will be played on Saturday. It feels so good to be back. College football’s first weekend card is not exactly stacked, but ball will be played on television. There will be some big viewership windows for the ACC after the league was ridiculed for last season’s playoff situation, and a very fun Group of Six matchup that might determine who receives a College Football Playoff bid. The madness has returned in 2026. KSR’s College Football Cheat Sheet is back for the 2025 season to set the table on Fridays for the football weekend all season long. College football’s regular-season sprint starts right now. Let’s enjoy the ride. We all know that some shenanigans are on the way. The Slate North Carolina vs. TCU (Ireland) Noon ET ESPN San Jose State at No. 14 USC 3:00 p.m. ET NBC NC State at Virginia 3:30 p.m. ET ESPN Jacksonville State at North Dakota State 5:30 p.m. ET CBS Sports Network Sacramento State at Eastern Michigan 6:30 p.m. ET ESPN+ Hawaii at Stanford 7:00 p.m. ET ACC Network New Mexico State at Florida State 7:00 p.m. ET The CW Memphis at UNLV 10:00 p.m. ET FOX Week Zero Preview KSR’s “11 Personnel” podcast has shifted to a daily model for the 2026 college football season. Every Thursday on KSR’s YouTube channel, Nick Roush and I will preview the weekend’s slate, give out our favorite picks for the weekend, and discuss what’s going on in the world of college football. Smash that play button. Subscribe to the KSR YouTube Channel for press conferences, interviews, original shows, fan features, and exclusive content. A big weekend for the ACC The SEC and Big Ten will get the lion’s share of attention all season long as the race to the 2026 College Football Playoff begins. College football’s Big Two will come into the limelight next weekend. Another power conference will hog the spotlight in Week Zero. There are three games involving ACC teams on Saturday. TCU vs. North Carolina : Another college football season gets started in Dublin. Only this time it will not be a conference game. After seeing Georgia Tech-Florida State in 2024 and Iowa State-Kansas State in 2025, it will be an ACC vs. Big 12 showdown. TCU is a dark horse in the Big 12 with new offensive coordinator Gordon Sammis and Harvard quarterback transfer Jaden Craig . The Frogs could be sneaky this season, but this game isn’t really about them. Can year two for Bill Belichick actually be worse? He already lost his general manager and will be calling plays in this game. Can Bobby Petrino provide an offensive spark? Why did they not go portal-heavy? Underdogs have typically been live in this game. Will that hold this year? What a fascinating Week Zero matchup this is. NC State at Virginia : A game that was supposed to be played in Brazil has moved back to ACC country. Scott Stadium has sold out for the conference clash between NC State and Virginia. The Hoos rode a high-volume portal class to the ACC Championship Game last season. They’ll be looking to do that again. NC State got star quarterback CJ Bailey back, but it came at a cost. The Pack lost multiple big-time starters to power conference programs. Both squads are seen as potential dark horses in the ACC race. Both avoid Miami, Clemson, and Notre Dame on the schedule. The winner could have double-digit win upside. The loser could walk away feeling like they missed a very big opportunity. This is the perfect Week Zero game. New Mexico State at Florida State : Mike Norvell is on the hot seat. Everyone knows that. Saturday will give the Seminoles a nice opener to begin a pivotal season before they host SMU on Labor Day. Norvell is calling plays, and Ashton Daniels takes over at quarterback. Defensive coordinator Tony White has a defense that could make some noise. FSU faces a brutal schedule. Norvell needs a fast start. That will have to begin in Week Zero. A very important year for Lincoln Riley starts now USC handed out a fat contract to hire Lincoln Riley away from Oklahoma. After a strong 11-3 debut with Caleb Williams at quarterback, the Trojans have not looked great. Riley is just 24-15 over the last three seasons with zero top-15 finishes in ESPN’s SP+ rankings. This proud program is 11-7 in Big Ten play. This is not what USC signed up for. The Trojans took a step in the right direction in 2025 as they produced a top-40 defense for the first time in Riley’s tenure and won big home games against Michigan, Iowa, and UCLA. Unfortunately, defensive coordinator D’Anton Lynn left for Penn State, and there are some doubters. This program made a huge splash when they hired general manager Chad Bowden away from Notre Dame. That led to a rockstar 2026 high school recruiting class. Many of those recruiting wins will see the field, but Riley needs wins right now. Oregon, Penn State, Ohio State, and Indiana all showing up on the schedule makes things tricky. That run will start on Saturday afternoon against San Jose State. That game will feature former TCU head coach Gary Patterson returning to the field as the new defensive play caller in Los Angeles. We won’t learn a lot about USC this weekend, but this is a no-doubt pressure-cooker season for Riley. The rest of the college football card There was some conference realignment this offseason that included a bunch of Mountain West teams leaving for the new Pac-12. That left some open spots. FCS powerhouse North Dakota State has filled one of those spots and is eligible for postseason play this year. Could the Bison emerge as a College Football Playoff dark horse? Their FBS debut in the Fargodome will occur against former FCS powerhouse Jacksonville State. articles.title: Show HN: Pictiur: Image converter, optimizer and resizer, all in one
articles.summary: Disclaimer: This project was entirely vibe coded, this was done by a professional, do not try to reproduce this at home. I also fully understand that this may not match some people's values, so I'd like to point out that I built this project for my personal use first and foremost. If my approach
articles._body: Disclaimer: This project was entirely vibe coded, this was done by a professional, do not try to reproduce this at home. I also fully understand that this may not match some people's values, so I'd like to point out that I built this project for my personal use first and foremost. If my approach still bothers you, well, that's ok. For personal reasons, I've had to do document scans every day for the past month, photos of my ID papers, and I realized something: the online offering for processing images is horrible. Generally these tools focus on one thing, conversion, optimization, or resizing, but rarely 2 tools in one, and even less 3. It could pass if, on top of that, the offering wasn't riddled with sites full of dumbass ads, with "DOWNLOAD" buttons that are a trap, and with data processing that's dubious at best. I've also been running a home server for a while now, on which I install lots of self-hosted projects (with Coolify I also wanted to see what Deepseek Flash was capable of, beyond the last questions I had asked it, namely how to set up my vegetable garden on 100m², and whether I should put my rainwater collector on a stand or not. So I dove into a benchmark on the best algorithms to use for my idea, how to architect the app, etc... In the end, after about an hour of back and forth, I had a complete implementation plan and a tech stack I already knew, in case I had to debug by hand and use my brain again. A few hours in the IDE and here is the final result: https://pictiur.pages.dev/ The site is 100% local, the whole process runs in the browser, it's a PWA so the app is installable and usable offline, and for now it supports the most well-known formats but I fully intend to add more. The repo is public in case you want to install it on your own server (and feel free to take the opportunity to trash talk the code quality and explain just how much of a disaster AI is, and how your nephew who's currently learning PHP would have structured this in a much more professional way). https://github.com/Etheonor/pictiur And feel free to tell me if you see any improvements to make. As I said at the beginning, it is built for my personal use, but if other ideas can be grafted onto it, I'm all ears. With seven days until South Carolina football kicks off 2026, a look back at No. 7 Nick Emmanwori
articles.summary: With seven days until South Carolina football kicks off 2026, a look back at No. 7, defensive back Nick Emmanwori
articles._body: South Carolina football will take the field for the first time in 2026 on Sept. 5 against Kent State. Williams-Brice Stadium will play host to the Gamecocks and Golden Flashes at 12:45 p.m., just seven days from today. Several all-time greats have worn the No. 7 at South Carolina, including Jadeveon Clowney, Spencer Rattler, and early-career Jaycee Horn. However, another great player wore No. 7 in his final year with the Gamecocks. Defensive back Nick Emmanwori played for his hometown team from 2022 to 2024. Questions about this story? Kevin Miller is discussing it with subscribers on The Insiders Forum. An Irmo, South Carolina native and product of the Irmo Yellow Jackets, Emmanwori played all over his high school’s defense. Because of that, there were many who weren’t sure what position he would play after committing to the Gamecocks as an underrated player in the class of 2022. As it turned out, the recruiting industry wisened up, ranking him as a four-star prospect after his commitment. From there, Emmanwori turned into one of the best defensive backs in program history. After picking the Gamecocks, Emmanwori famously said he was putting Clemson “on notice” for ignoring him as a recruit. Despite USC not having won the Palmetto Bowl since 2013, Emmanwori went on to help Carolina win two out of three matchups against the rival Tigers. Emmanwori was thrust into early action as a true freshman. Though he played in the season opener, he logged 24 combined tackles the next two weeks against Arkansas and Georgia. Wearing No. 21 and moving around the defense, he finished the year well and earned tons of Freshman All-American honors as South Carolina’s leading tackler. He capped off the stellar debut season with the game-sealing fumble recovery against Clemson. 2023 was another good year for Emmanwori. Though he was primarily a safety, he played even more spots for defensive coordinator Clayton White than he did as a freshman. That included starting some games at nickel. Emmanwori had double-digit tackles twice and again did so against Georgia. He logged the first two interceptions of his career in the final two games against Kentucky and Clemson, picking off both the Wildcats and Tigers in the end zone, preventing touchdowns. As good as Emmanwori was his first two years, he took his game to a new level as a junior. Switching to No. 7, he became an easy choice for All-American teams. He led the Gamecocks in tackles (88) and was second in interceptions (four), taking two picks back for scores. Emmanwori had an additional interception eliminated by another player’s penalty, a would-be game-clinching 100-yard pick-six against LSU that was wiped out by a bad call. Several smaller news outlets picked Emmanwori as the SEC Defensive Player of the Year and/or college football’s National Safety of the Year. See other jersey countdown stories like this on GamecockCentral.com. Following his junior year, Emmanwori elected to forego his final year of eligibility to pursue a professional career. Projected by many to be a first-round pick after an elite season and an even better showing at the NFL Combine, teams made the mistake of passing on him in the first round. Then, early in the second round, the Seattle Seahawks drafted Emmanwori. The former Gamecock had an incredible rookie season, finishing as an NFL Rookie of the Year finalist. He also won the honor outright on Tom Brady’s annual award show. Along the way, Emmanwori became the first NFL player ever to block a field goal, sack the quarterback, register an additional tackle for loss, and intercept a pass in the same game. Just as he did in Columbia, Emmanwori played multiple roles for the Seattle defense. He became one of the most valuable and most versatile defensive players in the league. He then helped the Seahawks win Super Bowl LX alongside fellow former Gamecock Ernest Jones. Emmanwori has the chance at an elite NFL career and is a likely candidate to earn future induction into the University of South Carolina Lettermen’s Athletics Hall of Fame. Have a South Carolina football question for the GamecockCentral staff? Ask it on The Insiders Forum.
