articles.title: Offshore nuclear barges could power ports and data centers—starting with California, where nuclear is banned
articles.summary: Offshore nuclear power could potentially power everything from ports and data centers to merchant cargo ships and military fleets.
articles._body: As the U.S. paves the way for a nuclear renaissance to power the AI data center boom , the next frontier is building small nuclear reactors offshore to power coastal facilities and merchant ships. Strangely, the momentum could begin in California, a state that banned building new nuclear plants 50 years ago. This summer, the Port of Long Beach signed an agreement with the Trump administration to develop next-generation small modular reactors (SMRs) that could power ports, data centers, and vessels with emission-free energy. Offshore nuclear power sounds unusual, but naval submarines and aircraft carriers have run on small nuclear reactors for decades. In 2020, Russia put the world’s first floating nuclear power station on a barge into service, powering the remote Arctic town of Pevek—population 4,000—and its harbor. Long Beach and Los Angeles are a different scale entirely. The two ports adjoin one another and together form the largest container port complex in the Western Hemisphere. The Port of Long Beach is now working with local startup Bluecore Energy to build SMRs on floating barges—though the project remains at least a few years from reality. “I think it’s very viable. It’s just a question of when, not if,” said Max Hopkins, a nuclear power analyst at CITIC CLSA, speaking about the growth of offshore nuclear power broadly—not California specifically—across military, maritime shipping, and AI data center applications. “To put something into place fast, with production means, and then you can just float it somewhere—it seems like offshore barges are going to be almost ideal,” Hopkins told Fortune . “I think it’s going to become pretty accepted, much more so than people realize.” Still, Hopkins emphasized the technology is years from commercial deployment. Regulatory frameworks need to be built, and so do the supply chains and manufacturing systems. The progress isn’t confined to Long Beach. Denmark-based Saltfoss Energy is developing similar nuclear reactor barges in Europe. Nuclear’s maritime moment The future of powering military warfare and maritime merchant shipping could be nuclear, Hopkins said. Maritime vessels account for about 3% of global greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, which may not sound like much, but it’s roughly equivalent to the total GHG emissions of all of Africa. The federal push is accelerating on multiple fronts. This week, the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Maritime Administration (MARAD) announced a partnership with London-based Core Power to develop the regulatory frameworks and technology for a future fleet of nuclear-powered merchant cargo vessels. A day later, the U.S. and the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) launched the Atomic Technologies Licensed for Applications at Sea (ATLAS) initiative. The effort is designed to advance SMR and micro-reactor technologies for merchant shipping—“underpinned by the highest levels of nuclear safety, security, and non-proliferation,” the IAEA said. The appeal is speed and endurance: nuclear-powered ships only need to refuel every two or three years instead of every voyage, cutting fossil fuel use, and enabling faster transit. “At the same time, innovations such as floating nuclear power plants provide versatile energy sources that could deliver reliable electricity to coastal or remote communities and industry,” the IAEA said in a statement. A nuclear California? Long Beach-based Bluecore was founded only in January. It raised $10 million in a pre-seed round and quickly became the first nuclear company to partner with MARAD on offshore reactors. Founder and CEO Kofi Asante, 31, is a Ghanaian-American from Austin, Texas, who quickly became a Silicon Valley veteran before relocating to Southern California. He built his logistics and maritime-shipping expertise at Uber Freight, heavy-cargo drone company Elroy Air, and electric barge startup Arc—before starting Bluecore. His goal: use the maritime industry to provide clean, consistent power for ports and AI data centers. “The philosophy was really process of elimination: if you need that much energy, then you arrive at a nuclear reactor,” Asante told Fortune . “And if you need real estate, two-thirds of the world is water, so you can use barges for extra real estate.” “We can go miles away and connect via subsea cable—so we don’t have to be near neighborhoods, and we don’t have to be co-located at the port,” he added. All of this requires technology that’s already largely developed, Asante argued, including smaller versions of traditional light-water nuclear reactors. Each 10-megawatt reactor on a barge can power the equivalent of about 10,000 homes, can be moved via tugboats, and can be stacked alongside each other for extra power generation. Asante recognizes he’s pursuing this technology in a state that banned the developed of new nuclear reactors in 1976, citing environmental and safety concerns, including still-unsolved issues with radioactive waste . The Port of Long Beach knows this is a lengthy process. Port CEO Noel Hacegaba noted that state lawmakers are already debating legislation to study lifting the ban. “Nuclear is having a moment at the Port of Long Beach, and we are engaged with the private sector, along with state and federal legislators on this issue,” Hacegaba said in an emailed statement to Fortune . “This innovation is years away from becoming a reality due to the technological advancements and regulatory hurdles that still need to be cleared, and it cannot advance without state and federal approvals,” he added. “In the meantime, our new partners at Bluecore Energy are following state and federal laws as they provide the private-sector experience to research and develop SMR technology.” Can it be safe—and affordable? Two big questions loom over offshore nuclear: safety, and whether it can compete economically with natural gas and solar power. Asante draws a manufacturing analogy—with some exag

articles.summary: On Friday, the Dallas Cowboys encountered a few rough patches during their final preseason contest, a 27-24 loss to the New Orleans Saints. They were trailing by 15, 24-9, heading into the fourth period, but they deserve plenty of credit for at least making it a game towards the end. The Cowboys
articles._body: On Friday, the Dallas Cowboys encountered a few rough patches during their final preseason contest, a 27-24 loss to the New Orleans Saints. They were trailing by 15, 24-9, heading into the fourth period, but they deserve plenty of credit for at least making it a game towards the end. The Cowboys tied the game at 24, with backup quarterback candidate Sam Howell taking control and leading Dallas to two touchdown drives. Alas, that comeback attempt proved to be too little too late, as a field goal from the Saints was enough to give them the victory in the end. From that game, one would think that it became more obvious as to who’s in the lead for the backup job behind star man Dak Prescott, with Howell showing the requisite composure to lead his team back from a considerable deficit. Nonetheless, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said that the battle between Howell and Joe Milton III for the backup quarter job remains “neck and neck” as “both guys want to win the spot”, as per Calvin Watkins of Dallas Morning News. Howell was once the starting quarterback for the Washington Commanders, but he has since served as a third-string QB in the NFL, most recently serving as the third option for the Philadelphia Eagles. He did not play a single snap in 2025, as Jalen Hurts’ health held steady throughout the campaign. Meanwhile, the Cowboys believed in Milton enough to trade a fifth-round pick for him in April of 2025, and he served as the backup last season to Prescott. His advantage in this backup QB position battle is that he knows the team’s offensive system and playbook by heart after having already spent a season with the team, and Dallas may be more invested in him as a result. Nonetheless, this situation should get a resolution soon, as both QBs did everything they could to complicate Schottenheimer’s final decision. articles.title: At the ‘Super Bowl of trucking,’ a driver who trained 14 years wins the golden belt buckle
articles.summary: Miguel Corral first competed in 2012. This year, after facing over against 428 other rivals, and following a lifetime of safe miles, he finally won.
articles._body: This summer has been full of competition: from Spain winning the World Cup , to the NBA finals where the Knicks saw a historic comeback, to now, where an event in which drivers across the country are putting pedal to the metal and competing in the National Truck Driving Championships, colloquially known as the “Super Bowl of trucking.” This year’s competition saw 429 drivers from 49 states who have logged a combined total of nearly 775 million safe driving miles throughout their careers, which is over 31,000 circles around the earth. Drivers from 55 companies, ranging from small mom-and-pop companies to Fortune 500 giants like Walmart , FedEx , XPO , and UPS, all vied in tests showcasing their driving, turning and parking skills as they [safely] raced for glory in Pittsburgh earlier this month. “The entire motivation of this program is to make them better on the road and to continue to drive safe,” said Jacob Pierce, executive director of the American Trucking Associations’ Safety Management Council. “It creates a company culture where everybody buys into ‘every day is a safe day.’” American Trucking Associations. Why safety, not speed, wins In 2024, large trucks accounted for nearly one in ten (9%) of all vehicles involved in a fatal crash, according to a National Safety Council study . And with 11 billion tons of freight moved by truck in 2024, the stakes of getting safety right extend far beyond the competition floor. Maneuvering a vehicle that weighs thousands of pounds needs extra caution when it comes to maintaining safe roads. For example, a loaded tractor trailer requires 20% to 40% more distance than cars to stop, according to data analyzed by The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety. Large trucks were involved in 5,218 fatal crashes in 2024, up 30% over the past decade, according to National Safety Council data . Eric Ramsdell—a Walmart tank trunk driver who took first place in his division—said the championship reflects a responsibility that follows drivers on the road. “Every day we have to understand we have people’s lives at stake, equipment, our safe mileage record,” he told Fortune . The skills course, he added, puts competitors under pressure much like real-world driving does but requires them to “focus and maneuver safely around and do the pre-trip in a safe manner.” But for companies eager to participate in the “Super Bowl of trucking,” as the competition is known as in the industry, they have to prove their drivers have what it takes to take on the open road—and aren’t afraid to hit the brakes when needed. To qualify, drivers must win a top placement at their state competition, sport a clean, preventable accident-free safety record for the previous year, and meet full-time driving requirements with their company. And being “accident-free” isn’t as easy as avoiding a major crash: even incidents like hitting a curb and slicing a tire can cut drivers from the competition. Pierce told Fortune he’s seen drivers go to state “20-plus times and have yet to make it to nationals, but they keep coming back because they want their chance.” When inches matter more than speed American Trucking Associations. Competitions usually involve a mixture of timing and speed, but at NTDC, it’s all about precision—and not hitting a giant yellow duck. The three-day competition began with a written exam that tested drivers’ road knowledge and safety. Next, there was a pre-trip inspection in which drivers are to identify planted safety-risks that they could face in real life. Decoys ranged from something big like an unsecured load, to easy-to-overlook details like a crack in the passenger side frame, a wiper blade missing, or a loose lug nut.  Competitors also faced an obstacle course in which  drivers made their way down paths lined with cones and bright yellow, plastic ducks. To show off their precision skills, drivers made turns as close to the 3.5-inch-tall ducks as possible. Factor in the lack of safety-assistance-technology like backup cameras, and drivers are forced to rely on instincts and skill. “We have to cover all that up because that would make it too easy for them,” Pierce said. “We are purists when it comes to driving a truck.”  Walmart. The last truckers standing  When day three rolled in, companies like FedEx , Walmart, and UPS dominated the leaderboards. FedEx has 18 finalists across two company divisions; Walmart had nine finalists and UPS had five, while smaller freight and shipping company XPO sported three. After a grueling obstacle course where drivers navigated tight turns, tight parking reverses, and quick, controlled stops, winners were finally selected for each of the nine classes, divided by the size of the truck: from flatbeds to three, four, and five-axle vehicles.  Another Walmart driver, Richard Prescott, took first place for the flatbed division. For Prescott, a first-time national winner who has spent the last 45 years in the trucking industry, simply reaching Pittsburgh was the result of years of close calls and incremental progress. “That process is extremely hard to get through,” Prescott told Fortune . “You have to do baby steps.” When Walmart was announced as the flatbed winner, he initially thought the trophy belonged to a teammate. “My boss… grabs me from behind, and I told him Mark won, and he says, ‘No, you did,’” Prescott said. “It’s still sinking in.” Miguel Corral competed for UPS under the four-axle division, and took home the grand champion title. Corral told Fortune he’s a nine-time NTDC competitor, and though there are always “nerves” when he competes, the event “feels like a family reunion.” The competition may be high-pressure, but its core skills are familiar. He said he approaches the pre-trip inspection much as he does before a normal shift: “I inspect my equipment every day, making sure to be thorough and complete each time.”  On the obstacle course, drivers are tested on accuracy, not speed, and

Watch Trevon Diggs record his 1st interception with Seahawks
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks got an immediate glimpse of what Trevon Diggs can bring to their defense in his first game with the team, as the veteran defensive back plucked an interception against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium in the preseason finale. Diggs, who signed with Seattle on Aug.
articles._body: The Seattle Seahawks got an immediate glimpse of what Trevon Diggs can bring to their defense in his first game with the team, as the veteran defensive back plucked an interception against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium in the preseason finale. Diggs, who signed with Seattle on Aug. 19 on a one-year, minimum-salary contract, needed only three defensive series to make his presence felt. Midway through the first quarter, he intercepted Chiefs third-string quarterback Garrett Nussmeier, producing Seattle’s only defensive takeaway of the night. The play showcased Diggs’ experience and ball skills. Lining up near the hash in Mike Macdonald’s defense, Diggs stayed with his receiver and read Nussmeier’s intentions before breaking toward the pass. The throw was underthrown, allowing Diggs to get in front of Xavier Worthy’s route and secure the pick . Trevon Diggs picks up his first INT as a Seahawk pic.twitter.com/ofkLT3qcuz — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 29, 2026 Diggs then returned the interception deep downfield before reaching the end zone. The Seahawks were subsequently flagged for excessive celebration, but the turnover still gave Seattle an opportunity to put points on the board. Jalen Milroe and the offense converted the possession into a scoring drive, while Jason Myers later supplied a 46-yard field goal. The interception was stood out given Diggs’ previous production. He led the NFL with 11 interceptions in 2021 and earned first-team All-Pro recognition that season. The two-time Pro Bowl selection is now attempting to revive his career after knee injuries disrupted his progress. His debut was not flawless. Diggs made an impressive tackle on a Kansas City rushing play but also missed an opportunity to bring down tight end Travis Kelce in the open field. Still, the interception became the defining moment of his first appearance in Seattle. The Seahawks ultimately finished the preseason with a 9-9 tie after Myers missed a potential 52-yard game-winning field goal wide right as time expired. Diggs’ short appearance nevertheless gave Seattle a positive development as the team evaluates its crowded cornerback competition ahead of the Sept. 9 season opener against the New England Patriots. With Devon Witherspoon, Josh Jobe, rookie Julian Neal and either Nehemiah Pritchett or Noah Igbinoghene also competing for roster spots, Diggs’ first interception with the Seahawks give him an early highlight in that battle. articles.title: Ed Sheeran Reacts to Being Mocked in New ‘Ali G’ Trailer
articles.summary: Sacha Baron Cohen's comeback trailer named the singer alongside COVID and war as reasons the world got worse.
articles._body: Getting singled out by Sacha Baron Cohen ‘s most infamous character turned out to be good publicity, not an insult, for Ed Sheeran . Cohen’s Ali G: Who Iz I? , due in theaters Oct. 23 via Amazon MGM, resurrects the fictional interviewer 24 years after his last film outing. The character narrates his own return in the trailer, listing everything that went wrong during his two decades away — wars, the pandemic, and Sheeran by name — before pivoting into the film’s premise: a “documentary” built from real interviews and unsuspecting public figures, in the spirit of Cohen’s late-’90s TV show. Sheeran took the jab as an honor rather than a slight. “Tell 10-year-old me that Ali G would put him in his movie,” he wrote on Instagram. “Restecpa” — the character’s signature butchering of “respect,” first used in 2002’s Ali G Indahouse . View this post on Instagram The film marks Cohen’s first time directing a feature himself, after previous Ali G and Borat projects were helmed by other directors. Production was kept under wraps entirely; Cohen reportedly showed up in character at Wimbledon this year without tipping off the film’s existence. The plot centers on Ali G discovering his girlfriend, played by Morgana Robinson, is pregnant after he resurfaces in the public eye. Not every reaction has matched Sheeran’s good humor. The trailer has stirred real objections in the U.K., where critics and a cinema-boycott push have called out the character’s styling — dreadlocked wig, Rasta-style hat — as racial caricature that hasn’t aged well since Ali G’s original run. Cohen built Ali G into a defining piece of British comedy before moving on to bigger disguises: Borat , Brüno , a Madonna video cameo, and eventually straight dramatic work in projects like The Trial of the Chicago 7 and Marvel’s Ironheart .

articles.title: Giants’ Tony Vitello, Logan Webb ejected for arguing Nolan Arenado foul ball call
articles.summary: Emotions ran high for the San Francisco Giants in the third inning of an eventual 10-6 loss to the Arizona Diamondbacks. With a runner on first and already two outs in the inning, starting pitcher Blake Tidwell got Nolan Arenado to a 1-2 count as the Giants looked to keep their deficit at just on
articles._body: Emotions ran high for the San Francisco Giants in the third inning of an eventual 10-6 loss to the Arizona Diamondbacks. With a runner on first and already two outs in the inning, starting pitcher Blake Tidwell got Nolan Arenado to a 1-2 count as the Giants looked to keep their deficit at just one run, 3-2. Arenado, however, hit a sharp slicing ball towards the third base line, which the third base umpire called fair. However, from the Giants’ point of view, they felt as though that hit from Arenado, which ended up being a double, crossed the third base bag while in foul territory. They believe that Arenado should have returned to home plate and received another 1-2 pitch from Tidwell. This belief of theirs was so strong that manager Tony Vitello and starting pitcher Logan Webb both protested the call way too passionately for the umpire’s liking, and they ended up being ejected from the game. Tony Vitello and Logan Webb were both ejected after arguing that this Nolan Arenado double was a foul ball pic.twitter.com/QEq31OlQCp — Jomboy Media (@JomboyMedia) August 29, 2026 While Arenado’s hit itself did not score a run for the Diamondbacks, this allowed Arizona to extend the inning and bring Tim Tawa to the plate. Tawa subsequently hit a home run on the following at-bat, which must have made the Giants’ blood boil all the more as the Diamondbacks extended their lead to four runs, 6-2. Baseball is indeed a game of inches, and in real time, it certainly looked like when Giants third baseman Shay Whitcomb had the play on the ball, the ball was in foul territory. Perhaps the third base umpire saw that the ball bounced fair down the line before it ricocheted towards foul ground near Whitcomb. The Giants climbed back into the game, pulling it back to within one run, 6-5, by the end of the fifth inning. Alas, a three-run inning by the Diamondbacks in the sixth eventually doomed San Francisco for good, leaving the Giants to wonder how differently the game would have turned out had the third base umpire ruled Arenado’s hit a foul ball. articles.title: Buccaneers HC Todd Bowles reveals level of offensive line depth concern after shutout
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers entered their preseason finale with confidence in their starting offensive line, but Friday night’s 19-0 shutout loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars raised questions about what lies behind that first unit. With the Tampa Bay resting their starters, the game gave Todd B
articles._body: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers entered their preseason finale with confidence in their starting offensive line , but Friday night’s 19-0 shutout loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars raised questions about what lies behind that first unit. With the Tampa Bay resting their starters, the game gave Todd Bowles and his staff another opportunity to evaluate the players competing for depth roles ahead of final roster decisions The results were not encouraging. The team managed just 87 net yards of offense while allowing five sacks. When asked after the game about his level of concern regarding the offensive line’s depth, Bowles made it clear that the starters remain a different conversation. However, he did not dismiss what he saw from the group against Jacksonville. “I like the first five and when everybody’s healthy,” Bowles said. “I’ll look at the tape. If you judge by tonight, yeah there’s concern. I’ll look at the totality of the tape and see where it came from.” The former player-turned-tactician’s answer reflects the distinction between Tampa Bay’s confidence in its projected starters and the uncertainty surrounding the players expected to step in if injuries strike during the regular season. The Buccaneers have Tristan Wirfs, Ben Bredeson, Graham Barton, Cody Mauch and Luke Goedeke anchoring a starting group that is expected to be among the team’s strengths when healthy. That health qualifier is an important one, especially after the Buccaneers dealt with significant injuries along the offensive line in 2025. Tampa Bay’s offense struggled as the unit was forced to shuffle personnel throughout the season, making reliable depth a priority heading into 2026. Friday’s performance did little to provide immediate reassurance. Rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, who had helped lead comeback victories in Tampa Bay’s first two preseason games , completed eight of 15 passes for 57 yards and was sacked three times before leaving the game in the third quarter. The Buccaneers also struggled to establish the run and failed to find any offensive rhythm throughout the night. Bowles had already voiced concerns about the line’s performance during the game, saying the Buccaneers needed more push up front and better protection for their quarterback. Still, the head coach stopped short of drawing a final conclusion from one preseason outing. With roster cuts approaching, the film from Jacksonville will factor into a broader evaluation of the offensive line room. William and Mary score 13 points in 55 seconds to beat Villanova
articles.summary: William & Mary erased a 10-point deficit in the final 55 seconds Friday night, scoring 13 unanswered points to stun No. 7 Villanova 35-32 in the season and Patriot League opener for both teams. The Tribe’s comeback began when junior kicker Max Lipinski converted a field goal to make it
articles._body: William & Mary erased a 10-point deficit in the final 55 seconds Friday night, scoring 13 unanswered points to stun No. 7 Villanova 35-32 in the season and Patriot League opener for both teams. The Tribe’s comeback began when junior kicker Max Lipinski converted a field goal to make it 32-25. The 45-yard kick put an end to the game-winning sequence, which started when William & Mary recovered the ensuing onside kick at the Wildcats 39-yard line. With only 22 seconds left, junior quarterback Winston Watkins connected with sophomore receiver Kai Austin for a 37-yard touchdown. The extra point tied the game at 32-32 and completed a 13-point burst. William and Mary was down double digits to No. 7 Villanova with under a minute left to play. Then this happened pic.twitter.com/8BPsrbzrLj — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) August 29, 2026 Villanova had another opportunity after the kickoff, but sixth-year quarterback Pat McQuaide threw his third interception of the night with less than 10 seconds remaining. Freshman defensive back Cade Ellis intercepted the pass and returned it 24 yards to the Wildcats’ 28-yard line, putting the Tribe within range for the winning kick. Lipinski then converted his fifth field goal of the game, hitting from 45 yards as time expired to complete the 35-32 comeback. McQuaide finished 17-for-30 for 270 yards and one touchdown, but his three interceptions proved costly. His availability had also been uncertain before kickoff because of an eligibility dispute. A preliminary injunction issued just hours before the game allowed him to play after the Patriot League had previously ruled him ineligible. Watkins completed the night with 254 passing yards, two touchdowns and one interception. He also rushed for 72 yards on 21 carries and scored another touchdown. Villanova had entered the matchup after winning nine consecutive season openers, a streak dating to Mark Ferrante’s arrival as head coach. The Wildcats were also an FCS semifinalist the previous season and entered the game ranked among the nation’s top teams. Both programs were making their Patriot League debuts after moving from the Coastal Athletic Association, but William & Mary left the opener with a 35-32 win after its 13-point explosion in the final minute. articles.summary: Joe Fagnano has made the most of his opportunities throughout the Baltimore Ravens’ preseason, and the rookie quarterback is crediting one of the NFL’s biggest stars for helping him along the way. Fagnano has spent his first NFL training camp working alongside Lamar Jackson, giving the rookie an
articles._body: Joe Fagnano has made the most of his opportunities throughout the Baltimore Ravens’ preseason , and the rookie quarterback is crediting one of the NFL’s biggest stars for helping him along the way. Fagnano has spent his first NFL training camp working alongside Lamar Jackson, giving the rookie an opportunity to learn from a two-time MVP on a daily basis. For a young quarterback still adjusting to the professional game, those interactions have become an important part of his development. Speaking to reporters , Fagnano opened up about what it has been like sharing a quarterback room and practice field with Jackson. “It’s been great. He’s a special player, special human being,” Fagnano said. “He’s kind of helped me out a ton. He’s been very supportive. After plays, he’s talking about what he sees. Even on his plays, he comes back and talks to me.” " @Lj_era8 has helped me out a ton." @joefagnano pic.twitter.com/SGJclYUwZx — Baltimore Ravens (@Ravens) August 29, 2026 Jackson’s willingness to share what he sees on the field has given Fagnano a valuable perspective that goes beyond simply watching one of the league’s best quarterbacks operate. The rookie has tried to absorb as much as possible from those conversations. “So it’s been great. It’s something that I’m very appreciative of and just trying to be a sponge and take it all in,” Fagnano added. The Ravens signed Fagnano as an undrafted rookie out of UConn , and he quickly emerged as one of the more intriguing players competing for a roster spot. He entered the preseason battling for the No. 3 quarterback role behind Jackson and veteran backup Tyler Huntley. Fagnano’s play has only strengthened his case. He impressed in Baltimore’s preseason opener against the Philadelphia Eagles, completing 22 of 28 passes for 224 yards and a touchdown. He followed that performance by going 15-of-20 for 123 yards and a touchdown against the Minnesota Vikings. The rookie continued his strong preseason in Baltimore’s finale, helping the Ravens complete an unbeaten exhibition slate with a dominant win over the Washington Commanders. Of course, preseason success does not guarantee a spot on the final roster . But Fagnano has put himself firmly in the conversation with his performances and has had a rare resource available throughout the process. For now, whether the rookie earns a place on Baltimore’s active roster or continues his development elsewhere within the organization, the lessons he has picked up from the Ravens’ franchise quarterback could prove valuable as his NFL career begins. articles._body: All the talk around the state of Florida and even on a national level was surrounding the visiting Miami Carol City Chiefs when they traveled from Dade County to take on Georgia’s No. 7th ranked team, the Lee County Trojans. By the end of the game, the Trojans made sure the only talk was about them and not their visitors. [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] The Trojans shut out the Chiefs in the second half and pulled off a 23-20 victory on Friday night at Trojan Field in Leesburg, Georgia. Miami Carol City, which entered the game ranked nationally by multiple outlets, dropped their first contest of the season after coming off a 38-3 win over Daytona Beach (Fla.) Mainland team the week before. It was a fast start for the Chiefs on offense as Miami four-star wide receiver commitment Nick Lennear got the scoring going for Carol City when he hauled in a 20-yard strike from 2029 quarterback Malik Leonard to give themselves a 7-0 lead. Lee County (2-0) answered Carol City’s touchdown with a defensive one of their own when defensive back Kevin Streeter picked off Leonard and returned it back to pay dirt, giving the Trojans a 8-7 lead. The Chiefs re-took the lead when 2027 4-star athlete Zakari Johnson scored on a seven-yard run to go back up 13-8. Lennear would score one more time right before intermission, giving Carol City a commanding 20-8 lead. Once the second half began, the wheels slowly started to come off for the Chiefs. Former Colquitt County quarterback Cohen Lawson connected on a 29-yard scoring pass to Destin Bell , cutting the lead down to 20-15 for Carol City. The proverbial dagger by the Trojans offensively was 2027 running back Dominique Ball scoring on a touchdown run in the fourth quarter to put Lee County ahead 23-20. That’s when the Trojans dialed up the pressure on Carol City’s offense as they forced the Chiefs into a 4th and 31 situation with around three minutes remaining, forcing a turnover on downs and running out the clock for the win. Tennis legend Roger Federer makes unreal play in Newport grass court doubles action
articles.summary: Roger Federer reminded everyone in Newport that the magic never really left. On Friday, a day before his induction into the International Tennis Hall of Fame, the 20-time Grand Slam champion returned to the grass for a doubles exhibition and delivered a highlight-reel moment that sent the crowd i
articles._body: Roger Federer reminded everyone in Newport that the magic never really left . On Friday, a day before his induction into the International Tennis Hall of Fame, the 20-time Grand Slam champion returned to the grass for a doubles exhibition and delivered a highlight-reel moment that sent the crowd into a frenzy. Video of the play quickly spread online, a flash of the flair that made him must-see television for two decades. Federer took part in the Hall of Fame Celebrity Pro Classic on the iconic grass courts at the International Tennis Hall of Fame, his first competitive swing on the surface since retiring in 2022 . The setting could not have been more fitting. Federer built much of his legend on grass, winning a record eight Wimbledon titles, and the Newport lawns gave him a stage to show that his touch has not faded. The exhibition doubled as a reunion of tennis royalty . Federer was joined by fellow Hall of Famers including John McEnroe, Stefan Edberg, Lleyton Hewitt, Bob and Mike Bryan, Martina Navratilova, Arantxa Sanchez Vicario, and Gabriela Sabatini. Comedian and former pro Michael Kosta and television personality Joey Graziadei rounded out the field, with Olympic skiing champion Lindsey Vonn taking a turn in the umpire’s chair. The weekend marks the crowning honor of Federer’s career. He enters the Hall of Fame as a class of one, the only player elected in 2026, alongside broadcaster Mary Carillo in the contributor category. The official ceremony takes place Saturday on the historic grounds in Newport. Federer has not hidden how much the moment means. In an interview that aired this week, he called the induction his “final hurrah,” placing it near the top of a career that also featured 103 titles and a record 237 consecutive weeks at world No. 1. For fans who spent two decades marveling at his shot-making, the exhibition offered one more glimpse of the artistry that defined him. Federer may be years removed from the tour , but on a sunlit Newport grass court, he looked every bit the player who made the impossible seem routine, one more time before he took his place among the immortals. articles._body: The Colorado Avalanche made hockey history on Friday when they re-signed defenseman Cale Makar. Makar signed a historic $163 million contract with Colorado, making him the highest-paid player in NHL history. He is also the first player in NHL history to earn a salary of $20 million in a season. It’s a landmark deal for Makar and the Avalanche this summer. Colorado keeps its franchise defenseman around for eight years, which could make him an Avalanche for life. They also paid a hefty price to do so, which could impact roster building down the line. On Friday, Makar sent a message to Colorado fans after putting pen to paper. “To the Avalanche fans, thank you for your continued support and for welcoming us to Colorado years ago. Colorado has truly become a second home to us, and we are so grateful to be here. I look forward to getting back on the ice with my teammates and continuing to work toward our goal of bringing the Stanley Cup back to the Mile High City,” the Avalanche superstar said, via NHL.com Makar is one of the best defensemen in the NHL at this time. He has scored 90+ points twice in his career and has eclipsed the 75-point mark on four occasions. The Avalanche star has won the Norris Trophy as the best defenseman in the league on two occasions. The Avalanche are making a massive investment in their star defenseman. But the reward could certainly outweigh the risk if the team continues to have success on the ice. articles.title: Promising Eagles’ safety in a boot after being carted off field vs. Bengals
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles safety Andre’ Sam suffered a leg injury during the third quarter of Friday night’s preseason finale against the Cincinnati Bengals at Lincoln Financial Field. Sam was unable to put pressure on the leg and was taken off the field by cart. He gave the crowd a thumbs-
articles._body: Philadelphia Eagles safety Andre’ Sam suffered a leg injury during the third quarter of Friday night’s preseason finale against the Cincinnati Bengals at Lincoln Financial Field. Sam was unable to put pressure on the leg and was taken off the field by cart . He gave the crowd a thumbs-up while being taken into the locker room. The injury came during a tackle on Bengals running back Kentrel Bullock, who gained six yards on a run up the middle to the Cincinnati 26-yard line. The setback ended what had been Sam’s most productive performance of the preseason. Sam made several impact plays against the Bengals, forcing one fumble and recovering two others. One recovery came late in the second quarter after rookie linebacker Deontae Lawson stripped running back Gary Brightwell. Sam then recovered Tahj Brooks’ fumble on the opening kickoff of the second half at Cincinnati’s 37-yard line. He also recorded seven tackles through Philadelphia’s first two preseason games. Those plays were particularly meaningful because Sam entered the finale competing for one of the final places on the Eagles’ 53-man roster . His familiarity with Vic Fangio’s defense and contributions on special teams had given him a chance to compete for a backup safety position. Philadelphia had also recently released veteran safety JT Gray, creating another opportunity in the competition. The Eagles signed Sam as an undrafted free agent out of LSU in 2024. The 27-year-old has spent most of his first two NFL seasons on Philadelphia’s practice squad, while receiving limited opportunities during the regular season. He had also performed well during training camp, including the Eagles’ joint practices against the New England Patriots. Sam’s successful summer had helped him remain in the roster conversation despite being considered a long shot . His performance against the Bengals strengthened that case before the injury interrupted his night. Philadelphia will now need to determine Sam’s medical status through further testing. Depending on the severity, his options could include returning to the Eagles’ practice squad or being placed on injured reserve if the injury proves season-ending. articles.title: Unrivaled coach reveals how Dream’s Angel Reese has improved her offensive game
articles.summary: Angel Reese remains as divisive of a player as ever, but at just 24 years of age, there’s no denying that she has plenty of room to grow still as an individual and as a basketball player. Reese, in fact, has been making plenty of strides on offense for the Atlanta Dream amid a strong [̷
articles._body: Angel Reese remains as divisive of a player as ever, but at just 24 years of age, there’s no denying that she has plenty of room to grow still as an individual and as a basketball player. Reese, in fact, has been making plenty of strides on offense for the Atlanta Dream amid a strong season in which they’ve already booked a place in the playoffs. Reese is averaging a career-best 16.1 points per game this season in her first campaign in Atlanta, and she’s become a more aggressive force on the offensive end. And her former coach with the Chicago Sky, Teresa Weatherspoon, lauded her for the improvements she’s made as a scorer. “She’s a coachable young lady. She wants to be great. She understands those little things that are so important. She’s a detailed athlete, knowing what she must do for her team to be successful. The great thing is, now, she’s finally understanding where that pass may go because the game is slowing down for her,” Weatherspoon said on NBA TV. “She’s trusting her work.” @StephanieReady and Teresa Weatherspoon highlight the offensive strides Angel Reese has made this season. pic.twitter.com/EFRi6Nj4PK — NBA TV (@NBATV) August 29, 2026 Reese, of course, has plenty of improvements left to make in her game, for as much as some pundits have noticed the strides she’s made on that end of the floor. Her increase in output has come mostly from an increase in attempts from the field, which has then led to worse scoring efficiency. After going just 5-14 from the field and 6-8 from the foul line in a 101-83 loss for the Dream to the Portland Fire on Friday, Reese’s true shooting went down to 51.1 — which is around two points lower than her tally last year. Being an 18% shooter from deep for her career means that Reese may be best served excising that shot from her game. At the end of the day, the Dream forward’s main strength lies in her elite rebounding, and her defense isn’t too shabby either. More offensive contributions could be good, but not at the expense of scoring efficiency and all the other little things she does on the court. articles._body: The competition for the New York Giants’ placekicker job has officially come to an end. Head coach John Harbaugh confirmed following the preseason finale that rookie kicker Dominic Zvada has won the starting role over returning veteran Ben Sauls. Zvada put an impressive exclamation point on the battle during Friday night’s 23-6 victory over the rival New York Jets at MetLife Stadium. Given full handling of the kicking duties for the night, the former Michigan standout delivered a flawless performance. He went a perfect 3-for-3 on field goal attempts, connecting from 23, 46, and a booming 53 yards out, while also converting both of his extra point tries. The head-to-head battle had been tight throughout training camp, but Zvada’s consistent leg strength and poise during live action ultimately tipped the scales in his favor. Ben Sauls, who spent time on the roster previously and made all eight of his field goal attempts in 2025, put up a strong fight, but Zvada’s high ceiling and big-time distance capabilities proved too enticing for the coaching staff to pass up. For Harbaugh, who built his career on special teams coaching before launching his storied head coaching tenure, finding stability at the kicker position was a top priority entering the 2026 season. Zvada’s command during the exhibition phase made the decision clear as final cuts approach. With the preseason officially wrapped up, the Giants move into Week 1 with absolute clarity on their special teams unit. Zvada gets the nod to handle the high-pressure scoring duties, bringing a powerful leg and newfound momentum into his inaugural professional campaign. articles.title: Texans’ most agonizing roster decision looming on 2026 cutdown day
articles.summary: Cutdown day rarely arrives with a clean depth chart, but the Houston Texans have been handed an especially difficult puzzle at wide receiver. That creates a particularly uncomfortable problem for general manager Nick Caserio and head coach DeMeco Ryans. There may simply not be enough roster spots
articles._body: Cutdown day rarely arrives with a clean depth chart, but the Houston Texans have been handed an especially difficult puzzle at wide receiver. That creates a particularly uncomfortable problem for general manager Nick Caserio and head coach DeMeco Ryans. There may simply not be enough roster spots for every receiver who has earned consideration. With Nico Collins anchoring the group and a combination of many others competing for complementary roles, Houston must decide how much proven depth it can afford to carry. The answer could leave one deserving player on the outside when the 53-man roster becomes official . Bigger priorities Thomas Shea-Imagn Images While the Texans dropped all three preseason contests, the scoreboards were secondary to evaluating depth. However, the summer was abruptly complicated by brutal injury setbacks, most notably losing dynamic wideout Jayden Higgins to a torn ACL . That was alongside defensive end Dylan Horton’s torn Achilles. Caserio reacted with trademark aggression. He executed a bold trade to acquire Kayshon Boutte from New England while also signing experienced veterans Zay Jones and Sterling Shepard. Those moves have completely transformed the wide receiver room. Now though, it presents the coaching staff with its most agonizing cutdown dilemma. Wide receiver logjam The single most agonizing roster decision facing Ryans and Caserio on cutdown day centers directly on how to configure the final spots in the wide receiver room. Should they part ways with trusted contributor Xavier Hutchinson, or sacrifice newly acquired veteran insurance in Jones and Shepard? Collins remains the obvious centerpiece. Dell brings explosive ability when healthy. Noel provides route-running precision and return-game versatility. The acquisition of Boutte adds another intriguing perimeter option. The Texans’ own roster currently lists Hutchinson, Boutte, Jones, and Shepard among the active receivers. It underscores just how dramatically the room has changed in a short period. Hutchinson has spent the early portion of his career establishing himself as a physical, dependable target. He understands the offense and knows what Stroud expects from his supporting cast. Jones and Shepard offer something different. Their value is rooted in experience. Between them, they bring hundreds of NFL games. Jones has accumulated more than 3,000 career receiving yards, while Shepard entered Houston after a 2025 season in which he caught 39 passes for 371 yards. Weighing special teams utility This is where the decision becomes genuinely painful. Keeping Hutchinson gives Houston a player who can contribute in multiple phases. That familiarity and reliability matter. The Texans know precisely what they are getting from him. However, the argument for Jones and Shepard is equally compelling. The entire point of veteran depth is to prevent one injury from becoming a systemic problem. Higgins is already gone for the season. Dell’s availability has been an ongoing consideration during the summer. Houston therefore cannot afford to assume its preferred receiving combination will remain intact for 17 games. A veteran who can immediately step into a regular-season game plan is valuable precisely because there is no developmental runway when an injury strikes. That creates a fascinating contradiction. Hutchinson may offer greater roster continuity and special-teams utility. Meanwhile, the veterans provide Houston with an insurance policy. Waiver wire If Houston exposes Hutchinson to waivers, another team could view him as worth pursuing. The same principle applies to younger receivers who have flashed during camp. Once a player is released, Houston loses control of where his development continues. That is particularly important because the Texans have already demonstrated how aggressively Caserio is willing to reshape the room. The Boutte trade and the additions of Jones and Shepard were direct responses to Higgins’ injury. The final roster, therefore, is unlikely to be determined solely by who caught the most passes in August. Special teams, versatility, health, experience, and projected regular-season usage will all carry significant weight. Choose insurance policy Ultimately, the Texans’ most agonizing cutdown decision is a philosophical one. Do they reward a trusted contributor, or do they prioritize veteran insurance? There is a strong argument for both approaches. Keeping Hutchinson preserves continuity and physicality. Keeping Jones and Shepard protects Houston against the unpredictability of a long NFL season. Carrying all of them, meanwhile, could force the Texans to sacrifice valuable depth somewhere else on the roster. Caserio and Ryans have spent the summer trying to build a roster capable of competing deep into January. The unfortunate consequence of that ambition is that some NFL-caliber players will inevitably become casualties of the numbers. For Houston, the receiver room is where that reality has become impossible to ignore. Higgins’ injury created the problem. Caserio’s aggressive response may have made the final decision even harder. As things stand, though, the wiser but still painful choice is to keep Jones and Shepard. The post Texans’ most agonizing roster decision looming on 2026 cutdown day appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.summary: Former Minnesota Golden Gophers goalie Nathan Airey's dreams of playing in the NHL are not over.
articles._body: Former Minnesota Golden Gophers goalie Nathan Airey’s dreams of playing in the NHL are not over. The San Jose Sharks announced the former Gopher Friday as the program’s emergency backup goaltender. Airey spent each of the last three seasons with the Gophers appearing in 35 games and collecting a 16-11-3 record, a 2.86 goals against average, and a .893 save percentage. Last season, Airey was 3-7-1 in 13 games with a 3.39 GAA and a .888 save percentage. In 2024, the Cochrane, Alberta native had a career season with a 12-3-2 record and a 2.47 GAA while posting a save percentage of .900. This season is the first year in the NHL that teams will be required to employ their own emergency replacement goalie. The emergency replacement goalies may not have appeared in an NHL game under contract, appeared in a professional hockey game in the last three seasons or appeared in more than 80 professional games at any point. Some emergency replacement goalies will have day-to-day roles within the organization as well. For example, the Minnesota Wild’s emergency goalie Peter Thome is also a hockey operations analyst for the organization.

After opening the season as No. 3 in Rivals High School Football Composite Rankings, the Braves fell all the way to No. 11 following their loss to Bishop Gorman (Nev.) After being shut out in the first half, the Braves didn’t go away, with three-star quarterback Koa Malau’ulu throwing for two scores in the third quarter. However, ultimately, it would serve as too much of a deficit to overcome, as the Gaels cruised to a ten-point win. READ MORE: QB intel: Koa Malau’ulu has a handful of favorites but one connection cannot be ignored After falling in such a disappointing season-opener, the Braves looked much more up to speed in interstate action on Friday Night, taking on Roman Catholic (Pa.). The Pennsylvania side was opening their season tonight, coming off a 5A state championship and a 12-3 record in 2025. With junior quarterback Jahmil Hawkins stepping up as starter for the first time, after serving as backup last year, the Braves made life hell for the junior signal caller in the first half. Across the first quarter, Hawkins was sacked four times, with the Braves finishing the first half with five sacks. Down 31 points to end the half, Hawkins finally found his footing to open the second half, throwing for his first passing touchdown of the year. After St. John Bosco put up 31 unanswered points, Roman Catholic finally found a response with a 13-yard pass to Kaylin Bass. Despite his first-half struggles, Hawkins finished the night with three passing touchdowns. After that, St. John Bosco struggled to put anything together in the second half, taking multiple starters out of the game. Hawkins found his second passing touchdown of the night to make it a 3-score game, with a two-yard pass to Jayden Alford . However, the Braves had already done enough to seal the win. With Malau’ulu looking to bounce back after week one, the starting QB didn’t have much work to do in the first half. Putting up 86 yards passing with two touchdowns, it was three-star senior running back Maliq Allen who led the way for St. John Bosco on the ground. Across the first half, the three-star back, who ranks just within the top 100 at his position according to Rivals Industry Rankings , did absolutely everything. Hauling in a receiving touchdown, the senior finished the half with three touchdowns. With the Braves taking a 45-25 victory, the three-star back ran in the Braves’ final score of the game, finishing the night with three rushing scores and one receiving. After getting back to winning ways in dominant fashion tonight, St. John Bosco is back in California action next week. Falling to Orange Lutheran (Calif.) in the CIF Southern Section quarterfinals last year, the Braves will be looking to make a deeper run in 2026, in action against the No. 25-ranked Pittsburg (Calif.)

articles.title: Timberwolves acquire Cody Williams from Jazz after signing Jonathan Kuminga
articles.summary: The Minnesota Timberwolves have pulled off a trade to bolster the roster after signing Jonathan Kuminga this offseason. Minnesota has been significantly retooling the roster this summer. They traded away Julius Randle and Naz Reid while landing the likes of LaMelo Ball and Kuminga, taking a uniqu
articles._body: The Minnesota Timberwolves have pulled off a trade to bolster the roster after signing Jonathan Kuminga this offseason. Minnesota has been significantly retooling the roster this summer. They traded away Julius Randle and Naz Reid while landing the likes of LaMelo Ball and Kuminga, taking a unique direction in the Anthony Edwards era. Balancing out the starting five with Kuminga taking the power forward spot, Minnesota has focus on revamping bench depth. They made their latest move after landing Cody Williams and John Konchar from the Utah Jazz. In exchange, they sent out Josh Green and cash to Utah, per insider Shams Charania. “The Minnesota Timberwolves are trading Josh Green and cash to the Utah Jazz for Cody Williams and John Konchar, sources tell ESPN,” Charania wrote . “The Timberwolves are expected to keep Cody Williams, the No. 10 pick in 2024, and waive-and-stretch John Konchar, sources said. They found a home for Josh Green on a Jazz team that wanted an additional 3-and-D wing; moving his $14.7 million deal gives Minnesota the salary space to sign Jonathan Kuminga using the taxpayer midlevel exception.” “This is a terrific trade for the Timberwolves to add John Konchar as a utility guy off the bench and take a chance on Cody Williams deep on their bench. This move also opens up the cap flexibility Minnesota needs to officially sign Jonathan Kuminga,” NBA insider Brett Siegel mentioned . The Jazz are acquiring Josh Green and cash from the Timberwolves in exchange for Cody Williams and John Konchar, per @ShamsCharania . pic.twitter.com/l7SfwdykAL — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 29, 2026 What lies ahead for Timberwolves after latest move The Timberwolves will have plenty of optimism about their roster as Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball possess great potential as a dynamic duo next season. Minnesota finished with a 49-33 record last season, securing the sixth seed in the Western Conference standings. They finished above the Portland Trail Blazers and the Phoenix Suns while trailing the Houston Rockets and the Los Angeles Lakers. The Timberwolves made noise in the playoffs, stunning the Denver Nuggets in six games despite suffering significant injuries. However, their postseason journey ended after losing to the San Antonio Spurs in six games. Broncos’ Marvin Mims Jr. exits Vikings clash with a foot injury
articles.summary: Denver Broncos wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr. left the team’s preseason finale against the Minnesota Vikings on Friday night after suffering a right foot injury during the opening series. Mims was one of the few Denver regulars in uniform, but his night ended after only six plays from scrimm
articles._body: Denver Broncos wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr. left the team’s preseason finale against the Minnesota Vikings on Friday night after suffering a right foot injury during the opening series. Mims was one of the few Denver regulars in uniform, but his night ended after only six plays from scrimmage. The injury occurred on a third-down play when Mims went up for an overthrown pass from quarterback Jarrett Stidham. Mims and Vikings safety Jacob Thomas collided out of bounds as the ball went past the wide receiver. He immediately grabbed his right foot after hitting the ground and rolled over before getting back up. Mims initially tried to jog toward the sideline but was visibly limping. Team medical personnel accompanied him, and he threw his helmet down in frustration before sitting near the Broncos’ bench. He was then examined inside the team’s blue medical tent and subsequently headed to the locker room. Denver officially listed him as questionable to return . The fourth-year wide receiver had already missed the Broncos’ first two preseason contests after suffering a soft-tissue injury during training camp . He had also missed several practices because of a lower-body issue and entered Friday without recording a catch or return during the preseason. Mims was selected by Denver in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft and has since become a standout return specialist. He earned Pro Bowl recognition in each of his first two seasons and was named a first-team All-Pro as a returner in 2024. He also became only the second player in Broncos history, alongside Von Miller, to earn Pro Bowl and All-Pro honors during his first two seasons. Last season, Mims ranked second in the NFL with a 15.6-yard average on punt returns and found the end zone on a punt return during Denver’s Week 14 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. His offensive production became especially important during last season’s playoff run. Injuries to Troy Franklin and Pat Bryant created additional opportunities, and Mims responded with a crucial touchdown during the Broncos’ 33-30 overtime divisional-round victory over the Buffalo Bills. He also made crucial plays against the New England Patriots in the AFC Championship Game and finished the postseason as Denver’s leading receiver. Mims is entering the final year of his rookie contract, with no extension completed yet. The extent of his latest foot injury could therefore become another factor in his situation. The Broncos also have undrafted return options in Kolbe Katsis, Cameron Ross and Sean Fresch Jr. should Mims miss time. articles.title: Pittsburgh Central Catholic Rushes for Five Touchdowns in Win Over Bergen Catholic
articles.summary: The KDKA Kickoff Classic at the Wolvarena has annually marked the start of the WPIAL football season over the last handful of years, but the real ball starts in Pennsylvania whenever Pittsburgh Central Catholic takes the field for the first time. The Vikings have welcomed in prestigious programs fro
articles._body: The KDKA Kickoff Classic at the Wolvarena has annually marked the start of the WPIAL football season over the last handful of years, but the real ball starts in Pennsylvania whenever Pittsburgh Central Catholic takes the field for the first time. The Vikings have welcomed in prestigious programs from not only around the WPIAL, but all over the country, to be their annual first test of the season. This season was no different as the Vikings capped off the first night of the WPIAL season with a star-studded matchup against New Jersey powerhouse Bergen Catholic. Pittsburgh Central Catholic is always loaded on both sides of the ball. This year’s team is led by a pair of four-star offensive line recruits, Jimmy Kalis (Ohio State) and James Halter (Notre Dame), along with a plethora of other Division-I talent including quarterback Owen Herrick , running back Chrys Black Jr. and linebacker Roman Thompson . While the Vikings usually outshine other WPIAL teams in terms of star power, Bergen Catholic brought its own shiny pieces with them as they were led by four-star quarterback Trey Tagliaferri (Oklahoma) and a pair of three-star wide receivers in Austin Busso (South Florida) and Bryan Porter .  In total, over 300 Division-I offers were on the field for Friday night’s nightcap between the two storied programs. Bergen Catholic trusted its high-flying offense and took the ball first, and proved why just two plays into the game as Tagliaferri threw a strike to a crossing Busso in the middle of the Central Catholic defense. Busso hauled in the pass and took it 84 yards for a Crusaders touchdown. Pittsburgh Central Catholic, who is not easily rattled, went right to work on offense in response. After a couple of big plays and defensive penalties helped the Vikings move down the field, a 29-yard field goal got them onto the scoreboard. Tagliaferri looked to put the Crusaders up by multiple scores on the ensuing drive after picking apart the Vikings’ secondary en route to the redzone, but the first of two missed field goals ended the drive with the score still at 7-3. Pittsburgh Central Catholic capitalized on the mistake and cashed in on a 3-yard touchdown run by Thompson to take the lead, which the Vikings never surrendered after that point despite some second-half drama. 1Q | 1:34 Pittsburgh Central Catholic capitalizes on the missed FG and drives down the field to take the lead on Roman Thompson’s 3-yard touchdown. Pittsburgh Central Catholic leads 10-7. @PghSportsNow pic.twitter.com/AAX6w1M5vL — Adam Borst (@AdamBorstPGH) August 29, 2026 By the end of the first half, the Vikings scored 24-unanswered points, which included a 14-yard touchdown throw from Herrick to Connor Melnik and a short scrambling touchdown from the highly-touted quarterback prospect, to lead the Crusaders by the score of 24-7. Pittsburgh Central Catholic quickly extended its lead out to 31-7 early in the third quarter after the first of three second-half touchdowns from running back Chrys Black Jr., but Bergen Catholic threw one last punch as it rattled off 16-straight points to bring the game back to one score. 3Q | 9:28 Pittsburgh Central Catholic rewards Chrys Black after a long punt return with a 7-yard rushing touchdown. This one is getting out of hand as PCC leads 31-7. @PghSportsNow pic.twitter.com/iJIB4uDTIt — Adam Borst (@AdamBorstPGH) August 29, 2026 While the back-to-back touchdowns pumped some life back into the Crusaders’ sideline, Black was determined to end the game on his terms. A series after a crippling fumble, Black re-extended his team’s lead with his second touchdown, a 31-yard burst, just before the end of the third quarter. Black scored again midway through the fourth which officially put the game out of reach for good. He finished the game with 16 carries for 153 yards and three touchdowns. He added two catches for 37 yards and a pair of long punt returns. Despite a late touchdown pass from Tagliaferri and the Crusaders, the Class-6A favorite Vikings dominated the trenches, scoring five of their six touchdowns on the ground, en route to a marquee victory over one of the top programs from New Jersey to start the 2026 WPIAL football season. Pittsburgh Central Catholic will return to the Wolvarena next weekend for a non-conference matchup against a Woodland Hills team that lost much of its production from a season ago.

Tagovailoa prepares for the seventh season of his NFL career, his first with the Falcons. He spent the first six years with the Miami Dolphins before the team cut him in
articles._body: Tua Tagovailoa looks to make a statement in Kevin Stefanski’s offense going into the Atlanta Falcons’ 2026 season . Tagovailoa prepares for the seventh season of his NFL career, his first with the Falcons. He spent the first six years with the Miami Dolphins before the team cut him in the offseason. Eventually, he signed a one-year, $1.215 million contract with Atlanta. Tagovailoa took part in the Falcons’ preseason finale against the Dolphins. He completed seven out of eight passes for 95 yards, splitting reps with Cooper Rush and Jack Strand. Stefanski, preparing for his first year as the Falcons’ coach, reflected on Tagovailoa’s performance after the game. “I thought Tua did a nice job operating, obviously moving the football for a couple drives. Plenty to clean up. An avoidable center-to-quarterback exchange. We have to clean that up. And we will. I thought by and large, [he] operated,” Stefanski said, per reporter Marc Raimondi. How Tua Tagovailoa, Falcons played against Dolphins Tua Tagovailoa has going down to the wire with Michael Penix Jr. for the Falcons’ starting job. With the preseason over, it is up to Kevin Stefanski to make the important decision. The Falcons ended the preseason with a 2-1 record, coming out of the finale with a 17-12 win over the Dolphins. Atlanta did all of its damage in the first half, scoring all 17 points as they prevented Miami from getting a touchdown at any point of the contest. Brian Robinson Jr. led the rushing attack with five carries for 17 yards and a touchdown. Meanwhile, Kyle Pitts Sr. caught three passes for 57 yards and Jack Velling made four receptions for 30 yards and a touchdown. They will seek to improve on their 8-9 record from the previous two seasons. They also intend to make the playoffs after an eight-year absence and end their nine-year NFC South title drought. The Falcons’ regular season commences on the road against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sept. 13 at 1 p.m. ET. Ravens HC Jesse Minter completes perfect preseason in statistically dominant fashion
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens closed the 2026 preseason with another convincing performance, defeating the Washington Commanders 41-3 Friday night at M&T Bank Stadium. The win completed a 3-0 preseason for first-year head coach Jesse Minter, with Baltimore outscoring its three opponents 78-13. The Rav
articles._body: The Baltimore Ravens closed the 2026 preseason with another convincing performance, defeating the Washington Commanders 41-3 Friday night at M&T Bank Stadium. The win completed a 3-0 preseason for first-year head coach Jesse Minter, with Baltimore outscoring its three opponents 78-13 . The Ravens opened the preseason by beating the Philadelphia Eagles 24-7 before earning a 13-3 road victory over the Minnesota Vikings. Baltimore then produced its largest offensive output of the exhibition schedule against Washington, while its defense allowed only one touchdown throughout the entire preseason. Friday’s numbers painted a clear picture of the gulf between the Ravens and Commanders. Baltimore generated 456 total yards compared with Washington’s 177, collected 26 first downs to seven and controlled possession for 33:45. The Commanders converted only one of 12 third-down opportunities and never reached the red zone. The Ravens also maintained their defensive dominance despite resting several players, including rookies Vega Ioane and Ja’Kobi Lane. Baltimore held Washington without a touchdown, recorded three sacks, six quarterback hits and two pass deflections, while also forcing multiple fumbles and recovering one. Undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano again led the Ravens’ quarterbacks in passing, throwing for 162 yards and a touchdown. Baltimore’s quarterbacks combined for 261 passing yards, compared with 102 for Washington. Defensively, the Ravens were outstanding against the Vikings as well, finishing with five sacks and forcing two turnovers. Those outings gave Minter a statistically impressive start, as his first preseason concluded with Baltimore securing the 13th perfect exhibition record in franchise history over 31 seasons. The Ravens must now reduce their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. on Aug. 30. Several defensive roster decisions remain, while the starting center position is still unsettled. Baltimore opens the regular season against the Indianapolis Colts on Sept. 13. articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys suffered a major blow to their defensive depth during Friday’s preseason finale. Outside linebacker Marist Liufau exited early after sustaining an injury, which offensive coordinator Brian Schottenheimer later confirmed as a broken left forearm. The injury occurred in the first
articles._body: The Dallas Cowboys suffered a major blow to their defensive depth during Friday’s preseason finale. Outside linebacker Marist Liufau exited early after sustaining an injury, which offensive coordinator Brian Schottenheimer later confirmed as a broken left forearm. The injury occurred in the first half of Dallas’ 27-24 loss against the New Orleans Saints at AT&T Stadium. Liufau, selected in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of Notre Dame, was initially evaluated on the sideline for a wrist issue before being ruled out for the remainder of the contest. While the loss itself does not impact the regular-season standings, losing a key linebacker right before Week 1 creates a serious headache for defensive coordinator Mike Zimmer. Liufau had been enjoying a promising preseason, carving out a role as a dependable rotation linebacker and core special teams contributor. He had posted steady snaps and pressure metrics through training camp, making him a projected piece of the defensive scheme. Now, the Dallas Cowboys must adjust their roster decisions ahead of the official 53-man roster cutdowns. As for the game itself, the Cowboys fell just short despite late-game heroics . Quarterback Sam Howell led a fourth-quarter rally, completing 10 of 11 passes for 141 yards and two touchdowns, including a 21-yard strike to Brevyn Spann-Ford. Wide receiver Jordan Hudson shone as a top target, logging three catches for 88 yards and a touchdown. However, the New Orleans Saints edged ahead late with a 53-yard field goal by Daniel Carlson to seal the 27-24 victory. With the preseason officially wrapped up , the Dallas Cowboys now face tough decisions on how to manage their linebacker room and special teams units while awaiting further updates on Marist Liufau’s recovery timeline. articles._body: After opening its 2026 season with a tough loss, Lipscomb Academy (Tenn.) got back on the horse and picked up a nice 16-6 road victory over Ravenwood on Friday night. It’s the first win of the year for returning Mustangs head coach Trent Dilfer . The former Super Bowl-winning quarterback opted to return to the high school ranks after his tumultuous stint as the head coach at UAB . Lipscomb brought Dilfer back in January. He had a great first stint in charge, going 44-10 with three straight conference titles from 2020-22. Lipscomb carried a 10-0 lead into halftime at Ravenwood. Kicker Tyson Robbins nailed three field goals from 39, 42 and 42 yards in the win. The Mustangs didn’t allow a score until the fourth quarter and held strong to improve to 1-1 on the season. They lost 27-24 at McCallie to open the campaign last week. The Mustangs brought in multiple notable transfers heading into this season, including a pair of quarterbacks. Dilfer also brought former UAB linebackers coach Matthew Wright in to be the new defensive coordinator. After Dilfer left Lipscomb Academy for UAB, the Mustangs saw their winning ways begin to go downhill as they have gone 12-20 from 2023-25, finishing below the .500 mark each season. In each of Dilfer’s four seasons leading the Mustangs, the team never fell below the .500 mark, with the former NFL’er’s worst season being his first in 2019 when the team went 7-6. The Mustangs entered this week as the No. 15 team in Tennessee, according to the Rivals Composite Rankings . They now gear up for their home-opener and another big matchup vs. Knoxville Catholic next week on Sept. 4. More about Lipscomb Academy Lipscomb Academy, located in Nashville, Tennessee, is a distinguished private school known for its strong academics, competitive athletics, and vibrant extracurricular programs. Offering a range of AP and honors courses, the school prepares students for higher education and future careers. Lipscomb Academy’s athletic teams are successful, often achieving regional and state recognition. Emphasizing leadership, community involvement, and personal growth, the school ensures students are well-rounded and prepared for future challenges. articles._body: The Miami Dolphins have completed their preseason slate of games. As a result, they have completed all of their pre-Week 1 tune-ups. The only thing remaining is for head coach Jeff Hafley to make his final roster decisions . Miami is likely to run a rather young roster this season. The Dolphins are widely not expected to compete in the AFC East this year. And it seems as if Hafley could be embracing a youth movement. At the same time, the first-year head coach knows that there is more to measuring success than simply the results of the game. “Let me say this. Me and I want to win everything we do. But success is not just defined by winning. Winning for sure, right? That’s why we play the game. I think every competitor wants to win in everything that we do… At the same time, we need to make sure that this foundation and process is built the right way,” the Dolphins head coach said, via C. Isaiah Smalls II of The Miami Herald. The Dolphins made some big moves in the offseason. Miami cut ties with former fifth-overall pick Tua Tagovailoa this offseason after a dismal 2025 season. In his place is Malik Willis, who played with the Green Bay Packers last season when Hafley was their defensive coordinator. Miami is preparing for a season that could be both challenging and rewarding. Seeing this young roster blossom into something special may make some of the tough losses worth it. Five things to look for going into the 2026 Stanford Women’s Volleyball season
articles.summary: Here are five things to look for as No. 5 Stanford women's volleyball begins their 2026 season.
articles._body: Credit: GoStanford.com With the season getting underway, below are five things to look for going into the 2026 Stanford Women’s Volleyball season. The Cardinal are ranked No. 5 in the nation at the start of the season. Ok, let’s get after it! READ: Breaking down the 2026 Stanford Women’s Volleyball schedule #1. How good will Logan Parks be at setter? Logan Parks has big shoes to fill in being the heir apparent to Kami Miner , who graduated after the 2024 season. Miner was an elite setter during her time on The Farm and was a big reason for all the success that they had. Parks averaged 10.11 assists per set last season, so she had a strong freshman season. Now, it’s just about taking her game up a notch and settling in even more. If Stanford wants to contend for a national championship, it’s going to have to start with Parks at setter emerging into one of the best in the nation. #2. Who will lead in kills per set? This is really a more technical way of asking who will be the new go-to player for the team. Last year, Eila Rubin filled that role, averaging a team-high 3.33 kills per set while hitting .284 on a team-high 957 total attacks. Rubin was the go-to player last year. When they really needed a kill, she was the one who more often than not delivered the goods. It’ll be interesting to see who emerges to fill that role. Senior Jordyn Harvey , redshirt juniors/seniors Julia Blyashov & Ipar Kurt , and junior Lizzy Andrew are the ones who are the frontrunners to take on that role. Sophomore Erika Sayer also a possibility. Perhaps it won’t be one person that takes it on, but instead it will be a situation where they all collectively step up. Regardless, how those shoes get filled will be very interesting to see. #3. How big of an impact with Spencer Etzler make at libero? Another key piece for Stanford this season is going to be sophomore libero Spencer Etzler . Great Stanford teams have always had great liberos like Elena Oglivie and Morgan Hentz . If Etzler can emerge into the next great Stanford libero, that would be massive. #4. What will the identity of this team be? Stanford has a lot of different weapons and ways to beat teams. They got the pins on the outside, they have the middle blockers, and they hopefully have the defense. It’ll be interesting to see if this becomes a team that relies more on the middles, more on the pins, or if it’s truly a balanced mix of both. Every team takes on its own identity. It’ll be fun to see what identity this year’s team undertakes. #5. Can Stanford go undefeated at Maples? This might sound like a lofty goal, but in truth, when you look at the schedule, it’s entirely conceivable than an undefeated season at Maples will come down to that Tuesday, November 24 th match against Pitt. The vast majority of their tough matches are away from Maples. The chance to go undefeated at Maples is certainly there. Especially in the regular season. And then if they enter the postseason with a top four seed and an undefeated home record, that should make them even tougher to beat in the NCAA tournament. articles.summary: On Friday, Tarik Skubal returned to Detroit as part of the Los Angeles Dodgers. He came away victorious with a 2-1 win in which he pitched six innings and recorded seven strikeouts. Meanwhile, Skubal had to deal with fans of his former team now opposing him. During the game, when his name was men
articles._body: On Friday, Tarik Skubal returned to Detroit as part of the Los Angeles Dodgers. He came away victorious with a 2-1 win in which he pitched six innings and recorded seven strikeouts. Meanwhile, Skubal had to deal with fans of his former team now opposing him. During the game, when his name was mentioned, roars reverberated. However, it is not entirely definitive whether he was being booed or cheered. After all, his nickname “Skoob” could be interpreted as boos. In the locker room after the game, Skubal was asked what he thought and gave a funny admission, per Jeff Riger of 97.1 The Ticket. “You know with the last name Skoob, you don’t know if they are boos or they’re cheering for you and I gotta assume they were cheering for me,” Skubal said. “That’s all I gotta say about that”. Tarik Skubal addresses the media in the visitors locker room. As for if he got booed tonight? “You know with the last name Skoob, you don’t know if they are boos or they’re cheering for you and I gotta assume they were cheering for me. That’s all I gotta say about that” pic.twitter.com/G6hHUezpD1 — Jeff Riger (@riger1984) August 29, 2026 Skubal is now 8-7 with 153 strikeouts and a 2.85 ERA. Meanwhile, the Dodgers are 81-54 and just waiting for the day to lock up the National League West Division. Skubal also joins at a time when the Dodgers are looking to win their third straight World Series title. In early August, the Tigers traded Skubal to the Dodgers . He spent his first six MLB seasons with the Tigers. In 2024 and 2025, Skubal won two American League Cy Young Awards. He also became a two-time American League All-Star. In 2024, Skubal won the American League pitcher’s triple crown with 18 wins, 228 strikeouts, and a 2.39 ERA. The Dodgers’ second game against the Tigers is Saturday at 12:10 pm CST at Comerica Park.
