Odell Beckham Jr. vows to ‘give his whole heart’ to NY if he makes the Giants roster
articles.summary: Odell Beckham Jr. is not taking his return to New York for granted. Speaking after the Giants’ preseason finale, the veteran receiver made an emotional case for a roster spot, telling fans exactly what a homecoming with the team that drafted him would mean. “It would mean everything.
articles._body: Odell Beckham Jr. is not taking his return to New York for granted . Speaking after the Giants’ preseason finale, the veteran receiver made an emotional case for a roster spot, telling fans exactly what a homecoming with the team that drafted him would mean. “It would mean everything. It would be my dream. This is where I started,” Beckham said in a sideline interview . “There’s no place I want to give my whole heart to more than this place right here.” Odell Beckham Jr on what would it mean for him to play for the New York Giants again this year pic.twitter.com/vvqlXDAp5Y — Talkin’ Giants (@TalkinGiants) August 29, 2026 Beckham, now 33, rejoined the Giants this offseason more than a decade after they made him the 12th overall pick in 2014. He spent his first five seasons in New York, earning Offensive Rookie of the Year honors and three Pro Bowl nods while becoming one of the most electric receivers of his era. He later won a Super Bowl with the Rams and posted five 1,000-yard seasons across his career. This summer, he has been fighting from the bottom of the depth chart just to earn his way back. The comeback has not been a straight line. Beckham has not appeared in a regular-season game since 2024, his lone season in Miami, and he sat out all of last year. His preseason production has been modest, with a pair of quiet outings against the Vikings and Dolphins, though he flashed his old form with a one-handed grab in practice this week. His odds may have improved at the right moment . The Giants lost wide receiver Calvin Austin III to a serious knee injury , potentially opening a spot behind locks Malik Nabers, Darius Slayton, and rookie Malachi Fields. Coach John Harbaugh, who had Beckham with the Ravens in 2023, has praised the receiver’s fight and humility without tipping his hand on the final decision . The timing gives Beckham’s words extra weight. New York must trim its roster to 53 players by Sunday , meaning his football future in the place he loves most could be settled within hours. Beckham has framed the moment as the fulfillment of a dream rather than a long shot, and after everything it took to get back, he is leaving no doubt about how much a Giants roster spot would mean. articles._body: The biggest clash in Oklahoma high school football this week, the matchup between Bixby (Okla.) and Owasso (Okla.), was suggested to be a de facto state championship game, and it certainly delivered like one. In a one-score game, Bixby held on to open their season with a 1-0 record. A rematch of last year’s Oklahoma high school football 6A-I state championship game, last year’s clash between the two sides also ended in Bixby’s favor. Defeating Owasso 31-17 for its seventh straight title, the gap between the two teams has closed significantly according to Friday Night’s clash. READ MORE: Owasso (Okla.) 2026 Preview: State title return odds, game-by-game predictions With four-star tight end Connor Arrant opening the scoring for the Trojans, the 6A-I state champions took an early 14-0 start as Isaiah Butcher ran one in on his first start. Transferring from Jenks (Okla.), the 2028 signal caller finished the night with three rushing scores. However, Owasso had its own transfer standout on the night, with four-star athlete Kamieon Compton-Nero , who joined from Rejoice Christian School (Okla.). The 6-foot-3, 187-pound standout is the No. 2 athlete and No. 60 overall prospect in the 2028 class, according to the Rivals Industry Rankings Coming off a breakout season, Compton-Nero finished the year with 3,335 all-purpose yards and 49 touchdowns, and with 95 tackles, six interceptions, and three pick-sixes on defense. On the night, the four-star athlete hauled in two touchdown passes, both making it a one-score game. Following his big performance tonight, the four-star prospect, who is currently unrecruited, has a busy few weeks ahead. Recently speaking with Rivals, the number one prospect in Oklahoma high school football has nine-game day visits scheduled over the next few weeks. “He will visit Oklahoma (Sept. 4); Oklahoma State (Sept. 13); Ole Miss (Sept. 19); Alabama (Sept. 26); SMU (Oct. 3); Oklahoma (Oct. 10); Texas Tech (Oct. 17); LSU (Nov. 7), and Notre Dame (Nov. 21).” Rivals’ Sam Spiegelman reported, as Compton-Nero broke down his recruitment. , READ MORE: Blue-chipper Kamieon Compton-Nero intel: Leaders emerging, game-day visits set Despite Compton-Nero’s performance, Bixby managed to come through on the night, solidifying themselves as the number one team in Oklahoma high school football. Gunning for its ninth straight state championship, the Spartans look well on their way to defending their crown. With one of the best rosters in Oklahoma, the Spartans have one of the top tight ends in the country in Arrant, as well as one of the top offensive-line prospects in four-star Kaeden Penny . Additionally, Penny is also joined on the line by four-star junior offensive lineman Gavin Wilson . Following their win tonight, Bixby is back in Oklahoma high school football action next week, taking on Stillwater (Okla.). Meanwhile, Owasso will be looking to bounce back from a narrow loss, taking on the No. 2 Jenks (Okla.) coming off the back of a heartbreaking loss at the Cotton Bowl.

articles.summary: You couldn’t have blamed Mount Carmel (Ill.) if it lied down and accepted an 0-2 start to its 2026 season on Friday night. St. Joseph Regional (N.J.) made the trip down to Chicago and had the Caravan in a world of hurt early. The visiting Green Knights led 30-0 just one play into the second [&
articles._body: You couldn’t have blamed Mount Carmel (Ill.) if it lied down and accepted an 0-2 start to its 2026 season on Friday night. St. Joseph Regional (N.J.) made the trip down to Chicago and had the Caravan in a world of hurt early. The visiting Green Knights led 30-0 just one play into the second quarter, though the deficit likely felt like 100 in the moment for Carmel head coach Jordan Lynch. His team lost by 19 points in their season-opener last week. It looked like this was going to, stunningly, be far worse for a staunch program that’s rattled off four-straight state titles. This is high school football, though. Not many leads are insurmountable, especially when you’ve got a loaded roster filled with blue-chip playmakers. Lynch scraped his team off the mat and steadied the waters. The Caravan limped away with a 48-44 win in what will surely be a contender for high school football game of the year. $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage Mount Carmel quarterback Brady Cloherty connected with senior wide receiver Quentin Burrell down the right sideline for a 35-yard touchdown to give their team their first lead of the night with just over five minutes to go in the fourth quarter. Cloherty finished with a whopping seven passing touchdowns, four of which came in the first half, somehow shrinking that early 30-point deficit down to two. Burrell, a four-star prospect committed to Michigan , reeled in three of those scores. The first half was rife with miscues and chaos, and while the second wasn’t free of either, it did feature longer drives, better football and all the tension that comes with a heavyweight battle. St. Joseph led 44-35 after the third quarter, but the Caravan wouldn’t be denied. St. Joseph poured it on early It looked like it was going to be an absolute beatdown. It certiainly was for the first quarter-and-a-half. After stuffing Carmel on fourth down near midfield in the opening drive of the game, St. Joseph drew first blood thanks to some trickery. An end-around turned into a passing play as Will Mitchell fired a 27-yard touchdown strike to senior Stalin Knowlden . Andrew Wilson then exploded up the middle for a 52-yard score, capping off another quick drive to make it 14-0. Carmel then fumbled a punt in the end zone, which the Green Knights pounced on for another score. The ensuing Carmel pass was intercepted. The first quarter ended with St. Joseph forcing a safety. Blocked punt ALERT St. Joseph Regional (NJ) up 21-0 in a HURRY pic.twitter.com/qNeLM5kc5G — SportsCenter NEXT (@SCNext) August 28, 2026 The Caravan was trailing 23-0 in a flash. That then became 30-0 after Knowlden ran the ensuing kick back for his second score of the night. An absolute mess for the home team. Normally, that spells the end of your night in a hurry. Mount Carmel comes to life All it takes is one score to get the ball rolling. That’s a hard sell when you’re down by 30, but once Carmel got on the board, you could see the momentum shift. Junior four-star WR Marshaun Thornton caught two touchdowns in the win, including his team’s first of the evening. Burrell then got back on the board with a slick one-handed grab toward the back right pylon. It began to snowball from there. St. Joseph was forced to punt on the ensuing possession, and the snap went over the punter’s head, leading to a turnover that gave the Caravan the ball back in the red zone. Senior WR Duran Sims then got in on the action, hauling in a TD courtesy of Cloherty. St. Joseph had to travel without head coach  Augie Hoffmann , who’s suspended for the first two games of the season for violating school policies around offseason training. It made a questionable decision on the ensuing drive, going for it on fourth down near their own 30-yard line. Carmel stuffed it, then drove down the field once more, scoring again as Cloherty hit Thornton for the second time. From 30-0 to 30-28 in the blink of an eye. Halftime couldn’t have come fast enough for the Green Knights, who were just riding the highest of highs no less than 20 minutes ago. The Caravan prevails late St. Joseph, to its credit, looked un-phased as it scored on the opening drive of the second half. Knowlden burnt the Carmel secondary and was wide-open, hauling in a deep TD pass. The teams then traded scores after finally putting together some long drives that didn’t need one glaring mistake or a wave of penalties to lead to a touchdown. Yes, the Caravan allowed 44 points tonight, but it’s hard to blame the defense for much of anything that occurred in the first half. It really buckled in and came up with some big stops late as the pressure ramped up. Senior four-star linebacker Roman Igwebuike , in particular, was making heaps of plays all over the field. Down two scores, Carmel was in need of a jolt and it received just that as Cloherty hit streaking junior tight end Ty Kennedy down the middle of the field for a wide-open touchdown. Surprisingly, Lynch and Co. went for a 2-point conversion that failed, instead of taking the extra point that would’ve made it a 44-42 St. Joseph lead. That decision wouldn’t come back to bite, however, as the St. Joseph offense continued to stall down the stretch. Carmel got the ball back, worked it down the field and Cloherty fired the game-winning TD pass to Burrell with around five minutes to go. Its defense stood tall two more times, ending with a Joe Tracy interception to seal an absurd comeback victory. ESPN thinks Kentucky could be college football’s next Indiana
articles.summary: ESPN's Bill Connelly included Kentucky in his list of the 20 college football teams that could follow in Indiana's footsteps by winning their first title.
articles._body: Since he took the job at Kentucky in December, Will Stein has pointed to Indiana as a model for winning big in Lexington, even having his own Curt Cignetti moment at SEC Media Days . In his first season in Bloomington, Cignetti took the Hoosiers to the College Football Playoff; in his second, Indiana won the whole thing, the first national championship in program history. Indiana’s run is proof that with the transfer portal and NIL/rev-share, even college cellar dwellers can become champions, which Stein wants to replicate at Kentucky. He’s not alone in thinking it’s possible. ESPN’s Bill Connelly included Kentucky in his list of the teams that could follow in Indiana’s footsteps by winning their first title . The Cats are one of 35 Power Four teams without a national championship to their name, six in the SEC. Using historical poll finishes, recent SP+ rankings and averages, ESPN’s Future Power Rankings, and revenue data, Connelly came up with 20 contenders; Kentucky is No. 15, in large part because of Stein. “Like rival Louisville, Kentucky derives a level of revenue from basketball that few others could hope for and also boasts recent gridiron success. Mark Stoops couldn’t keep the good times rolling after 10-win seasons in 2018 and 2021, and last year’s team was UK’s worst in a decade. But the school grabbed former Oregon offensive coordinator Will Stein, and no new head coach in this cycle puts off more Potential Dan Lanning vibes. “Stein immediately made some aggressive moves to upgrade the Wildcats’ line play, and his first Kentucky team will be big, physical and likely improved. We don’t know nearly enough about the Wildcats’ potential ceiling under Stein, but they have money and a young, hungry head coach. That’s often an exciting combination.” If you’re curious, Kentucky’s revenue from the last relevant fiscal year on record is $159.1 million, which ranks No. 16 in the country per USA Today . As Connelly mentions, a lot of that comes from men’s basketball, and with J Batt now in charge and the Champions Blue LLC model humming, the school reportedly has “Scrooge McDuck” money to fund its teams. In fact, only one of the 20 teams Connelly listed had more reported revenue than Kentucky: Virginia, at $161.9 million (SMU and Vanderbilt, also on the list, are private and therefore don’t have to report their numbers). What other teams could be the next Indiana? No. 1 is the one Stein left to return to the Bluegrass: Oregon. The Ducks are the obvious choice, reaching the title game in 2010 and 2014, and the College Football Playoff semifinals last year, where they lost to the Hoosiers. The Ducks are ranked No. 2 going into this season, a reminder that Stein left a pretty good thing in Eugene to come home. Texas Tech, Ole Miss, Iowa, and Missouri round out Connelly’s top five. Louisville is No. 6, South Carolina No. 11, Vanderbilt No. 16, and Arkansas No. 17. James Madison even made the list at No. 20. Again, as Connelly said, Kentucky’s a bit of a mystery heading into Stein’s first season, but it’s nice that a respected national voice sees the potential in Lexington. [ESPN: After Indiana, who could be college football’s next first-time national champion]

Jimmie Johnson delivers massive endorsement of Carson Hocevar amid NASCAR controversy
articles.summary: Jimmie Johnson backs Carson Hocevar as a personality NASCAR needs, despite admitting his own frustrations with the polarizing young star.
articles._body: The year and week of Carson Hocevar continues.  That week started with a viral pre-race spin at New Hampshire. irritating several other drivers, an accusation of causing a caution intentionally to get back on the lead lap, and all of that to just get a P19 finish in the Dollar Tree 301 . It continued with a massive merchandise sales statistic, and now, NASCAR Hall of Famer Jimmie Johnson has weighed in on the phenomenon that is Carson Hocevar.  The 7-time NASCAR Cup Series champion took to Twitter on Friday night and placed a massive seal of approval on Hocevar for the sport.  He did, however, add a few qualifiers.  Johnson backs Hocevar It was odd that there was very little lead-up to this.  This came during the dramatic finish of the NASCAR O’Reilly Auto Parts Series regular season finale at Daytona.  But alas, it was a well-received sentiment from one of the GOATs of the sport to Hocevar’s ever-growing fanbase.    “My opinion: Carson Hocevar is one of many personalities our sport needs,” said Johnson via Twitter . “Now I should state a few things…  “1. He drove for us and has only spoken to us once in two-ish years since.  “2. I’m frustrated with his mistakes wrecking our cars.  “3. I by no means won over the core NASCAR fan base.  “And 4. Merch sales don’t lie” My opinion: @CarsonHocevar is one of many personalities, our sport needs. Now I should state a few things… 1. He drove for us and has only spoken to once in 2ish years since. 2. I’m frustrated with his mistakes wrecking our cars. 3. I by no means won over the core @nascar fan… — Jimmie Johnson (@JimmieJohnson) August 29, 2026 Those merch sales The news broke this week in a press release by NASCAR titled: “Does Everybody Hate Carson Hocevar?”  The subtitle was equally compelling: “The Chase has 16 drivers. Carson Hocevar might have 15 enemies.” Before the press release was widely available, Jeff Gluck tweeted the most intriguing portion of it:  “NASCAR says Carson Hocevar ranks No. 1 in online retail sales (on the NASCAR Shop website) and is in the top five of trackside sales,” tweeted Jeff Gluck . “At this time last year he ranked 32nd.” The news itself is hardly surprising, considering the legion of fans that Hocevar is building through social platforms.  Say something negative and find out, I dare you.   Hocevar is a phenomenon.  Hell, he’s a movement.  And that movement is driving trackside and online sales.  And that’s despite just a single Cup victory to his credit.   Hocevar responds in the most Hocevar way Carson Hocevar responded to Gluck’s tweet.  And it’s in the most Hocevar way possible.  No words, just a ripped TikTok montage of The Wolf of Wall Street moments and quotes.   pic.twitter.com/uaJKKokK6f — Carson Hocevar (@CarsonHocevar) August 27, 2026 That’s Hocevar.  A racer of the meme generation.  A gamer.  A brilliantly self-aware marketing machine that knows his audience.  And is growing it.   And what makes him so interesting is that the way he wants to race is more akin to Dale Earnhardt Sr.  A throwback, in that regard.  Now, Dale Sr. might’ve stuffed Hocevar in more than a locker or two in the garage, but Dale Sr. the businessman was ahead of his time when it came to building a brand and taking control of your own image licensing for himself and his peers.  He would’ve undoubtedly respected that side of Hocevar’s brand-building efforts.

articles.title: Around the American: Week 0
articles.summary: The American enters 2026 after a record-setting postseason, but coaching changes and roster turnover have left plenty of uncertainty. Here’s a look at the conference landscape, plus Saturday’s Week 0 matchup between Memphis and UNLV.
articles._body: College football returns this weekend, although most of the American Conference will have to wait another week to join the fun. Memphis is the lone exception. The Tigers travel to UNLV on Saturday night for the conference’s only Week 0 game, giving us a first glimpse of the new-look Tigers. As the season gets underway, let’s set the table for what the American looks like heading into 2026. A tough act to follow Nine American teams played in the postseason last year, a conference record. Five of them won. Only the Big Ten and ACC had more postseason victories. Navy , North Texas and Tulane all won at least 11 games, while the American was the only conference in the country to post nonconference wins over teams from the Big Ten, Big 12, SEC and ACC. The question now is how much of that carries over. Five programs have coaches beginning their first full seasons: Charles Huff at Memphis, Brian Hartline at USF , Alex Mortensen at UAB , Neal Brown at North Texas, and Will Hall at Tulane. Along with the coaching turnover, there is roster turnover thanks to the portal. UTSA brought in nearly 40 players through the portal this offseason. Rice lost more than 50 players between graduation and transfers. The American lost a lot of star power across the board; league commissioner Tim Pernetti noted at media day that 78% of the American’s first- and second-team all-conference players with remaining eligibility transferred to a Power 4 program in the offseason. It makes projecting the 2026 season a daunting task. Continuity under center With so much uncertainty, one potential advantage some teams will have is continuity at quarterback. There are at least a few familiar names at the position, and stability under center could be a point of separation in the conference race. Florida Atlantic has Caden Veltkamp back after he threw for 3,641 yards last season and finished fifth nationally in passing yards. UTSA returns Owen McCown , who threw 30 touchdown passes against seven interceptions, while Tulsa brings back Baylor Hayes after he set school freshman records for total offense and touchdown passes. Army also returns Cale Hellums , who rushed for 1,223 yards and 18 touchdowns last season. While it doesn’t guarantee success, having an established quarterback at least gives you something to build around. For Navy, Veltkamp is the most immediate name to watch. The Mids travel to FAU on Sept. 12 for their conference opener. The Owls finished fourth in the American in total offense last season behind the nation’s top passing attack, but they also finished 13th in the conference in both total defense and scoring defense. If head coach Zach Kittley can find some answers on that side of the ball, his team could be a dark horse contender. Into the unknown No team embodies the uncertainty around the conference quite like North Texas. The Mean Green won 11 games last season, reached the American Conference Championship Game, and led the league in both total offense and scoring offense, averaging 512.4 yards and 45.1 points per game. Zero starters return from that team. Neal Brown takes over after previous stops at Troy and West Virginia , and he had to lean on the portal to rebuild the roster. Among the additions are West Virginia transfer running back Jaheim White and UCF transfer quarterback Tayven Jackson . It’s hard to imagine a wider gap between what a team accomplished last season and what we actually know about them this fall. Navy will find out for themselves when they host the Mean Green on October 24. Game of the Week: Memphis at UNLV Memphis gets the first chance to make a statement when it travels to Las Vegas on Saturday night in a matchup of two teams expected to contend for the G6 Playoff spot. Charles Huff’s Tigers are another rebuilt squad, with 81 newcomers on the roster, including 61 transfers. Only four players who started a game for Memphis last season are back. Huff did bring some familiarity with him. Eighteen players followed him from Southern Miss , including several pieces from a defense that led the nation in interceptions last season. Quarterback is less settled, with South Carolina transfer Air Noland and West Florida transfer Marcus Stokes competing for the job throughout the offseason. Stokes, who originally committed to Florida out of high school but had his offer pulled after some controversy , was the Gulf South Conference Offensive Player of the Year last season at the Division II level and is expected to start. UNLV should provide a challenging first test. Dan Mullen ‘s team went 10-4 in his first season, and the Rebels have played in three straight Mountain West championship games. They also return running back Jai’Den Thomas , who rushed for 1,036 yards and 12 touchdowns while averaging 7.0 yards per carry last season. One game won’t answer every question facing what has been a perennial league favorite, but it should at least give us a better idea of what Huff has put together. Memphis and UNLV kick off at 10 p.m. Eastern on FOX.

articles.summary: Shohei Ohtani’s return to the mound remains up in the air. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said it is still undecided whether the two-way superstar will start Sunday’s series finale against the Detroit Tigers, keeping Los Angeles and the rest of the baseball world waiting a little longer
articles._body: Shohei Ohtani’s return to the mound remains up in the air. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said it is still undecided whether the two-way superstar will start Sunday’s series finale against the Detroit Tigers, keeping Los Angeles and the rest of the baseball world waiting a little longer. Ohtani threw a 20-pitch bullpen session ahead of the Dodgers’ game, another step in a careful buildup toward his first pitching appearance since July 3. Roberts said the team will see how Ohtani responds before making a call on the Sunday outing. The right-hander has been sidelined on the mound by left knee inflammation, though he has continued to rake as the Dodgers’ designated hitter throughout the layoff. When Ohtani does return, the Dodgers plan to ease him in. He is expected to work as an opener for roughly one inning before handing off to Tyler Glasnow, who would follow as the bulk pitcher. That arrangement doubles as a preview of how Los Angeles could deploy the two in October, when the club will chase a third straight World Series title. The stakes for the stretch run are clear. A Sunday return would line Ohtani up for about five starts before the end of the regular season, giving him a runway to build back toward a traditional starter’s workload by the playoffs. The Dodgers have been deliberately cautious, prioritizing his health over rushing him back, with the postseason as the real target for their two-way star. Even without pitching, Ohtani has remained one of the sport’s most productive players. He is hitting .288 with 30 home runs and 80 RBIs while anchoring the middle of the Los Angeles lineup, keeping himself in the National League MVP conversation alongside Pete Crow-Armstrong . On the mound earlier this season, he posted a 1.79 ERA across 14 starts before the knee issue interrupted his year. For now, the answer is the same one the Dodgers have been giving for weeks. Ohtani is close, the pieces are lining up, and the decision comes down to how his body responds. Roberts and the Dodgers will take one more look before telling everyone whether Sunday is the day. articles.title: Angel Reese will not miss Dream-Lynx clash after 8th technical foul gets rescinded
articles.summary: Update: Angel Reese will not miss the Atlanta Dream’s clash with the Minnesota Lynx after her eighth technical foul was rescinded by the WNBA, according to ESPN’s Alexa Philippou. Angel Reese may have to watch one of the Atlanta Dream’s biggest remaining games from the bench. Th
articles._body: Update: Angel Reese will not miss the Atlanta Dream’s clash with the Minnesota Lynx after her eighth technical foul was rescinded by the WNBA, according to ESPN’s Alexa Philippou. Angel Reese may have to watch one of the Atlanta Dream’s biggest remaining games from the bench. The star forward was assessed her eighth technical foul of the 2026 season during Friday night’s home game against the Portland Fire, putting her on track for an automatic one-game suspension that would sideline her for Sunday’s matchup with the Minnesota Lynx. Reese picked up the technical in the fourth quarter after making contact with Portland’s Carla Leite. Under the WNBA’s rules, a player who reaches eight technical fouls in the regular season is automatically suspended for one game and fined $1,500, with an additional suspension for every two technicals after that. The 24-year-old leads the league in technical fouls and has been the WNBA’s most-penalized player for much of the season. The play that led to Angel Reese's 8th technical foul and a suspension for Sunday against the Lynx unless it is rescinded: pic.twitter.com/G8wsa09F37 — Underdog WNBA (@UnderdogWNBA) August 29, 2026 There is still a path for Reese to play. The suspension only takes effect if the technical stands, and the league office can rescind it on review. Until that ruling comes down, the 7th overall pick in the 2024 WNBA Draft’s status for Sunday’s game will remain up in the air. The timing could hardly be worse for Atlanta. Reese has been playing the best basketball of her season down the stretch, stacking double-doubles and closing in on the WNBA’s single-season rebounding record . Over one recent stretch she averaged 24 points, better than 11 rebounds, and nearly five assists a night as the Dream surged. Atlanta sits at 25-14 and has already clinched a playoff berth for the fourth straight year, but the Dream are still fighting for seeding and home-court advantage. Sunday’s opponent makes the stakes clear. The Lynx own the league’s best record at 31-8 and loom as a possible playoff foe, making it the kind of measuring-stick game where the Dream would want their leading rebounder on the floor . This is not new territory for Reese. She served a technical-related suspension last season while with the Chicago Sky, missing a game after reaching the same threshold, and was the only WNBA player suspended for technical fouls all year. A year later, in a new city and in the middle of a career-best run, she is again one league decision away from a night in street clothes. This time around at Heritage Stadium on Friday night versus East St. Louis (Ill.), the Patriots would welcome back multiple starting offensive linemen and look more like the program that has won back-to-back state championships. With the victory, American Heritage evens their record at 1-1 as they go into a difficult stretch of games that includes Chaminade-Madonna Prep (Fla.), Trinity Christian Academy (Fla.) and Lakeland (Fla.), respectively. Lawrence and the offense continued to find themselves in sync as the Texas commit threw two more touchdown passes and built up a 28-7 lead into the fourth quarter. Supported by world-class facilities, exceptional coaching, and a culture emphasizing academic achievement, leadership, and competitive excellence, American Heritage regularly contends for district, regional, state, and national honors across multiple sports. articles._body: St. Frances Academy (Md.) finished last season on top of the high school football world. The Free State powerhouse wants all the smoke in 2026 — and it received just about all it could handle in its season-opening 49-35 win on the road over DeLand (Fla.) on Friday night. It took two fourth-quarter scores and snuffing out a fake punt for the visiting Panthers to finally pull away down the stretch. Senior running back Sa’Nir Brooks and senior receiver Vegas Brown were responsible for getting St. Frances over the finish line. $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage The former broke off a 47-yard touchdown run to give his team the lead for good. The latter caught a 20-yard TD pass at the right pylon from sophomore four-star quarterback Justin Merriman to put the Panthers up two scores with less than seven minutes to play. St. Frances led 35-21 in the third quarter, but the Bulldogs continued to fight, running the ball well while finding ways to get off the field on defense. Constantly throwing the Panthers different looks, they routinely drove into the red zone and converted on the ground, scoring twice to even things up at 35, converting a 2-point conversion and missing a PAT in the process. The Panthers, who entered as the No. 2 team nationally per the Rivals Composite Rankings, headed South to take on one of the top programs in the Sunshine State; DeLand entered as the No. 11 team in Florida. On paper, it looked like SFA had both the clear defensive and offensive edge. That wasn’t always the case. The Bulldogs were more than up for the challenge on their home field. Keeping the St. Frances defense off-balance, they found pay dirt three times in the first half and entered the locker room tied up at 21. DeLand attempted multiple onside kicks and played like a group that felt it could defeat the No. 2 team in the nation. DeLand was up for the task early DeLand struck first with a long drive that resulted in a red zone rushing touchdown in the middle of the first quarter. It then made it clear that it wasn’t going to bullied by the Panthers’ offense, as it sacked Merriman, the son of Shawne Merriman, forcing a punt. Merriman would soon scramble to his left for a 15-yard score to get St. Frances on the board later in the quarter. The Bulldogs had an answer, though. Junior four-star running back Taihj Moore was a handful for the Panthers and he broke off multiple long runs on Friday night. The two teams traded scores, but it was DeLand that executed a 2-point conversion while SFA’s extra point was blocked, resulting in a 14-13 lead for the home team. St. Frances soon got the lead thanks to a punt return score via Brown, who later iced it with the TD reception. It then had a chance to add on before halftime, but a fumble was recovered by DeLand, which then drove down the field again and punched in another score. Big plays propelled St. Frances The long 75-yard punt return from Brown saw the senior shake off a couple of tackles before hoofing it up the left sideline then toward the middle of the field. While DeLand showed it has the roster capable of hanging with the Panthers, it was the occasional burst that really made the difference. Merriman connected with sophomore Kentae Davis on a drag from around 35 yards out and he quickly cut up the field for a long score to give St. Frances a 28-21 lead in the third quarter. That lead grew to two scores on its next drive as Brooks, a three-star prospect in the 2027 cycle, peeled off the pile, spinning out to his right for a 49-yard TD run. articles._body: Arkansas basketball coach John Calipari has shared his thoughts on the S outheastern Conference’s new eligibility rules . College basketball is still facing uncertainty as players look for ways to play extra seasons. Calipari, one of the SEC’s most well-known coaches since joining Arkansas , said he supports the conference’s approach in a talk with Andy Katz. His remarks come as the eligibility case involving former Missouri player Mark Mitchell and others is still unfolding. “I like what the SEC is doing,” Calipari said, according to Katz. “If a player doesn’t like what the SEC is doing, what? Go to another league.” Katz noted that coaches who do not agree with the conference’s rules could also choose to leave the SEC. Calipari answered strongly. “Just do it. Make it hard. Do it right,” the Arkansas coach said. The SEC recently adopted rules that prevent athletes who have declared for the professional draft or signed pro contracts from returning to play in the conference. This policy has sparked debate, especially as legal fights continue over eligibility for players from the 2022 high school class. Mitchell is one of the players affected by the eligibility dispute. Even though a court said he could try for another season, the SEC’s new policy has raised more questions about whether he can play. For Arkansas and Calipari, this situation shows how fast college basketball is changing. With legal issues still ongoing, it is not yet clear how the SEC’s eligibility rules will ultimately affect matters. Many are waiting to see whether these changes will truly benefit student-athletes and shape the sport’s future. articles.summary: Caitlin Clark was unstoppable as she made WNBA history following her performance in the Indiana Fever’s 111-91 blowout win over the Connecticut Sun on Friday night. Clark is going through the third season of her WNBA career with the Fever. After going through injuries in 2025, she has enjoy
articles._body: Caitlin Clark was unstoppable as she made WNBA history following her performance in the Indiana Fever’s 111-91 blowout win over the Connecticut Sun on Friday night. Clark is going through the third season of her WNBA career with the Fever. After going through injuries in 2025, she has enjoyed a healthy season as Indiana looks forward to playoff basketball. Going into Indiana’s clash with Connecticut, Clark has showed off strong momentum with a tendency to make records in unique ways. This time, she channeled the double-double side of her game. In 34 minutes of action, Clark outmatched with Connecticut defenders in every way she wanted. She finished with a stat line of 34 points, 12 assists, five rebounds, and three steals. She shot 12-of-19 from the field, including 6-of-12 from beyond the arc, and 4-of-6 from the free-throw line. Her efforts allowed her to have the second consecutive game of getting a double-double with 30 or more points and 10 or more assists throughout WNBA history. Caitlin Clark is the first player in WNBA history with consecutive games of 30 points & 10 assists https://t.co/phL3SyGtJX pic.twitter.com/yQYjYJNZrA — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 29, 2026 How Caitlin Clark, Fever played against Sun Caitlin Clark enjoyed lighting up the nets with her performance as the Fever rolled over the Sun with the blowout victory. Four players scored in double-digits for Indiana in the win, including Clark. Kelsey Mitchell delivered a strong performance with 34 points, four assists, three rebounds, and one steal. She shot 12-of-19 overall, including 4-of-9 from downtown, and 6-of-10 from the charity stripe. Aliyah Boston came next with 14 points and two rebounds, while Makayla Timpson provided 10 points and eight rebounds. Indiana improved to a 26-14 record on the season, sitting at first place in the Eastern Conference standings. They are above the Atlanta Dream and the New York Liberty at the moment. The Fever will look forward to their next matchup, being on the road. Being on break due to the FIBA Women’s World Cup, they will return when they host the Toronto Tempo as tip-off takes place on Sept. 18 at 7:30 p.m. ET. articles.title: Eagles’ Jalen Hurts gets real on constantly changing offensive system
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts has grown used to starting over. The Philadelphia Eagles quarterback is working with his sixth offensive coordinator in seven NFL seasons, and this time it is new play-caller Sean Mannion running the show. Rather than treat the latest overhaul as a burden, Hurts is leaning into it. &#
articles._body: Jalen Hurts has grown used to starting over. The Philadelphia Eagles quarterback is working with his sixth offensive coordinator in seven NFL seasons, and this time it is new play-caller Sean Mannion running the show . Rather than treat the latest overhaul as a burden, Hurts is leaning into it. “Every year is its own year, and I’ve treated it that way,” Hurts said in an interview by NFL on CBS’ AJ Ross. “Especially as I’ve gotten older, because you have to embrace the change. I think working with Sean has been really good.” Jalen Hurts on his way with words, new offense, playing with Makai Lemon and more : @AJRoss_TV pic.twitter.com/bqPCZO86zZ — NFL on CBS (@NFLonCBS) August 29, 2026 Mannion’s arrival marks the most significant schematic shift of the Nick Sirianni era . A first-time play-caller out of the Sean McVay coaching tree, Mannion is installing a motion-heavy, play-action system built on wide-zone runs that will put Hurts under center far more often than in years past . It is a clear departure from the offense Philadelphia ran during its recent Super Bowl run. The change followed a disappointing 2025 season in which the passing game regressed and the offense lost its rhythm. Hurts, though, framed the reset as an opportunity rather than a setback, describing himself as being in “sponge mode” while soaking up Mannion’s system through training camp. “I’m excited to see how things go in the season as we put things together,” Hurts said. He added that he has stayed locked in on the process, calling the constant turnover “some of the beauty of the NFL” because “it changes year to year.” Hurts has navigated this cycle before. The list of coordinators he has learned under keeps growing, from Shane Steichen and Brian Johnson to Kellen Moore and Kevin Patullo, with several leaving for head coaching jobs elsewhere. Continuity has been the missing piece, and Hurts made clear he values building fluency in one system over the long haul. The stakes are real. Philadelphia reshaped its roster this offseason, trading receiver A.J. Brown to New England and drafting rookie Makai Lemon to help fill the void alongside DeVonta Smith. With a new coordinator, a new scheme, and a retooled supporting cast, the Eagles are betting that Mannion’s system finally gives Hurts something that lasts. Dodgers’ Tarik Skubal delivers in bittersweet homecoming vs. Tigers
articles.summary: Tarik Skubal was filled with gratitude and emotion when he returned to Comerica Park for Friday’s inter-league showdown between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Detroit Tigers, but once he stepped on the mound, the shark emerged. The two-time American League Cy Young winner stymied his former ba
articles._body: Tarik Skubal was filled with gratitude and emotion when he returned to Comerica Park for Friday’s inter-league showdown between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Detroit Tigers, but once he stepped on the mound, the shark emerged. The two-time American League Cy Young winner stymied his former ballclub for most of the night, with a Max Clark RBI triple serving as his only real mistake. The left-handed ace earnestly hoped that a midseason split could be avoided, but he is not going to take pity on anyone. Not even the organization he represented for eight years. Skubal had a job to do , and to no one’s surprise, he did it well. The veteran southpaw flourished in his old stomping grounds, allowing only one run on four hits and recording seven strikeouts without walking a single batter. His six-inning gem allowed the Dodgers to buy time before they took the lead via a Freddie Freeman single in the eighth. Skubal did not get the win, but he enjoys a marvelous homecoming just the same. The prized acquisition maintained his poise in a lively environment and posted the best start of his brief LA tenure. He is healthy, mentally sharp and hungry for championship success. The three-peat chasing Dodgers should be salivating. Tigers fans, on the other hand, have a tough night of sleep ahead of them. Detroit knew it had to say goodbye once the season turned sour, but a practical choice does little to mend the wounds left by the loss of a franchise great. Perhaps both parties will get the opportunity to make more memories together down the road. But right now, Tarik Skubal is sprinting alongside LA all the way to October. articles._body: Odell Beckham may have secured himself a place on the New York Giants roster as the preseason comes to a close this weekend. Beckham is preparing for the 11th season of his NFL career, his sixth with the Giants. He returns to New York after last representing the Empire State from 2014 to 2018, having shined as one of the best receivers in the league. The veteran receiver worked out for New York this summer, reuniting with John Harbaugh after playing for him on the Baltimore Ravens in 2023. Looking to prove himself as a key player in the receiving corps, he has been active throughout the preseason. Beckham made his first highlight in the Giants’ preseason finale against the New York Jets on Friday night. It took place midway through the first quarter with a solid catch as the broadcasting booth mentioned the receiver’s place on the roster. “Talking to the Giants people sounds like OBJ is going to make the team,” the booth said. Jameis Winston finds Odell Beckham Jr. for the Giants first down pic.twitter.com/Ew2TVgyc4p — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 29, 2026 How Odell Beckham Jr., Giants played against Jets Odell Beckham Jr. had his moments to shine in the Giants’ offense as the team cruised to a 23-6 win over the Jets. They end preseason action with a 2-1 record to show for it. The Giants did an excellent job keeping the Jets quiet. Conceding the touchdown in the first quarter, the Giants responded by shutting out the Jets for the remainder of the game. Jake Haener completed six out of seven passes for 101 yards and a touchdown. Tyrone Tracy Jr. rushed four times for 37 yards and a touchdown, while Xavier Gipson caught two passes for 54 yards and a touchdown. They will seek to improve upon their 2025 record of 4–13 and make the playoffs after a three-year absence. They also intend to end their 14-year NFC East title drought, currently the longest active drought in the NFC, and put an end to three consecutive seasons with fewer than seven wins. The Giants will have their regular season go underway at home. They host the Dallas Cowboys as kickoff takes place on Sept. 13 at 8:20 p.m. ET. articles._body: New York Jets rookie running back Chip Trayanum was carted off near the end of the first half of Friday night’s preseason game against the New York Giants. Per the team, Trayanum is awake, alert, and has movement of his extremities on route to the hospital. Prior to suffering the injury, Trayanum rushed for 38 yards and one touchdown on 12 carries. He signed with the Jets as an UDFA this offseason and was battling for a roster spot. Across three postseason games, he totaled 21 carries for 62 yards and one score. Trayanum is most known for his lengthy college football career, which spanned across six seasons and four different programs. The Akron, Ohio native spent two seasons at Arizona State (2020-21) and Ohio State (2022-23), and one season each at Kentucky (2024) and Toledo (2025). All in all, he rushed for 2,273 career yards and 25 touchdowns. Perhaps finest moment came when he scored the game-winning touchdown in Ohio State ‘s 17-14 win over Notre Dame in 2023. The score came with just one second remaining in the game, giving the Buckeyes a monstrous win over the No. 9 ranked Fighting Irish. Trayanum is one of six running backs currently on the Jets’ roster ahead of cut day. While the RB1 ( Breece Hall ) and RB2 ( Braelon Allen ) spots were all but solidified, Trayanum was surely in the running for that RB3 spot alongside Isaiah Davis , Kene Nwangwu , and Dominic Richardson . New York Jets head into second season under head coach Aaron Glenn The New York Jets are coming off a lowly 3-14 season, in which they finished last in the AFC East. New York owns the longest postseason drought in the entire NFL, spanning 15 seasons. The Jets last made the Playoffs in 2010. New York heads into its second season under head coach Aaron Glenn , who shined as the defensive coordinator for the Detroit Lions from 2021-24. Jets ownership was hoping this success would carry over to their organization, but it has not yet. “We’re going to be at our best at whatever we have to do to win the game,” Glenn said during a WFAN segment heading into the season . “The only focus I have is ‘how do we become a good team and a good organization overall?’ That’s the only thing I think about.” The Jets open the season against the Tennessee Titans on Sept. 13. The game will be played in Nashville.

articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings have not had many secrets regarding their roster this summer. The focus for head coach Kevin O’Connell has been on the quarterback position since the end of last season. That’s when the 9-8 Vikings took a hard look at their season and came to the conclusion that
articles._body: The Minnesota Vikings have not had many secrets regarding their roster this summer. The focus for head coach Kevin O’Connell has been on the quarterback position since the end of last season. That’s when the 9-8 Vikings took a hard look at their season and came to the conclusion that they did not get the kind of quarterback play they needed to win the NFC North or make the playoffs. They could have been fooled, because they closed the season with a 5-game winning streak. However, the truth was told in the first 12 games of the season when they were just 4-8 on the season. That was largely due to the inaccuracy and inconsistency of quarterback J.J. McCarthy. O’Connell, one of the foremost quarterback whisperers in the NFL, did not like what he saw. There were a number of games where McCarthy had the opportunity to get the ball to All-Pro wide receiver Justin Jefferson. Instead of producing a game-changing play to one of the most dangerous receivers in the NFL, McCarthy missed the big-play specialist by significant amounts. Jefferson is not the kind of receiver who is going to show up his quarterback with words or gestures, but the look on his face was unmistakable. “If you had gotten me that ball, I would have scored.” There is no doubt that O’Connell came to the same conclusion and that’s why the Vikings brought in Kyler Murray. The former Arizona Cardinals quarterback had apparently run out of rope in the desert and O’Connell wanted him to compete for the starting job. At least that was the theory. However, instead of seeing how both quarterbacks performed in preseason games, O’Connell quickly declared Murray as the team’s starting quarterback and the winner in the competition. Will McCarthy maintain his spot on the roster? The Vikings struggled last year because they did not have a veteran quarterback who could step in when McCarthy had issues. After signing with the Vikings late in training camp, it took him a while to grow into the Vikings system. He would later end up on Injured Reserve. He was re-signed by the Vikings and has an excellent understanding of what O’Connell wants from his quarterback. In addition to knowing the Minnesota system, he has been a winning quarterback in his 10-year career. That has raised the question of whether the Vikings would be better off with Wentz as the No. 2 quarterback or does McCarthy deserve the job. If the answer is Wentz, should McCarthy be on the team as the No. 3 quarterback? The Vikings certainly don’t want to look at the No. 10 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft and declare him a failure, but they don’t want to turn the most important position on the field over to a player that the coaching staff and the Vikings players don’t believe in. McCarthy was hoping to make a stand in the Vikings’ final preseason game against the Denver Broncos, but he had lingering soreness in his ankle from an injury suffered against the Baltimore Ravens in the second preseason game. It did not appear to be a serious injury, but perhaps it will result in McCarthy being placed on the Injured List. That means Wentz would serve as the No. 2 signal caller and second-year QB Max Brosmer would be the third-team quarterback. It is clearly an agonizing situation for the Vikings organization. Wide receiver represents a tough call as well Mandatory Credit: Matt Krohn-Imagn Images The Vikings feel like they have one of the strongest trio of wide receivers in the NFL. While Jefferson did not have a banner year in 2025, he exceeded 1,000 receiving yards for the sixth consecutive season. Jordan Addison has explosive speed and he has developed a brilliant rapport with Murray in training camp. The Vikings signed former 49er Jauan Jennings in the offseason and he should be an excellent No. 3 wide receiver. He caught 55 passes for 643 yards and an eye-catching 9 touchdowns last year, and that came a year after his eye-opening 77-975-6 performance in 2024. The Vikings also have confidence in Myles Price and Tai Felton to fill out the receiving crew, but they have also liked what they have seen from Dillon Bell, an undrafted rookie from Georgia. He has size at 6-1 and 210 pounds, and if the Vikings don’t keep him around, he is likely to be plucked by another team on cutdown day. The Vikings will certainly keep him around and put him on the practice squad, but that may not be enough to keep him in the fold. If they decide to keep him, they may put themselves in a vulnerable spot at another crucial position. That’s something the Vikings can’t afford, especially on the defensive side of the field.   The post Vikings’ most agonizing roster decision looming on 2026 cutdown day appeared first on ClutchPoints .

Rajah Caruth races into NASCAR O’Reilly Series Chase as full 12-driver field is set, Ryan Sieg gets first win
articles.summary: Rajah Caruth raced his way into the NASCAR O’Reilly Series Chase as a dramatic Daytona finale determined the full 12-driver postseason field.
articles._body: All eyes tonight in the Winn-Dixie 250 at Daytona were on the Chase cutline.  The hornets nest battle between three Joe Gibbs Racing teammates and Rajah Caruth, who entered the race at 14th in the Chase standings at the final race of the regular season. Caruth took the first major step by winning his first career pole in the NASCAR O’Reilly Auto Parts Series when he needed it most.  That set the stage for high drama, and Caruth ultimately raced his way into the 12-team Chase field.  The hornets nest at the cutline Brent Crews and William Sawalich entered the race sitting at 11th and 12th, tied with the same amount of points.   In 13th was Taylor Gray.  In 14th was Rajah Caruth.  The difference between 14th and 11th was just 15 points .  That’s the hornets nest there, and there were some wild dynamics at play.  Caruth was 15 points away from 11th and 12th, a tie between Crews and Sawalich.  Taylor Gray was one spot below the cutline in 13th, just 14 points ahead of Caruth.  Caruth finished P2 in Stage 1 Caruth finished second in Stage 1, which ended with 2 laps remaining under caution.  The bigger news is that Brent Crews was in was involved in the wreck.    At the end of the stage, Caruth had jetted up to 12th in the Chase standings, passing Crews and Sam Mayer, who was also involved in the wreck.  Caruth wins Stage 2 Caruth got even closer to making the Chase in Stage 2, which ended early because of Austin Hill getting turned.  Before that happened, however, William Sawalich was also involved in a wreck.  Caruth won the stage , putting him further inside the Chase field with one stage to go. With the stage win and the bad luck to Sawalich and Brent Crews, Rajah Caruth had moved up to 10th in the live Chase standings and +30 points to the cut line.   Taylor Gray had leapfrogged both of his JGR teammates to land in 12th, three points clear of Sawalich and six points clear of Brent Crews.  The finish With five laps to go, Caruth was running second to Carson Kvapil. Points leader Justin Allgaier was directly behind Caruth, making it JR Motorsports, 1-3. While getting a push from Allgaier, Caruth got off center and spun with five laps to go. Caruth received heavy damage in the wreck. “I barely pushed him,” said Allgaier over the radio. “I had him square. It was the perfect push.” After the wreck, Caruth was in 12th, the final Chase spot. Seven points above the cutline and William Sawalich. At the checkered flag, it was Ryan Sieg. In his 424th start, Sieg got his first career win. John Calipari rips state of college sports, calls on commissioners to step in and ‘be the a**holes’
articles.summary: Amid eligibility lawsuits and judge’s rulings that paved the way for former professional athletes to be eligible for college sports, Arkansas men’s basketball coach John Calipari again spoke in favor of the Protect College Sports Act. He did so while sharing strong thoughts on the curren
articles._body: Amid eligibility lawsuits and judge’s rulings that paved the way for former professional athletes to be eligible for college sports, Arkansas men’s basketball coach John Calipari again spoke in favor of the Protect College Sports Act. He did so while sharing strong thoughts on the current landscape. Calipari admitted he disagrees with parts of the bipartisan bill, which is expected to receive a formal vote next month once the Senate returns from recess . Still, he has been vocal in his support for the legislation and was part of a coalition that signed a letter to Congress in June urging its passage. $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage As for why he’s such a staunch supporter, Calipari argued the Protect College Sports Act will help bring “guardrails” college athletics needs. In the meantime, he said the space isn’t settling down, which is why he called on the commissioners to help spur action. He also praised the SEC for its efforts and rules related to professional athletes returning to college sports. “I like what the SEC is doing,” Calipari told Andy Katz on The Sideline earlier this week. “If a player doesn’t like what the SEC is doing, what? Go to another league. … Just do it. Make it hard. Do it right. “And everybody says, ‘Cal, you’re spending all this time.’ Well, I got a son that’s in this profession. Do you honestly think … I want to leave this profession the way it is right now? I want to leave the profession and say, ‘This could have got ugly. But we all came together. Nothing was perfect. Everything is going to continue to move. But we needed guardrails now. The leagues did the right thing.’ We need these commissioners to step in here and – I’ll use the term – be the a**holes. Be that. And then, have rules that there are no waivers, guys. There’s not a waiver.” John Calipari’s warning for college sports Over the last few years, John Calipari has been a vocal opponent of multiple-time transfers and waivers for extra seasons. Of course, now that the NCAA approved an age based, five-year eligibility model, the days of redshirts are seemingly coming to an end. Waivers can be handed out in certain situations, though. That age-based model has been at the center of the latest eligibility lawsuits, though. It is not retroactive for the Class of 2022. As a result, athletes from the class have taken to court seeking a fifth year of eligibility. One now includes the SEC and commissioner Greg Sankey after they were added to a TRO on Friday, seeking to prevent the league from enforcing its new rules. SUBSCRIBE to the On3 NIL and Sports Business Newsletter But when asked about the idea of collective bargaining coming to college athletics to settle things, Calipari had a warning. He said that would not be a quick process to bring together, which is why he said the Protect College Sports Act can spur quicker action. By waiting any longer, Calipari thinks donor fatigue could become a bigger part of the landscape. “If we get that and then five years down the road, there’s some sort of collective bargaining, I’m good with it,” Calipari said. “But that ain’t going to happen this next year. Sorry. We can’t go two or three more years like it is. And if anybody says, ‘Well, they say that every year,’ there is a tipping point. I wouldn’t be surprised if the donors finally say, ‘I’m done. I’m not doing this anymore.’ Well, they won’t. A guy is a billionaire or worth half a billion because he makes good decisions. That’s why he’s that. “And you know what? He probably got grandkids, great grandkids and he’s like, ‘I’m just giving this for what? What is this?’ And then the kid got hurt, and then transferred. I paid him all this money. He got hurt, did not play and then left, and left with the money. I mean, we’re getting to that point.”

articles.title: Phillies legend Larry Christenson passes away at 72
articles.summary: Former Philadelphia Phillies pitcher Larry Christenson, also known as L.C., died unexpectedly Friday at age 72 while on a fishing trip with family and friends in Washington, the team announced, having spent his entire 11-year Major League career with the organization. A native of Everett, Washing
articles._body: Former Philadelphia Phillies pitcher Larry Christenson, also known as L.C., died unexpectedly Friday at age 72 while on a fishing trip with family and friends in Washington, the team announced, having spent his entire 11-year Major League career with the organization. A native of Everett, Washington, Christenson was selected by Philadelphia with the No. 3 overall pick in the 1972 MLB Draft out of Marysville High School. He reached the majors at just 19 years old and remained with the Phillies from 1973 through 1983, making 220 starts, the ninth-most in franchise history. Christenson finished his career with an 83-71 record and a 3.79 ERA. He became an important member of Philadelphia’s rotation during the club’s run of three consecutive National League East titles from 1976 through 1978. During those three seasons, he went 45-28 with a 3.65 ERA across 616 innings. His best season came in 1977, when he won a career-high 19 games. He also surpassed 200 innings in 1977, 1978 and 1982. In 1980, Christenson was part of the first Phillies team to win the World Series. Although injuries limited him to 14 starts that season, he went 5-1. His best postseason outing came in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series against the Houston Astros, when he threw six scoreless innings in a game Philadelphia eventually lost 1-0 in extra innings. Injuries, particularly problems involving his right elbow that required multiple surgeries, eventually shortened his career. His final MLB season came in 1983, when the Phillies won the National League pennant before falling to the Baltimore Orioles in the World Series. Christenson also produced one of the more unusual offensive performances by a Phillies pitcher. On Sept. 5, 1976, he hit two home runs while pitching 8⅓ innings and allowing one run in a 3-1 win over the New York Mets. He was also the starting pitcher when Philadelphia debuted its burgundy “Saturday Night Special” uniforms on May 19, 1979. The Phillies lost 10-5 to Montreal, with Christenson taking the loss, and the uniforms were not used again that season. He later wore the jersey when introduced after the final game at Veterans Stadium in 2003. After retiring, Christenson settled in the Philadelphia area, became successful in business and supported local charitable causes, including Phillies Charities, Inc. He was also included on a list of notable Phillies who never appeared in an All-Star Game. The post Phillies legend Larry Christenson passes away at 72 appeared first on ClutchPoints .

No. 3 Kentucky VB overwhelming in home opener, earns sweep over Utah State
articles.summary: Kentucky volleyball dominates Utah State in its home opener, sweeping the Aggies as everything goes right for the Cats.
articles._body: Under the familiar lights — and a brand-new 2025 runners-up banner — of the Historic Memorial Coliseum, No. 3 Kentucky volleyball dominated Utah State in a home-opener sweep (25-13, 25-14, 25-17) on Friday night. The Cats were impressive on both sides of the ball with a staggering 80.4 side-out percentage and a .436 hit percentage. Brooklyn DeLeye was all over the floor, leading the game in kills with 16, adding three aces and four digs. Lizzie Carr and Morgan Gaerte added nine and seven kills, respectively. “We knew we had a lot of work to get done,” remarked Carr on this week’s preparation for the Bluegrass Battle. “We went into this week with a new attitude…so we really focused on being able to show that each day.” Utah State had trouble getting anything going, finishing with a .117 hit percentage. Ava Nakai and Olivia Roy led the Aggies with six kills apiece, which would’ve placed fourth on the Cats. “We didn’t know a lot about Utah State, they haven’t played a match yet, so we really just focused on what was going to go on our side,” said Carr. “Sometimes you get thinking on what they’re gonna do, but we just focused on what we were going to do.” Kentucky started off overwhelming, flexing their height and power, getting blocks and spikes that the Aggies couldn’t keep up with. Then the Cats got crafty, floating balls into soft spots on the floor. This culminated in a .696 hit percentage in the first frame with zero errors. The three-headed monster of DeLeye (eight kills and an ace), Carr and Gaerte (seven kills combined) took the brunt of that, as the trio earned a .833 hit percentage. This offensive firepower, extreme efficiency and a near-100 side-out percentage led to a 25-13 dominating opening set. UK was slower to start in the second set and jumped to a 9-6 lead. They then embarked on a 5-0 run sparked by a Kassie O’Brien no-look kill and capped off by a kill from the sky-high Lizzie Carr, with her neck over the net. O’Brien finished the match with 33 assists and three crafty kills that preserved Kentucky’s momentum. DeLeye then stepped up to the plate, serving back-to-back aces as the Cats cruised to a 25-14 second set victory. With fatigue setting in for the Cats, the final frame started out competitive with a 3-3 tie. UK and Utah State would trade runs, as Kentucky would seem to pull away and the Aggies would claw back to make the game competitive. The Cats closed it out with an 8-1 run in the final stretch, including three DeLeye kills in this span, to complete the sweep with a 25-17 set victory. Before the game, Kentucky unveiled its 2025 National Runners-Up banner. “I think you play to the effort you give,” said head coach Craig Skinner. “If you’re giving the effort…it typically gives you return in the end.” The Cats resume with a Saturday evening match-up against South Florida, on Aug. 29 at 6 p.m.

Breaking down the 2026 Stanford Women’s Volleyball schedule
articles.summary: Stanford women’s volleyball enters the 2026 season ranked No. 5 in the nation, coming off a season in which they went 29-5 overall and 18-2 in the ACC, tying with Pittsburgh for the league championship.
articles._body: Credit: Al Chang/ISI Photos Stanford women’s volleyball enters the 2026 season ranked No. 5 in the nation, coming off a season in which they went 29-5 overall and 18-2 in the ACC, tying with Pittsburgh for the league championship. Stanford is picked by the coaches to win the ACC. Head coach Kevin Hambly is entering his 10th season at the helm. Jordyn Harvey is entering her senior year for the Cardinal, coming off a season in which she averaged 2.40 kills per set. Redshirt juniors/seniors Julia Blyashov (3.07 kills) and Ipar Kurt (2.57 kills per set) also look to be major factors out on the pin positions. Junior middle blocker Lizzy Andrew (2.42 kills) projects to be a force in the middle. They are set to begin their season this week, which means it is time to break down their schedule. Let’s get after it! GoStanford.com: Stanford Women’s Volleyball 2026 schedule Stanford’s opening match will be on Friday, August 28 th at 6:00 PM PT in Pittsburgh against No. 6 Wisconsin. The match will air on ESPN2. Stanford fell to Wisconsin in the Sweet Sixteen last year in Austin, Texas. So that makes this opening match a bit more interesting. It’s a very different looking Wisconsin team with their top players from last year having graduated, so in that sense, there really isn’t much carryover from last year. Regardless of what happened last year, what is true is Wisconsin is ranked No. 6 and expected to be a force this season. This will be a great opening test for the Cardinal. Stanford will stay in Pittsburgh for a match on Sunday, August 30 th against No. 15 Kansas. That will air on ESPN at 11:30 AM PT. Kansas went 24-11 overall and 13-5 in the Big XII, losing to No. 1 Nebraska in the Sweet Sixteen. The Jayhawks are led by junior pin Grace Nelson , who averaged 2.50 kills per set last season. This will be another good early test for Stanford. While they are ranked higher than Kansas, Stanford cannot take this match lightly. The Jayhawks should be fired up and eager to get a statement win of their own. Stanford will then have their home opener on Thursday, September 3 rd against South Florida at 7:00 PM PT on ACCNX. The Bulls lost in five sets to Eastern Kentucky in their opener on the road to start the season. They are coming off a season in which they went 17-13 overall and 12-4 in the American Conference. Stanford on paper ought to win this match. Especially with it being at home. Ideally, this match is a sweep. Stanford will want to send a message in this one. Stanford will then stay home to face Marquette on Sunday, September 6 th at 1:00 PM PT on ACCNX. Marquette is receiving votes in the AVCA Coaches Poll, coming off a season in which they went 18-11 overall and 11-5 in the Big East, losing to Louisville in the second round of the NCAA tournament. With this match being at Maples, this one Stanford has to get and should get, but the Golden Eagles should put up more of a fight than South Florida. At least on paper. As long as Stanford doesn’t get taken to a fifth set, they should be pleased with a victory. Stanford will then head to Florida to face No. 8 Texas A&M for an ACC/SEC Showdown match. That will be on Wednesday, September 9 th at 6:00 PM PT on ESPN2. Texas A&M are the defending national champions, going 29-4 overall and 14-1 in the SEC last season. They’ve also received one first place vote in the AVCA Coaches Poll. That said, they have fallen to No. 7 Louisville and No. 11 SMU already this season. They lost some key pieces from last season’s championship squad, so they clearly have some things to figure out. Still, the Aggies are expected to be really good this season and by the time Stanford faces them, they’ll have had a few matches under their belts. Stanford will then face No. 10 Penn State in Philadelphia on a neutral floor on Friday, September 11 th at 3:00 PM PT on Big Ten Network. The Nittany Lions are always a strong team and they are coming off a season in which they went 19-13 overall and 12-8 in the Big Ten, losing to Texas in the second round of the NCAA tournament. While this is technically a neutral site match, Penn State in many ways will have home court advantage since the match is being played in their home state. This will be a real test for the Cardinal. Stanford will stay in Pennsylvania for a third straight match on Sunday, September 13 th against Ohio at 10:00 AM PT. Ohio went 14-17 overall and 12-6 in the MAC last season. On paper, this should be a 3-0 sweep for Stanford. Stanford will then return to the West Coast but still be away from home as they’ll head to San Luis Obispo for three matches against Arizona State (Thursday, September 17 th ), Santa Clara (Friday, September 18 th ), and Cal Poly (Sunday, September 20 th ). Arizona State is ranked No. 12 in the nation while Cal Poly is receiving votes. Santa Clara is not receiving votes. Cal Poly went 27-8 overall and 14-4 in the Big West last season, losing in the Sweet Sixteen to Kentucky. Arizona State went 28-4 overall and 17-1 in the Big XII last season, losing to Creighton in the Sweet Sixteen. Santa Clara went 17-12 overall and 12-6 in the WCC, failing to make the NCAA Tournament. They did however end the regular season on back-to-back home sweeps over Washington State and Seattle, so that’s a feather in their cap. After these three matches in San Luis Obispo, Stanford will begin ACC play on the road at No. 11 SMU on Friday, September 25 th at 6:00 PM PT on ACCN. The Mustangs went 27-6 overall and 17-3 in the ACC last season, losing in the Sweet Sixteen to Purdue. This will be a legit opponent for Stanford to open up ACC play. Stanford will then stay on the road to face No. 4 Pittsburgh on Sunday, September 27 th at 5:30 PM PT on ESPN. As I mentioned earlier, Pitt shared the ACC title with Stanford last season, going 30-4 overall and 18-2 in the ACC, losing in the Final Four to Texas A&M, who went on to win the national title. Stanford will need to come to play in this one. Stanford will come

articles._body: The Pittsburgh Steelers still haven’t offered Joey Porter Jr. a contract extension . He wants a $33 million-per-year deal as he heads into the final year of his current contract. In July 2023, the Steelers signed Porter to a four-year $9.6 million deal as a rookie. On Friday, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler explained the predicament as a “classic stalemate” and laid out a few specifics, per SportsCenter. “This is a classic stalemate,” Fowler said. “I am told the player has not been happy with the way things have gone because they paid other players. They haven’t made him a formal offer that matches his skill set. It feels like he’s been a really good corner for them. It’s a situation where they want him to play out the contract essentially because they haven’t made him an offer. He hasn’t been practicing. He’s listed with a back injury, but really it’s about his contract as well. ” Then Fowler explains that this situation can go one of two ways. “Something’s going to have to give here. Do teams maybe call the Pittsburgh Steelers to see if he’s available?” Names to watch over the weekend and where things stand with Christian Gonzalez and Joey Porter Jr. @SportsCenter with @KevinNegandhi @itsthebaldgirl pic.twitter.com/vMQBfkog0q — Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) August 28, 2026 Other Pittsburgh players have received contract extensions. TE Darnell Washington signed a four-year $42 million contract extension in July. That same month, LB Nick Herbig signed a historic $100 million contract extension . DT Keeanu Benton signed a $72 million contract extension . In his rookie year, Porter played in 14 games and recorded 35 tackles, including 34 solo tackles. He also came away with one interception, 14 pass deflections, and one sack. Meanwhile, Porter has been out during training camp due to a back injury. He is on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list. The post Joey Porter Jr. contract situation labled a ‘classic stalemate’ by Insider appeared first on ClutchPoints .
