Jeremy Fowler delivers latest on Joey Porter Jr’s contract impasse: ‘Something’s gonna have to give’
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is heading into his fourth NFL campaign this season, all of which have come with the organization that drafted him in 2023. It marks the final year of his rookie contract, in which he will be earning a base salary of around $3.9 million. A contract exte
articles._body: Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is heading into his fourth NFL campaign this season, all of which have come with the organization that drafted him in 2023. It marks the final year of his rookie contract, in which he will be earning a base salary of around $3.9 million. A contract extension hasn’t come yet for the Penn State alum, and he’s let everyone know his feelings about it. “Definitely,” Porter said in June when asked if he deserves an extension. “I feel like I was the lead guy since I’ve been in this league, and I’m happy that I’m getting the respect that I feel like I’m owed.” Across three NFL seasons (47 games), Porter Jr. has accrued 165 tackles, 31 pass deflections, three interceptions, and one sack. While defensive players such as T.J. Watt , Nick Herbig , and Keeanu Benton have received extensions from the organization in the past year, Porter Jr. is still awaiting his turn. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler delivered the latest on Porter Jr.’s situation during Friday evening’s edition of ‘SportsCenter’. “This one is a classic stalemate,” Fowler said. “I’m told the player has not been happy with the way things have gone because they’ve paid other players. They haven’t made him a formal offer to measure with his skillset. He feels like he’s been a very good corner for them, and it’s a situation where they want him to play out the contract essentially. “He hasn’t been practicing. He’s listed with a back injury, but really, it’s about his contract as well. Something’s gonna have to give here. Do teams maybe call the Pittsburgh Steelers to see if he’s available?” Joey Porter Jr. heads into fourth season with Steelers Porter Jr. heads into the season on the PUP-P list with a back injury. The 2023 PWFA All-Rookie Team selection was present for some OTAs and mandatory minicamp this offseason, but did not participate in any drills. As Fowler noted, however, the contract impasse has also factored into this decision. “I learned this in my early years as a head coach: You have to separate the business and football,” Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said on Monday . “Sometimes it’s easier than others. This is a challenge for both Joey and us because we’re first-year staff. We’ve seen them play, compete against Joey. “I would love the opportunity to coach Joey Porter . I know our defensive guys would love the opportunity. So we’re at an impasse right here, and you’ve got to respect that. Every one of us has a contract. The organization, they have beliefs and so forth. But yeah, that’s just kind of where we are.” It remains up in the air whether or not Porter Jr. will receive an extension by the time Pittsburgh plays in its season opener against the Atlanta Falcons on Sept. 13.

articles.title: Matt Campbell brings Victory Day tradition to Penn State
articles.summary: Matt Campbell brought his Victory Day tradition to Penn State on Friday, giving children with disabilities and their families a special night at Beaver Stadium.
articles._body: The voice of a PA announcer boomed over the new Beaver Stadium sound system on picture-perfect Friday evening at Penn State. Welcoming dozens of children with disabilities and their families to the Penn State football experience, the first Victory Day had commenced. All of the Nittany Lions were there on the field, guiding drills and simulating goal-line plays leading to special touchdown celebrations. The cheerleaders and Blue Band were there, building the atmosphere around the special night. Calling it a great night for the Penn State football program, the community that surrounds it, and the kids and their families, new head coach Matt Campbell embraced all of it. “This world’s about giving back and making a difference,” Campbell said. “To be able to do that tonight, and be able to be with so many great families and young people that may never get the opportunity to play the game of football, it’s a special opportunity for us.” Buzzworthy: Penn State exits preseason camp with plenty of reasons for optimism Victory Day traces origins For Campbell and the Nittany Lions, it’s an opportunity born out of inspiration early in his career. Recounting the event’s genesis to reporters, he said a high school coaching colleague, Aaron Segedi, instituted a “Victory Day” as an opportunity to give back to his community. Inspired by the sentiment, Campbell organized a similar event for his Toledo football program and continued it at Iowa State. “I just felt if I could bring this to college football and teach our young guys the value of making a difference in our community, I thought it was really important,” said Campbell. “We talk a lot in our program right now about perspective. And I think it’s easy in our sport right now to lose perspective of what our responsibility is and the victories of what you see out here today.” Penn State QBs Rocco Becht, Alex Manske and Connor Barry Shared One Trait During Camp: Decisiveness Next steps for Penn State football That message carries particular importance for Campbell as he works to establish the culture and values he wants for the Penn State football program. Fresh off the grind and immense challenges of preseason camp, with Marshall game-week preparations beginning earlier in the day Friday and the season itself set to begin in just eight days, the event’s timing added to its potential impact. “Giving back, using your platform to make a difference in other people’s lives,” said Campbell. “You see their smiles, you see these parents; it just puts things into perspective before the chaos of a football season comes into play. “It’s why it’s so great to have it now. Right before you can get caught up in everything – and rightfully so in some ways. But the reality of it is, our responsibility is still to help teach young people how to be great 22, 23, 24-year-old men, and how to give back and use your platform to make a difference.” Ready for what’s next Pleased to see Penn State’s players embrace the opportunity, Campbell described them as engaged throughout the event. The shared experience, he said, could serve the Nittany Lions well in the weeks and months ahead. “Our kids did an unbelievable job tonight,” he said. “To know that no matter what storms we come into here together, man, you can lean back on nights like this and watch the service and the leadership of young men. “I think we’ll lean back on some of these moments in a positive way as you get ready for a college football season. You feel pretty good about the human beings and the leadership we have in our locker room.” New Penn State Rhoback is in. Use code “BWI20” for 20 percent off. articles._body: Four-star shooting guard Chase Lumpkin has narrowed his list of offers to six schools, he told Rivals. Moving forward, the 6-foot-4 rising senior out of McEachern (GA) will consider Alabama , Arkansas , Kentucky , Louisville , Michigan , and USC . To this point, Lumpkin has completed an official visit to Michigan and unofficially visited Alabama. He’s scheduled to take an official visit to USC this weekend, followed by an official visit to Alabama the weekend of September 19th. Lumpkin is ranked as the No. 30 overall recruit in the 2027 class and the No. 8 ranked point guard, according to the  Rivals Industry Ranking , an average of all three major recruiting media companies (Rivals, ESPN, 247Sports). [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] In addition to his finalists, he also received offers from Auburn, Georgia Tech, Florida State, Ole Miss, Georgia, Tennessee, Oregon, Providence, UCLA, Indiana, Miami, Iowa, Vanderbilt, UConn, and others. This summer on the Nike EYBL Circuit, Lumpkin averaged 17.3 points, 5.7 rebounds, 4.5 assists, and 2.2 steals per game for Jet Academy. He previously spoke with Rivals about what he’s looking for in a school. “I really need to go somewhere I can develop the most and get to the next level and become a pro player, where I’ve got belief in the coaching staff and they’ve got belief in me. I just want to get to the next level.” Scouting Lumpkin Rivals national recruiting analyst  Jamie Shaw  has evaluated Lumpkin multiple times in person this summer. Here is what he’s written about the highly regarded guard: “Lumpkin is very confident on the ball. He has good feet and solid positional size in the 6-foot-4 range. He shot the cover off the ball, stepping into shots and knocking down catch and shoots. Also showed passing acumen, delivering on target and on time as a primary initiator. Lumpkin played a streamlined and confident game. He got to spots and put consistent pressure on the opposing team. Lumpkin finished with 29 points and 8 assists on 8 of 15 shooting in the Jet Academy win. “Lumpkin was the breakout player of the weekend. The Jet Academy guard did a little bit of everything for his team, initiating offense, finishing plays, and generally creating advantages for his team. He showcased excellent vision on the ball, and he processed quickly and efficiently, whether that was getting the ball to his teammates or making shots on his own accord. Lumpkin got into the paint consistently, and he finished well at the rim.”

In addition to the YSL roster, the 41-track project also includes appearances from Lil Baby , Travis Scott , Future , Yeat , Trippie Redd , Cash Cobain , Veeze , Rob49 and more. articles.title: Ty Bryant and Jordan Castell are giving Kentucky’s new defensive staff an early edge
articles.summary: The experience of Kentucky's safety room has showed up.
articles._body: There are many unknowns about the Kentucky defense under new defensive coordinator Jay Bateman . What is known is what is at safety and how important that position group will be to this unit in 2026. New position coach Josh Christian-Young has inherited some known commodities in the SEC. Kentucky retained Ty Bryant after the new staff was hired and quickly got Florida transfer Jordan Castell committed when the transfer portal opened in January. That was all for a reason. This is your new starting safety tandem in Lexington. Bryant and Castell have combined to make 60 starts, play 3,384 defensive snaps, log 331 tackles, seven interceptions, and 15 pass breakups. UK needs this duo to form a strong team in the backend. Kentucky’s defense will need top-end safety play this season. That means getting consistent performances from both Bryant and Castell. This has occurred throughout the offseason and in fall camp. It’s making Christian-Young’s job as a coach easier. “I think Jordan’s over 2,000 snaps. I think Ty’s 1,500 snaps. Cyrus (Reyes) has played a lot in the SEC. And so when you have guys that have a lot of game day experience, you can’t replace that. That’s one of the No. 1 things that’s hard as a coach to simulate is game day experience,” Christian-Young told the media on Thursday. “And with those three guys kind of having that, it makes your life a little bit easier.” “I kind of feel like sometimes I’m coaching pros.” The two starting safeties have played enough football to qualify as pros. Bryant is expected to be one of the most impactful players on Kentucky’s football team this fall. Castell is entering his fourth-year as a starter in the SEC and brings stability to the lineup. Reyes in a Mississippi State transfer who has been a special teams stalwart in this league. Now the Texas native will get a chance to play some real snaps but it could be hard to bring Bryant and Castell off the field. The new starting duo has been working closely together ahead of the season. “Every time I see them together they’re always watching film..We game plan, we do stuff, then I’ll go use the restroom or something, and pop in, and they’re in there watching film together. I think that goes a long way,” Christian-Young said about Kentucky’s safety tandem. “One of Coach Stein’s big things is connection, right? It’s our No. 1 kind of DNA trait that we have and I think you kind of feel that throughout the room. Kentucky’s experience at safety as shown up throughout the offseason. It’s shown up in fall camp. Now the Cats need it to show up on game days.

articles._body: https://github.com/herd-core/herd Lately, I have been trying to understand the security aspect of docker containers, and what I have realized is that all docker containers share the host's kernel. Any zero day vulnerability in the kernel can be used to gain access to the host os. In order to deal with this, I did some research turns out Amazon has open sourced the core technology behind their serverless technology lambda. But in its current state its very hard to setup, let alone run anything securely. This technology is called firecracker microvm's It started off as a go library, for creating process pools to just do a simple firecracker spawn, turned into a full fledged host side daemon. deploying a microvm through a docker image is now as simple as running `herd deploy --image postgres:latest -p 5432:5432 -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres` with boot times ~500ms PS - I recently lost access to `Greptile` free code review for OSS projects, my repo stars (38) Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49485801 Points: 2 # Comments: 0

articles._body: One of the biggest offseason transfers in all of high school football saw five-star quarterback Trae Taylor make the move to Millard South (Neb.) for his senior season. The Patriots began their 2026 season on Friday night in a big rivalry tilt at home vs. Millard North . Taylor broke the ice at the end of the first quarter. The future Nebraska Cornhusker barged his way into the end zone on a goal line sneak for the first touchdown of the night: 0:58 1Q | South 7, North 0 After throwing an INT on the second South drive, Nebraska QB commit Trae Taylor scores his first high school touchdown on Nebraska soil. pic.twitter.com/QgleU9yZGf — Bobby Schneider (@Bobby_Schneid) August 29, 2026 As a junior for Carmel Catholic (Ill.), Taylor had a great season, throwing for more than 3,500 yards and 38 touchdowns to just three interceptions. He rushed for another 12 scores and had more than 600 yards on the ground. The longtime Nebraska commit plans to enroll early in Lincoln next year, so he and his camp opted to move to the Husker State early to be closer to the Big Ten program. That led him to Millard South, which enters the year as the No. 1 team in the state and No. 41 team nationally, per the Rivals Composite Rankings. The Patriots won a state title last season and were guided by Rivals five-star QB Jett Thomalla , who has since signed with Alabama. Taylor now has the reins and he wants to get his new team back to the top of the mountain this year. “I want to go to a school where I can still be developed at the high school level. Having a bunch of coaches that played college ball is huge to me,” Taylor told Rivals back in January when he revealed his intentions to transfer. “Also they kinda play a national schedule at the beginning of the season. It’s also a place that knows how to handle a high profile QB. My senior year where ever I go I want it to be fun and be one of the guys like at Carmel. This group of guys just had Jett there. So me being there won’t be a big deal to anyone in that community.” Before arriving at Millard South, Taylor went out to Los Angeles to compete in the illustrious Elite 11 Finals. He was named Rivals’ MVP of the event. Last month, he received his fifth star in the updated Rivals300 rankings, jumping from No. 71 to No. 17 overall. Taylor was also named a Preseason High School All-American by Rivals’ Andy Villamarzo earlier this month. Cardi B Says ‘AH HA’ Music Video Cost More Than $1M, Claims She Was ‘Overcharged’ by NYPD for Permits: ‘They Was Doing Too Much’
articles.summary: Cardi shot the twerk-filled visual in Brooklyn.
articles._body: Cardi B took it to the streets of NYC for the gritty “AH HA” music video , but it cost more than she anticipated, as Cardi revealed the total price tag for shooting the visual was north of $1 million. The Grammy-winning rapper hopped on Spaces on Thursday (Aug. 27), where Cardi detailed the exhausting process of getting permits in NYC and working with the NYPD, who she feels overcharged her throughout shooting the video because of her A-list celebrity status. Related Cardi B Twerks Her Way Across Brooklyn — Hitting the Stoop, the Salon and the Street in Flashy ‘AH HA’ Video: Watch Nashville Airport to Be Renamed for Dolly Parton, Tennessee Governor Announces Juanes, Alejandro Sanz & More Launch Marea Viva to Rebuild Chocó After Earthquake & More Uplifting Moments “I don’t understand how the f— this music video was expensive. I swear to God, I wanted this music video to be simple. I wanted a very street New York summer vibe,” she said. “A lot of artists do videos in the streets, that this video would be about $250,000. Bro, this video came out to be over a million.” Cardi explained that she originally wanted to shoot the visual in her home borough of the Bronx, but ultimately was steered toward Sunset Park in Brooklyn. “If you look at the video, it doesn’t even give that. Because I’m Cardi B, I be getting overcharged. To get permits, I know for a fact the average rapper that do music videos on blocks, it doesn’t cost that much. I really wanted to do my music video in a small block in the Bronx,” she added. “No, they made me do it in different places.” Cardi continued: “To get permits, it was so expensive. I feel like they overcharged me for permits. They made it a big deal because I guess I’m Cardi B. It was about 40 NYPD cops, which made it impossible to motherf—ing shoot. NYPD was being so… They was just doing too much.” The 33-year-old claimed this will be the last time she does a video shoot with fans being able to watch from a distance due to it being an open set, as she gets nervous with hundreds of onlookers. “This will be the last time I ever do music videos in a public setting that I cannot get control. I was so overstimulated, I was so underwhelmed,” she said. “I did not enjoy doing this music video. … I’m not doing music videos in open settings ever again.” “AH HA” served as Cardi’s first single of 2026, which arrived on July 31, while the music video was released nearly a month later on Friday (Aug. 28). The DJ SqanQo-produced hit debuted at No. 25 on the Billboard Hot 100 and currently sits at No. 40 on this week’s chart.

articles.title: The Strait of Hormuz crisis threatened Asia’s oil and gas lifeline. Here’s how the region is rewriting its energy playbook
articles.summary: “Notwithstanding the rise of alternative and green technologies over the past decade, the global economy is still very reliant on oil and gas."
articles._body: The Iran war exposed just how much the world relied on a narrow 20-mile-wide waterway . Soon after the U.S. launched strikes on Iran, the latter threatened to strike ships trying to traverse the Strait of Hormuz, the channel for much of the Middle East’s oil and gas exports. The threat of shortages pushed countries across Asia to impose export bans, cut import duties, and start rationing fuel to maintain supplies. Six months since the onset of the war, doomsday scenarios —price spikes, long lines at gas stations, power outages, and grounded flights—haven’t quite come to fruition, as increased production and hefty stockpiles blunted some of the damage. It seems that normality, in some form, could be returning to the Strait. On Wednesday, Iran announced a new revenue-sharing agreement over the waterway, though a military spokesperson blamed the U.S. for “obstructing this process.” Yet the revelation of how easy it was for Iran to block, and continue blocking, one of the world’s most important waterways is pushing governments to diversify their sources of energy. And now, with the prospect of a U.S.-Iran deal in the near-term on life support and Iranian control of Hormuz now looking secure for years to come, what previously saved the global oil market in the first half of the year might not work for a second time. “Global oil and gas supply is still a major point of geopolitical leverage,” says Saul Kavonic, head of energy research at MST Financial. “Notwithstanding the rise of alternative and green technologies over the past decade, the global economy is still very reliant on oil and gas.” “Hostile actors can threaten that for their geopolitical ends.” A ‘big wake up call’ Before the war, roughly a fifth of the world’s oil trade passed through the Strait of Hormuz, which sits between Iran and Oman. More than 80% of that cargo was bound for Asia, primarily China, India, Japan, and South Korea. “Before this crisis many market observers would have told you it would be impossible to block or completely close the Strait of Hormuz, because a country like Iran did not have the capabilities. They tried in the 1980s, but they did not succeed,” says Carole Nakhle, CEO at Crystol Energy, an energy consultancy. Yet the conflict has shown “how easy and inexpensive it has become to threaten very expensive energy infrastructure,” she added, with relatively cheap drones capable of putting refineries, pipelines, ports, and other multibillion-dollar facilities at risk. “This has been the big wake-up call for the entire global energy industry. It’s a fundamental paradigm shift of the last 50 years of the energy industry,” says Kavonic. “We’re moving from just-in-time supply chains to just-in-case supply chains.” Energy importers are starting to diversify. Before the war, the Middle East accounted for 90% of Japan’s crude oil imports, and roughly 11% of its liquefied natural gas. “Japan found it was more vulnerable than expected , particularly when it comes to LNG—it imports 100% of its energy,” says Kavonic. “In Japan, if the LNG doesn’t arrive, the lights go off and the country shuts down.” Now, Tokyo is investing elsewhere to shore up future supplies. Japan’s Inpex, for example, formed a joint venture to expand its LNG investment in Australia’s Northern Territory. “It’s boomtime for Woodside and Chevron , two big LNG players who aren’t too concentrated in the Middle East. The oil majors are now also rapidly ramping up their investment in LNG,” Kavonic says, spotting an opportunity for buyers to diversify their sources of gas away from the Middle East. Exporters, too, are diversifying. For oil exporters, the major lesson has been the need to invest in alternate supply routes. That includes ploughing billions into building out ports in ports on both the western side of Saudi Arabia and the Gulf of Oman, effectively bypassing the strait entirely. Oil producers are also investing in pipelines , like Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline. If all these additional investments pan out, only 10% of the world’s oil will need to travel through the Strait of Hormuz, down from 20% before the war. Gas, far more than oil, could become the key energy commodity hurt by a prolonged closure of the Strait of Hormuz. While crude oil can be carried via pipeline–perhaps from oil producers in the Persian Gulf to ports on the western side of the Arabian Peninsula–gas can’t, meaning there are no alternative routes to get LNG to Asia if Hormuz is blocked. Qatar, one of the world’s leading producers of LNG, is trying to find some way to keep its export routes open, through diplomacy, finding new customers, and taking rare opportunities to get their product through Hormuz. It has also set up a fast recovery timeline so it can restart production once the strait reopens. Escaping an energy collapse Things didn’t collapse as analysts feared at the beginning of the conflict. In April, for example, the head of the International Energy Agency predicted that flights may soon need to be grounded in Europe due to jet fuel shortages. While oil prices did surge to as high as $126 per barrel, they didn’t hit the $150 to $200 a barrel level that some analysts feared. And while several Asian countries imposed emergency measures to conserve fuel, a lengthy and catastrophic shortage never materialized. “The global market is proving to be more resilient to major supply shocks than many thought,” Kavonic says. One reason was the sheer amount of oil sitting in reserve. The IEA mandates that its 32 member countries stockpile at least 90 days’ worth of oil; similar mandates for gas stockpiles were imposed after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. In March, the agency coordinated the release of 400 million barrels from these emergency oil stockpiles, the largest such intervention in its history.  Oil producers like the U.S., Saudi Arabia and the UAE also increased their production and carrying capacity. articles.summary: Kentucky introduced Will Stein as the Wildcats’ next head coach on Signing Day. However, a few days later, Kentucky did add a prolific pass-catcher who could make an impact
articles._body: Kentucky introduced Will Stein as the Wildcats’ next head coach on Signing Day. It’s safe to say he did not have much time to lock in a bunch of talented high school recruits from the 2026 class. However, a few days later, Kentucky did add a prolific pass-catcher who could make an impact for the Wildcats right away. Joe Sloan initially recruited Kenny Darby to play for him at LSU. When he became the Wildcats’ offensive coordinator, Darby decided to follow Sloan to Lexington. A four-star talent, the wide receiver was the No. 177 overall player in the Rivals Industry Rankings, immediately making him the top-ranked player in Kentucky’s high school class. The folks at 247 believe he has a bright future, naming Darby to their Preseason True Freshman All-American Team . “The explosive Darby is an elite separator who’s a threat to find the end zone any time the ball finds his hands,” writes Andrew Ivins . “The Wildcats are hoping for big things out of  Nic Anderson  after an injury-riddled 2025 season at LSU. Darby could give them quite the duo in Will Stein’s offense.’ During Darby’s junior season at Bossier City (La) Airline, he caught 100 passes for 1,764 yards and 24 touchdowns to lead the state of Louisiana in receiving. He followed that up with another productive senior campaign, tallying 83 receptions for 1,124 yards and eight touchdowns. Darby’s skills have been showcased throughout Kentucky football fall camp. Defenders highlighted his shiftiness, while wide receivers’ coach Joe Price III described him as “an electric player.” Aside from Anderson’s 2023 season at Oklahoma, the group of wide receivers Kenny Minchey will be targeting this fall is unproven. That’s giving this true freshman an opportunity to showcase his skills on Saturdays at Kroger Field. Darby in Luckett’s Scouting Notebook A record-setting receiver at Bossier City (La.) Airline, Darby led the state of Louisiana in receiving yards (1,754) as a junior. This was a highly productive wideout who scored over 30 total touchdowns with 180-plus receptions in his final two seasons of high school ball. The late recruiting win is a true generator with plus route-running skills. Darby touched the ball in numerous way and generated explosive play touchdowns as a senior on kickoff return and at tailback. On vertical concepts, this receiver is excellent at getting on the toes of cornerbacks and then snapping routes off to create easy separation. Shows the ability to run through contact as a tailback. Owns good awareness in space allowing blocks to to develop and feel when to change direction. There is a sizable catch radius on tape with good ball skills. This is a wide receiver with true inside-outside versatility with a tremendous YAC skill set who could provide value in the return game. A potential plug-and-play addition who could give the offense a spark in year one on schemed-up touches. Owns a high-ceiling as a receiver due to versatility and route-running potential.

articles.title: Dodgers’ Tarik Skubal gets emotional during pregame walk before Tigers clash
articles.summary: Tarik Skubal did not want to leave the Detroit Tigers. The Los Angeles Dodgers superstar pitcher was born in California and is obviously embracing the chance to compete for a championship on the most successful franchise of the 2020s, but he was passionate about playing the final year of his cont
articles._body: Tarik Skubal did not want to leave the Detroit Tigers. The Los Angeles Dodgers superstar pitcher was born in California and is obviously embracing the chance to compete for a championship on the most successful franchise of the 2020s, but he was passionate about playing the final year of his contract in the Motor City. He loved his first MLB home , and it showed on Friday night. Skubal wiped away tears and turned his head toward the big screen in Comerica Park, as the Tigers played a tribute video for his return to Detroit. The left-handed starter did not try to suppress his emotions before taking the mound. Instead, he acknowledged his former team by tapping his chest. It is obvious that Skubal left a huge chunk of his heart in this stadium. Dodgers’ ace Tarik Skubal emotional in his return to Detroit vs the Tigers (via @MLB ) pic.twitter.com/fg8GbBVzAo — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 28, 2026 Tigers fans had time to brace themselves for No. 29’s exit. They also knew that the loaded Dodgers were a likely landing spot. It still hurts to see him on the other side, though. The home crowd watched this ninth-round draft pick endure heartbreak and capture ecstasy during his near-six-year run with Detroit. Skubal overcome flexor tendon surgery, won back-to-back American League Cy Young Awards and a Pitching Triple Crown, and lifted the franchise to consecutive playoff appearances for the first time in more than a decade. He helped the Tigers return to relevance, even if it was rather brief, and the team and community extended him complete trust. That special relationship is on full display in this series opener . Tarik Skubal unsurprisingly looks quite comfortable in Comerica, but Detroit leads 1-0 nonetheless, at time of print. articles.title: Coundown to kickoff prediction series: South Carolina’s kicker battle will continue into the season before solidifying
articles.summary: Continuing the countdown to kickoff prediction series: South Carolina's kicker competition will continue into the 2026 season.
articles._body: In May, when the calendar revealed that it was 100 days until South Carolina kicked off the season, I posted a story on GamecockCentral entitled “100 predictions for the 2026 Gamecocks.” Now, that countdown is down to just eight days. The prediction paired with day eight read, “The placekicking competition between Kelley, Upton Bellenfant, Malik Orsan, and Mason Love will continue through the early portions of the season, with multiple players attempting field goals and PATs in September. One kicker will eventually claim the job, though, and he will perform well.” Let’s break down that prognostication. Have a question for the GamecockCentral staff? Ask it now on The Insiders Forum. The kicker room One of the major talking points for South Carolina football fans this offseason has been the uncertainty at placekicker. The Gamecocks have had two former walk-ons take the majority of the team’s PAT and field goal attempts the last two seasons, as Alex Herrera (2024) and William Joyce (2025) started. Both players are graduated now, and even with multiple scholarship kickers on the roster, things remain undecided at placekicker with just over a week until South Carolina’s first game of the 2026 campaign. Special teams coordinator Matthew Smiley made it clear that he would like to have a starter named before the opener. However, he said that a kicker doesn’t need long to mentally lock into that role. Smiley also implied that, although it is not ideal to try to work things out with game reps, the competition might not be over, even when a starter is potentially named next week. According to head coach Shane Beamer, starting punter Mason Love will not be the team’s placekicker. He will handle holder duties instead, per Smiley. That leaves returner Max Kelley — who was USC’s kickoff specialist as a true freshman in 2025 — and transfer portal additions Upton Bellenfant (Texas Tech) and Malik Orsan (Southeast Missouri State) vying for the gig. With uncertainty lingering this late into the process, it seems likely that the kicking battle will extend into the season. That isn’t ideal, but it also is not a death sentence. Back in 2022, Mitch Jeter barely won the battle, and he wasn’t solidified as “the guy” in the early weeks of the season. For those who remember, the North Carolina native went on to have a perfect season on field goal attempts. In 2017, Parker White actually lost the job to Alexander Woznick but got an opportunity several weeks in; he never relinquished the job from that point on and became the program’s all-time leading scorer. No one should disparage fans who have some anxiety about the kicking game. However, things could still play out well in time. What does this mean for the Gamecocks? Fellow subscribers are discussing it now on The Insiders Forum. South Carolina needs more Let’s be clear about something: both Alex Herrera and William Joyce were fine as South Carolina’s kickers in 2024 and 2025. However, the former walk-ons were limited. They combined to go 27-for-36 on field goal attempts, which is not a bad number in a vacuum. Neither Herrera nor Joyce had a particularly strong leg. Neither player made a kick longer than 49 yards, and that limited the offense’s scoring opportunities. In fact, Herrera only attempted one long field goal; Joyce tried none. Punter Mason Love tried the only 50-yard attempt of the last two years, a 53-yard miss in 2025. Against Alabama, Carolina went for it on 4th-and-12 in the first half instead of trying a 52-yard field goal. Solid efficiency is a good thing, and Herrera and Joyce provided that. However, South Carolina needs some more range from their placekicker this fall. The flexibility to feel pretty good about a 50-yard field goal attempt is something the Gamecocks haven’t had. Whoever wins the kicking job — whether it’s before opening kickoff or several weeks into the season — will have to provide a little more for South Carolina. If that happens, it will only help the Gamecocks’ pursuit of putting points on the board. What’s your prediction? Share it with fellow subscribers on The Insiders Forum.

articles.summary: The Denver Nuggets on Friday waived Julian Reese after acquiring the 6-foot-9 forward/center from the Washington Wizards in the Peyton Watson sign-and-trade. The move, confirmed by NBA.com’s transaction log, had already been expected when Reese was included in the deal. Reese was traded to
articles._body: The Denver Nuggets on Friday waived Julian Reese after acquiring the 6-foot-9 forward/center from the Washington Wizards in the Peyton Watson sign-and-trade. The move, confirmed by NBA.com’s transaction log, had already been expected when Reese was included in the deal. Reese was traded to Denver on August 20, 2026, after spending the previous season with Washington on a two-way contract. The Nuggets were able to take on his two-way deal even after being above the NBA’s second tax apron because players on two-way contracts do not count against the salary cap. The 23-year-old went undrafted in the 2025 NBA Draft after playing four seasons at Maryland. He joined the Los Angeles Lakers for the 2025 Summer League before signing an Exhibit 10 contract with the Toronto Raptors on October 17, 2025. He later joined the Wizards, signing a two-way contract on February 28, 2026. Reese made his NBA debut two days later against the Houston Rockets, starting at center because Washington’s other big men were unavailable due to injuries. He finished that game with two points, four rebounds and three steals while shooting 1-for-3, committing three turnovers and fouling out in nearly 28 minutes. His best performances came in March. On March 5, Reese recorded 18 points and 20 rebounds, including 10 offensive and 10 defensive boards, in a 122-112 loss to the Utah Jazz. That made him the first Wizards player since Antawn Jamison in 2010 to collect at least 10 offensive and 10 defensive rebounds in the same game . On March 25, he produced another double-double with 26 points and 17 rebounds, along with one steal and one block, during a 133-110 win over the Jazz. Across 13 NBA games last season, Reese averaged 11.8 points, 10.5 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 1.4 steals in 30.9 minutes, starting 10 times. He also appeared in 41 G League games, averaging 8.7 points, 7.4 rebounds and 1.0 block in 18.3 minutes. With Reese now waived, Denver has one open two-way roster spot. KJ Simpson and 2026 second-round pick Bryce Hopkins currently occupy the Nuggets’ other two-way slots. articles.title: Amid high gas prices and shrinking crude stockpile, Trump says U.S. to take control of 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil reserves
articles.summary: Venezuela has one of the largest oil reserves in the world, with an estimated 303 billion barrels of crude oil in the ground.
articles._body: President Donald Trump on Friday said the U.S. has entered an agreement with Venezuela to take control of 65 billion barrels of the South American country’s oil reserves. Trump in a social media post announced the agreement he said was negotiated by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Venezuela’s interim President Delcy Rodriguez. “The United States of America has just entered into an Agreement with the Country of Venezuela on, THE BIGGEST OIL DEAL IN WORLD HISTORY!” Trump wrote. The announcement of the deal comes nearly nine months after the U.S. military at Trump’s direction carried out an operation to  capture Venezuela’s president Nicolás Maduro  and spirit him to the United States to face federal narcoterrorism and drug trafficking charges. Trump faces mounting pressure to address high gas prices as  the war in Iran  reaches a six-month milestone with no conclusion in sight. The U.S. has tapped its strategic petroleum reserves, which in early August fell below 300 million barrels, down by more than 100 million barrels since the start of 2026. In the days following Maduro’s ouster in January, Trump floated the idea of U.S. oil companies returning to  Venezuela to tap its oil reserves . Trump has argued that Venezuela stole U.S. oil when former Venezuelan President Hugo Chavez’s moved decades ago to nationalize hundreds of foreign-owned assets, including those owned by American oil companies. Venezuela has one of the largest oil reserves in the world, with an estimated 303 billion barrels of crude oil in the ground. That’s about 17% of the world’s supply, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration. Unlike other parts of the world, where geologists have to search for untapped oil, the reserves under Venezuela’s soil are largely mapped and known, experts say. But because of dilapidated infrastructure, the country only produces about 1% of the world’s oil. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: 3 young Thunder players most likely to emerge in 2026-27
articles.summary: Only the Oklahoma City Thunder could trade three rotation players, including a veteran starter, in exchange for draft capital and still be considered the deepest team in the NBA. Amidst the many Thunder storylines to follow in 2026-27, which young player, including rookie Aday Mara, has the best
articles._body: Only the Oklahoma City Thunder could trade three rotation players, including a veteran starter, in exchange for draft capital and still be considered the deepest team in the NBA. Amidst the many Thunder storylines to follow in 2026-27 , which young player, including rookie Aday Mara, has the best possibility to emerge as an X-factor for the 2025 champion’s next chapter will be an intriguing development in Oklahoma City. Last season didn’t go as planned. All-NBA forward Jalen Williams battled injuries through the Western Conference Finals. Ajay Mitchell returned for the first three matchups of the Thunder’s best-of-7 series against the San Antonio Spurs, but missed the last four. Both sat for Game 7, where the Spurs crushed the defending champions’ plans to repeat in a series-clinching 111-103 win. But none of it deterred Thunder GM Sam Presti from splitting his core. Upon All-Star Chet Holmgren and Williams’ max deals kicking in, Presti traded Isaiah Joe, Aaron Wiggins, and Lu Dort without blinking, saving a combined $224 million in payroll and luxury tax. Plus, Holmgren should return in 2026-27 with vengeance to make up for his four-point dud against the Spurs with the Thunder’s season on the line. Mitchell and All-Defensive Second Team guard Cason Wallace will step into increased roles to make up for the loss of Dort. Ahead of his first full season with the Thunder, Jared McCain is a perfect replacement for Joe, but losing Wiggins could open up an opportunity for one Thunder prospect to potentially earn meaningful playing time. Sure, Jaylin Williams will reprise his back-up role behind Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein. And Alex Caruso and Kenrich Williams can undoubtedly fill in the blanks at the wing and backcourt positions. However, injuries have impacted the Thunder in one way or another over the years, and if OKC were to get bit by the injury bug once more this upcoming season, here are three prospects Thunder head coach Mark Daigneault could wind up leaning on in 2026-27. Aday Mara’s promising two-way game ahead of Thunder rookie season The Thunder’s 12th overall pick in this year’s draft demonstrated his dynamic blend as a 7-foot-3 scoring center with great hands and rim protection. Aday Mara’s passing, coupled with his defense and ability to clean the glass, makes for an ideal backup center of the future. While the projections painting Mara as the Victor Wembanyama stopper are premature, Mara has the potential to make his presence felt immediately. Out of all the Thunder prospects, he has the best chances of earning valuable minutes this upcoming season. Mara averaged 9.2 points, 7.0 rebounds, and 1.8 blocks in five games during summer league. He certainly beat the eye test as a promising center who’s still raw, but could catch on soon as he adapts to the NBA. Thunder’s young players, such as Aday Mara, showed off nifty passes, showcasing their talents as distributors who can read opposing defenses. The tallest first-round pick since the Grizzlies’ 2024 ninth-overall pick in Zach Edey showed off his accuracy from a unique vantage point on the floor. Could he steal some of Jaylin Williams minutes as the Thunder’s second-unit anchor in the frontcourt? Possibly. After recovering from a torn ACL prior to a testicular cancer diagnosis in 2025, Topic experienced yet another setback this summer. He underwent a minimally invasive lower back procedure that ruled him out of summer league after making his NBA debut in 2025-26. But Topic showed some promise in his rookie season as a facilitating point guard who isn’t afraid to attack the rim. Topic, selected 12th overall in 2024, was the first of four Thunder first-round picks in three years, including 2025’s Thomas Sorber and 2026’s Aday Mara and Bennett Stirtz, a sharpshooting guard who was selected 16th overall. Given the team’s depth and their recent picks, the Thunder will soon learn which young players stand out most , as ESPN’s Ben Golliver noted. “After the Thunder felt compelled by financial reasons to trade away some of their depth this summer — losing Dort, Wiggins and Joe in the process — they’ll be a bit more reliant on the youngsters to help them get through next season. To be clear, Oklahoma City would still rank among the title favorites even if none of these four recent first-round picks plays a single playoff minute; the Thunder still go 10-deep in quality players without them,” Golliver said. “But the Thunder would surely like to see meaningful youth development to help in both the short term — to keep those 10 established contributors fresh in the regular season — and the long term — when a further financial crunch will likely strip away even more depth. Topic averaged 5.2 points and 4.4 assists in 10 outings last season. The Thunder should have a better idea of where Topic stands after training camp. Although the NIL has been in place since 2021, schools around the nation for all sports are still in the Wild West
articles._body: It feels like every sport at the college level has gone through significant rule changes in recent years, as the NCAA is still seemingly navigating the NIL and transfer portal eras. Although the NIL has been in place since 2021, schools around the nation for all sports are still in the Wild West when it comes to managing players’ eligibility. On Friday, it was revealed that Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry is seemingly fed up with it all. Reports indicate that Landry informed ESPN that college sports are a complete mess and he’s ready for the U.S. Senate to step in , according to Pete Thamel of ESPN. Landry claimed that President Donald Trump and former Alabama Crimson Tide head coach Nick Saban were right to criticize the current state of the NCAA, as the rules have become confusing and jumbled. “I’ve been saying for a year that college sports need to be fixed,” Landry said to ESPN. “President Trump and Saban were right. The rules keep changing, and at this point, no one even knows what the actual rules are. The U.S. Senate needs to step up and fix this. The U.S. Senate needs to quit politicking and start working!” The latest drama in the NCAA came to fruition after the LSU Tigers attempted to sign two players who had previously declared for the 2026 NFL Draft. Although both players went undrafted, they did participate in training camps and were both eventually cut. The Big Ten and SEC announced on the same day that players who have previously worked with professional teams in any sport are not allowed to return to any school within their conferences. Other conferences followed suit, while others are reportedly expected to come to a similar conclusion. While the Louisiana Governor and many others hope for more clarity from the NCAA, college sports fans can look forward to the new football season. Week 0 kicks off on Saturday, August 29. Cale Makar’s Record Contract Marks Fourth Landmark NHL Deal in 11 Months
articles.summary: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images
articles._body: The NHL has its first $20 million man. Friday, the Avalanche announced an eight-year, $163.2 million contract extension with Cale Makar. The average annual value comes in at $20.4 million, handing the 27-year-old star defenseman the highest AAV in league history. It’s just below the league maximum at $20.8M, and the total contract, beginning for the 2027–28 season, is the largest in NHL history. Makar’s landmark agreement comes just a month after Sharks center Macklin Celebrini set a new high-water mark at $18.8 million AAV as part of a five-year, $94 million deal. Though bigger, Makar’s deal similarly contains eye-popping signing bonuses: In the final year, at age 36, Makar will be guaranteed a whopping $18.8 million. The highest NHL AAV has now been smashed four times throughout the past year—and three times this summer alone. In September 2025, Wild forward Kirill Kaprizov signed a then-record $136 million, eight-year extension at $17 million AAV, resetting the market for the league’s stars. In July, offer-sheet drama surrounding Leo Carlsson pushed the Ducks to sign the center to a five-year, $90 million deal with an $18 million AAV. But just weeks later, Celebrini agreed to his contract, and Makar knocked him off less than a month after that. Makar is the only defenseman of the four. Along with setting a new high bar in the sport, his deal also ratchets up the market for the NHL’s other top defensemen, whose new contracts are imminent: particularly Quinn Hughes, who was moved to Minnesota in a blockbuster trade last season; and Matthew Schaefer of the Islanders , who is coming off of a Calder Trophy–winning season during which he banked rookie records. Colorado snuck in the eight-year agreement before the NHL’s new CBA kicks in. Beginning Sept. 16, max-term contracts shorten by a year: seven for a player signing with his current team, and six for free agents. Under the new CBA, the salary cap will spike for the next several years, which may make max-term deals like Makar’s increasingly unusual as players sign shorter deals for a potentially bigger payday down the line. With Dolly on our hearts. @MT_FB will wear a commemorative jersey to honor Dolly Parton during its home opener against Murray State on 9/5. #TrueBlue pic.twitter.com/ZyGJblOy18 — Middle Tennessee Athletics (@MTAthletics) August 28, 2026 “Coach Derek Mason and I were talking about how we can honor one of the great Tennesseans and one of the greatest people in the world,” Massaro in a statement . “The football team is honored to wear this for our home opener.” The tributes poured in for Parton after her death earlier this week. articles.title: Why the Cubs are in serious trouble in NL Central after losing to Reds on Friday
articles.summary: The Chicago Cubs have been one of the streakiest teams in Major League Baseball this season. The Cubs have been riding the power bats of Pete Crow-Armstrong and Seiya Suzuki to make noise in the National League and attempt to challenge the Milwaukee Brewers for National League Central superiority
articles._body: The Chicago Cubs have been one of the streakiest teams in Major League Baseball this season. The Cubs have been riding the power bats of Pete Crow-Armstrong and Seiya Suzuki to make noise in the National League and attempt to challenge the Milwaukee Brewers for National League Central superiority. However, the Cubs have dropped three painful games in a row and manager Craig Counsell could see his team fall 8.0 games behind the Brewers if Milwaukee is victorious against the Texas Rangers Friday night. Chicago’s latest loss was a 10-8 defeat to the Cincinnati Reds as the Cubs returned home to Wrigley Field to take on the last place team in the NL Central. While the Cubs offense responded with six extra-base hits, including home runs by Michael Busch and Pedro Ramirez, the pitching fell apart in the middle innings and allowed the Reds to score 5 runs in the sixth inning. The Reds blasted four home runs to gain the edge on the Cubs. Chicago reliever Trent Thornton was victimized in the sixth inning as he gave up 5 runs, all of them earned, and he allowed 2 home runs. The Cubs have lost 6 of their last eight games. After dropping the series finale to the cross-town Chicago White Sox, the Cubs lost 2 of 3 games to the Seattle Mariners. They closed that series with a 19-2 triumph and followed that with a series-opening 7-0 victory against the Diamondbacks. However, they dropped the last two games to the Diamondbacks. Pete Crow-Armstrong is battling for the NL MVP award and has hammered 33 home runs. Ian Happ has contributed 23 long balls and Seiya Suzuki has blasted 22 homers. Nevertheless, the Cubs are struggling to win and the Central Division crown appears to be out of their reach. articles._body: For one day, LeBron James gladly surrendered the spotlight. Savannah James turned 40 on Thursday, August 27, and her husband welcomed the milestone with the kind of enthusiasm usually reserved for a championship celebration, Complex reports. LeBron posted an affectionate Instagram tribute that made his excitement impossible to miss. “HAPPY BIRTHDAY MY QUEEN!!! WE ALL ARE READY TO CELEBRATE YOU!! ESPECIALLY ME!” he wrote. “YOU’RE DESERVING OF ALL THE LOVE & VIBEZ YOU’LL RECEIVE TODAY & BEYOND!!” The photo captured the couple walking hand in hand into an event. Savannah commanded attention in a fitted black dress finished with feathers along the hem, while LeBron complemented her look in a black suit and sunglasses. He completed the message by declaring his endless love for Savannah and announcing that he felt ready to begin the festivities. View this post on Instagram Savannah James Previously Defended LeBron LeBron’s celebration arrived only weeks after Savannah addressed the cottage industry surrounding criticism of her husband. During a July installment of “Everybody’s Crazy,” Savannah and co-host April McDaniel discussed the backlash connected to LeBron ending his eight-season tenure with the Los Angeles Lakers. McDaniel noted how much negativity follows a public figure at his level. Savannah responded with a blunt assessment of the people who continually analyze his every move. “It’s crazy,” Savannah said. “People have definitely made careers out of talking about [LeBron].” That observation carried weight coming from someone who has experienced intense public attention alongside him. Yet Savannah’s birthday tribute showed another side of that visibility. Instead of answering critics or fueling another basketball debate, LeBron used his enormous platform to celebrate the woman he calls his queen. After more than 20 years as a magnet for headlines, he knew exactly when to step aside and let Savannah own the moment. articles.title: Show HN: Darwin-VM – run the latest iOS and macOS in QEMU
articles.summary: For the past few months, I've been building support for running the latest SPTM-based versions of iOS and macOS into qemu. The idea is to create a lightweight barebones environment for playing around with / debugging XNU and low-level Darwin internals, kind of like a tiny busybox Linux system exc
articles._body: For the past few months, I've been building support for running the latest SPTM-based versions of iOS and macOS into qemu. The idea is to create a lightweight barebones environment for playing around with / debugging XNU and low-level Darwin internals, kind of like a tiny busybox Linux system except running Darwin, and using an emulated Apple Silicon CPU (custom instructions/ privilege levels and all). With darwin-vm, you can directly boot the system using just an iOS/ macOS kernel and minimal ramdisk; no gigantic 40GB macOS VM disk images or downloading 10GB+ IPSW files like you need to for regular macOS VMs. It also works for iOS! And of course, since this is a VM you can use a debugger to debug anything in the system: SPTM, TXM, XNU, all kexts, launchd, dyld, and all user programs can be modified/ patched/ debugged. You can also run your own custom programs inside the VM as root. Getting this to work required reverse engineering the SPTM boot protocol and implementing it in qemu, eg. how SPTM expects the trusted execution monitor, boot kernelcache, ramdisk, trustcache, device tree, boot args, etc. to be laid out in physmem. I also had to add support for Apple's GXF instructions and guarded exception levels, which are parallel privilege levels that live next to your classical EL2 and EL0, and are used by SPTM and TXM respectively. Not to mention all of the random undocumented system registers and device tree manipulation the system expects the bootloader to take care of, as well as getting MTE to work for the latest hardware. The darwin-vm repository contains scripts that automate downloading just the files you need from an iOS or macOS update file, installing a root shell daemon into the ramdisk, and signing a trustcache for you so you don't have to deal with/ care about any of that. The hope is it's as "plug and play" as possible: you give me an iOS/ macOS update file, I give you a root shell inside a VM running that OS. I've tested this booting the very latest iOS and macOS betas on virtual iPhone 17, 16, 15, 14, 13, and 12, as well as M1-M5 virtual Mac Minis and Macbook Airs. Since it's all Qemu TCG, you can run this anywhere Qemu runs; no need for an ARM host. You do need a Mac to set up the VM files though since the setup scripts mess around with APFS images and code signing. I also included instructions in the readme for how to customize the kernel/ swap in a development kernel from a Kernel Debug Kit and get symbolic kernel debugging working in the VM via lldb, as well as how to compile and run your own programs in your iOS or macOS VM. Let me know what you think! Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49485263 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

articles._body: It remains unclear when or if J.J. McCarthy will play quarterback again for the Minnesota Vikings, but fans know it will not be on Friday night . The No. 10 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft suffered a “minor ankle injury” in last Saturday’s game versus the Baltimore Ravens and is unavailable for the team’s preseason meeting with the Denver Broncos, per ESPN’s Kevin Seifert. McCarthy logged light practice sessions to begin the week but sat out on Wednesday. Regardless of the 23-year-old’s status with the Vikings, both in the short and long term, it would have been nice for him to have one last opportunity to showcase his skills before the regular season begins. Alas, the injury bug bites McCarthy yet again. The former Michigan standout and national champion missed his entire rookie year with a torn meniscus and endured multiple ailments last season. The results have left plenty to be desired when he has been on the field. McCarthy completed only 57.6 percent of his passes for 1,632 yards and 11 touchdowns while tossing 12 interceptions in 10 starts. He is now stuck behind Kyler Murray on the depth chart, and possibly Carson Wentz , leaving many to question if Minnesota will trade him. Apparently, that is not the plan right now . The Vikings still do not know if Murray can be a viable option for an extended period of time. They will want to see how the former No. 1 pick handles Kevin O’Connell’s offense in a legitimate game before discarding a third-year signal-caller who showed bursts of promise last year. An unhealthy J.J. McCarthy is of little use to the team, though. Hopefully, he can quickly recover and make himself available for Minnesota’s Sept. 13 season opener. The post Vikings’ J.J. While a move for Garver to the Yankees from the minor leagues never materialized, there is a chance that the catcher leaves the team without playing a game for them. According to Gary Phillips of The New York Daily News, Garver “has exercised an assignment clause in his deal,” meaning he could look for major league opportunities around if possible. “I’m told that catcher Mitch Garver, at Triple-A with the Yankees, has exercised an assignment clause in his deal. Today was his deadline to do so. That doesn’t mean he’ll automatically leave the org, but he can seek big league opportunities elsewhere,” Phillips wrote on X, formerly Twitter. Garver has been in the MLB since 2017, playing the first five seasons with the Minnesota Twins, then two years with the Texas Rangers, leading to his stint with the Seattle Mariners, starting in 2024, though he was released on Aug. 4. When initially picked up by the Yankees, manager Aaron Boone praised his experience. “He’s got a ton of experience, and he’s a guy that’s had a lot of success in the league,” Boone said at the time, via MLB.com. “We’re trying to add to our depth and protection. We’ll get him into our system and see where we can help him, see what he has. You never know.” At any rate, Garver wouldn’t log a single game for the Yankees, having been in the minor leagues, as it remains to be seen whether Garver stays with New York or goes elsewhere. articles.title: Jemma Amoore — Kenny Brooks’ ‘favorite Amoore’ — brings needed experience, leadership
articles.summary: Last season was Kenny Brooks' first time in five years without an Amoore on his roster. He made sure to fix that going into the 2026-27 campaign.
articles._body: Last season was Kenny Brooks ‘ first time in five years without an Amoore on his roster. He made sure to fix that going into the 2026-27 campaign. Georgia Amoore was a back-to-back All-American under Brooks, once at Virginia Tech and then again at Kentucky. An undersized point guard, Amoore started 155 games throughout her five-year college career, all of them coached by Brooks. They made a Final Four run together in 2023 and then won the ACC regular season title in 2024. In Lexington, they set the stage for the beginning of the Brooks era, which has gone as well as hoped through two seasons. But Amoore is now in the WNBA. She was the 6th overall pick in the 2025 Draft by the Washington Mystics and made her professional debut this year after spending last season recovering from a torn ACL. Brooks found success with All-SEC point guard Tonie Morgan replacing Amoore in 2025-26, but he missed the Australian flavor that Amoore brought to his programs. So Brooks went out and brought in Georgia’s sister, Jemma Amoore , through the transfer portal in the offseason. “She’s my favorite Amoore,” Brooks joked earlier this summer. “I’ve said that for years.” Jemma is a bit shorter at 5-foot-4 than her 5-foot-6 sister, but she’s a talented hooper in her own right. The younger Amoore began her college run at Sacramento State as a freshman before transferring to IU-Indianapolis as a sophomore, averaging 1.2 points in 6.2 minutes across 48 games played. She was mostly a depth piece at those spots — and that’s the role she’ll fill at Kentucky — but she brings more to the Wildcats than just on-court skills. “We wanted to fill our roster out,” Brooks said. “We want a little bit more experience in the backcourt. Somebody who has some leadership qualities. How much will she play? I don’t know. I don’t know, but I know she’s gonna make a tremendous impact on our program. She already has made a tremendous impact in our locker room.” Brooks credits Amoore for being able to quickly adapt to her surroundings. She’s a hard worker behind the scenes. Amoore was a team captain for her Australian team in Victoria during the 2022 and 2023 seasons, also earning the Ballarat Basketball GRIT award in 2021. Her sister was praised for having similar qualities — and yes, the two siblings look very much alike. “She has a great wit to her. She works extremely hard,” Brooks added. “But the one thing I will tell you, she is Jemma. She’s not Georgia. And I’ve made the mistake and I called her Georgia, and I will not lie, there are times out of the corner of my eye, I kind of flinch. I’m like, what the hell’s Georgia doing here? They look alike, they sound alike. Her accent’s a little bit thicker than Georgia’s.” Brooks doesn’t need Jemma to be as productive as Georgia. But he does need her to exude the same leadership qualities. Having been around Brooks’ programs through her sister for several years makes it so Jemma knows exactly what that requires. “She’s gonna make a huge impact on our team,” Brooks said of Jemma. “Whether it’s in the locker room or on the floor.” Subscribe to the KSR YouTube Channel for press conferences, interviews, original shows, fan features, and exclusive content.

articles.title: Lil Durk Trial Week 1 Recap: Flipped OTF Crew Member Calls Quando Rondo Shooting ‘Sloppy’
articles.summary: Billboard is running down the key moments from the first week of Durk's murder-for-hire trial.
articles._body: The first week of Lil Durk ’s murder-for-hire trial featured text messages, an unreleased music video and key testimony from a former member of the Chicago rapper’s Only the Family (OTF) crew. You’re reading Billboard ’s weekly Lil Durk trial recap, a one-sheet breakdown of everything that happened in the murder-for-hire case over the past week. Stay tuned here each Friday for all the testimony and big events you might have missed. The trial began Monday (Aug. 24) in Los Angeles federal court, where the “All My Life” hitmaker (Durk Banks) is charged with ordering OTF members to kill rival rapper Quando Rondo in retaliation for the 2020 killing of his close friend and collaborator King Von. Rondo was shot at a Los Angeles gas station in 2022 and survived, but another man known as Lul Pab was killed in the crossfire. During opening statements, prosecutor Daniel Weiner argued that Durk was “consumed with revenge” after Von’s death. Weiner said Durk arranged for numerous OTF associates to travel from Chicago to L.A. and “track, stalk, hunt and kill” Rondo while he waited for updates in a nearby rental house. Two alleged participants in the killing, David “Browneyez” Lindsey and Deandre “OTF Dede” Wilson, are also on trial. Defense lawyer Marissa Goldberg responded in her own opening statement that the rapper had “nothing to do with” the shooting, arguing that there isn’t any evidence showing he paid for a hit on Rondo. Goldberg said the real mastermind of the plot was Kavon “Vonnie” Grant, one of the shooters who has flipped and become a government witness. “He thought, ‘Oh man, I’ve got an insurance policy,’” said Goldberg of Vonnie’s decision to point the finger at Durk. “I’ve got a big fish I can give them.” After openings, the first two days of Durk’s trial focused largely on hard evidence. Surveillance video was played on Tuesday (Aug. 25) from an In-N-Out Burger restaurant, where the shooters allegedly stopped for a bite after killing Pab. A detective who reviewed the tape testified that the men seemed to be “joking around” and “having a good time,” according to Los Angeles Magazine . Also on Tuesday, prosecutors showed numerous text messages sent by Durk after Von’s 2020 death. This included messages where Durk wrote, “I gotta go all out for him,” “I can’t let this slide” and “him dying turning me a different animal.” On Wednesday (Aug. 26), the jurors heard the first of what is expected to be multiple Durk songs admitted as evidence of Durk’s alleged motive. The prosecution played an unreleased 2021 music video for the song “Redman,” which depicts Durk reading news stories about Von’s death and then shooting a man that prosecutors describe as a Rondo “look-alike.” Durk’s lawyers maintain that his music should not be taken literally, but instead ought to be viewed as a performance in which he’s “challenging his emotions through his artwork.” Durk attorney Brian Steel drilled down on this argument while cross-examining an FBI agent about the “Redman” video on Wednesday, per Rolling Stone . “You know that Durk is a musical artist, a poet, true?” Steel asked the agent. The real fireworks began later on Wednesday when the first of multiple cooperating witnesses took the stand: Kacey “OTF Jam” Hester, a Chicago gang member and former friend of Durk’s who has admitted to being one of the shooters who targeted Rondo. According to Courthouse News Service , Jam said during direct testimony on Wednesday and Thursday (Aug. 27) that he regretted participating in the murder of an “innocent” man. He told the jury, “I wasn’t feeling good about it at all. I felt it was sloppy.” Jam testified Thursday that Durk offered a hefty cash reward for the shooting. While this promised sum was never paid, he allegedly received $10,000 to record a track with Durk. After being arrested in 2023 on separate gun charges, he wrote in a note to police, “I know about murders.” “I had to get it off my chest,” said Jam of his decision to become a government informant. “It was weighing on me.” Steel aggressively cross-examined Jam on Thursday and Friday (Aug. 28), pointing out that his story had “dramatically” changed over time. Steel suggested that Jam, who has been in and out of prison for much of his life, is lying about Durk’s involvement because he wants a reduced sentence. “Going home, that’s your mission?” Steel asked the witness, per Rolling Stone .  “Me, trying to go home? Yes,” Jam replied. The trial is set to resume Monday and run for several more weeks. It has already drawn some notable spectators , including Ye (formerly Kanye West) and mgk.

articles.title: Cardinals place Blaze Jordan on IL before Pirates clash
articles.summary: Ahead of Friday’s three-game series opener against the Pittsburgh Pirates, the St. Louis Cardinals placed infielder Blaze Jordan on the 10-day Injured List with a left ankle sprain after the 23-year-old was forced to leave Thursday’s 7-5 win over the Baltimore Orioles. Jordan suffered
articles._body: Ahead of Friday’s three-game series opener against the Pittsburgh Pirates, the St. Louis Cardinals placed infielder Blaze Jordan on the 10-day Injured List with a left ankle sprain after the 23-year-old was forced to leave Thursday’s 7-5 win over the Baltimore Orioles . Jordan suffered the injury in the top of the eighth inning. After reliever George Soriano threw out a runner at third base, Jordan went down immediately and needed assistance to leave the field. The injury comes after Jordan became a fixture in St. Louis’ lineup following his first promotion to the major leagues in June. He has appeared in 58 games this season, owning a .247/.276/.382 slash line and a .658 OPS. Jordan has also recorded three home runs, 28 RBIs, eight doubles, four triples and 16 runs scored across 199 plate appearances. To fill Jordan’s spot, the Cardinals recalled utility player Thomas Saggese to the major-league roster. The 24-year-old returns to the big leagues for the first time since June 3 after starting the season on the Opening Day roster. Saggese had a forgettable first stint in the majors , hitting .184/.244/.276 with one home run and four RBIs in 32 games. However, his production has improved considerably after moving to Triple-A, where he has logged a .258/.340/.446 slash line with 10 homers, 33 RBIs, nine stolen bases, 10 doubles and 35 runs scored in 55 games. Saggese also gives St. Louis defensive flexibility. He can handle second base, shortstop, third base and left field. With Masyn Winn out and JJ Wetherholt handling shortstop duties, Saggese could offer the Cardinals valuable coverage at second base and depth at shortstop. articles.title: Bill Simmons’ wild Bronny, LeBron James idea might be genius
articles.summary: LeBron James and Bronny James already made history as teammates. Now, their first professional matchup on opposite sides could inspire a strategy that sounds absurd until Bill Simmons explains it. With Bronny remaining with the Los Angeles Lakers and LeBron now playing in Philadelphia, Simmons pr
articles._body: LeBron James and Bronny James already made history as teammates. Now, their first professional matchup on opposite sides could inspire a strategy that sounds absurd until Bill Simmons explains it. With Bronny remaining with the Los Angeles Lakers and LeBron now playing in Philadelphia, Simmons proposed that the Cleveland Cavaliers acquire the younger James for one specific assignment. He wants Cleveland to deploy Bronny against his father during high-pressure playoff moments, banking on LeBron’s parental instincts to disrupt his aggression. “If you’re Cleveland, you trade like a minimum for Bronny, bring him back, LeBron is on the team, and now he’s just kind of lurking as almost like a kryptonite situation for LeBron,” Simmons said. His theory has nothing to do with Bronny shutting down one of basketball’s greatest players. It hinges on LeBron hesitating because the defender happens to be his son. Bill Simmons says the Cavaliers should trade for Bronny so he can guard his dad in key moments during a playoff series because LeBron wouldn’t want to embarrass his son “…if you’re Cleveland, you trade like a minimum for Bronny, bring him back, LeBron is on the team, and now… pic.twitter.com/RLN6SIvSbz — Basketball Forever (@bballforever_) August 28, 2026 Could Bronny Really Become LeBron’s Kryptonite? Simmons admitted that he would struggle to humiliate his own son before 20,000 spectators on national television. That emotional wrinkle makes the concept fascinating, even if Cleveland never seriously considers it. LeBron would face two choices in Simmons’ hypothetical scenario. He could attack Bronny without mercy and bury the theory immediately, or avoid the matchup by handing Jaylen Brown control of the possession. Philadelphia would certainly prefer the first option over watching sentiment interfere with a playoff series. The pitch also fits Simmons’ history of imaginative LeBron proposals. He previously suggested that James spend his final season signing with every NBA team, allowing the entire league to participate in his farewell tour. That plan lived far beyond left field. Turning Bronny into psychological playoff defense, however, contains just enough logic to make Simmons’ wildest recent idea sound almost brilliant. articles.title: Stove God Cooks Says He Sent Jay-Z a Hook: ‘I Don’t Want No Percentage, Just Send a Roc Chain’
articles.summary: Let's hope he didn't block his blessings by revealing this interesting tidbit of information as rumors of a new JAY-Z album continue to swirl.
articles._body: Stove God Cooks insinuated that he may or may not be on this mythical album JAY-Z is supposedly making. In a clip that’s been floating around rap social media circles, the Syracuse MC stopped by The Joe Budden Podcast recently and revealed that he sent Jigga a hook to use however and whenever he wants to. “I sent Hov a hook. Don’t let me get on this album. I’m really gonna dance on you n—as. Now we gonna talk,” he proclaimed, before making sure he mentioned that he has no clue if a new album is coming or not. “I’m not confirming that big homie got an album coming out, but big homie, if you got an album coming out, use that hook I sent you. You know I was talking on that verse. Let’s do that.” He added that he doesn’t want any money or percentage points for his contribution to whatever Jay has cooking; all he wants is a Roc-A-Fella chain. “I don’t want nothing. Keep everything,” he said. “Just send a Roc chain. I don’t want no percentage. Just send a Roc chain.” Stove has been dealing with his own issues when it comes to albums. Fans have been clamoring for his sophomore project since he dropped the Roc Marciano -produced classing Reasonable Drought back in 2020 and had a show-stealing hook on “F.I.C.O.” off the Grammy-winning Clipse album . However, after many pump fakes and back-and-forths with his current label Babygrande, however, it looks like they’ve finally hashed things out and found common ground because he posted that they renegotiated a new deal on his Instagram Stories earlier this week. “I salute real sh–, always,” he wrote. “Respect to Chuck [Wilson] at Babygrande. He came and sat down face-to-face and we got the renegotiation done! Album on the way.” As far as a new JAY-Z album is concerned, though? Roc Nation deaded those rumors earlier this month, calling the unsubstantiated claims “fake news” on the company’s IG Stories.
