articles.title: Coke Zero 400 qualifying results: Ross Chastain wins pole, full starting order for Cup Series race at Daytona
articles.summary: NASCAR’s new superspeedway package made its Daytona debut during qualifying for Saturday night’s regular-season finale.
articles._body: Daytona International Speedway weekend is underway, and qualifying is complete for Saturday night’s Coke Zero Sugar 400, and it was Ross Chastain who won the pole.  And with all the questions about the new superspeedway rules package , the drivers got their first opportunity to get on track and see how the car would react in single-lap qualifying. Early on, Riley Herbst and Austin Hill put down the fast times, followed by the Trackhouse trio of Ross Chastain, Connor Zilisch, and Shane van Gisbergen. Later in the opening run of qualifying, Ford flexed its might with Ryan Preece shooting to the top of the board along with two of the three Penske cars in the Top 10 along with Preece’s teammate, Chris Buescher. The story of the opening round was the lack of qualifying speed from the Toyotas with only Riley Herbst advancing to Top 10 qualifying. There was an odd situation where Ty Gibbs was allowed to run a second qualifying lap after registering P21 on his first attempt because caution lights misfired and came on during his run. Although he did improve to P14 on the re-do, Gibbs did not advance to Top 10 qualifying. Full qualifying results for Coke Zero Sugar 400 1. Ross Chastain 2. Chris Buescher 3. Austin Hill 4. Ryan Preece 5. Riley Herbst 6. Shane van Gisbergen 7. Connor Zilisch 8. Austin Cindric 9. Joey Logano 10. Kyle Larson 11. Corey Heim 12. Chase Briscoe 13. William Byron 14. Ty Gibbs 15. Erik Jones 16. Cole Custer 17. Tyler Reddick 18. Michael McDowell 19. Ryan Blaney 20. Alex Bowman 21. Brad Keselowski 22. Chase Elliott 23. Daniel Suarez 24. Josh Berry 25. Cody Ware 26. Bubba Wallace 27. John Hunter Nemechek 28. Carson Hocevar 29. Austin Dillon 30. Denny Hamlin 31. Ty Dillon 32. Ricky Stenhouse Jr. 33. Todd Gilliland 34. Zane Smith 35. Christopher Bell 36. AJ Allmendinger 37. Noah Gragson 38. Casey Mears 39. Daniel Dye 40. Joey Gase The full qualifying order will be updated when it’s official How to watch the Coke Zero Sugar 400 On Saturday, August 29th, NASCAR makes its return to Daytona International Speedway for the Coke Zero Sugar 400. This will be the fourth race on USA Sports, which will carry NASCAR coverage through the end of the season.  The race begins at 7:30 p.m. ET.  It will be televised on NBC, while carrying the USA Sports branding.  And it’s the final race of the regular season before the start of the Chase.  When the checkered flag waves, the field of 16 drivers for the NASCAR postseason will be set.  It will also be the first race using the new superspeedway rules package .   “The rear spoiler will be shortened from 7 inches to 4 inches, the same height as intermediate tracks, in an effort to reduce drag, along with a slight reduction in horsepower from 510 to 465 to adjust for the reduced downforce,” wrote Zach Sturniolo on NASCAR.com. “NASCAR officials anticipate single-car runs to be approximately 3 mph faster than the current package, but cars in a pack are expected to run about the same speeds.” A brief breakdown of the rules package and the expectations: Superspeedway Package Update: 14” spoiler and wide splitter stuffers (same as intermediate) Safety equipment remains the same as current SSW Engine tapered spacer reduced to 27/32” ~ 465 HP New spoiler braces Spoiler deflection device redesigned to accommodate 4” spoiler Performance Aspects: Single-car speeds estimated at 2-3 mph faster than current qualifying. Maximum pack speeds estimated in the same range as current. Dynamic passing maneuver CFD indicates completion of a pass with a 5-mph run is more likely with new package. Expect fireworks on and off the track at Daytona.

articles.title: Browns legend believes Myles Garrett trade lays out 2027 plans
articles.summary: One of the biggest moves of the offseason was the Cleveland Browns trading Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams. While it was a decision that removed one of the league’s most dominant pass rushers from the roster, it gave Cleveland a haul of draft picks for the future, along with a young p
articles._body: One of the biggest moves of the offseason was the Cleveland Browns trading Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams. While it was a decision that removed one of the league’s most dominant pass rushers from the roster, it gave Cleveland a haul of draft picks for the future, along with a young pass rusher to take over Garrett’s role. The plan is centered on the idea of long-term success. So much so that some are already convinced the front office may be wanting to tank for a high-value pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. On Friday, Browns legend Joe Thomas chimed in on the decision to trade the 30-year-old edge rusher and thinks the franchise is at least considering taking a quarterback next offseason. “I definitely think that they’re considering drafting a quarterback high wherever they are [in the draft] next year,” Thomas said on ‘The Herd’ with fill-in host Jason McIntyre. “They told you about it when they traded away Myles Garrett and added draft picks next year. Because they know [they] could possibly get [a quarterback] this next year. “It’s very clear right now because [the Browns] had a quarterback competition all training camp that they don’t belive there is one on their roster right now for sure… When you don’t know who your quarterback is that usually means you probably don’t have one,” Thomas continued. “And so, I definitely think they’re setting themselves up, but I don’t think they’re tanking in a sense that they did in 2016 and 2017 when I was there.” "I definitely think they're considering draft a QB high next year. They told you about it when they traded away Myles Garrett and added draft picks." @jasonrmcintyre and @joethomas73 on if the Browns are tanking for a QB in next year's draft pic.twitter.com/fKhuOF4xYI — Herd w/Colin Cowherd (@TheHerd) August 28, 2026 Joe Thomas did suggest that, although all signs indicate the franchise quarterback is not currently on the roster, the 2026-27 campaign still gives Deshaun Watson or Shedeur Sanders a chance to prove otherwise. Either way, Cleveland is set up nicely for the future. The Browns acquired Jared Verse, a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second-round pick, and a 2029 third-round pick that can turn into a first-rounder if the Rams were to trade Myles Garrett to an AFC North rival. Cleveland’s front office now just has to make sure to draft the right players in the coming years. articles._body: With the Los Angeles Dodgers looking to bounce back after a complete-game shutout by Atlanta Braves pitcher Chris Sale, the focus is now on the start of a new series against the Detroit Tigers, which begins on Friday night. In the opening game of the series, it will be Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal going up against his former team in the Tigers , as manager Dave Roberts gives his thoughts on what it will look like for the star. articles.title: Michael Jackson’s Top 50 Hit Songs on the Billboard Hot 100
articles.summary: From "Rockin' Robin" to "Rock With You" and "You Rock My World," the King of Pop's top hits cross several chapters of his legendary canon.
articles._body: In a career that spanned almost all 50 years of his life, Michael Jackson became a mainstay on the Billboard charts, evolving from a child star into a global phenomenon and an undisputed legend. His dominance on the Billboard Hot 100 reflects his record-breaking career: As a solo artist, 13 of his singles reached No. 1 – tied with Drake for the most by a male artist in history – and an additional four songs by the Jackson 5, with Michael on lead vocals, topped the chart. Jackson first gained major recognition as the lead singer of family band the Jackson 5 with his siblings Jackie, Jermaine, Marlon and Tito, who notched massive hits for Motown off the bat. By age 12, the earliest instance of Jackson’s record-shattering capabilities emerged: The Jackson 5 became the first act to have their first four Hot 100 entries all reach No. 1. Parallel to his siblings’ success, Michael scored solo hits – including Hot 100 champ “Ben” – through the 1970s. Although 1979’s Quincy Jones-produced Off the Wall was his fifth album, its bold creative direction positioned a then-21-year-old Michael as a fully-formed artist who would soon claim the King of Pop crown. The follow-up, 1982’s Thriller , is widely considered the best-selling album of all time and spent an astonishing 37 weeks atop the Billboard 200 – a record for an album by a single artist. In another first, th album’s seven singles all reached the top 10 of the Billboard Hot 100, with two, the immortal “Billie Jean” and “Beat It,” topping the chart. While Thriller showed Jackson at unprecedented commercial heights, the superstar continued to make Hot 100 history with subsequent projects. 1987’s Bad produced a record five No. 1 singles, a mark unmatched by any album until 2011, and “You Are Not Alone” in 1995, became the first song to ever debut at No. 1 on the Hot 100. Though his chart power had waned at the time of his death in 2009, posthumous releases with his musical descendants still generate buzz collaborations: 2014’s “Love Never Felt So Good (with Justin Timberlake) and a featured credit on Drake’s 2018 track “Don’t Matter to Me,” which samples an unreleased Jackson song, both reached No. 9. To review Jackson’s more than half-century of Hot 100 impact, here’s a review of the late icon’s 50 biggest hits on the Hot 100. For a wider scope of his influence, the list comprises his solo catalog as well as material by the Jackson 5 and The Jacksons. Michael Jackson’s Biggest Hot 100 Hits ranking is based on weekly performance on the Hot 100 (from its inception on Aug. 4, 1958, through Aug. 29, 2026). Songs are ranked based on an inverse point system, with weeks at No. 1 earning the greatest value and weeks at lower spots earning the least. Due to changes in chart methodology over the years, eras are weighted differently to account for chart turnover rates during various periods.

"People I've talked to inside the Raiders building and league-wide with other teams, expect Kirk Cousins to be named the starter eventually." — @JFowlerESPN on the Raiders' starting QB role pic.twitter.com/rYusotgmnZ — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) August 28, 2026 “People I’ve talked to inside the Raiders building and league-wide with other teams, expect Kirk Cousins to be named the starter eventually.” Head coach Klint Kubiak appears willing to let the competition continue through the end of the preseason. The AFC is too loaded this season. Mendoza should play only when Kubiak and his staff believe he is prepared — not because the fan base wants to see the rookie immediately. Cousins may no longer be a long-term solution, but he can help the offense function while allowing the Raiders to evaluate the rest of their roster. If he struggles or the team falls out of contention, Las Vegas can turn to Mendoza later in the season under less pressure. articles._body: With the Minnesota Twins still having playoff hopes , the latest injury to star slugger Byron Buxton will no doubt put a dent in some fans’ aspirations. As Buxton exited the Twins’ game against the Athletics last Tuesday, which ended in a 4-2 loss, with a hip injury, the latest update might worry fans about the future of the 32-year-old. According to Aaron Gleeman, Minnesota general manager Jeremy Zoll said that Buxton is currently “day-t0-day” and while the goal is to possibly avoid the injured list in the short term, an offseason hip surgery is an “option” on the table. “Twins general manager Jeremy Zoll said Byron Buxton (hip) is “stillday-to-day to day” and will attempt to avoid the injured list for now,” Gleeman wrote on X, formerly Twitter. “Zoll also revealed that Buxton eventually undergoing offseason hip surgery “is definitely a potential option as we sort through everything.” Buxton had been dealing with a nagging hip issue for the last few months , according to ESPN, as the 32-year-old had recorded a .254 batting average to go along with 25 home runs and 46 RBIs. At any rate, it remains to be seen when Buxton returns to the Twins’ lineup, as it appears it may not be too serious, when looking at the season is still ongoing. However, an offseason surgery could prompt two types of fan reactions: one of concern for next season or another of optimism about the attempt to relieve any lingering issues. Minnesota looks to keep their postseason dreams alive as the team is 64-70, which puts them third in the AL Central, as they’re four games back of a wild card spot. articles._body: Kalshi today lost a major ruling over whether it can evade state gambling laws, as a federal appeals court found that Nevada can stop the prediction market from allowing sports bets. While the Trump administration is trying to help prediction markets avoid state regulation, a panel of three Trump-appointed judges unanimously ruled against Kalshi in today's decision from the US Court of Appeals for the 9th Circuit. The Nevada Gaming Control Board today said the 9th Circuit "emphatically reject[ed] the view that the federal Commodity Exchange Act preempts application of Nevada’s gaming laws to sports-event contracts offered by Kalshi, Crypto.com, and Robinhood." Nevada Governor Joe Lombardo, a Republican, said that "prediction markets offering sports-event contracts constitute gambling and must comply with Nevada’s gaming laws and regulatory framework." The judges affirmed a district court order that let Nevada enforce state laws against Kalshi’s sports-related event contracts. Read full article Comments

articles.title: MLB suspends not-13-year-old Guardians prospect for wild international fraud plot
articles.summary: Major League Baseball has suspended Cleveland Guardians prospect Daury David Severino Damaso after an investigation uncovered an elaborate scheme involving his age and identity, ESPN’s Alden Gonzales reported on Friday. The prospect had been presented to Cleveland under the name David Sever
articles._body: Major League Baseball has suspended Cleveland Guardians prospect Daury David Severino Damaso after an investigation uncovered an elaborate scheme involving his age and identity , ESPN’s Alden Gonzales reported on Friday. The prospect had been presented to Cleveland under the name David Severino, with the organization believing he was 13 or 14 years old when it agreed to a $2.8 million pre-deal in December 2025. The agreement was supposed to be completed in 2029, when Severino would have reached the required age to sign. Instead, MLB’s investigation determined that both the player’s name and age had been falsified. Severino was actually born on April 2, 2010, making him 16 years old rather than the age claimed when the Guardians reached their agreement. Former trainer Francisco Nieves allegedly helped create a separate identity in 2023 with the approval of Severino’s parents, according to the investigation. A late birth registration was reportedly produced for the supposed younger identity, listing a December 20, 2011, birthdate. Medical and school documents were also allegedly created using that identity. The scheme went further two years later when a fraudulent death certificate was filed for Daury, claiming he had died from a respiratory illness on May 5, 2012. A fake tombstone was also reportedly placed at a gravesite in La Romana, Dominican Republic, about 75 miles from Santo Domingo. John Pereyra, a trainer who had worked with Severino, said he personally visited the site after becoming suspicious about the player’s documentation and was convinced by what he saw. Severino had impressed evaluators while competing against players aged 12 and 13, despite actually being old enough to compete in the Dominican Summer League with 16- and 17-year-olds. Several teams had reportedly developed suspicions before MLB’s investigation, although it remains unclear what specifically triggered the league’s inquiry. Cleveland terminated the agreement in May 2026 after the age discrepancy emerged, and Severino had not appeared in an affiliated game for the Guardians. MLB’s suspension means he must wait an additional year before becoming eligible for the international amateur market. His actual age would otherwise have made him eligible for the 2027 signing class. Cleveland is not facing discipline from MLB. Pereyra, who spent $20,000 acquiring Severino’s rights and continues to house him at his academy, said he hopes the player eventually receives another opportunity. One scout reportedly believes that a future contract could be worth around $10,000. articles.title: Rams fans won’t love Mike Florio’s Aaron Donald return timeline prediction
articles.summary: With the Los Angeles Rams preparing for the 2026 NFL season, the one storyline surrounding the team was the question if Aaron Donald would come out of retirement to return to the franchise. As fans want to see Donald come back to the Rams, this NFL insider has a prediction on the timeline that ma
articles._body: With the Los Angeles Rams preparing for the 2026 NFL season , the one storyline surrounding the team was the question if Aaron Donald would come out of retirement to return to the franchise. As fans want to see Donald come back to the Rams , this NFL insider has a prediction on the timeline that many might find frustrating. While there are a lot of high expectations around Los Angeles ahead of the 2026 season with or without Donald on the team, Mike Florio of ProFootballTalk knows one thing is for certain about the star: he won’t play when the season starts . The question now turns to whether he’ll come back by Week 14, with the Tuesday before being the deadline to sign with the team. “Three weeks ago, it felt like Aaron Donald would inevitably come out of retirement and play for the Rams in 2026. The Rams had a plan: ramp him up, get him ready to go, 30 to 40 snaps Week 1 in Australia against the 49ers,” Florio said. “Well, we’re now less than two weeks away from that game in Australia, and it’s looking more and more clear. Aaron Donald’s not going to be playing in Week One.” “Sean McVay, coach of the Rams, says ‘it’s all up in the air.’ The reality is, when they go up in the air to Australia, Aaron Donald’s not going to be there. The real question is: Will he be back before the window closes on any return for 2026? For a retired player, you got to come back by the Tuesday after Week 13,” Florio continued. Three weeks ago, it seemed inevitable that Aaron Donald would soon rejoin the Rams. Now? Nobody knows what’s going on. pic.twitter.com/IWZa1RMQjf — ProFootballTalk (@ProFootballTalk) August 28, 2026 At any rate, it remains to be seen if Donald comes back to the Rams, though the team is solely focused on Week 1, which takes place on Sept. 10 against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. articles.title: Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields Festival Raises $10 Million for Women’s Charities
articles.summary: The list of benefiting organizations includes Planned Parenthood and Center for Reproductive Rights.
articles._body: Olivia Rodrigo may not have found the cure for the issues women are facing all over the world, but $10 million — which the singer has already raised for organizations supporting reproductive rights, healthcare and domestic abuse survivors through Daisy Chain Fields — is a pretty good start. Related Olivia Rodrigo’s ‘Handmaid’s Tale’-Inspired Song ‘Serena Joy’ Is Now on Streaming After Record Store Release KATSEYE Drops Out of Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields Festival After Megan Sprains Ankle: ‘We’re So Incredibly Sorry’ Radio Rallies Around Dolly Parton After Her Death, Led by '9 to 5' At a press conference attended by Billboard on Friday (Aug. 28), Rodrigo revealed the eye-popping amount her festival’s ticket sales have brought in for its benefitting organizations. “It’s a real honor to announce that we are donating $10 million to be given directly to these 10 nonprofit partners,” she said, earning applause. “I’m so excited for tomorrow, I’ll see you guys there.” The news comes one day prior to the first-ever Daisy Chain Fields, a daylong event taking place in Irvine, California. Rodrigo personally curated the lineup, which features Chappell Roan, Doechii, Mitski, Garbage, The Breeders, Bikini Kill and more, as well as “special guests” Stevie Nicks, Karen O and Sarah McLachlan. KATSEYE was also intended to play a set, but it was announced Thursday that the girl group had dropped out in light of member Megan spraining her ankle, with Devon Again subbing in on the bill. Rodrigo first announced Daisy Chain in June. “i’ve had a dream of doing this festival for years and i am so ecstatic its finally coming true!!” she said at the time. “Daisy Chain Fields features an all-women lineup and 100 percent of the net proceeds will go to charities dedicated to advancing and advocating for women and girls … i firmly believe that joy, community, and music can be the drivers of meaningful change and I’m hopeful this festival will be just that.” The list of partner organizations benefiting from the $10 million also includes Baby2Baby, Black Mamas Matter Alliance, FreeFrom, Jhpiego, Johns Hopkins Center for Indigenous Health, National Domestic Workers Alliance, National Institute for Reproductive Health and National Women’s Law Center. Bitcoin Cools Off After $3 Billion ETF-Driven Surge
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Cools Off After $3 Billion ETF-Driven Surge Bitcoin slid Friday afternoon, cooling down after a phenomenal run following huge investment from U.S. ETF buyers.  The leading cryptocurrency was trading for $77,379 on Friday afternoon in New York after dropping more than 3% over a 24-hour period.  Bitcoin hit a high this week of $81,281 but slowed down after Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh gave his first major speech as head of the central bank — saying on Friday that he had “more work to do” to fight inflation. The Bitcoin price has in the past dropped when the Federal Reserve thinks inflation is too high because it means less chance of a rate cut; the leading cryptocurrency typically does better in a low-interest rate environment.  JUST IN: U.S. Bitcoin ETFs have brought in $1.14 billion in inflows this week. Over $3 billion has been added in the past 9 days! pic.twitter.com/ri1jE7enTZ — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) August 28, 2026 Bitcoin started surging last week after the U.S. Treasury would at least double the size of its liquidity-support buyback operations. The announcement last week hurt the dollar but non-yielding assets have benefited.  Exchange-traded funds, managed by the likes of BlackRock, Fidelity, and Grayscale have received net positive inflows for nine days in a row, according to Farside Investors data. Last week was their best week since October — when bitcoin hit a new all-time high — and that run has continued into this week.  Since August 17, investors have thrown over $3 billion at the funds. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust received the lion’s share of the investment, but Morgan Stanley’s new Bitcoin Trust — which debuted this year — also experienced significant inflows.  Analysts have said that the so-called debasement trade — when investors buy an asset as a way to hedge against a currency losing value — was leading investors to eye-up bitcoin again.  Investors taking part in the trade think that bitcoin, gold and other precious metals are a good way to protect themselves from excessive government spending.  Total U.S. debt crossed $40 trillion for the first time this month.  This post Bitcoin Cools Off After $3 Billion ETF-Driven Surge first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo .

articles.summary: It’s safe to say that the first two-plus years of Minnesota Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy’s career have not gone according to plan. After his rookie year was ruined by a torn meniscus, nagging injuries and inconsistent play prevented him from turning his second season into a memor
articles._body: It’s safe to say that the first two-plus years of Minnesota Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy’s career have not gone according to plan. After his rookie year was ruined by a torn meniscus, nagging injuries and inconsistent play prevented him from turning his second season into a memorable one. From @NFLGameDay Kickoff: While there are still questions about #Vikings QB JJ McCarthy, the argument can be made that his best-case scenario is answering them in Minnesota this year. pic.twitter.com/PFtuiOuAhQ — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) August 28, 2026 McCarthy has lost all semblance of being the Vikings’ quarterback of the future in his third season. Former Arizona Cardinal Kyler Murray has established himself as the team’s No. 1 quarterback. McCarthy will either be the second- or third-string signal caller. Head coach Kevin O’Connell will determine the Vikings’ QB pecking order after the team’s final preseason game Friday night at Denver. While it has been a fall from grace from the quarterback who led Michigan to the national championship in the 2023 season, McCarthy has not asked to be traded as of yet. NFL insider Ian Rapoport says that McCarthy’s contract status — he’s in the third year of a four-year rookie deal — means that the Vikings are not compelled to move him at this point. However, if the Vikings end up naming veteran Carson Wentz as the team’s No. 2 quarterback over McCarthy, that could change the environment in the locker room and the front office. The Vikings will certainly listen if other teams come calling about the No. 10 pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. He would certainly return a high draft pick in a trade, but the exact value has not been determined at this point. McCarthy completed 140 of 243 passes for 1,632 yards last season with 11 TDs and 12 interceptions. In addition to that ordinary performance, he lacked accuracy when throwing to wide open receivers and that may keep McCarthy from developing into a competent NFL quarterback. The post Vikings’ J.J. McCarthy has not requested a trade after benching, per NFL Insider appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Yeezy Spokesperson Milo Yiannopoulous Arrested by ICE in Louisiana
articles.summary: According to Homeland Security, the controversial political commentator overstayed a visa after coming to the U.S. in 2019.
articles._body: Milo Yiannopoulos — Yeezy head of special projects and spokesperson for Ye (formerly Kanye West ) — is in custody after being arrested by U.S. Immigration and Enforcement officers in Louisiana on Thursday. Online records show that Yiannopoulos, a U.K. native, is currently in ICE custody as of Friday (Aug. 28). Homeland Security released a statement confirming that Yiannopoulos was apprehended at Armstrong New Orleans International Airport in Kenner, Louisiana. DHS claims he legally entered the U.S. in May 2019 but has overstayed his visa and missed an immigration hearing in July, which resulted in a final removal order being issued. “On August 27, ICE arrested Milo Yiannopoulos, an illegal alien from the United Kingdom, at the Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport (MSY) in Kenner, Louisiana,” Homeland Security wrote on X. “Yiannopoulos legally entered the country on May 14, 2019, through New York City, New York.” DHS’ statement continued: “He chose to overstay his welcome in violation of our nation’s laws.   Yiannopoulos was issued a final order of removal by an Immigration Judge on July 22, after failing to show up for his immigration hearing. He will remain in ICE custody pending removal.” On August 27, ICE arrested Milo Yiannopoulos, an illegal alien from the United Kingdom, at the Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport (MSY) in Kenner, Louisiana. Yiannopoulos legally entered the country on May 14, 2019, through New York City, New York. He chose to… https://t.co/Hk6QBUmGDI pic.twitter.com/DbIhv8Z6PI — Homeland Security (@DHSgov) August 28, 2026 It’s possible that Yiannopoulos was traveling to New Orleans when he was arrested by ICE agents, as Ye is set to perform at the Caesars Superdome in the Big Easy on Friday night (Aug. 28). Milo Yiannopoulos became known as a political commentator in the years prior to aligning with Ye,l and joined forces with West when he attempted to make a presidential run in the 2024 election. He’s since served as a spokesperson, chief of staff and head of special projects for Yeezy. Yiannopoulos announced in 2024 that he was resigning from Yeezy, but seemed to find his way back to the company. In his recent posts to X, Yiannopoulos has been a staunch supporter of ICE and the deportation of illegal aliens. In July, he called for ICE agents to be stationed at supermarkets and government buildings in California “with on the spot deportation for anyone who can’t prove they are in the U.S. legally.” Billboard has reached out to Ye’s reps for comment.

articles.summary: Amid the NBA’s LeBron James sweepstakes, the New York Knicks were reportedly a dark horse to land the future Hall of Fame forward, which OG Anunoby addressed following his championship run. While Anunoby is still asked about his game-winner in Game 4 of the NBA Finals, OG also discussed how
articles._body: Amid the NBA’s LeBron James sweepstakes, the New York Knicks were reportedly a dark horse to land the future Hall of Fame forward, which OG Anunoby addressed following his championship run. While Anunoby is still asked about his game-winner in Game 4 of the NBA Finals, OG also discussed how he would have reacted to the Knicks landing LeBron after winning their first title in 53 years. In a question framed as would you rather compete against or not, Anunoby didn’t hold back on his take about James joining the Knicks, per Sports Illustrated. “If he wanted to join the team, then he could join,” Anunoby said. “He could do whatever he wanted to. He’s earned the right to choose his destination. He’s a legendary player. If he had wanted to come here, then, yeah, I’d welcome it.” OG Anunoby talks about whether he would have welcomed the idea of LeBron James joining the Knicks pic.twitter.com/FuVmqu5QsG — Sports Illustrated (@SInow) August 28, 2026 As LeBron James, Jaylen Brown, Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid, and the 76ers are projected to be one of the more competitive teams in the Eastern Conference, the defending champion Knicks will host them at Madison Square Garden on Opening Night. OG Anunoby reflects on game-winning shot amid Knicks’ Finals victory Knicks forward OG Anunoby’s game-winning tip-in won an ESPY for best play of the season. It’ll go down in history as the greatest shot in franchise history for the Knicks. Anunoby is still in awe of the moment, which topped off a 29-point Knicks comeback, as he reflected on the historic moment , per Fadeaway World’s Mark Medina. “I’m not over it as if I don’t care about it. It’s more about that I’m ready for the next season,” Anunoby said. “It was fun winning a championship. It was amazing. But we all want to do it again. So it’s about getting ready to start the next season. Hopefully we can do it again.” Anunoby’s and the Knicks’ 107-106 Game 4 victory secured a 3-1 lead before Game 5’s 94-90 win eliminated the Spurs, 4-1. Brandon, who was the No. 3 ranked quarterback in the Class of 2
articles._body: When Faizon Brandon starts for Tennessee in its season opener against Furman , he’ll join Nico Iamaleava (2024 Citrus Bowl) in becoming the second true freshman quarterback to start a game for the Volunteers in the Josh Heupel era. Brandon, who was the No. 3 ranked quarterback in the Class of 2026, beat out sophomore quarterback  George MacIntyre for the starting job this season. Brandon’s presence at quarterback will serve as a complete 180 at the position for Tennessee . Last season, Joey Aguilar was the starter while playing in his fifth year of college football. Now, Brandon is poised to make his first career appearance against the Paladins. $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage On Friday’s episode of ‘ The Jim Rome Show ‘, Tennessee head coach Josh Heupel opened up about what stood out to him about Brandon throughout spring ball and training camp. With Brandon leading the way, the Vols are looking to bounce back from a turbulent 2025 campaign, in which they lost four of their final seven games. “There’s a lot that goes into playing quarterback at a high level,” Heupel said. “As a young guy, his work habit since arriving here in January has been phenomenal. One of the first guys into the building and is here late into the evening. He just continued to get better with every opportunity that he got. From spring ball to training camp, he continued to grow.” Brandon’s teammate compares him to Lamar Jackson The expectations for Brandon’s first start at Tennessee were already high. The flames were stoked even higher by teammate Jordan Norman , however, as he compared the freshman quarterback to Lamar Jackson . That has Heupel ‘excited’ to see Brandon let loose inside Neyland Stadium for the first time on Sept. 5. “During the course of training camp, he did a great job controlling and commanding what we’re doing offensively,” Heupel continued. “Understand the run game, making checks, and his RPO game has continued to grow. He has the ability to distribute the ball at a really high level. He takes care of the football. “So, we’re really excited with what we’ve seen from that room during the course of training camp, and certainly Faizon as well. I’m excited to get to gameday and let that guy go paint the picture here and continue our journey as a football team this year.” Coming off an 8-5 campaign, Tennessee is seeking a return to the College Football Playoff this season for the second time in the past three years.

articles.title: Jazz’s Jusuf Nurkic dominates in Bosnia’s FIBA World Cup Qualifiers win over Italy
articles.summary: Bosnia and Herzegovina took on Italy in a FIBA World Cup qualifier on Friday and earned a big 78-76 win. Utah Jazz’s Jusuf Nurkic can be thanked for the team’s victory, as he went ballistic against Italy to keep Bosnia and Herzegovina alive in the tournament. In just 22 minutes of pla
articles._body: Bosnia and Herzegovina took on Italy in a FIBA World Cup qualifier on Friday and earned a big 78-76 win. Utah Jazz’s Jusuf Nurkic can be thanked for the team’s victory, as he went ballistic against Italy to keep Bosnia and Herzegovina alive in the tournament. In just 22 minutes of playing time, the 32-year-old center led the way for Bosnia and Herzegovina, recording 25 points and 14 rebounds while hitting 11 of his 19 field goal attempts. It was a great outing from Nurkic, who clearly did everything in his power to keep his team in the mix. Those numbers are well above Nurkic’s career averages in the NBA. In 41 games with the Jazz last season, the 12-year veteran averaged 10.9 points, 10.4 rebounds, 4.8 assists, and 1.3 steals per contest. He recorded those numbers while shooting 50.3% from the field and 35.2% from beyond the three-point line. We’re just past the halfway mark in the qualifying round for the FIBA World Cup. Bosnia and Herzegovina still has five matchups remaining on the schedule in the qualifiers. They are set to take on Lithuania on Monday, August 31, then won’t play again until November 26 against Iceland. The November game might be difficult for Jusuf Nurkic to make, as the NBA season will be underway. However, timing and scheduling for the upcoming campaign may change for the FIBA World Cup games. Bosnia and Herzegovina is tied for last place in Group J with just five games remaining in the qualifying round. The official FIBA World Cup tournament does not begin until next summer, as it will play out from August 27 to September 12. The tournament will take place in four different cities in Qatar, where 32 teams will battle it out for the championship. articles.title: Radio Rallies Around Dolly Parton After Her Death, Led by ‘9 to 5’
articles.summary: From 62 songs in a row in Nashville to deep cuts and cross-format airplay, programmers have responded to a loss unlike almost any other.
articles._body: For nearly 60 years, Dolly Parton moved country radio. In the days after her Aug. 25 death , she did it again. As tributes poured in around the world, U.S. radio broke from normal programming, loaded up on Parton’s music and reached across her deep catalog. Some stations even handed over their airwaves to her. Related Will Dolly Parton Earn Her First Billboard 200 No. 1 Album Posthumously? Dolly Parton Had the Second-Most Streams of Any Artist on the Day of Her Death Dolly Parton’s Top Billboard Hot Country Songs Hits According to Mediabase, encompassing all its U.S.-monitored terrestrial radio stations, Parton’s recordings drew more than 13,300 spins during a seven-day tracking period through Aug. 27, up from about 620 in the comparable previous period, a 2,000%-plus increase. Her music was heard on more than 930 stations, compared with about 135 previously, with 790-plus joining or returning to her catalog. A Catalog Six Decades Deep There was plenty to choose from. On reporters to Billboard ’s Country Airplay chart, which has tracked the format’s reach since its 1990 launch, Parton logged 28 entries during her lifetime, led by “Rockin’ Years,” with Ricky Van Shelton (1991), and as featured on “When I Get Where I’m Going,” with Brad Paisley (2006), both No. 1s. On the longer-running Hot Country Songs, her history totals 113 titles, dating to her 1967 debut, including 25 No. 1s — the most among women in the list’s history. In Nashville, iHeartMedia country WSIX threw out its playbook following news of Parton’s death, turning the station over to her music and to tributes from listeners and the local music community. “Wall-to-wall with the announcement and immediate tribute to Dolly,” iHeartCountry evp Rod Phillips tells Billboard . “We changed the format for Dolly, which turned into 62 songs in a row, plus more throughout the night and [Wednesday].” Other iHeartCountry stations increased Parton’s on-air footprint to multiple songs per hour, Phillips says. The company also launched a #GoodDeedsForDolly campaign encouraging listeners to perform acts of kindness in her memory. “After more than 35 years in radio,” Phillips says, “I’m not sure I’ve ever seen a reaction like we are experiencing with Dolly’s passing.” Beyond the Hits The tribute went well beyond the most obvious compositions. Across the Country Airplay panel, programmers played 66 different Parton titles in the days since her death, stretching from 1967’s “Dumb Blonde” to 2023’s “Wrecking Ball,” featuring Miley Cyrus (her goddaughter). Parton’s 1981 smash “9 to 5” — her first of two Billboard Hot 100 No. 1s — led with 799 spins across 135 stations in the week ending Aug. 27, followed closely by two 1974 Hot Country Songs leaders: “Jolene,” with 725 spins on 134 stations, and “I Will Always Love You,” with 665 spins across 133 stations. But programmers kept digging. At Connoisseur’s KUPL Portland, Ore., music director Jamie Tanchyk says that the station initially played Parton twice an hour before moving to hourly airplay. Personalities introduced the songs and talked about their own connections to her. “We chose to spin a few fan favorites that don’t typically see much airplay on ‘new country’ stations such as ours,” Tanchyk tells Billboard , citing “Two Doors Down,” “Why’d You Come in Here Lookin’ Like That,” “Here You Come Again” and “Coat of Many Colors,” while also leaning on “Jolene,” “9 to 5” and “I Will Always Love You.” Across the panel, 15 titles received one spin from one station each, including “Me and Little Andy,” “Baby I’m Burnin’ ” and “The Lord Is My Shepherd,” a rare departure for a medium known for relatively tight libraries and rotations. “Dolly was always bigger than country music,” Tanchyk continues. “She wasn’t simply a singer and entertainer. She was a true icon with a larger-than-life personality. Her relevance spanned generations and extended into so many different parts of our lives.” Related Fearless, Fabulous Dolly Parton and What We Can All Learn From Her: A Remembrance This One’s Personal That connection was personal for many in the business. Tim Roberts, Audacy vp of country, recalls a backstage meeting that he arranged years ago between Parton and a three-year-old girl with congenital heart disease who idolized her. In a crowded backstage area, Roberts says, Parton spotted the girl and walked immediately to her. “It was one of the greatest moments I’ve ever seen any artist do for someone,” Roberts says. “It was a beautiful moment from Dolly that truly showed the depth of her character.” Other Audacy stations responded with an expanded Parton playlist and special programming woven into their syndicated shows. Katie & Company , heard mostly in middays, featured Parton during its Superstar Power Hour, while The Rob & Holly Show , aired largely in evenings, ran a Parton-centric “top seven at 7″ countdown. At Cumulus Nashville, country WSM-FM afternoon host Tyler Reese went all in on Parton, notes the company’s vp of country, Travis Daily. Stories on the kindness she extended to people from all walks of life took center stage. “It really was incredible to listen to the outpour,” Daily tells Billboard . “Dolly is one of one and a real loss for the world.” Bigger Than Country Parton’s increased airplay was hardly confined to Nashville. WSM-AM and WSIX-FM ranked among stations taking the lead, but stations in Dallas, Knoxville, Tenn., and Austin, Texas, also leaned heavily into her music. Devotion ran deepest across the South and Appalachia, from Charleston, W. Va., to Birmingham and Mobile, Ala., even as her music reached coast to coast, from Portland, Maine, to Anchorage, Alaska. The response extended to satellite radio, too. SiriusXM launched a dedicated Dolly Parton Tribute Channel (105) built around her music and related artists and collaborators, augmented by listener recollections. Back on terrestrial radio, Parton’s reach stretched beyond country formats. H

articles.title: Will Dolphins’ Malik Willis, De’Von Achane play vs. Falcons?
articles.summary: Malik Willis and De’Von Achane will not play in the Miami Dolphins’ preseason finale against the Atlanta Falcons on Friday night. Many other starters will sit as well. Their absences will leave Miami focused primarily on evaluating the players competing for spots on its initial 53-man roster. Acc
articles._body: Malik Willis and De’Von Achane will not play in the Miami Dolphins’ preseason finale against the Atlanta Falcons on Friday night. Many other starters will sit as well. Their absences will leave Miami focused primarily on evaluating the players competing for spots on its initial 53-man roster. According to NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe, Cam Miller will start at quarterback, while Quinn Ewers will sit out because of an injury. Wolfe added that Miami is managing several injuries and depth concerns, making the team’s remaining roster battles the priority Friday. The most fascinating storyline, however, will be on Atlanta’s sideline. Former Dolphins quarterback Tua Tagovailoa will start against his old team while attempting to secure the Falcons’ QB1 job. Michael Penix Jr. will not play, giving Tagovailoa the entire spotlight in what could become his final audition before Atlanta selects its Week 1 starter. Tagovailoa has struggled to separate himself since joining the Falcons. A strong performance against Miami would provide a fitting way for him to strengthen his case, even if the Dolphins are resting several important players. Willis’ absence means there will not be a direct comparison between two potential starters. Achane sitting also removes one of Miami’s most explosive offensive players from the matchup. That may take some star power away from the Dolphins, but it only increases the attention surrounding Tagovailoa. The preseason finale may primarily be about roster evaluation for Miami. For its former quarterback, it could determine whether he opens the regular season atop Atlanta’s depth chart. articles.title: R&B Up-And-Comer of the Month TheARTI$t On The Moment She Realized ‘This Is My Purpose’
articles.summary: The rising Jersey artist talks about her viral single "Sober," new album 'DND' and touring with Kehlani.
articles._body: Before TheARTI$t knew exactly what she wanted her artist name to be, she was already practicing becoming one. Born Erica McCauley, the rising R&B artist has been a dancer, a preschool teacher and a basketball player, past lives that might seem disconnected from music at first glance, but each left lessons that she now carries onto the stage, into the studio and her everyday life. Dancing taught her precision. Teaching nurtured her creativity. Basketball taught her persistence: no matter how tired or exhausted she was, she refused to leave the gym until she made her last shot. When her 2023 single “Sober” went viral on TikTok, TheARTI$t began to understand the power of allowing listeners into parts of her private life. Now, with her latest project DND , a growing presence in the next generation of R&B and a supporting role on the road with Kehlani, she’s entering a new chapter, one defined by showing everyone who she truly is, on and off the stage. TheARTI$t’s newfound evolution extends far beyond music. Her recent collaboration with footwear brand Marc Nolan on the IRIS. loafer reflects an interest in fashion and design that has been part of her identity since childhood, while the shoe’s themes of love, devotion and connection mirror the values she wants to carry into everything she creates. If there’s one thing TheARTI$t wants people to understand about where she is in 2026, it’s that this is only the beginning. “I’m literally just scratching the surface in everything,” she says. “I’m so far from finished.” In our conversation, Billboard ’s August 2026 R&B Up-and-Comer TheARTI$t gets candid about the experiences that shaped her, learning to embrace vulnerability, finding community through her music and stepping into a new era of her artistry. Before music became the path, you were a dancer and preschool teacher and even considered basketball. What do you think those different versions of yourself taught you about the artist you are today? Dancing comes with a lot of practice and precision as well, and I feel like I carry that with me in my performance. Even in moments like these, just being precise in talking to the press and having interviews, even meeting people in the public eye, I just feel like it’s important to carry myself a certain way. And it’s kind of the same thing when it comes to dancing. As far as being a teacher, working with the younger age, like two, three year olds, the creativity that they have at such a young age truly is just inspiring. It can come down to anything, something as small as coloring to the way they put the blocks together. It just brings out the child in me, honestly. When I played basketball, I wouldn’t leave the gym until I made a shot. No matter if I just had a game, if I just had a two-hour practice, I’m exhausted, if I have an injury, I do not leave the gym without shooting and making it. And I feel like that’s the same thing in the studio and on stage. I feel like when I go into the booth, I don’t wanna leave the studio session if I’m like, “I didn’t accomplish anything.” You were born Erica McCauley, but you perform as TheARTI$t. What does that name represent to you, and where does Erica end and TheARTI$t begin? I feel like “TheARTI$t” represents everything that is me. I feel like everything in this world is art. You walk outside, look at the trees, it’s art. The cars driving, that’s art. And I feel like me as a whole, I’m so many things, but when it all comes down to it, I’m just an artist, truly, in my heart of hearts. And I feel like that’s how I wanna be represented. That’s how I want to represent myself. I’m just an artist. I’m full of art. And I feel like Erica, it’s never-ending because this is truly who I am. When I get off the stage, I don’t turn off anything. I’m just the same person on the stage, off the stage, in the studio, out of the studio. I’ve been learning lately, though, to have moments where I do kind of separate the two because I feel like it’s also important for me to nurture Erica still in order for TheARTI$t to be who TheARTI$t has to be. Your music is rooted in vulnerability, but vulnerability can be uncomfortable. Has there ever been a song where you questioned whether you were sharing too much? Yeah, a few songs. I feel like “Sober” was one of them, but I was so in my zone as far as getting that off my chest because I made that song years after I went through that experience. But I realized in that moment, in that session, that, yo, this is what’s been holding me back, the fact that I’m holding on to this. So I felt like I was just throwing it out there, and I’m like, “Damn, what if the person hears it?” But then it came to a point where I’m like, it doesn’t matter. Because once the feedback I got was like, “Me too,” that’s when I knew that my purpose was bigger than what I believed it to be at that time. ’Cause I was very, very early in my career, and it’s like, yo, it’s so much bigger than me. And I truly felt like that was when I realized, yo, this is my purpose. “Sober” took off on TikTok in 2023 and really accelerated your visibility. When you look back at that moment now, what do you think changed for you? I believe my ability to express changed, just even in my personal life outside of being an artist. I feel like I don’t really talk much about the things that I go through. I don’t want people to feel like they have to treat me differently or feel sorry. I’m a giver, a natural caretaker. So I feel like ever since making that song, it truly opened up a door for me to just be able to be vulnerable, period, and make music in my life and have conversations with a stranger. You know what I mean? I feel like it’s so necessary. It is so necessary to be expressive, honestly. What did the experience of watching people connect with “Sober” teach you about what your audience is looking for from you? It taught me that I believe they’re looking for someone who understands. articles.summary: The men’s FIBA World Cup Qualifiers got underway this week with Atlanta Hawks guard Buddy Hield among the several NBA players participating with their home countries. Hield was initially acquired by the Hawks as part of the Jonathan Kuminga trade at the deadline last season, although he was not f
articles._body: The men’s FIBA World Cup Qualifiers got underway this week with Atlanta Hawks guard Buddy Hield among the several NBA players participating with their home countries . Hield was initially acquired by the Hawks as part of the Jonathan Kuminga trade at the deadline last season, although he was not featured prominently in the team’s rotation. But suiting up for the Bahamas, Buddy Hield certainly made Hawks fans take notice with a flamethrower of a performance against Uruguay in a win. He finished with 28 points, seven rebounds, four assists and two steals while shooting 8-of-16 from the field and 6-of-11 from the 3-point line. Following the trade, Hield appeared in only seven games for the Hawks at just a little over seven minutes per game. He averaged 5.1 points and 1.1 rebounds with splits of 48.1 percent shooting from the field, 41.2 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 100 percent shooting from the free-throw line. During the Hawks’ opening round playoff series loss to the New York Knicks, he saw action in only two games at a little over six minutes per. Despite not being featured in the team’s rotation, the Hawks still opted to fully guarantee Hield’s contract for the upcoming season as it was only partially guaranteed. He holds a team option for the 2027-28 season before potentially hitting unrestricted free agency. The No. 6 overall pick in the 2016 NBA Draft, Hield will be entering his 11th season in the league. In addition to the Warriors and Hawks, he’s also had stints with the New Orleans Pelicans, Sacramento Kings, Indiana Pacers and Philadelphia 76ers. Communities from Lansing, Michigan, to Pflugerville, Texas, are ending their relationship with Flock, largely over concerns regarding out-of-control surveillance, unwanted data sharing, high expenses, and reports of police abusing the tool . Secure Justice , an Oakland-based advocacy group, has recorded 214 cities and counties that have dropped Flock since 2021 . articles.title: Coach Cal sides with Greg Sankey in Kentucky’s fight for Mark Mitchell
articles.summary: SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey does not want Mark Mitchell to play for Kentucky. It does not appear John Calipari wants Mark Mitchell to play for Kentucky, either. Sankey doubled down on the league’s intraconference transfer rule, which bars players from moving within the SEC outside designated
articles._body: SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey does not want Mark Mitchell to play for Kentucky . It does not appear John Calipari wants Mark Mitchell to play for Kentucky, either. Sankey doubled down on the league’s intraconference transfer rule, which bars players from moving within the SEC outside designated portal windows, with penalties ranging from fines of 50 percent of a sport’s annual budget to a half-season suspension for the head coach who rosters a player in violation. On the football side of things, this is an obvious jab at Lane Kiffin and LSU for not only taking commitments from NFL players recently cut from training camp, but also doing so from inside the conference. The SEC handled the first part of that equation by banning former pros, a rule that did not apply to Mitchell, since he did not sign a contract with the Denver Nuggets, despite a brief Summer League stint with the franchise. That was intended for the NFL guys, along with RJ Luis, who is trying to play for Will Wade and the LSU basketball program after signing two-way and Exhibit 10 contracts in the NBA. Sankey’s intraconference ban did apply to Mitchell, however, despite the temporary restraining order giving him access to the portal. “Expect the SEC to hold Kentucky to account here, as sources said the league believes it has the latitude and legitimacy to hold the line,” CBS Sports’ Matt Norlander reported on Thursday. Now, Mitchell is fighting back in court , with the next steps toward clarity coming at his next hearing scheduled for Monday in Louisville. Until then, Coach Cal is speaking his mind about all of the chaos in a sit-down interview with Andy Katz of NCAA.com. “I don’t begrudge any coach trying to do something to help his team win. I don’t begrudge a basketball player trying to get a fifth year because he’s going to make a lot of money — because if he were a pro, he’d be in the NBA or he’d be in Europe making a lot of money,” Calipari said this week. “The issue becomes, what is it doing to our recruiting with young kids? “Right now, we’ve got a lot of coaches making decisions to bring kids in late August, early September. I don’t begrudge them, but for me, what does that do to the players in my program if I did it? What does it do to a player that I have recruited and talked to? Maybe one that was waiting his turn? Maybe it’s a freshman? How do you have trust when you walk in in September and say, ‘We just changed. I know what we told you, but that’s not going to happen now because this kid’s coming in. You’ll have to wait.'” His solution was to allow players on rosters with late additions, like Kentucky with Mitchell, to enter the portal themselves without penalty. That’s if fifth-years have to make their way back into the game for this upcoming season, before 5-for-5 kicks in, allowing everybody a fifth year of eligibility. No more loopholes and waivers to skirt around rules — because that means the rule doesn’t work in the first place, as Calipari put it. “Do you know why we’re in the position we’re in? It’s called waivers,” he continued. “You have a rule, that is the rule. … If a rule can have waivers, the rule’s bad. It’s a bad rule. You put in a bad rule. Put in a rule that’s five years, no waivers, one-time transfer. If you’re 19 years or younger, you’re an amateur. It takes all the case-by-case waiver BS out of this.” For now, he likes the power conference pushback on keeping pros out of the top leagues, just as he likes the SEC holding firm on its intraconference transfer rules. That, of course, includes his former school adding an All-SEC talent at the 11th hour. “We need guardrails now. The leagues did the right thing,” Calipari said. “We need these commissioners to step in here, and I’ll use the term, be the assholes. Be that, and then have rules that there are no waivers. … “I like what the SEC is doing. If a player doesn’t like what the SEC is doing, what? Go to another league. And if a coach doesn’t like what the SEC is doing? Go to another league, which they’re free to do. Just do it. Make it hard. Do it right.” He wasn’t specifically calling out Mitchell and Kentucky, but he certainly wasn’t shying away from his situation inside the league.

articles.title: Cale Makar signs record-breaking $163.2 million contract extension with Avalanche
articles.summary: The Colorado Avalanche have finally completed their most important piece of offseason business, re-signing superstar defenseman Cale Makar to a record-breaking eight-year, $163.2 million extension that should keep the Canadian in Denver for most of the rest of his career. Makar will become the NH
articles._body: The Colorado Avalanche have finally completed their most important piece of offseason business, re-signing superstar defenseman Cale Makar to a record-breaking eight-year, $163.2 million extension that should keep the Canadian in Denver for most of the rest of his career. Makar will become the NHL’s first $20 million dollar player in terms of average annual value, signing the richest deal in league history, the team announced on Friday. The pact will run through the 2034-35 campaign. He’s established himself as the National Hockey League’s premier defenseman, helping the Avs win the Stanley Cup in 2022 and being named a Norris Trophy finalist in each of the last six seasons. He won the award in 2022 and 2025. Sportsnet hockey insider Elliotte Friedman first reported that the Avs were closing in on an extension with the defenseman on Thursday, while Evan Rawal of The Denver Gazette shared that Colorado agreed to terms with Makar on Wednesday night. The 27-year-old will first play out the final season of a six-year, $54 million contract he signed back in July of 2021. The Calgary, Alberta native was set to become an unrestricted free agent next summer. Makar has been on a remarkable run since chipping in 50 points in 57 games in his rookie campaign in 2019-20. Since then, he’s scored 124 goals and 457 points in 413 regular-season contests, adding a +156 rating while averaging over 25 minutes of ice time per game. He’s also been a difference-maker in the postseason, amassing 25 goals and 84 points in 80 Stanley Cup Playoff contests. He won the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP after scoring 29 points in 20 games in the 2022 playoffs. It’s been an incredible start to Makar’s career; he’s already 75th in all-time scoring among defensemen, and he is still just 27. If he continues at this pace — and plays 1,200 games — he will finish third in all-time scoring, behind only NHL legends Ray Bourque and Paul Coffey. Avalanche general manager Joe Sakic said earlier this week that he was confident Makar would sign an extension before the start of the new NHL season. That business is now complete, and Makar will be a focal point in Colorado’s quest to bring another championship to the Mile High City with its current superstar core. After winning the Presidents’ Trophy in 2025-26, the Avalanche suffered a disappointing four-game sweep at the hands of the Vegas Golden Knights in the 2026 Western Conference Final. With Makar locked up, the Avalanche will aim to bring a second Stanley Cup in six seasons to Denver in 2026-27. Why Pelicans expect crucial improvement at this key position in 2026-27 season
articles.summary: For the past few seasons, the Zion Williamson-led New Orleans Pelicans’ frontcourt has been a statistical sore spot. They have been near the bottom in rebounding and block rate while being routinely exploited at the rim. Even finishing at the rim has been a problem for Trey Murphy III, Herb Jones
articles._body: For the past few seasons, the Zion Williamson-led New Orleans Pelicans’ frontcourt has been a statistical sore spot. They have been near the bottom in rebounding and block rate while being routinely exploited at the rim. Even finishing at the rim has been a problem for Trey Murphy III , Herb Jones, Yves Missi, and Derik Queen. However, a quiet confidence has taken hold that 2026-27 will be different. Fortunately for new defensive-minded head coach Jamahl Mosley, fans still fretting over a relatively quiet status quo offseason already have some evidence. Yves Missi gave Cameroon 24 points, nine rebounds and four blocks in a 78-62 win over Nigeria in the second round of 2027 FIBA World Cup qualifying. Missi made nine of 13 shots and grabbed four offensive rebounds in 27 minutes. Karlo Matkovic was even more efficient for Croatia. Matkovic needed only 17 minutes to score 17 points in a 115-80 win over Latvia, making all eight of his field-goal attempts, including a 3-pointer. Both big men were providing exactly the sort of contributions the Pelicans will need to see more often beginning in October. There are encouraging developments closer to the Crescent City as well. Stephen Lew-Imagn Images Zion Williamson’s publicly documented offseason fitness work with trainer Kris Chrisp has drawn positive reviews, especially when shooting down unfounded trade chatter . Trey Murphy III added 20 pounds of muscle and has said he aims to make the All-Star team while averaging 30 points per game. Herb Jones is healthy again after injury setbacks and is positioned to contend once more for NBA All-Defense recognition. Coming off an ACL tear that cost him the entire 2024-25 season, Saddiq Bey posted 17.7 points, 5.6 rebounds, and 2.5 assists on 45.1% shooting. The 27-year-old emerged as a key contributor while posting career highs last season. He will be up for a potential four-year, $60 million contract if that progress continues. Derik Queen is expected to take a second-year step forward, while Trendon Watford provides reliable reserve production as a rebounder who can compete for minutes off the bench. Christian Koloko arrives at training camp with a clear role and path toward a roster spot. Taken together, the Pelicans see a young, deep frontcourt entering its collective prime. Internal growth from that core, better injury luck across the roster, improved chemistry after a full offseason together, and what several players have described as a chip-on-the-shoulder mentality are the driving forces behind New Orleans’ belief that its frontcourt numbers will look much better sooner rather than later. Well, there is no later if they look lazy on the boards again; someone would get traded if the frontcourt is viewed as a liability under Mosley. Whether that optimism translates into the standings will depend on health and consistency, two things that have eluded the Pelicans in recent years. But the pieces, on paper, are in place for a frontcourt built to take a real step forward. Vans’ Baddest Winter Boot Is Even Better as a Sneaker
articles.summary: Vans releases the Standard Low, a low-top sneaker-ish version of its toughest MTE winter boots.
articles._body: Remember Vans' MTE Standard snow boots? Well, they're essentially sneakers now called the Standard Low. The brand's new Standard Low takes all the great things about its baddest winter boots and brings them into an even more stylish, low-top sneaker style. It's still waterproof, warm, and wet-weather ready. It also keeps the All-Trac outsoles, which are designed specifically for cold, slippery terrains. But the Standard Low is even slicker, presenting cleaner uppers dressed in smooth suede. Vans has started the model off with two nice colorways: "Demitasse Brown" (like those r ecent tasty Slip-ons ) and classic black. They're now available on Vans' website for $125. We honestly should've seen this coming. The skateboarding brand already downsized with the Standard Mid boots, which snowboarder Blake Paul took for a spin in 2025. It only made sense to keep going lower. And it did. Vans isn't alone, either. Nike also recently dropped the top on its Air Max Goadome boots , resulting in basically an even cooler dadcore sneaker . It happens to the greatest of winter boots, it seems. Highsnobiety has affiliate marketing partnerships, which means we may receive a commission from your purchase. articles.title: Giants make final decision on playing Jaxson Dart vs. Jets
articles.summary: The New York Giants are set to play against the New York Jets in their preseason finale, and many want to know if Jaxson Dart will make an appearance. It looks like they’ve made their decision, and fans will have to wait until Week 1 to see the second-year player, according to ESPN’s
articles._body: The New York Giants are set to play against the New York Jets in their preseason finale, and many want to know if Jaxson Dart will make an appearance. It looks like they’ve made their decision , and fans will have to wait until Week 1 to see the second-year player, according to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler. “Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart is not expected to play tonight vs. Jets, per sources. Jameis Winston and Brandon Allen are next in line,” Fowler wrote on X, formerly Twitter. The Giants definitely want to play it safe by keeping Dart fresh until the regular season, and it also means they’ve seen enough of what he can do in training camp and practice to keep him sidelined. At the same time, it would’ve been nice to see him in a new offensive system, and getting reps against another team would help. There have been people against the idea of the starters not playing in the preseason, and it’s always a topic of discussion when teams do it. For teams that have adopted a new system over the offseason, it would make sense for them to see the starters in action during the preseason. The Giants are one of those teams, bringing John Harbaugh in as the new head coach and making changes across the board. They’re also still a young team, and they need as many reps as they can before the season begins. Dart had a solid rookie season for the Giants, but it was the concussions that were concerning for him. The hope is that he can protect himself better going into his second season, while also having the necessary help around him to succeed. articles.title: Notre Dame football names four captains for 2026 season
articles.summary: Notre Dame has named captains for the 2026 season, the Irish announced Friday evening. Here's who will wear a "C" on their jersey.
articles._body: Notre Dame football has named four captains for the 2026 season, the Irish announced Friday evening. Wearing the “C” on their jerseys this year will be senior linebacker Drayk Bowen , senior safety Adon Shuler , junior quarterback CJ Carr and senior wide receiver Jordan Faison . Bowen and Shuler are both two-time captains, the 28th and 29th in program history. The four of them will lead an extremely motivated Notre Dame team through a season with national championship expectations, leading the charge to “leave no doubt” after the Irish were snubbed from the College Football Playoff last year. Carr has been a leader since the moment he stepped on campus. He’s been the proverbial “quarterback of the future” since he committed to Notre Dame in 2022, and he made that official when he beat out Kenny Minchey for the starting job in 2025. Carr threw for 2,741 yards, 24 touchdowns and 6 interceptions, producing an elite pass efficiency rating of 168.06. Faison’s ascent to captain is remarkable, because he began his career as a walk-on whose primary sport was lacrosse. He won the national championship with men’s lacrosse in 2024 and came back to contribute to the football team’s own run to the title game, gaining respect from his teammates along the way. After becoming Notre Dame’s No. 1 wide receiver with 49 receptions for 640 yards in 2025, he gave up lacrosse to focus exclusively on football. That decision clearly paid off. According to Notre Dame Athletics, Faison is believed to be the program’s fifth captain since 2000 who began his career as a walk-on. The others are Shane Walton (2002), Joe Schmidt (2015), Austin Webster (2017) and Chris Finke (2019). Bowen and Shuler, meanwhile, will run it back as stalwarts in the middle of a Notre Dame defense that had several captain candidates around them. Junior cornerback Leonard Moore , sixth-year defensive tackle Jason Onye , senior defensive end Boubacar Traore and more are considered leaders as well. But the work Bowen and Shuler do to get everyone lined up and keep the defense on the same page is irreplaceable. Notre Dame begins its season against Wisconsin in a Shamrock Series matchup on Sept. 6 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisc. articles.summary: Week 0 of the college football season kicks off on Saturday. Many of the top offensive units in college fantasy football have star quarterbacks leading the charge. The wide re
articles._body: Week 0 of the college football season kicks off on Saturday. Last year, six different wideouts popped off for over 1,200 yards, while 16 of them found the end zone ten or more times. Many of the top offensive units in college fantasy football have star quarterbacks leading the charge . The wide receivers in those units could benefit, but there are multiple other top guys who are the only option in their system and could hit big. Some of the top receivers from last year are now gone from the college ranks, such as Skyler Bell and Makai Lemon. Still, there are some returning stars, such as Malachi Toney and Jeremiah Smith. With some receivers in new places, some working with new offensive coordinators, and others returning to great spots, these are the top ten college fantasy wide receivers in 2026. 1. Jeremiah Smith | Ohio State Adam Cairns/Columbus Dispatch / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images What receiver is better in the nation than Jeremiah Smith from Ohio State? He was WR2 in 2024 and WR3 in 2025. The stud receiver put up 1,315 yards with 15 touchdowns in 2024, and followed it up with 87 receptions for 1,243 yards and 12 scores last year. Smith is the reigning Big Ten Receiver of the Year and caught just about everything, bringing in an insane 79.8 percent of his targets last year. With Julian Sayin at quarterback and his accuracy, he should be in for a good year. Still, this is the first time being the top wideout in the offense in every game. He had Carnell Tate with him last year, and both Tate and Emeka Egbuka the year before. Still, he put up insane numbers and should do so again this year. 2. Malachi Toney | Miami (FL) Malachi Toney finished the 2025 campaign as WR1 in terms of fantasy points. He came away with 1,211 yards on 109 catche wth 10 touchdowns for Miami. He led FBS in receptions, while setting a Miami record for receiving yards in a season. Toney also ran for 113 yards and a touchdown, while completing four of seven passes for 82 yards and another two scores. Further, Toney did all of this as a true freshman. The receiver is not even 19 years old yet and is already setting records. He will have a new quarterback this year, and there is always the possibility of the sophomore slump, but his already proven track record shows he should get plenty of volume and be a top fantasy receiver again in 2026. 3. Amare Thomas | Houston Amare Thomas is the best receiver no one is talking about. After two solid years at UAB, he burst onto the scene last year at Houston. Thomas hauled in 67 receptions for 966 yards and 12 touchdowns. He was not the top target to start the season, though. Stephon Johnson went down in Week 5, and Thomas immediately stepped up, being named First-Team All-Big 12. After Week 5 on, he hauled in 51 receptions for 682 yards and ten touchdowns. Now, Thomas is entrenched as Connor Weigman’s top target, and his numbers should show that. 4. Nick Marsh | Indiana Rich Janzaruk/Herald-Times / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Last year, Elijah Surratt was WR13 overall, coming out of the Indiana offense. He did this while Omar Cooper Jr. produced on the other side, plus Roman Hemby and Kaelon Black both running for over 1,000 yards. Now, Indiana needs to replace that production, and Nick Marsh is the man to do it. Marsh brought in 59 receptions for 662 yards and six scores while having Aidan Chiles and Alessio Milivokevic throw him the ball. Marsh had 108 targets last year, but Michigan State quarterbacks were 72nd nationally in passing efficiency, limiting his production. Now, he has Josh Hoover throwing him the ball and in a much better offense. This is a massive upside play, and Marsh has all the talent needed to be one of the best in the nation. 5. Cam Coleman | Texas On the same line as Marsh, Cam Coleman is a receiver that upgraded his situation . Despite having to deal with three different quarterbacks throwing him the ball, including Jackson Arnold getting the bulk of the reps, Coleman put up a solid year. He brought in 56 receptions for 708 yards and five touchdowns. He also had a late-season star performance, bringing in ten catches for 143 yards and a score against Vanderbilt. Coleman already has the size and ball tracking ability to make him elite, but now has a quarterback to go with it, as Arch Manning will be slinging him the rock. 6. KJ Duff | Rutgers KJ Duff started the season with Rutgers in 2025 as the other option in the offense, behind Ian Strong. He did not end the season that way. He brought in 60 receptions for 1,084 yards and seven touchdowns. Duff did this all on a team that won just five games and while being doubled much of the end of the season. Heading into his junior season, he is the top wideout on the team, and with very little competition for targets, he will be the focus of the Rutgers passing attack. Rutgers has a solid defense and running game, which could lead to tight games and needing big plays late. That is where Duff is going to shine. 7. Beau Sparks | Texas State Matt Bush/Special to the Clarion Ledger / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images The only non-Power Conference receiver on the list comes from the same place as on the quarterback list, Texas State. Beau Sparks was a massive surprise last year. He was being drafted in round 20 or later in most leagues, and finished as WR5. Getting Sparks outside one of the first three rounds is not going to be an option this year. Soparks finished the year with 84 receptions for 1,200 yards and 10 touchdowns. He also scored once on the ground. Further, he became the top red-zone target for Brad Jackson, and will likely be that again. He gets a ton of volume and is one of the most efficient receivers in the nation, which makes him one ofthe best fantasy options as well. 8.
