articles.title: In Canada: OVO Sells Majority Stake to Authentic Brands Group, Drake Retains Significant Ownership
articles.summary: Canada stands firm on CanCon streaming regulations and the Juno Awards restructure several categories for 2027.
articles._body: October’s Very Own has a new home. Authentic Brands Group has announced the acquisition of a majority stake in the intellectual property of October’s Very Own, also known as OVO, the lifestyle brand and apparel company co-founded by Drake . The Toronto rapper will retain a significant ownership stake and remain involved with the brand as its driving force, continuing to shape its creative vision. Related Here’s Every Canadian Artist Who Has Topped the Billboard Hot 100 Dale Morris, Nashville Manager Who Guided Careers of Alabama & Kenny Chesney, Dies at 89 HYBE Pledges Over $300k for Colombia Earthquake Recovery Vince Holding Corp. (VNCE), a longtime partner of Authentic, will be taking over OVO’s operating business, handling clothing design, product development, merchandising and retail stores. “We’re just a couple kids from Toronto who started something we believed in. Here we are 20 years later, same kids with bigger dreams. Authentic and VNCE are the perfect partners to help us continue to grow,” says Drake. The chart-topping rapper co-founded OVO in 2008 with his close friends and collaborators, entrepreneur Oliver El-Khatib and producer Noah “40” Shebib, originally as a blog and lifestyle movement. The brand went on to become a Canadian staple worldwide, notably through its signature black-and-gold owl logo. It made major expansions into high-end clothing and streetwear. The OVO Sound label also spun off from that brand. In addition to its online store, OVO runs twelve flagship stores across Canada, the U.S. and the U.K., with locations in Toronto, New York and London. The brand has fostered collaborative relationships with some of the world’s biggest brands and institutions, curating several high-profile collections in tandem with the likes of MLB, New Era, UFC and the NBA, including an instant-classic merchandise capsule celebrating the Toronto Raptors’ 2019 NBA championship title. “OVO has earned a place among the world’s most influential lifestyle brands because it has always stood for something authentic and unmistakable,” says Jamie Salter , Authentic’s founder and executive chairman. “Drake and his team have built something with incredible cultural influence. We see a significant opportunity to take that even further, opening new markets, building new businesses and reaching more people around the world without losing what makes OVO, OVO.” Authentic Brands Group is a major licensing company in the U.S. whose portfolio includes the ownership of major brands like Sports Illustrated magazine, Champion and Nautica, as well as the licensing for the estates of celebrity legends Elvis Presley , Marilyn Monroe and Muhammad Ali. Now, it’s taking on one of Canada’s biggest brands, whose global success has long been grounded in its hometown of Toronto and the city’s essence and culture. Read more  here .  Canada Stands Firm on CanCon Streaming Regulations Despite Opposition from the U.S. Canada is standing firm when it comes to CanCon. The Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) confirmed that it is sticking with its plans to regulate how Canadian content is presented and made available to users on major streaming services, following recent resistance from the United States. A spokesperson from the CRTC  tells the  Canadian Press  it will move forward to determine exactly how streamers must ensure Canadian content is available and visible to audiences and is still finalizing the dates for the regulatory proceedings. The ongoing controversy surrounding the  Online Streaming Act , which became law in 2023, reached a fever pitch over the weekend after trade talks between Canada and the U.S. fell through, partly due to the Trump administration’s last-minute demand for American streaming platforms to be exempt from Canadian content regulations. “There were some things we wouldn’t do. We were not prepared to compromise Canada’s sovereignty or undermine our key industries,” Mark Carney said in an  extensive speech  following the collapse of the discussions. “We were not prepared to compromise on our sovereignty, the protection of the French language, and our culture. To our American colleagues, let us be clear: for my government and for Canada, these issues were never on the table, even though the United States tried until the very last minute.” It’s the latest development in a continuous back-and-forth between the Canadian government, Canadian companies and U.S. streaming companies, which stems from the controversial Online Streaming Act introduced by the Trudeau government in 2023. In its implementation, the CRTC mandated a  5% tax contribution  on all broadcasters making over $25 million, intended to fund the production of Canadian, French language and Indigenous content, which caused  major pushback  from affected streaming giants like Spotify, Apple Music and Amazon Music. Back in May, the CRTC announced plans to  triple that contribution to 15%  for audiovisual streaming services like Netflix, Amazon Prime Video and Apple TV in an attempt to stabilize the $200 million funding rate for Canadian companies. The Canadian government then stepped in and  announced a landmark, $600 million yearly investment , which includes covering the $200 million base contribution that would have otherwise been taxed on foreign streaming services. Beyond financial contributions, discoverability has also been a point of contention during discussions between Canada and the U.S. Back in December, Quebec passed Bill 109, the Act to affirm the cultural sovereignty of Québec, which sought to impose quotas on the amount of French-language content presented and promoted on the homepages of foreign streaming platforms like Netflix and Prime Video. Reds lose Ke’Bryan Hayes to injured list during Cubs series
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Reds have shown flashes of promise throughout the 2020s, but in the midst of what is trending to be a last-place campaign, it has become painfully obvious that this organization is far from solving the root of its problem. Although the front office has identified a few franchise pi
articles._body: The Cincinnati Reds have shown flashes of promise throughout the 2020s, but in the midst of what is trending to be a last-place campaign, it has become painfully obvious that this organization is far from solving the root of its problem . Although the front office has identified a few franchise pillars , it has mismanaged and misjudged talent at a worrying rate. Look no further than Ke’Bryan Hayes. The defensively elite third baseman was a poor hitter when he arrived in Cincy last summer, but he has tumbled even further in 2026. Injuries are only compounding his issues. He is landing on the shelf once again. The Reds are placing Hayes on the 10-day injured list (retroactive to Aug. 27) due to a left groin strain , per the team, and are recalling infielder Edwin Arroyo from Triple-A Louisville. The 2021 second-round draft pick last played for Cincinnati on July 29 and batted .244 with a .286 on-base percentage, .282 slugging percentage and .568 OPS in 44 games. He will try to get comfortable at the dish and provide the team with serviceable offensive production. But the Reds need Hayes to do the same. The two-time Gold Glove Award winner has five years remaining on his $70 million contract (club option in 2030), putting president of baseball operations Nick Krall in a tough spot moving forward. He is slashing .153/.213/.250/.463 with five home runs and eight RBIs in 211 plate appearances this season. Hopefully, Ke’Bryan Hayes will get the chance to rejoin the club and improve those numbers before year’s end. He could really use some good news, and so could Reds fans. articles.title: Nike's Crisp Black Denim Air Maxes Are Only Part "Jeaker"
articles.summary: Nike's latest Air Max 90 sneakers feature black denim moments, as well as other nice textures. So, don't call them "jeakers" just yet.
articles._body: Nike has released a new "Black Denim" Air Max 90 sneaker, which is actually only partially denim. So, don't call it another "jeaker." It turns out the new clean Air Maxes feature raw-edged denim and other nice textures. There's also creamy leather Swooshes, smooth nubuck, and tightly knit mesh, all bathed in black. This is not to say that Nike hasn't dropped full-denim Air Max 90s before (it has). The brand has also released denim Air Max sandals and Levi's x Air Max 95 sneakers . Although the newest pairs are only roughly 25% denim, they don't need the full "jeakers" moment to be good. They're just as nice-looking with a sliver of denim. It's also perfect for those easing their way into the denim-sneaker craze. It doesn't go full-throttle denim, but it offers just enough of the "jeaker" lifestyle . Speaking of which, the Nike Air Max 95 "Black Denim" sneakers are now up for grabs on Nike Luxembourg's website for €159.99, or around $185. articles.title: Warsh's 'quieter Fed' now includes a smidgen of guidance
DOJ is turning to an ancient body of law to capture Iranian oil tankers. It’s been so long since the U.S. used it, ‘we’d have to conduct a séance’
articles.summary: The Justice Department is reviving prize law, a centuries-old set of rules that could streamline the process of seizing enemy vessels.
articles._body: The Trump administration is bringing back a centuries-old legal tradition that would allow it to more easily seize Iranian oil tankers and sell off their assets. Aaron Reitz, who is the U.S. Attorney in the Houston-based Southern District of Texas,  confirmed to Fortune the revival of prize law, or a set of rules allowing for military forces to seize enemy vessels. “Our national security interests may require the United States military to seize vessels or cargo supporting the enemy during military conflict. If that happens, our federal courts must be ready to adjudicate the disposition of these captured vessels and cargo,” he said in a statement. “Prize law is an ancient body of maritime law—already codified in statute but which we are now reviving—that sets the rules for how seized maritime property is condemned, returned, or disposed of.” Invoking prize laws would allow U.S. forces to bolster the naval blockade of Iran and recoup costs from the war. The news was first reported by Bloomberg Law. Prize law contrasts with civil seizure laws that require the U.S. government to identify a statutory violation of a vessel and establish jurisdiction over that violation. It often entails extensive litigation, according to Michael Frevola, a maritime litigation partner at Holland & Knight LLP. By comparison, prize law does not require a captor to have a warrant or tie a vessel’s seizure to a violation of an existing stature. Rather than law enforcement authorities like the Coast Guard having to seize a vessel under civil seizure laws, the Department of Defense, usually through military force, can seize an enemy vessel instead. The ‘ancient’ roots of U.S. prize law Prize laws have existed since the Middle Ages, and have been baked into the U.S. legal canon since the beginning, with the Constitution outlining rules for capturing and confiscating enemy vessels during times of war in its Captures Clause .  During the 19th century, President Abraham Lincoln used the Prize Act of 1812 to blockade Confederate seaports —an act that was contested and eventually upheld by the Supreme Court. It was most recently invoked during the Spanish-American War , which legitimized the U.S. naval detainment of Spanish vessels as prizes of war. Reitz did not specify if the Justice Department will invoke the Prize Act of 1812, the Captures Clause, or another law. But the less complicated legal process for capturing an enemy vessel that prize law affords would have clear benefits for the Trump administration. “There’s definitely a financial interest in being able to sell the oil and being able to to sell the vessel and then just put that money into the coffers of the United States, which is another thing that this administration has shown is a priority,” Raymond Waid, a veteran naval officer and maritime lawyer at Liskow and Lewis, told Fortune . Will the Prize Act work in assisting the U.S. in the Iran war? Legal experts warned that while reviving prize law could in theory expedite the process of seizing Iranian ships, they anticipate ample legal complications that would hamper how effective this legal strategy really is. For one, there’s the sheer age of the law, which hasn’t been invoked since the Spanish-American War in 1898. “It’s not like the DOJ has some really veteran Prize Act litigators on their staff,” Frevola quipped. “So we’d have to conduct a séance to wind up getting serious counsel in terms of this.” The U.S. government will also need to prove that a capture takes place during a war with hostilities that are within congressional and presidential authority. Congress has not declared war against Iran, which may create some grey area around how appropriate prize law would be, and the lack of an official war declaration could also push Congress into getting more involved in a dispute it has largely avoided so far, Waid suggested. Allison Luzwick, a maritime lawyer and Frevola’s colleague at Holland & Knight LLP, told Fortune that the U.S. will also likely face litigation about the legality of its blockade and whether it was adequately declared and communicated. This is particularly sensitive for neutral vessels carrying cargo from other states and whether they’re subject to capture. “There’s going to be arguments about whether or not that vessel is even subject to the blockade, or if they received notice about the blockade, if they intended to run the blockade,” she said. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Meta’s $17 billion teen safety settlement is really a 1% tax — and a play to box in TikTok and YouTube
articles.summary: The deeper lesson of is that product design, as a site of legal accountability, is a workable legal strategy.
articles._body: Meta has agreed to pay up to US$17 billion over 10 years to settle claims brought by a bipartisan coalition of state attorneys general. The states argued that the company deliberately designed Facebook and Instagram to hook children into using its apps, misled the public about the harm and improperly collected data from children under 13. The settlement , announced by Meta on Aug. 26, 2026, ended a federal trial that had barely begun in Oakland, California. The potential financial exposure in the case was enormous, and Meta’s stock price took a hit. The states argued that penalties could reach hundreds of billions of dollars. Against that backdrop, and with a $1.4 trillion question mark hanging over its valuation , Meta settled, although the company continues to deny wrongdoing. The settlement still requires approval from Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers. As a technology policy and law scholar, I follow with interest the litigation against Meta and other social media companies. The basic contours of this settlement are now public, and I believe they deserve careful attention because of the product design changes it might compel Meta, TikTok and YouTube to make. What the states alleged The Oakland case consolidated lawsuits filed in 2023 by 29 state attorneys general following a nationwide investigation that began in 2021. Similar to prior litigation in Los Angeles and New Mexico , the states alleged that Meta engineered features – for example, infinite scroll, autoplay, push notifications, likes and appearance-altering filters – to exploit vulnerabilities associated with adolescent development and to maximize engagement. States alleged that Meta’s internal research documented links between Instagram use and harms including depression, anxiety and body-image concerns among young people, while the company publicly minimized or concealed those risks. A third set of claims concerned Meta’s collection of data from children under 13 without parental consent, allegedly in violation of federal children’s privacy law. And the states argued that these practices violated state consumer protection statutes as well. That consumer protection claim is particularly important. For decades, Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act has protected platforms from liability for content posted by their users. But the states sued Meta instead over the company’s own product design, business practices and alleged misrepresentations, not user-generated content. In opening arguments, California’s lawyer compressed the theory into four words, noting Meta’s business model was to “hook” users, “hold” them, “harvest” their data and “hide” the harm. And there was already precedent at the state level, in Massachusetts , of courts allowing this kind of claim to proceed. https://www.youtube.com/embed/MBL9musS6Po?wmode=transparent&start=0 The lawsuit and settlement focused on the design of Meta’s social media platforms and how the platforms need to change to protect teens. One legal battle, several different cases It is important not to conflate the cases. While the federal case in Oakland was settled as part of the agreement with the 47 states , major cases against Meta remain active. In Los Angeles, a separate California state-court case resulted in a jury finding Meta and Google liable for negligently designing their products in ways that contributed to a teen girl’s mental health harms, with damages of $4.2 million against Meta and $1.8 million against Google. Those amounts look modest until multiplied across the thousands of similar individual claims now pending. Meta is appealing that decision. And in New Mexico , the state pursued its own enforcement action, alleging that Meta endangered children and violated state consumer protection law. New Mexico won judgments against Meta totaling more than $900 million, which Meta is also challenging. Neither of those cases was part of the federal trial, so the settlement does not resolve them, nor does it create legal precedent. What the settlement actually changes The design changes, such as curbing infinite scroll and autoplay, are the substantive core of the agreement. Subject to court approval, teens under 18 on Instagram and Facebook in participating states will get: a default two-hour daily time limit, cumulative across both apps and across multiple accounts, that only a parent can lift a block on app access between midnight and 6 a.m. and muted notifications during school hours (8 a.m. to 3 p.m.), excepting direct messages usage prompts after every 15 minutes of continuous scrolling the option of a non-algorithmic, nonpersonalized feed the ability to turn off autoplay and for parents to set the default to “off” hidden like counts by default blocks on cosmetic surgery and extreme makeup filters strengthened age-detection systems for under-13 accounts Some of these measures are particularly significant because they change the default experience rather than simply adding another setting that users can choose to activate. This lowers the burden on the user. A safety tool that requires a teenager or parent to find, understand and turn on is fundamentally different from a safety constraint built into the product itself. The agreement addresses the architecture that determines how the product operates. In doing so, it recognizes that Meta shares responsibility for the environment it creates, which is crucial because Meta holds significant power to shape how its products are used. Among other changes, the settlement calls for Meta to mute notifications from Facebook and Instagram to teens during school hours. Drazen Zigic/iStock via Getty Images Why the design terms matter more than the money Even $17 billion, spread across a decade, amounts to only roughly 1% of Meta’s expected revenue over the same period. The company has told investors that the settlement will not change its financial guidance beyond a single quarterly expense. More consequential, for Meta and the public

articles.title: Nike's British Air Jordans Are as Handsome as They Are Hairy
articles.summary: The Air Jordan 4 "London" sneaker lands as a city-themed spin complete with faded fuzzy suede uppers & vintage-style details.
articles._body: Folks all over the world love Air Jordans. Over the years, the brand has shown that the feeling is quite mutal, dropping sneakers inspired the biggest cities around the globe. Think Milan-themed Air Jordan 1 Mids and all-black leather Jordan 10s inspired by New York City. Now, it's time for an Air Jordan 4 for London. The brand has released a clean grey Air Jordan 1 for the city before. Now, it's getting a nice-looking Jordan 4 in its honor. Emphasis on nice-looking. Nike's "British" Jordan 4 lands with faded hairy suede, plus classic grey and washed red accents. It even comes with a vintage-style shoebox, which further leans into the sneaker's "aged" aesthetic. There's also some clever "LDN" branding throughout, as well as a "Say Less" message on the inner tongue tag. The London connection is unclear there, but I think I understand the broader point. Less talking, more flexing. A few years ago, the Jordan 4 got a KAWS-coded all-grey makeover inspired by the streets of Paris. Now, it's getting washed in a London-inspired color scheme. Speaking of which, the Air Jordan 4 "London" sneakers are expected to drop on Nike's website in September. And good news (for Englanders): the shoes are reportedly a UK-exclusive. How Much Is Dolly Parton’s Catalog Worth?
articles.summary: Billboard breaks down how much Dolly Parton's songs generate in revenue, and how much her catalog might be worth
articles._body: When Dolly Parton was considering selling her music recording and publishing assets back in 2021, she was shopping catalogs which combined had net publishing and net label shares approaching $10 million, say some suitors and other financial sources who were aware of the deal. At the time, the rumor was that her management team was seeking about $500 million; now, other sources suggest discussions were more along the lines of a $230 million valuation. Whatever the price, a deal never closed, and it’s unclear if Parton pulled the deal or a suitor never completed it. The year before that rumor circulated, Parton told  Billboard  she was contemplating how to put her estate in order. Now, following her passing this week at the age of 80, some wonder if Parton left instructions that her music assets be sold — and if she did, what assets she owned, and what the numbers could be. Related Dolly Parton, One of Country Music’s Biggest & Brightest Icons, Dies at 80 Dale Morris, Nashville Manager Who Guided Careers of Alabama & Kenny Chesney, Dies at 89 HYBE Pledges Over $300k for Colombia Earthquake Recovery How Much Does Her Catalog Generate? Billboard estimates that her master recording catalog and her publishing combined generated $17.5 million in revenue on average over the last four years (2022-2025). But how much of that $17.5 million in revenue she takes home, as well as what is owned assets (known as an active investment) and how much is royalties (known as a passive investment) is less clear. Active music assets are more highly-sought-after than passive music assets, and therefore carry a higher valuation multiple. In 2021, when Parton was testing the waters to sell her music assets, she was coming off the second-biggest year for her catalog in the past decade, according to Luminate data. In 2020, a year largely defined by the COVID pandemic, her catalog generated 764,000 album equivalent units, likely spurred by a new Christmas album,  A Holly Dolly Christmas , with an hour-long TV special; high-profile philanthropic work, including a YouTube bedtime story series, “Goodnight With Dolly,” for children; and a Netflix holiday musical film,  Christmas On the Square . And the growth in streaming at the time also helped spur activity: during the period of 2017 through 2019, her catalog annually averaged about 256,000 album consumption units, or one-third of 2020’s total.  That helps explain the valuation of her catalog when she was shopping the deal, as the assets were at a high-water mark following 2020. And interest remained high, if not as high, in subsequent periods: After the banner year of 2020, Parton’s catalog activity fell to 550,000 album equivalent units in 2021 before rebounding to 610,000 album equivalents in 2022, all figures much higher than pre-pandemic years.  Related Will Dolly Parton Earn Her First Billboard 200 No. 1 Album Posthumously? Which brings us to the 2022-2025 period, the years most relevant to a current valuation for Parton’s catalog, as music asset buyers like at least a three-year history of performance when assessing valuations. During that period — which contains the catalog’s best year of the past decade, 2023, when her catalog generated 769,000 album consumption units — her catalog has averaged about 625,000 album equivalent units a year in the U.S., while globally her on-demand stream count averaged 1.16 billion plays. (Overall, since Luminate and its predecessor companies first began tracking sales and other activity in 1991, the Parton catalog has generated 16.5 million album consumption units in the U.S.) How Much Would She See? While Parton’s longtime manager Danny Nozell told Billboard in August 2020 that her publishing catalog generated $6 million to $8 million a year, based on the above performance of the catalog, Billboard estimates her publishing catalog generated $6.5 million in royalties, nowadays. Separately, Billboard estimates that her master recording catalog generated about $11 million in global revenue annually for the period. In terms of publishing, the revenue from her own recordings averaged almost $5.7 million annually over the past four years, with covers bringing in an additional estimated $800,000 based on information from industry financial sources, adding up to that $6.5 million figure. In terms of her master recordings, sources say Sony Music owns her masters from her RCA period, and also likely from her stint on Columbia Nashville, too, totaling some 23 albums. But in 1995, she issued the first album on her own Blue Eye label — still distributed by Sony — and since then owns most, if not all, of her subsequent studio recordings, or some 17 albums. Consequently, Billboard estimates that about 79% of Parton’s sales and streaming activity comes from masters owned by Sony Music. Applying that percentage against the estimated $11 million in total revenue her masters generate, Sony’s total comes in at $8.6 million, with the titles that Parton owns generating about $2.4 million in revenue. Related Forever No. 1: Dolly Parton, ‘9 to 5’ How much of that would go to Parton? On the recordings side, based on a superstar royalty rate of 33%, she would take home about $2.84 million in net label share from the Sony-owned recordings; of her owned recordings, assuming that she keeps 76% of revenue after production, distribution, marketing and other costs, that would total $1.83 million. The publishing side is more complicated, as might be expected, but given that she owned her own catalog for her entire career, it’s simpler than most:   Billboard  estimates she has about a 75% share of the 600 or so songs across her 49 albums, which would come out to about $4.25 million from the publishing on her own catalog. articles.title: NCAA files response to Alex Afari’s motion to join eligibility court case
articles.summary: The NCAA has filed its response to Alex Afari's motion to join the court case that has granted other athletes a fifth year of eligibility.
articles._body: The NCAA has filed its response to Kentucky football player Alex Afari ‘s motion to join the Louisville court case that has granted other athletes, including Mark Mitchell , an extra year of college eligibility. The motion, which was filed on Friday afternoon and can be found here , argues that Afari has no right to be added to the temporary restraining order that was granted earlier this month by Judge Brian Edwards. That TRO allowed Mitchell and several college athletes with exhausted eligibility the ability to play in the upcoming seasons. But the NCAA is asking the court to deny Afari’s attempted intervention, arguing that he signed an NFL contract and particpated in minicamp with the Green Bay Packers, meaning he cannot return to college and should be deemed ineligible. Afari, who played four seasons at UK, rejoined the program on Aug. 15 after Judge Charlotte Sweeney of the U.S. District Court of Colorado granted members of the high school class of 2022 a preliminary injunction to play this coming season. But the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 10th Circuit later granted the NCAA’s request for a stay  in that lawsuit, ruling him ineligible again. Afari then had to join a state lawsuit to continue his battle, which is what the NCAA is currently trying to block. Afari’s hearing in Louisville is scheduled for Monday. Jon Hale of the Herald-Leader reports that Afari was with the team at practice on Friday morning, but is unsure if he was a participant. Afari, a former four-star recruit out of West Chester (OH) Lakota West , played in 48 games with 42 starting assignments in his Kentucky career. In four years, he logged 193 tackles, 26.5 tackles for loss, and six sacks over 1,758 career defensive snaps.

Dolly Parton likely wrote 2 of her biggest hits on the same day
articles.summary: Three songs define Dolly Parton's genius more than any others.
articles._body: The world has lost a music legend in Dolly Parton, who has died at 80 after a “brief battle” with cancer. She’s remembered for her twanging country vocals, decades of hit recordings, Grammys, Emmys and a liberal splash of acting. But the biggest legacy Parton leaves is her songwriting, and three songs define her more than any others. Jolene , I Will Always Love You and 9 to 5 are not just memorable Parton songs – they are integral to popular music history. They show a skilful musician who knew how to blend the story of lyrics with the drama of music. Like many songwriters, Parton had things to say. What makes her contribution notable was when her lyrics told a story, and her music matched it. Jolene In Jolene, released in 1974, Parton’s lyrics capture the torment of watching your lover flirt with someone else. It’s a powerful human experience – particularly for women despairing over how easily the next pretty young thing grabs male attention. Parton’s desperate begging for Jolene not to take her man “even though you can” is comfortingly raw and honest. The song’s lyrics are a startling contrast to the common songwriting themes of the time about finding or losing love – such as The Carpenters’ Close to You (1970), Stevie Wonder’s You are the Sunshine of My Life (1972) and Carole King’s It’s Too Late (1971). Instead, Jolene sits on the precipice of change, telling a vivid story of how seeing a stunning young woman can make another woman insecure. Musically, the chords pound out an appropriately bleak minor key, ascending to higher chords with each dramatic call of the name “Jolene”. Accompanying the vocals sits an intriguing, rapid-fire, finger-picking guitar, performed in the recording studio by session musician Chip Young . It keeps an incessant motion that not only adds tension but draws admiration for skilful playing. I Will Always Love You I Will Always Love You was also released in 1974 and – remarkably – possibly was written on the same day as Jolene . This song shows Parton’s ability to once again blend story and music in an excellent pairing. The fear pumping through Jolene is replaced by the grief of farewelling a deep love because, while love endures, it is not always enough of a reason to remain in a relationship. https://www.youtube.com/embed/pW2TgGy5gjY?wmode=transparent&start=0 Again, Parton captures a more sophisticated theme than the excitement and wonder of love. She knows that love can mean letting go. The lyrics are sparse and the story of “bittersweet memories” is sketchy, but Parton once again nails the essence of human experience. We don’t need the details of what happened to relate with our own painful farewells. The elongated singing of the word “I” translates almost as a cry of agony in Whitney Houston’s extraordinary cover version. https://www.youtube.com/embed/3JWTaaS7LdU?wmode=transparent&start=0 The chord progression Parton chose to underpin the chorus is one of the most familiar, hit-producing patterns in popular music history. It appears in songs ranging from Stand By Me (1961), Blue Moon (1934), Crocodile Rock (1973) and Every Breath You Take (1983). But Parton’s usage is unique: the melody and lyrics don’t move with the progression. Instead, the melody holds one single note (with a few embellishments) and lets the chords do the work. 9 to 5 Parton wrote the song 9 to 5 for the movie of the same name in 1980, in which she starred alongside Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin. It needed to match the vibe to describe the bustle of a working week. To achieve this, Parton swapped her previously drawn out lyrics of love for the relentless patter describing the morning routine. Here Parton uses clever imperfect rhymes such as matching “kitchen” and “ambition” to sell the story. https://www.youtube.com/embed/UbxUSsFXYo4?wmode=transparent&start=0 The melody in the verse rises with each cluster of words, building the energy like the start of the day she describes. The chorus nails the hook by changing the rhythm, to let the phrase “9 to 5” ring out. In 9 to 5, Parton moved away from love songs to a feminist theme that belted out the injustices of working tirelessly in a work place like any other employee yet not able to get a “fair promotion”. The description of the “rich man’s game” and how “they never give you credit” highlights workplace inequalities that are sadly still prevalent today. Wendy Hargreaves , Academic in the School of Education and Creative Arts, University of Southern Queensland This article is republished from The Conversation under a Creative Commons license. Read the original article . This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Breaking down the top Group of Six commits in the 2027 cycle
articles.summary: Delaware — yes, Delaware — made a massive splash on the recruiting trail on Friday afternoon as Amarillo (Texas) Palo Duro four-star quarterback Julian Reese II announced his commitment to the Blue Hens. The CUSA program was able to beat out UNLV, UTEP, Houston and others for the coveted athlete who
articles._body: Delaware — yes, Delaware — made a massive splash on the recruiting trail on Friday afternoon as Amarillo (Texas) Palo Duro four-star quarterback Julian Reese II announced his commitment to the Blue Hens. The CUSA program was able to beat out UNLV, UTEP, Houston and others for the coveted athlete who’s got his sights set on being a signal-caller at the next level. It’s one of the bigger recruiting victories for the entire Group of Six in the 2027 cycle. $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage Reese is the No. 399 overall prospect and No. 28 QB in the cycle, according to the Rivals Industry Ranking , a weighted average that utilizes all major recruiting media companies. He’s the third blue-chip senior to commit to a G6 program. There have been some intriguing recruitments this cycle that have gone the way of the “little guy.” Rivals breaks down the 10 highest-ranked prospects who are currently committed to a G6 school, as of Aug. 28: ATH Justin Murphy — Georgia State Rivals Industry Ranking: No. 287 NATL. (No. 8 ATH) School: North Clayton (Ga.) About: Murphy is quite the dual-threat playmaker who wants to play quarterback at the college level. As a junior, he rushed for over 1,100 yards and 18 touchdowns and also threw for more than 1,500 yards and 11 scores to just five interceptions. The 6-foot, 200-pounder committed to Georgia State at the end of official visit season. West Virginia and Vanderbilt were among some of the bigger names giving him a look. OT Rashaun Lavata’i — Washington State Rivals Industry Ranking: No. 354 NATL. (No. 30 OT) School: Curtis Senior (Wash.) About: The 6-foot-6, 270-pounder opted for new head coach Kirby Moore and the Cougars over Washington, Utah and Oregon State. Lavata’i credited his relationships with the staff in Pullman when discussing his commitment with Rivals’ Brandon Huffman. Rivals ranks the four-star higher than other recruiting services; he checks in as the No. 118 recruit and No. 9 OT in the updated Rivals300. QB Julian Reese II — Delaware Rivals Industry Ranking: No. 399 NATL. (No. 28 QB) School: Palo Duro (Texas) About: Programs like Houston and Wake Forest were after Reese, but Delaware emerged as a finalist as the Blue Hens targeted him as a QB rather than an athlete who would likely slot in elsewhere. Reese accounted for more than 3,000 yards passing with 31 passing touchdowns and 12 more rushing scores in 12 games last fall. He’s dynamic with the football and will begin his senior season on Friday. Reese discussed his commitment with Rivals’ Sam Spiegelman — that can be seen here . RB Daylon Gordon — Texas State Rivals Industry Ranking: No. 431 NATL. (No. 32 RB) School: Wylie (Texas) About: Gordon is another Swiss-Army knife playmaker in the Lone Star State. He’s coming off a junior season that witnessed 11 rushing touchdowns, four receiving touchdowns and over 1,500 total yards. The likes of Houston and Rice got him in for official visits, but he’s headed for San Marcos in a big-time win for Texas State as it embarks on competing in the new Pac-12. EDGE Andrew Rogers — East Carolina Rivals Industry Ranking: No. 500 NATL. (No. 47 EDGE) School: Grimsley (N.C.) About: Originally committed to the old staff at Virginia Tech, Rogers flirted with reclassification and putting his name back on the board throughout the fall. He eventually did weigh his options once more and the in-state East Carolina Pirates emerged as a realistic option, leading him to a late-June commitment. The 6-foot-6, 240-pounder plays for one of the top HSFB programs in North Carolina and is coming off a 50-tackle, eight-sack junior year. WR Jordan Christie — Liberty Rivals Industry Ranking: No. 528 NATL. (No. 73 WR) School: Southwest DeKalb (Ga.) About: Christie is someone who’s impressed many in the Peach State for years and his recruitment was previously down to Arkansas, Florida State, Georgia, Georgia Tech and UCF. Things were quiet over the summer for The Opening Finals invitee, however, and on June 18, Liberty swiped his commitment. As a junior for Southwest DeKalb, he hauled in 48 catches and turned them into 927 yards and 11 touchdowns. QB Kevin Verpaele — USF Rivals Industry Ranking: No. 537 NATL. (No. 32 QB) School: Merritt Island (Fla.) About: In the middle of his junior year at Merritt Island, Verpaele made an early commitment to the Pitt Panthers. That pledge held strong for over seven months, but after taking some visits and hitting a reset button of sorts, the passer decommitted. It was USF and new head coach Brian Hartline that immediately began to trend and he locked in his commitment to the Bulls one day later on June 10. A Rivals300 four-star, Verpaele threw for over 2,700 yards and had 31 total touchdowns last season. WR Demaje Riley — Fresno State Rivals Industry Ranking: No. 599 NATL. (No. 80 WR) School: Tulare Union (Calif.) About: Riley has been on the California HSFB radar for a while now. As a freshman, he broke out with 67 catches, over 1,000 yards and 15 touchdowns. He hauled in 12 receiving TDs as a sophomore, then took it up a notch with over 1,500 yards and 13 more scores last fall, averaging over 126 yards per game. articles.title: Jon Sumrall on former NFL players returning to college football: ‘That ship has sailed for you’
articles.summary: Throughout this week, the power conferences announced new rules around former professional athletes coming back to college athletics in light of multiple court orders. Former NFL players are front-and-center in the discussion with college football season quickly approaching. Florida coach Jon Sumral
articles._body: Throughout this week, the power conferences announced new rules around former professional athletes coming back to college athletics in light of multiple court orders. Former NFL players are front-and-center in the discussion with college football season quickly approaching. Florida coach Jon Sumrall was the latest head coach to make his thoughts clear on players returning from the pro level. He told Paul Finebaum he’s against those athletes coming back and said the Gators aren’t looking to add any of them since the roster is “full.” $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage Sumrall’s comments are in light of the SEC’s rules against players returning from the NFL, NBA and WNBA. If those athletes suit up for a team in the conference, the coach and school would have to deal with stiff penalties. Sumrall pointed to the SEC’s stance while where he falls on the issue. “We constantly monitor anything going on in our sport, like the current stuff and the court rulings,” Sumrall said on The Paul Finebaum Show . “But I’ll say this, we’re not in a position right now where [we’re] adding anybody on our football team, and then we’re going to follow suit with what Commissioner [Greg] Sankey , our presidents and athletic directors in our league voted upon. “Our football team, our roster right now is currently full anyways. So to bring somebody on, we’d have to make a cut, which I’m not really interested in doing for guys that have been here all summer training, preparing and that sort of thing. This is college ball. If you’ve played pro football and you’ve been in that game, to me, that ship has sailed for you.” The issue of former NFL players returning to college athletics comes in light of a slew of eligibility lawsuits against the NCAA. The association’s age-based, five-year rule is at the center of it after it was not retroactive to members of the Class of 2022. As a result, lawsuits came down, including one in Louisiana that granted eligibility to multiple players who went through NFL training camps and preseason. The timing of the decision came just weeks before the 2026 college football season gets underway. While Jon Sumrall noted he’s familiar with late additions after bringing Jake Retzlaff to Tulane last year after he left BYU , he again said the SEC’s rules are clear. That’s why he argued the situation with former pro athletes is different. “Now, I’m always open to adding good players,” Sumrall said. “I added Jake Retzlaff last year in late July because I thought it’d make our team at Tulane better. So you’re constantly figuring out how can you improve yourself as a team and find competitive advantages. “But by everything that’s come out recently from our league office, I think it’s pretty clear that we’re not supposed to be trying to add those guys back to our roster.”

Max Fried’s return comes at an opportune time, as the Yankees are closing in on securing a playoff spot. Fried’s presence gives New York a huge uplift in the starting rotation moving forward. The four-game series against the Red Sox kicks off on Friday, which will be followed by the double-header before wrapping up on Sunday. Eagles player on roster bubble with most at stake in 2026 NFL preseason finale
articles.summary: Heading into the final week of preseason action, NFL teams like the Philadelphia Eagles have one final chance to see which players are worthy of a spot on the 53-man roster, the practice squad, or a firm handshake on their way out the door. Now granted, most organizations have a pretty good idea
articles._body: Heading into the final week of preseason action, NFL teams like the Philadelphia Eagles have one final chance to see which players are worthy of a spot on the 53-man roster , the practice squad, or a firm handshake on their way out the door. Now granted, most organizations have a pretty good idea of who they like, who they don’t, and which players are on the fence, but every chance to take the field is an opportunity for all 32 front offices to see what everyone has on their roster and if there are any players worth a waiver claim or even a trade over the weekend. As a result, a big preseason performance could help a marginal player make their current team, sure, but it could also force a general manager to keep a player on their 53-man roster who once looked like a practice squad guy, thus shuffling the proverbial deck even further to accommodate. As a result, some bottom-of-the-roster guys have a chance to have an undue influence on the 53-man roster and beyond, especially if they can do it two games in a row. In 2026, that player for the Eagles is Carson Steele, as after a dominant coming-out party against the Patriots, he has a chance to force his way onto Philadelphia’s 53-man roster just like Corey Clement a decade earlier. Eric Canha-Imagn Images Another big Carson Steele game could seal his Eagles’ 53-man roster Part of why it was so surprising to see Steele make so many big plays in the Eagles’ preseason clash against the Patriots is because he simply hasn’t been afforded a chance to do so at the NFL level. A three-year college player who broke 1,000 all-purpose yards during his lone season at UCLA, Steele joined the Kansas City Chiefs as a hybrid fullback-running back as a UDFA in 2024, recording 183 rushing yards plus 26 more as a receiver and 138 as a kick returner on five attempts. Despite only playing 338 total snaps as a rookie, 201 on offense and 137 as a special teamer , Steele was able to impress enough to finish second in AFC fullback Pro Bowl voting behind Patrick Richard of the Baltimore Ravens, leading the way for big expectations in 2025. Unfortunately, those expectations weren’t met, as after his second summer in KC camp, Steele was released in the final trimdown to 53. Despite re-signing with the team’s practice squad before Week 1, Steele never actually saw action for the Chiefs in 2025 and ultimately signed a futures contract with the Eagles in January in the hopes of challenging Cam Latu and, at the time, Ben VanSumeren, for the team’s fullback position in 2026. After a summer with players like Darius Cooper captured the spotlight, Steele really came into his own against the Patriots, where he ran the ball 12 times for 33 yards and caught six more balls for 84 yards and a touchdown. His two high-flying hurdles drew all of the attention , sure, but in a game where Philadelphia ran a vanilla offense with very few examples of razzle dazzle, Steele consistently made plays with the ball in his hands, jumping off the tape like few others as a result. Is Steele still a longshot to make the Eagles’ 53-man roster? Most certainly so, and if he does, he will be the team’s 53rd man, but at 23, Steele is one of the youngest players on the Eagles’ roster and would only be in Year 3 of his rookie contract if he was drafted out of UCLA. Considering how often he’s made plays on the field against an actual opponent versus, well, basically every other offensive position player on the team, one more big game may be enough for Steele to force the Eagles’ hand and earn another shot at a Pro Bowl spot at the fullback position. The post Eagles player on roster bubble with most at stake in 2026 NFL preseason finale appeared first on ClutchPoints .

Meanwhile, Waldrep and Schwellenbach — who are both impactful starters as well — will undergo surgery for their elbow injuries. Waldrep is set to undergo Tommy John surgery while Schwellenbach will have surgery as he battles an elbow fracture. The Braves’ starting rotation has serious uncertainty. Sale is the ace and he may end up finishing as a National League Cy Young finalist. Pitchers such as Bryce Elder, Martin Perez and Grant Holmes can help matters, while Tyler Mahle was acquired in a trade before the deadline. Nevertheless, the Braves’ starting pitching will have questions heading into the postseason. articles.title: Show HN: PorchWeather – a free site that pings you when it's nice outside
articles.summary:
I live in the Bay Area, and so the weather cools down to a comfy temperature in the evenings. Opening up the windows to let the fresh air in has saved me a decent amount on A/C bills. Checking a forecast every hour to catch that moment is exactly the kind of job a computer should do.

PorchWeath
articles._body: I live in the Bay Area, and so the weather cools down to a comfy temperature in the evenings. Opening up the windows to let the fresh air in has saved me a decent amount on A/C bills. Checking a forecast every hour to catch that moment is exactly the kind of job a computer should do. PorchWeather watches one saved location and a set of conditions you pick (temperature range, wind, rain, dew point, air quality) and sends you a notification when conditions become nice, and another when they stop. That's the whole product. It's free, web-native (not an app), and notifications are browser push or email. Some implementation details HN might find interesting: Stack: SvelteKit SPA, Rust backend, DynamoDB, Cognito for auth, SES for email, Self-hosted Open-Meteo for weather all on ECS Fargate. The weather layer serves ECMWF global plus NOAA HRRR at 3 km resolution for the US. Notifications are primarily through web push. I'd love to do SMS through twilio, but it seems prohibitively expensive for a free service unfortunately. iOS devices make this a little harder because you have to "install" the app on the home screen to get push notifications. I may end up creating an app at some point to make this easier if there's demand. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49484064 Points: 1 # Comments: 3

articles.title: Debasement Trade Is Here Thanks to Government Debt — And Bitcoin Will Benefit: Grayscale
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Debasement Trade Is Here Thanks to Government Debt — And Bitcoin Will Benefit: Grayscale The debasement trade is back — and will benefit bitcoin.  That’s according to asset manager Grayscale’s crypto research team, who wrote in a note this week that the U.S. government debasing its currency would lead to cash hitting digital assets.  “Unchecked government debt growth undermines the credibility of fiat currencies and drives investors to seek out alternative stores of value like physical gold and certain cryptocurrencies,” the note by the firm’s head of research, Zach Pandl, read, adding that primarily bitcoin would benefit.  US public debt has reached over $40 trillion. The Treasury is buying back bonds to ease rising borrowing costs, but core deficit remains. Grayscale Research believes this may drive investors towards the debasement trade: Bitcoin $BTC , Ethereum $ETH , and Zcash $ZEC . Read more… pic.twitter.com/tN3xgaNZ1l — Grayscale (@Grayscale) August 28, 2026 The so-called debasement trade is when investors buy an asset as a way to hedge against a currency losing value. The trade was hot last year, and helped bitcoin’s run, but the digital asset’s run lost steam after October as traders turned their attention to stocks related to artificial intelligence.  But since last week, bitcoin has benefited from news that the U.S. Treasury would at least double the size of its liquidity-support buyback operations. The announcement last week hurt the dollar but non-yielding assets have benefited.  “That buybacks are needed at all is the problem: heavy growth in government debt is driving up the cost of borrowing,” the note continued. “The Treasury is treating the symptoms (rising bond yields) because they cannot cure the disease (structural deficits).”  The note added that on the same day last week as the buyback announcement, the Treasury also said the U.S. public debt exceeded $40 trillion for the first time. As debt and interest payments grow, the government needs to either raise taxes, cut spending, or issue more debt.  Bitcoiners see the more politically likely path as expanding the dollar supply — which is ultimately bad for the dollar, and good for scarce assets like bitcoin.  After bitcoin started surging last week, the dollar had its worst week of August and was trading at a three-month low .  Bitcoin was trading for $77,493 on Friday afternoon in New York after hitting a high this week of $81,281. Over a 24-hour period, the coin now sits unmoved, but over a 30-day period, it has jumped by more than 20%.  This post Debasement Trade Is Here Thanks to Government Debt — And Bitcoin Will Benefit: Grayscale first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo .

articles.title: Bitcoin’s Moment Has Come for the Far East, Says Metaplanet CEO
articles.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bi
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin’s Moment Has Come for the Far East, Says Metaplanet CEO Bitcoin’s time has come in Asia — especially with a changing regulatory landscape — and its people and companies should take advantage.  That was the message Metaplanet CEO Simon Gerovich gave at this year’s Bitcoin Asia conference, where on Friday he spoke of how his company went from failing to the third biggest bitcoin treasury in the world.  Bitcoin Asia kicked off on Thursday in Hong Kong, bringing the biggest names in the space to Hong Kong to talk about everything from treasury companies to building apps from scratch.  JUST IN: Japanese public company Metaplanet CEO says the bottom for Bitcoin's price is in "The buyers arriving now aren't going anywhere. I believe the bottom is in. And I'm expecting a much brighter rest of the year." pic.twitter.com/zz0RUxspSz — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) August 28, 2026 “The previous cycles belonged to the West, and the first Asian cycle has already started,” Gerovich said. “The only question left is who builds it. Will you?” Often dubbed Asia’s answer to Nasdaq-listed Bitcoin treasury Strategy, Metaplanet pivoted from its core hotel and technology business to buying Bitcoin in 2024. The Tokyo Stock Exchange now holds 43,000 bitcoins worth about $3.3 billion at today’s prices. Gerovich said in his speech that his company was small and going nowhere fast until it started putting bitcoin on its balance sheet, basically allowing investors to buy exposure to the biggest digital coin via its regulated shares.  He said that the strategy is a major opportunity for Asian companies, which can now capitalize on the changing regulatory landscape and the growing interest in Bitcoin. Asian nations, including Japan, Hong Kong, and Singapore, are making regulatory changes to support digital assets. Gerovich noted that Japan in particular is a country where its citizens have saved like no other part of the world — and that capital can now be put to good use.  “Hoarding cash has stopped making sense, and every household in Japan can now feel it,” he said.  “Japanese households hold roughly 14 trillion dollars in financial assets. About half of that sits in bank deposits, earning almost nothing, and that’s just Japan, add Korea, Southeast Asia, and the wealth managed out of this place, Hong Kong, and you’re looking at the deepest pools of patient savings on Earth.  “And for the first time in a generation, these savings are looking for somewhere to go.” Gerovich added that Asian companies, institutions, and savers should take advantage of the current market conditions and build the Bitcoin infrastructure in their own regions. “The end of the cash hoarding strategy and new rules are arriving at exactly the same time, and together, they set up what I think is the single biggest opportunity in Asian markets today,” he added.  This post Bitcoin’s Moment Has Come for the Far East, Says Metaplanet CEO first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo .

One of the biggest questions perhaps surrounds the Orlando Magic and the future of star player Paolo Banche
articles._body: The start of the 2026-27 NBA season is a little less than two months away, and with the schedule already having been released, there’s been no shortage of predictions for the upcoming year. One of the biggest questions perhaps surrounds the Orlando Magic and the future of star player Paolo Banchero regarding a potential trade. In fact, former NBA player turned ESPN analyst Kendrick Perkins believes a move is simply a matter of when . During a recent segment of ‘Road Trippin,’ alongside Richard Jefferson, Channing Frye and Allie Clifton, Kendrick Perkins dropped his major prediction for the upcoming season in saying that the Magic will trade Paolo Banchero this year. “The Orlando Magic. You fired the coach. They’re not going to have a run like they’re expecting. You got a new head coach,” Perkins said. “They’re going to move on from Paolo Banchero eventually. He will be the first All-Star, All-NBA player traded.” The Magic did opt to part ways with head coach Jamahl Mosley, replacing him with Sean Sweeney . Meanwhile, Banchero will be heading into only his fifth season in the NBA. The Magic selected him with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2022 NBA Draft. Banchero was selected to his first All-Star appearance during the 2023-24 season, his second in the league, but has not been named since despite arguably putting up All-Star caliber seasons the past two years. This past season, the former Duke star appeared in 72 games at a little over 34 minutes per game. He averaged 22.2 points, 8.4 rebounds and 5.2 assists with splits of 45.9 percent shooting from the field, 30.5 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 77.5 percent shooting from the free-throw line. While rumors and speculation have come up this offseason even, the Magic have not indicated a desire to listen to potential Banchero trade overtures . articles.title: Interpol Reflects on ‘Expansive & Fresh’ New Album ‘This Mirror Weighs a Ton’ & Recording With New Band Members and Collaborators
articles.summary: Frontman Paul Banks speaks with Billboard Español about the band's new studio album and desire to return to Latin America.
articles._body: This Mirror Weighs a Ton brought Interpol back home after almost a decade. The New York band created the new album at Wyatt Studio in Manhattan, which became the place where it expanded its music, incorporating strings, wind instruments, acoustic guitars, layered vocals, synthesizers and experimental sound design — all without losing the rhythmic precision that has always defined its sound. Related The Warning Break Down 5 Essential Songs From New Album ‘Everything’s Falling’ Olivia Rodrigo, Alex Warren, JENNIE, Rod Wave & More: New Music Friday Guide Radio Rallies Around Dolly Parton After Her Death, Led by '9 to 5' “It was great to be back in New York City recording a record with our friend Andrew Wyatt, and I think we just came into this album with a lot of positivity and some new input,” frontman Paul Banks tells Billboard Español in a video call interview. “We had a new bass player, [Brad Truax], we had Andrew as the producer, and I think we really just got a new chemistry and created some exciting music.” Released on digital platforms on Friday (August 28) via Partisan Records, the group’s first album with original songs in four years also marks a sonic and lyrical evolution that reaffirms Interpol’s position as one of the most important alternative rock bands of its generation. In this new project, Banks explains, Interpol tackles introspective and deeply self-reflective themes in songs like “See Out Loud” and “Iron City.” “I think there’s a lot of themes on this record about reflection and being honest with one’s self,” he says. “And then I think there’s sort of the self-reflection that a band can go through, or the self-reflection that a nation can go through, and sort of evaluating who are we and, again, similarly, there can be a distorted reality via manipulative narratives, or there can be the honest look. And I think it’s just a very interesting thing the way that it’s very difficult to find universal truths in almost anything and that the world in this moment in time is sort of further than ever away from having kind of a sense of shared common reason.” Comprising 12 songs, This Mirror Weighs a Ton follows the band’s 2022 album The Other Side of Make-Believe . In addition to the official integration of Truax and the production by Wyatt — known for his work with artists like Rosalía and Charli XCX — the set was mixed by David Fridmann, a collaborator of MGMT and Sleater-Kinney. “Brad wrote bass lines on this record for the first time, and played the bass lines,” details Banks. “Usually he was just our live bassist, playing either what Carlos Dengler wrote or what I wrote on bass, but now he wrote the bass parts — so that was like having a new contributing member.” He adds that Wyatt composed much of the string arrangements and other orchestrations heard on the album. “I think, altogether, it just feels like a really well realized and expansive and fresh Interpol record.” Regarding a tour to promote the band’s new album, Banks reveals that an announcement will be made soon, and confirms that Latin America will definitely be included. The singer lived and studied in Mexico when he was 17, which partly explains why he considers the country “his second home,” as he told Billboard Español in 2024 , hours before Interpol’s performance at Mexico City’s Zócalo, which became the most massive show of the band’s career to date. After moving to New York to attend college, he returned to Mexico City in 2005 as a rock star and performed one of the most memorable concerts of his career. He recounts that night at the Salón Mexica in the city’s World Trade Center, where he felt the “terrifying” beauty of the Mexican audience as the venue nearly collapsed due to the sheer number of people gathered (around 7,000, according to promoter Iguapop). “We definitely have some plans to do shows in Mexico,” says Banks, who speaks perfect Spanish and alternates between full sentences in Spanish and English during the interview. “I’m not sure which ones have and haven’t been announced, but we are definitely gonna be down there soon, I believe, and very excited to do so. Mexico is one of the best audiences for us in the world, and we just have such an amazing time in all of Latin America.”

articles._body: The Boston Red Sox made one of the biggest moves at the MLB trade deadline by acquiring catcher Adley Rutschman from the Baltimore Orioles. It was a move to boost the Red Sox’s catching offensive production. Rutschman, however, has struggled at the plate so far with the Red Sox. Beat writer Chris Cotillo of masslive.com recently commented on Rutschman’s tenure with the ball club so far, via Foul Territory. “I’ve kind of argued this with a couple of the other beat writers who said, ‘It’s a catcher, you’re not just getting him for offense.’ Well, to me, if you just wanted good game-calling and ABS challenges and everything that comes with catching, they had (Carlos) Narvaez and (Connor) Wong who had complete command of the staff and familiarity and all that stuff,” Cotillo said. “The pitching staff was still one of the best in baseball with those guys. “They got Rutschman because they thought it was a huge offensive upgrade over what Narvaez, who has had a bad year, and Wong, who, you know, has not had a good two years in a row… If you look at it, he’s (Rutschman) hitting .170 in a Red Sox uniform. He’s not to the point where he can play two days in a row, he’s got this elbow thing going on that’s cost him the last couple games.” As of this story’s writing, Rutschman is hitting even worse than .170, as the catcher currently has a .146 batting average with the Red Sox. Rutschman has recorded just a .499 OPS and one home run across 12 games played with Boston. The Red Sox have played well which has been the big story in Boston. Cotillo believes Rutschman’s slump has been an “underrated storyline.” “It’s been an underrated storyline because the team has kept winning and there’s been other things to talk about… Rutschman really has not given them anything offensively,” Cotillo continued. “He’s hit some balls hard, he had one home run in a big spot at Fenway. But I think it’s been a disappointment so far… If he gets hot in September and they’re firing on all cylinders, it’ll be a different story, but I think they were hoping for more.” It is a small sample size and Rutschman features an All-Star ceiling. He could certainly turn things around. The Red Sox need Rutschman to find his rhythm sooner rather than later. Little Big Town Brings Fresh Energy to New Album, ‘It’s a Dying Art’: ‘There Is a New Excitement’
articles.summary: The country quartet's 12th album is out now.
articles._body: In 2024, Little Big Town celebrated its 25 th anniversary together. And when it came time to return to the studio to make It’s a Dying Art , their first new album since hitting that milestone, Karen Fairchild, Kimberly Schlapman, Phillip Sweet , and Jimi Westbrook  felt a renewed sense of purpose. “We felt like we should turn the page a bit and see what the next chapter could become,” Fairchild says of recording the band’s 12 th studio album, out Friday (Aug. 28) on MCA Nashville. “We don’t really have any boundaries on us at the moment from anybody saying, ‘You need to make this kind of music.’ We definitely just did whatever we wanted to do.” “There was a new excitement that we hadn’t felt in a while,” agrees Fairchild’s husband, Westbrook, during a Zoom interview from their Nashville home. That excitement also came from shaking up the process a little. For their first studio album since 2022’s Mr. Sun, the quartet— who have scored such hits as “Pontoon,” “Girl Crush,” “Day Drinking” and “Better Man” — turned to Gena Johnson , who had worked with Jason Isbell and Dolly Parton , to produce the set with Fairchild. Isbell also joined in, contributing guitar to “The Door,” while longtime friend Kelsea Ballerini sings on “Closing Time” and Ashley Monroe collaborates on “Sucker for a Sad Song.” While there are a few good-time songs on the set, like the fun, chipper “Crickets,” much of the album plumbs the depths of relationships and the highs and the lows. Additionally, the first song released, “Hey There Sunshine,” addressed mental health. After performing on Today Sept. 1 as part of Today ’s Citi Concert Series, the band starts the For the Art of It tour Sept. 24 in St. Petersburg, Fla. Below, Fairchild and Westbrook talked about the making of the album, playing with their famous friends and where they see themselves in 25 years. Did you approach this album any differently than you did the previous 11? Westbrook : I think it was different in a lot of ways, but not. The way it started was a little different. We didn’t have as a whole a group of songs that we were going, “This is what this record’s going to be like.” Not that we do that a lot, but sometimes we’ve had more of an idea of a number of songs. Fairchild : I think maybe the difference was being even choosier about songs, pickier about songs. We always are. We just we were either writing ones that we felt like were really holding the standard high, and then also finding songs that were blowing our minds. And then that also sets the bar really high. Westbrook : And then working with Gena behind the board and the vocal sounds that she gets was so inspiring and a definitely a catalyst for the spirit of this record. The sonic picture, she’s just so great at it, and that was exciting as the process started unfolding. The band that was playing that was a kind of an assembled group of players that we hadn’t played together with as a whole that were so great and vibey. I think sonically all of that stuff together really was kind of propelling things forward in a lot of ways. Karen, you and Gena had met when you were working on Shelby Lynne’s album. How was the decision made that you two were going to produce the album? Fairchild : I just knew she would be an incredible fit for the band, and we didn’t know if it would be production, co-production or just engineering and mixing the record. We just knew that she needed to be involved, and then we would let it kind of define itself as we were creating music. Westbrook : A Christmas song with Gena was the first time that we worked with her as a band, “The Innkeeper” that was added to our Christmas record. We just hit it off, and she’s so encouraging, and such a great spirit. We thought, “Oh, this this could be really fun.” Karen, obviously you were there as co-producer, but did Gena also bring a different energy than a male producer? Fairchild: I think so. I do think that a female brings an energy of nurturing. There is a nurturing spirit there. Maybe not for all women, but definitely with Gena. But she also is a straight shooter. There’s no bulls–t with her. She’s gonna say the truth, but there is a nurturing part of her and an openness to being creative and to not having to do it her way that I like a lot. I know you can find that in either gender. There’s also there’s different level of sonics that she brought in and then you were also working with different musicians, which you had mentioned, Jimmy. You guys just celebrated 25 years together. Did you feel like this was almost a fresh start with some fresh energy coming in? Westbrook: Yeah, absolutely. Fairchild: It felt like we should turn the page a bit and see what the next chapter could become. We don’t really have any boundaries on us at the moment from anybody saying, “Well, you need to make this kind of music.” We definitely just did whatever we wanted to do. Westbrook: We’ve experienced this in the past in making records where you don’t have to force anything, and it just starts happening and revealing itself, and I feel like we felt that on even the first couple of things that we cut. There was a new excitement that we hadn’t felt in a while. There’s an energy you feel when that starts happening that you start going, “Oh, man, I know this feeling!” It’s how the music is making us feel as a band. That started happening early on. You’re just hanging on and not wanting to define it to soon or say anything, but it’s like, “Isn’t this fun!” The first song we heard from the new album was “Hey There Sunshine” at the Academy of Country Music Awards. The deeply emotional song addresses coming out of a long dark period, whether from depression or illness or other circumstances. articles._body: The Los Angeles Rams officially have their eyes set on the regular season as they wrapped up their preseason finale against the Los Angeles Chargers on Thursday. The thing that everyone seems to be waiting on surrounding the Rams is whether Aaron Donald will be returning to the team after being in retirement. Donald has been working out and “trying out” for the team, but there hasn’t been an update on where things stand with him. ESPN’s Peter Schrager shared his thoughts on Donald and what the holdup could be with a possible return. “Aaron Donald needs to feel like he’s 100% ready to go, and that he feels like it’s 99 version of 99, like it was his Madden rating the last time they took the field,” Schrager said on the Pat McAfee Show. “There has to also be this feeling that the Rams are welcoming him in because the numbers have to make sense. We’re not even at the numbers yet, and here we are, August 28th, about 10 days away from when they fly out to Australia, and we don’t have them on board. "Aaron Donald needs to feel like he's 100% ready to go and the numbers have to make sense.. As of right now it doesn't feel like he wants to declare that he's coming back.. If he want to play he'll be there" ~ @PSchrags #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/XFRiRgN4k4 — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) August 28, 2026 “I thought if this was gonna happen, it was gonna happen in early August; it would happen at the end of camp when they broke out, after going to Loyola Marymount, and they said, ‘Okay, we’ve got our team.’ It hasn’t happened yet. Now I think they’re all just kind of in wait-and-see mode also. If Aaron Donnell wants to play, and the numbers make sense, he’ll be there.” At the end of the day, the Rams don’t need Donald, and they’ve been going on with their regular routine without him. If he does join the team, that means that he feels like the Donald that was dominating the league years ago, and that’s good news for the Rams. articles.title: Examining the QB position for Southern Miss to start the 2026 season
articles.summary: Questions are looming at the quarterback position to start the 2026 season. Photo: Southern Miss Athletics
articles._body: With the start of the 2026 college football season for Southern Miss a little over a week away, many questions remain as it pertains to starters and a depth chart. Head Coach Blake Anderson has pointed out many times that there is no depth chart amd with over seventy new players it is easy to see why. This is an unproven squad with very little experience at the FBS level. Thanks to recent court ruling that experience has gotten a boost from returning offensive linemen and a proven commodity on the defensive line. Of all the position groups on the field, the one group that has, perhaps, the most experience is the quarterback room. Transfer Ethan Hampton, Landry Lyddy, and John White all have in game experience. Yet, with the hand injury to Hampton, who will start the season as the signal caller is still in question. Hampton has an injury to his thumb. From what is being explained, it is a deep bruise to his thumb. Anderson has said the injury is taking longer to overcome than expected. It is difficult to almost impossible to throw a football if a thumb is injured. Just holding the ball and making solid throws is one thing, but the slightest hit to that hand could make things worse which is probably why Hamton has been held out of scrimmages and some practices. Hopefully he will be back soon, but if he isn’t, let’s not throw the baby out with the bath water just yet. As stated earlier both Lyddy and White have game experience under their belt. Lyddy played for a hurt Braxton last season and at times showed some really good signs but made some mistakes along the way. It seems Lyddy will be the one to start if Hampton isn’t ready just yet. The difference this season is Lyddy is running an offense that is centered around his and the other quarterback’s strengths. All three quarterbacks are very similar which makes a transition from quarterback to quarterback less difficult. Braxton was a totally different quarterback from Lyddy last season. Trying to reinvent the wheel in the middle of the season is a difficult thing to do. That isn’t happening this season. The gameplan will not change drastically depending on which quarterback starts. Let’s be honest, it shouldn’t matter which quarterback starts against Alcorn State, the Golden Eagles should win the game. If Hamoton is not fully healthy why take a chance on getting him hurt with the majority of the season and conference play to left? It is also a chance to see how they overcome adversity and find out who are the leaders of this team on and off the field.. This writer can’t remember when there were so many unanswered questions before the start of a new season. One thing is for sure, everyone will be waiting with anticipation to the start of the 2026 season no matter we who starts at quarterback. There is nothing like Staurdays at The Rock and it can’t get here fast enough.

articles.title: Cubs DFA pitcher with 3.53 ERA
articles.summary: The Chicago Cubs finally activated left-handed pitcher Hoby Milner off the injured list on Friday, but he is not rejoining the big-league club. Management is designating the 35-year-old reliever for assignment, per MLB.com’s Mark Feinsand. Milner posted a 3.53 ERA in 38 appearances for the
articles._body: The Chicago Cubs finally activated left-handed pitcher Hoby Milner off the injured list on Friday, but he is not rejoining the big-league club . Management is designating the 35-year-old reliever for assignment, per MLB.com’s Mark Feinsand. Milner posted a 3.53 ERA in 38 appearances for the Cubbies in 2026. That number is inflated due to a disastrous June 5 outing versus the San Francisco Giants, which saw him allow six runs in just 1/3 of an inning. He struggled again when he took the mound against the New York Mets on June 25, surrendering one run on three hits without recording an out. The veteran southpaw hit the IL a couple days later after undergoing an emergency appendectomy . He had spent the last three-plus weeks on a rehab assignment with Triple-A Iowa, so it was time for the organization to make a decision. Milner tossed a clean inning Tuesday and tallied a 2.53 ERA in 10 appearances for the squad. Assuming he still feels healthy, the 2012 seventh-round draft pick should be able to find work. Teams are always looking for bullpen reinforcements during the last month of the regular season. Milner could eat innings and help a manager preserve his top relievers for the playoffs. Many North Siders are probably confused why the Cubs are not assigning him a roster slot. Given Chicago’s frequent pitching injuries, it is a little surprising to see president of baseball operations Jed Hoyer cut Hoby Milner loose. It is done now, though. The Cubs presumably have an alternative plan, and it obviously does not include the Dallas, Texas native. The post Cubs DFA pitcher with 3.53 ERA appeared first on ClutchPoints .
