articles.title: Mets’ Juan Soto likely won’t need rehab assignment
articles.summary: The New York Mets have been without Juan Soto since late July as he’s working his way back from a left calf strain. His return is nearing, but it sounds like he may not have to conduct a rehab assignment beforehand. Reports indicate that the 27-year-old slugger indicated as such when asked
articles._body: The New York Mets have been without Juan Soto since late July as he’s working his way back from a left calf strain. His return is nearing, but it sounds like he may not have to conduct a rehab assignment beforehand. Reports indicate that the 27-year-old slugger indicated as such when asked about his injury recovery, according to Anthony DiComo of MLB.com. Soto is waiting for more information regarding his injury on Friday. Either way, it does appear Juan Soto will skip a rehab assignment . “Juan Soto (calf) does not anticipate needing a minor league rehab assignment,” DiComo reported. “Soto says he’s just about ready to return, but will know more after today — a big day in his rehab. Reading between the lines, it sounds like Soto’s return could happen in a matter of days.” It’s been an injury-riddled season for the five-time All-Star, as Soto has missed 50 total games so far this year. When healthy, however, he’s been as good as ever, totaling 83 hits, 21 home runs, and 52 RBIs through 293 at-bats, giving him a .283 batting average and .408 OBP. While a return to the lineup is exciting, the Mets are well behind the playoff race. Although the team is not technically eliminated and still has a chance, the club would have to go on a serious win streak while several other teams in the National League falter. New York is scheduled to take on the Houston Astros on Friday to begin a three-game series. The Mets will then take on the Tampa Bay Rays in a three-game road series. If the reports about Juan Soto are true, then he could be in line to return at some point during these series. articles.title: What Kentucky learned from Youngstown State’s 43-10 season-opening win
articles.summary: Youngstown State rolled to a 43-10 win in its season opener. Here's what Kentucky fans learned about Beau Brungard and the Penguins.
articles._body: Yesterday, we used the first college football Thursday of the season to do a little advance scouting on Kentucky’s Week 1 opponent. In our Kentucky Fan’s Guide To Youngstown State , we introduced the Penguins, reigning FCS Player of the Year Beau Brungard, and several other names to know before they visit Kroger Field next Saturday. Today, we have fresh film on Youngstown after last night’s 43-10 win over Mercyhurst. (That’s a real team.) The Penguins offense we previewed looked the part, scoring on their first five possessions and piling up 484 yards of offense in the blowout. By halftime, Youngstown led 29-3, then jumped up 36-3 before the offense was finally stopped. As we expected, Beau Brungard was the star. Yep, Brungard is good The reigning FCS Player of the Year, Brungard showed why he could be a repeat winner, and why Kentucky’s defense can’t overlook its FCS opponent. Against Mercyhurst, he accounted for 351 yards of offense and five touchdowns , completing 20 of 29 passes for 232 yards and three scores while rushing 21 times for 119 yards and two more touchdowns. It was the 11th time in his career that Brungard topped 100 yards both passing and rushing in the same game, and he almost did it by halftime. Of course, Brungard’s season debut came against a team still acclimating to Division I football. Kentucky’s defense is on a completely different level than what Youngstown hosted last night. Still, Brungard’s a dynamic QB, playing behind a veteran offensive line for one of the best teams in FCS. Containing him is the key to the game. Mercyhurst moved the ball early While Youngstown’s strength is its offense, the defense is mostly new, and last night, it nearly gave up a touchdown on the first drive. Mercyhurst took the opening possession 63 yards in 10 plays, reaching the YSU 2-yard line before the Penguins made their goal-line stand, helped out by a dropped touchdown pass. Mercyhurst settled for a 24-yard field goal to take an early 3-0 lead. From there, however, Youngstown’s defense locked in. Mercyhurst gained only 178 yards over the final 55 minutes and didn’t reach the end zone until the final two minutes. That opening drive should catch Kentucky’s attention, though. If Mercyhurst can move the ball 63 yards on its first crack at the Penguins, Kenny Minchey and Will Stein’s new-look offense should like its chances next Saturday. We’ll have plenty more on the Youngstown matchup and football in the Bluegrass as we count down to Sept. 5 in Lexington.

articles.title: Show HN: Dipstick Alerts – Search recalls and service bulletins for your car
articles.summary:
Hi HN!

When I bought my first car, a 2019 Subaru Forester, I also bought an extended warranty. I wanted to stay informed about problems that might be covered, so I started checking NHTSA.gov—the website of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, a U.S. agency—every month for new ser
articles._body: Hi HN! When I bought my first car, a 2019 Subaru Forester, I also bought an extended warranty. I wanted to stay informed about problems that might be covered, so I started checking NHTSA.gov—the website of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, a U.S. agency—every month for new service bulletins. Those bulletins pointed me to problems I might not otherwise have recognized as repairable. For example, my trunk would not open as far in cold weather. I probably would not have asked the dealer about it, but I found a service bulletin describing the problem and was able to get it fixed under warranty. I wanted a simpler way to find information relevant to my car and to be notified when something new appeared, so I built Dipstick Alerts. This was also my first substantial project built with extensive help from AI coding tools. You can use the site without signing up: select a year, make, and model to search for recalls and manufacturer service bulletins. Results include a plain-language summary, symptom notes, suggested next steps, and a link to the original manufacturer document when available. Email alerts are optional. NHTSA is the underlying data source, so coverage is currently focused on vehicles sold in the United States. Some of the information may still be useful elsewhere because many vehicles and components are sold globally, but models and bulletin applicability can differ between markets. A daily process scans for newly published recalls and bulletins, imports them through queues, matches them to applicable vehicles, tracks superseding bulletins, and prepares alerts for subscribers. Some of the plain-language content is generated from the source documents using Gemini. The original manufacturer documents remain the authoritative source. The application runs on Cloudflare Workers using D1, Queues, KV, and email sending. I’d especially appreciate reports of incorrect vehicle matches and feedback on whether the summaries are genuinely useful, whether anything in the search or alert flow is confusing, and how the site performs under load. I’ll be around to answer questions and fix problems. Thanks for trying it! Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49483465 Points: 1 # Comments: 3

articles.title: Blue Jays DFA pitcher amid postseason push
articles.summary: Although the Toronto Blue Jays are in last place in the AL East, the club is still right on the doorstep of potentially securing a playoff spot as a Wild Card team. With the organization making a final push for the postseason, the front office announced some roster moves on Friday. The Blue Jays
articles._body: Although the Toronto Blue Jays are in last place in the AL East, the club is still right on the doorstep of potentially securing a playoff spot as a Wild Card team. With the organization making a final push for the postseason, the front office announced some roster moves on Friday. The Blue Jays announced they are recalling right-handed pitcher CJ Van Eyk from Triple-A Buffalo, and he will be active for Friday’s contest against the Seattle Mariners. To make room on the roster for Eyk, Toronto DFA’d right-hander Simeon Woods Richardson. “ROSTER MOVES,” the Blue Jays announced. “RHP CJ Van Eyk recalled from Triple-A and will be active tonight. RHP Simeon Woods Richardson designated for assignment.” This will be Van Eyk’s second stint with the Blue Jays, as he made his MLB debut earlier this season with the club. The 27-year-old will have a chance to help Toronto’s attempt to reach the playoffs. Through 5.2 innings pitched so far in the majors, Van Eyk owns a 4.76 ERA and 2.118 WHIP with just one strikeout. The Blue Jays are hoping his play at the minor league level will shine through in the final stretch of the 2026 campaign. This season at Triple-A Buffalo, CJ Van Eyk has recorded 68 strikeouts through 95.0 innings pitched, giving him a 3.79 ERA and 1.337 WHIP. As for Simeon Woods Richardson, the fifth-year pro has been less than efficient this year, playing 12 games with the Minnesota Twins and eight with the Blue Jays . However, his time in Toronto has been much more successful than in Minnesota. His 18.1 innings pitched with the Blue Jays have led him to a 3.93 ERA and 1.418 WHIP. Todd Golden lands new 6-year contract extension with Florida
articles.summary: Florida Gators head coach Todd Golden is considered one of the best coaches in the college basketball business, and in this day and age of rotating rosters and coaches shuffling in and out, he won’t be going anywhere anytime soon. Golden has agreed to a new contract extension with the program for
articles._body: Florida Gators head coach Todd Golden is considered one of the best coaches in the college basketball business, and in this day and age of rotating rosters and coaches shuffling in and out, he won’t be going anywhere anytime soon. Golden has agreed to a new contract extension with the program for six years, as per Jon Rothstein of CBS Sports. Financial details regarding Todd Golden’s new contract extension with Florida were not immediately available, but he is expected to remain as one of college basketball’s highest-paid coaches, as per Rothstein. This upcoming year will be Golden’s fifth season at the helm as head coach after being hired ahead of the 2022-23 season. He led the program to the 2025 national championship, Florida’s first since the 2006-07 season. This past year, the Gators finished with an overall record of 27-8, and 16-2 in SEC play, while advancing to the round of 32 in the NCAA Tournament . In each of his previous four seasons as Florida head coach, Golden has reached the NCAA Tournament in three of them, while making it to the NIT in his first year. He holds an overall record of 103-41 while at Florida. The former Saint Mary’s point guard got his first coaching experience as an assistant with stints at Colombia, Auburn and San Francisco before taking over the Dons’ program ahead of the 2019-20 season amid Kyle Smith leaving for Washington State. He was head coach at USF for three seasons from 2019-2022, leading the Dons to an NCAA Tournament appearance in 2022, the program’s first in 14 years. In recent seasons amid his success at both USF and Florida, Golden has been mentioned as a potential NBA coaching candidate . articles.summary: While on his official visit to Xavier, four-star small forward Markus Kerr has decided to commit to Richard Pitino and the Musketeers, his agent Nate Conley told Rivals. The 6-foot-6 rising senior out of Wellington Sports Academy (FL) considered  Baylor, Maryland, NC State, and Tennessee as his othe
articles._body: While on his official visit to Xavier , four-star small forward Markus Kerr has decided to commit to Richard Pitino and the Musketeers, his agent Nate Conley told Rivals. The 6-foot-6 rising senior out of Wellington Sports Academy (FL) considered Baylor , Maryland , NC State , and Tennessee as his other finalists. Kerr is ranked as the No. 62 overall recruit in the 2027 class and the No. 16 ranked small forward, according to the Rivals Industry Ranking , an average of all three major recruiting media companies (Rivals, ESPN, 247Sports). This summer on the Nike EYBL Circuit, Kerr averaged 15.3 points, 5.9 rebounds, and 2.3 assists per game while playing with Team United. More on Markus Kerr Rivals National Recruiting Analyst Jamie Shaw has evaluated Kerr for a significant period of time. Here is what he recently had to say about his game: You really have to lock in on Markus Kerr to understand his value. Over the past 18-plus months, he has never been the top option on his team; however, his ability to consistently find his role within the team construct and thrive has been so intriguing to watch. At Brewster (NH) Academy last season, he played more of an energetic four-man role, not having much run for him, but still able to average 13.1 points, 5.5 rebounds, and 1.2 steals while shooting around 48-percent from the field. This summer, with the Team United program on Nike’s EYBL Circuit, Kerr played more of a hybrid-forward role, alongside two top-five ranked players, and worked his way into 15.3 points, 5.9 rebounds, and 2.3 assists on 47-percent shooting from the field. Then you find him with Garner Road in the Adidas 3SSB Championships, and you see Kerr in more of an on-the-ball role. His 3.0 assists per game were second on the team, and given his new spot on the roster, he came off the bench to also average 10.1 points. No matter the situation or the role, Kerr has always found a way to produce and make winning-type plays. A two-way player who is 6-foot-6, with explosive burst and ball skills; there is a lot of intrigue still left in the tank.

articles.title: WWE bringing Wrestlepalooza back, but there’s a catch
articles.summary: The very first WWE PLE on ESPN as part of their broadcasting deal was Wrestlepalooza, which will return in 2026, but not in the same location. On Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026, WWE announced that it will be returning to Perth, Australia, after Crown Jewel 2025, to bring Wrestlepalooza — which took plac
articles._body: The very first WWE PLE on ESPN as part of their broadcasting deal was Wrestlepalooza, which will return in 2026, but not in the same location. On Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026, WWE announced that it will be returning to Perth, Australia, after Crown Jewel 2025, to bring Wrestlepalooza — which took place in Indianapolis, Indiana, last year — there on Saturday, Dec. 12. Perth, Western Australia, will host WWE Weekend Takeovers annually over the next three years kicking off with Wrestlepalooza: Perth on December 12, 2026 live from RAC Arena. Three-event combo tickets go on sale Thursday, Sept. 10 at 10 AM AWST. https://t.co/5TEVoURgy1 pic.twitter.com/u5Ieg9oxff — WWE (@WWE) August 27, 2026 That will not be the only show in Western Australia in December. WWE will also broadcast the Friday Night SmackDown before (on Dec. 11) and the Monday Night RAW after (on Dec. 14) at RAC Arena. Fans can sign up for pre-sale access. Three-event combo tickets will be available to purchase on Thursday, Sep. 10 at 10 am AWST. WWE’s second-ever Wrestlepalooza Mandatory Credit: © Grace Smith/IndyStar / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images The card for the second-ever Wrestlepalooza is unknown as of the time of this writing. Expect it to be a star-studded show, if last year’s event is any indication. The first Wrestlepalooza was headlined by John Cena vs. Brock Lesnar for the last time. They have a storied history, but their feud was put to bed at the event. Unfortunately for Cena, it was no different than their matchup from SummerSlam 2014. The “Beast Incarnate” obliterated the 17-time world champion in the event’s opening match. This set the tone for the last leg of his retirement tour. Additionally, AJ Lee made her return to the ring for the first time in a decade. She teamed up with her husband, CM Punk, to face another WWE husband-wife duo, Seth Rollins and Becky Lynch. Stephanie Vaquer defeated Iyo Sky to win the vacated Women’s World Championship at Wrestlepalooza 2025. This marked her first world championship on the main roster. The main event was a singles match for the Undisputed WWE Championship between Cody Rhodes and Drew McIntyre. The “American Nightmare” beat the “Scottish Warrior” to retain the championship. articles.title: South Carolina addresses point guard need with crucial transfer
articles.summary: The South Carolina Gamecocks were dealt a major blow this offseason when point guard Maddy McDaniel announced her intentions to step away from the program and college basketball. McDaniel was in line to be the Gamecocks’ starting point guard next season, forcing them to pivot late in the process.
articles._body: The South Carolina Gamecocks were dealt a major blow this offseason when point guard Maddy McDaniel announced her intentions to step away from the program and college basketball. McDaniel was in line to be the Gamecocks’ starting point guard next season, forcing them to pivot late in the process. But South Carolina was able to rebound quickly with the addition of Brooke Daniels out of the transfer portal, as per Talia Goodman of On3, at least for now. Brooke Daniels had initially entered the transfer portal earlier this month amid court rulings that temporarily granted eligibility to multiple players from the class of 2022, and settled on South Carolina. While some of the rulings have been halted by higher courts , that hasn’t happened yet regarding Daniels. She also was not selected in the WNBA Draft and did not participate in training camp or the regular season, potentially helping her amid the SEC’s attempt to restrict players who had already been pros . While nothing is set in stone, if Daniels’ eligibility holds up, she most likely has the inside track to start at point guard for South Carolina this upcoming season. The fifth-year guard began her college basketball career at Oakland where she played from 2022-2024 before transferring to Michigan for what would have been her final two seasons of eligibility. This past year, she appeared in 35 games for the Wolverines, including 31 starts, at a little over 25 minutes per game. She averaged 5.9 points, 5.4 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 2.5 steals with splits of 48 percent shooting from the field and 69 percent shooting from the free-throw line. She was also named to the All-Big Ten Defensive Team this past season. The post South Carolina addresses point guard need with crucial transfer appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles._body: Chris Sale has been the talk of baseball over the past 24 hours after he pitched his first shutout since 2019 against the Los Angeles Dodgers. There’s another pitcher who has been in the headlines, and it’s Paul Skenes, but only because of his recent dip in velocity. Everyone has seemed to be worried about him, but Sale is one of the few who can understand what Skenes is going through, while also knowing everything is going to be fine . “Paul has one of the biggest lights on him of any baseball player, maybe even athlete in sports,” Sale said on the Pat McAfee Show. “Those things happen. You’re talking about a grind of a season. He’s really in his 2nd full season as a starting pitcher. “ @Paul_Skenes is really in his second full season as a starting pitcher.. You’re talking about a grind of a season and these things happen.. I’ve gotta be honest.. I laugh at the people that are worried about Paul Skenes” ~ Chris Sale #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/Xvw9k8VT3Q — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) August 28, 2026 “I remember my 1st full year as a starter in 2012; it was a grind to get to the end. It’s one of those things where it’s weird how it’s tough to do, but once you do it, it becomes a little bit easier to repeat. I’ve got to be honest, I laugh at the people who are worried about Paul’s games, and I envy their unawareness to the sport.” There should be no reason to have doubt that Skenes isn’t going to find his groove again. Pittsburgh Pirates manager Don Kelly definitely doesn’t have any concerns about his star pitcher, and as long as Skenes feels good, everything should be fine. “I think that the velo this year has been down and even consistently from the beginning of the season. I think that it’s something that you always have to be mindful of and monitor, and I think that the main thing is that Paul says that he feels good,” Kelly said on MLB Network Radio. articles.title: Derrick Odum Shares Updates About his Safeties Room
articles.summary: Utah safeties coach Derrick Odum shares some final updates before the 2026 season kicks off.
articles._body: Safety could end up being one of the biggest strengths of this Utah football team in 2026. Derrick Odum has an extremely deep and talented room, and the Utes will lean on this season. Throughout the course of fall camp, lots of focus has been on Utah using more three-safety sets this season. Odum again reiterated that earlier this week. “They’re really a versatile group. We have a few guys that can play multiple positions back there, whether it be a true safety or a nickel or something like that. We could have three of them on the field at any one time, and so you know we’re working through some of that right now, but feel good with the room and that versatility. Any of those guys can play multiple positions, and it helps our defense out because the more athletes you got on the field, the better. Especially in the back end, the better you’ll be. So it’s it’s it’s a good thing to have for sure,” Odum said. Jackson Bennee and Rabbit Evans have been singled out as guys who can play multiple positions in the defensive backfield this year. Odum spoke highly of the pair as well, saying both have made some strides to make themselves better before the season. “He’s taken on the details of the position a little bit more,” Odum said of Bennee. “I think he’s feeling more comfortable in his role, and he’s taking on the job of being more detailed in all the nuances of being a safety, whether it be a post player. You’re just not in the middle of the field, just hanging out and roaming around. There’s there’s a pattern to what you need to have with your eyes, and he’s really taking ownership in those little details, also he’s a really good man cover guy, and so him having that versatility of being in the post, playing man to man, maybe in a half field safety, all those things, he’s really honed in on the details of each of those job titles per call.” “Coming off that injury, he’s a lot quicker with his feet and just feels more confident in his ability to cover man to man down the field and such. So again, another guy that really, really pleased with where he’s at at this point,” Odum said about Evans. None of the versatility in this room will matter if the members of the secondary can’t tackle. Odum says that there has been some improvement in that area, but the group is continuing to get better every day. “It’s all about getting yourself in position to make tackles, and then the finishing part of a tackle. And we break it down in parts. The angles to make a tackle, tracking the near hip, not overrunning the ball, and then trying to get to the opposite leg to make those tackles,” he said. “We work on the details of that every single day, and hopefully it shows up when we get a chance to go live in our first game, but it’s an ongoing process. I feel like they’re getting more and more comfortable in those positions, and hopefully it shows.” Watch the full press conference below: Take your Utah fandom to the next level by joining the ultimate community for dedicated fans at UteZone. articles.title: Braves’ Chris Sale explains what led to 100 MPH fastball vs. Shohei Ohtani
articles.summary: As Atlanta Braves star Chris Sale recorded a complete-game shutout against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Thursday night, there was one instance that caught fans off guard. The Braves’ pitcher would throw a 100-mile-per-hour pitch for the first time in eight years, and it was against no one oth
articles._body: As Atlanta Braves star Chris Sale recorded a complete-game shutout against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Thursday night, there was one instance that caught fans off guard. The Braves’ pitcher would throw a 100-mile-per-hour pitch for the first time in eight years, and it was against no one other than Dodgers sensation Shohei Ohtani, as Sale revealed what led to that moment. In the impeccable game against the Dodgers, Sale would record 11 strikeouts, two of them coming against Ohtani, though the 100-mile-per-hour pitch came in the top of the third inning. Sale’s fourth pitch of the at-bat was a four-seam fastball that went 100 miles per hour , leading to Ohtani fouling it off as the 37-year-old said on “The Pat McAfee Show” that it was the “circumstances” of the game that led to the pitch. “Yeah, well, I dare you to throw a get-me-over fastball to Shohei,” Sale said. “He’d probably hit that thing to the freaking Comcast building. So yeah, I mean, I think the game will dictate and tell you when it’s time to kind of bear down and kind of dig in a little bit, and I think given the circumstances, when you have a generational guy like he is, because I mean, let’s face it, he’s kind of the gold standard guy right now of of what it is to be just an ultimate baseball player, right? I mean, he’s doing things no one’s ever seen, and you get in those situations, and it’s a tight game.” “I dare you to throw a get me over fastball to Shohei Ohtani The game will dictate and tell you when it's time to dig in a little bit.. Our fans were going crazy and I could feel that" Chris Sale #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/I437hGDQhf — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) August 28, 2026 Chris Sale threw Shohei Ohtani a 100.1 MPH fastball. It was the first time he's thrown over 100 MPH since 2018, and the seventh-fastest pitch of his career pic.twitter.com/zz0ysWakRF — Talkin' Baseball (@TalkinBaseball_) August 28, 2026 Braves’ Chris Sale on the atmosphere leading to 100-mile-per-hour pitch Sale would also credit the “atmosphere and adrenaline” of the contest, which was a full-packed house at Truist Park on Friday night that led to the incredible outing, leading to the Braves’ 1-0 win over the Dodgers. At any rate, Sale’s impressive season continues, as he’s now at a 2.06 ERA with 177 strikeouts and a 13-9 record, as his next scheduled start is on Sept. 2 against the Washington Nationals. It remains to be seen if the pitcher can reach 100 miles per hour again on a pitch. articles.title: SEC, commissioner Greg Sankey included in amended Louisiana eligibility TRO
articles.summary: The SEC and Commissioner Greg Sankey have been included in an amended Louisiana eligibility TRO, On3’s Pete Nakos has learned. Recently, the SEC voted to ban players who have played professional sports — football and basketball — from rejoining the conference. But lawsuits over the
articles._body: The SEC and Commissioner Greg Sankey have been included in an amended Louisiana eligibility TRO, On3’s Pete Nakos has learned. Recently, the SEC voted to ban players who have played professional sports — football and basketball — from rejoining the conference. But lawsuits over the matter continue down South as kickoff is just over a week away. The amended filing issued a show-cause order to the NCAA, demanding the organization appear before the Louisiana state court at 11 am CT on Sept. 3 to defend itself against a contempt of court charge for violating the TRO’s order in light of the SEC’s new pro player ban. The updated TRO also includes a citation that reveals the plaintiffs “do not seek to hold the SEC in contempt at this time,” but added the SEC and Sankey as defendants to “seek injunctive relief against them via a separate motion.” [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] A couple of names specifically tied to Lane Kiffin and the LSU Tigers are also named. Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris have both committed to play the 2026 college football season in Baton Rouge. However, the rule implemented by the SEC was thought to end the matter. Wright and Harris are still looking to suit up for LSU after previously being in NFL training camps. Sankey was recently named in another suit in Dallas, TX. A judge filed a TRO for multiple players, including former SMU Mustangs and Dallas Cowboys wide receiver Jordan Hudson . Nearly 40 players were named. Louisiana Governor calls out SEC, NCAA In both football and men’s basketball, LSU finds itself in multiple eligibility battles. Kiffin and Will Wade are both looking to improve rosters ahead of their respective seasons. In the case of Kiffin, Week 1 is under two weeks away. However, recent rule changes from the SEC state players from the NFL or NBA are not allowed to return to the conference . We might have gotten a sense of how LSU feels about the rule, as they were the  lone member to abstain from a vote confirming the penalties . Now, Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry is sharing his thoughts on the matter. Like plenty of other people in Baton Rouge, Landry is not all too happy. “This whole thing is ridiculous,” Landry said via Amanda Christovich of FOS . “Don’t hate the player, hate the game. I’ve been saying for a year that college sports need to be fixed. The NCAA could have done it. Congress could have done it. Neither did. Now the SEC is creating a legal mess over athletes it told were out of eligibility, only to change the rules afterward. “The SEC accepted the courts’ decisions on Diego Pavia and Trinidad Chambliss . Why is this different? You can’t tell athletes their college careers are over, watch them move on, change the rules later, and then punish them for not predicting the future.”

articles.title: The Warning Break Down 5 Essential Songs From New Album ‘Everything’s Falling’
articles.summary: The Mexican hard rock trio release their fifth LP, further cementing their rise as one of the most exciting young acts on the global stage.
articles._body: Mexican band The Warning took a three-month break from its international tour to focus on making their new album,  Everything’s Falling . The Villarreal Vélez sisters say they wanted enough time to capture the sonic and lyrical growth they’ve experienced in recent years as a standout hard rock and alternative band, whose music has connected with millions of listeners around the world. Everything’s Falling  arrived Friday (Aug. 28) on digital platforms via Lava/Republic Records. Across its 12 songs, the band — Daniela (vocals), Alejandra (bass) and Paulina (drums) — explore growth, resilience and uncertainty throughout their journey, while also delivering empowering lyrics about the challenge of being women in a male-dominated scene. “Being in different places in our lives, I think we gave ourselves the freedom to express ourselves in a much more personal and deeper way than we had before,” Daniela tells  Billboard Español  in a video interview. “We wanted to explore what we want The Warning to be in the years ahead.” “First and foremost, we gave ourselves permission to have a lot of fun, not take everything too seriously, and loosen up more when it came to the subjects we wanted to talk about,” Paulina adds. “We wanted to explore a heavier sound, so we worked with different guitar effects, different ways of singing, different songwriting styles, and new approaches to my drumming.” Everything’s Falling  was produced and co-written by Anton DeLost, helping the band achieve a sound inspired by ’90s alternative rock on songs like “Kerosene,” as well as nu-metal touches on the single “Ritual.” Other standout tracks on the powerful new album include “Bite My Tongue,” “Kill Or Be Killed” and “Bloodsport.” As with previous albums, the music is mostly in English, The Warning’s second language. This time around, though, the band from Monterrey, Mexico — a city near the U.S. border — also included a Spanish-language song titled “Ego.” “The world’s fascination with Latin music and Latin culture is really incredible. This year, the NFL invited us to the Super Bowl, we were part of Bad Bunny’s show, and seeing people’s reactions and the international response is something really beautiful,” Daniela says. “It’s beautiful to see how people are gradually becoming more interested in learning about cultures from other parts of the world.” This year, The Warning continues its global rise with shows across the United States, following stops in Europe, Asia and South America, as well as appearances at major festivals around the world and their own headlining concerts. Recent accomplishments also include “Love to Be Loved,” a country-meets-hard-rock duet with regional Mexican superstar Carín León. The band has cemented its place on the international rock scene, appearing on 10  Billboard  charts, including No. 1 on  Emerging Artists , No. 2 on Top Rock Albums ,, No. 4 on Top Hard Rock Albums and No. 6 on Top Album Sales , among others. Most recently, the band made history as the first Mexican act and the first all-female group to top Mainstream Rock Airplay with “Kerosene,” which leads the chart dated Sept. 5. Below, The Warning breaks down five essential songs from  Everything’s Falling . To listen to the full album, click here .

articles.title: ‘Like at McDonald’s’: Sports nurse practitioner sold opioids to athletes like ‘you gotta pay for your burger,” DEA investigation finds
articles.summary: Joan Rubinger had a client list that included hundreds of athletes—but the DEA found she doled out thousands of illegal prescriptions.
articles._body: Joan Rubinger overcame a catastrophic biking accident that left her paralyzed to become an influential pain-relief specialist helping top-tier athletes get back on the field after acute and chronic injuries. Her  website  touts a client list that includes 169 NFL Pro Bowl selections, 29 NBA and WNBA champions and 15 Olympic medalists. Among some of her most notable patients: NBA All Stars  Kobe Bryant  and Dwyane Wade, as well as MLB All Star Fernando Tatis Jr. But behind the scenes, the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration alleged in court filings, Rubinger doled out thousands of illegal prescriptions for  highly addictive painkillers , a “covert and slinking” scheme the nurse practitioner likened to selling hamburgers at a fast-food restaurant. Over a four-year period, federal authorities said, the nurse practitioner prescribed 260,000 pills containing controlled substances to patients in more than 20 states. Citing what an administrative law judge called egregious conduct, the DEA last month  revoked Rubinger’s ability to prescribe opioids . That action followed Rubinger’s agreement in March to pay $1.4 million to settle a parallel Justice Department  civil complaint  that accused her of dispensing controlled substances like oxycodone, Percocet, and Xanax on hundreds of occasions without any legitimate medical purpose. Rubinger did not admit any wrongdoing as part of that settlement and agreed to never again prescribe controlled substances. While authorities announced the settlement earlier this year, federal court papers unsealed at the request of  The Associated Press  provide new details of a medical provider who the DEA says was furtively enriching herself even as she put the health of her patients at risk. The scheme, the DEA alleged in a seizure warrant, expanded over the years “from professional athletes” to a wide-range of other clients, including members of an Ohio-based street gang, a confessed New Jersey drug trafficker and a New York City model. Along the way, federal authorities alleged, the nurse practitioner took steps to avert DEA suspicion, coaching clients over an encrypted messaging app on ways to avoid having their prescriptions flagged by pharmacies. The  DEA  described how two former athletes received illicit prescriptions from Rubinger, including former All-Pro Carolina Panthers linebacker Thomas Davis, whose wife alerted the agency to the nurse practitioner’s activities, according to the court records and an interview with the player’s now ex-spouse. Rubinger started prescribing Davis opioids as he was bouncing between teams before he retired after the 2020 season, according to his wife. In all, authorities alleged, he received more than 13,000 oxycodone and Percocet pills between November 2019 and March 2024. Davis did not respond to requests for comment and no one answered his door in North Carolina when visited by an AP reporter. The DEA identified another former reserve NBA guard who, along with his wife, paid Rubinger more than $50,000 for illicit prescriptions well after he left the league. He could not be reached for comment. Rubinger’s case did not result in criminal charges A spokesman for Rubinger, Erick Mullen, did not answer questions about the nurse practitioner’s treatment of Davis or any other athlete, citing medical privacy laws. “Joan’s case was not a criminal matter but a civil action,” he wrote in an email. “No raids with blue windbreakers carrying agency initials, and no loss of liberty at stake.” He said “no administrative or disciplinary actions” had been taken by nursing boards in California and New York, where she is licensed to practice. Mullen also did not address AP’s questions about Rubinger’s alleged ties to the Ohio-based Loyal to Brothers street gang but suggested they represented “actual harm” to his client. “You’ll have to imagine what kind of people threatened, intimidated, bullied and cajoled a paraplegic nurse practitioner and single mother into this kind of situation,” he wrote. Federal prosecutors declined to comment on why they did not pursue criminal charges even as they accused Rubinger in court filings of violating federal drug statutes and regulations 900 times. James Rafalski, a retired DEA investigator, said he worked many cases that ended in criminal charges and involved far larger volumes of pills. But Rubinger’s conduct stood out as especially flagrant, he said, adding he was surprised it did not result in a criminal prosecution. “Most doctors who abuse their DEA registration just write scripts without a thorough examination of the patient,” said Rafalski, who reviewed court records in the case. “She knowingly took steps to evade detection by the DEA and instructed her clients to do the same.” Prosecutors weigh a variety of factors in deciding whether to bring criminal charges, from the strength of the evidence to how a jury is likely to perceive a defendant. Eric Grant, the U.S. attorney in Sacramento, said in a statement to AP that “the significant financial penalty” and ban on Rubinger prescribing controlled substances “grants the public meaningful protections against the unlawful dispensing of dangerous drugs.” A nurse practitioner to the stars Like many of her clients, Rubinger, 49, was once an elite athlete. As a child, she competed internationally in gymnastics. Years later she rowed and pole vaulted at Syracuse University. After graduating, she coached women’s rowing at Indiana University, worked alongside elite NBA trainers and even assisted China’s Olympic volleyball team. “My sculpted physique and bronzed, sun kissed skin were fruits of very hard labor,” she boasted in a personal blog. “Earned. Day after pavement-pounding day.” She started All Pro Sports Medicine around 2010, describing her company as a niche service that offered athletes discrete medical attention at all hours of the day. In 2014, she was licensed as a nurse practitioner

articles.title: ‘We have work to do’: Fed Reserve Chair Warsh suggests rate hike in coming months amid high inflation
articles.summary: Warsh says recent reports on inflation coming down does not tell him "underlying trends have meaningfully improved."
articles._body: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said Friday that  inflation  is still too high and suggested the central bank may have to raise interest rates in the coming months to bring it down, a clearer signal than he had sent previously about his economic outlook. In his first high-profile speech at the Fed’s annual conference in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, Warsh acknowledged that recent U.S. reports  show that inflation has cooled a bit , but “they do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved.” “We must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to our objective, clearly and at sufficient speed,” Warsh said. “Otherwise, we have work to do.” Comments from the new Fed chair appeared to reassure Wall Street that fighting inflation remains the priority for the central bank. Warsh did not imply that a rate hike is imminent, but he appeared to dismiss perceptions that inflation is no longer a threat. He pointed to data showing that inflation remains stubbornly above the central bank’s 2% target. Warsh replaced Jerome Powell in late May after his predecessor’s term ended. The U.S. stock market held steady after the speech, but expectations are building in the bond market for  the Fed  to hike interest rates. The yield on the two-year Treasury, which closely tracks expectations for what the Fed will do with its federal funds rate, moved from 4.22% to 4.30%, a sign that investors expect short-term yields to move higher. Longer-term yields on 10-year and 30-year Treasuries were mostly flat, suggesting investors aren’t worried that higher rates will be needed for a long stretch of time to fight inflation. Jon Faust, an economist at Johns Hopkins and a former adviser to Powell, said Warsh succeeded in conveying a tougher approach on inflation while avoiding the kind of detailed guidance from the Fed that he has disparaged. “He found a way to convey that if necessary he would support raising rates, which is one thing people were concerned about,” Faust said. Yet Michael Strain, director of economic policy studies at the American Enterprise Institute, said the Fed chair has talked tough on inflation before without hiking the Fed’s key rate. His Friday remarks don’t provide any clearer guidance on the timing of any Fed moves, he added. The Fed chair faces high stakes with his speech as questions swirl  around Wall Street  about his focus on fighting inflation. Those concerns may have contributed to rising bond yields, which can increase the cost of borrowing for the government and everyone else. Yet Warsh has said he doesn’t want to provide what analysts call “forward guidance” about whether the Fed will hike or cut rates or stay on hold at upcoming meetings. He argues that it limits the Fed’s flexibility by committing it to a specific policy. Yet some economists have argued that he could say more about his views on Fed policy without tipping his hand about future actions. Warsh on Friday reiterated his skepticism about providing such guidance or even outlining his broad approach to interest-rate policy. But he did suggest that interest rates currently aren’t restricting economic activity, pointing to robust business investment in AI equipment and infrastructure and strong consumer spending. As a rule of thumb, interest rates often need to be high enough to limit borrowing and spending to cool inflation. The Fed next meets Sept. 15-16, and Warsh’s remarks don’t necessarily signal that the central bank will raise rates then. But his speech indicated that rates may not be high enough to bring inflation down to the Fed’s 2% target. Warsh said inflation data “are more concerning” than trends in the job market, where the unemployment rate is low. He also argued that inflation is unlikely to move back to the target on its own. Warsh noted that in the past year, 54% of goods and services tracked by the government have seen price increases of 3% or higher. While that is down from the pandemic peak, it is “well above” the 32% that saw such increases in the two decades before the pandemic. Inflation  cooled  in June and July after spiking in May from soaring gas prices, yet it remains above the central bank’s target. According to the Fed’s preferred measure, it was  3.7% in July . Warsh also sought to clear up some areas of confusion that arose after his remarks at a July 29 news conference. He specified that short-term interest rates are the “predominant tool” the Fed can use to lower inflation. Previous Fed chairs have often used speeches at Jackson Hole to address broad questions about interest-rate policy and the economy, or to signal upcoming changes in their approach. In 2022, with pandemic-era inflation having soared to 9.1%, Powell signaled the Fed would continue to sharply raise interest rates in a fight against runaway prices, and he acknowledged that such maneuvers would bring “pain” to consumers and businesses. Wall Street investors now see the chances of a rate hike at the Fed’s Sept. 15-16 meeting as basically a coin flip, according to futures pricing tracked by CME FedWatch, up from about one-third before Warsh spoke. Questions about Warsh’s approach have intensified amid President Donald Trump’s continued calls for lower interest rates. While Trump has continued to defend Warsh, whom he appointed, the president has criticized other Fed officials for supporting higher rates. Trump has also renewed his efforts to  remove  Fed Governor Lisa Cook, who was appointed by former President Joe Biden. Replacing Cook would enable Trump to appoint a majority of the seven-member board. Trump tried to fire her last year but was temporarily blocked by the Supreme Court. Longer-term rates have  steadily risen in recent weeks  because of a range of factors, including burgeoning U.S. government deficits and outsize borrowing by tech firms building AI infrastructure. articles.title: Rays’ $2.36B Ballpark Gets Final Approval in Tampa
articles.summary: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images
articles._body: The Rays are formally headed to a new, $2.36 billion ballpark in Tampa after the Hillsborough County Commission approved a public funding plan for the project. The commission’s 5–2 vote on Friday followed a narrow approval on Thursday by the City of Tampa council . The two jurisdictions will combine to supply up to $876 million toward the stadium, and the approval seemingly brings an end to an oft-twisting saga that had involved two decades of fruitless searching for a new stadium, an abandoned deal to stay in St. Petersburg , Florida, and an ownership shift to a Patrick Zalupski-led group , Groundbreaking is targeted for later this year at a site at Hillsborough College’s Dale Mabry Campus in advance of a planned ballpark opening in 2029. With that shift, the Rays will be much more centrally located in the Tampa region, and very close toTampa International Airport, and the Buccaneers’ Raymond James Stadium. The mixed-use development surrounding the stadium will be inspired in part by The Battery in Atlanta . “Today our entire region can celebrate the coming of a private finance and mixed-use neighborhood, a reinvested Hillsborough College campus, and a new ballpark that secures the long-term future of Major League Baseball here in Tampa,” said Rays CEO Ken Babby. As with nearly any debate surrounding taxpayer support of stadium and arena projects, Hillsborough County’s deliberation regarding the Rays was fraught with tension, including the optics of supporting a private business owned by a billionaire. Ultimately, though, changes in the final deal shifted more financial responsibility to the club, and the Rays will pay 63% of the ballpark construction costs—a percentage that is higher than what the Rangers and Braves paid, respectively, for Globe Life Field and Truist Park, MLB’s two newest stadiums. “I’ve wondered what I would say if we ever got to the position of being able to discuss and hopefully approve a ballpark agreement,” said county commissioner Ken Hagan, a key figure in the legislative approval process. “Do we want Tampa to be a world-class community? What side of history do you want to be on?” Looking Ahead These two political approvals in Tampa also will likely help accelerate MLB’s path toward expansion. For many years, the league’s consideration of adding teams was held up by facility issues with the A’s and Rays. The A’s, however, are now well along in construction for a new ballpark in Las Vegas, with the facility targeted for a 2028 opening. The Rays now have their situation settled, too, and interest is set to rise around expansion candidates such as Nashville, Salt Lake City, Sacramento , Raleigh, Vancouver, Montreal, and Mexico City. As of now, though, there is no formal process for MLB to expand, and one will almost certainly wait until after the league resolves a difficult labor negotiation with the MLB Players Association. “There’s a lot of markets in the United States and North America, quite frankly, Canada and Mexico, that would like to add Major League Baseball,” MLB commissioner Rob Manfred said earlier this year. “When people want your product, I think it’s kind of incumbent on you to try to figure out a way if you can deliver that product to them.” Manfred said last year at the Front Office Sports Tuned In summit that he would like to have two new markets selected before he finishes his tenure in early 2029 . Those teams would likely not be on the field before then, though. MLB last expanded with the arrival of the Diamondbacks and Rays in 1998. articles.title: Why J.J. Watt isn’t surprised Deshaun Watson is Browns starting QB
articles.summary: With the Cleveland Browns starting Deshaun Watson over Shedeur Sanders at quarterback for the start of the season, there is no denying that the decision has stirred a lot of opinions in the sports world. As the Browns will roll out Watson over Sanders, one person who has a strong opinion on the m
articles._body: With the Cleveland Browns starting Deshaun Watson over Shedeur Sanders at quarterback for the start of the season, there is no denying that the decision has stirred a lot of opinions in the sports world. As the Browns will roll out Watson over Sanders, one person who has a strong opinion on the matter is former star and analyst J.J. Watt. Also a former teammate of Watson with the Houston Texans, Watt would be asked on “The Pat McAfee Show” if he is surprised by the team’s decision to start the 30-year-old over Sanders, who is entering his second year in the league. Watt expressed that he isn’t, saying that if a competition is close, any team is likely to lean more towards the player with the monumental contract that Watson currently has. “I would say I’m not surprised,” Watt said. “It kind of seems like this is the way they had been going all offseason and training camp, and I would say in terms of if things are close at all in in a competition, we all know, if things are close, when you’re paying somebody 230 million dollars fully guaranteed, that’s the person that you’re going to want to give every single opportunity to, to hopefully somehow some way make you right on that contract that many people question and say is is one of the worst in history. It doesn’t surprise me that they’ve gone that way.” "I'm not surprised that Deshaun Watson was named the starter for the Cleveland Browns.. They haven't been able to find their quarterback for a very long time.. They have a really good fanbase and I would love to see them be successful" ~ @JJWatt #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/nW0MsZAfBI — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) August 28, 2026 J.J. Watt on when the Browns would start Shedeur Sanders There is another question that Watt ponders, which is when the Browns could potentially go away from Watson and start Sanders, as he’s unsure. “The question everybody asks: Is how long is this going to last, and how good will he be? And who knows? I don’t know the answer to that, but I’m certainly going to be watching. And it’s tough. They haven’t been able to find their quarterback there for a very, very long time,” Watt said. It remains to be seen how Cleveland’s quarterback situation develops over the season with Week 1 on Sept. 13 against the Jacksonville Jaguars. The post Why J.J. Watt isn’t surprised Deshaun Watson is Browns starting QB appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Cubs fans will appreciate this Clay Holmes admission
articles.summary: National League MVP contender Pete Crow-Armstrong leads all players this season with a +24 fielding run value, per FanGraphs, but Chicago Cubs starting pitcher Clay Holmes does not need to rely on his defensive excellence very often. The men who provide him with the most assistance occupy the dia
articles._body: National League MVP contender Pete Crow-Armstrong leads all players this season with a +24 fielding run value , per FanGraphs, but Chicago Cubs starting pitcher Clay Holmes does not need to rely on his defensive excellence very often. The men who provide him with the most assistance occupy the diamond. The veteran right-hander, who arrived in The North Side via a trade deadline deal with the New York Mets , is known for inducing a high number of ground balls. Therefore, he is extremely grateful for the support he consistently receives. Although the Cubs’ infield is overflowing with sure hands and superb instincts, Holmes is more impressed with his teammates’ relentless commitment . “Yeah, there’s a lot of Gold Gloves here, but I just think that the way the guys play here — they play hard,” the two-time All-Star closer told Marquee Sports Network before Friday afternoon’s series opener versus the Cincinnati Reds. “You see the effort behind you (every time), diving for balls in the hole. It just gives you that much more {of an} edge on the mound, and you can feel it out there. They’re wanting to make plays. “Especially a guy like me that can get the ball on the ground, it makes my job way easier. I can just trust the sinker and let those guys work.” "Every time you see the effort behind you, diving for balls in the hole, it just gives you that much more edge on the mound. You can feel it out there." Clay Holmes on his confidence in the Cubs' defense. pic.twitter.com/6xR50GGyd6 — Marquee Sports Network (@WatchMarquee) August 28, 2026 Two-time All-Star shortstop Dansby Swanson is currently on the injured list with an oblique strain, but he ranks in the top-five in outs above average (16). Fellow two-time Gold Glover Nico Hoerner is highly reliable at second base. Big free-agent acquisition Alex Bregman mans the hot corner with relative ease. And Michael Busch has made noticeable strides at first. Put everything together, and is obvious why Chicago coveted Clay Holmes. Aside from a shaky debut against the Kansas City Royals, the 33-year-old has been terrific for his new team. He has allowed just one run on nine hits in his last 19 innings pitched. Holmes has generated 37 ground balls during that span. This hurler is slated for a huge role this postseason, but he is counting on the gloves around him to stay elite. If this partnership continues to work as intended, then the Cubs could hang around a little longer this October. Maybe a lot longer. articles.title: Mystics’ Georgia Amoore backs up bold Sydney Johnson claim with career night vs. Mercury
articles.summary: The Washington Mystics have been led by center Shakira Austin, guard Sonia Citron, and forward Kiki Iriafen this season, but rookie guard Georgia Amoore is finding her groove too. The 25-year-old tallied a career-high 25 points (9-16 FG, 6-11 3-point) with four assists, two rebounds, and two stea
articles._body: The Washington Mystics have been led by center Shakira Austin , guard Sonia Citron, and forward Kiki Iriafen this season, but rookie guard Georgia Amoore is finding her groove too. The 25-year-old tallied a career-high 25 points (9-16 FG, 6-11 3-point) with four assists, two rebounds, and two steals over 30 minutes in an 80-73 win over the Phoenix Mercury on Thursday, and she now has three games with 10-plus points and three-plus assists in her last four appearances. Mystics head coach Sydney Johnson waxed poetic about Amoore when asked who the most underrated player on the team is on August 15. “Oh, I love that question. I love that question,” he told ClutchPoints. “Jeez, I don’t want to leave anybody out. I like this one. I know it’s gonna stir up a lot.” “Georgia Amoore is a player that plays for the team. Georgia has a lot that she can do individually,” he continued. “And yet, in a rookie year and coming off a major injury, she has tried to deal with that physically, mentally and emotionally, while also trying to bring her game back. And at times, we’ve seen flashes of that.” Amoore has experienced adversity since Washington drafted her No. 6 overall in 2025. The former Kentucky Wildcat tore her right ACL at the start of training camp, sidelining her for the season while Citron and Iriafen had All-Star rookie campaigns. She kept the starting point guard role this year, but she’s averaging 6.5 points on just 35.6% shooting (32.3% 3-point) with 3.4 assists against 2.1 turnovers over 22.9 minutes (39 games). However, Johnson never lost confidence in her. “Behind the scenes, her player development is through the roof in terms of various things that we’re focusing on,” he continued. “Scoring passes, getting her three-point reps, being solid-to-good defensively. But when she’s on the court, she’s able to help other players, whoever they are, play better, more connected.” The 5-foot-6 Amoore will never be a defensive force, but she will always provide value if she effectively facilitates the offense and hits open threes. She’s second to Citron on Washington in assists and is tied with forward Michaela Onyenwere for the lead with 1.4 three-pointers made per game, so she has room for growth in both areas. “It’s a culture and a feel that she brings to our team, which is not all that matters, but it’s a big deal,” Johnson said. “For me, she’s someone who really typifies what it is to be a Mystic, to play for others.” While Amoore’s primary job is to set up her teammates, sometimes “playing for others” means spearheading a comeback when the squad needs it. The Mystics were down 57-53 after three quarters on Thursday, but Amoore scored 16 of their 27 points in the final period to secure the victory. Plus, the rest of the group went just 1-of-6 from deep in the game, so her long-range shooting was crucial. Ahead of Friday’s road date with the Los Angeles Sparks, Amoore has scored 64 points (22-45 FG, 16-32 3-point) with 16 assists and eight turnovers over her last five games after totaling three points (1-17 FG, 1-13 3-point), 12 dimes and seven giveaways across the five contests before that. If she maintains her current momentum after the World Cup break, she could help Washington make a deep playoff run. Shakira Austin reflects on Mystics’ growth Soobum Im-Imagn Images Unlike Amoore and everyone else on the squad, Austin has played in Washington since 2022. The team went 22-14 and made the playoffs that year, but suffered three consecutive losing seasons before qualifying for the tournament again this season. She’s seen the organization change regimes and rebuild, giving her the best perspective on its growth. Austin told ClutchPoints on August 19 what the Mystics have learned about what it takes to win this season. “I think we definitely understood that our defense has to be our foundation,” the 2022 No. 3 overall pick said. “And that’s why the coaches and I are not [always] happy with how we play, just because we know we can be so much better defensively. We know that’s going to carry through the rest of the season and hopefully into the postseason.” Washington has allowed the second-fewest points per game (82.9) and has the second-best defensive field goal percentage (42.9) in the WNBA after ranking ninth (81.6) and eighth (44.4) in those categories last season, respectively. It’s no coincidence that the Mystics are 24-15 this year after going 16-28 in 2025. “Just allowing that to dictate a lot of what we do offensively and then just continuing to play smart, trying to protect the ball a little bit, cutting down our turnovers,” Austin continued. “Obviously playing through our posts and understanding the impact and the gravity that we’re going to have, and allowing that to get our teammates easier shots and get the three-ball going, hopefully.” Washington is second with 42.9 points in the paint per game and first with 25.1 free throws attempted, showing its ability to pressure the rim. That hasn’t led to a consistent three-point attack despite the natural spacing that creates outside, as it’s 14th with a 29.9% clip from deep, but Amoore converted several open long-range shots on Thursday. Integrating that into the offense more consistently will raise the team’s ceiling. The Mystics are currently sixth in the WNBA standings, one game behind the Indiana Fever and one ahead of the Dallas Wings. Friday’s matchup with the Sparks is their last before the World Cup break. Tennis Stars Excited About Grand Slam Council, Details Remain Sparse
articles.summary: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images
articles._body: NEW YORK — The tennis Grand Slams took a major step in working with its players last week, announcing they will create a Grand Slam Advisory Council and add a player support program alongside record prize money at the US Open . There is still, however, little that is set in stone about the council, including the players who will be a part of it, women’s No. 3 Jessica Pegula told Front Office Sports on Friday at the US Open. “We haven’t really gotten into the nitty gritty of how people will be selected for the council,” said Pegula, who is also part of the WTA Players’ Council. She added that there are “some top players and other players who are very interested.” A spokesperson for the USTA told Front Office Sports that the idea was for the council to be announced ahead of the tournament, but that the finer details will be ironed out in the weeks following the year’s final Grand Slam. Asked by FOS about the USTA’s announcements, world No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka, who has suggested the possibility of boycotting a tournament , said during her press conference Friday that she was “super happy” about the announcements. “Hopefully we’re not going to boycott media or tournament or anything in the future,” Sabalenka said. Pegula told FOS the main point of contention will continue to be players’ revenue share at the Grand Slams, which has consistently been at around 15%, including at Roland–Garros in May, when top players staged a coordinated media protest . There is no fixed revenue share at Grand Slams, and players are seeking 22% of revenue by 2030. Total player compensation at the 2026 US Open is $108 million, about 19.3% of the tournament’s operating revenue in 2024, the last publicly available number. “That’s something we’re still pushing for, and so I think hopefully with this council, that we’ll be able to continue those discussions because I know from our side, we still do believe that a revenue share is the best way, and now we’ll just have much more open communication,” Pegula said. Pegula said that there was no direct line of communication between players and Grand Slam organizers in the past, saying the way players would air their opinions was “very random” and that they would sometimes not even hear back. She cited the Grand Slam’s decision to institute 10-point tiebreaks for deciding sets, which start in 2022, as one example. “We, mostly, said no, and then they did it anyway,” Pegula said. “And we were like, ‘Well, what’s the point of even asking us?’” Pegula also commended the USTA for taking the lead among the Grand Slams in creating the council. “There is still of course more work to do and there’s going to be a lot of things that come up, but I am definitely appreciative of, especially the US Open, to kind of step forward with making those announcements and wanting to do that,” Pegula said during her press conference Friday. articles._body: The Chicago Cubs are trying to get healthy at this point in the season, and they’ve gotten some positive updates for some of their players. Dansby Swanson was placed on the 10-day injured list over a week ago after suffering a left oblique strain, but he’s been working his way back on the field. Swanson was recently seen taking some grounders , and this is a good sign for his return. Dansby Swanson was taking some grounders on the field today! pic.twitter.com/nZWOjLohf3 — Marquee Sports Network (@WatchMarquee) August 28, 2026 It’s still uncertain when he’ll be back, but the hope is that it’s sooner rather than later. At the time of the injury, it was expected for him to miss four weeks, which means he has roughly two or so weeks left until he can fully get back. If that’s still the timetable, he’ll be able to return before the postseason. The Cubs recently got some good news about Matt Shaw , who had missed the past two months with a left-hand sprain, and the team recently reinstated off the IL. Before his injury, he was batting .246 with six doubles, two triples, four home runs, 2o RBIs and a .737 OPS in 56 games. There’s no doubt that the Cubs have been missing what Shaw brings to the field, and this stretch of the season is important if they want to secure their position in the playoffs. The Cubs are currently 76-58 and are in second place in the NL Central. Getting healthy over the next few weeks will be key for them, and hopefully, when Swanson comes back, he doesn’t miss a beat. articles.title: WWE NXT star reveals Alopecia Areata diagnosis
articles.summary: In a social media post, WWE NXT star Thea Hail revealed that she has Alopecia Areata and shared a picture of her bald look as a result of it. She made the announcement on social media. Hail posted a carousel of images and videos, including a seemingly photoshopped picture of herself holding the N
articles._body: In a social media post, WWE NXT star Thea Hail revealed that she has Alopecia Areata and shared a picture of her bald look as a result of it. She made the announcement on social media. Hail posted a carousel of images and videos, including a seemingly photoshopped picture of herself holding the NXT Women’s North American Championship while bald. View this post on Instagram Hail also shared a close-up image of her “naked scalp” at the very end of the post. She appears to be in good spirits, though, as her caption read, “I now have alopecia areata… i have literally manifested going bald. Anyways swipe to see my naked scalp and some cute pics of me with and without hair.” Who is WWE NXT star Thea Hail? Hail is a WWE NXT Superstar who is best known for controversially beating Blake Monroe to win the Women’s North American Championship. By all accounts, it looked like a botch, as the referee counted to three despite Monroe kicking out. In turn, she won her first championship in WWE. However, her reign would not last long. She lost the title to Izzi Dame after 21 days. Before getting into professional wrestling, Hail, whose real name is Madison Knisley, was a gymnast. She made her professional wrestling debut in AEW in 2021, losing a couple of dark matches. The following year, she joined NXT and was part of the Chase University stable. The now-defunct stable has featured a variety of members, including Andre Chase, Duke Hudson, Jacy Jayne, and Ridge Holland. It disbanded in April 2026. It remains to be seen if Hail will be promoted to the main roster anytime soon. Another former Chase University member, Jayne, is currently on Friday Night SmackDown. She leads her own faction, Fatal Influence, which includes Fallon Henley and Lainey Reid. Perhaps Hail will join them on the main roster and cross paths with some of her former NXT cohorts soon. After finishing even on Thursday, he was in last place but had no playing partner due to J.J. Spaun withdrawing from the tournament with an injury. So, Young was able to be the first on the greens and didn’t have to wait for a single person. He took full advantage of it. Young scored a 30 on the front nine, and even though he did bogey the 12th on the back nine, he still scored a 32 after his eagle on the 18th. CAM YOUNG WITH A BOMB ON 18 FOR EAGLE, A 62, AND A SHARE OF THE LEAD pic.twitter.com/ZCWFSKZm0K — Fore Play (@ForePlayPod) August 28, 2026 Young kept the tradition alive by shaking an imaginary player’s hand. What an outstanding day for the American. About 15 minutes after Young’s round ended, Min Woo Lee, who was in a share of first alongside Young and Akshay Bhatia, had a disastrous 5th hole, scoring a triple bogey and seeing his score drop to -5. Now, he just needs to hope that only a few others surpass -8, and he will be in championship territory heading into the weekend. Playing by yourself is clearly an advantage. Not only did he play alone, but no pairing was in front of him. The American essentially played a practice round on his own with no pressure at all. Once he got closer to the 18th hole, the spectators started to show up. There is still a great chance that Young wins this event after an incredible 2026 season. Let’s see if he can snatch it from his pal Scottie Scheffler. Rory McIlroy is having quite the opposite tournament as Young. articles.title: Show HN: Boop – tiny, self-hosted push notifications for your apps built in Go
articles.summary:
Hi HN, I built Boop because I wanted application events sent directly to my phone without paying for another service or routing everything through Slack or Telegram.

Boop is a small, open-source server paired with an open-source iOS app. The server currently uses around 8 MB of memory on my mac
articles._body: Hi HN, I built Boop because I wanted application events sent directly to my phone without paying for another service or routing everything through Slack or Telegram. Boop is a small, open-source server paired with an open-source iOS app. The server currently uses around 8 MB of memory on my machine. It’s deliberately not an observability platform or a replacement for Sentry. It receives events from your applications, sends native push notifications, and keeps them in a purpose-built mobile inbox. I use Elixir, so I built an integration for ErrorTracker. ErrorTracker still captures and stores the errors; the plugin sends them to Boop so I can see them on my phone: https://github.com/chrisgreg/boop_error_tracker There’s also a general Elixir client: https://github.com/chrisgreg/boop_ex And a Node client: https://github.com/chrisgreg/boop-node The iOS app can be built and installed locally. I’ve included instructions for configuring private push notifications for your own device, so you don’t need to release anything through the App Store. Although errors were my original use case, Boop can receive any event worth knowing about: failed jobs, deployments, signups, payments, low disk space, or anything else your application can send. Built in Go because I wanted to save memory on my self-hosted machine so Go and Svelte felt like a good combo. Everything is free and open source. It’s early, so I’d especially appreciate feedback on the architecture, setup process, and which integrations would make it useful to others. articles.title: Miu Miu's Quirky, Spiky Leather Mule Is a Piece of Weird '90s Nostalgia
articles.summary: The Miu Miu Leather Mules in Caffè Brown subvert expectations by merging backless slide convenience with archival sole units.
articles._body: While Miu Miu has dominated the global footwear zeitgeist through viral, ultra-thin New Balance sneaker collaborations and distressed leather runners, Miuccia Prada’s label is shifting gears into weirdly captivating hybrid territory. The Miu Miu Leather Mules in Caffè Brown subvert expectations by merging backless slide convenience with archival sole units. There is no denying this is an intentionally weird-looking shoe and that is precisely why it works. Despite its surreal, mutated proportions, the fashion industry's appetite for mules remains rampant. By slicing the heel off a traditional upper and mounting it onto an aggressively textured, bubble-patterned rubber sole, Miu Miu channels the ugly-chic ethos that is so prevalent in footwear design these days. A rich, coffee-brown leather upper brings an air of traditional Italian craftsmanship, while the bulbous sole keeps the silhouette firmly grounded in the experimental. The upper is constructed from supple Caffè brown leather finished with a clean, rounded toe box and a subtle debossed Miu Miu logo across the vamp. The open-back mule layout is emphasized by a smooth leather insole for understated luxury against the foot. Beyond the luxe leather finish, the star of this show is the sole unit, though. The shoe trades standard flat mule soles for an unmatching textured rubber outsole that’s straight from the mid-90s. articles._body: After Atlanta Braves star pitcher Chris Sale recorded a complete-game shutout against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Thursday night, with the team winning 1-0, it’s led to the baseball world buzzing. With Sale’s shutout for the Braves against the Dodgers , this former player would speak on how he should be looked at when it comes to the NL Cy Young Award race. Speaking on “Foul Territory,” former player Erik Kratz would endlessly praise Sale for his outing against Los Angeles, striking out 11 batters and only allowing five hits. The 37-year-old has recorded a 2.06 ERA with 177 strikeouts and a 13-9 record in 24 starts, and while Kratz believes that could’ve been a Cy Young Award season in any other season , he mentions how the winner will clearly be Milwaukee Brewers star Jacob Misiorowsk. “Because you know you have a great bullpen, you know it’s a great lineup that you’re facing. I just, man, more in the tank,” Kratz said about Sale. “I don’t see how this guy doesn’t end up top three Cy Young this year. If it wasn’t for Misiorowski, what he’s doing in this type of performance in late August could have pushed him to win a Cy Young. The Miz is gonna win it, but let’s be honest. But man, Chris Sale to be doing this at this point in his career, Hall of Famer.” Chris Sale SHINED against the Dodgers last night. "I just don't see how he doesn't end up a top-three Cy Young Award candidate this year," says @ErikKratz31 . pic.twitter.com/vuS6xIX31e — Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) August 28, 2026 A look at Jacob Misiorowski’s season compared to Braves’ Chris Sale Looking at Misiorowski, he’s having a sensational eason, recording a 1.73 ERA with 222 strikeouts and a 14- 5 record in 25 starts. Not to mention the outstanding velocity he’s reaching, with pitches thrown at 103 and 104 miles per hour, and while Sale’s season has been spectacular and even him throwing 100 miles per hour on Thursday was impressive, Misiorowski’s year is unlike any other. Still, Sale’s performance this season shouldn’t be undermined, as he looks to help Atlanta in their World Series aspirations, as the Braves have a 79-55 record, putting them first in the NL East. articles.summary: Luke Fickell’s first three seasons as head coach of the Wisconsin Badgers are like watching a pumpkin roll down a big hill. After a 7-6 winning season in his first year, the program has completely deteriorated, going 5-7 the following campaign, then finishing last year with a 4-8 record. Wh
articles._body: Luke Fickell’s first three seasons as head coach of the Wisconsin Badgers are like watching a pumpkin roll down a big hill. After a 7-6 winning season in his first year, the program has completely deteriorated, going 5-7 the following campaign, then finishing last year with a 4-8 record. While his job security appears to be bleak, Bruce Feldman of The Athletic shared a silver lining regarding Fickell’s situation. Feldman believes that the 53-year-old head coach has at least the tools necessary to completely turn things around for Wisconsin. In his latest column for The Athletic, the popular college football insider pointed out how the Badgers finished last season. He likes the two wins over ranked opponents, as it shows the team never gave up on Luke Fickell. Additionally, the team added some exciting young talent for Fickell to work with. “Even though the record has gotten worse each year, it feels like [Fickell] might finally be on the right track,” Feldman wrote. “That’s because the Badgers finished 2025 with two wins in November against ranked teams, beating No. 23 Washington and whipping No. 21 Illinois. It’s also noteworthy because they ended October with back-to-back games against Ohio State and Oregon and never quit on Fickell or each other. “There is plenty of excellent young talent, especially on defense, led by budding stars Mason Posa and Cooper Catalano, a pair of sophomore linebackers who shined in those wins,” Feldman continued. “The hope is that speedy Old Dominion transfer QB Colton Joseph, the 2025 Sun Belt Offensive Player of the Year, can spark what has been a horrid offense.” While the Badgers still have a tough schedule this year (opens Week 1 on the road against Notre Dame), Wisconsin seems to be finally leaning into the new era of college football. It was only just recently that the program got more involved with NIL than ever before. That subtle change could help Luke Fickell acquire the players he needs in recruiting and the transfer portal, assuming he maintains his job after this season. There’s a real care for craft here and an understanding of the subtle magic that can transform a piece of work. Music has always been a part of Apple’s DNA, and I’m incredibly excited to join this team and help shape what music can bring to the work globally.” Across her career, Ahn Do has worked across music, brand and film. She had served as music supervisor on The Stroll on HBO. “Music is woven extraordinarily deep into fabric of the work we do for Apple,” Anderson said in a statement. “And we have the most talented music team in the world spread across our MAL offices. Ahn brings the precise sensibility, experience and hunger needed to lead that incredible team and together climb to dizzying heights. I couldn’t be more excited to have her here to lead our team globally.”  — Ariel King See more executive hires and promotions in this week’s column below.
