Kuminga’s former team, the Golden State Warriors, were not in the running for the free agent forward, but when his reason for signing with the Timberwolves be
articles._body: One of the last remaining dominoes in NBA free agency fell this week when Jonathan Kuminga agreed to sign with the Minnesota Timberwolves . Kuminga’s former team, the Golden State Warriors, were not in the running for the free agent forward, but when his reason for signing with the Timberwolves became public via his agent, Warriors fans had quite the reaction to the news. Jonathan Kuminga’s main reason for choosing the Timberwolves via free agency was because he wanted to be a part of a versatile defensive team while not caring about his offensive numbers, as per Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic. “He made this decision because of the defensive versatility of this team,” Kuminga’s agent Aaron Turner said via Krawczynski. “Offense is secondary to what he’s thinking about. It’s going to be whatever we gotta do to win that night. Nobody is going to care about stats or shots.” Predictably, Warriors fans flocked in droves to social media to convey their disbelief. Many of them were of the mind that Kuminga could’ve have been a $100 million-plus contract player with the team had he bought in to those same principles that Warriors coach Steve Kerr had preached. He would have gotten 200m from the Warriors if he showed that. Disappointing for everyone involved. https://t.co/cMTJtXVYwO — MIKE GRIER stan account (@AndyKHLiu) August 28, 2026 The quotes in here are insane. Turner is speaking in Kerr-isms. It’s like an article of the Twilight Zone. https://t.co/8D7kGu5FW2 — Brian Witt (@Wittnessed) August 28, 2026 Taking a paycut to have to become the player Steve Kerr advised you to become anyway is an interesting choice for sure https://t.co/zHTYlbHHdl — Dialpad Propagandist (@AGuyNamedNam) August 28, 2026 I love reading the “nobody is gonna care about shots or stats” line in August https://t.co/wZYNqqpx1d pic.twitter.com/YISoi6UlLI — Ⓒⓗⓡⓘⓢ Ⓛⓞⓤⓟⓞⓢ (@ChrisLoupos) August 28, 2026 Obviously the onus is on Kuminga to prove that he really is about what he and his agent are saying, and buying into that will go a long way towards the Timberwolves potentially being a contending team in the Western Conference next season. The former lottery pick is coming off a season in which he was traded from the Warriors to the Atlanta Hawks at the deadline. He appeared in a total of 36 games between both teams, including 14 starts, while averaging 12.2 points, 5.6 rebounds and 2.3 assists while shooting 46.3 percent from the field, 33.3 percent from the 3-point line and 72.4 percent from the free-throw line. articles.title: Beyond ‘Kawaii’: How ASOBISYSTEM Is Building a Global Future for Japanese Idol Culture
articles.summary: Billboard JAPAN talked to ASOBISYSTEM CEO Yusuke Nakagawa about the chances of globalizing Japan’s “oshikatsu” culture.
articles._body: With their performance on a Korean music TV show, CUTIE STREET’s “Can’t we just be cute? -Kawaii Dakejya Damedesuka?-” has crossed international borders. Seeing this response, KAWAII LAB. has decided to hold global auditions in five Asian countries. ASOBISYSTEM, the company behind KAWAII LAB. and its artists, like CUTIE STREET, Kyary Pamyu Pamyu, ATARASHII GAKKO!, and FRUITS ZIPPER, will be celebrating its 20th anniversary next year. Billboard JAPAN talked to its CEO, Yusuke Nakagawa, about the chances of globalizing Japan’s “oshikatsu” culture, his management style of avoiding setting goals, and what it takes to ensure long term success for artists.  In March 2026, CUTIE STREET appeared on a Korean music TV show and performed a Korean version of their song “Can’t we just be cute? -Kawaii Dakejya Damedesuka?-.” This created a lot of buzz, and the group’s Korean shows sold out immediately, leading them to come back to put on additional shows in July. What are your thoughts on their becoming a hit in Korea?   KAWAII LAB. has been using social media to engage with Korean listeners across the language barrier, such as by posting K-pop dance videos or having a Korean group do FRUITS ZIPPER’s “Watashi no Ichiban Kawaiitokoro” dance. I think CUTIE STREET’s success was the result of this kind of diligent, ongoing effort.  Even so, it was amazing how it spread like wildfire after their TV appearance. The way it was filmed was also surprising. There were a ton of cameras, even cameras for YouTube. That’s why the video got released right after the show was broadcast. They only appeared on a single Korean TV show, but their performance spread around the world through YouTube. It was really something to see.  They’ve released a music video for the Korean version of the song, too. How do you balance keeping a Japanese feel in videos while also localizing them for other countries, like Korea?   It depends on what triggers it. With CUTIE STREET, I was a little unsure about whether to go with the approach we ultimately did or to make a music video that was more evocative of K-pop. But after they appeared on M COUNTDOWN and became a hit, I thought about the reasons for their success and it seemed to me that it would be better to keep a Japanese feel. So we updated the video, keeping the feeling of a Japanese music video and creating a new, improved version of “Can’t we just be cute? -Kawaii Dakejya Damedesuka?-.” We paid a lot of attention to the translation, as well, and we’ve gotten a lot of feedback saying that we really understand Korea.  What countries are you planning to expand into in the future?   KAWAII LAB. is holding KAWAII LAB. ASIA GLOBAL AUDITION 2026, a global audition for people in Korea, China, Thailand, Indonesia, and Vietnam.  So you’re trying to create a group of idols from various different countries?   We haven’t decided on anything specific yet. We might create local groups, we might create one group for all of Asia, we might include Japanese members in the group. There are a lot of options available to us. As a general rule, I don’t really like picking specific goals. When people pick a goal, they try to squeeze whatever they do into the mold of that goal. The same is true for business. If you set a goal at the start, it cuts off future possibilities. I think the right approach is to keep thinking about it as you go along and make updates as needed.  With that approach, don’t you run the risk of losing your direction?   I actually think staying flexible about your direction is a strength. More important than the discipline to stay on track, I think, is the willingness to change course when conditions call for it. If you don’t do that, you’ll never be able to keep up with the times. So when I launch a new project, I’ll decide on a basic concept, but I’ll leave a lot of room for maneuvering, so I can change course as we go. The March 26 performance of “Can’t we just be cute -Kawaii Dakejya Damedesuka-“ on Korean TV generated a lot of buzz, so we released a Korean version on April 10. That kind of speediness is essential today. It’s really hard on the employees, though (laughs).   But on the creative front, I have the utmost respect for the opinions of staff and artists. I think the strength of your convictions is important when you’re making creative content, so while I will chime in with some of my opinions, I never go completely against what the creators are saying.  I saw an interview with you elsewhere in which you talked about globalizing “oshikatsu” (Japan’s unique superfan culture) to spread Japanese music around the world. What potential do you see in “oshikatsu?”   “Oshikatsu” is unique to Japan, but overseas there are also dynamic pricing and meet-and-greet ticket sales. I think that overseas there’s a culture similar to “oshikatsu,” it’s just individualized for artists.  I don’t think overseas music listeners will, as a whole, engage in Japanese-style “oshikatsu,” but I feel like the people who become fans of KAWAII LAB. are the kinds of fans who could engage in “oshikatsu.” Around the world, there are people who like Japanese global niche content, so I don’t think a market-driven approach would be possible without thinking about how to get those core fans.  Next year, ASOBISYSTEM will be celebrating its 20th anniversary. How do you think the definition of “cute” has changed over those 20 years?   There’s been a lot of change, but there have been even more aspects that haven’t changed. In managing artists, I always place a lot of value on artists themselves having fun and enjoying their work. I think that feeling of “I love being on stage” or “I’m so happy our song is a hit” is more important than anything else. That’s why I always strive to honor the creativity of artists.  Honestly, I never expected for us to be around as long as we have. I mean,

articles.title: Jermaine Dupri Drops Lawsuit Claiming $18M in Unpaid Royalties on Mariah Carey & Usher Albums
articles.summary: Less than two months after he filed it, the hitmaking producer and exec has dropped a case that claimed Sony Music owed him millions.
articles._body: Jermaine Dupri has quickly dropped a lawsuit against Sony Music that claimed he was owed $18 million in unpaid royalties tied to albums from Mariah Carey , Usher and others. The legendary hip-hop producer and his So-So Def Recordings sued Sony Music in July, accusing the label of a “systemic pattern” of using “contemptuous accounting practices” to underpay royalties for many years. Related Jermaine Dupri Sues Sony Music for $18M in Unpaid Royalties on Mariah Carey & Usher Albums Dale Morris, Nashville Manager Who Guided Careers of Alabama & Kenny Chesney, Dies at 89 HYBE Pledges Over $300k for Colombia Earthquake Recovery But less than two months later, attorneys for Dupri moved Friday (Aug. 28) to voluntarily dismiss the case, telling the judge that they had “resolved the matter.” The move did not come with a written explanation, and an attorney for Dupri did not return a request for comment. A spokesperson for Sony declined to comment. Dupri, who wrote and produced Kris Kross’s 1992 all-timer “Jump,” had a long career as a hit-making producer, helping Carey, Usher, Nelly and others create chart-topping tracks. He also released a pair of studio albums himself, featuring high-profile collab tracks with Jay-Z and Ludacris . The son of former Columbia Records executive Michael Mauldin , Dupri founded So-So Def in 1993 as a joint venture with Columbia and Sony, where he later signed Xscape , Bow Wow , Da Brat and others. That partnership ended in 2002 and, after several more years at Sony imprints, So-So Def hopped from EMI to UMG to several other distributors. In his July lawsuit, Dupri claimed that over a “32-year contractual and business relationship” Sony had repeatedly failed to pay proper royalties to him and his company:  “As it turns out, many of SME’s dealings with So-So Def have not been lawful and have harmed So-So Def in its business.” Dupri claimed he was owed more than $2 million for Kris Kross’s first two albums, including their smash, Totally Krossed Out , which featured “Jump.” He also accused Sony of using bookkeeping trickery to maintain unrecouped advances on other music. Friday’s dismissal will end all those accusations without any real litigation. But it came with a catch: Dupri’s lawyers moved to drop the case “without prejudice,” meaning they could theoretically refile it at some point in the future.

articles.title: Madeon’s First Official Remix Since 2012 Is a Shimmering Take on Ninajirachi’s ‘iPod Touch’
articles.summary: The French producer's edit infuses her 2025 hit with his take on early 2010s dance nostalgia.
articles._body: In news that makes absolutely perfect sense, Ninajirachi and Madeon have linked for a new remix of Ninajirachi’s 2025 hit “iPod Touch.” Related ‘I Wanted to Feel Courageous, Even If It Meant Risking Everything Going Down In Flames’: Madeon on His First New Album In 7 Years Porter Robinson & Ninajirachi on Their Debut Collab: ‘I’m Getting Messages From People I Didn’t Even Think Would Like It’ Yasuhisa Hara's 'Kingdom' Vol. 80 Tops Billboard Japan Book Hot 100 Out Friday (Aug. 28), the Madeon edit brings airy spaciousness to the original, before the French producer takes the song to the bubblegum stratosphere with a shimmering, soaring and early 2010s-style build/release that’s signature Madeon and total bliss. Listen to the remix below. In a post announcing the project, the pair shared a screenshot of a text exchange, with Madeon saying that “I took some sounds from my early FL projects to honor the era you’re talking about,” with Ninajirachi’s lyrics referencing downloading the DAW FL Studio. Madeon continued that he also “added a verse with my own memories” and noted that this is his first official remix since 2012, a sentiment to which Ninajirachi responded “Omg im freaking out this is so amazing.” The post also includes vintage photos of each artist as musically inclined children. Ninajirachi also recently worked with Madeon’s friend and collaborator Porter Robinson on the July single “WannaCry.” Meanwhile, Madeon released his first studio album in seven years , Victory , in late June. Of the project he told Billboard , “There was something a little rebellious about it, and that was appealing. I often say the number one sin of an artist is to be boring and to give people what they think they want, and I think you can recede into the background of people’s consciousness if you just pander. Because of the length of my career, I felt like I had earned the right to be risky, and I wanted to feel courageous, even if it meant risking everything going down in flames. That was appealing to me.”

articles.title: New York City sends 11,000 more pied-à-terre tax letters as it apologizes to the 1,200 wrongly targeted because it didn’t check 2025 tax returns
articles.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani admitted the city lacked 2025 tax data before sending 17,000 warning letters.
articles._body: New York City’s Department of Finance is sending a second wave of pied-à-terre tax letters to roughly 10,800 property owners, even as it mails a very different kind of letter to other owners from the first round, telling them, in effect, never mind. Roughly 17,000 owners received a notice this summer warning they might owe the surcharge, which applies only to non-primary residences amounts, with a rate of 0.8%–1.3% on homes over $5 million and 4%-6.5% on condos and co-ops over $1 million. But 1,210 are now being cleared outright, according to new court filings disclosed this week. The reason has nothing to do with a change in the law and everything to do with timing: New York State sent the city’s DOF preliminary 2025 income-tax records on Aug. 12, several months earlier than the agency would normally begin receiving them. Of that group, 630 owners were cleared because their 2025 tax returns listed the property as their primary home address; another 580 were cleared using a mix of 2025 extension filings and 2024 returns. “So by my last count, I think we sent out less than 20,000, ‘you may be subject to’ letters, I think it was about 17,000 or 18,000. And at the time that we sent those out, we did not have access to the 2025 income tax filings,” said Mayor Zohran Mamdani at a Wednesday press conference . He noted the timing wasn’t unusual on the state’s end: 2025 filings are “typically released in February of the next calendar year,” and the state simply gave DOF early access this time. Randy Mastro, the attorney suing the city over the rollout (and a longtime suer of the city in general), made his thoughts known in the court filing. “There are many thousands fewer property owners subject to this surcharge than this administration originally boasted when it flooded the landscape with 17,000 threatening Mailed Notices.” “The City has now effectively admitted” that some people who received the letters, Mastro said, “do not actually owe this surcharge.” He also argued the timing undercuts the city’s excuse: “The City admits that, after this lawsuit was filed on August 7, it obtained 2025 tax information within five days,” which is evidence, he claimed, that DOF could have gotten the same data before mailing anything, not just after being sued. Mamdani laid out three categories of properties the city is targeting. One is properties owned by a corporate entity like an LLC or a trust, about 6,400 households, where DOF doesn’t have enough information on primary residence holder. The 1,210 owners who were being cleared make up the second category. The third category, about 4,400 households, consists of properties where DOF doesn’t have 2025 tax returns that would indicate whether they are primary residences. The first and third categories make up the 10,800 letters going out to people. A rocky rollout New York Gov. Kathy Hochul, who stood alongside Mamdani when the tax was first announced in April, said this week she “wasn’t a fan of the rollout” and that City Hall was working to correct the problems. Mamdani, at the same press conference, held firm on the tax’s revenue target: “We continue to be confident in that assessment of what the annual revenue will look like.” Ryan Lavis, a DOF spokesperson, said: “From the beginning, we have been committed to ensuring that New Yorkers have the time and information they need. Property owners have until October 6th to file an exemption application. We have received the tax information from the state for 2025 and want to give New Yorkers more time to apply for an exemption, if applicable. Mamdani noted Oct. 6 isn’t necessarily the final word for owners who miss it. “If New Yorkers still want to appeal an assessment, they can still appeal to the tax commission until early next year.” New York City’s pied-à-terre tax initially began as a Tax Day pitch. Mamdani and Hochul announced it in April, with Mamdani unveiling the plan in a video filmed outside Citadel billionaire Ken Griffin’s $238 million penthouse . The state legislature passed it May 27, and Hochul signed it the next day. The rollout is what actually caused the uproar. DOF’s supplemental roll, meant to flag properties that might owe the surcharge, ballooned into an unfiltered list of nearly a million properties , instantly branded a “rich hit list” online, and united the ultrawealthy and merely well-off alike in opposition once thousands of legitimate primary residences got needlessly swept into DOF’s notices. That confusion is now the subject of Mastro’s active lawsuit. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

One player who maintained a fifth year of el
articles._body: The college basketball landscape is currently in a state of disarray as various court rulings and updated conference policies have created an inconsistent standard when it comes to college basketball eligibility across the nation for the class of 2022. One player who maintained a fifth year of eligibility amid the craziness is big man Micah Handlogten who recently committed to Ole Miss via the transfer portal, as per Joe Tipton of On3. Micah Handlogten had initially entered the transfer portal at the end of last season, and thus, his pathway to eligibility for Ole Miss this upcoming season might a little more smooth. The SEC is one of the athletic conferences looking to potentially bar fifth-year transfers from competing this season. The son of former NBA player Ben, Handlogten recently played in NBA Summer League for the Utah Jazz. He did not sign an Exhibit 10 contract which is another thing potentially working in his favor when determining eligibility. He appeared in a total of three summer league games with the Jazz, one in Salt Lake City and two in Las Vegas. He averaged 3.3 points and 5.7 rebounds with splits of 100 percent shooting from the field and 33.3 percent shooting from the free-throw line in a little over five minutes per game. Handlogten began his college basketball career at Marshall, playing one season for the Thundering Herd before transferring to Florida where he played for three seasons. He was a part of the Gators’ 2025 national championship team. Prior to committing to Ole Miss, he was coming off a solid year for the Gators, appearing in 34 games, including two starts, at a little over 14 minutes per game. He averaged 4.1 points and 5.9 rebounds while shooting 63.7 percent from the field. He holds a college career average of 64.6 percent shooting from the field. articles.title: Capital B Raises €21M From Adam Back and TOBAM To Buy More BTC
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Capital B Raises €21M From Adam Back and TOBAM To Buy More BTC Capital B , the Euronext Growth-listed company that bills itself as Europe’s first bitcoin treasury company, has raised €21 million ($24 million) in a private placement backed by Blockstream’s Adam Back and asset manager TOBAM — money it says could buy 270 more bitcoin and push its stack to roughly 3,415 BTC. The company said Friday that a total of 36,219,070 shares were sold at €0.58 each as part of the deal, a 6.45% discount to Wednesday’s closing price. Capital B said the net proceeds are expected to reach about €19.9 million after fees and transaction costs. JUST IN: French company Capital B announces a €21.0 million capital raise to "accelerate its Bitcoin Treasury Company strategy" pic.twitter.com/I3RcJYlSsI — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) August 28, 2026 Capital B is the 27th biggest publicly traded bitcoin treasury in the world, according to Bitcoin Treasuries, with a total of 3,145 bitcoins in its stash — worth $245 million at today’s bitcoin price of $77,960.  Capital B, which describes itself as Europe’s first bitcoin treasury, built much of that position through fundraising rounds during the first half of 2026.  In May, it acquired 192 coins for €13 million after completing three capital raises. Capital B’s announcement as other treasuries look to raise funds and accelerate their buys. Just this week, NYSE-listed AI-powered education company Genius Group said it was aiming to build parallel AI and bitcoin treasuries worth a combined $1.6 billion, after the company sold its entire bitcoin reserves to repay $8.5 million in debt.  Bitcoin treasuries have faced headwinds since 2025 when the price of the leading cryptocurrency took a hit. A number of companies in the space have had to liquidate their holdings, including the biggest corporate holder of bitcoin, Nasdaq-listed Strategy. This post Capital B Raises €21M From Adam Back and TOBAM To Buy More BTC first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo .

articles.title: Cowboys player on roster bubble with most at stake in 2026 NFL preseason finale
articles.summary: While the Dallas Cowboys can bask in the glow of having one of the league’s best wide receivers, they still face a tough roster decision. One of those receivers is a Cowboys player on the roster bubble with the most at stake in the 2026 NFL preseason finale. Things are certainly on the upswing fo
articles._body: While the Dallas Cowboys can bask in the glow of having one of the league’s best wide receivers, they still face a tough roster decision . One of those receivers is a Cowboys player on the roster bubble with the most at stake in the 2026 NFL preseason finale. Things are certainly on the upswing for Jonathan Mingo. And Camden Brown has looked pro-ready during training camp and preseason games. CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Ryan Flournoy, and KaVontae Turpin are locks at the receiver position. And if the Cowboys stick with only five receivers, that means either Mingo or Brown won’t be around after cutdown day. Cowboys WR Camden Brown needs one more good game Maybe the Cowboys go with six receivers, and this becomes a moot point. Mingo and Brown would both be in. Lock it. However, Brown can’t rest on that. And he hasn’t been resting on it this summer, according to dallascowboys.com. “Just doing what I gotta do,” he said. “Shoot, I just feel like I’m making the best of the opportunity whenever it comes my way. I’m blessed to even say I’m in his locker room with a bunch of vets that’s done it big.” Brown came to the Cowboys via the undrafted free agent route. That doesn’t help his cause, but the visuals in practice certainly do. “I feel like practice was really good, and that’s just where it started,” Brown said. “I start it from practice, and that’s the preparation piece of it. So when I come out here, it slows down for me. “I feel like just stacking a week on top of a week, that’s how I can make this team and keep doing what I got to do. So really, that’s really what it is, for real.” Brown has the size to succeed. He’s 6-foot-2 and 204 pounds. And he also has been able to overcome adversity. His sister died at the age of 17 because of kidney failure, according to dallascowboys.com. He said he’s trying to make his NFL dream a reality to honor her. “I know who I’m doing it for,” Brown said. “So, at the end of the day, it ain’t too big. I won’t make it bigger than what it is.” How does WR Jonathan Mingo figure into things? Mingo has enjoyed a good summer. He hasn’t done anything to hurt his chances. And he said he knows what is at stake against the Saints in the preseason finale, according to dallascowboys.com. “I know what I can do,” Mingo said. “It’s about time to finally come out there on the stage with everybody watching, so I’m going to try and do it again, show everybody what I’m about.” Mingo wants to get out of the shadow of limited success with the Cowboys. In 14 games, he only has six receptions for 71 yards. “I’m trying to play,” Mingo said. “I’m used to playing. I was starting when I first got in the league. Playing different roles can be a little frustrating. So I’m trying to get back on the field and making plays again, trying to get back to my old self. “I feel healthy. Went through a lot last year being hurt. Trying to get healthy this offseason. Got injured the first day of OTAs. I got my body back right, so I felt healthy coming into camp.” And head coach Brian Schottenheimer has been in his corner. “Could not be more proud of Jonathan,” Schottenheimer said. “Everybody, they figure it out at different stages of their career for different reasons. Being selected high like he was in Carolina and then being traded, that’s not easy. I mean, believe me, you’re talking to guys who have been fired a lot. “You kind of like start second-guessing yourself and whatnot. But he’s figured it out. And he’s not just done it on offense. He’s done it in another phase. Which is really important to us. And that’s special teams, whether it’s a gunner, whether it’s a returner. He’s figured out what creates value on a football team. And that’s versatility.” The Cowboys might keep both guys. But neither can feel overconfident with the carrot still dangling in front of them. "I expect Justin Herbert to be a MVP caliber performer this year." @DonteWhitner shares his expectations for Justin Herbert for this year pic.twitter.com/5BMRn01rjK — First Take (@FirstTake) August 28, 2026 “He’s going to get the easier throws of his career,” Donte Whitner said on First Take Friday. “It’s all based on motions, shifts, and deception. He doesn’t have to drop back 30 times a game and have defenders all over him and forcing him into coverage.” “I expect Justin Herbert to be an MVP-caliber performer this year. And if they start off hot, they are going to get the toughness from Jim Harbaugh. If Herbert is trusting his philosophy, they can get all the way to the big one and can win it.” Herbert has never lacked arm talent. The question has been whether Los Angeles could surround him with the coaching, healthy protection, and consistency needed to translate his individual ability into postseason success. Mike McDaniel is expected to unlock it. If the new-look offense creates more manageable throws without limiting Herbert’s aggressiveness, this could finally be the season when everything comes together. An MVP award would require an exceptional year. Based on Whitner’s prediction, Herbert may finally have the system necessary to produce one. On Thursday night in the preseason finale against the Los Angeles Rams, Herbert sent a 65-yard pass into orbit for a touchdown to Quentin Johnston early in the first quarter. articles.title: Rajah Caruth threatens to crash JGR Chase party in NASCAR regular-season finale
articles.summary: Rajah Caruth enters Daytona just 15 points from the Chase cutline, threatening three JGR teammates fighting for their postseason lives.
articles._body: All eyes are on the cutline for tonight’s NASCAR O’Reilly Auto Sports Series race at Daytona.  A dramatic storyline has emerged over the last few races with all eyes on a trio of Joe Gibbs Racing teammates and Rajah Caruth of JR Motorsports.  The Chase for O’Reilly, unlike the Cup Series’ 16-team field, is a 12-team field.  Tonight’s Winn-Dixie 250 is the regular season finale.  A hornets nest at the cutline Brent Crews and William Sawalich sit at 11th and 12th, tied with the same amount of points. In 13th is Taylor Gray. In 14th is Rajah Caruth. The difference between 14th and 11th is just 15 points . It’s a hornets nest there, and there’s some wild dynamics at play.  Caruth is 15 points away from 11th and 12th, a tie between Crews and Sawalich.  Taylor Gray is one spot below the cutline in 13th, just 14 points ahead of Caruth.  Crews, Sawalich, and Gray are teammates.  And loyalty might go out the window when all three are at the cutline separated by just one point.  Daytona is going to be very interesting if Caruth gets stage points early to tighten the divide.  Caruth confident ahead of tonight’s race “It’s not an ideal spot to be in,” said Caruth. “You want to be in the top ten or top right probably to make a run at the championship, but for me, I’m excited for the opportunity today. “I entered Atlanta 48 points out, and I have knocked 33 points from that, and going to a track where I have a knack for superspeedway racing, things can happen outside of your control, but I’m definitely confident going into Daytona today. “I would put our odds as good as anybody’s.  On my end, I love superspeedway racing, the aggression that it requires, just how aware you have to be with everything. “And I have a great spotter and a great group of guys with me.  So, we’ll see what tonight brings, but definitely very confident.” The confidence for Caruth came in iRacing on superspeedways Asked by Larry McReynolds and Alan Cavanna where his confidence from on tracks like Daytona, Caruth pointed to his roots and how he arrived in NASCAR. “Honestly, just sim racing,” said Caruth. “Obviously, iRacing is my foundation.  It’s how I got noticed to even start driving Legends cars.  “Obviously, I’m on the sim- if I’m at home five days a week, I’m probably on it 3-4 days. It came from there.  “Learning for over 10 years of me just racing online of what not to do, but also what puts you in the position to go and contend for wins. Racing online is super valuable. The best thing is, if a race goes bad, you’ll go and sign up for one in an hour or two.  “It really came from there, and there are things you can learn like situational awareness and managing your emotions.  There’s a lot of great things from sim racing and iRacing in particular.  “I just feel that speedway racing has directly benefitted from my online racing.”

articles._body: With the North Carolina football team in Ireland to take on TCU to open the season on Saturday, it starts what could be a pivotal season for head coach Bill Belichick and his job security. As many speculate that Belichick on the hot seat with the North Carolina football team , this college football insider explains why he also feels the same. In Bruce Feldman’s latest piece for The Athletic, he goes over how hot the seat is for various coaches around the country, saying that Belichick’s level is “muy caliente.” Feldman went into Belichick’s “horrible first season” with the Tar Heels after being hired by the school at $10 million a year, finishing 4-8 last year. Considering the program a “laughingstock” of college football, Feldman would go over the “dysfunction” going on, like with general manager Michael Lombardi being investigated over a human resources complaint. Feldman described his roster management with the school as being “botched.” “The GM boasted about how UNC was now the NFL’s 33rd team, yet the Tar Heels were unable to produce even one NFL Draft pick last year for the first time in a decade,” Feldman wrote. “Belichick fired his offensive coordinator and special teams coordinator after his first season but kept Lombardi, who is currently on paid leave while he is being investigated by the university regarding an HR complaint. Belichick’s son, Steve, the defensive coordinator, is on leave for medical reasons.” Bill Belichick on the hot seat for the North Carolina football team Feldman would continue talking about Belichick’s time with the North Carolina football program, saying that when he asked a source about his coaching future, the response wasn’t one certain he’d be there next season. “I’d be shocked if he’s coaching there next year. It’s a mess there…” the source said, via Feldman. Feldman would say that a 2-2 start to the season “should spark some optimism,” which hasn’t been felt within the school. It remains to be seen what happens when it comes to Belichick and the future of the North Carolina football program, as the season starts Saturday against TCU in Ireland. articles.title: It’s now or never for USC’s Lincoln Riley after ‘steamy’ hot seat rating
articles.summary: The last two seasons have been mediocre, to say the least, for Lincoln Riley and the USC Trojans. With the program going 9-9 against Big Ten opponents over the past two years, the offensive guru finds himself on Bruce Feldman’s hot seat list. Riley, who is 42 years old, is going into his fi
articles._body: The last two seasons have been mediocre, to say the least, for Lincoln Riley and the USC Trojans . With the program going 9-9 against Big Ten opponents over the past two years, the offensive guru finds himself on Bruce Feldman’s hot seat list. Riley, who is 42 years old, is going into his fifth season as head coach of the Trojans. With a new athletic director running the show for USC’s sports programs, The Athletics’ college football insider believes now is the time for Riley to right the ship in Southern California . Even if his contract buyout is substantial. “It’s Year 5,” Feldman wrote. “[Lincoln Riley’s] been paid a fortune, even by college coaching standards. His AD, Jen Cohen, did not hire him. His buyout is still massive, probably north of what LSU had to navigate to ditch [Brian] Kelly.” Feldman points out several positives for Riley going into the 2026-27 campaign. USC has the No. 1-ranked recruiting class for 2026, Jayden Maiava is serving as the starting quarterback once again, and Lincoln Riley hired a Hall of Fame coach in Gary Patterson to lead the defense. Additionally, the program has a rather favorable schedule to begin the campaign, but there are six notable Big Ten matchups that Feldman believes Riley must get the better end of. “The Trojans’ schedule starts fairly easy, opening with four opponents not anywhere near the preseason Top 25,” Feldman wrote. “But in late September things get interesting: No. 2 Oregon visits, then No. 17 Washington. A week later, the Trojans make the long trip to Happy Valley to face No. 18 Penn State in the Nittany Lions’ prime-time White Out game. “After visiting Wisconsin, they host No. 1 Ohio State before traveling to defending national champion Indiana after a bye week,” Feldman continued. “Going 9-3 against this schedule would actually feel impressive. Going 8-4, though, might cost him his job. Temperature check: Steamy .” USC’s offense has been solid throughout Lincoln Riley’s tenure, as he is arguably the best playcaller in college football. The defense has been a concern, but if n ew defensive coordinator Gary Patterson can turn things around, perhaps Riley can get himself off the hot seat this year. articles._body: On Wednesday, the Ole Miss staff extended an offer to 2029 four-star Braylen Alexander . Alabama and Florida State are the two other Power 4 programs who have extended offers. The 6-foot-4, 180 pound prospect is sure to add plenty more, too. Alexander is ranked as the 26th overall recruit in the 2029 cycle. He is also ranked as the No. 1 player in Alabama and the 7th-ranked shooting guard. Braylen Alexander has been scoring for a while now As an eighth grader, the sophomore prospect averaged 14.1 points, 3.5 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 1.1 steals per game. Last season, he jumped to 27.8 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.9 steals per game at Glenwood (Ala.) prior to transferring. Now he will get ready for his sophomore year where he will try to guide Central to a bounceback season. A year ago, the Devils finished just 12-12. When Alexander was on the team as a middle schooler, Central finished 29-5. It was also a perfect 7-0 in 7A Area 4 play. He will also have to navigate a growing recruitment. But he has his head in the right spot. “My mom always told me not to let like the hype get to my head because anytime the Lord can take it away from you,” Alexander said to WTVM’s Mackenzie Collins . “My name is, of course, getting out there, but it also means that any split second it can be taken away from me.” Ole Miss has gotten off to a nice start to 2029 class Chris Beard and his staff have already offered a ton of talent 4-star Academy of Central Florida (Fla.) SG RJ Evans (No. 2 overall) 4-star Prolific Prep (Fla.) SF Draydne McDaniel (No. 3 overall) 3-star Bella Vista College Preparatory School (Ariz.) PG Semaj Cuyler (No. 56 overall) 3-star Bartlett (Tenn.) PG Malachi Hill (No. 90 overall) Scouts rave about Alexander and think he can climb in the rankings. Coach Bruton from NGS Hoops is a huge fan . “He should become a coveted D1 recruit, despite being just a freshman. Excellent frame, good motor and aggressive. While Olivia Miles and Caitlin Clark both have compelling cases, the su
articles._body: The Las Vegas Aces (26-13) have struggled to keep pace with the Minnesota Lynx and Golden State Valkyries in the WNBA standings, but A’ja Wilson continues to cruise toward her third straight MVP Award and fifth overall. While Olivia Miles and Caitlin Clark both have compelling cases, the superstar forward is widely regarded as the heavy favorite. The only thing that can seemingly stop her is health. Wilson popped up on a stuffed injury report ahead of Friday’s home matchup versus the Toronto Tempo (11-27). The three-time champion and two-time Finals MVP has played in 36 of 39 Aces games this season, but with the FIBA Women’s World Cup and WNBA playoffs on the horizon, head coach Becky Hammon may want to monitor her juggernaut’s status and workload. The Tempo are already severely shorthanded , but if Wilson is inactive, then perhaps the expansion squad can make things interesting in Michelob ULTRA Arena. The two-way powerhouse led the reigning champs to a road victory over Toronto last Sunday, and fans are eager to see if she will have the chance to do the same tonight. Watch Aces vs. Tempo LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Latest injury updates for Aces-Tempo clash Wilson is listed questionable with a back issue , per the latest WNBA injury report. Frontcourt mate NaLyssa Smith suffered a brutal leg injury in Las Vegas’ 88-78 win in Toronto and will be sidelined for the remainder of the season, putting a bigger burden on No. 22 and the team’s other core players moving forward. Perhaps Dana Evans can lend a helping hand. The veteran guard is considered questionable after missing the previous six games with a leg injury of her own. The Tempo can certainly relate to the Aces’ recent run of bad luck. Toronto is shutting down both Brittney Sykes (foot) and Aneesah Morrow (knee) for the rest of the 2026 campaign, and leading scorer Marina Mabrey will be reevaluated in a few weeks after sustaining an abductor injury. Isabelle Harrison is questionable (foot). Obviously, head coach Sandy Brondello has a challenging final stretch ahead of her. With or without A’ja Wilson, Vegas should have enough to protect its house. The free-falling Tempo have nothing to lose, however, and could come out scrapping in this David versus Goliath battle. Final status updates are still to come. The post Is A’ja Wilson playing tonight? Aces vs. Tempo injury report appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Fired Stars and Stripes staffers sue Pentagon, claiming retaliation over reporting on deteriorating aircraft carrier
articles.summary: Stars and Stripes publisher Max Lederer, editor-in-chief Erik Slavin and Middle East reporter Lara Korte are named as plaintiffs in the federal lawsuit.
articles._body: Three staff members from the Stars and Stripes military news outlet are suing to challenge their  recent firings  by the Pentagon, accusing the Trump administration of violating their First Amendment free speech rights to speak out against government interference in their work. Stars and Stripes publisher Max Lederer, editor-in-chief Erik Slavin and Middle East reporter Lara Korte are named as plaintiffs in the  federal lawsuit  filed Thursday in Washington, D.C. The Pentagon, which partially funds the news outlet, fired them last week. A Pentagon spokesperson declined to comment on the suit’s allegations. Slavin says he was dismissed for insubordination after giving an interview to CBS News in which he objected to potential censorship by the U.S. military. Korte participated in the same interview. Their lawsuit says they were punished in retaliation for publishing a report on deteriorating conditions aboard the  U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln . “Stripes’ historical editorial independence is critical to its core mission of gathering and providing unbiased, credible journalism to the U.S. military community, particularly servicemembers and their families stationed overseas,” the suit says. Lederer was dismissed shortly after announcing his impending retirement, effective at the end of September. He said the Pentagon had installed a new deputy publisher, an active duty service member, under him at the newspaper without his prior knowledge. The suit’s plaintiffs are represented by attorneys from Democracy Defenders Fund, Lawyers for Good Government, Government Accountability Project and a Yale Law School clinic. The Defense Department and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth are among the named defendants. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Trump officially signs executive order directing government to rename Lake Ontario as ‘Lake America’
articles.summary: Trump, who signed the order at the Resolute Desk in the Oval Office, sat in front of a map with the words, “MAKING THE GREAT LAKES EVEN GREATER.”
articles._body: President Donald Trump said Thursday he is  renaming Lake Ontario  to be known as “Lake America” in the United States as he escalates his trade war with Canada. The Republican president signed an  executive order  directing the Interior Department to update the lake’s name in the U.S. geographic naming service. Trump cannot force Canada to follow along, however. Trump has been floating the idea of the name change in recent days as the U.S. announced it was imposing  50% tariffs  on $20 billion worth of Canadian goods over the weekend after talks between the countries broke down. Trump has been needling America’s northern neighbor since he returned to the White House last year, suggesting the ally with whom the U.S. once had warm relations should instead be absorbed as the  51st state . Canada responded to Trump’s import taxes this week by imposing retaliatory tariffs on $20 billion worth of American goods, including steel, dairy products, appliances and farm equipment. Trump, who signed the order as he was sitting at the Resolute Desk in the Oval Office, had a large sign behind him propped on a stand with a map of the Great Lakes. Over Lake Ontario, in big red letters, the map read “Lake America.” On the other side of the president was another map with the words, “MAKING THE GREAT LAKES EVEN GREATER.” Trump said as he was signing the order that he’d “notified all of the various people that we have to notify. So, we’ve done everything that you have to do.” “And this is official, effective immediately,” he added. But the executive order Trump signed shows that the changes are supposed to be made within 30 days. Canadian officials dismissed Trump’s move. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney rejected the move, invoking the lake’s Indigenous roots and noting that the name predates both Canadian Confederation and the U.S. Declaration of Independence. “Canadians also know that naming reality means calling it Lake Ontario — then, now and always,” he wrote. Ontario Premier Doug Ford, who has traded insults with Trump, said on X: “It’s Lake Ontario to Canadians and the rest of the world. Now and forever.” Nova Scotia Premier Tim Houston said, “We’re into some real foolishness now. It’s Lake Ontario, buddy.” The lake is one of multiple Great Lakes that the U.S. and Canada share borders along. New York Gov. Kathy Hochul, a Democrat whose state shares a border on the lake, wrote on X in response to the White House’s announcement that, “New York won’t be calling it that.” There is no single international body that determines names of international bodies of water and Trump has wide latitude over how the U.S. government recognizes geographic places and landmarks. The name Lake Ontario comes from the Huron Indigenous people’s word “oniatarí:io,” which means “lake of shining waters.” The province of Ontario, founded in 1867, took its name from the lake. Trump said that while his action was not meant to send any particular geopolitical message, “Canada’s been ripping us off for a long time” on trade and military issues. “They wanted to be treated like a state and they’re not a state,” the president said. “We just can’t do that anymore.” “We love the people of Canada,” Trump added. “I don’t think their representatives do, an appropriate job. Maybe they’ll change. I really don’t know. It doesn’t make much difference.” The move is reminiscent of his move last year to rename the Gulf of Mexico as the “Gulf of America.” Trump scribbled his name with a Sharpie pen on the executive order, then held it up for the cameras, offering, “And we filed all the necessary papers, documents, everything else.” He also suggested his push to rename bodies of water may not be finished. “So, if you think about it, we have a gulf and we have a lake. Now, all we need is an ocean,” Trump said. “So maybe we’ll have to change the name of the Atlantic and/or the Pacific. Maybe we’ll change them.” ___ Associated Press writer Rob Gillies in Toronto contributed to this report. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles._body: PITTSBURGH — With the 2026 campaign just a week away, Pitt football has revealed four team captains for the upcoming season. Quarterback Mason Heintschel , offensive tackle Ryan Baer , linebacker Braylan Lovelace and safety Cruce Brookins have been elected as the Pitt captains for the 2026 season. The captains were voted upon by fellow teammates and upperclassmen typically receive the designation at Pitt, which makes Heintschel’s election unique. It is believed that Heintschel is the first true sophomore in the modern era to be named a captain. The known redshirt sophomore captains include Tyler Palko in 2004, Lousaka Polite in 2001 and Alex Van Pelt in 1990. Since Heintschel arrived in January of 2025, he has displayed natural leadership that has been praised by teammates, coaches and those around the program. As a true freshman last season, Heintschel took over the starting quarterback role in early October. He went on to complete 201-of-316 passes for 2,354 yards and 16 touchdowns while adding two rushing scores. Heintschel went 6-3 as a started and earned ACC Quarterback of the Week honors once and ACC Rookie of the Week honors twice. Baer enters his fifth season with the Panthers and has been a key piece of the Panthers’ offensive line over the past few seasons. The 6-foot-7, 325-pounder started all 13 games last season and received honorable mention All-ACC recognition. Baer has made 35 career starts at tackle for Pitt. Lovelace, a Leechburg, Pa. native, made an impact immediately his freshman season. The senior became a full-time starter in 2025 with 80 tackles, 5.5 tackles for loss, two interceptions and four pass breakups. He was earned honorable mention All-ACC recognition in 2025. Brookins, a senior out of Steel Valley High School, is a pivotal piece of the Panthers’ defense and will start for the Panthers at the boundary safety position. Last season, Brookins, started eight of his 10 appearances with 53 tackles, two interceptions, two pass breakups and a half tackle for loss. Pitt kicks off the 2026 season on Sept. 5 against Miami (OH) at Acrisure Stadium. Game time is set for 12:30 p.m. on The CW.

articles.title: Miguel Says He & His Partner Have Been Targets of ‘Racist, Anti-Asian Attacks’ & ‘Abusive’ Comments About Their Child
articles.summary: The R&B singer spoke out about being subjected to racism, threats, harassment and stalking in a post on social media.
articles._body: Miguel is speaking out about the harassment, threats and racism he and his family are facing. The R&B singer posted a lengthy statement to social media on Friday (Aug. 28), describing how he and his family have been subjected to racism, threats, stalking, false allegations and an invasion of privacy. He also said there have been “anti-Asian attacks” directed at his partner Margaret Zhang, who is currently pregnant with the couple’s second child. “Over the past year, my family and the people i love have been subjected to racism, harassment, stalking, invasions of privacy, and false allegations,” the Grammy-winning singer wrote. “Recent racist and anti-Asian attacks directed at my partner – including comments and DMs, as well as abusive comments about my child – crossed a line that should require no explanation.” Miguel said he understands he will be open to certain aspects of criticism when it comes to his career as a public figure but believes a line has been crossed when it seeps into his family life and private affairs. “People can have opinions about me. about the music. about the work. I accept the realities that come with doing anything in public,” he added. “But racism, threats, harassment, stalking, invasions of privacy, and targeting of children are abuse. not opinion.” The 40-year-old continued: “It doesn’t become acceptable because someone dresses it up as criticism, fandom, speculation, or ‘concern.’ responsibility also lies with organizations and individuals that knowingly amplify or enable racism, harassment, or false allegations for attention and engagement. if you participate in this behavior, you are not supporting me. you are not part of this community.” The “Adorn” singer explained that legal action will be taken against those who continue to attack his family. “Where legal and ethical lines have been crossed, action has been and will continue to be taken,” Miguel stated. “To everyone who has treated my family with kindness, dignity, and respect: we see you. we deeply appreciate you.” The jarring post struck a chord with Miguel’s IG following, as an outpouring of support flooded his comment section. “Overwhelmed reading your comments of support loved ones, thank you,” he responded. Miguel and Zhang, who is the former editor-in-chief of Vogue China , welcomed a son, Angel, in 2024, and are expecting a second child. On the music front, Miguel released his CAOS album in October 2025. Find Miguel’s full statement below. Billboard has reached out to the singer-songwriter’s reps for comment. articles.title: South Carolina women’s basketball alum Aliyah Boston re-signs with Unrivaled, will defend DPOY crown
articles.summary: South Carolina women's basketball alum Aliyah Boston will play in the 2027 Unrivaled winter season this January.
articles._body: South Carolina women’s basketball alum Aliyah Boston will have a busy winter once again. Though the WNBA season ends in October, Boston will continue working. The last few offseasons, she has worked as a studio analyst on the Big Ten Network, and many would like to see that continue. On Friday, news broke that Boston would also be playing in the Unrivaled winter season once again. The league announced that the former Gamecock would spend this winter playing her third season in the 3-on-3 league. According to the release, Boston has signed a multi-year deal with Unrivaled. Last year, Boston was a second-team All-Unrivaled performer and the league’s Defensive Player of the Year. She was also the league’s fourth-leading rebounder and a major reason for her Phantom team being the No. 1 overall seed heading into the postseason. Questions about this story? Kevin Miller is discussing it with subscribers on the Women’s Basketball forum. Boston is in the midst of her fourth overall season as a professional in the WNBA. Already a four-time All-Star starter, she is averaging a career-best 17.0 points per game. She is also pulling down 8.4 rebounds per contest, dishing out 3.0 assists, and tallying 2.7 stocks (1.5 steals and 1.2 blocks). Boston has been remarkably efficient yet again, shooting 52.4% from the field, 41.7% from the 3-point arc, and 82.4% from the free throw line. Boston’s Indiana Fever team currently holds the No. 5 overall seed in the race for the WNBA Postseason. The Fever have clinched a playoff berth and are just one game back from the 3-seed. Before the WNBA regular season concludes, Boston will play in the 2026 FIBA World Cup. Fellow Gamecock legend A’ja Wilson will also be on the team that competes in Berlin from September 4 through 13. articles.title: PGA Tour’s Atlanta Future Unclear As Tour Championship Changes Loom
articles.summary: John David Mercer-Imagn Images
articles._body: ATLANTA — This week’s Tour Championship marks East Lake Golf Club’s penultimate year as the permanent host of the PGA Tour’s season-ending event—and the course’s future welcoming professional golf is uncertain. The historic Atlanta country club has hosted every edition of the Tour Championship since 2004, but its contract is up after next year’s tournament, and in 2028 the PGA Tour will begin rotating among new venue hosts for a revamped, two-week Tour Championship to annually conclude future seasons with match play for the first time. Many of those will be courses the PGA Tour has never played at before or doesn’t visit very often. East Lake won’t be out of the running altogether, though. “Yes, East Lake is very much in the consideration set for future Tour Championship events for sure,” PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp said Tuesday at his pre-tournament press conference. “We’ve had conversations with them. We’ll have more meetings this week.” The PGA Tour has not mentioned any other specific courses that will be considered for Tour Championships. Rory McIlroy mentioned in his Tuesday press conference that the new two-week tournament could be “one week on the West Coast, one week on the East Coast,” which could theoretically put East Lake in the mix. As the PGA plans its transition to a new two-track scheduling model in 2028, the tour earlier this year asked East Lake leaders if they would be interested in hosting springtime event on the new top-tier Championship Series. The club declined that opportunity, according to a letter to members from East Lake GM and president Chad Parker and chairman Larry Gellerstedt obtained by Golf Channel . For many golf observers, Atlanta seems like a natural fit to host an event around the Masters, given its proximity to Augusta. East Lake also hosted the Tour Championship in 1998, 2000, and 2002 before taking over full-time duties in 2004. In 2007, the FedExCup launched, and East Lake has been where each year’s season-ending FedExCup Champion has been crowned. “This is as high of an expression of professional golf as there is,” Tour Championship tournament director Alex Urban said of East Lake during a conversation with Front Office Sports this week. No matter East Lake’s future, being the first home of the FedExCup will be one of the course’s lasting legacies, according to Urban. “It’s a place where legacies of PGA Tour players were cemented and made,” he said. “There’s been some really big moments—and some still to come.” As this week’s 30-player field fight for the $40 million purse and $10 million first-place prize, fans are piling into East Lake despite the August heat. The course has grandstands and sponsored fan activities everywhere you look—and even a new signature cocktail, the Fuzzy Peach (vodka, peach sparkling water, grenadine, lime, and a candy peach ring). The post PGA Tour’s Atlanta Future Unclear As Tour Championship Changes Loom appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles._body: Asa Montgomery , one of the summer’s biggest risers, is taking an official visit to LSU this weekend, sources told Rivals. The 6-foot-7 small forward out of Hillgrove High School (GA) is now ranked as the No. 15 overall recruit in the 2027 class, according to the Rivals Industry Ranking . Montgomery, a high-four prospect, led the Nike EYCL Circuit in scoring this summer, averaging 27.9 points, 10.2 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 1.4 steals, and 1.9 blocks per game for AOT. In addition to the Tigers, he’s received offers Duke, North Carolina, Kentucky, UConn, Louisville, Florida, Alabama, Houston, Auburn, Arkansas, Georgia, Michigan, Michigan State, and more. Scouting Asa Montgomery + what he’s looking for in a school Rivals National Recruiting Analyst Jamie Shaw has evaluated Montgomery multiple times in person. Here’s what he had to say about him after watching him in July: In the most recent 2027 Rivals150 update Asa Montgomery jumped to No. 15 overall. The length and explosive 6-foot-7 forward has had as much success as anyone through the spring and summer. On Wednesday night, Montgomery was able to do whatever he wanted on the court. He showcased his handle, creating advantages for himself and his team. He knocked down multiple threes, both off the catch and the bounce. And he displayed top-level-type explosive burst finishing above the rim. The upside remains very high with Montgomery, but with that upside comes the current level of production he is seeing. A lengthy and explosive wing with positional size and three-level scoring ability is intriguing. Especially when you also look at his defensive upside. Montgomery has been one of the steepest spring risers, and I don’t expect that to change in the coming week. In a previous interview with Rivals, Montgomery discussed what he is looking for in a college program. “I want to go to a family-oriented team. A tight team, and I want to play for a coach that can help me develop and who will put me in the right situations for where I am trying to go.”

Tupac Trial Week 2 Recap: Murder Case Heads to Jury After Explosive Recording & More Testimony
articles.summary: Billboard is summing up the key moments from the second week of the epic murder trial over the hip-hop legend's 1996 killing.
articles._body: The second week of the Tupac Shakur murder trial saw an explosive jailhouse recording, prosecutors rest their case and attorneys for Duane “Keffe D” Davis quickly wrap their own brief defense, sending the trial to the jury far sooner than expected. You’re reading Billboard’s weekly Tupac trial recap, a one-sheet breakdown of everything that happened in the epic murder case over the past week. Stay tuned here each Friday for all the testimony and big events you might have missed. Related Tupac Murder Trial Week 1 Recap: An ‘Act of Revenge,’ Heated Testimony & Police Tapes Dale Morris, Nashville Manager Who Guided Careers of Alabama & Kenny Chesney, Dies at 89 HYBE Pledges Over $300k for Colombia Earthquake Recovery After a first week filled with fireworks, prosecutors resumed their case on Monday (Aug. 24) with testimony from filmmaker Michael Dorsey, who worked on a BET docuseries in which Davis gave interviews discussing his role in the killing. Jurors watched hours of unedited interview footage, which featured Davis declining to apologize to Tupac’s family. Later in the week, prosecutors called police officers and investigators to the stand, including Robert Ladd, who testified that Davis was a “shot caller” within his Compton gang. Ladd told jurors that Davis’ nephew Orlando “Baby Lane” Anderson, who allegedly pulled the trigger, could not have opened fire on Tupac without his uncle’s permission: “The younger gang members are supposed to do what they’re told without hesitation.” As prosecutors neared the end of their case, they played a jailhouse recording from 2023 in which Davis uttered a line that the state clearly wanted jurors to remember: “I got blood on my money,” he said in the tape . On Wednesday (Aug. 26), the prosecution rested its case — far sooner than expected for a trial that was anticipated to run for at least four weeks. In total, they had called 24 witnesses and played more than eight hours of recordings, mostly of Davis himself discussing his role in the killing. When the defense kicked off its case on Thursday (Aug. 27), it didn’t last long. They called just three witnesses — all of them former Las Vegas Metropolitan Police officers — in less than two hours, aimed at poking holes and raising reasonable doubt in the mind of jurors. One testified that he saw a light-colored Cadillac arrive leave Suge Knight’s Las Vegas mansion on the night of the crime — seemingly an effort by the defense to suggest that the vehicle used in the crime might have come from Knight’s own entourage. Another faced questions about the quality of the police work on the case, testifying that records had to be locked to avoid interference from “curious” staffers and that some files were later lost. Perhaps more notable was who didn’t testify: Davis himself. Defense attorneys rarely put a criminal defendant on the witness stand, since it subjects them to withering cross-examination by prosecutors. And in a case where jurors already heard from him so many times, Davis’ attorneys chose not to go against that conventional legal wisdom. With both sides rested, jury instructions were set to be delivered on Friday (Aug. 28) and closing statements are set for the morning on Monday (Aug. 31). After that, the trial — and the fate of the long-unsolved Tupac murder case — will be in the hands of the jurors. The time needed to deliberate in such cases varies widely, from just a few hours to many days, meaning verdict could come as soon as Monday.

articles.title: Matt Rhule blasts rising roster costs, suggests ex-NFL players ‘twice as good’ as current CFB players
articles.summary: Nebraska head coach Matt Rhule sees two major issues developing amid the latest changes across college football. As roster spending continues to climb, programs are now also dealing with the possibility of players returning to college after spending time with NFL teams.  Rhule believes those players
articles._body: Nebraska head coach Matt Rhule sees two major issues developing amid the latest changes across college football. As roster spending continues to climb, programs are now also dealing with the possibility of players returning to college after spending time with NFL teams. Rhule believes those players could have a significant advantage if they are allowed to return to the college level. Speaking with OutKick’s Dan Dakich on his Don’t @ Me! podcast , Rhule argued that even a player buried on an NFL depth chart could come back substantially better after experiencing professional training. $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage He also pushed back on continuing to describe college football’s compensation model simply as name, image and likeness. Instead, Rhule believes the sport has reached the point where programs are dealing with a rapidly increasing player payroll. “Twice as good, twice as good,” Rhule said when asked how much better a player could be after spending time in an NFL camp. “I mean, I think the hardest thing, you know, when you’re coaching these guys is you’re always telling them like, ‘Hey guys, do this, this is what it’s like, or the next level.’ You know, half of it is like as a kid, you know they’re kids, right? … Like just the growth you make.” Alas, the topic is one that’s swept the sports world, as players returning from the NFL has become one of the biggest points of contention in college football entering the 2026 season. Recent court rulings have opened the door for some former professional players to pursue additional college eligibility. Evidently, Rhule believes the time those players spend preparing for and participating in the NFL can make a major difference in their development: “They train for the combine. They train in a pro facility, had an agent pay for their meals, trained with NFL teams, they had training camp,” Rhule added . “I think if an NFL player came back, it would be twice, if not three times better than they were.” Matt Rhule: NIL spending ‘has gone up 60% every year’ However, Rhule’s concerns about the current state of college football extend beyond eligibility. With programs spending more money than ever to construct their rosters, the Nebraska leader believes the sport needs to change the way it discusses player compensation. He argued that “NIL” is no longer an accurate description of what has become a significant expense for programs around the country. “People use the term NIL for a while. We gotta get rid of that, it’s just payroll. It’s player payroll,” Rhule further explained . “You look at the National Football League, all the major sports, they all have a salary cap because they say the number one expenditure is paying players. In college football, the spending on players has gone up 60% every year.” Additionally, Rhule then offered an idea of how much the cost of building a competitive roster has increased: “What was once a $24 million roster is now a $30 [million],” Rhule elaborated . “Playoff teams this year, outside research, is about $45 million. Some of the numbers coming out might not have the right word, but some of the numbers are low, it’s about $45 million a year.” All told, Nebraska has access to significant resources, and Rhule acknowledged the school benefits from sponsorships and other revenue opportunities. Still, the changing financial landscape forces programs to determine how much they are willing to spend and where that money should go. For Rhule, the rapid increase in roster costs only makes those decisions more important as programs attempt to keep pace with the biggest spenders in college football. Whether or not it translates to wins on the field, and eventual championships, remains to be seen.

articles.title: Prince Estate Releases Funky, Career-Spanning ‘Timeless’ Vault Album Commemorating 10th Anniversary of Singer’s Death: Listen
articles.summary: The collection of rare and previously unreleased songs were recorded between 1977 and 2016, including material recorded when The Purple One was a teenager.
articles._body: The Prince estate released the 10-song vault collection Timeless on Friday (Aug. 28), a funky collection of rare and previously unreleased songs from the late pop icon’s infamously stacked vault as part of a year-long commemoration of the 10th anniversary of his death. The Estate — which released the set in partnership with Legacy Recordings — said it represents the first-ever Prince release to cover every major era of the singer’s career, spanning recordings tracked when he was a Minneapolis teenager in 1977 through ones cut in 2016; Prince died of an accidental fentanyl overdose on April 21, 2016 at his Paisley Park estate in Minnesota. The set opens with the horn-spiked funk jam “I Am You,” which, like most of the songs on the collection was written arranged, performed and produced almost entirely by Prince as a yearning plea for a lover’s return. It was recorded at Minneapolis’ Sound 89 studio in 1977 when he was just 19 years old. It’s followed-up by the blitzing, punky lust bomb of 1981’s “Tick Tick Bang,” which was released on the Graffiti Bridge album nine years later with a more funk-forward feel. “Heaven,” a spare pop jam from 1985, features backing vocals from Prince’s former girlfriend and Revolution band member singer Susannah Melvoin, while 1989’s “I Wonder” has a loping, gospel-country vibe. The emotional, lush piano ballad “With This Tear” (1991) was tracked before Prince gave the song to Celine Dion, who recorded it for her self-titled 1992 LP. The latter was previously released as a single from the collection alongside “Stone,” a previously unreleased slow-burn R&B tune from 1995. The set is rounded out by the 2003 hand-clapping soul jam “Calabama,” 2007’s rock burner “The Guilty Ones” and 2012’s majestic “Bestest Friend.” The final track is a live version of the fan-favorite non-album 1999 B-side “How Come U Don’t Call Me Anymore?,” recorded live at the Oracle Arena in Oakland, Calif. on March, 4, 2015, a month before Prince’s passing. The set was mixed and mastered by Grammy-nominated engineer/producer Chris James ( Plectrumelectrum ) and produced for compilation by estate co-manager L. Londell McMillan, who said in a statement, “ Timeless describes Prince in many ways, even beyond his musical genius. Prince was indeed one of only one, a legendary artist and master musician with unprecedented style, faith, courage, dignity and brilliance. His overall essence and spirit remains timeless. This current album covers 5 decades of Prince’s music from 1977 through 2016 with unreleased music from the Prince Vault, all on one album. Enjoy this music project along with his legendary catalog of released music, as it all is TIMELESS and more to come this year and beyond.” In addition to the album, the estate dropped an official video for “The Guilty Ones,” featuring a compilation of live and music video footage spanning the singer’s career. Listen to Timeless and watch “The Guilty Ones” video below.

articles.summary: The Minnesota men’s basketball has officially announced its non-conference schedule for the 2026-27 season as well as a neutral site series against ACC foe, SMU. The Golden Gophers will play two exhibition games ahead of the regular season, hosting Omaha on October 15 before traveling to face
articles._body: The Minnesota men’s basketball has officially announced its non-conference schedule for the 2026-27 season as well as a neutral site series against ACC foe, SMU . The Golden Gophers will play two exhibition games ahead of the regular season, hosting Omaha on October 15 before traveling to face Creighton on October 23. Minnesota’s 2026-27 season will officially begin November 2 when they host North Dakota. They’ll then host St. Thomas on November 6 before hitting the road for the first time for a November 9 matchup at Cincinnati. After the short trip to visit the Bearcats, the Gophers will return home for two games against Southern and Western Illinois on November 12 and 16 before traveling to Charleston, South Carolina for two matchups as part of the Shriners Children’s Charleston Classic. They’ll continue the neutral site matchups with a November 28 matchup against Cal at the Sanford Pentagon in Sioux Falls, South Dakota before facing SMU on December 12 at the Comerica Center in Frisco, Texas. That non-conference matchup was announced on Friday as well, with the intention of SMU returning the favor with a likely neural site game in 2028. “We’re really excited to add another Power-4 conference opponent to our schedule this year and face a tough SMU team that made the NCAA Tournament last season,” Minnesota Head Coach Niko Medved said in a press release. “We’re looking forward to playing at the Comerica Center, but also building a great partnership with SMU for a future date in the Minneapolis area during the 2028-29 season. I have no doubt it will be two great events against two competitive teams.” After the matchup in Dallas, the Gophers will end non-conference play against Alcorn State on December 20 and UTSA on December 29. Idiots review: Mason Thames leads a fittingly stupid movie
articles.summary: Generally speaking, calling a movie stupid sounds like a criticism, not a compliment. In Mason Thames’ follow-up to Nimrods, a film that’s tame in comparison to his next project, Idiots — which reunites him with Regretting You co-star Dave Franco and teams him with O’Shea Jackson Jr. — is fitting
articles._body: Generally speaking, calling a movie stupid sounds like a criticism, not a compliment. In Mason Thames’ follow-up to Nimrods , a film that’s tame in comparison to his next project, Idiots — which reunites him with Regretting You co-star Dave Franco and teams him with O’Shea Jackson Jr. — is fittingly stupid. Idiots is often a frustrating watch. It features good work from Thames — who is at his most unlikable — and Jackson, who is given a unique role in the film. However, unlike Thames’ last movie, Nimrods, which came out earlier in the month, Idiots isn’t as much of a redemptive tale. The characters grow in their own way, but it ultimately leaves them in the same place as where they began. Perhaps that’s the point. Idiots isn’t about heroes. At their best, some of the characters in Idiots are well-intentioned, while others are pathological liars. What is Idiots about? A still from Idiots courtesy of Independent Film Company. Davis (O’Shea Jackson Jr.) is down on his luck. He’s fired from his position at a church after taking kids to an inappropriate movie. In turn, he loses his van. Meanwhile, Mark (Dave Franco) is, to put it lightly, a bum. He wastes away his days doing drugs and is in need of a job. So, he takes a look at a transportation service for troubled teens. Because Davis doesn’t have a van and Mark has his small sedan, they are tasked with driving Sheridan Kimberly (Mason Thames), who comes from a wealthy family, to rehab. However, he is way more than what meets the eye. As Davis and Mark drive Sheridan to rehab, they hit constant roadblocks, each one crazier than the last, thanks to the kid. Mason Thames shines out of the leading trio To start positively, Thames is really good in the movie. He has grown a lot from his days as Finney in the Black Phone series. Nimrods showed that he can play characters who are jerks, as he played the blindly ambitious band leader Tommy in the Green Day movie. Now, Sheridan is hiding secrets behind his smug smile. This leads to some gut-wrenching moments, including one with a prostitute, in Idiots. If you’re a fan of Thames, Idiots can paint pictures that are hard to unsee. That’s the beauty of his acting — he has range that can make him a likable protagonist like in How to Train Your Dragon or Regretting You while also being able to portray a crappy person. Jackson similarly gets to showcase his range. He has played a variety of roles, but he is now the straight man in Idiots. It’s a unique role for him, as he gets to lean into different kinds of comedy. A lot of his success comes off the back of his rapport with Franco. Franco is the least flashy out of the leading trio, delivering his reliably steady performance you’ve seen in his other roles. The bonkers script A still from Idiots courtesy of Independent Film Company. All three characters — Mark, Davis, and Sheridan — are lowlifes. If nothing else, writer-director Macon Blair deserves credit for writing a very realistic story. None of them really get redemption, per se, and they ultimately end up where they probably deserve. Some of the side quests that Blair puts his characters on are insane. There’s no greater example of this than the characters’ run-in with a group led by Peter Dinklage. Idiots can sometimes feel overly cynical. Not every joke goes as dark as it could (which is a good thing), but plenty of them are more shocking than funny. There’s a reason that Judd Apatow, who made comparable movies in the early 2000s, found success with his projects. Something like Superbad has some characters with bad motives. However, the characters ultimately grow and learn from their mistakes, with their stories being neatly wrapped up in a bow. Blair doesn’t do the same with Idiots. Maybe it was by design, but it makes it incredibly hard to connect with any of the characters. Even Nimrods, which is an easy comparison, given its recent release and Thames’ performance, did a better job balancing the cynical with optimism. Should you watch Idiots? A still from Idiots courtesy of Independent Film Company. Idiots is a raunchy and cynical comedy that rarely gets made anymore. While it doesn’t save that subgenre, it might inadvertently reveal why it died. There are a few laughs, though it’s hardly consistent, and Blair does his characters no favors. Not since Funny Pages has a movie been filled with such irredeemable characters. The story itself starts interesting, but it ultimately becomes a vehicle to get from one “gag” to the next. There are some interesting moments, but Idiots undercuts most of them with its abrasive humor. Idiots tries very hard to bring audiences back to the early 2000s, but it fails in almost every regard. It really doesn’t help that Nimrods, which is similarly a road trip story starring Thames, just came out, and it’s a lot better. Nimrods succeeds in every area that Idiots fails, including (most importantly) having a heart. Idiots, like the characters in The Wizard of Oz, is missing heart, courage, and brains. Grade: D+ Idiots is in theaters. The post Idiots review: Mason Thames leads a fittingly stupid movie appeared first on ClutchPoints .
