articles.title: Chart Rewind: In 1976, Ronnie Milsap Took a ‘Stand’ at No. 1
articles.summary: The signature piano lick in “(I’m a) Stand by My Woman Man” generated a legal issue.
articles._body: When Ronnie Milsap’s “(I’m a) Stand by My Woman Man” reached No. 1 on Billboard ’s Hot Country Songs chart dated Aug. 28, 1976, the public accomplishment hid a private feud. Related Ronnie Milsap Brings His Country Soul to Nashville One More Time: ‘I’m Thankful’ Chart Rewind: In 2016, Jon Pardi’s ‘Boots’ Stepped to No. 1 on Country Airplay Chart Rewind: On July 1, 2006, Taylor Swift Made Her Billboard Debut During the recording session at RCA Studio A, producer Tom Collins (Barbara Mandrell, Steve Wariner) asked pianist Hargus “Pig” Robbins to play the kind of lick he might invent for a George Jones or Tammy Wynette cut in the “Stand by My Woman Man” chorus. The song’s title sounded similar to Wynette’s “Stand by Your Man,” and Robbins created a fill that likewise sounded a bit like one he played on “Stand by Your Man.” After Milsap’s recording was released, publisher Al Gallico allegedly sued Collins for a copyright violation. As a result, “Stand by My Woman Man” songwriter Kent Robbins (John Anderson’s “Straight Tequila Night,” George Strait’s “Write This Down”), who died in 1997, now shares writing credit with Wynette and her producer, Billy Sherrill (Charlie Rich, Tanya Tucker), according to the BMI.com Songview database. “Stand by My Woman Man” debuted on the Hot Country Songs chart dated July 10, 1976, reaching the top seven weeks later to become the sixth of Milsap’s 35 career No. 1s. It wasn’t the only honor that the song accrued. Milsap received the Grammy for best country vocal performance by a male in February 1977, and Kent Robbins (no relation to Pig) snagged a Country Music Association nomination for best country song. One extra bit of trivia: the Aug. 28 date for Milsap’s No. 1 aligns with the date that Wynette wrote and recorded “Stand by Your Man,” Aug. 28, 1968.

How Revolution Hall Turned a Shuttered School Into ‘One of Portland’s Most Popular Tourist Attractions’
articles.summary: The owners of Portland, Ore.'s Mississippi Studios helped turn "a bad investment" into a concert hall that has welcomed Laufey, Jack White, Indigo Girls and more.
articles._body: After more than 30 years of minimal to no use, the city of Portland, Ore., had three ideas for the old building that once housed Washington High School: tear it down, convert it into office buildings space, or — the more out-of-the-box idea — turn it into a music venue. The Washington High building “was a bad investment for anybody, honestly,” says Portland entrepreneur Kevin Craddock , who owns Revolution Hall, Mississippi Studios and Polaris Hall. But local developer and preservationist Art DeMuro had a vision for the long-standing brick building. He envisioned a concert hall within the more than 130,000-square foot facility with additional office spaces in the place of former classrooms. “DeMuro was savvy enough and respected enough and beloved enough that he got the deal done with the city,” backed by real estate developer PacTrust in 2013, Craddock adds. Related Why The Belly Up in San Diego Is a Magnet for Music Royalty — From The Rolling Stones to Snoop Dogg Dale Morris, Nashville Manager Who Guided Careers of Alabama & Kenny Chesney, Dies at 89 HYBE Pledges Over $300k for Colombia Earthquake Recovery Shortly after securing the high school — which first opened in 1906 and moved to its current location in 1909, then was rebuilt in 1924 following a fire — for an $18 million restoration, DeMuro passed away from cancer. But the project went on, and when it came time to design and build out the concert venue, the development company Venerable Properties reached out to the owners of Portland’s beloved indie venue Mississippi Studios, Craddock and Jim Brunberg , to build what would be called Revolution Hall. “I was having a sandwich next door at this place called Meat Cheese Bread, and Jim just rolled over with our talent buyer at the time and said, ‘Hey, we’re gonna go look at this high school. They want to turn it into a music venue,’” says Craddock. “I didn’t even go with them.” Craddock was familiar with the building. Back in his bartending days, he used to break into the high school after work through what he called “the door of debauchery,” and take in the stunning view of the city in the wee hours of the morning. He says that the door was never latched and earlier this year he got the original vestibule he broke in through tattooed on his leg. After the school shut down, Craddock also attended experimental shows called Time-Based Art put on by the Portland Institute of Contemporary Art at the building. At the time, there was no running water, only one usable bathroom on the bottom floor, and the event organizers had to run electricity from a generator. “I think they had permission, but maybe not,” says Brunberg. “It was permission light,” jokes Craddock. “Diet permission.” Revolution Hall in Portland, Ore. Jim Brunberg/Courtesy Revolution Hall By the time DeMuro’s team was ready to renovate Washington High, the whole place needed to be gutted. The restoration project included a historic overlay to preserve the exterior and design elements of the school, but new plumbing and electrical systems were installed, as well as a new roof. Despite the obvious cost and complications of renovating a space that hadn’t seen regular use in over three decades, Craddock and Brunberg, who always have a sawzall or some form of chainsaw in their cars to “tweak” things at one of their venues, were up to the task. Wanting to spend more time at home after years as a touring musician in bands like Box Set (which appeared on the cover of Billboard magazine’s best unsigned bands issue in 1994), Brunberg opened Mississippi Studios in 2003. Originally, the space had been a recording studio, but Brunberg transformed the former church into a 100-cap room that welcomed underplays from Yeah Yeah Yeahs , Brandi Carlile , Regina Spektor , Feist , Rickie Lee Jones and Hot Tuna . A few years later, Brunberg met Craddock at a mutual friend’s party. “I knew who Jim was the whole time, so when he very casually said, ‘The business isn’t doing good, I just had these kids and I’m on the road, be my business partner,’ I was like, ‘That sounds like a good idea,’” says Craddock, who had spent years in music-adjacent jobs and in construction. The trust was immediately apparent in their working relationship. “Jim announced to the staff before I even was a legal owner that I was one of the owners, and then he went on the road with [the band] Storm,” says Craddock. Revolution Hall owners Jim Brunberg (left) and Kevin Craddock. Byron Beck/Courtesy Revolution Hall In 2009, Craddock fully jumped in to improve food and beverage options and add structure to the business side of Mississippi Studios. Over the years, Mississippi Studios has been renovated several times and the pair added the Bar Bar restaurant, which claims to have the best burgers in town. “He saved the business because I was a dumbass musician trying to run this little venue,” says Brunberg. “We’re like a family. Everybody thinks that Kevin and I are either married or brothers, and that’s fine with us.” The jovial duo quickly realized the biggest initial expense in renovating Washington High was soundproofing the auditorium so that the other tenants wouldn’t be disrupted by soundcheck in the middle of the day. And the historic overlay meant even the curved wood auditorium chairs had to keep their original design. Related From ‘Dime-a-Dance’ to Hosting U2 & Bob Dylan: How Cain’s Ballroom in Tulsa Has Endured for Over a Century “The old seats were only 16 inches wide, but we did not notice that when we first got the tour of the building,” Brunberg says. Local codes mandate that seats be at least 21 inches wide. On that initial tour, Brunberg laughs that he patted himself on the back for bringing a tape measure to check the length of the seats. “They were 23 inches wide, which is great. FBS announces major CFB changes going into effect starting 2027
articles.summary: The structure of the college football calendar will look significantly different beginning in 2027. The Athletic’s Chris Vannini outlined several upcoming FBS changes, including an earlier start to the regular season, a redesigned spring-practice schedule, and a shorter winter transfer-portal win
articles._body: The structure of the college football calendar will look significantly different beginning in 2027. The Athletic’s Chris Vannini outlined several upcoming FBS changes , including an earlier start to the regular season, a redesigned spring-practice schedule, and a shorter winter transfer-portal window. The season will officially begin during what is currently called Week 0. Teams will no longer need waivers to play that weekend, creating a 14-week calendar in which every program can play 12 regular-season games and receive two bye weeks. The change could also eliminate the “Week 0” label altogether. Vannini indicated that the opening weekend will likely be renamed Week 1, meaning the traditional numbering system will shift beginning in 2027. Spring football is also receiving an overhaul. Programs will be permitted to hold two OTA-style periods totaling 21 practices, giving coaching staffs more flexibility when organizing their offseason work. The January transfer-portal window will shrink to only 10 days as well. That compressed schedule could create a hectic period for players evaluating their futures and coaches attempting to rebuild their rosters. Each change carries significant consequences. The earlier start gives teams additional rest during the season, while the new spring format allows programs to divide their preparation. The shorter portal window, however, will force transfer decisions to happen much faster. College football’s calendar has undergone constant changes in recent years. Beginning in 2027, even the meaning of Week 1 will be different. What is going on in college athletics is the talk of sports altogether right now. This is a very chaotic time that is making a lot of people unhappy. We will see how the NCAA handles this moving forward. articles.title: Stray Kids, aespa, TOMORROW X TOGETHER & Charlie Puth Headline 2026 TIMA Honors in Hong Kong
articles.summary: The second annual TMElive International Music Awards spanned two days and included more than 30 performers.
articles._body: Stray Kids , aespa , TOMORROW X TOGETHER and Charlie Puth were among the headliners for the 2026 TMElive International Music Awards, held across two days in Hong Kong this week (Aug. 22-23). Related 2025 TIMA Wraps in Macau After Performances From aespa, TWICE, ITZY & More Global Hitmakers Yasuhisa Hara's 'Kingdom' Vol. 80 Tops Billboard Japan Book Hot 100 John Mayer Says Dolly Parton's Death Brought a 'Fractured World' Together & Shares Electric Guitar Spin on 'I Will Always Love You' The TIMA honors, which were held for the first time last year in Macao and are put on by Chinese music giant Tencent, moved to Hong Kong’s Kai Tak Arena for this year’s edition. The weekend-long event featured more than 30 artists from China, Korea, Japan, Thailand, the United States and more performing on the arena’s main stage, interspersed with awards and speeches. During the event, Stray Kids won international group of the year; TOMORROW X TOGETHER won the award for best international group – male; aespa won best international group – female; BABYMONSTER won global icon group; Super Junior won most influential international group of the year; Puth won international artist of the year; and TAEYEON won most influential international artist of the year, among the two-dozen-plus awards handed out across two days. Courtesy TIMA Taeyong, from South Korean boy band NCT, opened the event on Saturday (Aug. 22) with his solo single “WYLD,” the title track off his first full-length solo album released earlier this year. Acts were then given between five and 30 minutes to perform selections for the tens of thousands in attendance, including Daniel Seavey (formerly of Why Don’t We) who performed his new solo single “Love’s A Gun”; AllDay Project, who performed their single “Famous” during their set; as well as Yeonjun, BABYMONSTER, RIIZE, aespa and TOMORROW X TOGETHER. Closing out night one was a set from trailblazing South Korean group Super Junior. Sunday (Aug. 23) opened with sets from rising artists like Korean-Japanese group NEXZ and Thai singer NuNew, as well as Korean girl group MEOVV, digital avatar collective PLAVE, and hitmakers such as NMIXX, NCT WISH and IVE. Girls’ Generation alum TAEYEON delivered a powerful rendition of her solo song “Letter To Myself” before Puth performed “One Call Away” and his massive, Billboard Hot 100-topping Wiz Khalifa collaboration “See You Again” with just a piano and acoustic guitar accompaniment. Stray Kids — riding high as their latest album, This & That , had just become their ninth straight release to debut at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 — closed out night two with “S-Class,” “Topline” and more favorites. articles.summary:
With the Tampa Bay Rays looking to make a postseason push, the future of the team is bright after the approval on Friday for a new stadium in the city for the team. As the Rays try to hold their lead in the AL East, the team will be getting a new stadium in Tampa […]

The post
articles._body: With the Tampa Bay Rays looking to make a postseason push , the future of the team is bright after the approval on Friday for a new stadium in the city for the team. As the Rays try to hold their lead in the AL East , the team will be getting a new stadium in Tampa Bay with the latest deal as details have been revealed. According to Ryan Bass, the Hillsborough County Commission has passed through a $2.3 billion stadium deal, as the saga surrounding a new stadium is complete “after nearly two decades.” “The Hillsborough County Commission has voted in favor of the $2.3 billion stadium deal, which follows Tampa City Council’s approval yesterday. After nearly two decades, the Tampa Bay Rays stadium saga is all but over. The #Rays have secured their forever home in Tampa,” Bass wrote on X, formerly Twitter, The baseball team has been playing inside Tropicana Field since the inaugural season of the Rays in 1998. More information on the Rays’ new stadium deal Rays chief executive officer Ken Babby released a statement on Thursday saying how “grateful” he is for the City Council members to approve the $2.3 billion deal, via ESPN. Funded by public and private money, whether through the Rays themselves or other avenues, Babby would continue to show his “deepest gratitude” for the movement in the stadium deal, according to Tampa Bay’s Spectrum News, “I want to express our deepest gratitude to Hillsborough County and the City of Tampa for their leadership, partnership, and willingness to say yes to what for so long had been considered impossible: a new ballpark for the Tampa Bay Rays,” Rays Manager Partner and Co-Chair Patrick Zalupski said in a released statement. “This has been a long and challenging process, and we know that transformational projects rarely come easily.” Team officials have said, “They want to be in the new facility in time for the 2029 season.” At any rate, it remains to be seen what the next steps are for the team’s new stadium, as the team is in the midst of the 2026 season. Durant revealed plenty in his chat with Speedy Morman, including more than one song he recorded alongside James. Durant laid down more than a couple of songs with LeBron
articles._body: In a recent interview , Houston Rockets veteran Kevin Durant admitted to making music with Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James. Durant revealed plenty in his chat with Speedy Morman , including more than one song he recorded alongside James. Durant laid down more than a couple of songs with LeBron, he said, per Boardroom. “Three songs, I think,” Durant said. “So, I went to Akron in like 2011 to work out with him for like four or five days. And he had a studio because Rich Paul and I were really the ones who got it going and convinced LeBron to rap, because Rich Paul was trying to recruit me when he first started Klutch. And, actually, I liked Rich. So, we hung out a lot.” Durant says the rapping started between him and James’ agent, Rich Paul, before the two eventually convinced James to step into the booth. “So, we were just rapping and convinced Bron to rap that one day,” Durant added. “He got in there and locked in. Anytime somebody do something for the first few times, it’s forced — it’s a little forced. But once you get that flow, he would’ve figured it out. He loves rap.” As for the songs with LeBron James, Kevin Durant can’t say what happened to them or whether the recordings exist. “I don’t know — that’s a good question,” Durant said. “They’re in that studio in Akron somewhere. The engineer or somebody’s got them. I think that’s who dropped it. The engineer dropped it. He dropped one of them, and that’s how people even heard about it.” A clip of one of James and Durant’s songs can be heard toward the end of Boardroom’s post on X, formerly Twitter. KD says he and @KingJames recorded three tracks together pic.twitter.com/JQGHGCCeZn — Boardroom (@boardroom) August 27, 2026 Rockets’ Durant also addressed his rage-baiters ahead of his second season in Houston. articles.title: Erykah Badu & The Alchemist’s ‘Before the World Blows’: All 16 Tracks Ranked
articles.summary: Two legends link up to bring Erykah Badu's first album in 16 years to life.
articles._body: After dropping their first single “ Next 2 U ” a little more than a year ago, Erykah Badu & The Alchemist have finally delivered on their much anticipated collab album, and it did not disappoint. Before the World Blows: The Abi & Alan Experiment is a 16-track journey into the minds of two legendary artists in their respective fields that decided to come together to create a work of art. And to think, this all started with Badu wanting to rap over Al’s “The Realest” instrumental from Mobb Deep ‘s 1999 album Murda Muzik . “It reminded us of like some Ron G mixtape s—t, the Alchemist told Billboard during an interview alongside Freddie Gibbs last year. “I’m still bugging that I have a record with her. This is a big step for me.” The two unlikely partners might have some curious about how something from them would sound and honestly, they exceeded my expectations of whatever it is that I thought I was gonna hear. That first single doesn’t even scratch the surface. As soon as you hit play on the intro track, “Echos,” you’re thrown into this immersive experience of ethereal sounds of psychedelic funk, R&B, jazz and hip-hop as if they threw everything into a pot and made some gumbo. This is surely a great look for the legendary producer, and puts his underrated versatility on full display. Maybe now, we can finally get that introspective jazz album with Young Thug . Anyway, I had the pleasure of getting a preview last summer on the rooftop of Electric Lady Studios in NYC and can’t wait to catch them live when they slide through Forest Hills Stadium next month in September. I’ve been hating on whoever got to experience this live during The Abi & Alan Japan Tour last year. It’s finally my turn. I can only imagine that seeing this in person would be nothing short of a spiritual experience, especially if it hits like it did for me last night when I had my headphones on with one lit and one rolled. Before the World Blows: The Abi & Alan Experiment features DJ Creole Princess (in a show-stealing performance,) Westside Gunn , Joi, DRAM , Steve Lacy , Thundercat , Earl Sweatshirt , Kamasi Washington , DJ Quik on percussion and Young Guru contributing to the project’s mixing efforts. Just read the credits to each track and it’ll make you yearn for a documentary that focuses on the studio sessions. I would watch that. In the meantime, you can check out Billboard’s rankings of every track below.

articles.title: Insider insists he’s not trolling Notre Dame football fans with Indiana repeat pick
articles.summary: The 2026 college football season is just about 24 hours away from the official kickoff of Week 0. And with insiders, pundits, and college football program loyalists picking their favorites, a football insider has recently picked the Indiana Hoosiers over Notre Dame, and he has no part in trolling
articles._body: The 2026 college football season is just about 24 hours away from the official kickoff of Week 0. And with insiders, pundits, and college football program loyalists picking their favorites , a football insider has recently picked the Indiana Hoosiers over Notre Dame, and he has no part in trolling the Fighting Irish. Ahead of the kickoff, The Athletic’s Stewart Mandel, Bruce Feldman, and Ralph D. Russo laid out their sheets on who they think should outsell the rest of the football programs. However, according to Mandel, Indiana is the most probable side to win this season. “It took me until last year’s Big Ten title game — 25 games into Curt Cignetti’s Indiana tenure — to finally acknowledge the once-woeful Hoosiers were a full-blown juggernaut. Now I’ve fully swung in the other direction. Cignetti, like his one-time mentor Nick Saban, has the secret sauce to reload and remain dominant,” he said in his report. As he mentioned, Cignetti has had a historic run with the Hoosiers. Hired at the end of 2023, Cignetti helped Indiana break a program record with 11 victories and a playoff appearance in 2024, also his first year. Last season, during 2025, he led the Hoosiers to a 16-0 season run that ultimately resulted in Indiana’s first NCAA championship, defeating the Miami Hurricanes. “Indiana is strong on both lines of scrimmage and has three starter-level running backs, two stud receivers and DBs galore. New QB1 Josh Hoover might not be Fernando Mendoza, but Cignetti will have him ready to rock come Big Ten play. If I’m right, Indiana will become the Big Ten’s first repeat national champion since Minnesota in 1940-41,” Mandel further added. However, when Mandel had to answer if he’s trolling Notre Dame fans with his pick, he had a clear cut answer. “Absolutely not,” he wrote. “Clearly I’m all in on Marcus Freeman’s Irish in picking them to reach the national championship game for the second time in three seasons… But the Irish happen to draw Indiana in the championship game. Cignetti canceling the teams’ home-and-home and his snarky joke about it could absolutely blow up in his face.” A little different from how Mendel picked his favorite, Notre Dame is among the popular football programs to win a championship this season. Though football fans also want some rivalry action against Ohio State, the prediction and speculation market is running at an all-time high. Feldman, on the other hand, named Notre Dame as his pick for the championship. “With a lot of chatter in NFL circles about the winning coach becoming the hottest commodity on the carousel, Freeman’s Irish give fans their first national title since 1988, going 15-0. It’s not quite as much of a gauntlet as Indiana survived in its 16-game season, but Notre Dame folks couldn’t care less what everyone else might be thinking,” Feldman wrote. That being said, with college football action starting soon, fans will have a busy schedule juggling between pro and college games. articles.summary: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images
articles._body: Roxanna Scott is out as ESPN’s top editor after fewer than 10 months on the job, sources told Front Office Sports . Scott was named SVP, editor-in-chief last December . Her role was eliminated this week in a reorganization of the network’s news division and there will be a new editorial structure that ESPN brass feels will better support its newsgathering needs, a source said. Scott’s exit is not being characterized as being part of a new round of layoffs. An ESPN spokesperson declined to comment. ESPN had other shakeups in its editorial ranks last year when several editors left amid an investigation into HR complaints. The specific nature of the complaints was unclear. Former executive editor Cristina Daglas is currently working in the front office for the Wizards and Mystics . Elizabeth Baugh was sidelined amid the investigation and reportedly seen as a loyalist to Daglas. She left before the resolution, going to Ring magazine . Former NFL editor Heather Burns also departed the company and ultimately landed at USA Today . After spending a long time at USA Today and a brief stint at The Athletic , Scott was hired into her job by former ESPN EVP Dave Roberts. Roberts retired earlier this year and Mike Foss was promoted into the role of EVP, executive editor, sports news and entertainment. Will Dolly Parton Earn Her First Billboard 200 No. 1 Album Posthumously?
articles.summary: With Parton's streams exploding following national mourning over her death, she may shoot to the top of the chart for the first time — but the timing will make it tricky.
articles._body: Over the course of her incredible six-decade career as an entertainer, Dolly Parton racked up a stunning number of achievements and accolades — including two Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 singles, 10 Grammy wins (including the Lifetime Achievement Award) and induction to both the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and the Country Music Hall of Fame. But one that eluded the legendary late performer during her lifetime was a Billboard 200 No. 1 album. Parton was certainly no stranger to the chart, having racked up a whopping 50 entries on the 200 in her career, starting with the No. 184-peaking Just the Two of Us alongside Porter Wagoner in 1969. But despite reaching the listing’s top 20 nine times and the top 10 three times, she never found her way to No. 1 on the chart — getting closest with the No. 3-peaking Rockstar in 2023. But the book might not be completely closed on that. Following Parton’s death earlier this week, her streams have exploded, as a nation in mourning looks to celebrate her life and work once more. On Tuesday (Aug. 25), the day of her death, she was the second-most-streamed artist in the country, with her official on-demand U.S. streams up over 2,000% from the prior Tuesday — and those streams just continued to rise on Wednesday, to over 46 million, according to early data provided by Luminate. Those streams are resounding enough to make her one of the most-streamed artists of the whole week, despite the fact that she was only racking up a little over one million streams a day in the first few days of the tracking week (which starts on Friday). And as far as the Billboard 200 goes, most of those streams are counted towards her 2003 compilation Ultimate Dolly Parton . ( Billboard chart rules determine that individual song streams count towards whichever album collection they can be found on which is the highest-selling set for that tracking week; Ultimate Dolly Parton has sold nearly 6,000 copies so far for the tracking week ending Aug. 27, according to early data provided by Luminate, making it her current best-seller.) Ultimate Dolly Parton has history on the Billboard 200, having debuted at No. 130 on the chart upon its 2003 release, and returned to a new peak of No. 112 on the Jan. 19, 2019 chart. The compilation includes many of the Parton classics currently performing the best on DSPs, including “Jolene,” “I Will Always Love You,” “9 to 5” and the Kenny Rogers duet “Islands in the Stream.” Will the collective streams be enough to get the modest-selling set to No. 1 for next week? The greatest challenge it will likely have is in getting past The Sin: Bliss , the new set from K-pop male vocal group ENHYPEN . That sextet is also looking for its first No. 1 on the Billboard 200 — and has gotten even closer than Parton in the recent past, getting to No. 2 twice on the chart, including with this January’s The Sin: Vanish: 7th Mini Album . ( Bliss is available for purchase in a wide variety of physical and digital variants on the group’s webstore, and is expected to sell very well.) The timing is also not particularly working in the favor of Parton’s set, as news of her death came on Tuesday afternoon, with just two and a half days in the tracking week remaining — as Billboard ‘s tracking week runs from Friday to Thursday. Even if Ultimate Dolly Parton doesn’t ultimately have the sales numbers to get past ENHYPEN on next week’s chart, it still has a very good chance of finishing No. 2 on the listing — which would still be a new career-best for Parton. And if her streams remain strong through the next week, with a full week of increased streams to work with, it could be in contention for the top of the following week’s Billboard 200 as well, as more and more listeners discover and rediscover Parton’s classic catalog.

articles.title: Show HN: Repobeats – self-hostable GitHub activity cards in Rust
articles.summary:
Hi HN,

I built Repobeats, an open-source, self-hostable service that renders GitHub repository activity as embeddable SVG cards.

Demo: https://repobeats.com/AprilNEA/OpenLogi

Source:
articles._body: Hi HN, I built Repobeats, an open-source, self-hostable service that renders GitHub repository activity as embeddable SVG cards. Demo: https://repobeats.com/AprilNEA/OpenLogi Source: https://github.com/AprilNEA/repobeats I had been using Axiom’s Repobeats, but noticed that some cards I relied on were no longer updating consistently. The original service is still online; I wanted an alternative where I could inspect and control the collection, storage, caching, and rendering pipeline. Repobeats runs as a Rust backend built with Axum and SeaORM. A repository owner opts in by installing a read-only GitHub App. The service then collects commits, issues, pull requests, and repository metadata. GitHub installation tokens are short-lived and are never stored. The generated cards support multiple themes, sizes, and time ranges, and use ETags and cache headers for browser/CDN caching. For self-hosting, SQLite is enough for a small single-instance deployment. PostgreSQL is supported for multi-instance deployments, with optional Redis caching in addition to the in-process cache. One important constraint: repositories must explicitly opt in by installing the GitHub App. Cards are public once connected. This also applies to aggregate activity collected from private repositories, so private repository owners should only connect repositories whose aggregate activity they are comfortable exposing. The project is still early, and I’d especially appreciate feedback on: - the GitHub App installation and opt-in flow - the usefulness and design of the generated SVG - deployment and refresh scheduling across multiple replicas Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49481365 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

At one point in the broadcast, Lake Erie was shown. Michaels onl
articles._body: During the preseason game between the Cleveland Browns and the New England Patriots, announcer Al Michaels took a shot at President Donald Trump ‘s hope to change Lake Ontario to Lake America amid his trade dispute with Canada. At one point in the broadcast, Lake Erie was shown. Michaels only acknowledged it as Lake Erie before taking a shot at the president’s conversation about another lake’s name. “That is Lake Erie. We think it is still called Lake Erie… We’re not quite sure at this point,” he said. “But we’ll be by Lake something like Ontario or whatever it’s going to be called by the time we get to Buffalo. Anyway, you know what I’m talking about… Read the news.” Al Michaels: "That is Lake Erie. We think it is still called Lake Erie… We're not quite sure at this point. But we'll be by Lake something like Ontario or whatever it's going to be called by the time we get to Buffalo. Anyway, you know what I'm talking about… Read the news." https://t.co/95yBtkta2U pic.twitter.com/zqOHbR7sST — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) August 28, 2026 For those unaware, President Trump signed an executive order to rename Lake Ontario to Lake America. Clearly, Michaels wasn’t amused by his antics. It was an interesting night for Michaels and Kirk Herbstreit. They talked extensively about Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson, who was accused of sexual misconduct and assault by over 20 women. They appeared to rationalize some of his actions, such as calling out fans for being “disrespectful” for booing him . Michaels painted Watson as a once-great quarterback who was salvaging his career, downplaying his off-field controversies by saying he’s trying to “save a career that right now looks like it’s bottomed out.” Michaels doubled down by saying, “He’s got a chance to bounce back.” Herbstreit agreed with Michaels’ assessment, defending Watson for his press conference moment. He explained that the quarterback “kind of lost his cool.” “He kind of lost his cool after that game in Buffalo. If you put yourself on the field, and you think about — you’re in your home stadium, and obviously, it’s been a disaster, but you can see how a guy can lose his cool and say something like that,” Herbstreit said about Watson’s comments. Noah’s Notes: Black T-Shirts Are for Weirdos
articles.summary: Plus: a new tennis brand that’s doing everything right, and a bit of Supreme drop nostalgia.
articles._body: For most people, it’s new-clothes season. But I don’t believe in buying cold-weather clothing while it’s still hot out. I prefer a wear-it-out-of-the-store kind of shopping experience. Which means that all of the sweaters and outerwear I want will be sold out by the time I’m ready to buy them. Oh, well. Here are some things I’m thinking about right now. A confounding new brand that I love I’m not sure how I first encountered BbbLllAaaHaa , but I’ve been following the brand closely for about a year now, watching how satisfyingly consistent and cohesive it is and how quickly products sell out. I love everything about this brand: the opulent and overstated labeling, the tightly constrained collections often based on a single color of one fabric, the highly functional clothes, the strange name. What I like most about it, though, might be that it’s fully committed to a vision that is not at all obviously commercially viable. Everything in life is so overly optimized, strategized, and market-tested. Bbb just is. And it seems to be working. I’ll be clicking fast when this next collection drops. A watch that I never thought I’d want to wear A good brand makes you reconsider your own style choices. And everyone has a plastic watch coming out this week that made me nostalgic for the days when I hunted for vintage Swatches on eBay . I don’t wear a watch and had no intention of starting to. But here we are, and here I am making room on my wrist for everyone’s Mono Watch. everyone was founded in 2022 by Ryo Miyoshi , who was previously director of the great boutique 1LDK — a regular stop for me whenever I pass through Tokyo. As the name implies, the brand doesn’t have a particularly specific vision — just a very specific approach to developing product. This, to me, is the model for brands of the moment. Fuck storytelling and world-building. I’m so sick of it. Just make good clothes, make them meticulously, and treat them with dignity. A tennis brand that I actually like Shade was started by Miraj Patel — one of the founders of the nu-GORP label Gnuhr — as a response to his experience working for outdoor brands that were mostly concerned with efficiency and vibes and didn’t care much about overusing synthetics or creating an abundance of waste. Shade is a small-scale brand that does things only a small-scale brand can do: meticulous design and construction, limited runs of hand-numbered editions, and a visual identity that feels more like an art project. As he was developing Shade, Miraj — like many of us — fell under the spell of tennis. So, much of the clothing’s functionality and the brand’s imagery is centered on the sport. I’ve always preferred to wear “regular” tennis clothes when I play. Typically, that means adidas shorts (the 7” Climacool Ergo short is the best tennis short of all time imo) and any random vintage cotton tee. But I just got Shade’s long shorts , and I’m really into them. Great fabric, interesting construction that doesn’t sacrifice comfort or create a weird silhouette, and a raw hem with bar-tack stitching at various intervals along the side seams so you can cut them to your preferred length. All Shade garments come with some version of this customization option, which might sound kind of wonky and annoying (like, don’t make me decide how long the shorts should be) but is actually executed in a smart and cool way. The importance of ritual They’re saying that Supreme has returned to form . I’ve certainly clocked more people wearing the brand lately, and this week there was significantly more buzz around the new collection preview than there has been for a while. It’s interesting that Supreme’s stock rises and falls like this because the reality is that Supreme is probably the most consistent brand of the last 20 years. The quality of the product has always remained very high for the price, the “Fuck Em” attitude never changes, the referential design sensibility varies only slightly, the caliber of collaborations with artists and other brands is steady. And every new collection is released at the exact same time in the exact same way, twice a year. The cornerstone of Supreme’s collection rollout scheme remains the preview grid , a seemingly endless product labyrinth that reveals every item the brand will release in the coming season. Supreme started doing these standardized online previews and lookbooks in 2011, which was when the web store first expanded to cover the EU and UK. (Supreme didn’t even have a web store until 2006, which might sound like a long time ago but was actually very late.) I love the preview. I haven’t bought anything from Supreme in years, but I still click through every slide out of habit. Once upon a time I’d be screenshotting the pieces I was planning to buy. The rigidity and predictability of how Supreme managed these rollouts — air-tight, sending the same emails at the same time in the exact same format — turned pretty standard promotional marketing into a kind of ritual. And rituals became central to the success and identity of Supreme: the preview ritual, the drop-day ritual, the Nike and Vans and Timberland and North Face collaboration rituals. For rituals to be effective, they need to be imbued with some kind of deep cultural meaning. I’d like to know the traffic numbers on Supreme’s preview page leading up to the first drop to see if it still has it. I bet it does. A final thought You have to be a total weirdo to wear a black T-shirt. Not going to explain it.

With Clothes This Good, You Only Need One Collection a Year
articles.summary: With his eponymous brand, designer Ryan Morrow is putting out exceptional clothes at a steady pace.
articles._body: Ryan Morrow is on the move. It’s a Friday afternoon when I get on the phone with the Sydney-based designer, which means he’s heading out of the city and up Australia’s eastern coast for the weekend. As well as the coast, he’s been heading to the bush for years since moving to the harbor city from his native Northern Rivers, near Byron Bay. It was afternoons like these when he was P. Johnson’s head of design, leaving the city in a beautiful suit to then go and set up a tent, that gave him the idea for his eponymous label: clothes that reflect and comfortably serve both spaces. Some of the clothes you’ll find in his weekend bag are also what populated his first collection (or Capsule), which launched the brand last year. He checks off them off as solutions: “I’ll pack one rain jacket” — the Dry Jacket — “or something light and breathable I can throw on when it rains” — the crisp Fly Anorak – “and what am I gonna put on for a nice dinner that night when I’ve still got sea salt on the skin?” — the breezy Screen Shirt. “Considering each piece I’d pack in my bag for a weekend away, I like that idea of making them the best they can be.” With this modular framework, his archetypal shapes are already starting to emerge. I first encountered the brand at one of Morrow’s pop-up installations in a concrete gallery showroom where I tried his Dry Jacket on for size. With its raglan sleeves and storm flaps, it hung off my shoulders like a tent would, I imagine; its drape came from the treated polyester that gave off the polished fuzz of a peach. It’s since evolved in his sophomore collection, released this past Australian winter, into a cotton/nylon blend, keeping that drape but with a sturdier handfeel. There’s also its beefier sibling in the Loft Jacket, made in Italian cotton canvas and filled with Australian and New Zealand wadding. After Morrow’s years at P. Johnson, outerwear, he admits, is a category he wants the brand to excel in. In a city, you’re safe to throw either on without it reading as the incongruity some people approached with the Barbour jacket a few seasons back — which, here, is performative by comparison. Not bearing the weight of a heavy wax cotton, say, which is to know you’re about to go outside and do something , is how Morrow likes it. He traces this attitude back to his upbringing enamored by the surf brands that dominated the late-90s and early-2000s. “In the surfing culture I grew up in, it was about how you carried yourself and how you performed, not about how you talk,” he says. “I kind of carry that in the way I design where I want to have a nonchalance and an ease to things, but have this coolness that is authentic and it comes down to the fact that it’s real.” Working in his palette of natural colors — with names like Bark, Mud, Fern — is shorthand for his intended environment, yes, but one immediately favored by those in the overlapping circles of fashion, design and architecture — who also have a penchant for weekend-trips. But the clothes have found their way in other trades, too. Builders and carpenters have DM’d Morrow to tell him about the compliments they’ve received wearing their Dry Jackets on shift. An unexpected client, perhaps, but one that gets closer to his original idea: treating clothes like tools and equipment. With his eponymous label only a year old, Morrow is keeping it small and slow, packing his single yearly collections with updates to fabrics and forms. “It’s almost like I don’t love clothes enough just to make heaps of it,” he says. In terms of where he plans on taking the brand next, he’s think about what actual tools can fit in the Morrow world, namely through collaborations with makers of his camp equipment. First up, a folding pocketknife. “I’m looking at the objects in my life that articulate this niche and what I’m trying to do with the brand,” he says. “It’s for someone who thinks about the objects they put in their lives.” Highsnobiety has affiliate marketing partnerships, which means we may receive a commission from your purchase. articles.summary: It might be safe to say that Rory McIlroy won’t be winning the 2026 Tour Championship, barring a late stretch of dominant golf. As Round 2 is underway, McIlroy is now eight shots back of the lead, but his play is heading in the wrong direction. So far through four holes, McIlroy is two over
articles._body: It might be safe to say that Rory McIlroy won’t be winning the 2026 Tour Championship, barring a late stretch of dominant golf. As Round 2 is underway, McIlroy is now eight shots back of the lead, but his play is heading in the wrong direction. So far through four holes, McIlroy is two over on the day, moving his total score from -3 back to even after he birdied the first hole. The blunder came on the third, as McIlroy would score a 6 on the Par-4. Rory McIlroy: One of us pic.twitter.com/LA57YDnlwE — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) August 28, 2026 The 3rd hole was a disaster for Rory. After a miserable approach shot 115 yards out from the middle of the fairway, Rory needed an up-and-down from that slope to save par, as you saw in the video. After he failed to get it up the first time, he then needed to try to save bogey. He would then two-putt for the double bogey. It didn’t get any easier on the 4th. Rory would bogey this hole as well, seeing his chances of winning this tournament go down the drain. It would take a dominant back nine from Rory to see this turn around. He’ll need to see his even score rise to at least -4 or -5 by the end of the day if he wants to give himself a chance. There is too much talent among these 29 golfers. The winning score may reach close to -20, especially if Scottie Scheffler and at least a handful of others should be north of -10 heading into the weekend. When Rory is at his best, he is almost unbeatable. It will take that type of play for him to be crowned Tour Champion. He has a lot of golf left to play. We will see what he does with it. articles.title: College football rumors: Pat McAfee’s alleged beef with ESPN producer at forefront of ‘College GameDay’ change
articles.summary: The college football season is finally here, as Week 0 kicks off the new campaign on Saturday, August 29. However, with the season about to begin, it appears ESPN has made a big change with its “College GameDay” program with rumors potentially linking Pat McAfee to the decision. It
articles._body: The college football season is finally here, as Week 0 kicks off the new campaign on Saturday, August 29. However, with the season about to begin, it appears ESPN has made a big change with its “College GameDay” program with rumors potentially linking Pat McAfee to the decision. It’s said that ESPN is removing Jim Gaiero from “College GameDay” as a lead producer, according to Drew Lerner of the Awful Announcing. While there are several narratives regarding the decision, the one that stands out is the alleged beef between Gaiero and McAfee. “One of the lead producers of ESPN’s flagship college football program, ‘College GameDay’, has been taken off the show,” Lerner wrote. “Jim Gaiero, a veteran ESPN producer who has served as a lead producer on ‘College GameDay’ for 10 years, will no longer produce the show, multiple sources confirm to Awful Announcing. Matthew Garrett, a vice president of production at ESPN, is expected to take over as executive producer of ‘GameDay’. “Following publication of the story, Awful Announcing has learned of competing narratives as to why Gaiero was removed from ‘GameDay,'” Lerner continued… “Those who spoke to Awful Announcing believed that, at the very least, friction with Pat McAfee was factored into the decision, pointing to comments McAfee made on social media in October of 2025.” The “competing narratives” Lerner mentions are that ESPN is giving Gaiero a different role altogether, as he will lead the program’s production prep for Super Bowl 61. It is said Gaiero will play a major factor in ESPN’s golf strategy moving forward, and he will also command Thursday night college football games as a producer. If anything, it sounds like Gaiero got a promotion. Despite that, the timing of the decision is what is sparking rumors, as Awful Announcing’s sources claim decision-makers at ESPN typically do not operate like this. Those sources believe the incident when Pat McAfee voiced his displeasure about unnamed ESPN producers on social media back in October 2025 as the reason for the change. At least that’s what sources speculated to Lerner and Awful Announcing. “Those who spoke to Awful Announcing believed that, at the very least, friction with Pat McAfee was factored into the decision, pointing to comments McAfee made on social media in October of 2025,” Lerner wrote. The decision to remove Jim Gaiero from “College GameDay” is reportedly not sitting well with former Alabama Crimson Tide head coach Nick Saban. It’s said that Saban has a close relationship with Gaiero and he is not happy with ESPN’s decision. “College GameDay” will air on September 5 for Week 1 of the season. Pat McAfee and the crew will host the show in Baton Rouge, Louisiana for the Clemson Tigers-LSU Tigers game. articles.title: Our 10 favorite scenes from T2: Judgment Day
articles.summary: James Cameron's 1991 sci-fi blockbuster returns to theaters this weekend for its 35th anniversary.
articles._body: I'm on record declaring James Cameron's Terminator 2: Judgment Day (1991) to be The Best Damn Sequel of All Time, and I stand by that assessment. August 29, the fictional date (in 1997) of the franchise's original nuclear holocaust, is fast approaching, and Judgment Day is celebrating its 35th anniversary this year. So StudioCanal has decided to mark both occasions with a special theatrical rerelease of the film this weekend. What better time to revisit some of our favorite scenes from this seminal sci-fi action blockbuster? (Many, many spoilers below.) Nobody really expected 1984's The Terminator to be a hit, but it racked up an impressive $78 million at the box office against its modest $6.4 million budget. Star Arnold Schwarzenegger was keen to do a sequel, but Cameron was busy with other projects, including Aliens in 1986 (another killer sequel). There were also legal complications over the film rights until Schwarzenegger convinced Carolco Pictures, the studio behind Total Recall (1990), to buy everyone out and hire Cameron to make Judgment Day . articles.title: Trevor Lawrence gives flowers to Jaguars ‘grinder’ receiver
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars have been getting some good things out of their players in training camp and preseason, and that could prove to be big when the regular season arrives. On offense, wide receiver Parker Washington has caught the eye of many, and he recently had a solid joint practice again
articles._body: The Jacksonville Jaguars have been getting some good things out of their players in training camp and preseason, and that could prove to be big when the regular season arrives. On offense, wide receiver Parker Washington has caught the eye of many, and he recently had a solid joint practice against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Trevor Lawrence knows what he can do on the field, but also sees the work he puts in when he’s not practicing. “He’s a grinder. Sometimes he’s in here, like 5:00am, 4:30am. He’s in here crazy hours. I think he might sleep here,” Lawrence said to NFL insider Jordan Schultz. I asked #Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence about WR Parker Washington, who has been the star of training camp: "He's a grinder. Sometimes he's in here, like 5:00am, 4:30am. He's in here crazy hours. I think he might sleep here." pic.twitter.com/xGm8H1HASi — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) August 28, 2026 Whatever Washington is doing, it seems to be working, which is good news for him and the team. Washington has been with the Jaguars for four seasons, and last season was his best, finishing with 847 yards and five touchdowns. That’s something to build on going into his fourth year, and he can prove to be a reliable receiver once again. The Jaguars have a solid receiver core with Washington, Brian Thomas Jr. and Jakobi Meyers, and they should make Lawrence’s job easy. It was a big reason why they were able to make it to the playoffs last season, but they lost to the Buffalo Bills in the Wild Card Round. They’ll look to make a deeper push this season, and the hope is that they have the right pieces in place to do so. For Washington, if he can get all of his teammates up that early in the morning to get the day started, the Jaguars may be destined for ultimate success on the field. articles.summary: Nike 24.7 combines full-length Air Bubble cushioning, slipper-inspired comfort, and minimalist styling for effortless post-training recovery and everyday wear.
articles._body: Any amateur athlete, avid gym-goer, or all-round pro will tell you recovery is the unsung hero of great performance. As Kobe famously stated, great performance is about commitment. The Nike 24.7 embodies that, on and off the track. Whether recovering from a rigorous training schedule or looking for comfort after long commutes, we all need a little rest time. With its black suede upper and clean design, it’s clear that this shoe wants us to claim it. The model's foam body and easy lace system are indicative of Nike having taken design notes from slippers to enhance its comfort. From the seamless upper to its slide-adjacent slip-on feature, even the laces aren’t a barrier to intentional rest and recovery. From the ’95 to the Vapormax, the Air Bubble technology used here has been part of Nike’s DNA since its introduction. But in the case of Nike’s premier recovery sneaker , we’re getting more bubbles than ever before, with a chunky black full-bubble sole completing the look. The minimal design is distinctly fashion-forward, with Nike showing that even recovery can get the runway treatment. Bringing a new kind of effortlessness to the styling, the 24.7 in Black and Anthracite is built to support high mileage. Releasing alongside an extensive collection of loungewear, the 24.7 sneaker is the star in an ensemble cast of plush sweatshirts and lightweight long-sleeve shirts. Comfort guaranteed. Nielsen Warns Networks Against Mixing Metrics With Outside Data
articles.summary: Denny Medley-Imagn Images
articles._body: Already in the midst of large-scale changes for the new television season, Nielsen issued a reminder to networks that could have significant impacts during a frenetic upcoming sports calendar. The measurement agency told networks that “mixing internal or third-party data with Nielsen metrics to make comparative statements in the press is not permissible.” While that’s not a new Nielsen rule, networks have still done that to varying degrees for years when issuing viewership reports regarding their live sports programming. NBC, most notably, has regularly used its Total Audience Delivery (TAD) figures, which combine Nielsen’s Big Data + Panel measurements with digital data from Abobe Analytics. The issue came to a head this summer during the recent FIFA men’s World Cup , when Fox issued viewership releases using strictly Nielsen data, but the NBCUniversal-owned Telemundo relied on that TAD blend of Nielsen and Adobe figures, and also touted its rising appeal during the tournament with non-Spanish speakers . In the wake of that, Nielsen is now heightening its scrutiny around competitive claims made by networks using blended audience data. NBC did not immediately respond to a request for comment, though the network’s NFL press releases have not traditionally used TAD data for comparative purposes. Fox, meanwhile, is pleased with the Nielsen directive as each of the NFL’s rights holders will jockey for audience supremacy during a 2026 season with heightened expectations . “Hopefully this clear, fair policy will be rigorously enforced during football season,” said Fox Sports president of insights and analytics Mike Mulvihill in a social media post . Changing Landscape Beginning on Monday, Nielsen is implementing a series of large-scale changes to its audience measurement, led by an expansion of its co-viewing methodology . Those shifts, representing the third major pivot for Nielsen in less than two years, will be felt during a frenetic sports calendar in the next few months that includes the start of the college and pro football seasons, the MLB and WNBA playoffs, and the start of the new NBA and NHL seasons. Despite that effort to better capture television consumption that is already occurring, the NFL remains frustrated with Nielsen’s progress . The league said last week that Nielsen’s moves are “overly rushed,” and that it is amplifying efforts to work with rival audience measurement companies. “Our concern is that this is going to make measurement for the upcoming season muddled,” NFL SVP of data and analytics Paul Ballew told Front Office Sports last week. “It’s been a real struggle with Nielsen, and these latest changes raise even more questions for us.” Each of these Nielsen moves, including the new press policy, will be especially felt in and around the NFL, as it remains by far the most-watched programming in U.S. television . articles.title: Carlos Beltran admits he’s ‘not a big fan’ of Chase Utley’s ‘dirty’ play’
articles.summary: For 20 years, Carlos Beltran left quite the mark on the diamond. That led to Beltran’s induction into the Hall of Fame in January. He played with and against some of the era’s top players. One of those was Philadelphia Phillies second baseman Chase Utley. However, Beltran doesn’
articles._body: For 20 years, Carlos Beltran left quite the mark on the diamond . That led to Beltran’s induction into the Hall of Fame in January. He played with and against some of the era’s top players. One of those was Philadelphia Phillies second baseman Chase Utley. However, Beltran doesn’t think too kindly of Utley, per SNY Mets. He said that the man known as “Silver Fox” was a dirty player. “In the game of baseball, you can play hard,” Beltran said. “But when you play dirty, it’s a different element.” Carlos Beltrán is "not a big fan" of Chase Utley: "In the game of baseball, you can play hard. But when you play dirty, it's a different element." pic.twitter.com/wqvLmeVm2g — SNY Mets (@SNY_Mets) August 28, 2026 Over his career, Utley earned a reputation as an aggressive player. In the field and on the base paths, Utley had a few notable moments. In Game 2 of the 2015 NLDS, Utley slid into Mets shortstop Rubén Tejada’s late, trying to break up a double play. Tejada ended up with a fractured leg. Some criticized Utley and accused him of intentionally touching Tejada rather than sliding into second base. That incident led to the creation of the so-called “Chase Utley Rule.” It bans dangerous slides to protect middle infielders. Furthermore, the rule states that the slider must make contact with the ground first before reaching the base. Beltran and Utley squared off in the 2017 World Series between the Astros and Dodgers. The Astros, with Beltran, defeated Utley and the Dodgers in seven games. It was Beltran’s only World Series title. Utley played in MLB from 2003 to 2018. When Beltran was inducted into the Hall of Fame, Utley received 59.1% of the vote in his third year of eligibility. articles._body: Feature flags are common these days, and the .NET feature management library provides a lot of the plumbing to make them easy to get started with. The missing piece is a UI for managing flags - unless you are using Azure App Configuration. Relying on `appSettings.json` gets awkward when non-technical users need to change flags, deploys are slow, or the application is running in a distributed environment. I built FeatureFlags.app to fill that gap - a simple UI for managing .NET feature flags that doesn't require Azure App Configuration. It's still early, so I'd love feedback from anyone who has dealt with feature flags in .NET. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49480960 Points: 2 # Comments: 0

articles.title: The Week That Broke College Football: Everything to Know
articles.summary: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images
articles._body: Just over a week ago, a local judge in Baton Rouge handed down a temporary ruling that sent shock waves across college football: A group of NFL players could return to college this season. College sports has undergone plenty of change throughout the past six years, from unrestricted transfers to NIL and revenue-sharing rights. But the ruling opened up a previously unthinkable possibility that professional football players could somehow regain college eligibility. Two of the plaintiffs in that case, Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, were scooped up by LSU. If another plaintiff, Jack Pyburn, gets cut from the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, he’ll also return to Baton Rouge, according to court documents . Since then, other NFL players have scrambled to determine whether they, too, could return to college—and some have since filed lawsuits. Meanwhile, conferences fought back, announcing a wave of policies aimed at preventing pros from coming back to college even if the NCAA couldn’t. Players initiated legal action to strike down the SEC’s new policy; LSU is expected to support them. The situation has set up a seismic legal battle over whether conferences can enforce basic eligibility rules, like preventing professionals from returning—one that could have ripple effects across football and even the entire college sports landscape. How did this start? The legal battle didn’t actually begin as a lawsuit over allowing pro players in college football. It stemmed from a flood of cases filed by a specific group of players seeking a fifth year of college eligibility. In June, the NCAA passed a new “age-based” eligibility policy , allowing players five years to complete five seasons (up from four) starting when they enter college or their 19th birthday—whichever comes first. But the NCAA chose not to include players who entered school in 2022 and had already exhausted four years. So many of those players sued, arguing they should be grandfathered into the new policy—and they started winning. The Louisiana case is one of those lawsuits; it just so happened to also include players who tried to get roster spots on NFL teams. The lawsuit argues they never would have gone pro if they had known the NCAA would change its rule this summer. The judge agreed, saying the NCAA was not allowed to prohibit them from playing this season. But the judge also said these players had to terminate their NFL contracts and return any money they earned. Is this expected to set a new precedent across college football? No. The Louisiana ruling was specific to the players who signed on as plaintiffs—anyone else would have to file a separate lawsuit and obtain their own court order. Plus, because the case was solely about the one-time situation freshmen from 2022 found themselves in, sources across the industry told Front Office Sports they believed this NFL player–return situation would be a one-off . Currently, none of the players have actually ever played regular-season NFL football. Wright, Harris, and Pyburn, for example, all went undrafted. Harris signed with the New Orleans Saints but never played preseason games due to an injury; he was cut from the team Aug. 8. Wright secured a spot for the Cleveland Browns and played in preseason but was waived last week. Pyburn is still on the Buccaneers; he has said his focus is on landing a spot on the team, but that he could take his spot at LSU back if he returns. How did the conferences take action? Multiple conferences—including all power conference leagues—scrambled to hold meetings to implement conference-specific policies. The Big Ten was first , saying players could not return if they went through the NFL Draft process as underclassmen without properly withdrawing, signed any NFL contract (including a preseason contract), or were listed on an NFL roster. Players could, however, return if they were automatically entered into the Draft and didn’t get chosen. They can also return if, as undrafted free agents, they participated in NFL “rookie minicamps,” a specific set of tryouts after the Draft, but didn’t get signed. Players in this situation include UCLA’s Trent Hendrick (part of the Louisiana lawsuit) and Texas’s Cole Hutson (who filed his own case). The SEC, Big 12, and ACC all implemented similar policies throughout the week. Each conference has its own set of penalties, ranging from coaching suspensions to hefty fees. Wright, Harris, and Pyburn would be ineligible according to all four power-conference policies. But can conferences enforce these policies if the NCAA can’t? At this point, it’s unclear. The question could be answered by the LSU situation with Wright, Harris, and potentially Pyburn (as well as men’s basketball player RJ Luis Jr. ). In the hours following the announcement of the SEC’s policy, Wright’s representation told FOS they still expected LSU to sign him. Then, on Wednesday, Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry weighed in, telling FOS he was in support of LSU’s position to sign these players. “Don’t hate the player,” he said , “hate the game.” School officials have declined to comment since then, but the players fully intend to battle it out with the SEC in court. They notched a small win Friday, when the judge in the Louisiana case expanded the temporary restraining order to enjoin the SEC as well as the NCAA, according to court documents obtained by FOS . A separate lawsuit filed Thursday in Dallas , which also includes players from NFL preseason camps, also named the SEC and commissioner Greg Sankey as defendants alongside the NCAA. A temporary restraining order issued in favor of players in that case also named the SEC. What’s the NFL’s position? The NFL has not taken a formal stance on whether it believes players who participated in preseason should be allowed to return to college. But the league said players who leave the NFL preseason for college football would not be able to come back to their team during the same season, FOS previously confirmed . In addition,

When speaking about Brock Boeser, NHL analyst Travis Yost has stated that Vancouver should trade him to gain more assets. “Boeser is 29, coveted around th
articles._body: With the 2026-27 NHL season weeks away, the Vancouver Canucks are committed to the rebuild, as they attempt to climb back to contention. When speaking about Brock Boeser, NHL analyst Travis Yost has stated that Vancouver should trade him to gain more assets . “Boeser is 29, coveted around the league, and playing on a team that’s going to get worse before it gets better. Given the fact we have likely seen his best years already, does the timeline of keeping Boeser around make sense, or is he the coveted trade asset you cash in on to accelerate the quality of this rebuild?” Yost asked in his column. Boeser had 22 goals and 48 overall points in the 2025-26 season over 75 games. Ultimately, this was similar to the 50 points he had in the previous season. It was just a year ago that Boeser signed an extension with the Canucks . However, with the team in a rebuild, they could opt to trade him. Boeser’s best season came in the 2023-24 campaign, when he scored 40 goals and 73 points while missing just one game. Significantly, he has not come close to that mark in any season. With teammates like Elias Petterson also linked to other teams, there is a chance the firesale in Vancouver could take full effect this season. Currently, the biggest challenge might be convincing a team to give multiple assets while also committing to the $7.25 million cap hit that comes with it. If the Canucks get off to a bad start, the rumors of a trade will intensify, and Boeser could see himself out of Vancouver. articles.title: Flock is going from the center of the surveillance debate to bipartisan target in record time
articles.summary: Two Arizona cities cut ties with the license-plate reader camera company hours apart, as Senators Sanders and Hawley took aim from Washington.
articles._body: In a country increasingly divided along political ideologies, partisan politics are coming together to answer the age old dynamic between privacy and security. On Wednesday, the blue-leaning Tempe, Ariz. turned off its Flock automated license plate readers and said the city would not seek another company to replace the system. Three hours later, the nearby red-leaning town of Cave Creek did the same. The same day in Washington, D.C., Senator Josh Hawley, a Missouri Republican, opened a formal investigation into the company, while independent Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders posted a lengthy statement pledging to introduce legislation against it. Tempe’s police department had used Flock’s cameras to help solve crimes, and the city said its own audits, conducted monthly, turned up no misuse. But that wasn’t enough to keep the system running. “These cameras have helped our police officers do their jobs, and we don’t discount that,” Tempe Mayor Corey Woods said in a statement shared with Fortune . “But the risk of misuse is too great. We have to be able to provide public safety in a way that maintains the trust of our community. For Tempe, that means taking these cameras down.” Tempe Councilmember Bobby Nichols said the decision was a matter of legal principle. “Any law enforcement tool used by the City must not pose a risk of infringing on residents’ civil liberties,” he said. “We have a responsibility to ensure that these technologies are only employed if they present a narrowly tailored solution to a compelling government interest.” The city’s contract with Flock was worth $80,000; its cameras will remain in place until Flock removes them, though they have stopped collecting data. Any data that was previously collected is stored temporarily and then deleted automatically unless it’s tied to an open case. Tempe already cut off automatic data sharing with other law enforcement agencies earlier in August and launched a public transparency portal, which will now be discontinued. “Every day, police departments across the country are solving countless serious crimes and making a measurable public safety impact with Flock technology, including as the city shared, in Tempe,” a Flock spokesperson told Fortune . “When a tool that is actively helping solve violent crimes, locate suspects, and find missing people is removed, public safety moves backward. That has real consequences: cases will take longer to solve, organized retail theft crews will operate with fewer obstacles, an Amber Alert may not be returned home, and victims may wait longer, or indefinitely, for justice.” The spokesperson added that misuse of Flock’s technology is unacceptable, and that every search is logged and reviewed through the company’s Audit Assistance tool, which flags unusual activity for administrators to review. Cave Creek’s decision , three hours after Tempe’s, cited privacy concerns, cases of misuse elsewhere in Arizona and around the country, and the theft of one of its own Flock cameras from an intersection. Public works crews removed the town’s remaining cameras for safekeeping after the theft. But the town’s core objection was structural: Flock’s networked design allows outside law enforcement agencies to search data collected locally, and town officials concluded there was no way to guarantee residents’ privacy once their information left Cave Creek’s jurisdiction. The town manager and town attorney are set to formally address the decision at a Sept. 1 council meeting. Officials from Cave Creek have not yet responded to Fortune’s request for comment. Reading between the [partisan] lines Tempe leans Democratic: roughly 63% of its voters back Democrats, making it one of the more reliably blue cities in a state that has been a purple battleground lately. Cave Creek, a small, affluent town north of Phoenix, leans Republican by comparison. The two towns landed in the same place, becoming at least the ninth and 10th Arizona municipalities to drop or restrict Flock in the past year, following Chandler, Surprise, Pinal County, Sedona, Flagstaff, Sierra Vista, South Tucson and Apache Junction. In the nation’s capital, Hawley, who chairs the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism, sent a letter to Flock CEO Garrett Langley announcing an investigation into the company’s “collection, retention, and dissemination” of data gathered by its cameras. The letter argued that Flock has built an “unprecedented national surveillance network” of more than 120,000 cameras across 49 states, scanning more than 20 billion vehicles a month, and that “Congress never authorized the network your industry has built.” He gave the company until Sept. 8 to turn over documents. A Flock spokesperson told reporters the company intends to cooperate. Hours later, Sanders posted a statement of his own on X, describing Flock as part of a system that risks tipping the country into what he called totalitarianism. He also pointed to the number of Flock’s cameras, adding that newer versions of the technology can match images of people and vehicles against databases of phone numbers, relatives and court records. “We must come together to stop Flock and AI mass surveillance,” Sanders wrote. “That is why I will soon be introducing legislation to do just that.” Hawley and Sanders sit at opposite ends of the Senate’s ideological spectrum. Their statements arrived within hours of each other, echoing the same split-screen convergence playing out in Arizona. Flock’s rapid expansion, and the scrutiny now following it, has moved fast. articles.title: Ella Langley Subtly Responds to Doja Cat Claiming ‘I Don’t Know What That Is’ About the Country Star
articles.summary: The rapper previously clarified that she simply isn't a country fan, but thinks Langley has a "pretty voice."
articles._body: Ella Langley is showing she has a good sense of humor after Doja Cat claimed she didn’t know who the Billboard chart history-making country artist was. Related Yasuhisa Hara's 'Kingdom' Vol. 80 Tops Billboard Japan Book Hot 100 Doja Cat Appears Not to Have Any Idea Who Ella Langley Is: ‘I Don’t Know’ Will Ella Langley’s ‘Choosin’ Texas’ Pass Mariah Carey’s ‘Christmas’ for the All-Time Hot 100 Record for Weeks at No. 1 — And Then Just Keep Going? In a Thursday (Aug. 27) post on Instagram featuring photos and videos from her recent travels and performances, Langley appeared to lightheartedly poke fun at the rapper’s comments about her by writing in the caption, “Ella Langley? What is that?” The post itself wasn’t related to Doja, with some slides showing Langley on an airplane and others capturing the Alabama native getting her makeup done, holding a butterfly or cuddling with an adorable dog. It comes a few days after the “Say So” artist guested on Sundae Conversation and, with her signature candor, responded to a question about whether she was a fan of Langley’s with, “I don’t know what that is. Ella Langley?” After her initial comments were met with disbelief from fans, Doja said she listened to Langley’s record-tying 19-week Billboard Hot 100 -topping smash “Choosin’ Texas” for the first time on a livestream. The hip-hop hitmaker acknowledged that Langley has “a very pretty voice,’ but ultimately said that she just doesn’t “give a f–k about country music.” “I don’t understand what’s so hard to believe about that,” Doja continued on the stream. “I never cared. I like that one Keith Urban song from 2004. I wouldn’t say that I like [Langley’s] music; she’s probably a fine lady. I don’t care for that type of s–t at all. It doesn’t inspire me, it doesn’t make me feel good.” “This is not my vibe, but she has a very pretty voice,” she added. “If this is No. 1 on the charts, I’m sure it’s on the radio. I could see them playing this s–t on the radio. I don’t like it, but that’s fine. It’s very earwormy it sounds like, it’s like catchy melody. I get it, and she’s pretty.” But while Doja isn’t a fan of “Choosin’ Texas,” it’s clear that countless other people are. The song recently tied Lil Nas X and Billy Ray Cyrus’ “Old Town Road” for second-most weeks at No. 1 on the Hot 100. If it remains at the top for another seven days, it’ll tie Mariah Carey’s “All I Want for Christmas Is You” for the longest reign at the chart’s summit.
