articles.title: Texas Football: 3 Games That Should Be on Your Radar, Not Named OU, A&M or Ohio State
articles.summary: The Texas Longhorns have one of the hardest schedules in the country in 2026. Here are some notable games that may quietly decide the season.
articles._body: Our very own Tyler Horka broke up the three tiers of Texas football’s schedule last week. Now it’s my turn to break it down further by early, middle, and late. With so many marquee games for Texas, it’s been hard to narrow down to just three that can play a pivotal role in assessing Texas’ prowess at each point. The Longhorns will face seven ranked teams this season in On3’s preseason poll — No. 1 Ohio State, No. 8 Oklahoma, No. 9 Ole Miss, No. 10 Texas A&M, No. 12 LSU, No. 20 Tennessee and No. 25 Florida. Interesting note: The Coaches and AP polls both tabbed Missouri at No. 25, with Florida just missing the mark. By season’s end, the Longhorns potentially will have faced eight ranked teams. Each game selected comes from three areas of the season — early, middle and end. With so many marquee games for Texas, it’s been hard to narrow it down to just three that can play a pivotal role in assessing Texas’ prowess at each point. Tennessee Volunteers – September 26 – Week 4  While the G6 opponents that come to DKR early in the season — Texas State and UTSA — are important for depth guys as their shot to get reps in a live game, under Sarkisian, the Longhorns have had no problems, aside from last season’s hiccup against UTEP, taking down their non-conference G6 opponents. Unlike the previous two seasons, Texas will not stay at home or have a bye week to prepare for its brutal conference schedule. This is largely due to the SEC’s move to a nine-game conference schedule, eliminating that fourth “cupcake” game that is crucial for starters to get rest before the slog of conference play.  Time will be tight for the Longhorns to pick their wounds against Ohio State and rally against UTSA to be in a good spot for their first trip to Neyland Stadium and face Tennessee in the early TV window. Tennessee brings in the 26th-ranked transfer class, a majority of it overhauling its defensive unit. Like another SEC team on this list, the Volunteers have a glaring issue: starting a young, inexperienced quarterback— easy pickings for a loaded Texas defense to force mistakes. This will be an early judge of all of the preseason confidence Texas has exuded in player media availabilities in a great, hostile environment. Pressure around the game will be high if the Longhorns drop one to Ohio State. A loss in Knoxville puts them essentially in the same position as last year – two losses heading into Red River.  Florida – October 17 – Week 6 The Longhorns have developed a nasty habit of having too much fun at the Texas State Fair during the Red River Showdown. Impressive beatdowns have only made the “Red River Hangover” hit even harder the past two seasons. When Texas looked like the world beaters in Dallas just a week prior, the inverse reared its ugly head just seven business days later — Georgia in 2024 and last season’s overtime sweater in the Bluegrass State. Yes, Florida is one of the many teams that can be hard to pinpoint: Who will be QB1? How’s the offensive line going to shape up? Is the defense going to be competent? Jaden Baugh and Dallas Wilson are major boosts on offense to solve some of their prevailing issues. Regardless of how good or bad Florida ends up, this is a very scary game. Shades of last season, much? It’ll be a great opportunity to see how much maturity this iteration of Texas has if they can take care of business in a trap-game situation. LSU – November 14 – Week 10 One of the early contenders for the games of the year, if both teams live up to expectations. The Longhorns will make their entrance at one of the grand palaces, Tiger Stadium, for the first time in program history. The storylines are even better than the environment. It’s going to be Lane Kiffin and Sarkisian facing each other on the field once again, a duo that coached some of the great teams in the 21st century together. Sarkisian has a chance to even the series, with Kiffin getting the better of him twice when the two were coaching in the Pac-12 in the early 2010s. And the obvious: Arch Manning returns to Louisiana for a chance to break his family’s 3-3 stalemate against the Tigers on their own turf. New LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt will also get another crack at the Longhorns after the thrilling 2024 Peach Bowl. The third CFP rankings of the season will be released on the following Tuesday. It will be intriguing to see how much weight the game holds for the CFP committee if either team picks up its first or second loss.

articles.title: Cubs get big Matt Shaw update before stretch run
articles.summary: The Chicago Cubs know that this is one of the most important parts of the season, and they’re going to need all hands on deck if they want the best positioning when the postseason arrives. Matt Shaw is one player who hasn’t been on the field for the Cubs in the past two months as [
articles._body: The Chicago Cubs know that this is one of the most important parts of the season, and they’re going to need all hands on deck if they want the best positioning when the postseason arrives. Matt Shaw is one player who hasn’t been on the field for the Cubs in the past two months as he’s dealt with a sprained left hand , but he’s working his way back. He’s played in a few rehab games with Triple-A Iowa, and it looks like the team is ready for him to take the next step as he’s been reinstated from the 10-day injured list. This is good news for the Cubs, and the hope is that he can play a vital part for the team for the remainder of the season. Before he was placed on the IL, he was batting .246 with six doubles, two triples, four home runs, 2o RBIs and a .737 OPS in 56 games. The Cubs are hoping to get healthy at the right time, but there are still some players they’re hoping to get back. Ben Brown has recently dealt with some neck issues, and it’s uncertain when he’ll be back on the field. That’s a hit to the bullpen, and it would be next man up for the Cubs in that regard. Nonetheless, the Cubs have shown fight throughout the injuries, and they’ve found themselves in the perfect position for a playoff spot. It’s going to take a lot for them to pass the Milwaukee Brewers for the top spot, but it’s not all the way out of the picture just yet. Patriots’ most agonizing roster decision looming on 2026 cutdown day
articles.summary: The New England Patriots didn’t know it at this time last year, but they were in an advantageous position as the 2025 season got underway. They had finished last in the AFC East in 2024 and the team’s modest goals included approaching the .500 mark. Instead, the pairing of Mike Vrabel
articles._body: The New England Patriots didn’t know it at this time last year, but they were in an advantageous position as the 2025 season got underway. They had finished last in the AFC East in 2024 and the team’s modest goals included approaching the .500 mark. Instead, the pairing of Mike Vrabel at head coach and Drake Maye gave the Patriots a formidable combination. Their fourth-place schedule also helped quite a bit. As a result, the Patriots zoomed past the .500 mark, put together a 10-game winning streak and beat out the heavily favored Buffalo Bills for the division title. They continued to play well in the postseason, dominating the Los Angeles Chargers and Houston Texans at home before going on the road and beating the Denver Broncos in the AFC Championship Game. Historically speaking, the victory by Vrabel and Maye in the Mile High City in a postseason game is something that Bill Belichick and Tom Brady never accomplished. While the Patriots ht an immovable wall in their Super Bowl defeat against the Seattle Seahawks, they clearly have a solid team that should be a legitimate postseason contender again this year. The Patriots have the major challenge of having a target on their back after their worst-to-first finish last season as well as a first-place schedule that includes a trip to Seattle to open the season, but there is talent up and down the roster. What there may not be is adequate depth as the Patriots hope to get the best of the Bills again and try to assert themselves in the AFC. Vrabel has been concerned with the overall depth throughout training camp, and the biggest concerns are on defense. Defensive roster decisions likely to have critical impact Specifically, where does the pass rush come from outside of Harold Landry, and which of the edge rushers on the team can support first-year defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr’s game plan? The other area is the secondary. Christian Gonzalez is one of the best cornerbacks in the NFL, but he has had a difficult time this summer. Both injury and contract negotiations have kept him from showing off his immense skills. Vrabel explained his absence midway through camp. “Christian was unavailable, physically unavailable for the practice,” Vrabel said , per the Patriots media department. “That’s the clarification. Just like other players that I told to have treatment, and everybody has a plan here, there were other guys that were in that same category. If you want to list the names, Christian Elliss, Brenden Schooler, Harold Landry, Christian Barmore, et cetera. So make sure they’re all included. They were all in the same group of what they did.” Gonzalez and the team still have not finalized a contract that is likely to make him the highest paid cornerback in the game. That should still happen — but it is troubling that a deal has not been finalized. Carlton Davis will start opposite Gonzalez and Marcus Jones will be the nickel back, but there are issues once the Pats get past that trio. Kindle Vildor has had an impressive training camp and he and Karon Prunty, a rookie from Wake Forest who was selected in the fifth round, are the likely backups. Prunty’s rookie status helps him here as well as his aggressive play on special teams probably gives him the final advantage. However, he will still have to prove it on the field. He makes the roster over Channing Canada, Brandon Crossley, Marcellas Dial Jr., Kobee Minor and Charles Woods. Pass rush is a major concern Mandatory Credit: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images The Patriots got the bulk of their pass rush last year from edge rusher Harold Landry as he led the team with 10.5 sacks. They are clearly depending on Landry to perform in that role again this season, but it may be a while before last year’s knee injury allows him to play. He has not been ruled out of the season opener against the Seahawks, but insiders are not optimistic about Landry’s return in that game. It seems more likely that he will be back for the Week 2 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers or Week 3 against the Jacksonville Jaguars. If he is not back by then, the Pats could be in trouble. The Patriots are counting on Elijah Ponder and rookie Gabe Jacas to step up. Ponder made the team a year ago as an undrafted free agent and he contributed 24 tackles, 4.0 sacks and 2 fumble recoveries. That was solid considering his status, but can he do enough if Landry can’t play? Jacas was a second-round pick in this year’s draft, but he has a long way to go and is still playing catch-up. He is not likely to hit his stride until the second half of the season. Hard-trying players like Bradyn Swinson, Quintayvious Hutchins and Xavier Holmes are unlikely to make the final roster, and cutting those players will be agonizing for the coaching staff. articles.title: 5-star DL Kellan Hall locks in gameday visit with Kentucky
articles.summary: One of the best high school football players in the entire country will come to Lexington in a couple of weeks. Kellan Hall, the nation’s No. 2 overall class of 2028 recruit, is a 6-foot-5, 275-pound defensive lineman out of Louisville (KY) Christian Academy. According to our friends at Rivals
articles._body: One of the best high school football players in the entire country will come to Lexington in a couple of weeks. Kellan Hall , the nation’s No. 2 overall class of 2028 recruit, is a 6-foot-5, 275-pound defensive lineman out of Louisville (KY) Christian Academy . According to our friends at Rivals, he’s locked in 10 gameday visits for the fall — one of them with the Kentucky Wildcats. Hall will be on campus for the first big game of the Will Stein era when UK hosts No. 13 Alabama on Saturday, Sept. 12 at Kroger Field. Hall, a five-star talent, will visit a different school basically every weekend throughout the entire college football season. Kentucky’s competition is loaded with big-name programs (and notably, no mention of nearby Louisville). Oklahoma is currently viewed as the favorite, with the Wildcats not far behind. Sept. 5 | Oregon Sept. 12 | Kentucky Sept. 19 | Oklahoma Sept. 26 | Georgia Oct. 3 | Texas A&M Oct. 10 | Ohio State Oct. 17 | Michigan Oct. 31 | Texas Nov. 7 | Notre Dame Nov. 21 | Tennessee As of last week, Hall is officially down to a dozen schools . Miami and LSU are also among his finalists, but do not currently have gameday visits on his schedule. NEWS 2028 No. 2 recruit Kellan Hall has locked in his game-day visits for the fall, @SWiltfong_ reports Read: https://t.co/boIPHAhqTc pic.twitter.com/jl0b2ketVC — Rivals (@Rivals) August 28, 2026 Stein has still yet to coach a game for Kentucky, but he and his staff have done a terrific job recruiting the homegrown talent thus far. Hall came to Lexington for an unofficial visit in February , where he met with Stein and other UK coaches. He returned with his family for a spring practice visit in March . That relationship has been growing ever since. While the Sooners appear to hold the edge, Kentucky has put itself in a good spot. An impressive debut season for Stein could swing this recruitment in the Wildcats’ favor. “Certainly,” Rivals’ recruiting expert Steve Wiltfong said last week when asked if UK can land Hall. “I think they’re closer to the top of the list with what Will Stein and this new coaching staff has been able to do, the energy that they’ve injected into the program. I think Kellan Hall and his family believe the Wildcats are on the right track.” These gameday visits will be important for Hall. Kentucky pulling off the upset over the Crimson Tide in Week 2 would be massive. Green was drafted by the Cleveland Browns in the sixth round of the NFL Draft in April and got his first taste of action against the New England Patriots in the third and final game of the preseason. articles.summary: Najee Harris is expected to make his New York Giants debut against the New York Jets for the 2026 preseason finale. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported that Harris is expected to receive his first game action with the Giants tonight. It will also mark the running back’s first appearance since tearing h
articles._body: Najee Harris is expected to make his New York Giants debut against the New York Jets for the 2026 preseason finale. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported that Harris is expected to receive his first game action with the Giants tonight. It will also mark the running back’s first appearance since tearing his Achilles in Week 3 of the 2025 season with the Los Angeles Chargers. Harris has endured a lengthy rehabilitation process, and returning to a game setting represents an important step toward being available for Week 1. The Giants will want to evaluate his movement, confidence, and ability to operate within their offense. New York should not need to give him a heavy workload. A few carries or passing-game opportunities could be enough to help Harris regain his rhythm without unnecessarily pushing him in his first action back. It may not even be that many reps. The Giants do have other backs they want to look at before making the roster decision next week. His appearance could also offer an early indication of how the Giants plan to use him during the regular season. Harris built his reputation as a physical and dependable runner before the injury, but it may take time for him to return to his previous workload. A healthy Harris is very elite. The results against the Jets will be less important than how Harris responds physically afterward. If he completes his scheduled snaps without a setback, the night should be considered a success. For Harris and the Giants, getting him back onto the field is the biggest victory of all. The post Is Giants’ Najee Harris playing in preseason game vs. Jets? appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Former linemen impressed by new Alabama OL coach Adrian Klemm
articles.summary: Alabama GM Courtney Morgan and Joe Moore Award founder Aaron Taylor praised Adrian Klemm and his impact on the Crimson Tide offensive line.
articles._body: Courtney Morgan is biased when it comes to Alabama’s new offensive line coach. The Crimson Tide’s general manager has known Adrian Klemm since the former was working at a football skills training company, almost 15 years ago. Klemm recommended then-UCLA coach Jim Mora to hire Morgan as the Bruins’ director of player development for the 2013 season. The two men reunited this offseason, as Kalen DeBoer hired Klemm to coach the offensive line, and Morgan, who is entering his third year as Alabama’s GM, had high praise for his old friend. “He’s one of the best coaches I’ve been around, and I played the position,” Morgan said on Hey Coach . Klemm is back in a familiar role after spending the 2025 season as a defensive analyst at USC. The new offensive line coach has served stints at UCLA and Oregon, as well as in the NFL with the Pittsburgh Steelers and New England Patriots before making his way to Tuscaloosa. One of three new assistant coaches at Alabama, Klemm has been tasked with turning around an offensive line that didn’t meet expectations, which is why a change in leadership was made.  After 30-plus official practices, the group is beginning to look a little different. Joe Moore Award founder and College Football Hall of Famer Aaron Taylor attended one of the Tide’s practices, and the first thing that he noticed was how detail-oriented Klemm was during his drill work. But there was also a much more physical approach to what the offensive linemen were doing. “This unit wants to come downhill and come off the football,” Taylor said . “Last year was a little bit more lateral shuffling, double under, marrying your hips. When you do that, your feet stop. There was none of that at practice. It was running off the football, accelerating on contact, good use of hands with inside leverage. “… Every single player of the 10 that went through the two deep and a couple of the threes that went used their hands to punch. They started the fight.” Klemm’s ability to not only coach his players but also to teach them the fundamentals has been highlighted by his new colleagues since he arrived at Alabama, with Morgan being the latest. “One thing I know in my history and working with Coach Klemm is that his players love him,” Morgan said. “He’s going to coach them hard, but he’s going to love them up. And he’s a great teacher, he’s a great teacher.  “And I think you can see that when you come out to practice, you’re seeing the growth of our offensive line from Practice 1 to Practice 16, 17. They’ve gotten better, and they’re going to continue to get better. And they like playing for him.  “I think the offensive line, they’re very talented. They’re young, but they’re talented. But we have talent. So at the end of the day, you got a great coach, you have talented players, and you have a chance.” Alabama struggled to run the football in 2025, ranking 125th out of 136 FBS teams in rushing offense (104.13 ypg). But DeBoer addressed it this offseason by bringing in Klemm and 11 new linemen, including six transfers. The hiring of Klemm could prove pivotal to the Tide’s success. “Alabama will run the football, and it’ll be the hiring of Adrian Klemm and his impact — assuming that they can stay healthy — that will have Alabama back in the playoffs,” Taylor said. articles.summary: Taylor Zdrojewski scored her third goal of the season off a pinpoint ball from Emma Torres as Texas Tech responded to a late Pepperdine goal and earned a 1-1 draw. The Red Raiders dominated the second-half attack but lacked consistency in the final third in front of a program-record 2,971 fans.
articles._body: Texas Tech found the response it needed after conceding a late goal Thursday night, but lacked enough consistency in the final pass or finish to turn a dominant edge in shots into a win as the Red Raiders settled for a 1-1 draw with Pepperdine in front of a program-record 2,971 fans at the John Walker Soccer Complex. “If we were missing anything tonight, it wasn’t the goal-scoring touch,” Texas Tech head coach Tom Stone said. “It was the final pass, final decision, final choice to cross or shoot or pass or shoot, and the quality just wasn’t there for us tonight.” The Red Raiders outshot Pepperdine 13-2 in the second half and earned seven corner kicks after halftime. That pressure frequently carried Tech down the flanks and into dangerous areas, but too many attacks ended without the final ball needed to test Waves goalkeeper Jillian Medvecky. Tech finished with a 16-5 advantage in shots and earned 10 corner kicks to Pepperdine’s two, but placed just four attempts on frame. “We were on the doorstep, but I think only four shots on frame, and that’s not enough to beat a team like Pepperdine,” Stone said. Despite spending much of the second half defending, Pepperdine broke through first in the 78th minute. A moment of hesitation around the top of the box allowed the Waves to pounce on a loose ball before Kyra Murphy found Kate Ryan for the opening goal. Pepperdine’s lead lasted just three minutes. The goal immediately brought a different urgency out of the Red Raiders, who generated three of their four shots on target during the final 13 minutes. Kaitlyn Giametta forced two saves from Medvecky during the closing stretch, while Taylor Zdrojewski provided the equalizer in the 81st minute. Emma Torres created the goal with a pinpoint ball into the box, finding Zdrojewski in front of the net for her third goal of the season. “It definitely felt like something we practiced before and something that I know Emma’s capable of,” Zdrojewski said. “She hit the perfect ball and I was in the right spot. I’m glad that we were able to combine.” Torres continued to show why she has emerged as one of Tech’s most creative attacking players. The sophomore repeatedly challenged Pepperdine defenders off the dribble, including a pair of nutmegs, and produced the moment of quality Tech had lacked for much of the night. “She is so slippery and creative, and she loves the art of the dribble and loves to get people off balance,” Stone said. “It’s very instinctual. She’s just got a real natural flavor to her that is hard to defend.” Torres said the desperation Tech showed after falling behind needed to arrive earlier. “Once we were down 1-0, we were like, ‘We can’t lose. We don’t lose here.’ I think we really needed to get that goal to get us back in, but I think it should have come earlier.” Stone described Tech’s late push as creating “a ton of chaos” around the Pepperdine box. While that chaos produced the equalizer and multiple chances to find a winner, it also highlighted how different the Red Raiders looked once the possibility of their first loss became real. “The truth is they could see the game slipping away and didn’t want it to be that way,” Stone explained when asked what the change was. “They did not accept that, which is the part I love about this squad.” Zdrojewski was proud of how the Red Raiders responded, even if it did not produce the result they wanted. “I’m proud of the team that we had to fight to keep fighting after going down. I know that this team is a team that will always fight to the last whistle, and that’s what our fans got to see today. Unfortunately, our fight just wasn’t enough to get the result that we wanted.” The match could have taken a much different turn in the first half if not for a remarkable reaction from Addie Todd. A deflection off one of her own defenders sent the ball toward the top of the net, but Todd exploded out of her set position to tip it off the crossbar before collecting it and preventing an own goal. “You never expect the ball to go off your own player and about to roof you,” explained Stone. “Her time to see it, react to it and explode was nothing. It was zero. She just literally lifted off like a rocket, tipped it into the bar and back down and fell on it.” Todd finished with three saves, all in the first half, to keep Tech level while Pepperdine enjoyed its best stretch of the match. Both teams entered the night unbeaten and receiving votes in the national poll. The draw moved both teams to 2-0-2. All in front of a record-setting crowd came just four days after more than 1,800 fans attended Tech’s home-opening victory over Boise State. This time, nearly 3,000 fans packed the John Walker Soccer Complex to establish a new high for the program. “It was a night to remember, and we are fortunate to be playing in that environment,” Stone said. “That’s two games in a row, and we’re going to try to keep them coming back.” Texas Tech will return to action Thursday when it travels to Dallas to face SMU. articles._body: Delaware surged down the stretch and landed a commitment from one of the nation’s most dynamic quarterbacks on Friday. Four-star Class of 2027 quarterback Julian Reese committed to play for the Blue Hens just hours before kicking off his senior season at Amarillo (Texas) Palo Duro . Delaware edged past UTEP, Delaware, UNLV, and Houston for the No. 28-rated passer in the country. Reese accounted for more than 3,000 yards passing with 31 passing touchdowns and 12 more rushing touchdowns in 12 games as a junior. He added almost 500 more yards on the ground as well. He’s stoked about his opportunities at Delaware. “Delaware is on top for me because of the way the players and coaches made me feel. It was like they’ve known me forever,” Reese told Rivals of his decision to commit to the Blue Hens on Friday, after evaluating his finalists for most of the summer. “They make it feel like home by the way they treated me … it was like they had been knowing me my entire life. I feel like I fit in at Delaware because of the schemes they run … it’s very similar to my high school’s, so it will pretty much be the same thing I’m doing now,” he continued. “I also feel like Coach (Ryan) Carty believes that I can be the face of the program. It just feels like home to me.” The multi-sport athlete from West Texas was a top performer at the Rivals Camp in Nashville. Rivals Director of Scouting and Rankings Charles Power raved about Reese’s performance in the camp setting. “Reese is an elite athlete for the position and showed encouraging passing ability,” Power wrote. (He is) re currently on the cusp of four-star status with Rivals.” As a junior, Reese passed for 3,053 yards with 31 TDs compared to 3 INTs. He added another 449 yards and 12 TDs rushing. He also landed 2 INTs in snaps at defensive back. Houston and Wake Forest loved the four-star QB at safety.

Bitcoin Drops Before Shrugging Off Fed Chair’s Inflation Comments
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Drops Before Shrugging Off Fed Chair’s Inflation Comments Bitcoin dropped, then popped after Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh gave his first major speech as head of the U.S. central bank and said he had “more work to do” to fight inflation.  The leading cryptocurrency was recently trading for $79,474 after dropping as low as $78,630 before quickly rising again.  Bitcoin has typically done well in a low interest rate environment but the Federal Reserve has been reluctant to lower borrowing costs due to sticky inflation in the world’s biggest economy.  “But on the price-stability side of our mandate, the numbers are more concerning,” Warsh said after talking about employment.  He added: “We must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to our objective, clearly and at sufficient speed. Otherwise, we have work to do.” Bitcoin has in the past dropped on news that the Federal Reserve thinks inflation is too high because it means less chance of a rate cut. Following Warsh’s speech, traders priced in a 50% chance of rate hike in September.  But Bitcoin has appeared to — at least for now — shrug off the speech.  Bitcoin’s started surging last week after the U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced the department would double the size of its long-dated bond buybacks.  The news sent yields down lower, and the dollar slid while non-yielding assets like bitcoin and gold jumped.  Positive regulatory news also helped the coin: President Donald Trump last week said that the long-awaited crypto Clarity Act was a “very, very powerful” piece of legislation, and urged lawmakers to get it over the line.  The proposed law will establish a framework for distinguishing between digital assets that are securities, commodities or payment stablecoins — legislation that the crypto industry has long called for.  The Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City is on Friday holding the annual event at Jackson Hole, Wyoming, where central bankers, Federal Reserve officials, policymakers and academics will gather to discuss “Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy.” According to the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City website, this year’s event will touch on how “recent years have seen a dramatic increase in innovation in financial intermediation and payments,” including new technologies such as “cryptocurrencies and stablecoins.”  This post Bitcoin Drops Before Shrugging Off Fed Chair’s Inflation Comments first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo .

With Babcock on board, Edmonton has made another coaching hire, according to Oilers.com. “We are excited to ha
articles._body: Last month, the Edmonton Oilers hired Mike Babcock to be their newest head coach. The Oilers 2026-27 season will rest on how he does, and how the coaching staff guides the players. With Babcock on board, Edmonton has made another coaching hire , according to Oilers.com. “We are excited to have Misha (Donskov) join our coaching staff. We believe his wealth of experience, people skills and professionalism will make our group better. We look forward to the positive impact he will have on our staff, players and the Oilers organization,” Babcock told Oilers.com. Donskov will act as a coaching consultant. Ultimately, he will only appear at home for a few select days a month for the Oilers. Donskov will also continue to serve as Hockey Canada’s Vice President of Hockey Operations. Likewise, he will continue to serve as the head coach for the National Men’s team. Donskov has NHL experience as an assistant coach with the Dallas Stars from 2023 to 2025. Prior to that, he spent seven seasons as the Director of Hockey Operations with the Vegas Golden Knights. Before that, he was a team consultant with the Columbus Blue Jackets and Atlanta Thrashers, as well as an assistant coach with the London Knights and Ottawa 67s. With Babcock managing the top talent in Edmonton , the team will have another experienced voice. As the Oilers attempt to win the Stanley Cup , they will go all out to ensure it happens. Donskov will bring over 20 years of combined experience to give the Oilers all the help they need. Ultimately, as the Oilers attempt to keep Connor McDavid, the pressure will be on the team to perform at the level many believe they are capable of. Meta makes AI glasses slightly less creepy with limit on nonconsensual recording
articles.summary: Meta fixes AI glasses to stop recording any time users cover up the safety light.
articles._body: Meta is rolling out an obvious fix to make its AI glasses less creepy amid backlash over the glasses' non-consensual recordings that have flooded the Internet . On Friday, The Verge reported that Meta closed a loophole that made it easy for smart glasses users to cover up an LED light that is supposed to alert bystanders that the device is actively recording. Meta had previously deactivated recording if a user attempted to start capturing video after placing a sticker over the light, but people quickly learned that they could get around that by reversing the order of the steps and covering up the light after they started recording. In a post on Threads, Meta’s executive vice president of wearables, Alex Himel, explained that an update would be rolled out soon that ensures that “the camera will now stop working if the light is covered during a recording." That way “the capture LED can reliably alert bystanders when photos or videos are being captured for someone’s gallery,” Himel said. Read full article Comments

articles.title: An 87-year-old American billionaire bought the first Ferrari Luce for $40 million, and the purchase could save him $13 million in taxes
articles.summary: Dr. Herbert A. Wertheim, an optometrist and philanthropist with a $4.8 billion net worth, bought the EV earlier this month. It had a presale estimated cost of $1.1 million.
articles._body: The American billionaire who bought Ferrari’s first electric vehicle model for an eye-watering eight figures may be able to cash in on a tax write-off perk from the purchase.  Earlier this month, 87-year-old optometrist-turned-businessman-turned-philanthropist Dr. Herbert A. Wertheim bought a Ferrari Luce at a Sotheby’s public auction for $40 million . The auction was part of a charity effort to benefit the Ferrari Foundation, which funds global education initiatives. The $40 million buying prices on the auto was more than 36 times the model’s presale estimates of $1.1 million. (The Luce retails for $640,000, but the auctioned car had a higher price tag because it had a pre-production chassis.) Now, it seems Wertheim may end up getting a large chunk of that purchase back, as part of a longtime American tradition of the country incentivizing the nation’s wealthiest philanthropists into giving back. Large charity donations like Wertheim’s can lend themselves to massive tax write-offs as a result of America’s tax system. Automotive content creator and television presenter Peter Greaves first brought attention to the potential for Wertheim to gain millions back on the purchase of his Luce in a recent Youtube video. When Wertheim files his 2026 taxes, he would have to subtract the estimated sale value of $1.1 million from the $40 million the car sold for. As of the IRS’s 2026 tax rules, he would then have to take away a 0.5% floor of his adjusted gross income, which Greaves estimated to be $200 million, leaving $37.9 million. The U.S.’s 2/37ths rule created under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which caps tax savings of itemized deductions at 35% compared to the previous 37% for top earners, would further reduce the sum to $35.85 million. According to tax law, 37% of that total could be claimed, meaning Wertheim could receive more than $13 million back from the U.S. government for his purchase. Wertheim, who did not immediately respond to Fortune ’s request for comment, has made no public comments about possibly taking advantage of the tax write-off for the Luce, or for any previous charity auction purchases. The philanthropist has an estimated net worth of $4.8 billion and has previously participated in a previous charity auction for luxury vehicles, reportedly paying $26 million for the Ferrari Daytona SP3, or “599+1.” He has donated more than $200 million to various causes, including  $50 million to UC Berkeley Optometry and $100 million to Baptist Health Foundation. In February, Wertheim paid $2 million at a Mar-a-Lago charity event for a private visit with President Donald Trump at the White House. It’s not his only recent brush with politics: Wertheim briefly launched a Congressional bid in Florida’s 22nd District earlier this year. For its part, the Maranello, Italy-based carmaker has weathered controversy around the rollout of its EV. Former Ferrari president and chairman Luca di Montezemolo joined analysts and investors in mocking the model as ugly and decidedly un-Ferrari-like at a time where other luxury automakers were scaling back their own EV efforts amid low demand. Ferrari may be getting the last laugh however: the Financial Times reported last month that Ferrari exceeded its short-term sales goal of 500 units.  How the Trump administration transformed charity tax breaks  Tax breaks for philanthropy is an American tradition dating back to 1917 after the passage of the War Revenue Act , in which Congress created a federal income tax deduction for charitable gifts as part of an effort to keep private philanthropy alive and well during World War I, which would relieve the U.S. from funding essential social welfare programs. Those benefits have slowly expanded over the last century. But the Trump administration has made it more for the wealthy to get money back for their donations come tax season, with the One Big Beautiful Bill Act effectively slashing the benefit from 37% to 35%, with itemized taxpayers having to deduct donations only in excess of 0.5% of their adjusted gross income. The policy changes with lower tax incentives may alter the future of philanthropy itself. The new 35% limit could reduce donations by between $4.1 billion and $6.1 billion , according to the Indiana University Lilly Family School of Philanthropy. Experts warn that fewer big donors—or big donors giving less—would place a larger burden on middle-class givers to bridge a gap that isn’t realistic as financial pressures for less-wealthy households increase . “The nonprofit sector says that every dollar matters, and so incentivizing small donations from every household could have a meaningful impact for certain kinds of organizations,” Elena Patel, co-director of the Urban-Brookings Tax Policy Center, told CNBC last November . “But the truth is that those kinds of contributions, however, just are not the bulk of charitable giving in the charitable sector. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles._body: Four months after being released by WWE , former Superstar Zoey Stark has landed a new gig in TNA, debuting on the latest episode of Impact. During the Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026, edition of Impact, Stark made her debut in TNA as a heel, attacking another former WWE star, Indi Hartwell. She debuted under the ring name Zoey Serrano. Serrano is her real last name. She has gone by Zoey Serrano since rejoining the indies after her WWE release. It's OFFICIAL – @ZoeyStarkWWE has signed with TNA! #TNAiMPACT pic.twitter.com/6W6HEoYcqn — TNA Wrestling (@ThisIsTNA) August 28, 2026 TNA later confirmed the signing , making it clear that she is a full-fledged member of the roster. It appears she will be feuding with Hartwell upon her debut. Zoey Stark’s WWE career before her release Joe Camporeale-Imagn Images. Before joining TNA, Stark was in WWE from 2021 to 2026. She was released while on a hiatus from her knee injury. Stark suffered a knee injury in May 2025 in a Money in the Bank-qualifying match against Kairi Sane and Rhea Ripley. That would be her final appearance in WWE. She was released in April 2026, ending her five-year tenure with the company, before she had made her return from injury. She returned to the independent circuit after her WWE release. Stark would get to reunite with her former WWE tag team partner, Shayna Baszler, in Revolution Pro Wrestling. Now, she appears to have found a home in TNA. TNA and WWE frequently work together. Perhaps she will make a return to her former employer at some point. During her WWE tenure, the only title she won was the NXT Women’s Tag Team Championship, which she won with Iyo Sky, who was known as Io Shirai at the time. While on the main roster, Stark was mostly a midcard talent. She started as Trish Stratus’ sidekick in her feud against Becky Lynch in 2023. Eventually, she would go off on her own and begin teaming with Baszler. However, they never won tag team gold. articles.title: Kirk Cousins is obvious Raiders QB1 over Fernando Mendoza, and that’s OK
articles.summary: There are things Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza can learn from Kirk Cousins. And Cousins isn’t worried about not being named QB1 yet. But Cousins is the obvious choice over Mendoza, and that’s OK. Cousins said he’s taking things in stride, according to a Raiders post on YouTube. “
articles._body: There are things Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza can learn from Kirk Cousins. And Cousins isn’t worried about not being named QB1 yet. But Cousins is the obvious choice over Mendoza, and that’s OK. Cousins said he’s taking things in stride, according to a Raiders post on YouTube. “I think it’s just up to Coach,” Cousins said. “You do the best you can with the opportunities you’re given. Lead as well as you can. Compete. You’re never a finished product.” Raiders will lean on Cousins’ experience It’s pretty obvious that Mendoza isn’t ready to be thrown into the fray. It wouldn’t do the Raiders any good at this point. There’s not a great chance for the Raiders to win football games this year. So that would go against Mendoza’s career mark. It’s not so much about protecting his win-loss record. But it matters. If he can wait until Week 8 or so, he will have a much better feel for what goes on in the games. And that will give him a better chance to be successful. In the final preseason game against the Raiders, Mendoza entered the game in relief of Cousins after the veteran played the first two drives. Mendoza saw tons of pressure and didn’t have a great game. He finished with seven completions in 14 attempts for just 51 yards. He also had an interception. Another reason to keep Mendoza on the sidelines is the offensive line is OK — but not ready to protect a rookie quarterback for four quarters while he learns on the fly. The Raiders aren’t great along the line, but rather average. They are ranked No. 18 in the NFL, according to Pro Football Focus. “The Raiders made Tyler Linderbaum by far the highest-paid center in football, and he should have a huge impact on their ability to run the football,” Gordon McGuinness wrote. “The former first-round draft pick has earned PFF pass-blocking grades below 65.0 in each of the past two seasons but PFF run-blocking grades above 80.0 in three of his four seasons in the NFL. “Look for this to be an ascending group in 2026 and one with serious potential to move up these rankings throughout the season.” Kirk Cousins gives the Raiders a safety net Cousins has been in every tough situation you can imagine in the NFL. He knows how to survive at the quarterback position even when things are not ideal. The Raiders can lean into that for at least half of the season, if not more. And who knows? If Cousins leads the Raiders to a 4-4 start, he might stick around as long as they are legitimately in the playoff chase. But that’s unlikely to happen. Cousins is the placeholder. And actually, he’s a good placeholder. The Raiders did the right thing to bring him. That gives them a chance to move Mendoza into the starting lineup at their own pace. And at Mendoza’s pace. There’s no rush here. And that’s a good thing for the Raiders and this quarterback situation. Kelley
articles._body: An Alpha Kappa Alpha member just won Miss USA and made history in the process. Miss Virginia USA Justus Kelley won the Miss USA pageant on Thursday evening, becoming the first mother to ever win the title, as well as becoming the first married woman to win and the first winner in her 30s. Kelley is 31 and married to Tyler Kelley. View this post on Instagram The win comes after Miss USA lifted its restriction that prohibited contestants who were mothers and over the age of 28 from competing, restructuring its guidelines to allow women over 18 to compete. Per E! News, Kelley’s win netted her a $150,000 salary during her time as titleholder, along with a one-year lease on a luxury Miami apartment, a Range Rover, a Westgate vacation home club membership, a Miss USA wardrobe valued at $30,000, and additional prizes. She spoke about her victory in a video posted by Miss USA on Instagram. “I’m Justus Kelley and I just won Miss USA 2026. This opportunity means the world to me, and not only are we celebrating the 75th anniversary but we made history tonight. I’m the first married woman, first mom, and first woman in her 30s. It’s a great night.” Kelley is a member of Alpha Kappa Alpha and was initiated into the Tau chapter at Indiana University, where she served as president from 2016 to 2017, according to information obtained by Watch the Yard. She also competed in the Alpha Phi Alpha Miss Black and Gold pageant during her time at the institution, which she shared in an interview with Empowerment with Elizabeth. In July. She said that the Alpha Phi Alpha-organized event was her first foray into the pageant world. Founded by nine collegiate women at Howard University in 1908, Alpha Kappa Alpha has since expanded into one of the world’s largest Black Greek-letter organizations, now counting more than 355,000 members across 12 countries. articles.title: Yankees rumors: New York planning unsurprising Brian Cashman decision
articles.summary: While the New York Yankees are busy wrapping up the 2026 campaign, the organization has some decisions to make regarding the front office. Brian Cashman is in the final year of his contract, and rumors suggest the club is on the verge of doing the obvious. The buzz in the rumor mill suggest the Y
articles._body: While the New York Yankees are busy wrapping up the 2026 campaign, the organization has some decisions to make regarding the front office. Brian Cashman is in the final year of his contract, and rumors suggest the club is on the verge of doing the obvious. The buzz in the rumor mill suggest the Yankees are planning to bring the 59-year-old general manager back for next year and beyond , according to Jon Heyman of the New York Post. Although there has been noise from the fanbase to move on from Cashman, the franchise appears to be on the verge of extending Cashman, as the team is in the middle of a 29th winning season with him in the GM role. “Yankees GM Brian Cashman’s contract is up, and yes, there’s no reason to believe he won’t be extended again,” Heyman wrote. “This may disappoint some ring-thirsty Yankees fans, but his 29th straight winning season is secure. And that ain’t easy.” The Yankees initially promoted Cashman to general manager back in 1998 when he was just 30 years old. New York went on to win three-straight World Series with Brian Cashman leading the front office (1998, 1999, 2000). The club won a fourth title with Cashman as general manager in 2009. Despite the Yankees remaining competitive all these years, the team has failed to win another championship since that 2009 season. The World Series dry spell has been a gripe for Cashman, as it’s the reason why part of the fanbase likely won’t be happy when the organization seemingly gives him an extension. It’s not entirely clear when that deal could come to fruition, but based on Heyman’s claims, fans shouldn’t be shocked when it’s announced. In the meantime, the Yankees will continue playing the 2026 campaign. New York begins a four-game series against AL East rival the Boston Red Sox on Friday. articles.title: Kevin Warsh finally threw Wall Street some crumbs on what he’s thinking: ‘There is one signal nobody can miss: 65 months of elevated inflation’
articles.summary: But make no mistake: “We should not indulge a regime in which market participants are looking primarily to the Fed for their next trade.”
articles._body: Wall Street hadn’t heard a peep out of Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh for a month, until he walked onstage for his keynote speech at Jackson Hole today. Warsh’s speech at the Fed’s annual gathering came with added scrutiny this year : Not only was it Warsh’s first as chairman, but he has also caused analysts some discomfort with his pullback from giving now-familiar forward guidance (in which the central bank indicated the general direction of travel for the base interest rate). On forward guidance, Warsh stuck to his guns , saying: “You might know about my longtime discomfort with early pronouncements of future policy decisions … Forward guidance as a regular practice was adopted by my colleagues—and me—during the Global Financial Crisis. It was essential at the time, and we introduced it with much fanfare. “But as with other legacies of crises past, I believe the practice has outstayed its welcome. In normal times, the role of forward guidance should be limited and circumscribed; otherwise, it risks creating ambiguity in the name of clarity. Oversharing policy deliberations and overcommitting to future decisions can lead markets, businesses, and households astray, and I believe when policymakers make quasi-commitments on interest rates throughout the cycle, we inhibit our own freedom to make the right calls when it’s time to decide.” His tone was firm: “We should not indulge a regime in which market participants are looking primarily to the Fed for their next trade.” And while Warsh has repeated his commitment to the Fed’s dual mandate of inflation at 2% and maximum employment, neither he nor his central bank staffers are living under a rock: Bond yields tracked higher following Warsh’s July press conference, as markets digested a Fed on hold and the suggestion that markets may be doing some of the legwork for financial tightening that they had come to expect from the Fed. But more alarmingly—for some corners of the street— were the questions hanging over the established frameworks the Fed uses to make decisions about the base rate. Analysts questioned if these frameworks might be subject to change, searching for answers on how policymakers were thinking, even if they didn’t know what action it might prompt. Here, Warsh shared insights. While his outlook on the economy wasn’t necessarily rosy, it nevertheless described the balance of priorities within the Fed. Price stability is front of mind, he suggested, in the balance of risks in the Fed’s mandate. He said: “But on the price-stability side of our mandate, the numbers are more concerning. The Fed’s preferred measure of inflation, the 12-month change in the PCE [personal consumption expenditures] price index, stands at 3.7%, while the six-month change is 4.1%. “None of these measures are perfect, but they all tell a similar story: Inflation is running above our 2% target. So the Fed’s predominant focus right now should be on prices.” The employment side of the Fed’s mandate is doing “well,” he said, courtesy of a robust consumer and a “rematching” of employers and employees after the COVID pandemic. He added: “As of now, I believe the labor markets are broadly consistent with full employment, but on the price stability side of our mandate, the numbers are more concerning.” With speculation swirling as to how actively the Fed will commit to its mandate, Warsh moved to nix concerns: “There is one signal nobody can miss: The responsibility for 65 months of sustained, elevated inflation sits squarely with the central bank. And that is where it belongs … I stand here today committed to a discipline, not to a decision. My Fed colleagues and I are hardly the first to hold these positions in a time of great consequence. We are determined to redeem the time by doing our very best work. “We take our responsibility seriously, with humility and with resolve. So much depends on choices we make. Sound monetary policy helps households and businesses to prosper. When carried out effectively, it broadens and deepens the momentum of our economy … and helps to secure America’s leadership in the world. And I know that our country needs us to think carefully and act wisely.” Warsh’s latest speech (at the time of writing) seems to have sidestepped any sharp reaction from markets: the price of gold—a safe-haven asset relied upon during times of volatility—dropped by approximately 1% during Warsh’s speech. The VIX volatility index also declined 1%, while longer-dated Treasuries also lowered. The CME FedWatch index, which tracks Fed fund futures, shows 57% of traders believe the Fed’s next rate move in September will be a hike of 0.25%, to the 3.75% level. Early reaction from analysts suggests Warsh learned from the pushback earlier this summer. Eric Winograd, chief U.S. economist at AllianceBernstein, wrote that while the Fed chairman’s speech was light on details of central bank transformation, it did “correct a couple of mistakes he made at his last press conference, reinforcing that PCE is the target measure for inflation and that interest rates are the Fed’s primary tool. “Those corrections make the speech hawkish compared to his last remarks and should offer some relief to the back end of the yield curve, where some worries about Warsh’s willingness to act with rates to bring inflation down contributed to rising yields.” ‘The productivity pixie’ One thing some Wall Street analysts—unusually—didn’t want to hear too much about was AI. As UBS’s Paul Donovan quipped ahead of the speech: “The worst case would be a reiteration of Warsh’s belief in the productivity pixie, and platitudes about future higher growth. Technology’s impact on macroeconomic productivity is uncertain, and risks of a ‘brain drain’ from the U.S. and lower immigration also affect growth.” The boomerang central banker hit on the topic early, but with questions rather than expectations as to how it might shape the Fed’s mandate. articles.title: Bulls’ plan with new analysts to fill Stacey King’s place
articles.summary: The Chicago Bulls will enter the 2026-27 season with a huge void. They will not have the beloved Stacey King in his analyst seat in the broadcast booth. In June, King unexpectedly passed away at the age of 59. The cause of King’s death was cardiovascular disease. As a result, the void is gr
articles._body: The Chicago Bulls will enter the 2026-27 season with a huge void. They will not have the beloved Stacey King in his analyst seat in the broadcast booth. In June, King unexpectedly passed away at the age of 59. The cause of King’s death was cardiovascular disease . As a result, the void is great and will be hard to fill. On Friday, the Bulls announced their search , albeit begrudgingly, to find the next Stacey King, if that’s even remotely possible, per Ryan Glasspiegel and Michael McCarthy of Front Office Sports. They are looking to bring on a rotation of analysts for the season. One name being floated is Robbie Hummel. Hummel is a former basketball player at Purdue. He played from 2007 to 2012 and was a two-time All-American. Afterward, Hummel played for the Minnesota Timberwolves from 2012 to 2017. He has also done work as a college basketball commentator for ESPN and the Big Ten Network. He has also filled in for Bulls games from time to time. However, even though there is mutual interest, Hummel is unlikely to take the Bulls job full-time because of his current position, per Jeff Agrest of The Chicago Sun-Times. King played for Chicago from 1989 to 1994. He was part of the first Bulls three-peat teams from 1991 to 1993. Beginning in 2006, King was a color commentator. Along the way, King became a popular fixture whose catchy one-liners and fan-like demeanor made him one of a kind. In truth, he can never be replaced. All they can really do is hope for the best. articles.title: Noah Cyrus Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton: ‘Dolly Was a Rainbow … She Was An Angel Among Us’
articles.summary: Miley Cyrus' younger sister said she wanted the "Flowers" singer to have the first chance to eulogize the country legend who died at 80 on Tuesday (Aug. 25).
articles._body: Noah Cyrus posted a loving tribute to late country icon Dolly Parton on Thursday (Aug. 27) in which she noted that she waited a beat to allow older sister, and Parton’s goddaughter, Miley Cyrus , to share her thoughts first. Related See the Best Dolly Parton Musical Tributes, From Harry Styles, Katy Perry, John Mayer, Jack White & More Why Is the New Tropical Storm Spinning Up in the Atlantic Called ‘Dolly?’ It’s Not What You Think Dolly Parton Wasn’t Eligible for Song of the Year Grammy for ‘I Will Always Love You’ for This ‘Unforgettable’ Reason In a post featuring a number of classic, glamorous images of Parton — including one of her sharing a mic with the sisters’ dad, singer Billy Ray Cyrus — Noah wrote , “i wanted the first words you heard to come from miley, and now that she’s spoken, i’d like to share a few words about dolly.” The 26-year-old singer then shared what so many people have said about the iconic country singer who died on Tuesday (Aug. 25) at 80 after a short battle with cancer, that she was a unique, and uniquely kind individual the likes of which we may never see again. “dolly was singular, one of a kind. dolly was a rainbow to our world for nearly six decades, and no one could ever come nor will ever come close to replacing her,” Cyrus wrote. “her impact on the world, and on me as an artist, is unparalleled. she was an angel among us who not only wrote songs that spoke to us all, but whose kindness, compassion, and empathy toward those who truly needed it were at the core of who dolly was.” She continued, “she never forgot where she came from, and she never stopped being her true self. she made it her duty to help others, not only through her music, but through her kindness and her commitment to helping those in need. her beautiful relationship with my family, especially my sister, is one i will be grateful for my entire life. i am so grateful to her for inspiring me to be who i am, wear those wigs, have those long nails, to write my stories, and to heal people through music.” Miley was equally emotional in her post on Wednesday (Aug. 26) in a tribute to her “Aunt Dolly,” whose loss she said she was struggling to put into words. “Our most sacred moments were private and they’ll stay there behind the stage, beneath the glamour & between our hearts,” Miley wrote. “What I KNOW is Dolly would want me to feel it, write a song about it, and then continue on and be strong,” she continued. “I have an angel by my side. I always have. One of our last conversations was about music and metamorphosis.” Cyrus pledged that she will “always love her and want to make her proud,” adding that “we’re in this loss together.” Noah’s post — which ended with an emotion-packed clip of Miley and Dolly duetting on “I Will Always Love You” — concluded with heartache and joy. “i am heartbroken she is gone, but only physically. she came into this world, shared her light, and changed it forever,” Noah wrote. “she will now live in our hearts, and her music will continue to be a friend when lonely, and to celebrate with happiness. it will inspire and encourage young songwriters that will discover and learn from the Great Dolly Parton. Dolly, you got your wings. we will ALWAYS love you. 🦋🦋🦋.” The Cyrus’ were among the many friends, family and peers who have expressed their love, admiration and sadness about the loss of the generational singer who transcended genre, led with her heart and spread joy for over six decades.

articles.title: Bruins’ Marco Sturm reveals plan for young players in 2026-27
articles.summary: The Boston Bruins will be heading into the 2026-27 season looking to build on some of the things they were able to accomplish last year. They’ll have some new players joining the roster, one that includes 19-year-old James Hagens, who was selected seventh overall in the 2025 NHL Entry Draft
articles._body: The Boston Bruins will be heading into the 2026-27 season looking to build on some of the things they were able to accomplish last year. They’ll have some new players joining the roster, one that includes 19-year-old James Hagens, who was selected seventh overall in the 2025 NHL Entry Draft. Though Hagens has experience playing in different leagues, he’ll be heading into his first NHL training camp, which could be a different beast. That’s where he’ll show what he’s really made of, and head coach Marco Sturm has a plan set in place for Hagens, as well as the other young players who want playing time this season. “They have to show me first. The player for me always dictates how much they want to play in certain situations… and if Hagens shows me that he’s ready for that next step, I will give him that. I’m not that dumb. It’s tough to explain a little bit and it’s just again with my experience working with young kids and being through it and now being here and acutally being through it with the Khus and Mints and these guys it’s just helps me and Hagens will be another guy,” Sturm said Bruins on CLS. Marat Khusnutdinov and Fraser Minten happened to be two players that fought their way into the rotation last season, and they did it by playing hard and showing up. The hope is that the same can happen with Hagens, as he has the talent to be on the ice, but he has to apply it. It sounds like Sturm will give him every opportunity to earn his playing time, but he has to take it and own it. articles.title: Karol G’s Complicated and Relatable Heartbreak Brought Her Back to the Top of the Charts (Critic’s Take)
articles.summary: Here's why the Colombian star’s ‘No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto’ ended Bad Bunny’s run at No. 1 on Top Latin Albums.
articles._body: It took a whole lot of heartache to bump Bad Bunny’s Debí Tirar Más Fotos and its title track off the No. 1 spots on Billboard ’s Top Latin Albums and Hot Latin Songs chart. But Karol G did it. Not with hardcore perreo or the female empowerment anthems that have become her trademark, but with the vulnerability of a broken heart. Karol G’s No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto (I’m Not Sorry for Feeling So Much) debuted at No. 1 on  Billboard ’s  Top Latin Albums  chart (dated Aug. 22), putting an end to Bad Bunny’s reign on top with Debí Tirar Más Fotos , which hadn’t moved from the top spot since Jan. 24. All told, that album has spent a record 77 nonconsecutive weeks atop the chart, and could easily claim that spot again. Not this week, though: Karol G’s Me Arrepiento holds firm at No. 1 for a second week (on the Billboard 200, the album dropped from No. 8 to No. 11). And on top of that, the Colombian star has also continued to hold “DtMF” from the top spot on Hot Latin Songs. There, Karol G claimed the top spot last week with “Ahí,” featuring Drake, and this week, she did it again with a different song — “Bby WOW” — featuring two Spanish up and comers: singer-songwriter Judeline and producer-keyboardist rusowsky. It takes a lot to move Bad Bunny from any position of dominance. That Karol has managed to do so with unconventional pairings and unconventional music (for her) says a lot about the rarified position she’s carved for herself in today’s pop music landscape, able to traverse genres and moods and still hold fast to her fans. Her feat also highlights how those fans are willing and able to move from the heavy-handed reggaetón beat that long dominated the charts to more sophisticated and understated fare, underscoring that Latin music tastes have decidedly evolved over the years, regardless of what new music playlists decide to include. Bad Bunny also made a big change to his sound with his Fotos album. But while Bad Bunny delved back into his roots for his acclaimed blockbutser, Karol G went more into a universal pop/dance/alt mood, and the two tracks from her new set that have topped Hot Latin Songs offer glimmers of mid-tempo rhythm on an album where melancholy dominates, awash in different sonic ambiences.   And then, there are the lyrics. Karol G thrives musically on heartache. Her best songs have long been rooted in failed relationships — their aftermath and then, their redemption — going back as far as 2017’s melancholic “A Ella,” dedicated to the woman who stole her man. But here, nearly a decade later, she’s amped up her message. She’s devastated rather than angry; her loneliness doesn’t throw her into other arms; she’s not looking for revenge. She’s looking for understanding, and, like her album title, she’s not afraid of feeling so much. Feeling too much is a tough path to take for women — or even men — in music. We’ve grown used to them heartbroken, vindictive or vindicated. But the steady supply of sadness, regret, pain and loss that Karol G dishes out in Me Arrepiento is not customary. To be clear, there is that one bichota , “female empowerment” track. “Matadora” gets very explicit in its description of a woman ready for non-romantic sex, and it’s also racking up streams. It’s the kind of club-banger that can propel an album. But this isn’t a banger album, and “Matadora” isn’t the biggest song from it so far. No Me Arrepiento is more defined by a slow burn of emotions, beautifully and painfully put into words. It’s a different kind of diva that Karol is giving us now — and audiences are showing that we like her, too.

articles.title: Dolly Parton’s advice on running a successful, sprawling business empire: ‘Rely on “higher wisdom,” look your best, and don’t boss anyone around’
articles.summary: “I just try to put people that are smarter than me in all the right places, and then I go on about my business.”
articles._body: Dolly Parton, the legendary singer turned business mogul and philanthropist, could always be relied on for some straight-talking advice. Even when it came to emulating her massive success, the country music star’s guidance was simple: “Work your butt off.” Friends, family, and fans of Parton are reminiscing and celebrating her accomplishments—be it her music, entrepreneurship, or philanthropy—after her nephew and head of security, Bryan Seaver, announced her death in a statement earlier this week. Parton died at 80 years old, with Seaver telling fans: “She never saw a door she couldn’t open, and the doors she opened made and changed history.” He added: “Dolly called me and said she wants to rest in a beautiful bed of plush cotton because after a life wearing heavy rhinestones, she finally deserves to be comfortable and have some rest.” Indeed, the famed “9 to 5” singer suggested to Bloomberg she had always put in more than just the standard office hours. As co-owner of the Dollywood Co., Parton helped oversee the Dollywood Theme Park, the Splash Country water park, several diner ventures, as well as a spa and hospitality venues in the Great Smoky Mountains. Her portfolio also included pet apparel business Doggy Parton, a fragrance brand, and a series of baking kits with Duncan Hines. Forbes valued Parton—who was also a fierce philanthropist—at $450 million, though other outlets placed her wealth closer to $650 million. But despite the brand her name became, Parton said she never became the “step on the bossman’s ladder” she once wrote about. When asked how she ran her empire so successfully, Parton said she had been “blessed” in her endeavors, working with great people and letting them get on with it. Parton never sought to micromanage, she added: “I don’t boss anybody around, because I don’t even have the time or the energy to even do that. I just try to put people that are smarter than me in all the right places, and then I go on about my business.” Parton, also an author, made it clear her talents lay in the creative side of the business, saying there were aspects of her empire that she didn’t know anything about—but didn’t need to because of the team she had in place. “I’m more of the creative force and the one that has an overall sense of things,” she said. “I try to find the best people, and I try to trust them to do what they say they can do. Then I have people looking out after all of them.” The “Islands in the Stream” singer also said her hands-off management approach with senior executives was paired with instinct, and she trusted that if an individual isn’t right for their role, it would eventually be revealed. “We know if somebody’s not right, they’ll show themselves, or it’ll be pointed out so many times by other people that you do trust, you’ll know it’s time to move on from that person,” she said. “So I depend on my own higher wisdom of knowing if I’m in the right place with the right people.” ‘Looking like a woman and thinking like a man’ Parton, who was awarded the Carnegie Medal of Philanthropy, said that from her early days performing in Nashville, she knew she had talents she could monetize. Or as Parton put it: “Looking like a woman and thinking like a man, so to speak.” Appearance is another area in which Parton had some sage advice—which may help Gen Z employees who reportedly are entering the workforce unsure of how they should dress for the office. For Parton, known to be a big fan of wigs and brightly colored suits, the aim is to be comfortable, adding: “You know what business you’re in, and you pretty much know what’s expected. “If you’ve got a dress code, just look the best you can, take it right to the limit. You can kind of bend the rules a little bit, but if that’s the job you want and you already know the rules, then go by the rules.” A version of this story was published on Fortune.com on February 12, 2024. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Steve Ballmer, Clippers discussing ‘settlement’ with NBA for Kawhi Leonard investigation
articles.summary: With training camp for the 2026-27 NBA season set to begin around the league in about a month, the league has yet to provide any updates on the ongoing investigation into the LA Clippers, owner Steve Ballmer, and star Kawhi Leonard for potential cap circumvention violations. Commissioner Adam Sil
articles._body: With training camp for the 2026-27 NBA season set to begin around the league in about a month, the league has yet to provide any updates on the ongoing investigation into the LA Clippers, owner Steve Ballmer, and star Kawhi Leonard for potential cap circumvention violations. Commissioner Adam Silver pointed out in July that he hoped the investigation would conclude before the new season begins, and it appears that a little more clarity is emerging. On August 17, ESPN published a lengthy report detailing how the NBA had not yet found any evidence to prove that Ballmer funneled money through team sponsors to pay Leonard and circumvent the salary cap. It was said in this report that the league was “focused” on Kawhi’s introduction to team sponsors and whether these constituted a violation of the league’s rules prohibiting salary cap circumvention. The NBA responded to these reports , claiming that ESPN’s story contained “numerous and significant inaccuracies.” “ESPN’s article regarding the LA Clippers investigation — for which the NBA declined to cooperate — contains numerous and significant inaccuracies,” NBA Chief Communications Officer Mike Bass said in the statement. “The results in this matter will be made clear once the investigation is concluded.” While there is still no telling when this investigation will conclude and what the ultimate findings will be, ESPN’s Ramona Shelburne continues to shed light on the matter with key updates from the Clippers’ side of things. “I know that the investigators have presented initial findings, but they’re still making calls and putting things together. But they are having conversations with Balmer and his lawyers already,” Shelburne told ESPN LA 710 on Thursday. “They’re talking about it. I don’t know if you would call it a settlement or some kind of negotiation, but that’s already happening.” Despite this investigation still ongoing, Shelburne claims the conversations to this point between the league and Ballmer have not revolved around anything that would signal potential cap circumvention. Instead, the sides have been discussing his failure to monitor the situation as a whole following the initial introductions between him, Leonard, and the team sponsors. “The conversations have been more about this failure to supervise and the nature of the introductions that were made between the Clippers and Kawhi’s people rather than direct evidence of salary cap circumvention done by Steve Ballmer. If you’re doing the easy parlance, that would be the murder charge. That’s a really serious charge that’s very hard to prove.” So, will the Clippers and Ballmer face any penalties from this whole year-long Kawhi saga? Although Shelburne’s reporting over the last month suggests that Ballmer won’t be hit with the “murder charge” in terms of potential cap circumvention being the worst, it is still possible other penalties and sanctions are handed down, specifically regarding his involvement in the matter and failure to supervise what was happening. Even so, any penalties that potentially get handed out to Ballmer, the Clippers, or Leonard once this investigation concludes will certainly be contested through rounds of arbitration and appeals. Once the final verdict on the investigation is given by the league and the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, more legal battles will ensue to dispute any potential wrongdoing. Throughout the matter, Ballmer and the Clippers have remained adamant that they did nothing wrong and did not partake in any potential cap circumvention practices. In response to ESPN’s story earlier in August, the team said in a statement that Kawhi and his team handled their own negotiations with sponsors and that a player having a relationship or deal with a team sponsor is not evidence of cap circumvention. As far as what could potentially happen with Leonard and his trade to the Toronto Raptors, which is currently on hold until more clarity on the investigation presents itself, Shelburne claimed that the Clippers would welcome Kawhi back and are fine with keeping him should the Raptors cancel the trade for any reason. The NBA has yet to provide any timeframe for when this investigation will conclude. The post Steve Ballmer, Clippers discussing ‘settlement’ with NBA for Kawhi Leonard investigation appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: After decades in the music industry, Pharrell Williams admits he never stops working: ‘If you do what you love everyday, you’ll get paid for free’
articles.summary: Grammy Award–winning artist Pharrell Williams says he’s always “being a student” and plans to “never stop working.” He advises others to follow their passion, not money.
articles._body: It’s easy to become jaded in a job that’s unfulfilling , especially when dreams of a more meaningful career clash with the need for financial stability.  But successful entrepreneurs contend that chasing their true ambition inspires them to show up and work every day; those who really love their job, like musician Pharrell Williams , never plan on retiring.  “I’m so blessed to call this a job. I’ve never stopped loving this job; I’ve never stopped being a student,” Williams said onstage after winning the Dr. Dre Global Impact Award at the 2026 Grammys. “So everyone here, I’ve just got to tell you, never stop grinding. And listen, never stop working.” Williams has witnessed firsthand how passion plays a huge role in success; the now 53-year-old philanthropist and artist has been releasing, writing, and producing music since the 1990s, amassing more than three decades of chart-topping hits. With an estimated net worth of $250 million, the “Happy” singer’s years of musical prowess and business collaborations have resulted in a lifelong fortune. But Williams said he doesn’t think too much about the number in his bank account—what really keeps the Gen Xer working is his love for the job. “Stop doing anything else but working. Work, man,” Williams continued. “I’m 52, I get to do this every day—I love what I do. And if you do what you love every day, you’ll get paid for free.” Williams says the American Dream isn’t about making millions Generations of workers have bucked their true calling for a tolerable job with a solid paycheck. With nearly half of U.S. citizens believing the American Dream is no longer possible, or never even existed, many are stuck in a lifeless, steady job rather than a profession that makes them happy.  Growing up in Virginia Beach, Williams said he often heard the same rhetoric: that careers should be centered around stability and making money. But the Grammy winner wants to change that narrative. Chasing the biggest paychecks, he said, is a misnomer.  “The American Dream is not about making the most money. In fact, the human dream and the consumers’ dream shouldn’t be about making the most money,” Williams said at the 2024 Web Summit. “It should be about spending the most time doing something that you love.” The philanthropist pointed out that many young people are pressured to pursue high-paying careers in college, such as medicine and law, whether they want to or not. Some are able to switch tracks despite the chagrin of their family, Williams explained, but the vast majority “go after it, and they don’t get it.” After that, they might be stuck in a job they hate, prioritizing a paycheck over their true passions. Williams advised that professionals can avoid this identity crisis by working in a role or industry that interests them.  “If you can find a vocation around something that you love, you now have a dream job. You will be the first one there, and you’ll be the last one to leave,” Williams continued. “To me, that is what we should be telling our children—that is the way that we should be leading society—for people to do what they love.” ‘Pursue a career that does not feel like work’ Williams is one of many leaders who have proved that sticking with a career you love can pay off. Walmart ’s former CEO, Doug McMillon , who stepped down from the top role earlier this year, spent four decades climbing the ranks of the now–$819 billion retail giant. And during his ascent from being an hourly worker all the way up to chief executive, McMillon said he’s never “been bored one single day.” “Pursue a career that does not feel like work. Life is too short to invest so much time doing something you don’t enjoy,” McMillon told graduates during a commencement address at the University of Arkansas in 2024. “I hope you find your spot quickly like I did, but if you don’t, my advice is that you shouldn’t give up until you do … If you’re in the right place, most days, work won’t even feel like work.” Christian Toetzke, cofounder and CEO of global fitness race Hyrox , also said that he loves his job so much that it doesn’t feel like a chore . His best advice for professionals hoping to strike the right work-life balance is to actually enjoy their careers; that way, it’s never a drag to show up at the office.  “I’m a massive believer in work-life balance, but the question is always how we look at this. And I’m a very privileged person because I don’t consider what I do as work,” Toetzke said on the Opening Bid Unfiltered podcast last year. “I do what I really love. It’s also my hobby. For me, work is not a punishment. It’s almost kind of a reward.” A version of this story was published on Fortune.com on February 3, 2025. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com
