articles.title: Raiders’ Klint Kubiak fully absolves Fernando Mendoza of blame for opening-drive INT vs. 49ers
articles.summary: The preseason is over, and Fernando Mendoza had plenty of in-game action in the Las Vegas Raiders’ finale against the San Francisco 49ers. One of the lowlights was a series-opening interception. Coach Klint Kubiak fully absolved his new quarterback of the opening-drive interception, accordi
articles._body: The preseason is over, and Fernando Mendoza had plenty of in-game action in the Las Vegas Raiders’ finale against the San Francisco 49ers. One of the lowlights was a series-opening interception. Coach Klint Kubiak fully absolved his new quarterback of the opening-drive interception , according to Raiders beat writer Ryan McFadden. Kubiak on Mendoza’s interception: “I think it was a dropped ball.” pic.twitter.com/ksKJ5BWBUb — Ryan McFadden (@ryanmcfadden_) August 28, 2026 The pass tipped off the top of Jalen Nailor’s hands and into the air. From there, linebacker Tatum Bethune picked it off and took it the other way. Ultimately, it was not the best way to start a drive. Kubiak gave his honest review of Mendoza and what he could possibly work on. Significantly, he finished 7 of 14 with 57 yards, no touchdowns, and an interception. Mendoza also took two sacks. Comparatively, Kirk Cousins went 8 of 11 with 51 yards while taking no sacks. Mendoza and Cousins have worked hand-in-hand this offseason. Yet, one of them will be the starter, though the Raiders have not made a decision. Some believe Mendoza should start in Week 1 and get the reps early in his career. So far, his performance has been uneven. Mendoza went 8 for 15 last week against the Houston Texans while passing for 86 yards with no touchdowns and one interception. Before that, he went 10 for 16 with 97 yards and a touchdown. Mendoza will have a week and a half to prep if the Raiders name him the starter. If the team chooses Cousins, he will have some time to work on his game as the season ramps up. Regardless of what happens, Mendoza will have a chance to make his mark, especially after the Raiders spent the top pick of the NFL Draft on him. articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams rookie Ty Simpson turned heads in the preseason with his impressive performances in three games, helping the team to a 3-0 record. Despite already having superstar Matthew Stafford as quarterback, the Rams selected Simpson with the No. 13 pick in April, which came as a surprise t
articles._body: Los Angeles Rams rookie Ty Simpson turned heads in the preseason with his impressive performances in three games, helping the team to a 3-0 record. Despite already having superstar Matthew Stafford as quarterback, the Rams selected Simpson with the No. 13 pick in April, which came as a surprise to many. But it looks like the team made the right call in picking the former Alabama standout. Simpson threw 47-of-60 for 382 yards, three touchdowns, and zero interceptions in the preseason, showcasing his efficiency and high IQ. He had a 109.9 passer rating. Several analysts, including NFL Network’s Manti Te’o and ESPN’s Chase Daniel, heaped prais e on the 23-year-old newcomer. “The young man has taken care of the football, he’s been productive, and I think he’s surprised a lot of people,” said Teo. "I've been very impressed with this guy" Manti Te'o on Ty Simpson's preseason performance @RamsNFL | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/V7EuyI9r9A — Good Morning Football (@gmfb) August 28, 2026 “He’s been really, really sharp. The poise, accuracy, and command of the offense have stood out every time he’s been on the field,” observed Daniel. Ty Simpson through 7 quarters of football: 47/60 (78.3%) 382 yards 3 TD & 0 INT He’s been really, really sharp. The poise, accuracy, & command of the offense have stood out every time he’s been on the field. https://t.co/93sJU4QZmV — Chase Daniel (@ChaseDaniel) August 28, 2026 Some fans, however, were not as high on Simpson, noting how he largely leaned on short passes and nothing downfield. “I mean, yeah, strong showing, but it’s clearly the preseason,” said @Michaeloptv. “That completion rate is elite, but three TDs in 60 attempts suggests he’s playing it safe. Did he take any shots downfield?” asked @Web3__Youth. “No, he’s been a total checkdown merchant,” wrote @LARamilyMan. “Bunch of checkdowns, and a playoff team. Put him on the (Cleveland) Browns or (Las Vegas) Raiders and see what he’d do!” posted @SavageRaider100. “I’ll never be impressed by anyone averaging less than 10 yards per completion,” commented @BlueberryGerb. Rams coach Sean McVay said they are still choosing between Simpson and Stetson Bennett for the backup role behind Stafford. Bennett went 23-of-37 for 219 passing yards, zero touchdowns, and zero interceptions in two games in the preseason. He is in his fourth year with the Rams. Simpson said he is staying in the moment and soaking up all the knowledge he can get in his rookie campaign. articles.title: Why Is Nike Suddenly Part of Sorority Rush Season?
articles.summary: Nike
articles._body: Nike has been a mainstay in college sports locker rooms for decades, and currently outfits more than half of Division I FBS football programs. This back-to-school season, the retailer made clear that another on-campus group is also top of mind: sororities. Throughout August, Nike sponsored rush events for at least six sororities at colleges across the country, including South Carolina, Texas, and Arizona State. Nike supplied some of its latest training, running, and sportswear products to sisters, who donned the gear in videos posted to their personal and sorority-wide social media channels—often to the tune of millions of views . Giant Nike-branded banners featured prominently in the background of most videos, usually unfurled over the stone columns of the chapters’ Greek Revival houses. View this post on Instagram A post shared by ARIZONA STATE DELTA ZETA (@asudeltazeta) Although the company has seeded product on campuses before, it’s the first time that the brand has formally engaged with sororities, Emily Johnson, Nike’s college business director, tells Front Office Sports . She says the company refers to sorority members—along with other engaged, active college students—as “campus athletes.” “We know now more than ever that students are looking to their peers for inspiration,” Johnson says, adding that “18- to 22-year-old females are powerful cultural forces on college campuses.” Nike’s play is new, but sorority rush has been an annual fixation for a while. In 2021, dozens of Alabama freshmen went viral for documenting their experiences (and outfits) while trying to score a bid. (One of the original stars of so-called #RushTok, Kylan Darnell, now frequently appears on ESPN platforms.) In the years since, brands have pounced on the monthlong moment, including many of Nike’s younger, more niche competitors in the activewear space, such as Alo Yoga and Set Active. Still, Nike says it has not seen any of its major sportswear peers activate around sorority rush in such widespread fashion—and Johnson suggests it’s not a one-time deal. She tells FOS the brand is focused on “creating long-term relationships with campus athletes,” like sorority members, who are “helping drive” the conversation around sport, style, and culture forward “in a really unique way.” Nike declined to share how these sponsorships are brokered, or whether the company provided any compensation beyond gifted product. Several national sorority organizations and university offices of fraternity and sorority life did not respond to FOS requests for comment about their involvement. At least some of the partnerships appear to be facilitated by a company called Campus Launch, which bills itself as a “Gen Z marketing agency making brands go viral on campus.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by CampusLaunch | Sorority Marketing (@campuslaunch_) Nike has also dabbled in brand deals with other new-age female tastemakers lately, including Dallas Cowboys cheerleader Abby Summers and Substack lifestyle writer Madeline Hill. The women-centric swings come as challenges mount at Nike, which is navigating a plunging stock price and struggling revenue as its turnaround slogs along . The sorority tie-ins, at least, are a well-received effort that Nike says is moving the needle for them. “We’re thrilled with how this collaboration launched,” says Johnson, “and we will continue to learn and reshape how we can best partner in this space.” The post Why Is Nike Suddenly Part of Sorority Rush Season? appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: Cardi B Twerks Her Way Across Brooklyn — Hitting the Stoop, the Salon and the Street in Flashy ‘AH HA’ Video: Watch
articles.summary: The hard-hitting loosie single produced by DJ SwanQo was released last month.
articles._body: Cardi B hits the streets of Brooklyn for the flashy, fun video for her hard-hitting single “AH HA.” The one-off that dropped last month as her first new music since last year’s long-awaited sophomore album, Am I the Drama? , is a club banger with hot lyrical shots that are matched by the steamy outfits Cardi shuffles through in the visual. The late summer heat is alluded to in the very first shot, which features an old man holding up a gigantic newspaper headline reading “¡QUE CALOR!” (“It’s so hot!”), followed by images of a golden string bikini getting aired out on a clothesline by a spinning fan and the thermometer soaring past 100 degrees. Then comes Cardi strutting down the ave in a skin-tight red, black and white crop top and booty shorts twin set and massive Jesus piece, standing on a stoop rapping, “I just hold up my wrist, I’m like ‘Ah ha,’/ Broke! B–ch, you wish, I’m like, ‘Ah ha’/ I’m on my s–t.” Her waist-length jet-black hair swinging behind her, Cardi lays into all her haters, male and female, including a line referencing the president, “I’ll give a ho exactly what she want in this b–ch/ Black trucks at the club, look like Trump in this b–ch (f–k him),” she raps. The action picks up again at the beauty salon, where Cardi and four friends grind and drop it low in their chairs while sitting under dryers with their hair in curlers before the rapper hops on the back of a quad to take ride while dudes on four-wheelers stage a crosswalk takeover. The outfits are increasingly outrageous, including a number featuring knee-high pink leather boots paired with same colored short shorts and a leather bra and long lime green hair. The temperature really spikes, though, near the midpoint, where Cardi busts out a red, white and blue sling thong bikini — and flame red hair — as she poses on a wheelie-position quad and struts on the street in a thong that leaves little to the imagination. “Let me show off my ‘fit, I’m like ‘ah ha,'” Cardi raps for real as she walks by Kash Doll, who makes a cameo timed to the line “I probably should’ve sent this beat to Kash Doll.” Does it end with a dance crew doing an impromptu routine in the street at night while getting drenched by a wrenched-open fire hydrant as girls do double-dutch in the background? You know it does. The video comes after Cardi hit the road for a her first-ever North American arena headlining Little Miss Drama tour earlier this year and came in at No. 1 on Billboard’s Hottest Female Rappers list for the first half of 2026. “AH HA” recently became Cardi’s 30th top 10 hit on Billboard ’s Hot Rap Songs chart; the song also hit No. 25 on the Billboard Hot 100. Watch the “AH HA” video below.

articles.title: The ‘ruthless’ Kirk Cousins skill that Fernando Mendoza wants to replicate
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders went against the San Francisco 49ers in their preseason finale, and though they lost 18-12, there are some positive things they can take from the game. All four quarterbacks hit the field for the Raiders, as Kirk Cousins got things started. Afterwards, it was rookie Fernando
articles._body: The Las Vegas Raiders went against the San Francisco 49ers in their preseason finale, and though they lost 18-12, there are some positive things they can take from the game. All four quarterbacks hit the field for the Raiders, as Kirk Cousins got things started. Afterwards, it was rookie Fernando Mendoza, who had a solid night but threw an interception and took two sacks. For most of the offseason, Mendoza has been under Cousins’ wing, learning different things and becoming better at the position. Through it all, Mendoza noted after the preseason finale that he wants to replicate this one trait from Cousins. “Fernando Mendoza said Kirk Cousins plays ‘ruthlessly efficient.’ Said he wants to model the way Cousins has been able to end his drives with points,” Sam Warren of The Athletic wrote on X, formerly Twitter. That’s a good trait to have, and it’s something that Cousins has mostly been known for. He knows how to push the ball down the field, but he doesn’t do it in a manner that causes him to turn the ball over all the time. That’s what every quarterback should strive to do, and Mendoza knows once he can consistently do that, it’ll be hard to stop him and the offense. There are still some things that Mendoza is learning, and the Raiders don’t want to throw him out to the fire yet, even if he was the No. 1 pick. The best thing for him is to learn from Cousins, and there will possibly be a time this season when he ends up taking the QB1 spot. It’s uncertain what would have to happen for him to do so, but Mendoza seems ready for the moment. He’s the quarterback of the future for the Raiders, and they know he’ll be ready for the moment as well. articles.title: One Good Mule That's Not On Everyone Else's Feet Yet
articles.summary: One Good is Highsnobiety's series on the tried, tested, and trusted products we can’t stop fawning over. This round features a Boston-eqsue mule from... Vans?!
articles._body: You're reading One Good , a series shedding light on the tried, tested, and trusted products our editors can’t stop fawning over. For more recs on fashion, beauty, and tech, visit the Shopping tab or subscribe to our newsletter . Slip-ons, mules, clogs, call them what you want, but the fact of the matter is, people simply can’t get enough of them. Take it from us. The appetite has gotten so out of hand that just about every reliable, already-celebrated sneaker has been ozempicified in the process. Brands that once lived and died by their streetwear credentials have done a complete 180, suddenly finding themselves with entire sections dedicated to these so-called “half-sneakers.” Yes, we’re looking at you, Vans. Now, before I sound too pessimistic, I have to hand it to them. There’s an art to replicating a silhouette everyone on the planet associates with a certain brand and, in this case, city ( you know who ). But Vans has managed to keep its flair and energy alive in a plush mule, no less. In the case of the Harbor Mule , less really is more. This one isn’t trying to impress you. It’s not flashy or gimmicky, it’s just a damn reliable slip-on, and at the end of the day, that’s gotta be enough. It’s the kind of shoe you reach for without thinking twice, whether you’re running out the door for an overpriced pilates class, nipping out to the corner shop, or just generally refusing to put on a pair of shoes that require any effort, AKA laces. Maybe this whole mule-ification surge is simply a reflection of us getting lazier. If that’s the case, I can’t say I blame us. There’s something to be said for a shoe that asks absolutely nothing of you. While at first glance, these may resemble a Boston, after a couple of wears, I can safely say they’re... far more comfortable. Usually, a mule or clog-adjacent shoe needs a bit of breaking in before you reap the benefits. Not this one. The plush lining helps, sure, but these felt good from the get-go, which is more than can be said for most shoes in this category. It may fall into a severely oversaturated market, but at this point, it’s time to get on board. This seems as good a place as any to start. articles.title: Lions’ most agonizing roster decision looming on 2026 cutdown day
articles.summary: Cutdown day is when the NFL’s cold business finally catches up with every team. For the Detroit Lions, that reality is particularly uncomfortable because one of their deepest position groups has also become one of their most difficult to sort. Detroit appears to have legitimate competition
articles._body: Cutdown day is when the NFL’s cold business finally catches up with every team. For the Detroit Lions, that reality is particularly uncomfortable because one of their deepest position groups has also become one of their most difficult to sort. Detroit appears to have legitimate competition for jobs that once looked relatively straightforward. Nowhere is that more apparent than at cornerback. Forging identity Junfu Han / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Foregoing joint practices, the Lions have treated every practice rep and preseason snap as a high-stakes proving ground. On the field, Detroit split its opening pair of exhibition contests against the Cincinnati Bengals and Washington Commanders. The exhibition action has highlighted an intense, high-energy battle for rotational positioning across all three phases. The preseason has provided clarity in many areas while simultaneously muddying the waters at the back end of the defensive depth chart . High-stakes CB standoff The most agonizing roster decision for the Lions isinside an overhauled cornerback room. Ennis Rakestraw Jr and Nick Whiteside find themselves locked in a dramatic battle for survival. DJ Reed and Rock Ya-Sin have emerged as the leading pieces on the outside. Roger McCreary offers important flexibility inside. Keith Abney II brings another intriguing coverage option. Khalil Dorsey provides special-teams value. Detroit’s own training-camp coverage identified the No. 2 outside cornerback competition as one of the team’s most important battles. Ya-Sin, Rakestraw, and Whiteside have all received meaningful opportunities. That might be stressing out general manager Brad Holmes and head coach Dan Campbell. Keeping seven cornerbacks would provide. However, that also comes at the expense of another position group. Detroit needs enough bodies along the defensive front, offensive line, and special teams to survive the attrition of a 17-game regular season. The question, then, becomes brutally simple: who has done enough to make sacrificing another roster spot worthwhile? Production over pedigree This is where the Rakestraw-Whiteside battle becomes particularly uncomfortable. Rakestraw arrived in Detroit after being selected 61st overall in the 2024 NFL Draft. His athleticism, physicality, and coverage instincts remain obvious. The Lions have continued to invest opportunities in his development. Yet his path through this summer has not been perfectly smooth. He began camp competing for the outside role and suffered an ankle injury during practice. Whiteside, meanwhile, has attacked the competition from the opposite direction. The cornerback has consistently made plays during camp. He has earned increased opportunities as a result. Campbell has essentially acknowledged that the coaching staff could no longer overlook his production. The Lions have repeatedly emphasized competition as a foundational element of Campbell’s program. If a player consistently wins his reps, there is only so long a coaching staff can dismiss him. Whiteside’s emergence has therefore complicated the depth-chart battle. And that is why cutting Whiteside could be just as difficult as moving on from Rakestraw. Waiver-wire gamble The decision becomes even more consequential because Detroit cannot assume either player will simply be waiting on the other side of the waiver process. If the Lions decide to move on from Whiteside, they risk losing a corner with special teams utility. Whiteside also moved into first-team opportunities when Reed was sidelined. Conversely, exposing Rakestraw to waivers would mean risk his being picked up by another squad. His recent preseason production also provides reason for optimism. Rakestraw recorded five tackles and a pass breakup against Cincinnati before adding three tackles against Washington. That is the nightmare scenario for Holmes. Keep the player who has earned the spot, and potentially surrender the higher-upside developmental investment. Protect the former high draft pick, and risk alienating a player who has spent the summer forcing his way into the conversation. There is no clean answer here. What Detroit values most Junfu Han / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Ultimately, the Lions’ cutdown decision is a referendum on roster philosophy . Keeping Rakestraw would represent patience. Keeping Whiteside would say that production matters, regardless of how long the organization has invested in someone else. Keeping both might be disastrous. Detroit has legitimate needs elsewhere. Carrying an unusually deep cornerback room would create vulnerabilities at another position. That is what makes this particular decision so agonizing. The Lions are not choosing between an obvious keeper and an obvious cut. They are choosing between two different definitions of value. articles.title: Braves’ Chris Sale drops bar on first 100 mph pitch in 8 years
articles.summary: In what was potentially a playoff preview, Chris Sale shut down the Los Angeles Dodgers, leading the Atlanta Braves to a 1-0 shutout win. In addition to shutting out the Dodgers, he also threw his first 100 MPH pitch in eight years, according to an interview by our team at ClutchPoints. "You thre
articles._body: In what was potentially a playoff preview, Chris Sale shut down the Los Angeles Dodgers, leading the Atlanta Braves to a 1-0 shutout win. In addition to shutting out the Dodgers, he also threw his first 100 MPH pitch in eight years , according to an interview by our team at ClutchPoints. "You threw a pitch over 100 MPH for the first time in 8 years. How?" Chris Sale: “With my arm.” (via @MLB ) pic.twitter.com/Y0YaDeuy3o https://t.co/yoCplWX9KS — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 28, 2026 Sale kept it short and to the point when discussing his pitching against the Dodgers. Overall, he tossed a complete-game shutout, striking out 11 and allowing five hits. The only run came in the first inning when Drake Baldwin slammed a leadoff home run, and that was all Atlanta needed. Sale threw the 100 MPH pitch against Shohei Ohtani in the third inning. Significantly, it was the first time he had reached such heights since the numerous injuries he has sustained since then. Sale set many records in the win, carrying the Braves on his back, preserving the game even when the offense did little. The win helped the Braves complete a three-game sweep over the Dodgers. Additionally, they pulled to within one game of them for second place in the NL. The Braves snagging second place would be huge, as they would avoid the wildcard round and have a week off before the playoffs start. Sale improved to 13-9 with a 2.06 ERA. He has been efficient and reliable for the Braves all season, in a campaign that has not always featured strong starting pitching. Now, the Braves will continue their homestand this weekend against the Colorado Rockies. Sale’s next turn to take the mound will likely come next week against the San Francisco Giants. articles._body: “AIR FORCE VETERAN. SMALL BUSINESSMAN. TRUMP CONSERVATIVE.” The all-caps headline on Texas Republican congressional candidate Carlos De La Cruz’s website used to align him with President Donald Trump. Not anymore. “NATIVE TEXAN. AIR FORCE VETERAN. SMALL BUSINESSMAN. PROVEN CONSERVATIVE,”  it reads now . De La Cruz’s campaign rejected any suggestion he was backing away from the president, whose knack for mobilizing his loyalists remains critical for Republicans in this fall’s midterm elections. The overwhelming majority of Republicans on the ballot this fall are embracing Trump despite  his dismal approval ratings , an unpopular  war with Iran  and  lingering inflation. However, as the two-month sprint to Election Day begins, a small collection of Republican candidates have quietly begun to distance themselves in subtle ways from Trump now that they’ve won contested primaries in which his endorsement was often the most coveted prize. The shift is easy to miss, often only a few words or new pictures. And Republicans insist there is no shift at all. Mike Marinella, a spokesman for the National Republican Congressional Committee, called it a “manufactured storyline.” “President Trump and House Republicans have delivered historic results for the American people, and our candidates are eager to take that record directly to voters alongside the President on the campaign trail,” he said. But from California to Texas and Kentucky to Alaska, candidates in recent weeks have tweaked their campaign messaging to downplay their connection to Trump. A handful of others have highlighted their opposition to his policies. It’s an extremely delicate balance for vulnerable Republican candidates, who must expand their appeal beyond Trump’s MAGA base to win in the general election this fall, but are also afraid to trigger a backlash from Trump or his hard core supporters if they create too much distance. Trump’s unpopularity could weigh down his party Most candidates are still wrapping their arms around Trump. Republican allies of the president argue there is little upside for candidates to turn away from Trump, despite his weak polling numbers. Democrats will try to cast every Republican running as a Trump acolyte, regardless of their actual stances, they said, and midterm successes typically depend on turning out base voters. Trump remains the Republican Party’s best motivator. “The whole Republican brand is that we’re aligned with Trump so you gain nothing from it,” said Jason Roe, a Republican who advises Rep. Tom Barrett, who is fighting for reelection in a competitive mid-Michigan district race. It is typical for candidates from both sides to tweak their messages after primary elections. Some Democrats, for example, have begun pitching themselves as moderates after highlighting endorsements from progressives like Sen. Bernie Sanders during their primaries. Still, the slight shift among at least a half-dozen Republican congressional candidates could signal the beginning of a more significant move within the party as the weight of Trump’s unpopularity with the general public comes into view at a critical moment. Just 33% of adults approve of Trump’s job performance, according to  Associated Press-NORC polling  from July. And Trump gets relatively poor ratings on his handling of the economy, immigration and foreign policy. Meanwhile, Trump will not make it easy for vulnerable Republicans to avoid him. As voters typically begin paying much closer attention to politics after Labor Day, the president will headline a two-day Republican convention in Dallas as he urges voters to act as if he were on the ballot. “The problem that we have is they say that Trump does great when he’s on the ballot, but when he’s not on the ballot, his people don’t come,” Trump said as he recently stumped in South Carolina. “So what I really want you to do is pretend, please, that I’m on the ballot,” he went on. “Just say that I’m on the ballot one more time.” Shifting emphasis moving into the general election A number of Republicans have removed or downplayed references to Trump from their websites after winning their primaries. Eric Flores, a former assistant U.S. Attorney and Texas Army National Guard infantry captain running against Democratic Rep. Vicente Gonzalez Jr. in South Texas,  once featured  “SUPPORT PRESIDENT TRUMP’S AGENDA” as No. 2 in his list of priorities on his campaign homepage. That item has now been replaced with “  LOWER THE COST OF LIVING ,” a top issue for voters. Trump does not appear anywhere else on the website, aside from a list of endorsements that previously appeared on the homepage but has been moved to a separate page. Flores’ campaign declined to comment. In Kentucky, Ralph Alvarado, running to represent the overwhelmingly Republican 6th Congressional District, removed all references to Trump from  his campaign homepage , as well as a photo of the two of them together after winning his primary in May. He now promises to offer “INDEPENDENT LEADERSHIP” after previously running as an “AMERICA FIRST FIGHTER.” NBC News  first reported  the changes to Alvarado’s website. Campaign manager Andy Westberry noted Trump’s photo still appears elsewhere in a media gallery. “The socialists are going to have to do a lot better than this nonsense to win this district,” he said in a statement. Some changes do not mean Trump has been erased. While De La Cruz no longer touts himself as a “TRUMP CONSERVATIVE” at the top of his homepage, a video that is embedded lower down features the Air Force veteran speaking at a Trump rally. He still calls himself a “TEXAS TRUMP CONSERVATIVE” on his bio page and lists “Supporting President Trump’s America First Agenda” as among his priorities on a “Mission” page. articles.title: Judge: Pentagon punished Anthropic for ‘arrogance,’ and that’s illegal
articles.summary: Anthropic has also filed a separate and narrower case that is still pending in the federal appeals court in Washington, D.C.
articles._body: A federal judge has ruled in favor of artificial intelligence company Anthropic in its  legal battle against the Pentagon  after the government labeled the company as a supply chain risk earlier this year. U.S. District Judge Rita Lin issued a written order Thursday night that the Pentagon acted illegally by punishing the AI company for its criticism of the Department of Defense’s views on AI use. The government is expected to fight the ruling. The dispute between the AI company and the government broke out in February when President Donald Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth accused Anthropic of endangering national security and designated the company a supply chain risk. Anthropic CEO  Dario Amodei refused to back down  over concerns the company’s products could be used for mass surveillance or autonomous armed drones. Lin wrote that the government’s actions “were based on a desire to make a public example out of Anthropic for its ‘arrogance’ in criticizing the government, not based on any articulable basis to believe that Anthropic would actually sabotage its model.” An Anthropic spokesperson said in a statement that they welcome the judge’s ruling: “We remain focused on working productively with the government to harness AI for our national security so all Americans benefit from this technology.” The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In the 59-page ruling, Lin, an appointee of former President Joe Biden, wrote that neither the Constitution nor the federal statute the government invoked allows them to “impose sweeping penalties based principally on Anthropic’s critique of the Administration’s views.” Anthropic  sued the Pentagon  over the supply chain risk designation in March for what it called an “unlawful campaign of retaliation” over its refusal to allow unrestricted military use of its technology. The legal challenge intensified an unusually public dispute over how  AI can be used in warfare  and mass surveillance. Anthropic’s primary tech industry rival, ChatGPT maker OpenAI, made its own deal to work with the Pentagon just hours after the government punished Anthropic for its stance. Anthropic and OpenAI are each ramping up for  buzzy initial public offerings . Anthropic has also filed a separate and narrower case that is still pending in the  federal appeals court in Washington, D.C.  That case involves a different rule the Pentagon is using to try to declare Anthropic a supply chain risk. Earlier in the legal proceedings, Lin had temporarily blocked the Pentagon from labeling the company as a supply chain risk and blocked enforcement of  Trump’s social media directive  ordering all federal agencies to stop using Anthropic and its chatbot Claude. In a hearing July 30, Lin had said that the government’s position was “really troubling” to her and that it seemed “at odds to me with the First Amendment.” She also said she believed the record had “gotten worse for the government” over time. In that same hearing, Department of Justice lawyers argued that the nature of AI models is “so staggeringly enormous and opaque” that the Defense Department cannot evaluate it in the same way it would a physical piece of hardware. Anthropic lawyer Michael Mongan said in that hearing that the government’s actions “profoundly harm Anthropic” and that they “threaten more broadly to chill speech and debate on a very important issue.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.summary: As the Iran War marks its six-month anniversary, Trump insists he's “not in a hurry” to get back to the negotiating table.
articles._body: President  Donald Trump  arrives at an awkward moment for his presidency on Friday as the U.S.-Israel  war against Iran  reaches  the six-month mark,  a notable milestone for a conflict that the Republican leader repeatedly assured Americans would be a  “little excursion”  lasting a matter of weeks. The war isn’t over, though Trump claims that through bombs and blockade, he has already devastated  Iran’s leadership , military  and economy . And this week his administration said it would turn its focus to  increasing economic pressure  — rather than military action — to try to finish off Iran. The shifting strategy centers on threats to punish any country or entity that continues to  conduct business with Tehran . The turn to using sanctions as the cudgel of choice comes as the administration weighs diminished munitions stockpiles after months of war, sparking concerns that the prolonged conflict could  undermine U.S. military readiness in other parts of the globe. As the conflict grinds on, Trump’s talk of finding a quick end to the war also appears to be fading. He stressed this week that he’s  “not in a hurry”  to get Iran  back to the negotiating table , and he continues making the case that the  Islamic Republic’s leadership is on the ropes. “They’re not paying their troops. They’re in deep trouble. They have very little capacity,” Trump told reporters Thursday. “We don’t want to speak to them. We’re not looking to meet or anything,” he said. It’s unclear how — or if — Trump will address the six-month anniversary of a conflict that has already cost the United States  more than $37.5 billion  and  done damage to his popularity  ahead of critical November elections for his party. The president is spending Friday in Houston, where he’ll honor the  Artemis II  NASA crew for their 10-day mission around the moon earlier this year. Trump is declaring ‘mission accomplished’ — a phrase that hurt a Republican predecessor On its face, the moment is complicated for the “America First” leader who fiercely criticized his White House predecessors for wasting American taxpayer money and U.S. troops’ lives in Middle East conflicts and  vowed  on the campaign trail to keep the military out of “endless wars.” But Trump has bristled at suggestions that this war — in which no American troops have deployed into Iran — can be compared with the yearslong wars in Iraq and Afghanistan in which more than 7,000 Americans were killed. His Republican predecessor, President  George W. Bush , was widely mocked for a 2003 speech aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln beneath a White House-produced banner that read “Mission Accomplished.” It came to symbolize a premature declaration of victory for the Iraq War, which would go on for nearly nine more years. More than two decades later, there are still U.S. troops stationed in Iraq. Trump’s war has stretched on far longer than he told Americans it would. It didn’t stop him from sharing a social media post this week declaring “MISSION ACCOMPLISHED 2026.” The AI-generated image features Trump against a backdrop of U.S. fighter jets, a warship and American flags above smaller images of Bush and former Iranian Supreme Leader  Ayatollah Ali Khamenei ,  who was killed in an Israeli strike  in the opening salvos of the war. Trump has consistently emphasized that the U.S. and Israel campaign  has been devastating  for Iran’s navy and air force. Iranian officials have said the  country has suffered  $270 billion in direct and indirect damage. Israeli military strikes in the first weeks of the war wiped out much of the theocratic government’s leadership structure, including  Khamenei . But Iran has found leverage through its own strikes in the critical  Strait of Hormuz , where relatively few vessels carrying oil and liquefied natural gas are risking passage. Trump again declared Thursday that the “Strait of Hormuz is open,” saying 24 vessels passed through a day earlier. That’s a fraction of the roughly 130 vessels that passed through the vital waterway daily before the war began. Trump is showing little interest in talks Mediators Qatar and Pakistan  continue to press for a diplomatic off-ramp  from the two sides. Qatar’s prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, was in Tehran on Thursday to discuss a proposed plan between Iran and Oman to boost traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. But in Washington, Trump has shown little interest in getting back to the  preliminary deal reached in June  that aimed to reopen the strait and launch talks about Iran’s nuclear program. That deal fell apart within weeks after Iran started attacking ships. At the same time, Trump says the U.S. effort to  economically choke off Tehran  is working, with a U.S. naval blockade preventing Iranian oil from making it to market as the trickle of vessels carrying oil from other Gulf nations pass through. “We have control and we have the blockade,” Trump said. “Iran is not getting anything. Nothing is going through.” Iran is badly battered, but has a history of showing resilience There’s no doubt that the strikes combined with decades of international sanctions have battered Iran, said Aarathi Krishnan, a geopolitical risk analyst at RAKSHA Intelligence Future. But as Trump tries to turn to a new chapter in the war, Krishnan argues the Republican may be misguided in concluding that more pressure on Tehran — which has spent decades adapting to international economic sanctions — will produce the political outcome he wants. articles.title: Rams’ Sean McVay not worried about possible Puka Nacua suspension despite Tutu Atwell trade
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams surprised NFL fans and pulled off a Tutu Atwell trade that many did not see coming. The Rams sent running back Jarquez Hunter in exchange for the trade to the Miami Dolphins. While the Rams now have more than enough options at the wide receiver position, speculation links a p
articles._body: The Los Angeles Rams surprised NFL fans and pulled off a Tutu Atwell trade that many did not see coming. The Rams sent running back Jarquez Hunter in exchange for the trade to the Miami Dolphins. While the Rams now have more than enough options at the wide receiver position, speculation links a potential suspension for Puka Nacua given the timeline. However, Rams head coach Sean McVay recently cleared the air about the speculation . He clarified that the move was made just in order to add depth to the roster rather than a preplan for suspension for Nacua. According to The Athletic’s senior writer for the Rams, Nate Atkins, the superstar wide receiver will also not be bumping into any candidate set for the roster. “Sean McVay said the Tutu Atwell decision is not related to any potential suspension that could come to Puka Nacua. He said they wanted Tutu for depth. He also said it won’t bump any WRs they wanted to keep off the roster either. They have plans to be flexible with the 53,” Atkins wrote on X, formerly Twitter. With everything said and done, ifs and buts around a potential suspension have always been in discussion. Even ESPN’s Adam Schefter mentioned that Nacua could miss Week 1 of NFL action. “Cases that I believe are now being reviewed include that of the Rams wide receiver, Puka Nacua, who could potentially face discipline for some of the off-season headlines that accompanied him and some of those incidents last year with another woman, what did and didn’t occur. We’ll leave that to the NFL to figure out what did and didn’t happen, but it’s possible that when the Niners and Rams play in Australia, it’s within the realm of options that Puka doesn’t play in that game,” Schefter reported earlier in August. Potential discipline looms over a group of NFL players, including Rams WR Puka Nacua and Packers RB Josh Jacobs. Cc: @tyschmit https://t.co/mTwS98lcWO pic.twitter.com/e5fW2ZoQwV — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 11, 2026 Now with Atwell at the helm, the Rams’ 53-man roster gets a major boost . If anything, the team will have one more candidate on the offensive side. His role as a blocker was in question, and he still needs to work on his receiving abilities. Reports also say that bringing back Atwell could push Xavier Smith to contest for his role. His limited role as a wide receiver also adds to the speculation. However, while there’s no hard and fast way to draw lines and say who will make it to the roster and who will not, it’s only about time before we find out what this trade brings out for the Rams. The post Rams’ Sean McVay not worried about possible Puka Nacua suspension despite Tutu Atwell trade appeared first on ClutchPoints .

Luke Bryan on His New Album, ‘Signs’ and the Track Unlike Anything He’s Recorded Before: ‘I’ve Tried to Be the King of Not Overthinking Things’
articles.summary: Billboard reveals the title of two more songs on country superstar’s Sept. 18 set.
articles._body: “My fans have naturally kind of made me the guy that they go to to have fun,” says Luke Bryan . It was with that thought in mind that the country superstar picked the songs for Signs, his ninth full-length studio album that comes out Sept. 18. But as the artist who brought the world such good-timing party anthems like “Country Girl (Shake It for Me)” and “All My Friends Say,” ponders further, he notes that his fans equally respond to beautifully reflective songs like “Drink a Beer.” “A big thing you always hear from fans, too, is they want to hear songs of mine that throwback to where I was right when I came out and I feel like there’s several songs on this album that could be considered throwbacks,” he says. “But there are also songs that reflect a more modern side, such as the title track, that gravitate towards pop-country.” So maybe, the American Idol judge figures, with Signs , he’s made an album that ticks all the boxes. Bryan, who co-wrote two of the tracks on the set (“Fish Hunt Golf Drink” and “Crooked Rows of Corn”) says, he’s “really, really blessed. By the time I make an album, I’ve had a lot of songs land in my lap [from outside songwriters]… But you know, the main thing with me is to just truly enjoy the process and try to make a well-rounded album, and I certainly feel like this is [one].” Bryan, who again played stadiums this summer with his buddy Jason Aldean (as well as arenas on his own Word on the Street Tour dates), talked to Billboard about making the album. He began rolling out the track listing on Aug. 18 via a dedicated album website , and Billboard is exclusively revealing two more song titles, “Killer” and “Woods.” First single, “Country and She Knows It,” stands at No. 15 on Billboard ’s Country Airplay chart dated Aug. 29. Billboard is announcing two more song titles on the new album, including “Killer.” That’s a song unlike any you’ve ever done before, from the perspective of a bullet in a gun. It’s really deep subject matter, a really dark song — and really one of more well-written songs I’ve ever been a part of. These boys [Davis Corley, Mark Addison Chandler and Nate Kenyon] that wrote this song really wrote something very unique and special, and they went out there on a limb. Obviously, anytime you bring up guns — certainly in music and movies and art — it’s a slippery slope, and [there are] so many different polarizing opinions. This is just a story told from the perspective of a gun. I don’t think it’s my job to start some pro-gun or non-pro-gun awareness campaign, but when you hear a song like this, I just think the song is so great somebody needs to sing it, and I just said, “I’m gonna be the guy that does it.” What did you think the first time you heard it? It took my breath away. When I think about my reaction the first time I heard “Drink a Beer,” and how it just floored me, I think this song does the same thing. I think it’ll take the listener on a ginormous emotional ride. It just gets better and better with every listen. It’s just a tremendous thought process of a song. The other one song name we’re revealing is “Woods,” which feels very much in your wheelhouse. This is one of those songs that I feel like my fans, when they hear me perform this, they’ll be like, “Oh yeah, that sounds like the Luke Bryan that we know. It just describes how important the relationship [between] the woods and a kid from the country is. It just really marries that relationship. I didn’t write the song, but everything in that song spoke to me as if I wrote it, and I think it’ll speak to everybody out there that has grown out in the sticks, and the way we lived. This song really embodies that. You turned 50 last month. Though the album was likely finished before your birthday, are you selecting any songs now that you wouldn’t have selected 10 or 20 years ago? I don’t know if I think about it. Mentally, I think I’m 30 anyway. I don’t necessarily know if I think about stuff in that context. My biggest challenge as an artist that’s been doing this for close to 20 years now is to try not to be overly redundant with your material, but then try not to stray away from what butters your biscuit. At the end of the day, I want a song to really touch me and, therefore, I think the odds are that it will do that to my fans. That’s kind of the way I’ve approached every album. The bottom line is, I don’t necessarily know if I approach it with a 50-year-old brain, I think I approach it with which songs are connecting with me the most, and which songs do I believe will connect with my fans the most. You’ve worked with Jeff Stevens almost your whole career. Now, he and his son Jody produce your albums together, including this one. What do they bring to the process? The beauty of the dynamic with me and Jody and Jeff is Jeff is just the old rock in the room that really digs in and sticks to the core of what me and him are. Jeff and I inadvertently struck gold together. Jody [co-wrote] “Signs,” and that production on “Signs” is really young and fresh. So, Jody coming in and having that production is very important. Jody could literally build all our tracks if we wanted him to. It’s kind of like you got the old and you got the young and then you got me, and we all get in there together for one common goal. Jeff and Jody really don’t get caught up in the politics of the town. They’re kind of quiet behind-the-scenes guys that want to make their work speak for them. articles._body: The Cleveland Browns did not go winless in the preseason after Dillon Gabriel led the squad to a blowout victory over the New England Patriots, 37-13, at Huntington Bank Field on Thursday. Gabriel put on a masterclass, throwing 12-of-15 for 186 yards, three touchdowns, and zero interceptions. He is presumed to be the third-string quarterback behind Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders, but he might have accorded himself another look from coach Todd Monken after he dismantled the Patriots. He is expected to make the 53-man roster, but the veteran signal-caller cannot be too complacent, especially after Monken’s response when asked about their quarterback room , as reported by The Athletic’s Zac Jackson. “Monken said he’s not getting into anything regarding how many QBs the Browns will keep on the 53. Said he and Andrew Berry still have to discuss that,” said Jackson X. Taylen Green is also in the lineup. He went 5-of-7 for 27 yards against the Patriots. He also had eight carries for 66 yards. He was drafted by Cleveland in the sixth round in April. Gabriel, who was picked by the Browns in the third round in 2025, had his moments in his rookie year. In 10 games, including six starts, he threw for 937 yards, seven touchdowns, and two interceptions. He has remained even-keeled amid the quarterback situation in Cleveland , stressing that he is not sweating the things he cannot control. “I don’t take things personally. It’s a business. I’m focused on what I need to do to get better, and that’s all I’m focused on. I’m present with that,” said Gabriel. The Browns will battle the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1. articles.title: Ravens’ most agonizing roster decision looming on 2026 cutdown day
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens enter the final stretch of the preseason riding some momentum after going 2-0 in their first couple of games. The defense in particular has performed at an elite level. The second- and third-string units have executed with impressive efficiency. Baltimore’s coaching sta
articles._body: The Baltimore Ravens enter the final stretch of the preseason riding some momentum after going 2-0 in their first couple of games. The defense in particular has performed at an elite level. The second- and third-string units have executed with impressive efficiency. Baltimore’s coaching staff has used the preseason to evaluate a crowded group of edge defenders. That embarrassment of riches has transformed standard position battles into fierce wars of attrition. And nowhere is that more apparent than along the edge. Edge rusher dilemma Mitch Stringer-Imagn Images The Ravens entered camp with a dramatically revamped edge-rusher group. Trey Hendrickson was brought in as an established premier pass rusher . Tavius Robinson and Mike Green offered different forms of size, power, and explosiveness. Behind them, Adisa Isaac, Kaimon Rucker, and Ethan Burke have created precisely the kind of competition that makes final roster construction so difficult. Baltimore’s own training-camp preview identified the number of edge defenders the team can retain as one of its central questions. Ordinarily, carrying four or five dedicated edge rushers provides enough flexibility. Baltimore, though, may have a problem that no general manager wants: too many players who have made legitimate cases to stay. Hendrickson is obviously safe. Robinson’s ability to set the edge gives the defense a dependable presence against the run. Green’s pass-rush potential adds another explosive dimension. That leaves Isaac, Rucker, and Burke fighting for whatever room remains. Ethan Burke makes the decision harder Burke’s performance has transformed this from a routine depth-chart decision into a genuine roster dilemma. Against the Vikings, he produced a drive-killing sack and forced a fumble that became Baltimore’s first takeaway of the preseason. Burke also added a pass breakup while consistently affecting the quarterback. The performance was not an isolated flash, either. Burke has repeatedly generated pressure and shown the ability to contribute from different alignments. That strengthens his argument for a place on the 53-man roster. Baltimore cannot simply evaluate him as a developmental prospect. He is producing now. Kaimon Rucker has likewise continued to make his presence felt with a relentless motor and backfield disruption. Meanwhile, Isaac brings a different proposition. His athletic profile and pass-rush traits remain enticing, but his previous injury setbacks make his roster situation considerably more complicated. Suddenly, cutting any one of the three becomes difficult to defend. Every cut is a gamble The obvious solution would be to keep the five established options and expose one of the bubble players to waivers. That sounds reasonable until the rest of the league gets involved. Pass rushers are among the most valuable commodities on the waiver wire. Finding an edge defender who can consistently threaten the quarterback is quite difficult for many teams. If Baltimore releases Burke after his preseason performance, another team could basically poach him. The same applies to Rucker, whose pressure production makes him an intriguing developmental asset. Even Isaac could attract interest because of his athletic traits. That leaves Eric DeCosta facing a classic roster-building trap. Keep six edge defenders and potentially sacrifice valuable depth elsewhere, or keep five and hope the player you expose somehow survives the waiver process? There is little reason to believe Baltimore can count on the latter. Ripple effect The agony of the edge-rusher crunch does not exist in a vacuum. Every roster spot spent along the defensive front has consequences elsewhere. Baltimore has several intriguing candidates competing for opportunities in the secondary. Those include Bilhal Kone, Keyon Martin, and Robert Longerbeam. The tight end room presents another difficult calculation. Mark Andrews remains the centerpiece. Meanwhile, Durham Smythe supplies veteran blocking and reliability. Behind them, Matthew Hibner and Josh Cuevas have both strengthened their cases throughout the summer. Carrying an additional edge defender could therefore force Baltimore to sacrifice a player who offers genuine offensive or special-teams utility. That is the hidden cost of the pass-rush decision. The Ravens are choosing between an edge rusher and another player who could become important when injuries inevitably arrive. What Baltimore values most Mitch Stringer-Imagn Images Ultimately, DeCosta and Minter have to determine whether the extra pass-rushing insurance is worth the opportunity cost. The case for keeping six outside linebackers is compelling. Baltimore has built a group capable of attacking quarterbacks in waves. Defensive depth becomes particularly valuable over a 17-game season. Hendrickson can lead the charge, and Robinson can provide physicality. Green can develop into a high-impact disruptor, and the remaining trio offers a combination of motor, athleticism and upside. But roster balance matters more. The Ravens cannot afford to become dangerously thin at cornerback, safety, tight end, or another position. A bad outcome is easy to imagine: Baltimore keeps the roster balanced, releases a promising pass rusher, and then watches that player become a meaningful contributor for another AFC contender. Yet the alternative carries its own danger. Hoarding edge defenders could leave the Ravens vulnerable elsewhere. That would create a different kind of roster imbalance that becomes apparent only after injuries strike. There really is no perfect answer. The post Ravens’ most agonizing roster decision looming on 2026 cutdown day appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Why Is the New Tropical Storm Spinning Up in the Atlantic Called ‘Dolly?’ It’s Not What You Think
articles.summary: The name was actually picked more than 30 years ago.
articles._body: There are so many ways people are paying tribute to country legend Dolly Parton following her death on Tuesday (Aug. 25) at age 80. From President Trump ordering the nation’s flags to fly at half-staff , to the Library of Congress honoring her good works and a drive to have the Nashville International Airport renamed in her honor , not to mention the raft of fellow artists honoring her and performing her songs in concert . Related Forever No. 1: Dolly Parton, ‘9 to 5’ AMC Theaters Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton By Bringing Two of Her Classic Movies Back to the Big Screen Dolly Parton Wasn’t Eligible for Song of the Year Grammy for ‘I Will Always Love You’ for This ‘Unforgettable’ Reason One of the weirdest, and, as it turns out, most unrelated tributes, however, spun up on Thursday (Aug. 27), just days after Parton’s passing, when a new tropical storm was forming in the Atlantic Ocean. That storm’s name? Dolly. But, according to The Associated Press , the bizarre coincidence has nothing to do with Parton at all, but is merely an unexpected quirk of the naming convention used by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO), by which a list of names is recycled every six years, with the ones in the Atlantic running in an alphabetical order and alternating male and female names. So, while this season began with storms named Arthur in June, followed by Bertha in July and Cristobal, which flared up and then flamed out quickly earlier this month, the latest storm brewing was already fated to be called Dolly. For now, it’s not expected to turn into a major storm, but the National Hurricane Center issued a statement explaining the coincidence just in case. “The timing of the use of the name Dolly for this storm is purely coincidental,” the organization said . “Tropical storm and hurricane names for the North Atlantic Basin originate from six predetermined rotating lists established by the World Meteorological Organization Region IV Hurricane Committee. The name Dolly replaced Diana after the 1990 hurricane season and was first used in 1996.” The name, which was chosen 30 years ago by the WMO as part of the naming protocol using the rotating group of storm names, will not be changed. After each storm season, a committee for the North Atlantic basin reviews the names and decides if any should be retired due to severity and major loss of life and property; around 100 names have been retired from the Atlantic list to date. There were a number of named “Dolly” storms and hurricanes during Parton’s lifetime, including 2008’s Category 2 storm, which hit southeast Texas, again in 2020 and for the first time in 1996 to replace “Diana,” a Category 2 that hit Mexico in 1990, killing 139 people. At press time, Tropical Storm Dolly continues to move quickly westward toward the Leeward Islands, with heavy rains forecast for late Saturday into Sunday for the series of islands in the Lesser Antilles in the Caribbean, with possible further impacts on the Virgin Islands, Puerto Rico and Hispaniola on Sunday and Monday. It was unclear at press time if the storm will make landfall in the U.S.

articles.title: Why Exelon’s CFO is stepping into a new strategy role
articles.summary: As electricity demand surges, Exelon is giving its longtime CFO a bigger say in where the company places its biggest bets.
articles._body: Good morning. At Exelon, one of the nation’s largest utility companies, finance is getting a bigger seat at the strategy table. Jeanne Jones, the finance chief since 2022 and an almost 20-year veteran of the company, will take on the newly created role of EVP of finance and strategy on Oct. 5, putting her at the center of corporate strategy as electricity demand surges and utilities face mounting pressure to invest without driving up customer bills. Jones will continue to report to Exelon President and CEO Calvin Butler. Robert Kleczynski will succeed Jones as CFO and become her direct report. Kleczynski currently serves as SVP, controller and head of tax. “Jeanne’s leadership has been instrumental in helping Exelon deliver strong financial performance while maintaining our focus on delivering safe, reliable and affordable service for our customers,” Butler said in a statement . In her new role, Jones will continue to work “across the business and the energy sector to identify opportunities to deliver value for our customers and shareholders,” he said. A shift in the CFO’s mandate The move reflects a broader shift in the CFO’s role. The corporate strategy  playbook is increasingly landing on the CFO’s desk. While finance chiefs have long led capital allocation and investor communication, they’re increasingly expected to help determine where the company places its biggest long-term bets alongside the CEO, Andy West, a senior partner at McKinsey and global co-leader of the firm’s Strategy and Corporate Finance practice, recently told me. That evolution is particularly relevant in the utility industry, where electricity demand is growing, grids need modernization and companies face mounting pressure to invest while keeping customer bills affordable. At Exelon, Jones will continue to oversee the company’s financial activities while helping lead integrated strategy efforts focused on trends affecting Exelon, its operating companies and the broader energy industry. The structure is designed to strengthen alignment between long-term strategy, capital allocation and operational execution, according to a company spokesperson. A pure-play utility investing in the future Chicago-based Exelon ( No. 189 on the Fortune 500) serves 11 million customers through six regulated transmission and distribution utilities. Since spinning off its power generation business, Constellation Energy , in 2022, Exelon has focused solely on regulated utility operations. It doesn’t own power plants; instead, it manages the infrastructure that delivers electricity and gas to end users. That makes capital allocation especially consequential. Exelon has to determine where and how aggressively to invest in its networks as demand rises, while balancing the costs ultimately borne by customers against the need to build infrastructure for the future. Jones has experience across utility operations, corporate finance, and the company’s former generation business. She served as CFO of ComEd, one of the nation’s largest electric utilities, then as Exelon’s CFO, guiding the company through a period of consistent operational and financial performance following the separation. Her experience gives a perspective that crosses different parts of the energy value chain. Now she’ll be asked to apply that experience to questions that increasingly blur the line between finance and strategy: how much to invest, where to invest it and how to do so while keeping costs under control. Exelon reported second-quarter earnings on July 30 and revenues totaled $5.97 billion, beating estimates. The top line increased 10% from the year-ago figure of $5.43 billion. Adjusted operating earnings increased 10.3% to 43 cents per share from 39 cents in the year-ago quarter.  Reflecting on her journey, Jones told me last year that her best career advice is to stay open to new experiences and not get overwhelmed by distant goals. Don’t let the pressure of a specific end goal cloud your enjoyment of the ride. “Keep going for the next thing that’s going to develop you,” she said. Have a good weekend. Sheryl   Estrada Sheryl.Estrada@fortune.com This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Ty Simpson’s strong preseason finale still not enough to earn Rams QB2 nod over Stetson Bennett
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams went undefeated in three games in the preseason after beating the Los Angeles Chargers, 20-18, at SoFi Stadium on Thursday. Ty Simpson made a good account of himself, throwing 18-of-23 for 119 yards, one touchdown, and zero interceptions. He connected with Brennan Presley for
articles._body: The Los Angeles Rams went undefeated in three games in the preseason after beating the Los Angeles Chargers, 20-18, at SoFi Stadium on Thursday. Ty Simpson made a good account of himself , throwing 18-of-23 for 119 yards, one touchdown, and zero interceptions. He connected with Brennan Presley for an 11-yard score to give the Rams the lead, 10-7, in the second quarter. They never relinquished the advantage en route to the victory. It was Simpson’s best performance in the preseason, boosting his chance to get the nod as the backup quarterback to Matthew Stafford . Despite the promising rookie’s laudable showing, Rams coach Sean McVay said he remains undecided between Simpson and Stetson Bennett on who should be the QB2, as reported by The Athletic’s Nate Atkins. “Sean McVay didn’t commit to a No. 2 QB tonight between Stetson Bennett and Ty Simpson. He said he likes what he’s seen out of both and will make the decision after giving it more thought,” wrote Atkins on X. Bennett did not play against the Chargers, with Matthew Caldwell seeing action as the other signal-caller. Caldwell went 5-of-10 for 31 yards, one touchdown, and zero interceptions. Many were surprised when the Rams selected the 23-year-old Simpson with the No. 13 pick in April. While the 38-year-old Stafford, the reigning MVP, remains the team’s go-to guy, Simpson should be a key piece in the team’s future-building. The 28-year-old Bennett, meanwhile, is in his fourth year in Los Angeles. He has never seen a single snap since the Rams drafted him in the fourth round in 2023. The Rams will face the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1. The post Ty Simpson’s strong preseason finale still not enough to earn Rams QB2 nod over Stetson Bennett appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: The Download: a secretive antiaging drug and joining virtual power plants
articles.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. A startup claims it’s found a drug to make your blood young —Antonio Regalado I knew I’d officially become a “longevity influencer” when a company cal
articles._body: This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. A startup claims it’s found a drug to make your blood young —Antonio Regalado I knew I’d officially become a “longevity influencer” when a company called Generation Lab offered me the chance to write about—and even receive—their new rejuvenation treatment. This wasn’t just any antiaging treatment, either. A company fact sheet says that it “blocks the systemic spread of aging in the bloodstream, reawakens the body’s own repair mechanism and restores health and youth to multiple tissues.” The approach is based on research by Generation Lab’s irascible scientific founder, Irina Conboy. She found that joining the circulatory systems of old and young mice improved the old animals’ ability to heal from injury. Conboy now says she has found a combination of two existing drugs that can produce youthful effects without the need for any bodily fluid exchange. But Generation Lab won’t reveal what the drugs are, making the proposition hard to take seriously. Read the full story on the drug combo that claims to “stop the spread of aging.” How to sign up for a virtual power plant—and decide whether you should Your thermostat may not look like a power plant. Neither does your electric vehicle, home battery, or HVAC system. But utility and energy companies increasingly want to treat them like one. That’s the idea behind a virtual power plant , or VPP, a collection of household devices (such as smart thermostats, EV chargers, and solar panels) that a utility can control, usually by commanding them to draw less electricity during peak hours. In exchange, participants receive a discount on their energy bills and, in some cases, a signing bonus. Here’s how to sign up for a VPP—and decide whether it’s worth it . —Eshan Raul This story is part of MIT Technology Review’s How To series, which gives you practical advice on getting things done. Check out the rest of the series here . The must-reads I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology. 1 A judge has blocked the Pentagon’s blacklisting of Anthropic The court found the designation violated First Amendment rights. ( NYT $) + And ruled that the designation was based on retaliation. ( CNBC ) + Anthropic still faces a separate case in Washington, DC. ( Reuters $) + The Pentagon’s culture war against Anthropic backfired. ( MIT Technology Review ) 2 Tech giants have called for a defensive surge to defeat AI-driven hacks Over 100 companies warned that a wave of cyberattacks is imminent. ( BBC ) + And urged government and industry leaders to take rapid action. ( Quartz ) + Their main solution, unsurprisingly, is more AI. ( Gizmodo ) + Here’s why OpenAI agents hacked Hugging Face. ( MIT Technology Review ) 3 Anthropic has launched an AI tool that conducts scientific experiments It lets AI agents autonomously operate microscopes, lasers, and robotic arms. ( FT $) + And includes rules designed for safe operations in labs. ( Wired $) + It’s Anthropic’s first tool designed for the physical world. ( Ars Technica ) 4 India’s data center boom is leaving the people it displaces with nothing Policymakers courting Big Tech are sidelining local communities. ( Rest of World ) + No one wants a data center in their backyard. ( MIT Technology Review ) 5 OpenAI is testing a “persistent” AI agent that keeps working Codex could continue tasks until it’s “put to sleep.” ( Wired $) + And generate follow-up tasks without prompting. ( Gizmodo ) 6 A lawsuit alleges that Grok was trained on child sexual abuse material It claims victims’ images entered the chatbot’s training data. ( Ars Technica ) + A federal judge says AI has outpaced child-abuse laws. ( WP $) 7 AI writing has reached a turning point in the media Sparked by the Wall Street Journal defending an AI-written op-ed. ( Atlantic $) 8 China’s robotic racers are exposing the limits of human speed Their advances are revealing what our bodies can’t do. ( Reuters $) 9 Young workers are turning to “AI-proof” traditional crafts They’re drawn to creative, hands-on skills that tech can’t easily replicate. ( Guardian ) 10 Scientists have a new army to fight invasive crabs: 150,000 baby octopuses Italian researchers just released the animals into the Adriatic Sea. ( New Scientist $) Quote of the day “ The academic record is being quietly haunted.”  —A new preprint research paper from Samsung and the University of Warsaw warns that a torrent of AI-generated study papers written by fake researchers is contaminating academic publishing. One more thing The problem with thinking you’re part Neanderthal There’s a theory that many of us have an “inner Neanderthal.” The idea is that Homo sapiens and a cousin species once bred, leaving some people today with a trace of Neanderthal DNA.  This DNA is arguably the 21st century’s most celebrated discovery in human evolution. But in 2024, a pair of French geneticists called into question the theory’s very foundations.  They proposed that what scientists interpret as interbreeding could instead be explained by population structure—the way genes concentrate in smaller, isolated groups. Find out what it all means for human evolution . —Ben Crair We can still have nice things A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? articles.title: Show HN: I built a tool showing how AI providers (should) throttle their models
articles.summary:
OP here: this project was born out of the frustration/paranoia that AI providers are throttling their models when their server load is too high. So, I set out to model and study the problem mathematically to understand what was happening, what I found was quite surprising.

The idea seems natura
articles._body: OP here: this project was born out of the frustration/paranoia that AI providers are throttling their models when their server load is too high. So, I set out to model and study the problem mathematically to understand what was happening, what I found was quite surprising. The idea seems natural: as the data center demand increases momentarily through the day, throttling their models (either using quantized versions, reducing the context window or lowering the tier of the model to a smaller one) seems appealing as the replacement model in principle uses less electricity. The problem is that this can cause the opposite effect: as users are trying to solve a question, if the degraded AI model gives a bad answer, the user is likely to keep re-asking. On the AI provider side this looks paradoxical: throttling to a lower model creates in fact more demand for their data center. This problem is even worse for agentic workflows, as these are more likely to create a re-ask storm, and maybe explains the outages and anecdotal experiences of users that feel the models are degraded. The model: I used mainly queueing theory arguments solving the optimal scheduling serving for an AI fleet with heterogeneous users solving a finite horizon Dynamic Programming optimization problem. Insights: The industry standard practice of throttling once the number of users in system exceeds a given threshold is in fact what’s causing the problem, the optimal rule implies separating users that won’t feel degradation as much with users that are very sensitive to it (agents and power users vs users doing simple tasks). Limitations: The visualization and paper examples are a toy example to illustrate the problem, only the providers have enough data to properly calibrate these instances. In the paper there are some interesting calibrated instances. Technical Details: The visualization is around 100 lines of flask plus js frontend (LLM assisted with ground truth based on the original numerical example of the paper). Paper with proofs/theory: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23986 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49477620 Points: 3 # Comments: 0

articles.title: Authorities arrest 2 alleged members of prolific hacking group TeamPCP
articles.summary: The group infected more than 1,000 organizations in a relentless supply-chain attack campaign.
articles._body: Authorities in Australia said Wednesday that they arrested two men accused of participating in cybercrimes for TeamPCP, a prolific group of hackers that, over nine months, has carried out a relentless series of supply-chain attacks that infected more than 1,000 organizations worldwide. In a statement , the Australian Federal Police said the two men were arrested and charged with 14 offenses. The statement said the men were members of TeamPCP, which by the authorities’ count, compromised more than 1,000 organizations worldwide. The statement didn’t identify the men, except to say they lived in the Western Australian towns of Cottesloe and Mandurah. KrebsOnSecurity, citing a lengthy investigation, provided what it reports to be both defendants' names , along with an extensive background of their lives and the mistakes that led to their downfall. The hacks that keep on hacking TeamPCP has vexed law enforcement officials and security personnel around the world since it emerged in December. The group is best known for a sustained series of supply-chain attacks that laced open source software with malware that self-propagated from one package to another. The viral infections worked by targeting organizations’ CI/CD pipelines, which are used to rapidly develop, update, and deploy software. Read full article Comments
