Hey now, we’re hosting All-Star 🌟 It’s official: @WNBA All-Star 2027 is coming to the Bay. See you there. pic.twitter.com/kfwrjEueec — Golden State Valkyries (@valkyries) August 18, 2026 It’s an opportunity to bring her mission of athlete wellness directly into the weeklong celebration. Marty is the CEO of Beyond the Game Health . Because of ailments she’s dealt with and is currently dealing with, her goal is to educate athletes from all over on how to advocate for themselves, make them aware of various aspects of their health and provide an outlet for them to grow in and outside of their sport. Here’s how Marty described her mission to Swish Appeal : I saw that the power of sports and also just really getting to know a lot of players throughout my journey and seeing what they go through, and I saw something there. I can use sports as a vehicle of ways to help raise awareness… I started navigating through the different sports industries, especially with the WNBA before the new agreement that came out, and we’re still fighting.  Though I mean, it’s a great agreement, but just learning-you know what? Healthcare is not really there after the game. It’s not really there. How can we protect our players? Because I know that there are things out there that can be done, and what can we do about that? What happens when the checks stop coming? Through health fairs, literacy programs, panels and other events and activities that tie an athlete to the community and their health, Marty is determined to reach anyone who wants to discover an extensive range of possibilities that can stretch their potential in the right direction. And now, she has the opportunity to bring that work to one of the biggest weeks on the women’s basketball calendar. After already partnering with Tiffany Hayes, Shamekka Marty has big plans for All-Star Weekend in the Bay Marty not only works closely with both professional basketball teams in the Bay Area, but she also has a close relationship with Valkyries guard Tiffany Hayes. Through prioritizing transformational over transactional relationships, she’s collaborated with Hayes through her foundation, Living On Purpose, and helped coordinate the WNBA Legends Brunch during All-Star Week. Meeting Hayes through a mutual friend, the two maintained their relationship off the court and came together to find ways to be there for their fellow athletes while also helping each other grow their brands. Hayes was someone who joined the Valkyries during their inaugural season in 2025. Since then, she said that she was all in from the start on what Golden State had to offer. As Hayes wrote in The Players’ Tribune : I still remember that day last year when I arrived for the first time. I’d recently won the Sixth Player of the Year award after my one season in Vegas. But for whatever reason, something just really drew me to Golden State. I loved the idea of doing something that might be uncomfortable, and trying to build something from the ground up.   That same feeling is what the Bay Area wants fans from all over to experience in 2027. Marty excitedly spoke to Swish Appeal about the activations she’s planning under her brand and what she’s looking forward to seeing come to life during the event. “What I can say is it’s going to be craziness. I mean, I know I’m not going to be able to breathe or just have five minutes myself.” The first activation will be a mixer honoring Black and Brown women in sports. The next will be a brunch with a panel that ties a health component to it. She also wants to host a few clinics free of charge for people to take part in alongside their favorite athletes. As Marty explained: Accessibility is a huge thing. Like I said in the beginning of the conversation, some people love sports and are really big sports fans, and no one thinks about the families that can’t afford it because of food insecurity. Or they might have parents that can’t afford it due to medical reasons. I want to make it free for them…That resonates with a lot of kids, where they’re like, “Oh my God, I can, I can even be able to meet them (the players). I can even be able to talk with them,” and have some of the OGs of the game—the Cheryl Millers, the Lisa Leslie, Dawn Staley—to be a part of it. And lastly, Marty wants to incorporate an event just for moms to enjoy a wellness reset while they’re there called “Moms of the Sport.” She emphasized: Nobody talks about how much they (moms) have sacrificed to get their children. Especially Tiffany (Hayes) talks about this all the time. She’s like, “It was just me and my mom.” We want to honor them, give them a spa treatment, take them somewhere, put that together. Nobody does the activations for the moms, and we want to be first to do something like that. WNBA All-Star 2027 is just part of Shamekka Marty’s advocacy for athletes Marty has lived in the Bay Area for 11 years, but she’s made the city her home and wants her advocacy for health in sports to be at the forefront in what adds to the city’s sports scene. She’s already helped organize and take part in conferences and events to support athletes, especially WNBA athletes. Now, with the WNBA All-Star 2027 being local to her and her community, she can take advantage of the opportunity to educate more people of all ages on the importance of taking care of themselves

articles.title: As the WNBA prepares to pause for the FIBA World Cup, what does the playoff picture look like?
articles.summary: As the FIBA World Cup break looms, the WNBA’s playoff picture is looking a lot clearer. We know who will be playing in the postseason now that all eight teams have clinched their spots. However, seeding is still very much up for grabs. Only three games separate the No. 3 seed and the No. 8 […]
articles._body: Napheesa Collier and Kayla McBride. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images As the FIBA World Cup break looms, the WNBA’s playoff picture is looking a lot clearer. We know who will be playing in the postseason now that all eight teams have clinched their spots. However, seeding is still very much up for grabs. Only three games separate the No. 3 seed and the No. 8 seed, so which teams will have homecourt in the opening round and beyond is still unknown. Here is an overview of the current playoff outlook for each team, with every team having about five games left to play. No. 1-seed Minnesota Lynx (31-8) The Minnesota Lynx are sitting pretty as the top seed. They are three games in front of the No. 2-seed Golden State Valkyries, and considering that they won the season series, only an utter collapse will have them falling in the standings. Minnesota is right where they want to be: in complete control of their destiny. No. 2-seed Golden State Valkyries (28-11) The Valkyries might not catch the Lynx, but they have to keep playing to win. The Las Vegas Aces are right behind them, just two games back in the standings. Since they lost all three matchups against Las Vegas, the Aces own the tiebreaker. So, the Valkyries need a couple more wins to lock up the second-best record in the WNBA. No. 3-seed Las Vegas Aces (26-13) Here is where things start to get interesting. The Aces are just a half game ahead of the Atlanta Dream and a full game in front of the Indiana Fever. Even with just five games left, that leaves plenty of possibilities. Las Vegas owns the tiebreaker over the Dream, but they lost the season series against the Fever. Luckily, they have the easiest schedule in the WNBA , giving them an advantage as they try to maintain their position. However, the season-ending injury to NaLyssa Smith could result in the Aces experiencing more challenges than their strength of schedule suggests. No. 4-seed Atlanta Dream (25-13) The Dream have had a very good year. Head coach Karl Smesko has his team on track for another season with a better than 60-percent winning percentage. They are hanging on to the No. 4 spot, just a half game in front of the Fever. Atlanta and Indiana split their head-to-head matchups, and they are currently neck and neck on the next tiebreaker, which is the best record against teams with a record over .500. The Dream are 11-11 and the Fever are 10-12 against winning teams, so the team that will end up with the fourth seed will likely come down to the last weekend of the WNBA season. No. 5-seed Indiana Fever (25-14) The Fever have the firepower to win it all. But, they need to stack up some victories to be in position to do it. That’s not going to be easy for Indiana because they have so many matchups left against playoff opponents. They play the Lynx twice and face the Washington Mystics, New York Liberty and Dallas Wings. If they are truly title contenders, then they’ll win more than they lose and will stay at the No. 5 spot, and perhaps even jump up in the standings. No. 6-seed Washington Mystics (24-15) The Mystics have been the pleasant surprise of the year. Their youth movement is ahead of schedule, and they’ll be competing in the playoffs this year instead of tanking for a draft pick. They are only a game ahead of the Wings and Liberty, so they could still drop down to eighth if they have a bad ending to the regular season. Regardless, it’s been a good year in Washington, and they are playing with house money. There is no pressure at this point, and whatever happens will be a good learning experience for the Mystics as their rebuild is going better than anyone, even if the organization itself, could have envisioned. No. 7-seed Dallas Wings (23-16) The Wings have been up and down lately. While they’ve won three-straight games, they’re 5-5 over their last 10 contests, and with Azzi Fudd out for the rest of the year, it’s hard to see how they can make a jump in the standings. However, with Paige Bueckers, all things are possible. Dallas is just a game behind the Mystics, so there is hope they can avoid the bottom two playoff spots. No. 8-seed New York Liberty (23-16) The Liberty’s entire year has been a struggle. They were supposed to take a step forward, and they’ve done the opposite. Unless they dominate their remaining schedule, they’ll finish with their worst winning percentage since 2022. The good news is they’re in the playoffs. Also, with five games left, a strong finish could push them as high as the No. 4 seed. It’s unlikely they’ll end up that high, but they can finish better than they currently stand. Despite all eight teams securing their spot, just getting in isn’t the only thing that matters. Last year, the only lower seed to win in the first round was the No. 6-seed Fever. Homecourt advantage is incredibly value, so every team needs to try to set themselves up for success. When the World Cup break ends, there will be just one week of WNBA regular-season action for these eight teams to improve their playoff position, or put themselves at risk of an early postseason exit. Jump in the comments and let us know how you think the playoff seeds will shake out.

articles.title: WNBA gameday discussion: Can DeWanna Bonner help Atlanta realize their championship Dream?
articles.summary: DeWanna Bonner is now an Atlanta Dream, arriving with the goal of fulfilling one, final championship dream. On Aug. 24, Bonner and the Phoenix Mercury amicably agreed to a contract buyout, with the organization announcing through a statement from general manager Nick U’Ren: DeWanna has been an impor
articles._body: Rhyne Howard and Allisha Gray speak to new teammate DeWanna Bonner. | NBAE via Getty Images DeWanna Bonner is now an Atlanta Dream, arriving with the goal of fulfilling one, final championship dream. On Aug. 24, Bonner and the Phoenix Mercury amicably agreed to a contract buyout, with the organization announcing through a statement from general manager Nick U’Ren : DeWanna has been an important part of our team and brought tremendous leadership, experience and competitiveness to the Mercury. Because of the relationship we have with DeWanna, we worked out a buyout agreement that gives her the opportunity to chase a title in what could be her final postseason. After making the decision with the Mercury, Bonner herself said : At this stage of my career, I don’t know what the future holds, but I’m grateful to the Mercury for giving me the opportunity to play in what could be one of my final postseason opportunities. Eh, I’d say DeWanna had a pretty good idea about her immediate future, as she would not have sought the buyout if she did not already have a strong inkling about her next destination. Per ESPN’s Alexa Philippou , the Las Vegas Aces and New York Liberty also expressed interest in Bonner, while the Dream’s pursuit of the Fairfield, AL native and former Auburn star reportedly went back years. Breaking: Free agent DeWanna Bonner is signing with the Atlanta Dream, sources told ESPN. A huge addition for the championship-hopeful Dream, who will now be incorporating a two-time WNBA champion and 6x All-Star into the mix pic.twitter.com/2AzUfnQ3qU — Alexa Philippou (@alexaphilippou) August 26, 2026 So, will DeWanna achieve her Dream of going out with a third WNBA championship? On the court, the theoretical value that Bonner can add to the Dream is obvious. She’s a three-time Sixth Player of the Year who bolsters a rather weak and inexperienced Atlanta bench. Her willingness to fire away from behind the arc certainly fits the philosophy of head coach Karl Smesko, and her length will allow her to function within Atlanta’s elite defense. But, there’s a reason that value is theoretical . The 39-year-old Bonner is the second-oldest player in the league. And while she is a six-time All-Star who has scored the third-most points in WNBA history, her 10.2 points per game is the second-lowest average of her career, with her field goal percentage of 39 percent standing as the lowest mark of her career. From 3, she’s converting just 25.6 percent of her 4.5 attempts per game, her worst percentage from deep since 2020. But, maybe Bonner will stumble into a timely hot streak and her shots will begin to fall? For that to happen, she probably needs to play, and it’s unclear how much time she’ll receive. A huge reason Atlanta’s bench has underperformed is because Smesko rides his starters. Considering Atlanta’s starting five of Jordin Canada, Rhyne Howard, Allisha Gray, Naz Hillmon and Angel Reese has the best net rating in the league, Smesko is probably smart to allocate as many minutes as possible to that fivesome. According to databallr’s adjusted net rating , Atlanta’s five has a +12.9 net rating, which is three points clear the net rating of the Minnesota Lynx’s starting group. And Smesko certainly pushes his favored five. Howard leads the league in minutes per game at 34.4, with Gray ranking ninth at 32.9. All five starters are in the top 30 in total minutes. In the postseason, expect Smesko to extend the minutes of his starters, as it is customary for a team’s best players to receive rare rest in the playoffs. So, it’s hard to see Bonner getting more than 10 or 12 minutes per game, especially if she continues to shoot so inefficiently. I wouldn’t be surprised if she is limited to a two-minute cameo here or there in tightly-contested games. All that paints a pretty pesimisstic picture of Bonner’s impact in Atlanta. But, her addition is not all for naught, as she can have a significant off-the-court influence. 2x WNBA champion. 6x WNBA All-Star. One of the most accomplished players in WNBA history. Welcome to the A, DeWanna 🅰️ pic.twitter.com/m4O60VonF9 — Atlanta Dream (@AtlantaDream) August 27, 2026 As I’ve emphasized since Atlanta traded for her , Angel has injected the Dream with a needed intensity and urgency. In just her first season with a team, she’s emerged as a leader. But, she’s also a third-year player who has never played a playoff game. Bonner, who also plays with her own visible brand of passion and pulse that can complement that of Reese, not only has two titles, but also has 98 playoff games and 3,016 playoff minutes on her resume. She plays with a fire, and she’s been through fires. Imparting all the knowledge gained from those infernos can benefit a Dream squad that, last postseason, crumbled in the first-round playoff crucible against a lower-seeded team. Bonner has two daughters. In joining the Dream, she might have acquired 11 more. Being a stern-yet-sensitive mom who shares wisdom, rather than the former Sixth Player of the Year who bombs triples, might be Bonner’s primary role for this team. In speaking to USA TODAY about Bonner joining the Dream, Reese called her “a big sister,” while also emphasizing that DB will offer “veteran leadership” from “knowing what it takes to be a champion.” “I was really excited to have her here. She's probably been trying to get here for a couple of years now.” Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream welcomed the DeWanna Bonner era today. Here’s more from Reese and Atlanta: https://t.co/kUpXN14AVu — Meghan L. Hall (@ItsMeghanLHall) August 27, 2026 Unfortunately for us eager fans, Friday night will not offer a first opportunity to see Bonner in Dream threads, as she is expected to be in attendance but not yet make her debut when Atlanta hosts the Portland Fire (7:30 p.m. ET, ION). Brionna Jones, a former teammate of Bonner with the Connecticut Sun for five seasons, also remains sidelined, with little clarity about the st

articles.title: Will four-time winner A’ja Wilson or rookie phenom Olivia Miles go down in WNBA MVP history?
articles.summary: Last year, in addition to becoming the first four-time MVP in WNBA history, A’ja Wilson became just the second back-to-back MVP. Cynthia Cooper accomplished the feat 27 years earlier in the league’s first two seasons. Now, Wilson is the frontrunner to win an unprecedented third MVP in a row. It woul
articles._body: A’ja Wilson and Olivia Miles. (Photo by Matt Krohn) | Getty Images Last year, in addition to becoming the first four-time MVP in WNBA history, A’ja Wilson became just the second back-to-back MVP. Cynthia Cooper accomplished the feat 27 years earlier in the league’s first two seasons. Now, Wilson is the frontrunner to win an unprecedented third MVP in a row. It would be her fifth total, which is mind-boggling, especially considering she just turned 30 years old and likely has quite some time left in her career. 𝑀'𝑽𝑃 in her element 🫡 For the 32nd time in her career, A’ja Wilson earns @wnba Western Conference Player of the Week honors. pic.twitter.com/cKQcE61mac — Las Vegas Aces (@LVAces) August 25, 2026 Wilson leads the player many consider to be second in the running, Olivia Miles, by a whopping 8.3 statistical points when you add up their averages in points, rebounds, assists times 1.5, steals and blocks. Miles has a slightly higher effective field goal percentage and a slightly higher free throw percentage, but Wilson’s lead in stat score is overwhelming. A’ja Wilson: 43.7 stat score / 54.9 eFG% / 85.8 FT% Olivia Miles: 35.4 stat score / 55.4 eFG% / 86.9 FT%   But should the MVP only be about statistics? Should voters think outside the box and give the MVP to Olivia Miles? Miles has led a Minnesota Lynx team that nobody expected to have best record in the league. The Lynx are 3.5 games ahead of the next closest team in the current WNBA standings and five games ahead of Wilson’s Las Vegas Aces, who were considered to be one of the frontrunners at the beginning of the season. Miles has done it all, all while facing the pressure of being a rookie. These circumstances will undoubtedly be factored in when the media votes; already, major media outlets have been portraying the race as closer than the numbers indicate it should be. "Wins. I love helping my team win." Impacting the game on every level, Olivia Miles takes the most pride in helping her team earn the dub ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/GkAXj5HGFx — USA Sports (@usasports) August 25, 2026 Then there’s the historic bias against guards that has to be taken into consideration. Miles, a 5-foot-10 point guard, shouldn’t be expected to rebound the ball at the same rate as Wilson, a 6-foot-4 forward/center. That’s not part of her job description. As I wrote about in my 2025 MVP ladder 2.0 , the WNBA MVP award has only been given to a true guard three times: Cooper twice and Diana Taurasi once. Clearly, the stat score method I use when determining my MVP favors frontcourt players, even though I multiply assists by 1.5. Other analysts have their own formulas or considerations when trying to capture a player’s statiscal impact, but they keep coming up with the same answer: The most-deserving MVP candidates are almost always versatile 3s, 4s and 5s. Shooting guard Kelsey Mitchell of the Indiana Fever is a great example of someone whose stat score is always low for a star because she doesn’t fill out the box score beyond scoring. But she is rightfully in the MVP conversation this season alongside Wilson and Miles because basketball experts who watch the games can see that she affects the game beyond the box score because of how much of a threat she is to score. Sometimes doing one job (in this case scoring) really well is all a player should need to gain consideration. Miles is probably a more gifted passer than she is a scorer, and that may always be the case. But she has turned into someone who loves to score. As a result, her assist average (6.1 per game) isn’t a top-five mark in the league, but it’s still very good. Plus, she’s averaging nearly 20 points per game, which good enough to be in the conversation for the scoring title most years. And the intangibles have been phenomenal. “The Spectacle” has electrified the league with thrilling performance after thrilling performance. Again, all this has come while dealing with the challenge of getting used to the professional level. “I haven’t seen anything like her coming in as a rookie and being as dominant since Candace Parker.” @tinacharles31 is a big Olivia Miles fan 👏 pic.twitter.com/tVqQb2jbvA — espnW (@espnW) August 21, 2026 What if it’s not yet someone else’s turn? Isn’t A’ja Wilson still the best? Let’s argue Wilson’s case though. It seems Miles has a legitimate shot at getting some first place votes. But if Miles wins the award, that won’t properly reflect that Wilson is still in the midst of her reign as the best player in the world. Are we subconsciously discriminating against Wilson because we think it’s someone else’s turn? The MVP award can only go to one person, and years from now, when we see that one name listed, we will automatically think that player was the clear-cut best player in the league that year. The name on the list doesn’t tell the true story of all the arguments that were had for other players. When future generations look back on 2023, they will see Breanna Stewart’s name and not be aware of the intense debate that occurred between Stewie, A’ja and Alyssa Thomas. It’s unlikely many people will dig deeper, look at the voting and realize that AT actually got the most first-place votes. So Miles’ name may go down in history as the MVP this year. She would be the second rookie to win the award, after Candace Parker in 2008. And she might be deserving. But it would be a shame for people to not remember how close Wilson came to three MVPs in a row and five in seven years. We should celebrate the accomplishment that has been A’ja showing up and being A’ja Wilson yet again. We shouldn’t take it for granted. Yet, it will likely be forgotten if she doesn’t win MVP. In my stat score, what Wilson gains in having 9.5 rebounds per game is pretty much canceled out by multiplying Miles’ assists per game by 1.5, which comes out to 9.2. The real difference between the two is Wilson’s incredible scoring average of 26 points per game being 6.3 pointes higher

articles.title: After a season of missteps, a (finally) forthcoming practice facility is a step in the right direction for the Los Angeles Sparks
articles.summary: Not much has gone right for the Los Angeles Sparks in 2026. But on Wednesday, Aug. 26, with the heat blazing in El Segundo, CA, a ray of sunshine landed on LA’s WNBA franchise as they held their topping-out ceremony for their practice facility. Things are far from done. There is no pavement to be [&
articles._body: Cameron Brink, Chance Gray and Kate Martin. | Getty Images Not much has gone right for the Los Angeles Sparks in 2026. But on Wednesday, Aug. 26, with the heat blazing in El Segundo, CA, a ray of sunshine landed on LA’s WNBA franchise as they held their topping-out ceremony for their practice facility. I'm here for the LA Sparks’ training facility topping-out ceremony. pic.twitter.com/fJd6KR5R3y — Edwin Garcia (@ECreates88) August 26, 2026 Things are far from done. There is no pavement to be found surrounding the building. It’s just a ton of dust, uneven ground and rocks. However, the frame is ready, the images are rendered and a practice facility, finally, is on the way for the Sparks. Current players were in attendance to celebrate this momentous occasion. Here’s what Nneka Ogwumike said: So all in all, today is an exciting day because we can finally stand firmly inside something we’ve talked about and imagined for so long. I know I’ve been a part of many displacements with the Sparks over the years. And even though I may not necessarily be playing as a player in this facility next year, it is filling my heart to see it completely represented in the legacy that has and will always be the Sparks. Not only is this a $150 million, state-of-the-art practice facility, but it also gives the Sparks a permanent home. In recent years, the Sparks have been renters in Los Angeles. They’ve spent 2025 and 2026 practicing in a facility in Torrance, CA, and during the 2024 and 2023 seasons they practiced at El Camino Community College. No community college, no matter how nice, is fit for a professional organization. Those days will be a thing of the past. The Sparks will now go from questionable conditions to some of the best in the WNBA. Here is everything their new practice facility will offer, all surrounded by panoramic views of the Pacific Ocean: WNBA’s first-ever indoor-outdoor player sanctuary, featuring: An outdoor spa pool for recovery and pre-hab/rehab Dedicated nap rooms Flexible wellness spaces for yoga, meditation and quiet reflection Hydrotherapy and spa suites Two WNBA regulation basketball courts Circular locker room designed to foster team unity State-of-the-art weight room and training spaces bathed in daylight to support energy and recovery The organization has further proclaimed : The Los Angeles Sparks’ training facility is more than a home base for athletes—it is a statement of intent about the future of the WNBA in Los Angeles. Designed as a year-round home away from home, it reflects the franchise’s mission to invest deeply in its players while cementing its place in LA’s vibrant sports culture. Sparks players were all smiles, even with temperatures over 100 degrees on this August day. They signed a beam that needed to be put in place and watched, along with assembled media and the rest of the organization, as it was secured. And here is the beam being put in place. https://t.co/X3NbgVReE1 pic.twitter.com/fW5NdElhKj — Edwin Garcia (@ECreates88) August 26, 2026 With the beams in place and the ceremony complete, the facility is set to open by the start of next season, according to team president Stacy Johns. The 2027 season will be an important one for the Sparks, although they have a laundry list of things to do before if tips offs, including selecting a couple of first-round picks in the draft, hiring a general manager and building out a new vision for the team now that Kelsey Plum has been traded and Ogwumike is retiring . While the path to title contention is daunting, the expectation is that building that culture and getting players to buy in starts with this facility. As Johns explained: This is a huge recruiting tool. We’re a mile from the ocean in Los Angeles, CA, specifically the city of El Segundo, but I think when you’re looking for a reason why you want to play here, you’re gonna come here, and you’re not gonna see another facility like this in the WNBA.

articles.title: WNBA gameday discussion: Who is the most-underrated player in the league? And why is it Breanna Stewart?
articles.summary: Imagine telling someone six years ago that Breanna Stewart, who then would have been fresh off her second WNBA title within the first five seasons of her pro career after winning four national championships in four college seasons at UConn, along with garnering a slew of collegiate and professional
articles._body: Veronica Burton races up the court against Breanna Stewart and Marine Johannès. | Getty Images Imagine telling someone six years ago that Breanna Stewart, who then would have been fresh off her second WNBA title within the first five seasons of her pro career after winning four national championships in four college seasons at UConn, along with garnering a slew of collegiate and professional individuals accolades, would be underrated. Yet, I think that’s where we are. In a WNBA, like the larger sports world, that obsesses over who is new and next, the steady, lowkey consistency of Stewie is passé. Stewie is Stewie, and that’s it. Just a 🐐 bein’ a 🐐 pic.twitter.com/lhYEYYN6fz — New York Liberty (@nyliberty) August 19, 2026 A few years ago, Zack Ward wrote about Stewart settling in as the second-best women’s basketball player world, permanently behind A’ja Wilson. Now, a healthy Napheesa Collier occupies that second spot, with Stewart pushed down, or even out, of the top five. I’d argue she still has a pretty solid case for No. 3. I expect her greatness to be quite clear at next month’s FIBA World Cup, when she will reprise her role alongside Wilson as the present-day foundation of the Team USA dynasty. This season, the floundering state of the New York Liberty has somewhat sullied a stellar season, even though New York certainly would have sunk without her superstar services. STEW-S-A 👏🫡 🇺🇸 #USABWNT 🔟 @breannastewart pic.twitter.com/xgltVF8Nyo — USA Basketball (@usabasketball) August 25, 2026 Help the Helper’s wRAPM (regularized adjusted plus-minus) metric has consistently rated Stewart as the most impactful player in the WNBA during the 2026, as she sports a +6.6 wRAPM valuation. That metric, aimed at capturing a player’s contextualized impact on her team’s performance, indicates Stewie’s excellence exceeds her still-superb traditional stats: 20.8 points, 8.1 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.4 blocks per game. And, she’s achieved all the production and impact even with her persisting and puzzling troubles from behind the arc, as she’s barely hitting over 25 percent of her 3-point attempts. Maybe a potential playoff run , where Stewie leads the Liberty out of the first, or even the second, round would inspire an appreciation of her still-towering talent. On Thursday, Stewart and the Liberty host the visiting Golden State Valkyries, the type of team, and possibly the exact team, New York projects to have to beat in order to go on an underdog playoff run (8 p.m. ET, Prime Video). The Valkyries themselves also feature a player who could credibly challenge Stewie for the WNBA’s most-underrated crown, as do the combatants in Thursday night’s second game: the Washington Mystics and Phoenix Mercury (10 p.m. ET, Prime Video). In the comments, let us know if you consider Stewie, as well as these three other candidates, some of the most-underrated players in the W. Also be sure to share the names of other players who you think deserve more love. Veronica Burton (Golden State Valkyries) Last season’s Most Improved Player and an All-Defense selection, who also won an Unrivaled championship with Stewart over the offseason, Veronica Burton seemed fated for an All-Star honor in fifth WNBA season. Burton, instead, landed on a long list of snubs, with her inefficiency as a scorer, plus Golden State’s outstanding depth, keeping her out of the midseason festivities. Her raw scoring statistics—12.3 points per game on 42.7 percent shooting—fail to capture how she makes good things happen for the Valkyries. She has the highest on-court plus-minus on the team, with Golden State outscoring opponents by an average of 6.2 points per game in her minutes. That’s also a top-15 mark in the league. According to Help the Helper’s wRAPM, Burton rates even more highly, with +3.9 wRAPM estimate ranking seventh in the league. Databallr’s VPM (value plus-minus) metric, which incorporates lineup-adjusted plus-minus data with box-score stats to offer a valuation of player impact, gives even more credit to Burton, scoring her as +3.9, which is the fifth-best mark in the league. Yes, a player’s scoring efficiently is important, but winning a player’s minutes—any way, any how—is more important, ultimately determining which team wins the game. And this season, Golden State just wins more with Burton. That certainly happened on Wednesday night. Burton logged just 20 minutes, scoring 12 points and dishing seven assists as she was a game-best +24 in the Valkyries’ comfortable win over the Connecticut Sun. Sonia Citron (Washington Mystics) Soaring after her All-Star snub, Shakira Austin also belongs in the most-underrated conversation. Sonia Citron, however, also is deserving of more appreciation. Advanced stats evaluate Citron as the Mystics’ most impactful player, with databallr rating her as the only positive offensive player on the Mystics with a +1.6 OVPM and a team-best +2.2 VPM. Help the Helper measures Citron, Austin and Kiki Iriafen as equally impactful, with all three of the Washington stars owning a wRAPM estimate of +0.7. Similar to both Stewart and Burton, Citron is registering this impact in spite of some shooting struggles. Almost automatic from 3 as a rookie, Sonia’s 3-pointer has been off this season, with her percentage hovering in the low 30s. If she ascends back over 40 percent, look out! Encouragingly, Citron made three of her six 3-point attempts in the first game of the two-game set between the Mystics and Mercury, with those triples, plus 6-for-7 work from the line, helping her score a team-best 19 points as she also was a team-high +18. And although not an All-Star snub like Austin, she was, arguably, the most significant Team USA snub for the World Cup. The American guard room is a bit overstocked with primary ball handlers who are questionable defensively.
